title: vta-sdk-v0.71.0
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Every surface shows a member the same community rooms, and finishes an acceptance any other began ([#2186](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2186))

* feat(rooms): every surface shows a member the same community rooms, and finishes an acceptance any other began

  A member reaches their community from several surfaces — the member portal
  through their wallet, pnm, OpenVTC — and each kept no shared view: offers/list
  drops an accepted offer after seven days, so a room accepted in one surface
  was invisible to the others after that, and an acceptance one surface began
  could be finished by no other (its mint replaced the private half the kept
  Welcome is sealed to, and the community answered alreadyAccepted).

  VTC
  - vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1: the community's own record of the signer's
    admissions to the rooms it owns — offered, admitted, removed; never a
    withdrawn offer, never a credential — with repeatAcceptUntil while a sealed
    admission's Welcome is kept. Answers only an active member, for themself.

  VTA
  - rooms/keys/key-package/0.2: returns the outstanding KeyPackage for the same
    room, member and invitation (alreadyMinted: true, original expiresAt), and
    mints only otherwise; serialised so concurrent requests get the same one.
    RetrySafe, where 0.1 is Keyed.
  - rooms/keys/welcome/0.1: a Welcome under a spent invitation, for the member
    who joined with it, is alreadyJoined (welcome/0.1's rule) rather than
    "invitation already used" — so a surface finishing another's acceptance
    reads it as success.
  - rooms/keys/act/0.5: 0.4 ([#2183](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2183)), and vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1 —
    COMMUNITY_TYPES, 0.4's OFFER_TYPES_0_4 and memberships/list. 0.3 and 0.4
    refuse memberships/list (their schemas' type pattern); an acceptance's
    KeyPackage may come from key-package 0.1 or 0.2.

  SDK / pnm
  - VtaClient::room_key_package_v0_2, room_act_community (act 0.5, then 0.4 and
    0.3 for the offer types an older VTA completes), unsigned_community_request,
    is_community_type.
  - pnm rooms memberships: the community's record beside the VTA's custody, as
    every surface shows it. pnm rooms offers accept checks custody first, asks
    for the KeyPackage at 0.2 (0.1 against an older VTA), and reads
    alreadyJoined as joined.

  pnm's offer steps keep #2183's OfferStepError and offers/list 0.2 to 0.1
  fallback, now through room_act_community.

  trust-tasks-rs floor 0.31.16.

- **vtc**: Vtc/rooms/community/members/remove 0.2 — a removed member is refused at the room's host at once ([#2175](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2175))

* feat(vtc): vtc/rooms/community/members/remove 0.2 — a removed member is refused at the room's host at once

  The community half of trust-tasks-tf #804. A member removed from a room the
  community owns kept every credential the room gave them, honoured at the host
  until `validUntil`; on an `open` room removal withdrew nothing at all.

  `vtc/rooms/community/members/remove/0.2` (0.1 still served, unchanged):
  - item 2, admitted member: `open` — the community's VTA withdraws them
    (`rooms/owner/revoke`, one `subject` withdrawal, delivered to this community
    as the room's host); `attributed` — `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.2`,
    withdrawing first and then advancing (a member with no leaf is withdrawn
    alone); `private` — `group/remove/0.1`, the group alone;
  - item 3: an open offer is withdrawn, and on `open` and `attributed` its
    credentials at the host too;
  - recorded only once the VTA answered and, on `open`/`attributed`, the host
    accepted the withdrawal; a refused delivery is `keyHolderRefused`, an
    unconfirmed one `keyHolderUnavailable`;
  - item 4: the answer carries `revocation` (the list's head) and `revokedAt`
    beside `member` and, on a sealed tier, `epoch`; the `ext` notice says what
    the tier's removal does.

  The removal is one function (`rooms::departures::remove_member`) used by the
  administrator's request and by the departure worker ([#2156](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2156)), so a member who
  leaves the community is withdrawn at the host of every room it owns too. Every
  departure removal now asks the VTA, so a pass stops at the first silent VTA.

- **rooms**: Rooms/keys/act 0.4 — a member reads each offered room's description (vtc/rooms/offers/list 0.2) ([#2183](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2183))

Serve `rooms/keys/act/0.4` (trust-tasks-tf #810) beside 0.3, 0.2 and 0.1.

  - VTA: 0.4's offer row adds `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2` beside `0.1`, on
    the same terms — no presentation, `issuer` required and resolved without
    a room credential (recipient item 2b). `room_act::OFFER_TYPES` stays
    0.3's closed table; `OFFER_TYPES_0_4` is 0.4's, and `ActVersion::
    completes_offer` picks by the version asked, so a 0.3 request wrapping
    list 0.2 is still refused `typeNotActable` (0.3 recipient item 1).
    Dispatch, policy-gate subject (`/document/issuer`), conformance witness
    and `RetrySafe` classification as for 0.3.
  - SDK (breaking): `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_4`; `room_act` and
    `unsigned_room_request` take and return the 0.4 generated types. A room
    request is asked at 0.4 → 0.3 → 0.2 → 0.1, list/accept 0.1 at 0.4 → 0.3,
    and list 0.2 at 0.4 only (`UnsupportedTaskType` otherwise).
    `is_offer_type` includes list 0.2.
  - pnm: `rooms offers list` asks list 0.2 through act 0.4 and prints each
    room's description on an `about:` line, every control character replaced.
    It falls back to list 0.1 (act 0.3 when the VTA lacks 0.4) when either
    the member's VTA or the community answers `unsupportedType` /
    `unsupportedVersion` — each party's refusal is kept apart
    (`OfferStepError`). `accept` reads the offer the same way.
  - Member portal: the offers card shows the description the wallet carries
    (`PageOffer.description`), as text, bounded to the schema's 1000.
  - Docs: community-rooms (the description gap closes; what remains is an
    older VTA or VTC), the quickstart, data-rooms, the files design note.
  - trust-tasks-rs floor 0.31.15 (the act 0.4 and offers/list 0.2 generated types).

- **rooms**: Rooms/owner/revoke and group/remove 0.2 — the owner's VTA withdraws a member at the host before it advances ([#2174](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2174))

The key-holder half of trust-tasks-tf #804. Only the room signs a revocation
  list, and the owner's VTA holds the room's key, so the VTA is where lists are
  made.

  - The list is kept with the room's key: `room_groups` (backed up, encrypted),
    `room-revocations/<roomId>`, one per room whatever persona signs. Building
    and signing a room's next list is serialized per room (owner/revoke item 3),
    signed as the room through `RoomKeySigner` — the gated oracle that mints the
    room's credentials, `ProtocolDefined` — and kept and persisted before it is
    delivered anywhere (item 4).
  - `rooms/owner/revoke/0.1`: roomSubject, noSigningKey, noAuthority, noList
    before anything is signed (item 1); the tier from registration or
    `rooms/info` when a withdrawal names anyone (entryNotPermitted on private,
    tierUnknown otherwise; item 2); `revokedAt` stamped at signing; delivered to
    every host with `rooms/revocations/put` presenting the owner persona's
    `admin`, each outcome reported (`accepted` only when the host answered with
    this list's head; item 5). A success whatever the deliveries (item 6); a
    `stale` answer is surfaced as a security signal. Before signing it asks each
    host for its list and adopts a later one the room signed (verified under the
    room's own key and a method under the room's DID) — recovery for a key
    holder restored from an old backup.
  - `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.2`: signingKeyId required, `mirrors`, `until`;
    refuses a private room (privateRoom). The commit, link and the signed list
    are retained as the room's pending advance before anything is sent (item 5);
    the list goes to the host first and nothing advances until it is accepted
    (item 6: a refused list discards the whole removal, list included, rolling
    the held list back only while nothing was built on it); then the advance (a
    refused advance keeps the withdrawal); then the mirrors (`mirrorsPending`).
    A later request settles a pending removal by delivering its list again first
    (item 8). `hostUnreachable`/`hostRefused` carry `details.stage`.
  - `rooms/owner/register` records the room's tier and delivers the list it
    holds to the host before answering, so a room moving hosts arrives with its
    withdrawals.
  - SDK: `room_group_remove_v0_2`, `room_owner_revoke`; both `Keyed` in
    `retry_safety`, in the budget's host-reaching set and the MCP guard as
    Sensitive. `room_group_remove` stays 0.1.
  - pnm: `rooms owner group-remove --signing-key` asks 0.2 and falls back to
    0.1 only on `privateRoom` — the one case the specification hands to 0.1;
    without `--signing-key` it is 0.1 and says the credentials stay valid.
    `rooms owner revoke --host … [--subject|--credential|--reset]` (no
    withdrawal re-delivers).

- TEE first-boot enrols the claim DID as the bootstrap admin instead of minting a key ([#2066](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2066)) ([#2182](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2182))

A TEE VTA's first-boot claim (`POST /bootstrap/request`) used to mint an
  admin did:key inside the enclave and HPKE-seal its private key back to the
  claimant (`SealedPayloadV1::AdminCredential`). That contradicts VTI-CLT-001 /
  VTI-CLT-002: the client generates its own key and its private key never
  leaves it. Since #1987 the claimant already arrives with a key of its own,
  the pre-registered `tee.bootstrap_claim_did`, so the enclave now enrols that.

  Server (wire version 2, `vta_sdk::tee_bootstrap`):

  - On a verified claim, under `MODE_B_LOCK` and with the same carve-out
    ordering, durability and integrity-manifest reseal, the enclave writes an
    ACL entry for the claim DID itself (VTI-CLT-010): Admin, unrestricted (as
    the minted admin was), expiring after 24h (VTI-CLT-014), and marked as a
    hand-off (VTI-ACL-054) whose granter is the VTA DID as first-boot authority
    and whose bound is an unrestricted, permanent admin.
  - The answer is an attested acknowledgement (`FirstBootAck`) with no key
    material: vtaDid, adminDid, expiresAt, producerDid and the Nitro quote. The
    quote's user_data is unchanged (SHA256(client || nonce || producer)), so
    --expect-pcr0 / --expect-pcr8 pinning works as before. Nothing is sealed,
    so no SealedPayloadV1 variant is added and none is reshaped.
  - The claim signature now binds the target VTA DID under a new domain tag:
    `vti/bootstrap-claim/v2\0 || client_pub || nonce || utf8(vtaDid)`. The
    enclave refuses a claim naming any DID but its own (403, before the
    carve-out, after the claimant check). Together with the quote this means
    the acknowledgement for a nonce can only come from an enclave holding the
    DID the claimant signed.
  - `GET /bootstrap/request` answers `{version, vtaDid}` for `--vta-url`
    clients (declared in REST_EXCEPTIONS beside the POST).
  - `acl/grant/0.1` with `ext["org.openvtc"].handoffRollover: true` exercises
    the caller's hand-off marker onto a successor the caller minted
    (VTI-CLT-017, VTI-ACL-055 - 057), via the existing `exercise_handoff`.

  Client (`pnm bootstrap connect`):

  - Signs a v2 claim, verifies the acknowledgement against the claim
    (`FirstBootAck::verify`) and the pinned image, registers the VTA, mints the
    long-term did:key locally, persists it, exercises the hand-off as the claim
    DID, confirms by authenticating as the new key, then destroys the claim key
    (VTI-CLT-033 - 035). A 403 stays the substitution signal (VTI-CLT-016).
  - Not `acl/swap-key`: a rotation preserves expiry exactly (VTI-CLT-029), so
    rotating off the expiring bootstrap entry would leave the VTA's only admin
    expiring with it, and nobody could lift it.
  - An interrupted run is resumed by re-running `connect`: a 410 for a slug
    that already registered that VTA DID (only written after a verified, pinned
    acknowledgement) continues the hand-over with the staged key.
  - `--expect-digest` / `--no-verify-digest` are removed from `connect` (there
    is no bundle to digest); `--expect-pcr0` is required, `--no-verify-pcr0` is
    the warned opt-out.

- **vtc**: Community rooms carry their own name — create 0.3 and update 0.2 write the label and description into the room ([#2179](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2179))

Implements the community side of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#807:
  vtc/rooms/community/create/0.3 and vtc/rooms/community/update/0.2, on top
  of the community-room details ([#805](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/805)).

  - create 0.3 (step 5, items 8-9): once the room is stored, the community's
    own VTA is asked (rooms/keys/profile/write, as the community, with this
    VTC as host) to write the label as the profile's `name` and the
    description as its `description` — never the tags. The answer's
    `roomProfile` is `written` only when the VTA answered written, otherwise
    `pending`; the room stands either way.
  - update 0.2 (items 10-12): a change of label or description writes the
    profile again, first reading the current one and carrying over the tags,
    emoji and ext a curator set in the room; a room made before create 0.3 (or
    one still pending) is written even when nothing changed, and that is not
    audited as a change; a tags-only change answers `unchanged`. The change to
    the owner's record never depends on the write. Update 0.1 still never
    reaches the VTA.
  - rooms::community_profile: the one retry owner for `pending` profiles — a
    record per room (`room-profile:<room>`, beside the owner's record),
    written pending before the VTA is asked and written only after it
    answered, one attempt per due room per pass with a capped backoff and
    jitter (1 min to 6 h), always writing the room's label and description as
    they are at the attempt, so a later update supersedes a pending one.
  - get/list carry ext["org.openvtc"].roomProfile (written / pending with the
    retry state / none); the console shows it on a room's page and creates at
    0.3 and updates at 0.2, toasting a `pending`; cnm rooms create/update use
    0.3/0.2 (falling back to 0.2/0.1 against an older VTC) and get/list show
    the state.
  - The community's entry at its VTA needs `room-open` for the profile tasks:
    added to the capabilities the VTA-access fix commands name, and to the
    docs. The community's own authority already confers admin, write and
    curate (create item 6), so item 12's re-issue is never needed here.
  - Both new versions dispatched, with conformance entries, OpenAPI wrappers
    (openapi.json and wire.ts regenerated) and the console manifest.

- **rooms**: A room's own profile — rooms/keys/profile/{read,write}, sealed inside the room ([#2171](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2171))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#807 on the key holder's side. A
  room's name, description, tags and emoji (RoomProfile) now live inside the
  room: one record per epoch at profile_key(E) — HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch's
  storage key, info "openvtc/room/profile/v1" || roomId || u64be(E), 16 bytes,
  base64url — sealed like any record, so the host stores one more opaque record
  and cannot tell which one names the room. An open room's is the record at
  `room-profile`, its signed body in cleartext.body.

  VTA (vta-service):
  - rooms/keys/profile/read/0.1: walks from the current epoch down (bound 32),
    fetching each location as the member under their own `read` grant,
    verifying the host's reply as rooms/keys/read does, and takes the newest
    profile it accepts (`found`, `stale` below the current epoch), stops at a
    retraction (`cleared`), or answers `absent`, with `searched`.
  - Readers decide who may name the room
    (operations::room_profile::check_statement): the SealedRecordBody rules
    (1)-(4) — no unknown member, the author's assertionMethod proof, signed for
    the location read, the host-recorded author on attributed — plus
    RoomProfileStatement items 1-4: a profile and nothing a record carries,
    sealed under the epoch that located it, issuedAt within
    [updatedAt − 1h, updatedAt + 5m], and an authority chain conferring
    `curate` or `admin` on the author at the room's scope, every link valid at
    issuedAt (vti_rooms_dtg::profile::verify_profile_authority). Anything that
    fails is ignored and reported in `rejected` with its reason and author; a
    rename by a member holding only `write` is `noAuthority` and the room keeps
    the profile before it. This VTA holds no RevocationList, so item 5 never
    applies (revocation is not retroactive).
  - rooms/keys/profile/write/0.1: refuses `noAuthority` before contacting the
    host without `write` and `curate`/`admin` (`curate` to clear); signs the
    statement as the principal (assertionMethod, through the gated oracle) with
    the room-issued chain inside, pads the signed body to a 1 KiB multiple,
    seals it under the current epoch and puts it as the member under a `write`
    grant; re-seals for the version the host assigned, then `contended`.
    `clear` retracts the current location with a `curate` grant, storing a
    profile there first when it holds none. Delegates are refused.
  - The epoch-advance re-write: rooms/owner/group/{add,remove,renew} read the
    profile before the advance and write it again under the new epoch as the
    owner once the host accepts — never failing, delaying or undoing the
    advance (tried a few times, then logged), never for `absent`/`cleared`,
    never retracting the earlier one (add 0.1 and 0.2, remove, renew; the
    speaker is HostCall::profile_speaker, so a later version reuses it).
  - rooms/keys/read does not open a profile location (answers
    ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].roomProfile) and rooms/keys/browse leaves profile
    records out, counting against everything the host listed.
  - Both tasks dispatched ([None Secret true] / [Mutating Metadata true]),
    classified RetrySafe in vta_sdk::retry_safety, counted in budget, guarded in
    vta-mcp, with conformance entries.

- **vtc**: Community-room details administrators can see, edit and track (trust-tasks-tf #805) ([#2170](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2170))

* build: raise the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.31.14 (trust-tasks-tf #805)

  0.31.14 carries vtc/rooms/community/update/0.1, the 0.2 community-room
  create/get/list and vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2.

- **rooms**: A member's own private name, description, notes and tags for each room they hold ([#2167](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2167))

* build(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.31.14 — rooms/keys/label/0.1 and rooms/keys/list/0.2

## `vta-sdk`

## [0.71.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.70.0...vta-sdk-v0.71.0) — 2026-10-18 ### Added - **rooms**: Every surface shows a member the same community rooms, and finishes an acceptance any other began ([#2186](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2186)) * feat(rooms): every surface shows a member the same community rooms, and finishes an acceptance any other began A member reaches their community from several surfaces — the member portal through their wallet, pnm, OpenVTC — and each kept no shared view: offers/list drops an accepted offer after seven days, so a room accepted in one surface was invisible to the others after that, and an acceptance one surface began could be finished by no other (its mint replaced the private half the kept Welcome is sealed to, and the community answered alreadyAccepted). VTC - vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1: the community's own record of the signer's admissions to the rooms it owns — offered, admitted, removed; never a withdrawn offer, never a credential — with repeatAcceptUntil while a sealed admission's Welcome is kept. Answers only an active member, for themself. VTA - rooms/keys/key-package/0.2: returns the outstanding KeyPackage for the same room, member and invitation (alreadyMinted: true, original expiresAt), and mints only otherwise; serialised so concurrent requests get the same one. VTA - rooms/keys/key-package/0.2: returns the outstanding KeyPackage for the same room, member and invitation (alreadyMinted: true, original expiresAt), and mints only otherwise; serialised so concurrent requests get the same one. RetrySafe, where 0.1 is Keyed. - rooms/keys/welcome/0.1: a Welcome under a spent invitation, for the member who joined with it, is alreadyJoined (welcome/0.1's rule) rather than "invitation already used" — so a surface finishing another's acceptance reads it as success. - rooms/keys/act/0.5: 0.4 ([#2183](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2183)), and vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1 — COMMUNITY_TYPES, 0.4's OFFER_TYPES_0_4 and memberships/list. 0.3 and 0.4 refuse memberships/list (their schemas' type pattern); an acceptance's KeyPackage may come from key-package 0.1 or 0.2. SDK / pnm - VtaClient::room_key_package_v0_2, room_act_community (act 0.5, then 0.4 and 0.3 for the offer types an older VTA completes), unsigned_community_request, is_community_type. - pnm rooms memberships: the community's record beside the VTA's custody, as every surface shows it. pnm rooms offers accept checks custody first, asks for the KeyPackage at 0.2 (0.1 against an older VTA), and reads alreadyJoined as joined. pnm's offer steps keep #2183's OfferStepError and offers/list 0.2 to 0.1 fallback, now through room_act_community. trust-tasks-rs floor 0.31.16. - **rooms**: Rooms/keys/act 0.4 — a member reads each offered room's description (vtc/rooms/offers/list 0.2) ([#2183](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2183)) Serve `rooms/keys/act/0.4` (trust-tasks-tf #810) beside 0.3, 0.2 and 0.1. - VTA: 0.4's offer row adds `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2` beside `0.1`, on the same terms — no presentation, `issuer` required and resolved without a room credential (recipient item 2b). `room_act::OFFER_TYPES` stays 0.3's closed table; `OFFER_TYPES_0_4` is 0.4's, and `ActVersion:: completes_offer` picks by the version asked, so a 0.3 request wrapping list 0.2 is still refused `typeNotActable` (0.3 recipient item 1). Dispatch, policy-gate subject (`/document/issuer`), conformance witness and `RetrySafe` classification as for 0.3. - SDK (breaking): `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_4`; `room_act` and `unsigned_room_request` take and return the 0.4 generated types. A room request is asked at 0.4 → 0.3 → 0.2 → 0.1, list/accept 0.1 at 0.4 → 0.3, and list 0.2 at 0.4 only (`UnsupportedTaskType` otherwise). `is_offer_type` includes list 0.2. - pnm: `rooms offers list` asks list 0.2 through act 0.4 and prints each room's description on an `about:` line, every control character replaced. It falls back to list 0.1 (act 0.3 when the VTA lacks 0.4) when either the member's VTA or the community answers `unsupportedType` / `unsupportedVersion` — each party's refusal is kept apart (`OfferStepError`). `accept` reads the offer the same way. - Member portal: the offers card shows the description the wallet carries (`PageOffer.description`), as text, bounded to the schema's 1000. - Docs: community-rooms (the description gap closes; what remains is an older VTA or VTC), the quickstart, data-rooms, the files design note. - trust-tasks-rs floor 0.31.15 (the act 0.4 and offers/list 0.2 generated types). - **rooms**: Rooms/owner/revoke and group/remove 0.2 — the owner's VTA withdraws a member at the host before it advances ([#2174](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2174)) The key-holder half of trust-tasks-tf #804. Only the room signs a revocation list, and the owner's VTA holds the room's key, so the VTA is where lists are made. - The list is kept with the room's key: `room_groups` (backed up, encrypted), `room-revocations/`, one per room whatever persona signs. Building and signing a room's next list is serialized per room (owner/revoke item 3), signed as the room through `RoomKeySigner` — the gated oracle that mints the room's credentials, `ProtocolDefined` — and kept and persisted before it is delivered anywhere (item 4). - `rooms/owner/revoke/0.1`: roomSubject, noSigningKey, noAuthority, noList before anything is signed (item 1); the tier from registration or `rooms/info` when a withdrawal names anyone (entryNotPermitted on private, tierUnknown otherwise; item 2); `revokedAt` stamped at signing; delivered to every host with `rooms/revocations/put` presenting the owner persona's `admin`, each outcome reported (`accepted` only when the host answered with this list's head; item 5). A success whatever the deliveries (item 6); a `stale` answer is surfaced as a security signal. Before signing it asks each host for its list and adopts a later one the room signed (verified under the room's own key and a method under the room's DID) — recovery for a key holder restored from an old backup. - `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.2`: signingKeyId required, `mirrors`, `until`; refuses a private room (privateRoom). The commit, link and the signed list are retained as the room's pending advance before anything is sent (item 5); the list goes to the host first and nothing advances until it is accepted (item 6: a refused list discards the whole removal, list included, rolling the held list back only while nothing was built on it); then the advance (a refused advance keeps the withdrawal); then the mirrors (`mirrorsPending`). A later request settles a pending removal by delivering its list again first (item 8). `hostUnreachable`/`hostRefused` carry `details.stage`. - `rooms/owner/register` records the room's tier and delivers the list it holds to the host before answering, so a room moving hosts arrives with its withdrawals. - SDK: `room_group_remove_v0_2`, `room_owner_revoke`; both `Keyed` in `retry_safety`, in the budget's host-reaching set and the MCP guard as Sensitive. `room_group_remove` stays 0.1. - pnm: `rooms owner group-remove --signing-key` asks 0.2 and falls back to 0.1 only on `privateRoom` — the one case the specification hands to 0.1; without `--signing-key` it is 0.1 and says the credentials stay valid. `rooms owner revoke --host … [--subject|--credential|--reset]` (no withdrawal re-delivers). - **rooms**: A room's own profile — rooms/keys/profile/{read,write}, sealed inside the room ([#2171](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2171)) Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#807 on the key holder's side. A room's name, description, tags and emoji (RoomProfile) now live inside the room: one record per epoch at profile_key(E) — HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch's storage key, info "openvtc/room/profile/v1" || roomId || u64be(E), 16 bytes, base64url — sealed like any record, so the host stores one more opaque record and cannot tell which one names the room. An open room's is the record at `room-profile`, its signed body in cleartext.body. VTA (vta-service): - rooms/keys/profile/read/0.1: walks from the current epoch down (bound 32), fetching each location as the member under their own `read` grant, verifying the host's reply as rooms/keys/read does, and takes the newest profile it accepts (`found`, `stale` below the current epoch), stops at a retraction (`cleared`), or answers `absent`, with `searched`. - Readers decide who may name the room (operations::room_profile::check_statement): the SealedRecordBody rules (1)-(4) — no unknown member, the author's assertionMethod proof, signed for the location read, the host-recorded author on attributed — plus RoomProfileStatement items 1-4: a profile and nothing a record carries, sealed under the epoch that located it, issuedAt within [updatedAt − 1h, updatedAt + 5m], and an authority chain conferring `curate` or `admin` on the author at the room's scope, every link valid at issuedAt (vti_rooms_dtg::profile::verify_profile_authority). Anything that fails is ignored and reported in `rejected` with its reason and author; a rename by a member holding only `write` is `noAuthority` and the room keeps the profile before it. This VTA holds no RevocationList, so item 5 never applies (revocation is not retroactive). - rooms/keys/profile/write/0.1: refuses `noAuthority` before contacting the host without `write` and `curate`/`admin` (`curate` to clear); signs the statement as the principal (assertionMethod, through the gated oracle) with the room-issued chain inside, pads the signed body to a 1 KiB multiple, seals it under the current epoch and puts it as the member under a `write` grant; re-seals for the version the host assigned, then `contended`. `clear` retracts the current location with a `curate` grant, storing a profile there first when it holds none. Delegates are refused. - The epoch-advance re-write: rooms/owner/group/{add,remove,renew} read the profile before the advance and write it again under the new epoch as the owner once the host accepts — never failing, delaying or undoing the advance (tried a few times, then logged), never for `absent`/`cleared`, never retracting the earlier one (add 0.1 and 0.2, remove, renew; the speaker is HostCall::profile_speaker, so a later version reuses it). - rooms/keys/read does not open a profile location (answers ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].roomProfile) and rooms/keys/browse leaves profile records out, counting against everything the host listed. - Both tasks dispatched ([None Secret true] / [Mutating Metadata true]), classified RetrySafe in vta_sdk::retry_safety, counted in budget, guarded in vta-mcp, with conformance entries. - **rooms**: A member's own private name, description, notes and tags for each room they hold ([#2167](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2167)) * build(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.31.14 — rooms/keys/label/0.1 and rooms/keys/list/0.2 ### Fixed - **rooms**: A curated sealed record opens again — keep the version its body was sealed at ([#2185](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2185)) * fix(rooms): a curated sealed record opens again — keep the version its body was sealed at Archiving, restoring or pinning a record on an `attributed` or `private` room left it unreadable to every member ("record did not open: it was sealed under a different key, epoch, or location"). `curate_record` keeps the body unless it retracts but moves the record to a new version, as rooms/records/curate/0.1 requires; the body is bound — by the AEAD (`sealed.rs`, `room|key|version|epoch`) and by its author's signed location (`SealedRecordBody`) — to the version it was sealed at, and nothing remembered that version. Every reader opened at the new one. No test curated a sealed record and read it back. Rooms `_shared/0.1` `SealedRecord` gains `version` (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf): Host (vti-rooms, both room-host and vtc-service): - `Record::sealed_version` keeps the version a kept body was sealed at, set at the first curation of a sealed body and never moved by a later one; a new body (`put_record`) or a retraction clears it. Stored rows without it load unchanged (`serde(default)`). - Served as `sealed.version` only where it differs from the record's own, so no record changes shape until a curation needs it; part of `sealed`, so the committed leaf covers it. Mirrors copy it (`Record::from_wire`). - `SealedContent::sealed_at` refuses a `sealed.version` above the record's. Agent (vta-service): - `room_groups::open_record_at` opens at a given version and, with `Search::Earlier`, searches earlier ones newest first — never later — and names the version that opened. For records curated by a host predating `sealed.version`: the AEAD makes a wrong guess fail rather than mislead. - rooms/keys/read and the profile reader open at `sealed.version` (searching where the host gave none) and check the profile's location there. rooms/keys/open searches from the version the caller passed. Both say where the body opened in `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].sealedAt` when it is not the version asked, because the caller verifies the author's signature there. CLI (vta-cli-common): `open_and_verify` opens at the sealed-at version and verifies where the VTA says it opened (refusing a later one). `pnm rooms file get` parses the host's reply with a generated type that gains `version` with the next trust-tasks-rs; until then the VTA's search covers it. - **rooms**: Say whose each rooms/keys/list entry is, and let a client name the member a custody task acts as ([#2161](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2161)) One VTA can hold two members of one room: an administrator whose VTA is also the community's holds the community's own place in a room the community owns and their own membership in it. rooms/keys/list then returned the room twice with nothing saying whose each entry was, and every custody task refused as ambiguous ("act from the context of the one you mean") — which a client whose session acts in both contexts cannot do. The wallet and the member portal hit both in a live test: the room listed twice, and sharing it with the portal refused as rooms/keys/act:principalAmbiguous. - rooms/keys/list: one entry per (room, member) as before, and ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].held, index for index with rooms: the member (persona DID), the trust context its key lives in, and the actions the room's grant to it confers. The specification's entry has no member of its own and forbids extra members, so it rides in ext. - read, browse, backfill, open, seal 0.1, file-key, commit and chain take ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].member, naming the persona to act as. It only narrows: a persona the caller may not act as answers as "no group state", the same as one nobody here holds. Naming none keeps the refusal for two (rooms/keys/read/0.1: "acts as the one its caller acts as, and refuses rather than choose"); rooms/keys/act keeps taking the member as issuer (act 0.3 recipient item 2). - pnm rooms keys list prints the member of each entry. - Member portal: Share rooms passes the signed-in member to the wallet (choose({ hostDid, member })), which only picks among the identities it holds for this community; each shared room says whom it is shared as; a wallet refusal for a room held as two identities is explained in plain words.
## `cnm-cli`
## [0.37.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/cnm-cli-v0.36.0...cnm-cli-v0.37.0) — 2026-10-18 ### Added - **vtc**: Vtc/rooms/community/members/remove 0.2 — a removed member is refused at the room's host at once ([#2175](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2175)) * feat(vtc): vtc/rooms/community/members/remove 0.2 — a removed member is refused at the room's host at once The community half of trust-tasks-tf #804. A member removed from a room the community owns kept every credential the room gave them, honoured at the host until `validUntil`; on an `open` room removal withdrew nothing at all. `vtc/rooms/community/members/remove/0.2` (0.1 still served, unchanged): - item 2, admitted member: `open` — the community's VTA withdraws them (`rooms/owner/revoke`, one `subject` withdrawal, delivered to this community as the room's host); `attributed` — `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.2`, withdrawing first and then advancing (a member with no leaf is withdrawn alone); `private` — `group/remove/0.1`, the group alone; - item 3: an open offer is withdrawn, and on `open` and `attributed` its credentials at the host too; - recorded only once the VTA answered and, on `open`/`attributed`, the host accepted the withdrawal; a refused delivery is `keyHolderRefused`, an unconfirmed one `keyHolderUnavailable`; - item 4: the answer carries `revocation` (the list's head) and `revokedAt` beside `member` and, on a sealed tier, `epoch`; the `ext` notice says what the tier's removal does. The removal is one function (`rooms::departures::remove_member`) used by the administrator's request and by the departure worker ([#2156](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2156)), so a member who leaves the community is withdrawn at the host of every room it owns too. Every departure removal now asks the VTA, so a pass stops at the first silent VTA. - **vtc**: Community rooms carry their own name — create 0.3 and update 0.2 write the label and description into the room ([#2179](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2179)) Implements the community side of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#807: vtc/rooms/community/create/0.3 and vtc/rooms/community/update/0.2, on top of the community-room details ([#805](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/805)). - create 0.3 (step 5, items 8-9): once the room is stored, the community's own VTA is asked (rooms/keys/profile/write, as the community, with this VTC as host) to write the label as the profile's `name` and the description as its `description` — never the tags. The answer's `roomProfile` is `written` only when the VTA answered written, otherwise `pending`; the room stands either way. - update 0.2 (items 10-12): a change of label or description writes the profile again, first reading the current one and carrying over the tags, emoji and ext a curator set in the room; a room made before create 0.3 (or one still pending) is written even when nothing changed, and that is not audited as a change; a tags-only change answers `unchanged`. The change to the owner's record never depends on the write. Update 0.1 still never reaches the VTA. - rooms::community_profile: the one retry owner for `pending` profiles — a record per room (`room-profile:`, beside the owner's record), written pending before the VTA is asked and written only after it answered, one attempt per due room per pass with a capped backoff and jitter (1 min to 6 h), always writing the room's label and description as they are at the attempt, so a later update supersedes a pending one. - get/list carry ext["org.openvtc"].roomProfile (written / pending with the retry state / none); the console shows it on a room's page and creates at 0.3 and updates at 0.2, toasting a `pending`; cnm rooms create/update use 0.3/0.2 (falling back to 0.2/0.1 against an older VTC) and get/list show the state. - The community's entry at its VTA needs `room-open` for the profile tasks: added to the capabilities the VTA-access fix commands name, and to the docs. The community's own authority already confers admin, write and curate (create item 6), so item 12's re-issue is never needed here. - Both new versions dispatched, with conformance entries, OpenAPI wrappers (openapi.json and wire.ts regenerated) and the console manifest. - **vtc**: Community-room details administrators can see, edit and track (trust-tasks-tf #805) ([#2170](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2170)) * build: raise the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.31.14 (trust-tasks-tf #805) 0.31.14 carries vtc/rooms/community/update/0.1, the 0.2 community-room create/get/list and vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2. - **vtc**: A VTA permission refusal shows the pnm commands that fix it ([#2160](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2160)) When the community's VTA refuses a community-room step for lack of permission, the console and `cnm rooms` show the `pnm acl` commands that fix the VTC's entry at its VTA, filled in with the VTC's DID and contexts. The entry must cover the context holding the VTC's own DID, not only the `[rooms.community]` context: the VTA acts as the community only for a DID in a context the entry covers, and a scope covers descendants, never a parent. An entry scoped to `vtc-test/rooms` with the DID in `vtc-test` is refused "... is not a persona you may act as". The fixes ride `vtc/rooms/community/list` (`ext["org.openvtc"].communityRooms.vtaAccess`), answered to holders of `vtc.rooms.manage`, not the refusal: a trust-task-error message may not carry consumer-internal state such as VTA contexts, and keyHolderRefused's details admit only the VTA's code and message. Each fix names the refusals it answers, so clients apply one rule set as data. The list also warns when the rooms context is outside the DID's context or `vta_context` is unknown. New optional config key `vta_context` (written by `vtc setup`) records the VTA context holding the VTC's DID; absent, the commands use a placeholder. Docs gain a troubleshooting section; quickstart §12 now passes `--contexts vtc`.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.32.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc/directory**: The member directory — fields, cards, entries, introductions, admin notes, export — and community groups ([#817](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/817))

Rebuilt on main after #815, #819, #820 and #821. Groups: dynamic-group opt-out, issuance through keys/sign-document, the vtc-group template shape, a 30-day credential default. card/update admits a key delegated under auth/oob/grant/0.2, except for widening to public or turning on external listing. Shared defs named FieldVisibility, CardBlobRef and GroupJoinRequest so they do not collide with the rooms family's Visibility and BlobRef or the existing JoinRequest in generated bindings.

- **auth/oob**: A sign-in grant may delegate signing of named task families to the starter key for the session ([#820](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/820))

prove/0.2, grant/0.2 and respond/0.2. Step 2 may offer a `signingScope`
  (task families as slug prefixes); the grant copies it, so the member's
  assertionMethod signature over the grant is the delegation: the starter
  key K_b may sign documents of those families as the member, for the
  session redeem creates, and no longer. The service checks the scope at
  respond against what step 2 offered.

  grant/0.2 states what a delegated key may never sign, whatever the
  scope: anything needing an assertionMethod proof or a gesture; anything
  that confers or withdraws authority (role, capability, ACL entry,
  membership, credential, key, delegation, session — asking for a
  credential the member's own agent accepts as an offer, or ending its
  renewal, is not that, so plain group join/leave is allowed); a consent or a
  publication beyond the service's members; or an identifier asserted in
  the member's name to another party. Authority is the member's standing
  read at execution time, on the session's own surface only.

  Motivated by the VTC member directory ([#817](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/817)): the member portal signs
  vtc/directory and vtc/groups documents with its sign-in key.

- **keys**: Sign-document — a Data Integrity proof from a held key, as the DID the document names ([#819](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/819))

A VTC issues DTG credentials as its community DID and as each group's
  DID, but the keys behind those DIDs are held by its VTA and never leave
  it. keys/sign cannot produce a Data Integrity proof at a custodian that
  frames its general oracle, and keys/derive-and-sign-document signs as a
  derived path, not as a DID with a key record.

  keys/sign-document/0.1 is a narrow sibling of sign-jws and sign-csr:

  - The producer names a key and sends a document without a proof; the
    custodian canonicalises it (RFC 8785), writes the proof configuration
    (cryptosuite, verificationMethod, created) and signs only the
    eddsa-jcs-2022 hash data. No caller-supplied signing input.
  - Issuer binding: the document's issuer (or issuer.id) and/or controller
    must name a DID the key is a verification method of, compared
    verbatim, and that DID's document must list the key under the
    requested proofPurpose (assertionMethod or authentication only). A
    document naming neither is refused, as is one already carrying a
    proof (never stripped, never extended into a set).
  - Ed25519 / eddsa-jcs-2022 only: the P-256 keys custodians hold are
    bound to foreign protocols that fix the curve, and none is an
    issuer's.
  - Gated on its own signDocument capability (sign-document in 0.1),
    registered in device/_shared; sign is neither required nor accepted.
  - An unknown key and one outside the producer's scope are the same
    keys:notFound.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart); no version bumps.

- **persona/contact**: Stars, petnames, lists and directory links kept only by the holder's agent; admin events 0.3 add directory and groups ([#815](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/815))

A member directory needs the four things a member keeps about others — a
  star, a private nickname, a personal list, a link to a directory entry — and
  none of them may live at the community: a VTC that stored them would hold the
  graph of who watches whom. They go in the member's own agent, beside the
  contact they are about.

  - persona/_shared/0.1/contact-annotations (new): Petname (<= 64, one line),
    ListId, ListIds, ListName, ListColour, ListOrder, DirectoryEntryId (opaque,
    pattern + maxLength only) and DirectoryRef {vtcDid, entryId}, ContactList.
  - persona/contact/put 1.1: starred, petname, lists, directoryRef (+ notes)
    as contact-level annotations, never part of a revision. A second,
    annotating form (contactId, no document) changes them without appending a
    revision; each given replaces, removeX removes, absent is unchanged. New
    codes notFound and listUnknown.
  - persona/contact/get 1.1: returns the contact's current annotations with any
    revision; `starred` always present.
  - persona/contact/list 1.1: annotations on every summary (not notes);
    filters starred, listId and directoryVtcDid; listUnknown.
  - persona/contact/lists/{list,show,put,delete} 1.0 (new): the holder's
    lists, context-scoped. Membership is set on the contact, so it has one
    writer; delete takes every contact off the list and deletes no contact.
  - Every one says the annotations never leave the holder's agent, and that
    being on a list, starred or given a petname must not be inferable by the
    person annotated or by any community — including through what the
    holder's client reads from a directory.
  - vtc/admin/events/{subscribe,event} 0.3 + _shared/0.3: topics `directory`
    (holders of vtc.directory.admin or vtc.directory.notes) and `groups`
    (holders of vtc.groups.manage, per qualified group). Hints only: no
    record, record id or DID in any member, ext included. Otherwise 0.2.

  1.0 and 0.2 are unchanged. Design: VTI docs/05-design-notes/vtc-member-directory.md
  §6, §7.3, §10.2, §11.3.



### Specifications

- **rooms/owner**: Register 0.2 reports the room's revocation list; group/remove 0.3 settles a refused redelivery ([#821](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/821))

Two gaps found implementing room revocation ([#804](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/804)) in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure.

  rooms/owner/register 0.2. rooms/owner/revoke requires a key holder to deliver
  the room's revocation list to a host before answering a registration, and
  register 0.1 declared no outcome for "registered, but the list did not reach
  the host". 0.2 answers success (the registration took effect) and adds a
  `revocation` response member: the list's head and `status` inForce / pending /
  refused (+ the host's `code`). hostUnreachable / hostRefused now report the
  registration only. The recipient SHOULD keep delivering a pending list on its
  own and MUST NOT repeat a refused one; a caller MUST treat anything but
  inForce as a room served without its withdrawals, MAY redeliver with
  rooms/owner/revoke (no withdraw), and MUST NOT re-register to repair it.
  Retention moves to durable for the outstanding delivery only. A 0.1 request in
  that state SHOULD still be refused with a message saying the room is
  registered — the least harmful answer 0.1 can give.

  rooms/owner/group/remove 0.3. 0.2 item 8 redelivers a pending removal's list
  and did not say what to do when the host refuses the repeat. Discarding it as
  item 6 does is unsafe here: the first delivery's outcome is unknown, so a
  `stale` (host accepted a later list) or `permissionDenied` refusal may come
  from a host enforcing this very list, and dropping the list would make the
  key holder's next list fail notAppendOnly or collide at a sequence the host
  holds. Item 8 now: listInvalid / entryNotPermitted / sequenceConflict discard
  the whole removal (list only while still held), as item 6; stale with a later
  held list delivers that list and confirms through it; anything else discards
  the advance and keeps the list. Whatever is discarded, the settling request
  is refused with the new code earlierRemovalRefused {member, code, listKept}
  (at another task, its own hostRefused), so a removal reported pending never
  vanishes inside a later success. Schemas unchanged.

- **rooms**: A curated record keeps the version its body was sealed at ([#816](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/816))

Curation MUST assign a record a new version (rooms/records/curate/0.1),
  and every curation but a retraction keeps the body. But a sealed body is
  bound — by the AEAD's associated data and by its author's signature
  (SealedRecordBody, rule 3) — to the version it was sealed at, and nothing
  in a stored or served record remembered that version. So archiving,
  restoring or pinning a record on an `attributed` or `private` room left it
  opening for nobody: every reader opened it at the new version. Two halves
  of the rooms family were contradicting each other.

  - SealedRecord gains an optional `version`: the version the ciphertext was
    sealed at, where that is no longer the record's own. A host records it
    when it stores a body, never changes it while the body is kept, and MUST
    serve it whenever it differs from the record's version — absent
    otherwise, so no record changes shape until a curation needs it. It is
    inside `sealed`, so the data commitment covers it.
  - Readers open and verify at it, and MUST refuse a `sealed.version`
    greater than the record's own (a body cannot be sealed for a version the
    room had not reached). SealedRecordBody's rule (3) now checks the body
    against the location it was sealed at.
  - A record curated by a host predating the member opens at neither version.
    A reader MAY try earlier versions, newest first, never above the record's
    own: the AEAD makes a wrong guess fail rather than mislead, and the
    author's signed location makes the one that opens the one the author
    wrote, so recovery does not trust the host for the answer.
  - rooms/records/curate/0.1 states the rule from its side: a curation MUST
    NOT alter a kept record's sealed content.

  Edited in place, as #807 added `roomProfile` to SealedRecordBody: the rooms
  family and its shared component are `draft`, and the addition is optional.
  Libraries regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart); one negative example added
  (sealed.version 0).

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.31.16` → `0.32.0` | breaking |

| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.31.16` → `0.32.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.31.16` → `0.32.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.31.16` → `0.32.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.31.16` → `0.32.0` | breaking |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.17` → `0.26.18` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.18`) | `0.8.17` → `0.8.18` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.17` → `0.8.18` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

body:
## Summary

- **New chapter `spec/12a-vtc-directory.md`, area `DIR`** (VTI-DIR-001 – 130): cards and field ceilings; audiences, with the subject's visibility, the community's ceiling and policy intersected; discoverability (listing, search, introductions, external), defaulting to `listed` with display name and role; random, community-scoped entry identifiers; introductions that never reveal whether the recipient exists or received them; administrators' notes kept off the card; community groups (static and dynamic, separate visibility of the group and its member list); **group identities** minted and held by the community's VTA, issuing group membership credentials under a community → group authorization credential, never consulted for authority at the VTC; room bindings; grant bindings provisioned into the ACL with the group as source, static-only, never setting the community or administrative role; anti-enumeration; departure and rotation; a disclosure statement generated from configuration. Members' annotations about each other stay in their own VTA (VTI-DIR-001).
- **`13-registries.md`**: lands the F.5 proposal. VTI-REG-001 is scoped to recognition; **VTI-REG-004** bounds publication for any other purpose (purpose stated, subject told before publication, nothing beyond the purpose, member-signed where the data is the member's own statement).
- **Appendix F**: the F.5 git-ns publication entry is re-filed against VTI-REG-004, which it still does not meet (items 2 and 3); F.8 gains a rule for re-filing an entry whose requirement changed.
- **Appendix C.3**: `vtc.directory.admin`, `vtc.directory.notes`, `vtc.groups.manage` (qualifiable `group:<id>`). `vtc.rooms.manage` was already registered (#63).
- **`12-vtc-lifecycle.md`**: a note under VTI-MEM-033 naming directory entries, group memberships and credentials, and administrators' notes.
- Registration: `specs.json`, `intro.md` (structure and reading tables), `STRUCTURE.md` (chapter map, status), `95-conformance.md` (`Community` profile, `DIR` area), and the VTC chapter's chapter list.

Design: [`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-member-directory.md`](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/blob/docs/vtc-member-directory-design/docs/05-design-notes/vtc-member-directory.md) on the VTI branch `docs/vtc-member-directory-design`.

## Checks

- `npm run render`: clean, no warnings.
- `npm run healthCheck`: the one failure (markdown-tables) and three warnings all predate this change and are in other files.
- Requirement identifiers: no duplicates, no citation of an undefined identifier.

title: feat(vtc/directory): the member directory — fields, cards, entries, introductions, admin notes, export — and community groups
body:
Specifies the VTC member directory and community groups. The design is in the VTI repository, branch `docs/vtc-member-directory-design`, at `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-member-directory.md`. Its §13 decisions are settled: personal annotations stay in the member's VTA, groups carry grant sets only, and new cards default to `listed`.

## Tasks (all draft 0.1)

**`vtc/directory/*`** (extends the family)
- `fields/{list,define,update,retire}`: the directory schema. Base fields plus reverse-DNS community fields, each with a ceiling and a default visibility. A community field is retired, never deleted, and its key is never reused. A widening is held as host behaviour and never changes a member's own choice.
- `card/{show,update,assert,present}`: the member's own card. `update` is signed and requires `issuedAt`; a stale document gets `superseded`. Admin-sourced values are written only by `assert`, and credential-sourced values only by `present`, which keeps the disclosed claim and never the presentation.
- `entries/{list,show}`: browse, search and filter, through the projection (member choice ∩ ceiling ∩ policy). Withheld fields are absent, and the same `notFound` covers "no such entry" and "nothing visible". Cursors are bound to the question, facet counts below *k* are suppressed, search is capped at 50 matches, and only admins can address an entry by DID.
- `introduce` / `introduction`: contact through a pairwise DID. The answer is always `accepted`.
- `notes/{list,append,export}`: append-only admin notes, never in a projection.
- `export`: JSContact, admin-only, paged.
- `query/0.1`: the wire is unchanged. It gains `related` and a short note naming `entries/show` as its successor.

Shared schemas in `vtc/directory/_shared/0.1/`: `directory-card` (EntryId, Audience, card, entry projection, JSContactCard), `field-definition`, `admin-note`.

**`vtc/groups/*`** (new): `list`, `show`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, `members/{list,add,remove}`, `join`, `leave`, `requests/{list,decide}`, `bindings/{list,add,remove}`, plus `vtc/groups/_shared/0.1/group.schema.json`.
- Each group gets its own DID, minted by the community's VTA from the `vtc-group` template on a remote-first path modelled on `vtc/rooms/community/create`. Errors: `noKeyHolder`, `keyHolderUnavailable`, `keyHolderRefused`.
- When `issuesCredentials` is set (default true), the community issues the group a VAC and the group DID issues each member a DTG `MembershipCredential` through the `credential-exchange/offer` path. These credentials are short-lived and renewed while the member stays. There is no per-group status list (VTI-CRD-014). Deleting a group revokes its VAC.
- Normative: the community never consults a group's credential or record for its own authorization. Authority is provisioned into the ACL with the group as its source.
- Room bindings and grants/role bindings follow design §9.3 and §9.4. A group that carries authority must be static and closed. Adding a member to it is held like a grant, and removing one is a reduction.

## Validation
`npm run validate` / `npm run build` (also under `TT_STRICT_SECURITY_PRIVACY=1 TT_STRICT_DISCLOSURE=1`), `npm run check-bindings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, TS `npm test` + `smoke` + `tsc`, `go build/vet/test`, `dart analyze --fatal-infos` + `dart test`, `test:infra`, `test-ceremonies`. All bindings are regenerated.

## Open points
- **Policy purposes.** `directoryWrite` and `groups` are named in prose only. This repo does not enumerate VTC policy purposes (`policy/*` and `vtc/policies/test` take a free string), so no enum changed.
- **The VTA-side task for issuing as the group DID** is not specified. Create and the member tasks say "has its VTA issue, as the group's DID".
- **`vtc-group` DID template** has to be added to VTI's built-ins.
- **Leaving a dynamic group** is refused (`dynamicGroup`). The design does not cover this case.
- **External cards** depend on the VTI-REG-001 change. Until then `card/update` refuses `external: true` with `notAvailable`.
- **`admin/events` 0.3 topics** (`directory`, `groups`) and the **`persona/contact` minor** (stars, petnames, lists, `directoryRef`) belong in follow-up PRs.
- **The admin-notes and export step-ups** are described as SHOULD host behaviour, not mandated.

title: feat(rooms): every surface shows a member the same community rooms, and finishes an acceptance any other began
body:
This is the VTI side of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#813, released in `trust-tasks-rs` 0.31.16.

It builds on #2183 (`rooms/keys/act/0.4`): its `OFFER_TYPES_0_4`, `OfferStepError` and offers/list 0.2-to-0.1 fallback, and the portal's offer description; it doesn't reimplement them.

## The problem

A member reaches the rooms a community owns from three surfaces: the member portal (through the browser wallet), `pnm`, and OpenVTC. Each surface saw only `vtc/rooms/offers/list`, so:

- a room accepted in one surface disappeared from the others once its offer aged out;
- an acceptance one surface began could not be finished by another. Every surface minted a new KeyPackage, and the VTA overwrote the pending one for (room, member), which destroyed the private half of the KeyPackage the community's kept Welcome was sealed to. The repeat was `alreadyAccepted`.

## Behaviour

- **VTC: `vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1`.** The community's record of the caller's rooms: `offered`, `admitted` or `removed`, with dates, label and description, and no credentials.
  - An offer withdrawn before it was accepted is not listed.
  - `repeatAcceptUntil` is set on a sealed room while the Welcome is kept: one week from the admission.
  - The authority is being the member the offers are addressed to, checked as for `offers/list`.
  - The refusal code for a caller who isn't a member is `MEMBERSHIPS_LIST_NOT_A_MEMBER`.
- **VTA: `rooms/keys/key-package/0.2`.**
  - Returns the outstanding KeyPackage for the same room, member and invitation (`alreadyMinted: true`, original `expiresAt`) instead of minting another. A different invitation still mints a new one.
  - A process-wide lock makes concurrent requests get the same KeyPackage.
  - A 0.2 KeyPackage is held for 14 days, so it outlives the Welcome the community keeps for a week from admission. 0.1 keeps its 7 days.
- **VTA: `rooms/keys/welcome`.** A repeated Welcome for an invitation already used, where the member holds the group, now answers `alreadyJoined` (per welcome/0.1) instead of "invitation already used".
- **VTA: `rooms/keys/act/0.5`.**
  - `COMMUNITY_TYPES` is 0.4's `OFFER_TYPES_0_4` plus `vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1`.
  - Each version is checked against its own schema, so 0.3 and 0.4 refuse memberships.
  - Policy gate, conformance and retry-safety entries are added.
- **SDK.**
  - New: `room_key_package_v0_2`, `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_KEY_PACKAGE_0_2` and `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_5`.
  - `room_act_community` asks at 0.5 and falls back to 0.4, then 0.3, for the offer types those versions complete. `room_act` (#2183) is unchanged.
  - `pnm`'s offer steps now go through it, keeping #2183's `OfferStepError`.
- **`pnm rooms memberships`.** Every room the community offered you and where each stands, read from the community's record and your VTA's `rooms/keys/list`:
  - offered;
  - joined;
  - unfinished (accepted, not joined, finishable before `repeatAcceptUntil`);
  - needs re-admission;
  - removed.
  - Accepting checks custody first and treats `alreadyJoined` as success.
- **Member portal.** "Rooms from this community" lists every room in those standings.
  - Accept or Finish for offered and unfinished rooms.
  - "Open it here…" for joined rooms.
  - Needs-re-admission rooms point to an administrator; removed rooms are listed with no action.
- Docs: `docs/03-vtc/community-rooms.md` and CLAUDE.md.

## Deployment

The browser wallet's matching change (pnm-browser-plugin `feat/rooms-cross-channel`) requires act 0.5 and key-package 0.2 with no fallback, so it should go out with this. OpenVTC's Rooms panel needs the `vta-sdk` released from this.

## Tests

- VTC integration: `every_surface_reads_one_record_of_a_members_rooms` (states, withdrawn offers, `repeatAcceptUntil`, not-a-member).
- VTA key-package and welcome:
  - `an_acceptance_begun_on_one_surface_is_finished_on_another`: same KeyPackage, same Welcome, `alreadyJoined`, expiry more than 13 days out.
  - `only_the_same_invitation_is_given_the_held_key_package`.
- VTA act:
  - 0.5 completes every community type as its `issuer`;
  - 0.3 and 0.4 don't complete memberships. #2183's own 0.4 tests cover offers/list 0.2.
- SDK, CLI and admin-ui tests for the standings and the portal card.

## Checks run locally

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`: clean.
- vta-service `room_*` tests: 208 passed. `conformance`: 9 passed.
- vtc-service `trust_tasks`: 249 passed. `community_rooms` integration: 30 passed.
- vta-sdk (all features): all passed, including every integration binary.
- vta-cli-common and pnm-cli: all passed.
- admin-ui: `tsc` clean; vitest 1211 passed.

* feat(rooms): every surface shows a member the same community rooms, and finishes an acceptance any other began

A member reaches their community from several surfaces — the member portal
through their wallet, pnm, OpenVTC — and each kept no shared view: offers/list
drops an accepted offer after seven days, so a room accepted in one surface
was invisible to the others after that, and an acceptance one surface began
could be finished by no other (its mint replaced the private half the kept
Welcome is sealed to, and the community answered alreadyAccepted).

VTC
- vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1: the community's own record of the signer's
  admissions to the rooms it owns — offered, admitted, removed; never a
  withdrawn offer, never a credential — with repeatAcceptUntil while a sealed
  admission's Welcome is kept. Answers only an active member, for themself.

VTA
- rooms/keys/key-package/0.2: returns the outstanding KeyPackage for the same
  room, member and invitation (alreadyMinted: true, original expiresAt), and
  mints only otherwise; serialised so concurrent requests get the same one.
  RetrySafe, where 0.1 is Keyed.
- rooms/keys/welcome/0.1: a Welcome under a spent invitation, for the member
  who joined with it, is alreadyJoined (welcome/0.1's rule) rather than
  "invitation already used" — so a surface finishing another's acceptance
  reads it as success.
- rooms/keys/act/0.5: 0.4 (#2183), and vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1 —
  COMMUNITY_TYPES, 0.4's OFFER_TYPES_0_4 and memberships/list. 0.3 and 0.4
  refuse memberships/list (their schemas' type pattern); an acceptance's
  KeyPackage may come from key-package 0.1 or 0.2.

SDK / pnm
- VtaClient::room_key_package_v0_2, room_act_community (act 0.5, then 0.4 and
  0.3 for the offer types an older VTA completes), unsigned_community_request,
  is_community_type.
- pnm rooms memberships: the community's record beside the VTA's custody, as
  every surface shows it. pnm rooms offers accept checks custody first, asks
  for the KeyPackage at 0.2 (0.1 against an older VTA), and reads
  alreadyJoined as joined.

pnm's offer steps keep #2183's OfferStepError and offers/list 0.2 to 0.1
fallback, now through room_act_community.

trust-tasks-rs floor 0.31.16.

Spec: trust-tasks-tf #813 (vtc/rooms/memberships/list 0.1,
rooms/keys/key-package 0.2, rooms/keys/act 0.5).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(rooms): hold a key-package 0.2 KeyPackage for 14 days, so it outlives the Welcome the community keeps for a week from the admission

The community keeps the Welcome seven days from the admission, which comes after
the mint; a KeyPackage held seven days from the mint expired first, and an
acceptance the community still offered to finish could not be. key-package 0.2
asks a key holder not to expire one sooner than the communities it serves keep
theirs. 0.1 keeps seven days.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-admin-ui): the member portal shows every room the community offered, where each stands, as the member's other surfaces do

The portal listed only open offers (and any accept begun in this browser's
wallet), so a room accepted in OpenVTC or pnm never appeared here, and one
begun elsewhere could not be finished here. The wallet now hands the page the
community's record (vtc/rooms/memberships/list) read beside the member's
agent's keys, with one standing per room — offered, joined, unfinished,
needsReadmission, removed — the same every surface shows.

- PageOffer carries that standing (and the admission dates) instead of
  open|accepted + inProgress, beside #2183's description.
- "Rooms from this community" lists offers and unfinished acceptances with
  Accept / Finish accepting, and joined, needing-re-admission and removed rooms

title: ci: run cargo doc one job at a time so it fits the runner's memory
body:
The `cargo doc` job documents `trust-tasks-rs` while rustc is still checking it. The two together use more memory than the runner has.

Peak resident memory, summed over every rustc and rustdoc process of `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features`, measured locally:

| Tree | Peak | Time |
|---|---|---|
| main | 16.1 GB | 130 s |
| main + #817 (vtc/directory, vtc/groups) | 19.7 GB | 142 s |
| main + #817, `-j 1` | 12.2 GB | 255 s |

`ubuntu-latest` has 16 GB, so main already sits at the limit. On #817 the job is killed with exit 143 and no error, once after 28 minutes and once after 4. Running `cargo check` first does not help, because `cargo doc` checks `trust-tasks-rs` again.

This PR sets `-j 1` on the doc job only. The cost is a slower doc job, and every other job is unchanged. Merging this first unblocks #817.

Queues **Increment 3 of #17**, explicitly stacked on #20 (which is stacked on #19). No main-branch merge is requested until the earlier increments have received maintainer review.

- Add `tools/validate_all.py`, a supported entry point composing the existing corpus and **explicitly selected** review validators. Preserve `--data`, `--risks`, `--strict` behavior and failure exit codes.

The review vocabularies (`control_plane`, `finding_status` and `resolution_type`) now live in `method/vocabularies.yaml`, with a definition for every value. `review/validate_spec_review.py` fails if the schema's enums drift from that file.

- **`review/validate_spec_review.py`:** a new `check_vocabulary()` compares each review enum in the schema against `vocabularies.yaml` and reports anything missing or extra. It runs on every review validation, so CI catches drift too.

title: Move the review vocabulary into `method/vocabularies.yaml`, with definitions
body:
At the 14 Oct TF meeting we agreed to move the review vocabulary into `method/vocabularies.yaml`. This issue records that decision and tracks the work. Background is in the discussion on #9 and #21.

## The problem

The specification review records under `review/` use three controlled lists:

- `control_plane`: where treatment of a finding belongs
- finding `status`: what has happened to the finding
- `resolution.type`: how a closed finding was closed

Right now these lists exist only as enums inside `review/spec-review.schema.json`. That causes three problems:

1. **They're not where the method lives.** `method/vocabularies.yaml` says it holds the method vocabularies, the part another working group keeps when it adopts RAHP. A WG using RAHP to review its own spec needs `control_plane` just as much as `severity`, but it isn't there.
2. **There are no definitions.** Every other vocabulary defines its values. These don't, so nothing tells a reviewer how `governance` differs from `operational-policy`, or what `none` means. `ADOPTION.md`, `docs/data-model.md` and `docs/pressure-testing-a-spec.md` explain the *ideas* well, but not the individual values.
3. **They'd be kept in two places.** #21 adds a hard-coded copy of the enums to `tools/validate_all.py` to catch drift. That's a sensible safety net, but it means maintaining two copies by hand, and it still doesn't add definitions.

## What we agreed

One home, with definitions, and the checks read from there.

## Plan

**PR 1 (Nicky):**
- Add `control_plane`, `finding_status` and `resolution_type` to `method/vocabularies.yaml`, using exactly the current values, so no existing review record breaks, plus a definition for each value.
- Add a check to `review/validate_spec_review.py` that the schema's enums match `vocabularies.yaml`, so the YAML is the single source and any drift fails the build.
- Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry, since vocabulary changes count as breaking.

**Then on #21 (@sankarshanmukhopadhyay):**
- Drop the hard-coded `REVIEW_ENUMS` and rely on the check above.
- Have `CORPUS_VOCABS` loop over whatever is in `vocabularies.yaml` instead of a fixed list, so new vocabularies get checked automatically.
- Rebase #22 on top.

## Follow-up: validator checks (not in PR 1)

PR 1 writes these rules into the definitions. Enforcing them in the validator will be a separate follow-up PR:

- **`risk_accepted` and risk-acceptance records.** A `risk_accepted` finding must reference an `RA-nnn` record whose decision is `accepted` or `accepted_with_conditions`. All of those are `pending` until Q3/Q4 are answered, so in practice nothing can be risk-accepted yet. I think that's correct.
- **Critical risks.** `vocabularies.yaml` says Critical "may not be risk-accepted", so a `risk_accepted` finding that cites a Critical risk should fail. The validator already looks risks up, so this is a small change.
- **`control_plane: none`.** It should only be allowed with a terminal status (`out_of_scope`, `superseded`) or a `no-action` resolution. At the moment an `open` finding with no plane passes validation.
- **`superseded` pairs with `superseded`.** A finding with status `superseded` must have resolution type `superseded`, pointing at the successor. This mirrors how `risk_accepted` already requires `risk-acceptance`.

## `control_plane` vs `control_type`

The corpus `control_type` (Technical / Governance / Procedural / UX / Legal) is a close cousin of `control_plane`. The definitions treat them as separate dimensions: `control_type` is *what kind* of control, and `control_plane` is *where* it lives. Aligning them would mean a breaking change to the corpus for little gain.

## Question for comment

- **Mixed casing.** The status values use underscores (`risk_accepted`), while the other two lists use hyphens. I'm leaving this alone, because renaming would break existing records, but I'm flagging it.

Comments welcome, especially on the definitions once the PR is up.

Related: #9, #17, #21, #22
