The member portal page that renders `description` is in the companion VTI PR. ## Tests - core: list 0.2 at act 0.4 with descriptions; VTA-lacks-0.4 → act 0.3 + list 0.1 (list 0.2 never reaches the community); community-lacks-0.2 (`unsupportedType` and namespaced `…:unsupportedVersion`) → act 0.4 + list 0.1; a non-unsupported refusal does not fall back; accept follows the read's act version in both fallback cases; the existing #346 attribution tests (act 0.4 and 0.3 both refused → `actUnsupported`; community refusing both list versions → `noRoomOffers`). - extension: views carry a trimmed, bounded description; the portal view carries it and no tags; the consent prompt carries it; render tests show the description as text with no `` element, in the lane card and in the consent window, and cut at 1000 characters. - Locally: `npm ci`, lint, build, test (all pass) and every bundle/package assertion in ci.yml. title: fix(rooms): refuse a host with no HTTPS endpoint before minting the room
body:
## Why

Creating a room on a host whose DID document advertises only TSP and DIDComm failed at registration:

> rooms/owner/register/0.1 failed: no transport in common with `…:airport-electric`: it advertises [tsp, didcomm] and this agent can initiate [rest] … only a Trust-Task HTTPS endpoint, where the document's proof is the authentication, can carry it

That failure came **after** the form had minted the room's identity, so the identity was left orphaned (`rooms:ephemeral`).

Two facts make such a host unreachable, and neither is something the wallet can work around:

- **The agent can start a conversation with a room host only over HTTPS** (`OUTBOUND_SUPPORTED` in vta-service's `room_host.rs`). The create form already says so under "The host needs a URL, today".
- **TSP and DIDComm couldn't carry this request even if the agent spoke them.** The registration is signed by the wallet's holder, but those transports identify the sender as the agent's own DID, so the host would refuse it as `identityMismatch`.

## What changes

- As soon as step 2 settles on a host, the create form resolves that host's Trust-Task HTTPS endpoint (`prepareRoomFiles`, the lookup the file transfers already use).
  - **A definite "publishes none"** closes step 3 and disables **Create room** before anything is minted. A note explains why, and what would work: a host minted here with a Host URL, or asking an outside host's operator to publish one.
  - **Any other resolution failure** is not a verdict about the host and does not close the step.
- **Matched by code, not message (R3.7).** The offscreen document reports `noTrustTaskService` (`isNoTrustTaskService`) on `OFFSCREEN_ROOM_HOST_ENDPOINT`. The background passes it through `RUNTIME_ROOM_FILES_PREPARE`, and `prepareRoomFiles` throws it as `RoomFilesError.code`.

## Tests

`rooms-create.render.test.mts` has two new cases:
- A host with no HTTPS endpoint closes the steps, disables Create room, and **mints nothing**.
- A host that couldn't be resolved just now leaves the step open and registers as before.

`npm test`, `npm run build` and the CI bundle-guard steps pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): reuses the existing endpoint resolution.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): this is the point. No room identity is minted for a host that cannot be told about it.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): no loops added.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound path untouched.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): internal bridge responses gain an optional `code`; every producer and consumer is updated here. Matched by code (R3.7).
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): only a definite answer closes the step; an unknown one leaves registration to report what it finds.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): the check is read-only.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: feat!: TEE first-boot enrols the claim DID as the bootstrap admin instead of minting a key (#2066)
body:
Closes #2066

Spec side: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#64 (whether a configured claim identifier counts as an offline enrolment) is followed separately.

## What changes

A TEE VTA's first-boot claim no longer mints an admin key inside the enclave and seals it back (VTI-CLT-001/002). On a verified claim the enclave **enrols the claim DID itself** and returns an attested acknowledgement that contains no key material. `pnm` then hands that entry over to a long-term `did:key` it mints locally, and destroys the claim key (VTI-CLT-034).

### Server: `POST /bootstrap/request`, wire version 2 (`vta_sdk::tee_bootstrap`)
- Under `MODE_B_LOCK`, the order is: claimant check (403), then the claim must name **this** VTA's DID (403), then the carve-out (410). The attest-first ordering, `insert_raw_if_absent` sentinel, `persist()` and integrity-manifest reseal all work as before.
- **What gets written:** an ACL entry for the claim DID. It is `Admin` and unrestricted, as the minted admin was. It expires after **24h** (VTI-CLT-014) and carries a **hand-off marker** (VTI-ACL-054). The marker's granter is the VTA DID, acting as the first-boot authority. Its bound is an unrestricted, permanent admin.
- **Response:** `FirstBootAck { version, vtaDid, adminDid, expiresAt, producerDid, attestation{format, quoteB64} }`. It is plain JSON with no sealed payload, so `SealedPayloadV1` is untouched. The quote's `user_data` is still `SHA256(client ‖ nonce ‖ producer)`, so PCR0/PCR8 pinning works unchanged.
- **Claim signature:** `vti/bootstrap-claim/v2\0 ‖ client_pub ‖ nonce ‖ utf8(vtaDid)`. A version-1 body gets a 400 with an upgrade hint. A version-1 signature relabelled as v2 does not verify.
- **`GET /bootstrap/request`** returns `{version, vtaDid}` for `--vta-url` clients. It is declared in `REST_EXCEPTIONS` next to the POST.
- **Rollover:** `acl/grant/0.1` with `ext["org.openvtc"].handoffRollover: true` exercises the caller's hand-off onto a successor the caller minted (VTI-CLT-017, VTI-ACL-055–057). It goes through the existing `exercise_handoff`. The flag is explicit, so an ordinary grant from a marked caller is never treated as a rollover (VTI-ACL-058).

### Why a hand-off rollover and not `acl/swap-key`
A rotation preserves expiry exactly (VTI-CLT-029; `acl/swap-key` step 6). Rotating off an expiring bootstrap entry would therefore leave the VTA's **only** administrator expiring with it, and on a TEE VTA nobody could lift that expiry. The hand-off marker is the spec's mechanism for this case (rationale to VTI-ACL-054–058). With a hand-off, the successor is bounded by the marker, so it is permanent.

### Client: `pnm bootstrap connect`
1. Signs the v2 claim.
2. Verifies the ack with `FirstBootAck::verify`: same claim DID, same signed VTA DID, and a genuine Nitro quote over its key and nonce. Then pins PCR0/8.
3. Registers the VTA, mints and persists the long-term key, then runs the rollover as the claim DID.
4. Confirms by authenticating as the new key.
5. Destroys the claim key.

A 403 is still the substitution signal (VTI-CLT-016).

**Resume:** re-running after an interrupted hand-over gets a 410. If the slug already registered that VTA DID (which only happens after a verified, pinned ack), `pnm` resumes the hand-over with the staged key. That also covers a commit whose response was lost.

**CLI:** `--expect-digest` and `--no-verify-digest` are removed from `connect`, since there is no bundle to take a digest of. `--expect-pcr0` is now required; `--no-verify-pcr0` is the opt-out, and it prints a warning.

### `--vta-url` and trusting a DID the server supplies
With `--vta-url`, `pnm` learns the DID to sign from `GET /bootstrap/request`. This is safe because a pinned enclave image refuses any claim that names a DID other than its own:
- A host that lies about the DID gets a claim no genuine enclave will accept.
- A host that rewrites `vtaDid` in the ack fails the comparison with what was signed.

What `--vta-url` still cannot pin is *which* VTA answered: an attacker could run the genuine image under its own DID, with the public claim DID configured. That is the identity pinning `--vta-did` provides and `--vta-url` was always documented to give up. The connect docs say this.

### Docs
- CLAUDE.md: *TEE Mode B bootstrap* rewritten. The `pnm bootstrap connect` digest-pinning exception is removed, because `connect` is no longer a sealed transfer and its anchor is the pinned image plus the DID binding.
- `docs/02-vta/tee-architecture.md` updated.
- `docs/05-design-notes/sealed-bootstrap.md` has a new *Mode B since #2066* section.
- Small updates to `deploy/nitro/README.md` and `docs/01-concepts/architecture.md`.

## Breaking
This is a clean cutover with no compatibility window.
- An older `pnm` against a new VTA gets a 400 with "Upgrade pnm". The carve-out is not spent.
- A new `pnm` against an older VTA fails on `GET`/`POST` with a version message.
- `vta_sdk::sealed_transfer::BootstrapRequest` loses `claim_signature`, `new_signed_claim`, `verify_claim_signature` and `claim_signing_input`. Use `vta_sdk::tee_bootstrap::FirstBootClaim` instead.

## Tests
New tests:
- **vta-service `routes::bootstrap`:**
  - the claim writes an expiring, hand-off-marked super-admin entry for the claim DID, and the ack contains no key material
  - the carve-out closes, and a second claim gets 410
  - a stranger gets 403 and nothing is written; with no claim DID configured, nobody is admitted
  - a missing sentinel still refuses a stranger
  - a claim signed for another VTA's DID is refused
  - a v1 body and a v1-tagged signature are both refused
  - tampered, forged, or unknown-member claims are refused
  - `GET` names the VTA
  - full rollover: the claim DID hands over to a permanent client-minted admin
- **vta-service `trust_tasks`:** `acl/grant` with the rollover ext, through the dispatcher and schema validation.
- **vta-sdk:**
  - claim round-trip
  - the signature binds key, nonce and VTA DID
  - a v1 signature is refused
  - `deny_unknown_fields`
  - the rollover grant body conforms to the published `acl/grant/0.1` schema
- **pnm:** anchor flag matrix, malformed pins rejected before any I/O, resume gating.

Run locally (macOS):
- `cargo test -p vta-service --no-default-features --features tee,rest,didcomm --lib routes::bootstrap`: 13 passed.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6204 passed, 2 timed out under machine load:
  - `vta-backup every_backed_up_keyspace_survives_a_round_trip`
  - `vta-service every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry`

  Both pass when re-run alone (about 33s each).
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`: passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- All the `features-vta-service-builds` check and clippy variants, plus `clippy --features tee,rest,didcomm --all-targets`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- **Not run:** the separate VTC test job (`nextest -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`). vtc-service compiles under workspace clippy, and its only use of the changed type is `BootstrapRequest::new`.

title: TEE Mode B: enrol the claim DID as the bootstrap admin instead of minting an admin key in the VTA
body:
Follow-up from #1987 (review: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1987#issuecomment-6146155409).

## Problem

Since #1987, a TEE VTA's first-boot claim (`POST /bootstrap/request`) is accepted only from the operator's pre-registered `tee.bootstrap_claim_did`, a `did:key` minted client-side with `pnm bootstrap claim-did create`. After the claim succeeds, though, `mint_mode_b` still **generates a new admin `did:key` inside the enclave** and HPKE-seals its private key back to the claimant (`SealedPayloadV1::AdminCredential`).

That is the remaining part of Mode B that contradicts the spec's client onboarding:

- **VTI-CLT-001 / VTI-CLT-002:** the client generates its own key pair, and the private key never leaves the client. A node must not hold a client's private key. The rationale given there is that a compromised node should be unable to impersonate its own clients.
- **VTI-CLT-010:** standing comes from an ACL entry, enrolled for an identifier the client minted.

The client now arrives with its own key, so the node no longer needs to mint one.

## Proposal

On a verified claim, under `MODE_B_LOCK` and with the same carve-out and integrity-manifest semantics:

1. Write an **expiring bootstrap ACL entry** for the claim DID itself (VTI-CLT-014), instead of minting an admin DID.
2. Return an attested acknowledgement that contains no private key material. The Nitro quote stays and binds the claimant's key, the nonce and the producer's key, so `--expect-pcr0` / `--expect-pcr8` pinning is unchanged.
3. `pnm` authenticates as the claim DID and **rotates** to a long-term identity through the normal onboarding rotation (VTI-CLT Step 3, `acl/swap-key`). The claim key is then destroyed (VTI-CLT-034), as it is today.

Open questions:

- The response wire shape. `SealedPayloadV1` variants are additive, but this response may not need a sealed payload at all. Decide whether the digest-pinning exception documented for `pnm bootstrap connect` in CLAUDE.md still applies.
- Interop with older `pnm` releases. This is a breaking change to `POST /bootstrap/request` either way.

## Also worth deciding

Today the claim signature covers `vti/bootstrap-claim/v1\0 ‖ client_pub ‖ nonce`. It does not bind the target VTA's DID or anything the enclave contributes. That is harmless at present, because the response is sealed to the claim key, so a replay can only use up the claim, which the host could do anyway. If the response changes as proposed above, decide whether the signature should also cover the VTA DID.

## References

- `vta-service/src/routes/bootstrap.rs` (`mint_mode_b`, `authorize_claimant`, `verify_claim_proof`)
- `pnm-cli/src/bootstrap.rs`, `pnm-cli/src/bootstrap_claim.rs`
- `docs/02-vta/tee-architecture.md`, `docs/05-design-notes/sealed-bootstrap.md`

title: feat!: TEE first-boot enrols the claim DID as the bootstrap admin instead of minting a key (#2066) (#2182)
body:
feat!: TEE first-boot enrols the claim DID as the bootstrap admin instead of minting a key (#2066) (#2182)

A TEE VTA's first-boot claim (`POST /bootstrap/request`) used to mint an
admin did:key inside the enclave and HPKE-seal its private key back to the
claimant (`SealedPayloadV1::AdminCredential`). That contradicts VTI-CLT-001 /
VTI-CLT-002: the client generates its own key and its private key never
leaves it. Since #1987 the claimant already arrives with a key of its own,
the pre-registered `tee.bootstrap_claim_did`, so the enclave now enrols that.

Server (wire version 2, `vta_sdk::tee_bootstrap`):

- On a verified claim, under `MODE_B_LOCK` and with the same carve-out
  ordering, durability and integrity-manifest reseal, the enclave writes an
  ACL entry for the claim DID itself (VTI-CLT-010): Admin, unrestricted (as
  the minted admin was), expiring after 24h (VTI-CLT-014), and marked as a
  hand-off (VTI-ACL-054) whose granter is the VTA DID as first-boot authority
  and whose bound is an unrestricted, permanent admin.
- The answer is an attested acknowledgement (`FirstBootAck`) with no key
  material: vtaDid, adminDid, expiresAt, producerDid and the Nitro quote. The
  quote's user_data is unchanged (SHA256(client || nonce || producer)), so
  --expect-pcr0 / --expect-pcr8 pinning works as before. Nothing is sealed,
  so no SealedPayloadV1 variant is added and none is reshaped.
- The claim signature now binds the target VTA DID under a new domain tag:
  `vti/bootstrap-claim/v2\0 || client_pub || nonce || utf8(vtaDid)`. The
  enclave refuses a claim naming any DID but its own (403, before the
  carve-out, after the claimant check). Together with the quote this means
  the acknowledgement for a nonce can only come from an enclave holding the
  DID the claimant signed.
- `GET /bootstrap/request` answers `{version, vtaDid}` for `--vta-url`
  clients (declared in REST_EXCEPTIONS beside the POST).
- `acl/grant/0.1` with `ext["org.openvtc"].handoffRollover: true` exercises
  the caller's hand-off marker onto a successor the caller minted
  (VTI-CLT-017, VTI-ACL-055 - 057), via the existing `exercise_handoff`.

Client (`pnm bootstrap connect`):

- Signs a v2 claim, verifies the acknowledgement against the claim
  (`FirstBootAck::verify`) and the pinned image, registers the VTA, mints the
  long-term did:key locally, persists it, exercises the hand-off as the claim
  DID, confirms by authenticating as the new key, then destroys the claim key
  (VTI-CLT-033 - 035). A 403 stays the substitution signal (VTI-CLT-016).
- Not `acl/swap-key`: a rotation preserves expiry exactly (VTI-CLT-029), so
  rotating off the expiring bootstrap entry would leave the VTA's only admin
  expiring with it, and nobody could lift it.
- An interrupted run is resumed by re-running `connect`: a 410 for a slug
  that already registered that VTA DID (only written after a verified, pinned
  acknowledgement) continues the hand-over with the staged key.
- `--expect-digest` / `--no-verify-digest` are removed from `connect` (there
  is no bundle to digest); `--expect-pcr0` is required, `--no-verify-pcr0` is
  the warned opt-out.

BREAKING CHANGE: clean cutover with no compatibility window. A VTA with this
change refuses version-1 claims from older pnm with 400 and an upgrade hint
("Upgrade pnm and re-run `pnm bootstrap connect`"); the carve-out is not
spent by the refusal. An older VTA does not serve version 2, so upgrade the
VTA and pnm together. `vta_sdk::sealed_transfer::BootstrapRequest` loses
`claim_signature`, `new_signed_claim`, `verify_claim_signature` and
`claim_signing_input`; use `vta_sdk::tee_bootstrap::FirstBootClaim`.
`pnm bootstrap connect` drops `--expect-digest` and `--no-verify-digest`.

The spec question of whether a configured claim identifier counts as an
offline enrolment is trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#64, followed separately.

title: feat(vtc)!: the last proof-required tasks are served only as signed documents (#1641)
body:
Closes #1641. The last seven VTC tasks that declared `proof` REQUIRED but were served on a bearer token are now signed documents only. Their bearer routes are deleted: 49 of 49 are closed.

## What moved (bearer routes deleted)

| Task | Removed route | Served by |
|---|---|---|
| `auth/passkey/list/0.1` | `GET /v1/admin/passkeys` | `trust_tasks::admin_passkey_tasks` |
| `auth/passkey/enroll/start/0.2` | `POST /v1/admin/passkeys/register/start` | 〃 |
| `auth/passkey/enroll/finish/0.2` | `POST /v1/admin/passkeys/register/finish` | 〃 |
| `auth/passkey/revoke/start/0.1` | `POST /v1/admin/passkeys/revoke/start` | 〃 |
| `auth/passkey/revoke/finish/0.1` | `POST /v1/admin/passkeys/revoke/finish` | 〃 |
| `vtc/auth/admin-session/0.1` | `POST /v1/auth/admin-session` | `trust_tasks::admin_session_tasks` (HTTPS only; sets cookies) |
| `auth/whoami/0.1` | `GET /v1/auth/whoami` | `trust_tasks::whoami_tasks` |

### Passkeys
- Authority comes from `admin_signer`, which admits exactly what the old routes' `AdminAuth` did. A console key acts for its administrator.
- Every passkey these tasks touch is the signer's own; nothing takes a subject from the payload.
- The in-request user-verification check against an existing passkey is unchanged. `enroll/finish` still requires it, although the 0.2 spec makes it optional for a first enrolment: this door never serves one, because `enroll/start` answers `reauthUnavailable`.
- The tasks now emit their declared error codes where the routes answered bare HTTP statuses.

### admin-session
- The access token is checked first (`invalidToken`).
- The document must then be signed by the token's subject, or by a console key with an active delegation from that subject. A token alone no longer opens a cookie session.

### whoami: a key bound at sign-in (decided 2026-10-17)
Every console sign-in binds a browser key to the session it mints. The binding uses the existing `Session::session_pubkey_b58btc` field; no new field was added.

- **Trigger-link wallet sign-in (`auth/oob/*`, admin audience):** `K_b` was already bound. The console now keeps `K_b` after the sign-in instead of dropping it.
- **Passkey login:** the console names a fresh key in `ext["org.openvtc"].sessionKey` on `login/finish`. A malformed key is refused before the ceremony is spent.
- **SIOPv2 wallet sign-in (`admin-session`):** the same `ext` member, inside the signed document, so the signer's proof covers it. A session already bound to a *different* key can be rebound only by the subject's own signature, never by a console key.
- **`auth/authenticate/0.2`:** unchanged; it already carries `sessionKey`.
- **Install claim:** mints no console session, so there is nothing to bind.

`whoami` answers for one of two signers:
1. The key bound to a **live** session: authenticated, inside its refresh expiry and absolute end, and not idle past `auth.admin_idle_timeout`.
2. A console key with an active delegation, when the signer has no ACL row of its own. The answer is the administrator's most recent live session.

Everything else is `permissionDenied`, and the subject must still be an administrator. The cookie confers nothing.

On the console side:
- The browser session key is a non-extractable WebCrypto Ed25519 pair in its own IndexedDB record, separate from the console signing key. It is minted fresh for each sign-in, kept once the sign-in binds it, and forgotten at sign-out.
- `whoami` now reports when the session ends, not when the access cookie expires. The console learns the cookie's expiry by renewing through `auth/refresh/0.1`.

### Behaviour change on the deprecated SIOPv2 path
A wallet that cannot `signTrustTask`, in a browser that holds no console key for that identity, can no longer finish this sign-in. The operator is told to use the trigger-link wallet sign-in or a passkey.

### Docs
- `vtc-trust-task-proof-enforcement.md`: status set to closed (49/49), the last batch recorded, §6c records the decision, and `vtc/backup/import/0.1` is noted as superseded by the chunked `backup/*` family.
- `vtc-console-signing.md` §8: marked decided (#1684).
- `03-vtc/website-and-admin.md`: updated.
- `openapi.json` and `wire.ts`: regenerated.

## Tests
- **New VTC tests:**
  - every moved task: signed success, unsigned refused, wrong or non-admin signer refused
  - a token signed by someone other than its subject
  - console-key delegation, and revocation of it
  - only the subject can rebind a session key
  - a malformed session key is refused
- **`whoami_signed.rs`:**
  - succeeds when signed by the bound key
  - unsigned is refused
  - a key answers only for its own session
  - a key bound to no session is refused
  - fails after sign-out, refresh expiry, absolute end, idle timeout, or ACL removal
  - the console-key path works, and stops after revocation
  - capabilities are reported
- **Sign-in binding:** passkey login binds its key (`admin_passkeys.rs`); trigger-link `K_b` is bound (`member_portal_oob.rs`); admin-session binds its key (`wallet_login_siop.rs`).
- **Extractor tests:** the cookie, audience, idle-timeout and CSRF suites used the bearer whoami as a generic token check. They now use a probe route over the same `AuthClaims` extractor (`common/session_probe.rs`).
- **Admin UI:** `admin-session.test.ts`, `my-passkeys-api.test.ts`, `whoami.test.ts`.
- **Runs:**
  - `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3270/3270 passed
  - `cargo test --doc`: ok
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
  - `cargo fmt --check`: clean
  - admin-ui `npm run lint`: clean; `npm test`: 1131/1131 passed

VTI-OPS-020, VTI-OPS-021, VTI-OPS-093.

title: vtc: tasks that declare proof REQUIRED are served on a bearer token, and the dispatcher does not enforce the requirement (VTI-OPS-020/021/024/093)
body:
Tracks the intended resolution of two divergences recorded in the VTI specification's divergence register (Appendix F.2) by trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#35. It follows from #1631, which bound `vtc/members/credentials/0.1` this way and noted that the other admin members routes do the same.

## 1. REST-only, bearer-token routes for tasks that require a proof

`vtc-service` binds 47 tasks whose front matter in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf declares `proofRequirement: REQUIRED`. It serves them only as REST routes: the body is a flat payload, the task URI is checked against the `Trust-Task` header (`routes/mod.rs` `tt()`/`ttl()`), and the caller is authenticated by `AdminAuth` / `SuperAdminAuth` / `ManageAuth` / `AuthClaims`. No document proof is verified. `issuedAt` does not exist, although the definitions declare it REQUIRED for 41 of the 47. Nothing enters the replay record.

**Community tasks (30)**
- Admin (18): `vtc/members/{credentials, update, admin-remove, purge}`, `vtc/join-requests/decide`, `vtc/admin/invites/{create, revoke}`, `vtc/community/profile/update`, `vtc/config/{export, import}`, `vtc/backup/{export, import}`, `vtc/registry/sync-jobs/{retry, discard}`, `vtc/endorsement-types/{register, delete}`, `vtc/website/{files/delete, rollback}`
- Member session (12): `vtc/members/{renew, rotate-challenge, rotate, self-remove, personhood/assert, personhood/revoke}`, `vtc/relationships/revoke`, `vtc/endorsements/{issue, revoke}`, `vtc/invitations/{issue, revoke}`, `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant`

**Canonical tasks shared with other node types (17):** `acl/{grant, change-role, revoke}`, `config/{patch, reload, restart}`, `policy/{upsert, activate}`, `audit/list`, `auth/{whoami, sessions/list, revoke-session}`, `auth/passkey/{list, enroll/start, enroll/finish, revoke/start, revoke/finish}`

**Plus:** `vtc/auth/admin-session/0.1` is unauthenticated. It takes an access token in the body and carries no proof.

The two REST routes that do verify a document proof are `auth/authenticate/0.1` and `vtc/relationships/publish/0.2`, and they are the model to follow.

## 2. The document dispatcher does not enforce `proofRequired` or `issuedAt`

`trust_tasks::dispatch_trust_task_core` verifies a proof whenever one is present. When it is absent, the dispatcher falls back to transport attribution, including for tasks that declare the proof REQUIRED: `join-requests/{submit, status, withdraw, supplement}`, `members/{self-remove, vmc, personhood/assert}` and `vetting/{revoke-statement, vetters/grant}`. `retention_policy()` is retention-only, and no acceptance window is applied to `issuedAt`. This is deliberate and documented in the code (`spine_proof_tests`), because joining over DIDComm/TSP carries no proof today.

## Intended resolution

1. Bind each task in list 1 in `DISPATCHED_URIS` / `dispatch_typed`. Accept a DI-signed Trust Task document over `POST /v1/trust-tasks` (and over messaging), with the proof verified against the issuer's authority and `issuedAt` checked against an acceptance window. Authorization is taken from the verified signer's ACL entry.
2. Keep the bearer-JWT REST route only as a **documented transitional path** with a stated removal point, and say so in the OpenAPI description of each route.
3. Make the dispatcher enforce `Payload::IS_PROOF_REQUIRED` and `IS_ISSUED_AT_REQUIRED` (SPEC §7.2 items 7 and 13, VTI-OPS-024). This needs a decision on the DIDComm/TSP join path: either the producers sign, or the task definitions change upstream. Changing a definition is a change proposal, not an entry in the divergence register. Without this step, step 1 moves the divergence instead of closing it.
4. Close the Appendix F entries when both are done.

Clients that call these routes today (at least the admin console, `cnm` and `vtc-client`) need the signed path before the bearer routes can be removed.

title: feat(vtc)!: the last proof-required tasks are served only as signed documents (#1641) (#2180)
body:
feat(vtc)!: the last proof-required tasks are served only as signed documents (#1641) (#2180)

* feat(vtc)!: an admin's own passkeys and the cookie bridge are served only as signed documents (#1641)

#1641's last batch. Six of the seven tasks still served on a bearer token
while their specifications declare `proof` REQUIRED (VTI-OPS-020) move to the
signed door, the admin console signs them, and their bearer routes are
deleted.

- `auth/passkey/list/0.1`, `auth/passkey/enroll/{start,finish}/0.2` and
  `auth/passkey/revoke/{start,finish}/0.1` (`trust_tasks::admin_passkey_tasks`;
  operations in `routes::admin::passkeys`). Authority is `admin_signer` (the
  routes took exactly `AdminAuth`); every passkey named is the signer's own,
  or its administrator's for a console key. The in-request UV against an
  existing passkey is unchanged and is required on `enroll/finish` even
  though 0.2 makes `uvCredential` optional for a first enrolment, which this
  door never serves (`enroll/start` answers `reauthUnavailable`). The declared
  codes (`credentialNotFound`, `enrollmentNotFound`, `attestationInvalid`,
  `revocationNotFound`, `userVerificationFailed`, `lastCredential`) are
  emitted. Removed: `GET /v1/admin/passkeys` and
  `POST /v1/admin/passkeys/{register,revoke}/{start,finish}`.
- `vtc/auth/admin-session/0.1` (`trust_tasks::admin_session_tasks`), HTTPS
  only, setting the cookies through the door's `HttpContext` as
  `auth/oob/redeem` does. The signer must be the access token's subject, or a
  console key with an active delegation from it — a token alone no longer
  becomes a cookie session. The console has the wallet sign it as the
  identity that signed in, falling back to its console key. Removed:
  `POST /v1/auth/admin-session`.

`auth/whoami/0.1` does not move: it is the console's probe of its own cookie
session and runs before a browser may hold a signing key, so a signed whoami
has no signer to attribute for that browser. Moving it needs a design
decision, recorded in vtc-trust-task-proof-enforcement.md §6c.

The console's My passkeys page and the SIOPv2 sign-in sign their calls
(`lib/my-passkeys-api.ts`, `lib/admin-session.ts`); openapi.json and wire.ts
regenerated. Design notes brought up to date: vtc-trust-task-proof-enforcement
(status, final batch, §6c, `vtc/backup/import/0.1` superseded by the chunked
`backup/*` family) and vtc-console-signing §8 (decided, #1684).

BREAKING CHANGE: the six bearer routes above are removed; a client must send
the tasks as signed Trust Task documents on `POST /v1/trust-tasks`. A SIOPv2
wallet that cannot sign Trust Tasks, in a browser with no console key for
that identity, can no longer finish the deprecated sign-in.

VTI-OPS-020, VTI-OPS-021, VTI-OPS-093.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc)!: auth/whoami is answered for a key bound at sign-in, never a cookie (#1641)

Decision on #1641 (2026-10-17): every console sign-in binds a browser key to
the session it mints, and `auth/whoami/0.1` is a signed document answered for
that key. The bearer route `GET /v1/auth/whoami` is deleted, which closes the
last of the 49 proof-REQUIRED tasks served on a bearer token.

Binding reuses `Session::session_pubkey_b58btc`, which
`auth/authenticate/0.2`'s `sessionKey` and `auth/oob/redeem`'s `K_b` already
fill:

- auth/oob (audience admin): already bound; the console now keeps `K_b`.
- passkey login: `ext["org.openvtc"].sessionKey` on `login/finish`, an
  Ed25519 did:key, refused before the ceremony is spent if malformed.
- vtc/auth/admin-session: the same member inside the signed document. A
  session already bound to a different key is rebound only on the subject's
  own signature, never a console key's.
- install claim: mints no console session, so there is nothing to bind.

`trust_tasks::whoami_tasks` answers for the key bound to a live session
(authenticated, inside its refresh expiry and absolute end, not idle past
`auth.admin_idle_timeout`), or for a console key with an active delegation,
for a signer with no ACL row of its own. Anything else, including a signed-out
or idled-out session, is permissionDenied, and the subject must still be an
administrator.

Console: a browser session key (non-extractable WebCrypto Ed25519, its own
IndexedDB record, separate from the console signing key) is minted for each
sign-in, kept once bound, used to sign whoami and forgotten at sign-out. The
access cookie's expiry is learned by renewing through auth/refresh/0.1.

Tests that used the bearer whoami as a generic token check now use a probe
route over the same AuthClaims extractor (tests/it/common/session_probe.rs).
openapi.json and wire.ts are regenerated. vtc-trust-task-proof-enforcement.md
§6c records the decision: 49 of 49 closed.

BREAKING CHANGE: `GET /v1/auth/whoami` is removed. Send `auth/whoami/0.1` as a
document signed by the session's bound key (or a console key).

VTI-OPS-020, VTI-OPS-021, VTI-OPS-093.

title: VTC: messaging/message/status reply lost on the 12-minute token-refresh reconnect, bounced as unsupportedType
body:
## What we see

A running VTC logs this pair every **12 minutes**, exactly (:05:20, :17:20, :29:20, :41:20, :53:20):

```
WARN vtc_service::messaging: enveloped Trust Task refused — trust-task-error returned task="https://trusttasks.org/spec/messaging/message/status/0.1#response" thid=… status=422 code=unsupportedType
WARN vtc_service::messaging: received unhandled problem-report — not replying (a reply would loop) from="did:webvh:…:mediator" code=e.p.delivery.refused comment=Message not accepted for delivery
```

It isn't a security problem and no delivery is lost, but it's a real defect and fills the logs with noise.

## Diagnosis so far (not yet confirmed)

1. `affinidi-messaging-delivery`'s `outbox_drain_loop` (every 10s, `vtc-service/src/messaging.rs`) calls `DidCommTransport::outbox_status` → `trust_tasks().message_status()`, which waits for the mediator's reply over the websocket (`send_message(…, wait_for_response = true)`).
2. affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.33.0 refreshes the access token and **reconnects the websocket at 80% of the token's TTL** (`websocket.rs`, `refresh_after_secs`). A 15-minute token gives the 12-minute cadence. The reconnect calls `fail_pending_requests()`, which drops the waiter.
3. The mediator's reply (threaded correctly, `thid` = envelope id, checked against mediator 0.37 `trust_tasks.rs`) then arrives with no waiter. It goes to the VTC's general inbound router, which has no handler for a `#response` and answers with a `422 trust-task-error`.
4. The mediator won't deliver that error (`e.p.delivery.refused`) and sends the VTC a problem-report. The VTC correctly doesn't reply, so it stops there.

The SDK treats the failed `message_status` as "receipts unavailable" and falls back to the outbox listing for that round, so the push itself still settles.

## Open questions

- **Why every cycle?** A ~300µs query on a 10s poll should rarely overlap the reconnect, yet it hit 5/5. Something makes them coincide. Candidates: the refresh's HTTP `refresh()` call is awaited inside the websocket task's `select!` while a query is queued, or the reply is held and flushed after the reconnect.
- **Why is the outbox ever non-empty?** `outbox_status` sends nothing for an empty hop-id list, so a query every cycle means the VTC holds an outbox entry that keeps being polled. Check the outbox keyspace for a member push that never settles.
- Do pushes in flight across a reconnect ever escalate to a second transport (a duplicate delivery to the member) because their receipt was lost?

## Likely fixes

- **SDK (affinidi-tdk-rs):** keep reply registrations alive across a self-initiated token-refresh reconnect, or re-issue the query instead of failing it, so the late reply reaches its waiter.
- **VTC (this repo):** the inbound Trust Task router should never answer an unsolicited `#response` with an error. Drop it with a debug log, the same rule as for problem-reports. Check whether vta-service's router has the same behaviour.
- Consider logging the proactive refresh/reconnect at INFO so this pattern can be read from the logs.

title: test(vta): every declared error code must be shown emitted, or baselined (#1600)
body:
Closes #1600.

#1600's gap was that the conformance ledgers check only the success path. The VTC half closed with #1636 and the follow-ups that emit the declared codes (#1644, #1649, #1668, #1887). The VTC baseline is down to 9 codes, each with a stated reason. This PR adds the VTA half.

**`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/error_code_census.rs`**
- Scope is `conformance::resolved_uris()` (dispatched ∩ published). Declared codes come from `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::error_codes_for`, and no code strings are written by hand.
- Witnesses are derived from the tree, not listed. A code counts as witnessed when test code in the crate asserts on it, either as the full wire string (the usual VTA form, `assert_eq!(code(&out), "keys/…:notFound")`) or as its generated constant path. "Test code" means `tests/`, `*_tests.rs`, or anything after `#[cfg(test)]`. The constant path has to match the task, version and identifier, so a same-named constant on another task doesn't count.
- Every other code goes in a typed baseline. That baseline only shrinks, under a ratcheting `UNWITNESSED_CEILING`.

Today 468 codes are declared in scope: 100 are witnessed and 368 are baselined. The baseline is large, but it's measured now, and from here a new dispatched task can't add codes that nothing tests.

Test: `cargo test -p vta-service --lib error_code_census`. Clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

title: Conformance ledger witnesses the success path only — declared error codes are never checked
body:
## The gap

The conformance ledgers (`vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/conformance.rs`, and the
VTA's equivalent from #857) witness the **success** path only. Of 71 witnesses
in the VTC table, **zero** carry an error code, and nothing anywhere else in
the workspace checks one either — a grep for `extended_code` or any `*_ERR_*`
constant across `vtc-service/tests` and `vta-sdk/tests` finds no census.

So a specification can declare extended error codes under SPEC §8.5, the
service can emit none of them, and every gate in the repo stays green.

This is precisely the defect class the file was written for, applied to the
other half of the wire. Its own module docs say:

> a VTC response could diverge arbitrarily from the schema its URI names and
> every gate in the repo stayed green

That is now true of the error response.

## It is not hypothetical — it shipped this week

`vtc/join-requests/withdraw/0.1` (#1591) declares two extended codes,
`withdraw:notFound` and `withdraw:alreadyDecided`. The handler returned
through the generic `app_error_to_reject`, which flattens `NotFound` and
`Gone` into a bare `taskFailed` carrying only English prose. **Neither
declared code was ever emitted**, and the ledger was green — the success
witness conformed, because the success path was fine.

It was caught only because I happened to add a dispatcher-level test asserting
the codes. Nothing required that test, and nothing would have noticed its
absence. The same shape recurred immediately afterwards on
`submit:requestAlreadyOpen` (#1592) and the three `supplement:*` codes
(#1593), each caught the same ad-hoc way.

Worth noting what this costs externally: telling `notFound` from
`alreadyDecided` without parsing prose is the entire reason a spec declares
two codes, and Keyring's KR-27 — auth refusal answered untyped — is a finding
of exactly this class that we received from outside rather than caught here.

## Why this is not a one-line census

The obvious fix is a derived census: for every witnessed task, assert the
service can emit each error code its specification declares. **The declared
codes do not reach the Rust bindings.** `errorCodes` lives in spec front
matter and in the upstream `registry.json`; `trust-tasks-rs` 0.21.6 emits no
`error_codes` constant, no `ErrorCode` type, and nothing in `schema_index`
exposes them. Our extended-code constants are hand-written string literals in
`vta-sdk` (`JOIN_REQUEST_WITHDRAW_ERR_NOT_FOUND = "vtc/join-requests/withdraw:notFound"`).

So there are two routes, and the cheap one is the wrong one:

1. **Hand-maintain the list in the ledger.** Cheap, and it reintroduces
   exactly the failure mode this file's design deliberately avoids — its URI
   census is "derived, not hand-maintained" for a reason, and the
   trust-tasks-tf CLAUDE.md documents four separate defects shipped by
   hand-maintained lists drifting from the tree.
2. **Have `trust-tasks-codegen` emit the declared codes**, then derive the
   census from them the way the URI census is derived. Upstream work in
   dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf first, then a census here. This also removes the
   hand-written literals in `vta-sdk`, which today can silently disagree with
   the spec that defines them — nothing checks that
   `"vtc/join-requests/withdraw:notFound"` is a code the specification
   actually declares.

Route 2 is the one worth doing. Route 1 is worth considering only as a stopgap
if route 2 is blocked, and should carry a comment saying so.

## Scope note, so this is not closed prematurely

Two further limits are **stated** in the file and are not part of this issue,
but are worth keeping visible in the same place:

- the VTC ledger covers `spec/vtc/*` only; the 36 shared
  `spec/{acl,audit,auth,config,policy}/*` URIs it also binds are uncovered,
  pending a decision on which daemon's response shape is canonical;
- a witness is a fixture the author writes. Only 7 of 17 `to_v` witnesses
  project through production code (e.g. `routes::join_requests::manifest::
  response_v0_1`); the rest are transcribed by hand, so they assert that a
  shape the author believes in conforms, not that the service emits it.

The second is the point the plan's execution step 5 was making: the ledger
measures fixtures, not the running service. Filing it here so it is not closed
along with KR-09.

title: feat(rooms): step-track communities, verified file previews, and queued background fetches
body: ## Why Follow-up to #348, from using it: - **The Communities lanes** drew offered / held / shared as three equal cards with arrows. That named each room three times, read as a pipeline, and titled the lane by the DID's host (`webvh.storm.ws`) rather than the site the member signs in to. "Its portal can see" was unclear. - **Room files** could only be downloaded; there was no way to look at a picture or a note first. - **Background fetches** contended with each other: room names waited for every profile read to finish, and the newest-record reads all started at once. ## What changes (two commits) **1. Communities as a step track** - A room is one row, named once, with a three-step track: `Offered → Joined → On its website`. - A filled dot means the step is done. - A blue ring means it waits on the member, with Accept… on the row. - Amber means stuck: accepted, but the keys haven't arrived. - A hollow dot means not yet, always said in words. - "Its portal can see" becomes **On its website**, with a hint saying what a share lets the site do. **Stop sharing** sits under it. - A lane is titled by the member-facing site (portal origin, else the offers endpoint), with the DID secondary. - The long held-as identities now live only in the room's detail. **2. Verified previews, and queued background fetches** Previews (`file-preview.ts`): - One verified fetch serves both preview and download. The bytes reach the console only after the offscreen document matched every one against the author's signed digest. - **What is drawn is chosen from the bytes, never from the record's claimed type.** This keeps the rule in `room-files.ts` that no member chooses how the console handles their file. - Raster images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) are drawn in an ``, with click-to-enlarge. - Plain UTF-8 text is shown as a text node. SVG is shown as its text, never drawn. - PDF and office documents are download only: a `blob:` URL here carries the extension's origin, so nothing is framed. - Pictures up to 2 MiB in the newest records preview without a click, but only where the host permission is already held. The permission is still only asked for in a click. Queued fetches (`limit.ts`): - Background record reads (2), profile reads (3) and thumbnails (1) each go through a small ordered queue, so the top of the list fills in first. Clicks bypass the queues. - Profiles land on their cards as each arrives. - A loading thumbnail holds its size, so rows don't jump. - A row or transfer that is left stops updating, and an abandoned transfer is aborted. - A file record shows its thumbnail and download without being expanded. ## Tests - **New:** `file-preview.test.mts`. - Signatures are recognised. - SVG, PDF and `.docx` are never drawn. - Text with control characters is refused. - Auto-fetch is bounded. - The queue keeps order, caps how many run at once, and survives a failed task. - **Updated:** `rooms-offers.render.test.mts` for the track. - The lane is titled by its site. - The room is named once. - "not yet" / "not shared" are said in words, and Stop sharing is offered. - `npm test`, `npm run build` and the CI bundle-guard steps pass locally. **Not** yet exercised in Chrome against a live agent. ## Pre-merge checklist - [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new network paths; previews reuse the existing verified file transfer. - [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): the queue holds a slot, not a lock, and a failed task releases it. - [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): nothing new is stored. - [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added; every fetch is a read. - [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): no loops added. - [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound path untouched. - [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire changes. - [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): unrecognised bytes are download only; no host permission means no automatic fetch. - [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): a preview appears only after verification, and says so. - [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): read-only paths; an aborted transfer leaves nothing behind. - [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: feat(rooms): step-track communities, verified file previews, and queued background fetches (#349)
body: feat(rooms): step-track communities, verified file previews, and queued background fetches (#349) * feat(rooms): draw each community's rooms as a three-step track The lanes drew offered / held / shared as three equal cards with arrows, naming the room three times and reading as a pipeline. They are three facts about one room, so a room is now one row, named once, with a track: Offered -> Joined -> On its website. A dot is filled when the fact holds, ringed when it waits on the member (an offer to accept) or is stuck (accepted, keys not arrived), hollow when it does not, always in words. "Its portal can see" becomes "On its website", with a hint saying what a share lets the site do. A lane is titled by the site the member signs in to rather than the DID's own host, which can be a DID-hosting service. The long held-as identities live in the room's detail. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * feat(rooms): preview room files from their verified bytes; queue background fetches Previews. A room file's picture or text can now be seen without saving it. One verified fetch serves both: the bytes reach the console only after the offscreen document matched every one against the author's signed digest, and what is drawn is chosen from those bytes (file-preview.ts), never from the record's claimed type — raster images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) in an , plain UTF-8 text as a text node. SVG is shown as text; PDF and office documents are download only, since a blob: URL here has the extension's origin and is not framed. A thumbnail opens full size; Escape closes it. Pictures up to 2 MiB in the newest records preview without a click, and only where the host is already allowed: the permission is still asked for in a click. Async. Nothing the pane fetches on its own blocks it or contends with what a person clicks: - background record reads, profile reads and thumbnails go through small ordered queues (limit.ts), so the top of the list fills in first; a click goes straight through. - room profiles land on their cards as each arrives, instead of all at once after the slowest host. - a thumbnail holds its size while loading, so rows do not jump; a row or transfer that is left stops updating, and an abandoned transfer is aborted. - a file record shows its thumbnail and download without being expanded. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(rooms): an automatic preview survives React's development double mount Under StrictMode (every development build) React mounts, unmounts and remounts each component. The unmount aborted the automatic thumbnail fetch, and the remount found it marked started and never ran it again, so a picture never previewed itself. The effect now undoes itself — aborting its own fetch and clearing the mark — so the remount starts it afresh; a fetch aborted that way is quiet rather than reported, and cannot overwrite the state of the one that replaced it. It is keyed on the claim's fields rather than the object, which the record row re-creates every render. rooms-file-preview.render.test.mts drives a preview through a fake transfer port under StrictMode, and fails on the previous code. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * chore(rooms): log room-file transfers at both ends A transfer that dropped left no trace: the offscreen document logged nothing, and the console's one message reads the same whether the port never reached the offscreen document or was closed part-way. The offscreen document now logs each transfer's start (verb and record id), its outcome, a failure with its message and code, and the console going away mid-transfer. The console logs a dropped port with how long it ran and how many messages it heard, and Chrome's reason where it gives one. No key, body or byte is logged. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * chore(rooms): say whether a finished transfer reached the console The offscreen document logged "got" before sending the file, and a send that failed was silent, so the log read as delivered when it may not have been. It now logs after the send, saying whether the console was there, and logs a failed send with its message. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(rooms): the service worker no longer closes every console file transfer Every console download failed 1-2 ms in with "the wallet's background document closed before the transfer finished", while the offscreen document logged the transfer started and carried on. chrome.runtime.connect from the console reaches every extension context, the service worker included, and the worker answered ROOM_FILES_PORT with port.disconnect() — on the reasoning that the console hears a disconnect only once every receiver has closed. It does not: a receiver's explicit disconnect() closes the whole channel. The console's end closed at once with no message heard; the offscreen document, never told, finished a transfer nobody was reading. (Logs from both ends: console "dropped after 2 ms, 0 messages heard"; offscreen "started", no stop.) The worker now ignores the port. A receiver that merely goes away only drops itself, so that is safe; what holding it costs is the case the old line guarded — an offscreen document dying mid-transfer would be unheard while the worker holds its end — so the console gives up after TRANSFER_STALL_MS (90 s) without a word, and closes the port. room-files.test.mts pins both: a silent transfer is given up, and background.ts may not single the port out again. CLAUDE.md records the rule. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore --------- Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.15
body:
### Added

- **vtc/community/theme**: Show and update — a community's own stylesheet for its console and member portal ([#811](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/811))

* feat(vtc/community/theme): show and update — a community's own stylesheet for its console and member portal

  A community could set an accent colour and a logo (vtc/community/branding),
  and nothing else about how its pages look. Administrators want to restyle
  their console and member portal at run time, without the operator-only
  admin_ui directory mode.

  vtc/community/theme/update/0.1 (new, draft):
  - An administrator replaces one stylesheet; the empty string removes it.
    Proof and issuedAt REQUIRED; audited by digest, never by text.
  - `dryRun: true` checks and answers with what would be stored, storing
    nothing, so a client can preview a theme exactly as stored.
  - The theme profile (P1-P8): design tokens on :root (light/dark), plus a
    small set of cosmetic properties on ordinary elements — colours,
    gradients, bounded borders/radius, font family/weight. No url()/@import/
    @font-face (a theme loads nothing), no !important, no escapes or `<`, and
    nothing that can move, size, hide, overlay or add content.
    `outsideProfile` names the line, column and profile item broken.
  - maxDocumentBytes 48 KiB both ways, for a 32 KiB stylesheet.

  vtc/community/theme/show/0.1 (new, draft):
  - Proof OPTIONAL and answerable to an unidentified caller: sign-in pages
    draw the theme before the visitor holds any identity.
  - Client requirements: re-check the profile before applying; render every
    surface where a person decides, approves, consents, signs or is warned
    in structural isolation from the theme; mark that a custom theme is on.

  Why no second-administrator consent: the profile and the isolation
  together mean a theme cannot change what another administrator is asked
  to approve, so it stays an ordinary configuration write.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).



### Specifications

- **rooms/keys**: Act 0.4 — a member lists their offers at vtc/rooms/offers/list 0.2, and sees what each room is for ([#810](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/810))

rooms/keys/act/0.3's closed table admits vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1 but not
  vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2 ([#805](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/805)), which shows each offered room's current
  label and description (never its tags). A key holder conforming to act 0.3
  refuses a 0.2 listing with typeNotActable, so a surface that reads offers
  through act — pnm, the browser wallet — cannot use 0.2, and a member never
  sees a room's description before accepting.

  act 0.4:
  - The table's offers/list row lists vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1 and
    vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2 on the same terms: no presentation inserted,
    issuer REQUIRED and the DID the offer is addressed to (Producer item 2),
    resolved without a room credential (Recipient item 2b, which now names
    list/0.2 too).
  - New "What changed from 0.3" note; a request example completing a
    list/0.2 as the member.
  - Schemas otherwise identical to 0.3 (the type pattern already admits
    vtc/rooms/offers/); no error code added. vtc/rooms/offers/accept has only
    0.1, so nothing changes for it.

  vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2, in place: its "Signing as the member" paragraph
  pointed at act "0.3 or later", which does not list it; it now points at
  act 0.4. Prose only; its wire is unchanged (SPEC §5.2 editorial, as #797).

title: chore: release 11 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.31.14` → `0.31.15` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.31.14` → `0.31.15` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.31.14` → `0.31.15` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.31.14` → `0.31.15` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.31.14` → `0.31.15` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.31.14` → `0.31.15` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.31.14` → `0.31.15` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.31.14` → `0.31.15` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.15` → `0.26.16` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.16`) | `0.8.15` → `0.8.16` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.15` → `0.8.16` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: First administrator of a TEE node: is a configured claim identifier an offline enrolment, or a VTI-ACL-001 divergence?
body:
## Context

A node running in a TEE (an AWS Nitro Enclave VTA) cannot have its first administrator written to storage by an operator. The host owns the storage but must not be trusted, and the enclave has no operator console. The VTA reference implementation therefore uses an attested *first-boot claim*: a one-time request after which the node creates its first administrator entry.

Until recently, any caller who reached a fresh node first could make that claim. Standing came from deployment state alone ("the carve-out is still open"), which conflicts with **VTI-ACL-001** ("Configuration, deployment state, network position … MUST NOT confer authority") and **VTI-CLT-010**. That divergence was never recorded in Appendix F.

OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1987 narrowed it:

- Before the node exists, the operator mints a `did:key` client-side, as in VTI-CLT-001, VTI-CLT-003 and VTI-CLT-006.
- The public identifier reaches the node in its **configuration**, either baked into the measured image or delivered at runtime in an allowlisted overlay that the host supplies and the node attests.
- The node accepts the claim only from a request signed by that identifier.
- The claim key is destroyed after use, per VTI-CLT-034.

## Question

The right to make the one-time claim now comes from a configured identifier, not from an access control entry. Which reading is correct?

1. **Offline enrolment.** Delivering the identifier is the operator enrolling the first administrator before the node runs. That is the same act §3a *Offline writers* already exempts, carried through configuration because a TEE node's storage cannot be written by a trusted party. If so, the spec should say so explicitly. The exemption could be bounded: one-time; identifier fixed before the node first runs; included in the node's attested configuration; recorded under VTI-AUD-001 when used; and conferring nothing after the first entry exists.
2. **A divergence from VTI-ACL-001.** If so, it belongs in Appendix F with a resolution.

## A related point for VTI-CLT-015 and VTI-CLT-016

When the host delivers the identifier at runtime, the host is the enrolment channel, and the substitution threat described in the VTI-CLT-015 rationale applies. The implementation's mitigations:

- The identifier is part of the attested configuration, so it can be verified there.
- A refused claim by the legitimate holder is reported to the operator as possible substitution (VTI-CLT-016), not as a transport failure.

Should the spec require the configured identifier to be covered by the node's configuration attestation wherever a host-controlled channel delivers it?

## Separately

The implementation still mints the first administrator's key **inside the node** and sends its private half back to the claimant, which conflicts with VTI-CLT-002. That is being addressed in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2066 and may also warrant an Appendix F entry until it is fixed.

title: Add the Trust Registry to the explore stream, and move binaries to nightly
body:
## Summary

The explore stream stood up VTA, Mediator, DID Host and VTC but not the Trust Registry, so a VTC had nothing to sync membership to. This adds it as a fifth service, provisioned from the VTA with `pnm` and configured through a `.env` file, following the upstream [Trust Registry + VTA setup guide](https://github.com/affinidi/affinidi-trust-registry-rs/blob/main/VTA_SETUP.md). The registry and the VTC each need the other's DID, so the registry is provisioned before the VTC wizard runs and started only after the VTC DID exists.

## Changes

- **Walkthrough, new Step 5.** Provisions the registry context and `did:webvh` with `pnm contexts provision`, opens the sealed bundle with `pnm bootstrap open --out`, and writes the `.env`. The registry is not started here.
- **Walkthrough, Step 6 (was Step 5).** The VTC wizard takes the registry DID; the step saves the VTC DID (6a) and VTC Admin DID (6b), puts the VTC DID into the registry's `ADMIN_DIDS`, starts the registry, then adds a `[registry]` section to the VTC's `config.toml` before starting the VTC. The wizard prompt only publishes a DID-document referral; without that section the VTC reports the registry as `degraded` with the syncer off.
- **Known Issues.** New entries for an expired VTC install URL (`vtc admin invite`), a duplicate registry context (`pnm contexts reprovision`), a registry binary built without the `vta` feature (the `PROFILE_CONFIG` error), and a bundle opened without `--out`.
- **Version table.** Adds a Trust Registry column and refreshes every version from the nightly and main branches.
- **Server setup.** Adds the registry to the service table and both download lists, plus an Option B build with the feature set the walkthrough needs and a check that the installed binary carries the `vta` feature. The unverified download list moves from `main` to `nightly` builds, and the Option B checkouts point at `nightly` where the repo has one. The mediator now lives in `affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator`; the clone and crate paths follow, pinned to its first release.
- **Indexes.** The root README diagram and component table, the sysop and explore READMEs, and the community-manager link to the renumbered VTC step.

## Notes for review

- No DNS record or Nginx vhost is added for the registry. Its REST API binds to loopback for health checks; clients reach it through its DID and the mediator. The page says how to expose it with `TR_PUBLIC_URL` if wanted.
- The registry step has had one pass on an explore box, which is where the `[registry]` section, the `vta` feature check, and the install URL re-mint came from. The walkthrough still carries a "not yet verified" callout under the version table; remove it once a clean end-to-end run has happened.
- `markdownlint-cli2` passes on all pages.

title: Should a VTC's identifier be required to be "public", or may a restricted community be "directed"?
body:
The spec says, in three places that a VTC's identifier can only truthfully be declared `public` ("a community that cannot be found cannot be joined"). This is likely too strong due to the following reasons:

1. __Restricted communities are contemplated.__ The VTC definition says a VTC may be "a family … a company … a nation state." A family community's identifier is likely not something public so that anyone can find it.
2. __Joining is by invitation, not only discovery.__ A prospect joins via a VIC (verifiable invitation credential), which contains the community's identifier. The prospect does not "find" the community — they are invited. So "cannot be found, cannot be joined" does not justify `public`.
3. __"Findable" and "public" are being conflated.__ Resolvability (can the DID document be fetched?) and correlation scope (how widely is the identifier intended to be correlated?) are different properties. A community's identifier must be resolvable by whoever verifies its members' credentials — at minimum, its members — which is `directed`, not `public`


Proposed: a VTC's identifier is `directed` at minimum (its members must be able to find it) and `public` if the community is open to outsiders; never `pairwise` (a community has more than one member). This matches the witness case, which is already "directed at minimum."

Decision: is `public` a hard requirement (every VTC discoverable by anyone, for third-party verification) or a choice (a restricted community may be `directed`)? If a choice, the three places in the spec - (`verifiable_trust_community.md`, `body.md` VMC section ~383, and the Correlation Scope section) - have to be updated; if a requirement, the "family to nation state" range needs reconciling.
author: martipos

title: feat(vtc): community rooms carry their own name — create 0.3 and update 0.2 write the label and description into the room
body:
This is the community side of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#807. It adds `vtc/rooms/community/create/0.3` and `vtc/rooms/community/update/0.2`, and builds on #2170 (community-room details).

The VTA tasks it calls, `rooms/keys/profile/{read,write}/0.1`, are in #2171. This PR does not depend on #2171 to build or test: the VTC reaches its VTA only over the link and is tested against a stand-in VTA. In a deployment, the community's VTA must have #2171, otherwise every write stays `pending`.

## Behaviour
- **create 0.3** (step 5, items 8–9)
  - Once the room is stored, the community's own VTA is asked, as the community and with this VTC as host, to write the room's profile into the room. The label becomes `name` and the description becomes `description`.
  - The tags are never sent.
  - The response's `roomProfile` is `written` only if the VTA answered `written`; otherwise it is `pending`. The room is created either way.
- **update 0.2** (items 10–12)
  - Writes the profile again when the label or description changes.
  - First reads the current profile and keeps the tags, emoji and `ext` a curator set in the room.
  - A room created before 0.3, or one whose write is still pending, gets its profile written even when the update changes nothing. That write is not audited as a change.
  - A change to tags alone answers `unchanged`.
  - The update to the owner's record never depends on the profile write succeeding. Update 0.1 is unchanged and never reaches the VTA.
- **Retry owner**: `rooms::community_profile` is the only thing that retries a `pending` profile.
  - It keeps one record per room in `community_rooms`.
  - The record is written `pending` before the VTA is asked and `written` only after it answers.
  - One attempt per due room per pass, with a capped exponential backoff plus jitter (1 minute up to 6 hours).
  - Each attempt writes the room's label and description as they are at that moment, so a later update replaces a pending one. A lapsed room keeps refusing until it is renewed.
- **Showing the state**: get and list carry `ext["org.openvtc"].roomProfile` (`written` / `pending` with the retry state / `none`).
  - The console shows it on a room's page and toasts when a create or update comes back `pending`. It now creates at 0.3 and updates at 0.2.
  - `cnm rooms create` and `update` use 0.3 and 0.2, falling back to 0.2 / 0.1 against an older VTC; `get` and `list` show the state.
- **VTA permission**: the community's entry at its VTA now needs `room-open`. It is added to the VTA-access fix commands and the docs.
  - The community's own authority already confers `admin`, `write` and `curate` (create item 6), so the item 12 re-issue is never needed here.
- **Registration**: both new versions are dispatched, with conformance entries, OpenAPI wrappers (openapi.json and wire.ts regenerated from a default-feature build) and the console manifest updated.

## Tests
- create 0.3 writes the label and description and never the tags, after the room is stored, and none of it reaches the host record.
- A refused write answers `pending`. The sweeper waits out the backoff, then writes it, and never re-writes a room already written.
- update 0.2:
  - a rename re-writes the profile and keeps the curator's tags and emoji;
  - a tags-only or no-op update answers `unchanged`;
  - a refusal stays `pending` until the next update replaces it;
  - the first 0.2 update of a pre-0.3 room writes the profile without auditing a change;
  - update 0.1 never reaches the VTA.
- Console and cnm tests for the profile-state display.

## Checks run locally
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- nextest, vtc-service + vtc-client: 3253 passed.
- `--features vetting-pcs` openapi + community_rooms tests: 40 passed.
- workspace nextest: 6173 passed.
- doctests.
- admin-ui `npm run lint` and vitest: 1128 passed.
- After rebasing onto main (with #2170 merged), I re-ran the openapi, community_rooms, manifest and conformance tests (73 passed) and the admin-ui lint and tests.

title: feat(rooms): a room's own profile — rooms/keys/profile/{read,write}, sealed inside the room
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#807 on the key holder's side: a room's own **profile** (name, description, tags, emoji), sealed inside the room, readable only by members.

Rebased onto main. Main already has trust-tasks-rs 0.31.14 and the regenerated OpenAPI document from #2170, so the separate floor-bump commit was dropped. The branch also builds on #2167 (personal labels): in `pnm rooms keys list --host-did`, your own label shows first, then the name the room gives itself, then the DID.

## VTA
- **`rooms/keys/profile/read/0.1`**
  - Computes `profile_key(E)` (HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch's storage key, exactly as the spec defines it; `room-profile` on an open room).
  - Walks down from the current epoch (bound 32), fetching each location as the member under their own `read` grant, and verifies the host's reply as `rooms/keys/read` does.
  - Returns the newest accepted profile (`found` / `stale`), stops at a retraction (`cleared`), or answers `absent`, with `searched`. Every ignored record goes in `rejected` with its reason and author.
- **Readers decide who may name the room** (`operations::room_profile::check_statement`):
  - The SealedRecordBody rules 1–4.
  - The statement is a profile and carries nothing else a record carries.
  - It is sealed under the epoch that located it.
  - `issuedAt` falls within [updatedAt − 1h, updatedAt + 5m].
  - Its chain confers `curate` or `admin` on the author, valid at `issuedAt` (`vti_rooms_dtg::profile`).
  - This VTA holds no RevocationList, so item 5 does not apply.
- **`rooms/keys/profile/write/0.1`**
  - Refuses `noAuthority` before reaching the host: setting needs `write` plus `curate` or `admin`; clearing needs `curate`.
  - Signs the statement as the principal (assertionMethod) with the room-issued chain inside, pads it to 1 KiB, and seals it under the current epoch.
  - Puts it under a `write` grant, re-sealing on a version race and answering `contended` if that keeps failing.
  - `clear` retracts the record under a `curate` grant. Delegates are refused.
- **Epoch-advance re-write**: `group/add` (0.1 and 0.2), `remove` and `renew` read the profile before the advance and re-write it as the owner after the host accepts.
  - It never fails, delays or undoes the advance.
  - Nothing is written for `absent` or `cleared`.
  - The profile is fetched through `HostCall::profile_speaker`, so remove 0.2 (#804) needs only one call to pick this up.
- **Records listing**: `rooms/keys/read` does not open a profile location (it answers `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].roomProfile`), and `browse` leaves profiles out. Browse's count is still checked against everything the host listed.
- **Registration**: both tasks are dispatched, classified RetrySafe in `retry_safety`, counted in the budget, guarded in vta-mcp, and have conformance entries.

## Clients
- `VtaClient::room_profile_{read,write,clear}`.
- `pnm rooms profile {show,set,clear}`:
  - `set` carries over what you don't give; `--no-*` drops a field.
  - Text is printed inert, and a rejected rename is said in words.
- `pnm rooms keys list --host-did` shows each room's own name.

## Tests
- Every statement check, including **the forged rename by a write-only member**: refused by their own VTA, and when stored around that refusal, ignored by every reader as `noAuthority`, with them named.
- The chain check: write alone, another member's chain, a self-issued chain, and validity judged at `issuedAt`.
- The derivation, pinned against the spec's formula.
- End to end against a real `room-host`: write and read on a sealed room, `absent`, the re-write at add and renew (a member who joined later reads it at their own epoch), clear stopping the walk and being reversible, `curate` needed to clear, `notAMember`, browse/read keeping the profile out, and an open room.

## Checks run locally
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo deny check`.
- After the rebase: nextest workspace (excluding vtc), 6228 passed; vtc-service + vtc-client, 3250 passed; doctests, fmt and clippy clean. Before the rebase, two tests timed out under load and passed when re-run alone.
- Doctests, `vtc-service` + `vtc-client` nextest (3245 passed), the openapi tests with and without `vetting-pcs`, and admin-ui `npm run lint`.

## Follow-ups
- The VTC's create 0.3 / update 0.2 (the community's VTA writes label and description as the profile, with a pending-retry owner) come in a separate PR on top of the #805 implementation.
- Plugin: OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#336.

feat(rooms): a room's own profile — rooms/keys/profile/{read,write}, sealed inside the room (#2171)

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#807 on the key holder's side. A
room's name, description, tags and emoji (RoomProfile) now live inside the
room: one record per epoch at profile_key(E) — HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch's
storage key, info "openvtc/room/profile/v1" || roomId || u64be(E), 16 bytes,
base64url — sealed like any record, so the host stores one more opaque record
and cannot tell which one names the room. An open room's is the record at
`room-profile`, its signed body in cleartext.body.

VTA (vta-service):
- rooms/keys/profile/read/0.1: walks from the current epoch down (bound 32),
  fetching each location as the member under their own `read` grant,
  verifying the host's reply as rooms/keys/read does, and takes the newest
  profile it accepts (`found`, `stale` below the current epoch), stops at a
  retraction (`cleared`), or answers `absent`, with `searched`.
- Readers decide who may name the room
  (operations::room_profile::check_statement): the SealedRecordBody rules
  (1)-(4) — no unknown member, the author's assertionMethod proof, signed for
  the location read, the host-recorded author on attributed — plus
  RoomProfileStatement items 1-4: a profile and nothing a record carries,
  sealed under the epoch that located it, issuedAt within
  [updatedAt − 1h, updatedAt + 5m], and an authority chain conferring
  `curate` or `admin` on the author at the room's scope, every link valid at
  issuedAt (vti_rooms_dtg::profile::verify_profile_authority). Anything that
  fails is ignored and reported in `rejected` with its reason and author; a
  rename by a member holding only `write` is `noAuthority` and the room keeps
  the profile before it. This VTA holds no RevocationList, so item 5 never
  applies (revocation is not retroactive).
- rooms/keys/profile/write/0.1: refuses `noAuthority` before contacting the
  host without `write` and `curate`/`admin` (`curate` to clear); signs the
  statement as the principal (assertionMethod, through the gated oracle) with
  the room-issued chain inside, pads the signed body to a 1 KiB multiple,
  seals it under the current epoch and puts it as the member under a `write`
  grant; re-seals for the version the host assigned, then `contended`.
  `clear` retracts the current location with a `curate` grant, storing a
  profile there first when it holds none. Delegates are refused.
- The epoch-advance re-write: rooms/owner/group/{add,remove,renew} read the
  profile before the advance and write it again under the new epoch as the
  owner once the host accepts — never failing, delaying or undoing the
  advance (tried a few times, then logged), never for `absent`/`cleared`,
  never retracting the earlier one (add 0.1 and 0.2, remove, renew; the
  speaker is HostCall::profile_speaker, so a later version reuses it).
- rooms/keys/read does not open a profile location (answers
  ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].roomProfile) and rooms/keys/browse leaves profile

  classified RetrySafe in vta_sdk::retry_safety, counted in budget, guarded in

chain, self-issued, validity at issuedAt), the derivation pinned against the
