title: feat(vtc/community/theme): show and update — a community's own stylesheet for its console and member portal
body:
A community could set an accent colour and a logo (vtc/community/branding),
and nothing else about how its pages look. Administrators want to restyle
their console and member portal at run time, without the operator-only
admin_ui directory mode.

vtc/community/theme/update/0.1 (new, draft):
- An administrator replaces one stylesheet; the empty string removes it.
  Proof and issuedAt REQUIRED; audited by digest, never by text.
- `dryRun: true` checks and answers with what would be stored, storing
  nothing, so a client can preview a theme exactly as stored.
- The theme profile (P1-P8): design tokens on :root (light/dark), plus a
  small set of cosmetic properties on ordinary elements — colours,
  gradients, bounded borders/radius, font family/weight. No url()/@import/
  @font-face (a theme loads nothing), no !important, no escapes or `<`, and
  nothing that can move, size, hide, overlay or add content.
  `outsideProfile` names the line, column and profile item broken.
- maxDocumentBytes 48 KiB both ways, for a 32 KiB stylesheet.

vtc/community/theme/show/0.1 (new, draft):
- Proof OPTIONAL and answerable to an unidentified caller: sign-in pages
  draw the theme before the visitor holds any identity.
- Client requirements: re-check the profile before applying; render every
  surface where a person decides, approves, consents, signs or is warned
  in structural isolation from the theme; mark that a custom theme is on.

Why no second-administrator consent: the profile and the isolation
together mean a theme cannot change what another administrator is asked
to approve, so it stays an ordinary configuration write.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

title: feat(rooms): readable records, a context tree, and one Communities lane per community
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #347, from using the new pane:

- **Records** showed random keys until each was opened, then the signed record as one line of JSON, with a full verdict box under every record.
- **The New room context picker** was a flat `<select>`, so sub-contexts read as siblings of their parents.
- **Offers and Shared with sites** were two tabs describing one relationship from either end. Nothing said that a share on one was of the room accepted on the other.
- **Owner tools** made you type a room DID and signing key, even for a room this console had just created.

## What changes (three commits)

**1. Records by title and content**
- In a sealed room the title is sealed with the body, so the newest 5 records open as the list arrives (`AUTO_OPEN`); the rest open on a click. Retracted records are never opened unasked.
- A row is a title and a two-line preview, with author and date. A note reads as its text; a file shows its name, size and Download. The signed record is folded under "The signed record".
- A clean verdict is one line, with the full words one click away. An adverse one (conflicting answers, a short count, a failed trace) is still said in full, on the row, expanded or not.
- Upload is a button that opens the form.
- No `v<n>` on rows: `manager-version-display.test.mts` caught that a version is the room's write counter, not a revision.

**2. A context tree picker** (`context-picker.tsx`)
- The console's own context tree, used as a picker: top-level contexts first, with "N inside" counts.
- Expand on click, and a search that finds a sub-context wherever it sits. It folds to the chosen context, with Change.
- A parent the caller's ACL doesn't reach is drawn so its children show, and can't be chosen.

**3. Communities lanes, and the owner pick**
- **Communities** replaces Offers and Shared with sites. Each community is a lane and each room is one row across it: offered to you → in your rooms → its portal can see.
  - Offers are marked new / accepted / unfinished.
  - Accepted-but-not-held says the keys haven't arrived yet.
  - Shares are revocable in place, and a held room opens in My rooms.
  - `community-lanes.ts` joins the three sources by room. Only this agent's shares are included.
- `useRoomOffers` and `useRoomShares` replace the two cards. The pane owns the offers polling, so the tab badge counts whichever tab is showing.
- **Owner tools:** rooms this console creates are remembered with their signing key, beside the host, and offered as a pick that fills both fields. Rooms created before this change aren't remembered, so they still need typing. A created room's detail has **Issue in its name**.
  - This relaxes the "typed, never looked up" rule in `rooms-owner.tsx`, and its comment now says why. Both fields stay editable, and a stale key fails loudly the first time the credential is checked, exactly as a mistyped one does.

CLAUDE.md now names the Communities tab where it named the two old ones.

## Tests

- **New:** `community-lanes.test.mts` and `context-picker.render.test.mts`.
- **Extended:** `rooms-records`, `rooms-offers` (now renders the lanes), `rooms-owner`, `rooms-create` (drives the tree picker), and `room-groups` (the remembered key).
- `npm test`, `npm run build` and the CI bundle-guard steps pass locally. The pane has **not** been exercised in Chrome against a live agent.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new network paths. Record reads use the existing `rooms/keys/read` through the agent.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): a room's signing key is remembered only after `rooms/owner/register` succeeded.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added. Opening the newest records happens once per listing.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): the offers poll is unchanged, just moved into a hook.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound path untouched.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire changes.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): with nothing remembered, the owner form starts empty as before.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): adverse verdicts are never folded; accepted is not shown as held.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): a lost hint write means one more typed field, nothing else.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: spec(rooms/keys): act 0.4 — a member lists their offers at vtc/rooms/offers/list 0.2
body:
## The problem

`rooms/keys/act` is how a member's own client (pnm, the browser wallet) gets a request signed **as the member** — as the DID a community addressed its offer of a room to, whose keys only the member's key holder holds. Its table of completable types is closed (Recipient item 1).

`act/0.3` admits `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1` and `vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1`. It does not admit `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2`, which #805 added so a member sees each offered room's current label and **description** (never its tags). A key holder conforming to `act/0.3` refuses a `0.2` listing with `typeNotActable`, so surfaces that read offers through `act` are stuck on `0.1`, and members never see what a room is for before accepting. `offers/list/0.2`'s own prose even pointed at "`act` 0.3 or later", which does not list it.

## Versioning decision (SPEC §5.2): new `act/0.4`, not an in-place edit

`act/0.3` is `status: draft`. §5.2 lets a draft take a breaking change as a MINOR increment, and requires an **in-place** edit only for an *editorial or normalization* change — re-casing, a wire-neutral `$ref` re-pin, rewording prose — one that "carries no semantic difference on the wire".

Admitting one more inner type is not that: a type a conforming `0.3` recipient refuses, a `0.4` recipient completes and signs as the member. That is a change in observable behaviour, so not editorial — the in-place rule does not cover it, and a MINOR increment is what §5.2 prescribes. It is also exactly how `act/0.3` itself was made (#797): widening the table was a new version, not an edit to `0.2`. One could argue the general draft allowance ("MAY change without notice") permits editing `0.3` in place; I took the conservative reading, consistent with this slug's own history and with the fact that implementations (VTI) already ship `0.3`'s table.

## What changed

- **`specs/rooms/keys/act/0.4/`** (copied from `0.3`):
  - The table's offers/list row lists `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1` **and** `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2`, on identical terms: no presentation inserted; `issuer` REQUIRED and the DID the offer is addressed to (Producer item 2); resolved without a room credential (Recipient item 2b, which now names `list/0.2`); same delegate refusal (item 3).
  - New *What changed from 0.3* note (the previous note becomes *What 0.3 changed from 0.2*); a request example completing a `list/0.2`; the Abstract links `offers/list/0.2`.
  - Schema: `$id`/response type → `0.4`; the `issuer` description names `list/0.2`. Otherwise identical to `0.3` — the `type` pattern already admits `vtc/rooms/offers/`. No error code added. Invalid examples unchanged.
- **`vtc/rooms/offers/accept`** has only `0.1`, so nothing changes for it.
- **`specs/vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2/spec.md`**, in place: the *Signing as the member* paragraph now points at `act` `0.4` or later. Prose only; wire unchanged (§5.2 editorial, as in #797).
- **Bindings regenerated** (Rust, TS, Go, Dart): additive `act/0.4` modules + index/conformance entries only.

Checks run locally: `npm run validate` / `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings` (818 specs, all four languages agree), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, TS `tsc --noEmit`, `go build ./...`, `dart analyze` on the new module.

## Downstream follow-up (after this merges and is released)

- **VTI** (`OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure`): serve `rooms/keys/act/0.4` and add `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2` to `vta-service/src/operations/room_act.rs` `OFFER_TYPES` — it is held until this spec lands so the implementation does not diverge from the spec.
- **pnm** and the **browser wallet**: send `act/0.4` wrapping `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2` once the `trust-tasks-rs` / `@openvtc/trust-tasks` release carrying `act/0.4` is out, so members see room descriptions.

title: feat(rooms): redesign the rooms pane as tabs, grouped cards and a room detail
body:
## Why

The rooms pane rendered every room's full detail at once: the history explanation, the custody caveat, **two separate empty host fields** (records and history), the records, and a four-field label editor per row. Two rooms filled two screens, and the host DID had to be typed again on every visit.

## What changes

- **Tabs:** My rooms · Offers (count badge) · Shared with sites · Owner tools. **New room** opens the create flow on its own, under a back link.
- **One card per room**, grouped by where the room was last found, or by trust context. A room held as two members is one card that says "Held as 2 identities".
- **Room detail** (`rooms-detail.tsx`):
  - An **Acting as** switch picks one place at a time. Everything under it is still keyed by `heldRoomKey` and names that member, so the agent is never asked to choose.
  - **Records** lists straight from the remembered host, with **Change** and **Refresh**. Files stay here, because a file is a record carrying a file claim.
  - **About** shows the room's own profile, the community's name and your label side by side. The label editor is a popover.
  - **Access** holds the two epochs and what they mean, **Fetch the history**, the custody-vs-permission statement and the full DIDs.
- **The custody caveat is said once**, above the cards (dismissible), instead of under every row.

## Remembered hosts (new state)

`room-hosts.ts` keeps `room-hosts:<vtaDid>` in `chrome.storage.local`. It records a host the console created the room at, or one that answered a listing. A community's offer (`room-names:`) is read as the same kind of hint, and the console's own record outranks it.

It is a **hint, never authority**. The agent still keeps no host, every request still goes through the agent, and *Change* is always offered. A wrong hint costs one refused listing and grants nothing. CLAUDE.md's Data rooms section now records this, and what breaks it.

## Tests

- **`rooms-pane.render.test.mts`:** three assertions moved into the room detail.
  - New cases: one card plus the place switch, listing from a known host with no host field, a host remembered once it answers, and grouping by context.
- **`room-groups.test.mts` (new):** which hint wins, nothing unwritten is believed, the size cap holds, and no room is dropped by either grouping.

`npm test` and `npm run build` pass locally. I have **not** exercised the pane in Chrome against a live agent.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new network calls; the pane uses the existing agent tasks.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): a host is remembered only after it answered a listing, or after registration succeeded.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): no loops added; the existing offers poll is unchanged.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound path untouched.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire changes.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): no hint means the pane asks for the host, as before.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): the host is labelled "last found at", not "hosted at".
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): a hint write lost to a crash means the room asks for its host once more.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: feat(vtc)!: community-room details administrators can see, edit and track (trust-tasks-tf #805)
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#805 (merged; trust-tasks-rs 0.31.14).

Two commits: the trust-tasks-rs floor bump on its own (`build:`) so a rebase against the revocation work (#804), which raises the same floor, is trivial; then the feature.

## What

- **`vtc/rooms/community/update/0.1`**:
  - Gate and checks: `vtc.rooms.manage`, no step-up and no parking. Proof and `issuedAt` are required, enforced by the spine from the spec.
  - Each detail given replaces the stored one. `tags: []` clears the tags; `removeDescription` removes the description; `minProperties` and `dependentSchemas` are checked against the schema.
  - A no-op answers `changed: false` and writes nothing: no `detailsUpdated*` and no audit row. Tags compare as sets.
  - A room the community only hosts is `notFound`.
  - The details are stored on the owner's record (`community_rooms`), never on the host record or anything sent to the VTA, and an update sends no live hint.
- **0.2 alongside 0.1**:
  - `create`, `get` and `list` 0.2 answer `CommunityRoomV2`; `list` takes a `tag` filter that is applied before paging.
  - `offers/list/0.2` returns the room's *current* label and description, and never its tags.
  - The 0.1 versions keep their published shapes.
- **Audit**:
  - `CommunityRoomChanged`, with a new event `detailsUpdated`.
  - `CommunityRoomChangedData` gains `details: Vec<FieldChange>` (reusing the existing type: field, old, new). A create's row records the details the room started with.
  - The struct is not `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new field breaks vti-common's API; that is why the title has `!`.
- **Concurrency**: an update and an authority renewal both re-read the owner's record and write it under one new record lock, so neither writes back a stale copy of the other's change.
- **Censuses**:
  - The dispatched-URI list.
  - `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF`: get/list 0.2, which declare proof RECOMMENDED.
  - Conformance samples for every new payload and response.
  - An error-code witness for `update:notFound`.
  - The console's `SPINE_DOCUMENT_TYPES`: it now sends create/get/list 0.2 and update 0.1.
  - `list-limits.json`.
  - OpenAPI wrappers in `vta_sdk::openapi`, with the snapshot and `wire.ts` regenerated. The snapshot test passes under default features and under `vetting-pcs`.
- **cnm**:
  - `cnm rooms update <room> [--label] [--description|--remove-description] [--tag …|--clear-tags] --reason`.
  - `cnm rooms list --tag`, and `create --description/--tag`.
  - `list` and `get` show the description, tags and who last changed the details. They fall back to 0.1 against an older VTC (except with `--tag`).
- **Console**:
  - On a community room's page: Edit details (sends only what differs; asks for no gesture), plus the description, tags and "details last changed" by whom and when. The page title is the label and the lead is the description.
  - On the list: tag chips and a tag filter (`?tag=`).
  - The description is also shown on the host Rooms pages, through #2157's `useRoomNames`; tags are never shown there.
- **Docs**: `community-rooms.md` (a new "A room's details" section), the data rooms quickstart §12, and `website-and-admin.md`.

## Not done / open

- **`vta_sdk::retry_safety`**: not classified. That table is the VTA's catalogue: its census runs over `vta_sdk::trust_tasks::ALL_URIS`, and a `vtc/*` entry would fail `no_classification_without_a_task`. No VTC task is classified there today.
- **The description in `pnm rooms offers list`**: not shown. pnm has the member's VTA sign offer requests with `rooms/keys/act/0.3`, and that spec's table lists `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1` only. Completing 0.2 at the VTA would diverge from the spec. Recorded under "What is not here yet" in `community-rooms.md`. It needs the act table to admit `offers/list/0.2` (act 0.3 is a draft) before the VTA's `OFFER_TYPES` and pnm can switch.
- **The label at room creation**: a create still sends the label to the VTA, as `LABEL` and the key record's label in `vta/webvh/dids/create`. That is not a `rooms/*` task, so create 0.2 item 8 permits it. Only the label goes there, never the description or tags. After a rename, the VTA's key label is stale.

## Verified locally

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6172 passed. On an earlier run two tests hit the 5-minute timeout under load; both pass when run alone: vta-backup `every_backed_up_keyspace_survives_a_round_trip` (188 s under nextest) and vta-service `every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry` (34 s under `cargo test`; it timed out alone under nextest).
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: everything passed except 12 tests that need the embedded admin UI (the run used `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`). Those 12 pass with the UI built.
- `cargo test --workspace --doc`.
- admin-ui: `wire:check`, `tsc`, vitest (1127 passed) and `vite build`.

title: fix(rooms): quiet the Offers card for parties without room offers, and blame each failure on its source
body:
## What the member saw

On the console's Data rooms → Offers card, one entry per party the wallet signs in to:

1. Old dev VTCs with no `TrustTaskHTTPS` service: a red *"The wallet could not find where this community takes requests: … advertises no TrustTaskHTTPS service …"*.
2. A **DID-hosting service** the wallet signs in to (a `didSelfIssued` entry from the WebVHHosting sign-in), not a community: a red *"Your agent does not serve rooms/keys/act 0.3 …"*. The member's VTA serves act 0.3 fine.

## Root cause

**Misattribution.** `communityRoomOffers` calls the member's VTA (`rooms/keys/act/0.3`) and then the community (`vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1`), and let either party's error escape untagged. `listRefusal` ran every one through `actRefusal`, which reads `unsupportedType` as "your agent lacks act 0.3" and `permissionDenied` as the wallet lacking `room-present`. So the hosting service answering `unsupportedType` to offers/list was blamed on the member's VTA.

**Noise.** Offer sources are every party the member signs in to. Most make no room offers. No `TrustTaskHTTPS`, or `unsupportedType` / `unsupportedVersion` on offers/list, is that ordinary answer, and the member can do nothing about it. The card still showed it in red.

## Fix

- `offers.ts`: each failure is tagged with the party that produced it (`OfferReadError`, stage `act` | `community`).
- `offer-accept.ts`: act-stage errors still go through `actRefusal`. Community-stage errors go through a new `communityListRefusal`, which gives `noRoomOffers` (new), `notAMember`, `communityRefused` (new), retryable `noAnswer`, or the community's own message prefixed with its DID. The accept path reads offers through the same function, so it is fixed too. A generic refusal of the acceptance now also names the community.
- `host-channel.ts`: `roomHostEndpoint` now throws a typed `NoTrustTaskServiceError`. It is still `e.client.parse` and is matched with `isNoTrustTaskService` (R3.7).
- Extension: the offscreen document maps both quiet cases to the code `noRoomOffers` (`NO_ROOM_OFFERS`). The background leaves those parties off the card (`OffersOverview.noOffers`), and `forPortal` returns `{ offers: [] }` for them. When no party offers rooms, the card shows one muted line. A community that serves offers and fails still shows its error, named as the community.
- No new network call. The endpoint lookup already resolves the DID document, and nothing is sent to an unverified party.

## Tests

- core `rooms.offers.mjs`:
  - a community `unsupportedType` / `unsupportedVersion` on offers/list gives `noRoomOffers` and does not mention act 0.3;
  - the VTA refusing act with `unsupportedType` still gives `actUnsupported`, and nothing reaches the community;
  - a community `permissionDenied` gives `communityRefused`, and a network failure gives `noAnswer`, both naming the community and not "Your agent". The VTA's own `permissionDenied` is still `capability`;
  - a missing `TrustTaskHTTPS` is detected by type, not by the message text.
- core `rooms.offer-accept.mjs`: during an accept, a community refusal of the offer read is attributed to the community.
- extension `room-offers.test.mts`:
  - parties with no `TrustTaskHTTPS`, or that don't serve offers/list, are left off and listed in `noOffers`;
  - a failing community keeps its error;
  - the portal gets an empty list;
  - the offscreen endpoint lookup returns the quiet code.
- extension `rooms-offers.render.test.mts` (new):
  - no red error for quiet parties;
  - a muted line when every party is quiet;
  - a failing community's error is shown and named.

## Verified locally

`npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` and `npm test` all pass: core 1020, extension 1151, plus the other workspaces. Every bundle guard in `ci.yml` passes, including "no page-reachable bundle names a rooms task" (background.js) and the single-bundle checks. `scripts/package.mjs` packages.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no new fetch
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — no mutation changed
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — unchanged
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — internal bridge type only (OffersOverview.noOffers); errors matched on codes (R3.7)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — real failures still surface, attributed to their source
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — read-only paths
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

title: fix(rooms): quiet the Offers card for parties without room offers, and blame each failure on its source (#346)
body:
fix(rooms): quiet the Offers card for parties without room offers, and blame each failure on its source (#346)

The Offers card asks every party the member signs in to with the wallet (each
didSelfIssued sign-in entry) for its room offers. Two things went wrong.

Misattribution. Reading offers talks to two parties in turn: the member's VTA
completes the request as the member (rooms/keys/act/0.3), then the community
answers it (vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1). communityRoomOffers let either party's
error escape untagged, and listRefusal ran every one through actRefusal, which
reads unsupportedType / unsupportedVersion as "your agent does not serve
rooms/keys/act 0.3" and permissionDenied as the wallet lacking room-present at
its VTA. So a DID-hosting service the member signs in to, answering
unsupportedType to offers/list, was reported as the member's own VTA needing an
update — while that VTA served act 0.3 fine. communityRoomOffers now tags each
failure with the party that produced it (OfferReadError, stage "act" or
"community"); the act stage still maps through actRefusal, and the community
stage through its own mapping (noRoomOffers, notAMember, communityRefused,
noAnswer, or the community's message prefixed with its DID). The accept path
reads the offers first through the same function, so it is fixed by the same
change; a generic refusal of the acceptance itself now names the community too.

Noise. Most parties the member signs in to make no room offers at all: a
DID-hosting service, an old community without rooms. Advertising no
TrustTaskHTTPS service, or answering offers/list with unsupportedType /
unsupportedVersion, is that ordinary answer, not an error the member can act
on — but the card showed both in red. roomHostEndpoint now throws a typed
NoTrustTaskServiceError (still e.client.parse, matched with
isNoTrustTaskService), the offscreen document turns it and the community's
unsupported refusal into the code noRoomOffers, and the background leaves those
parties off the card (OffersOverview.noOffers) and gives the portal an empty
list. When no party offers rooms, the card says so in one muted line. A
community that serves offers and fails (network, timeout, permissionDenied,
notAMember) still shows its error, named as the community. No new network call:
the endpoint lookup already resolves the DID document.

title: Keyring findings: Tier 2 + Tier 3 backlog (restated, because their document moves)
body:
Durable home for the Keyring findings we accepted but have not yet done.

**Why this exists.** Their report lives at `berkmancenter/keyring-wallet`,
`docs/VTI_UPSTREAM_FINDINGS.md`, on the branch `feat/prague-farm-membership` —
a branch in a fork we do not control. Every anchor into it rots when it moves
or merges, and the document is **edited in place**: VTI-31 gained a "Fixed
upstream" note, and a retraction of its own proposed fix, between our first
read and our second. So the findings are restated here rather than linked.

Tier 1 is closed (10 shipped, 3 already fixed before we read the report). This
issue covers what remains. Split an item into its own issue when someone picks
it up; this is the index, not the work.

Full triage and reasoning: `design-docs/keyring-remediation-plan.html`.

---

## Tier 2 — accepted, not yet scheduled

- **KR-15 — `VTCRest` endpoint omits `/v1`.** The template emits a bare
  `{URL}`; its status-list sibling already carries `/v1`. Fix the template,
  and accept both forms on the resolver side for DIDs already minted.
- **KR-21 — no channel delivers an invitation to its invitee.** Admission is
  push-shaped with no join ceremony — a known shape, not a surprise. Needs a
  delivery path to the invitee, not only to the admin.
- **KR-32 — an invitation is too large for the channel it must travel on.**
  An `InvitationCredential` link is 6,331 bytes; QR byte mode tops out at
  2,953, and base64url's `-`/`_` rule out alphanumeric mode. **Do this with
  KR-21, not separately** — they are one problem seen from each end, and
  invite-by-reference (a short identifier the client resolves, as it already
  resolves a manifest) answers both.
- **KR-23 — manager operations require admin.** Folds into the existing ACL
  capability-narrowing work; `keys.rs:229` already calls `require_admin` a
  "role floor", so the least-privilege path is a known gap.
- **KR-17 · KR-18 — provisioning leaves a DID unusable.** One issue, not two:
  re-provision binds to a dead hostname, and a self-managed mint produces a
  DID with no services the VTA will accept.
- **KR-08 — worker stack overflow creating a context.** Debug-build only, with
  a 32 MiB workaround, so it does not block them — but a stack that deep is
  worth understanding rather than papering over.
- **KR-07 · KR-16 · KR-20 — three small operational fixes.**
  `functions_file` resolved against cwd; admin invite needing the daemon
  stopped; a persona mint printing instructions that do not apply. Cheap,
  unglamorous, and each cost them an afternoon.

## Tier 3 — answered in prose, not code

- **KR-01 · KR-11 — bootstrap order is undocumented.** A fresh VTC cannot
  authenticate its own admin, and the first vetter has no documented path.
  Both are real sequences that simply are not written down. A setup runbook is
  the deliverable, and it is the cheapest high-value item in the whole set for
  the next integrator.
- **KR-22 — consent policies inert by default.** The default stays off:
  flipping it would silently turn every written-but-not-intended policy into a
  gate across existing deployments. Document it as opt-in **and** add a
  startup warning when policy rows exist while `policy.enforcement` is false —
  the missing warning is the actual defect they hit.
- **KR-25 — card delivered, not returned inline.** A deliberate change on
  Eucalyptus that was never written up. Changelog entry and a migration note.

## Not in this issue

- **Declined or re-scoped** (KR-02, KR-10, KR-12, KR-13) — each answered with
  a written reason in the plan; no work queued.
- **KR-06** — blocked until their configuration reproduces it.
- The conformance-ledger gap is #1600.

title: feat(rooms): a member's own private name, description, notes and tags for each room they hold
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#806 (released in trust-tasks-rs 0.31.14, #809): a member's own private name, description, notes and tags for each room they hold, kept by their VTA.

Two commits:
1. `build(deps)`: trust-tasks-rs floor 0.31.14.
2. `feat(rooms)`: the implementation. The commit body has the details.

## VTA
- **Storage**: `room-label/<roomId>/<persona>` in `room_groups`, next to the group state, so it is backed up and protected the same way. Each write is one conditional `Batch`: the group state must still be present and the label row unchanged since it was read. That means a label can never be written for a room whose group state was just discarded, and two devices editing different details both land. `room_groups::forget` discards the label along with the group state (item 8). When a commit removes the member, both are kept.
- **`rooms/keys/label/0.1`**: checks run in this order:
  - `roomOpen`
  - a delegate (AI-agent or mediator ACL kind) gets `permissionDenied` (item 1)
  - one `notHeld` answer covers both "not held" and "not a member you act as", decided before the stored label is read (item 2)
  
  Writes are patches (item 3): each field given replaces the stored one, a `removeX` removes one, and absent fields are unchanged. A request with only `ext` is `malformedRequest`. Removing the last field deletes the label (item 4). A no-op returns `changed: false`, writes nothing and leaves `updatedAt` alone. Comparison is exact for strings and set-wise for tags (items 5–7). The policy subject is `/member`.
- **The text is never logged or audited** (item 10):
  - The audit row `rooms.keys.label` records only the room, the member and changed/unchanged.
  - The dispatch spine no longer logs a schema error's text for these tasks.
  - The spine does not keep label or list-0.2 responses for replay redelivery (`carries_personal_text`).
- **`rooms/keys/list/0.2`**, served beside 0.1:
  - Each entry names its `member`.
  - `personal` is included only with `includePersonal: true`.
  - A delegate gets an empty list.
  - `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].held` (context and actions) is still sent on both versions.
  - 0.1 is unchanged (#2161's ext stays).
- **Labels never reach act/seal/present** (item 9): the list handler is the only reader. A source census test pins that, and a seal/open test runs with a label stored and checks the output.
- Registered in dispatch, the conformance witnesses and `retry_safety`: label and list 0.2 are both RetrySafe. Label is idempotent by spec.

## Clients
- **vta-sdk** (additive):
  - `room_list(include_personal)`: 0.2, falling back to 0.1 with each member read from `ext`.
  - `room_label(room, member, &RoomLabelEdit)` and `room_label_payload`, which check the request against the schema before sending.
  - `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_{LIST_0_2,LABEL_0_1}`.
- **pnm**:
  - New command: `pnm rooms keys label <room> --member <did> [--label --description --notes --tag … --remove-label --remove-description --remove-notes --remove-tags]`.
  - `pnm rooms keys list` now shows the member and your label. Control characters other than line breaks and tabs are shown as U+FFFD. A not-held error says to take `--member` from the list.
- **vta-mcp**: `rooms/keys/label` is classed as Mutating. Its arguments and error text are fully elided from the call log, because `label` was otherwise a safe key there.

Docs: `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md`.

## Verification (local, macOS)
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passes.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passes.
- The two reduced-feature `vta-service` clippy runs: pass.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6197 passed. In an earlier run, `audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry` hit the 300 s timeout under load. Rerun alone, it passed in 154 s.
- Workspace doctests: pass.
- vtc-service and vtc-client nextest and doctests: see the follow-up comment.

## Re-test
```
pnm rooms keys list                         # note the member DID beside a room
pnm rooms keys label <room> --member <did> --label "Northwind" --tag work
pnm rooms keys list                         # your name first, DID beside it
pnm rooms keys label <room> --member <did> --label "Northwind"   # "nothing changed"
pnm rooms keys label <room> --member <did> --remove-label --remove-tags
```

The browser plugin counterpart is OpenVTC/pnm-browser-plugin (linked from there).

* feat(rooms): a member's own private name, description, notes and tags for each room they hold

trust-tasks-tf #806 adds rooms/keys/label/0.1 and rooms/keys/list/0.2: a
member's personal label for a room, kept by their key holder for their eyes
only, and a list that names each entry's member and returns the labels when
asked.

VTA:

- Storage: `room-label/<roomId>/<persona>` in `room_groups`, beside the group
  state (so backed up and protected with it). Written by one conditional batch
  that requires the group state still present and the label row unchanged, so
  a label never outlives a `forget` and two devices editing different details
  both land. `room_groups::forget` discards it with the group state (item 8);
  a commit removing the member keeps both.
- rooms/keys/label/0.1: `roomOpen`, then a delegate (AI-agent / mediator entry)
  is `permissionDenied` (item 1), then one `notHeld` for "no group state as
  this member" and "not a member you act as" (item 2), decided before the
  stored label is read. Patch semantics (item 3): each detail given replaces,
  `removeX` removes, absent is unchanged; a request naming no change (only
  `ext`) is `malformedRequest`. Removing the last detail deletes the label
  (item 4). Nothing written and `changed: false` when nothing would change,
  strings compared exactly and tags as a set (items 5–7). Policy subject is
  `/member`.
- Never logged or audited (item 10): the audit row `rooms.keys.label` names
  room, member and changed/unchanged only; the dispatch spine no longer logs a
  schema error's text for these tasks and does not keep a label or a 0.2 list
  response for replay redelivery.
- rooms/keys/list/0.2 beside 0.1: each entry names its `member`; `personal`
  only with `includePersonal: true`; a delegate is listed nothing.
  `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].held` (context, actions) stays on both versions,
  and 0.1 is unchanged.
- Labels never reach act/seal/present (item 9): the only reader is the list
  handler, pinned by a source census test and a seal/open run with a label
  stored.
- Dispatch, conformance witnesses, `vta_sdk::retry_safety` (label RetrySafe —
  idempotent by specification; list 0.2 RetrySafe).

Clients:

- vta-sdk: `room_list(include_personal)` (0.2, falling back to 0.1 with each
  member read from `ext`), `room_label(room, member, &RoomLabelEdit)`,
  `room_label_payload`, and `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_{LIST_0_2,LABEL_0_1}`.
- pnm: `pnm rooms keys label <room> --member <did> [--label --description
  --notes --tag … --remove-label --remove-description --remove-notes
  --remove-tags]`; `pnm rooms keys list` shows the member and your label
  (control characters other than line breaks shown as U+FFFD).
- vta-mcp: `rooms/keys/label` classified Mutating; its arguments and error
  text are fully elided from the call log (`label` is otherwise a safe key).

Docs: data-rooms (your own name for a room, reference table).

title: vtc: the admin console cannot sign, so every bearer route #1641 would retire has to stay
body:
Design note: [`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-console-signing.md`](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/blob/main/docs/05-design-notes/vtc-console-signing.md). Read it before starting — this issue is the work list, not the reasoning.

## Why

#1681 moved the first four admin member verbs onto the signed-document dispatcher and kept their bearer routes, because **the admin console cannot author a signed Trust Task document**. `vtc-trust-task-proof-enforcement.md` §6b states that as the removal point for every bearer route in the #1641 migration. The console is the only one of the three blocking client surfaces (admin SPA, `cnm`, `vtc-client`) with no path at all, and it is the largest share: **34 of the 49** bearer-served proof-REQUIRED tasks are console-reachable, including all four #1681 kept.

Premise verified: `vtc-service/admin-ui/src` has no signing primitive outside generated OpenAPI doc comments, and no crypto dependency. The passkey cannot substitute — the `webauthn-vti-v1` cryptosuite that would have let a WebAuthn assertion *be* a Data-Integrity proof was superseded in this repo on 2026-05-20.

## The shape

**A console signing key is a credential of the operator's existing admin DID, the way a passkey is** — not an identity of its own. The operator already *is* a DID with an `acl:<did>` row; that DID is a `did:key`, so it cannot grow a second verification method, and #1658's `Invariant::SelfPromotion` (VTI-OPS-050) blocks giving the console key its own admin ACL row. So the VTC stores a **delegation**: "console key K may act as admin DID D", enrolled by D behind the step-up the console already runs, listed beside the passkeys, individually revocable, conferring no role on its own.

Authority stays an ACL row read at execution time, so #1681's stated property (`admin_signer` never consults `sessions_ks`) survives.

Server-side signing is **rejected**, not deferred — VTI-OPS-021 / -093. See §5E.

## Decisions needed before starting

1. **Option A or B** — durable per-device delegation (recommended) vs ephemeral key bound via the already-plumbed `session_pubkey_b58btc` (materially cheaper, authority returns through the session, forward-compatible).
2. **Browser-support floor.** WebCrypto Ed25519 (Chrome 137+ / Firefox 130+ / Safari 17+) buys a non-extractable key; `@noble/curves` works everywhere but the key is extractable by definition.
3. **May an operator sign from two devices?** The note assumes yes, N delegations per admin DID, mirroring passkeys.
4. **Default delegation lifetime**, and whether a key survives sign-out.

## Work, assuming A

- [ ] **Client signing module.** Lift `affinidi-webvh-service/did-hosting-ui/lib/session-key.ts` (zero-dependency, already implements the construction) with three changes: `extractable: false` + an assertion, per-origin IndexedDB record, `created` back-dated 60 s. Sign at the `src/lib/api.ts` seam, not at call sites.
- [ ] **JCS conformance test** — round-trip each dispatched payload's canonical form against Rust `serde_jcs`. The lifted canonicaliser is "good enough for our documents", not conformance-tested (number serialisation, Unicode normalisation).
- [ ] **`console_keys` keyspace** — `console_key:<consoleDid>` → `{ admin_did, label, created_at, created_by, expires_at, last_used_at }`. Classify in the backup census (`EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP` — a restore must not resurrect a browser's signing authority). Sweeper tick for `expires_at`.
- [ ] **Enrolment verbs** mirroring `auth/passkey/{enroll,revoke}`: `POST /v1/admin/console-keys` (`AdminAuth` + live `StepUpAuth`), `GET`, `DELETE /{consoleDid}`. Needs an upstream Trust Task spec in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf before it can be dispatched — see `new-task-family-needs-upstream-spec-first`.
- [ ] **`admin_signer` delegation step** — signer's own ACL row first (unchanged), then the delegation → the delegating admin's ACL row, at execution time.
- [ ] **Audit carries both** the admin DID (actor) and the console DID (acting credential), via `AuditLogEntry.detail`.
- [ ] **Console UI** — "enable signing for this browser" + a key list beside `myPasskeys.tsx`; graceful degradation to the bearer path when unsupported or not yet enrolled.
- [ ] **Keep the step-up where it is.** A console key is possession of a browser profile; the passkey is possession of an authenticator plus UV. Admin-conferring verbs on the signed door must still consult `elevation::verified` on the delegating admin's live session.
- [ ] **Retire the four #1681 kept** — move `plugins/members.tsx` to `POST /v1/trust-tasks`, check `members/update`'s `extensions` bag against the signed door's **64 KiB** cap (vs 1 MB on the bearer chain), give `vtc-client` the same path, delete routes + OpenAPI entries, regenerate `openapi.json` + `wire.ts`.

## Follow-ups

- [ ] Report upstream to `affinidi-webvh-service`: `did-hosting-ui/lib/session-key.ts` passes `extractable: true` to `generateKey` on the stated reasoning that it is needed to export the raw public key. It is not — WebCrypto sets `publicKey.[[extractable]]` unconditionally and `privateKey.[[extractable]]` from the argument — so the session private key is exportable by any script in the origin. One-character fix. Measured table in §4b of the note.
- [ ] **Where this should end up** (§7): if the operator's admin identity were a `did:webvh` rather than a `did:key`, the console key would be published as a verification method in the operator's own DID document, `issuer` would be the admin DID, and the delegation record would disappear — along with the objection that it is not publicly readable. Larger change; should not gate this one.

title: feat(rooms): your own private name, description, notes and tags for each room, in the console
body:
Plugin side of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#806: a member's own private label (name, description, notes, tags) for each room they hold. The VTA keeps it, and only the member's own console shows it. The VTA side is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2167.

Two commits:
1. `build(deps)`: `@openvtc/trust-tasks` ^0.26.15, which carries the `rooms/keys/label/0.1` and `rooms/keys/list/0.2` bindings.
2. `feat(rooms)`: the change itself.

## What changes
- **`@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms`**:
  - `roomsKeysList` now uses `rooms/keys/list/0.2`. The member comes from the entry itself, and context/actions still come from `ext`.
  - It takes `{ includePersonal }`, off by default. If the caller did not ask for labels, any label in the reply is dropped.
  - New `roomsKeysLabel` / `roomLabelPayload` send the label change as a patch. An edit that changes nothing, or that both gives and removes a field, is refused before sending.
- **Console, Data rooms**: the list asks for `includePersonal`. Each row shows names in this order:
  1. your label, marked "your name for it"
  2. the community's offer label (#334), shown as "community's name: …"
  3. the DID
  
  The community's name and the DID stay visible next to yours. Tags appear on the row, and description and notes in its detail. Each row has a "Your name for this room" form for its own member. The form sends only what changed: values are trimmed, an emptied field is removed, and tags compare as a set. "Forget my label" removes every field. The room's own profile name is not available to the plugin yet. It belongs between your label and the community's name once rooms carry one.
- **Member portals**: the offscreen `held` list asks without `includePersonal` and passes no label to a page. **There is no per-site opt-in**, so a page never receives a label. I left the opt-in out because it was not simple. `rooms/keys/*` is still refused to pages by `page-task-policy` (now tested for `label/0.1` and `list/0.2`).
- Task surface resynced from vta-sdk; coverage goes from 220 to 221.

## Needs
A VTA serving `rooms/keys/list/0.2` and `rooms/keys/label/0.1` (VTI #2167). Per this repo's rule that nothing is deployed, the plugin does not fall back to list 0.1.

## Verified locally
`npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` and every "Assert …" bundle step from ci.yml pass.

## Re-test
1. Load the extension against a VTA running #2167, open Console → Data rooms and expand a room.
2. Fill in NAME and TAGS, then Save. The row shows your name first, with the community's name and the DID still beside it.
3. Clear NAME and Save. Only the name is removed.
4. Open a community's member portal: its room list shows no labels.

title: Interop: receive and verify ES256 SD-JWT VCs from did:web / did:webvh issuers with IETF Token Status List (swiyu, EUDI)
body:
**Summary.** An SD-JWT VC issued on the Swiss swiyu stack or on the EU EUDI profile cannot be received or verified by OpenVTC today. Those profiles use ES256 / P-256, `did:web` or `did:webvh` issuers, holder binding with a P-256 `cnf.jwk`, and the IETF Token Status List (`statuslist+jwt`). This makes the stack unable to take in the credentials that Swiss and EU wallets carry, for example to admit a member on the strength of one.

**What we ran** (at `49f5f1b`, 7 Oct 2026). We used a real IterationSeal credential minted by our own seal library with a throwaway key. It verifies with its embedded public key in our verifier, and the vector is below. We fed it to `vta_vault::receive::receive_sd_jwt_vc` in a local test:

| Case | Result |
| :- | :- |
| As issued: `iss` = `did:web:validant.ai`, `alg` = ES256 | `` Validation("issuer `iss` (did:web:validant.ai) is not a resolvable did:key: Decoding error: Expected 'did:key:' prefix") `` |
| `iss` swapped to an Ed25519 `did:key` (header still ES256) | `Validation("issuer signature verification failed: Verification error: unexpected alg (want EdDSA)")` |

**Where the limits are**:
- `vta-vault/src/receive.rs`, lines 93 to 97: `alg` must be `EdDSA`. Around line 183, the issuer must be a `did:key`.
- `vtc-service/src/credentials/vm_resolver.rs`, lines 65 to 90: Ed25519 verification methods only.
- `vtc-service/src/credentials/exchange/jwt.rs`, lines 36 to 45: the `cnf.jwk` must be OKP Ed25519.
- `vta-vault/src/status.rs`: the resolver expects a W3C `BitstringStatusListCredential`, so a `statuslist+jwt` fails.

**Request**:
1. ES256 / P-256 issuer signatures in vault receive and in the VTC verifier, with issuer keys resolved from `did:web` and `did:webvh`.
2. P-256 `cnf.jwk` holder binding.
3. A Token Status List resolver next to the Bitstring one. It must verify the token's signature before decoding, and check that `sub` equals the referenced URI.
4. Later: plain HTTPS OID4VCI/VP bindings, so a swiyu or EUDI wallet can talk to a VTC directly.

We are happy to provide more test vectors and to test a branch. Context: we issue AI fairness assessments as SD-JWT VCs on the swiyu stack, and we are proposing an `assessed` statement predicate for the DTG graph. We would like both expressions of one assessment to be usable inside OpenVTC communities.

title: feat(rooms): show a room's own profile — its name and what it is for — in the console and the member portal
body:
trust-tasks-tf #807: a room's name, description, tags and emoji are sealed inside the room, at a location only a key holder can compute. The wallet asks the member's VTA (`rooms/keys/profile/read/0.1`), which reads the profile from the host as the member, checks that whoever wrote it held `curate` or `admin`, and returns the newest one it accepts, naming any newer one it refused.

**What changed**
- `@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms`:
  - `roomsKeysProfileRead` sends `{roomId, host}` with the member in `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"]`.
  - `roomProfileView` is the only way to read an answer. It keeps text as text (control and bidi characters stripped, bounded by the schema) and turns `rejected` entries with reason noAuthority, timing or revoked into "somebody tried to rename this room".
  - `roomProfileNotices` says that, and `stale`, in words.
  - Task surface resynced (profile/read, profile/write); coverage 220 → 221.
- Member portal room views and share prompt:
  - `RoomPageGates.displayNames` lays each room's profile over the community's offer label. The profile name wins (`labelSource: "profile"`), and `description`, `profileStale` and `renameRefused` reach the page view.
  - A new offscreen op, `roomProfiles`, reads profiles as the member each room is held as; one failing room only loses its own name.
  - Profiles stay in memory, read at most once a minute per room and member, and are never written to `chrome.storage`.
- Console:
  - The rooms list shows the profile name (with its emoji), description and tags, and the rename/stale notices. This works for rooms whose community the wallet knows (`rememberedRoomHosts`).
  - Under any row, once its host is named, `RoomProfileAt` shows the profile or says the room has no name the member can read.
  - Display order is: the member's own label (#806, when it lands) > profile name > offer label > DID (`roomDisplayName`).
- A VTA without the task leaves every name as it was.
- `@openvtc/trust-tasks` ^0.26.15 (the rooms/keys/profile bindings).

**Needs** a VTA serving `rooms/keys/profile/read/0.1`. VTI PR: feat/rooms-profile in verifiable-trust-infrastructure (to follow).

**Checks run locally:** `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (all workspaces green: core 997, extension 1124, plus the other packages).

**Overlaps:** the personal-labels plugin work (#806, not yet opened) slots in first in `roomDisplayName`. Open PR #335 (room offers) touches `room-page-policy.ts`, so a rebase may be needed.

title: chore(deps-dev): Bump @vitejs/plugin-react from 6.1.1 to 6.1.2
body:
Bumps [@vitejs/plugin-react](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/tree/HEAD/packages/plugin-react) from 6.1.1 to 6.1.2.
Release notes

Sourced from @​vitejs/plugin-react's releases.

plugin-react@6.1.2

Fix HMR for compound components (#1484)

Adding or removing a component from a compound component was not handled, creating stale updates. Doing this now triggers hmr invalidate on the file and propagates the invalidation to importers.

Fix compiler.logDiagnostics option not working (#1483)

With oxc-transform-react >= 0.148, the logDiagnostics was not working. This version fixes it and requires oxc-transform-react >= 0.152 as a peer dependency if you are using the compiler option. compiler.logDiagnostics option is now deprecated and should be swapped for the builtin compiler.reportDiagnostics.

Disable refresh for non-jsx with compiler enabled (fix #1478) (#1485)

When the compiler was enabled, TS files could trigger fast refresh which would cause runtime errors. The logic now follows what the builtin oxc plugin in Vite does.

Changelog

Sourced from @​vitejs/plugin-react's changelog.

6.1.2 (2026-10-05)

Fix HMR for compound components (#1484)

title: feat(rooms): see and accept a community's room offers from the wallet
body:
A member took up a community's offer of one of its rooms only with `pnm rooms offers list|accept`. The wallet now does the same, step for step (VTI `vta-cli-common::commands::rooms::cmd_rooms_offers_{list,accept}`), from the console's **Data rooms → Offers** section and from the community's own member portal.

## What it does

- **Core** (`@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms`, `rooms/offer-accept.ts`): `acceptCommunityRoomOffer`. It stores the offer's membership and authority credentials in the VTA vault (`vault/credentials/receive`). On a sealed tier the **VTA** mints a KeyPackage against the offer's invitation (`rooms/keys/key-package`). The acceptance is built unsigned, completed by the VTA as the member (`rooms/keys/act/0.3`) and sent to the community unchanged over its `TrustTaskHTTPS`. Then it joins from the Welcome (`rooms/keys/welcome`).
- **A lost answer retries with the SAME KeyPackage.** The KeyPackage is journaled (IndexedDB) **before** the acceptance leaves, and every later attempt sends that one, so the community answers with the same Welcome (accept 0.1 "Repeating an accept"; group/add 0.2 item 8). That covers a timeout, a closed console and a torn-down offscreen document. An `alreadyJoined` from welcome counts as done. A `keyPackageNotHeld` drops the journal so the next attempt mints. A row whose accept is still in progress shows **Finish accepting**.
- **Who is asked comes from the wallet's own sign-in record.** Each `didSelfIssued` entry's (community, identity) pair is asked, and never the community's own DID. The community's endpoint is resolved from its DID document, never guessed. Nothing is read from a community the wallet may not reach yet: the console has an *Allow* button. One community's offers to one identity are read at most once a minute, and the console polls every 5 minutes while it is open.
- **Every accept is confirmed in the wallet's own window** (`confirm.html?kind=room`, `offer` view). The window names the community, the room (with its label marked as the community's), the identity it joins as and what accepting does. There is no "remember" option.
- **Portal (P7b):** `window.vtaWallet.rooms.offers({hostDid})` and `.acceptOffer({hostDid, roomId, member?})`.
  - Both go through the same gates as the other room methods: the page must be the community whose verified `SignInPortal` it is, and only identities the member uses there are offered.
  - The page gets views only. It never sees an offer's credentials, a KeyPackage or a Welcome.
  - `page-task-policy` now refuses `vtc/rooms/offers/*`, so a page cannot get the wallet to sign or request one through the generic prompt.
- **Errors carry stable codes** (`RoomOfferError.code`, R3.7) and say how to fix them:
  - A VTA without act 0.3 gets "must be updated".
  - A capability refusal (`room-present` / `vault-write`) prints `pnm acl update <wallet DID> --capabilities-all`.
  - `admissionPending` and `noAnswer` are retryable, and the message says the same key package will be sent.
- **Badge:** when no approval is waiting, the badge shows open offers in blue. Approvals still take precedence, in red.
- There is no **Decline** button, because no specification task declines an offer.

The offer and KeyPackage task URIs are bundled only into the offscreen chunk. The background imports no `rooms/*` task. All CI bundle guards pass locally.

## Deploy / dependencies

- Needs a VTA serving `rooms/keys/act/0.3` (VTI #2148). Against an older VTA, Offers says the agent must be updated.
- Needs a community serving `vtc/rooms/offers/*`.
- The portal card is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2165. It only appears once a wallet has these methods, so the two PRs can merge in either order.

## Re-test

1. Have a community offer a room to the identity you sign in to its portal with (`cnm rooms community members add …`, or from the console).
2. Open the wallet console, go to **Data rooms**, and press *Allow* on the community if you are asked. The offer is listed with its label, tier, actions, valid-until date and the "as" identity, and the extension badge shows `1`.
3. Press **Accept**. The wallet window names the community, the room and the identity. Accept it, and the room appears in the list below, joined.
4. To check the lost-answer path, kill the network after you press Accept, or close the console mid-accept. The row shows *Finish accepting*. Pressing it sends the same KeyPackage (the core tests pin this), and the community answers with the same Welcome.
5. Portal: on the member portal's Data rooms page, *Offers from this community* lists the offer, and *Accept…* opens the same wallet window. Calling `vtaWallet.rooms.offers` from any other origin is refused.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new bare fetch; the community channel is `RoomHostChannel` (guarded and timed) (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). The KeyPackage is journaled before the acceptance is sent. Credentials are stored by id, so repeats replace them.
- [x] Every retry is bounded and backed off, and non-idempotent operations are not blind-retried (R1.4). Nothing here retries on its own: the member retries, with the same KeyPackage.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). The poll records a failure for each identity and goes on.
- [x] Acks and deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). The journal is dropped only after the join.
- [x] New wire types use the generated `@openvtc/trust-tasks` bindings; page views are camelCase (R3.*)
- [x] Config absence means the most restrictive behaviour (R5.*): no sign-in entries means nobody is asked, and no host permission means nothing is read.
- [x] Logs and status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" is answered for every mutation (R2.1)
- [x] No deviations from the guide

title: Witness credentials are reasoned about but never built or verified
body:
## Summary

The ceremony engine treats `WitnessCredential` as a policy fact — with
trusted-issuer, validity and holder-binding predicates — but no VWC is ever
constructed or verified anywhere in the stack. `DTGCredential::new_vwc` and
`digest_multibase` are never called.

## Detail

`WitnessCredential` occurs in `ceremony/verify.rs`, `ceremony/facts.rs`,
`ceremony/evaluate.rs`, `routes/ceremonies.rs` and `policy/default.rs` — in
every case as a `credential_type` string in a fact the policy reasons over, not
as a credential the code builds or checks.

The exacting part is therefore entirely untested here. Per DTG Credentials the
VWC's `credentialSubject.digest` MUST be:

- the SHA-256 hash of the witnessed VRC,
- canonicalised with JCS (RFC 8785),
- encoded as a Multibase-encoded Multihash,
- `sha2-256` (header `0x12`, length `0x20`), base58btc (`z` prefix).

And Security Considerations 4 requires a verifier relying on that binding to
have the referenced VRC in hand, recompute the hash, and compare **decoded
digest bytes rather than encoded strings**.

`dtg-credentials` implements all of this correctly (`DTGCredential::digest`,
`digest_multibase`), including the recent multibase change. Nothing calls it.

## Why it matters

A ceremony can currently reach a decision on the *assertion* that a witness
credential was present, without any code path that could have established it
was valid or that it witnessed the edge in question. Security Considerations 4
is explicit that without recomputing the digest against the referenced VRC, a
VWC "should not be treated as evidence of which edge was witnessed".

## Suggested fix

1. Build VWCs through `new_vwc` on whatever path is meant to issue them.
2. On receipt, recompute the digest against the referenced VRC and compare
   decoded bytes.
3. `taskContext` is REQUIRED on the VWC specifically — see #1065, which is a
   prerequisite rather than a parallel task.

Conformance audit finding **F8**.

title: security(deps): ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0367/0368/0369 (zip extract) — nitro_attest's build script never extracts
body:
cargo-deny is red on every branch since three zip advisories (published 2026-10-09) landed in the advisory DB. Every CI job behind it is skipped, which includes Clippy and both test jobs.

**Why ignoring them is safe:**
- `zip` 2.4.2 is only a **build-dependency** of `nitro_attest` 0.2.0, which is a vta-sdk dev-dependency under the `builder` feature.
- Its build script checks the bundled AWS Nitro root-certificate archive against a pinned SHA-256, then reads `root.pem` with `ZipArchive::by_name`. It never calls `extract()` and writes no file from the archive.
- All three advisories are about `extract()`.
- `nitro_attest` 0.2.0 is its latest release and requires `zip ^2.2`, while the fix is in `zip` >= 9. So there is no upgrade path.

Each ignore records why it is safe and when to drop it.

Found while CI on #2167 was skipped behind it. #2167 carries the same commit so its suite can run; whichever merges second drops it on rebase.

Verified: `cargo deny check` reports advisories, bans, licenses and sources all ok.

Updates `wrangler` from 4.148.0 to 4.150.0
Release notes

Sourced from wrangler's releases.

wrangler@4.150.0

Minor Changes

  • #16231 091e5ec Thanks @​WalshyDev! - Upload source maps by default for wrangler deploy, wrangler versions upload and wrangler preview

    When upload_source_maps isn't set in config or via --upload-source-maps, Wrangler now generates and uploads source maps so stack traces in logs and wrangler tail point at your original source without extra setup. In this default mode, source maps that can't be resolved (for example inline data: maps or missing .map files from a custom build) are skipped rather than failing the upload. Setting upload_source_maps = true keeps the existing strict behaviour, and upload_source_maps = false (or --no-upload-source-maps for deploy and versions upload) opts out.

    wrangler build --experimental-cf-build-output is unchanged and still only includes source maps when upload_source_maps = true.

  • #16128 daae435 Thanks @​redsteadz! - Stop wrangler deploy, wrangler versions upload and wrangler preview in projects that build for the Cloudflare CLI (cf)

    If your project builds through cf, deploying it with Wrangler reads a different configuration, so it could update the wrong Worker or fail without explaining why. These commands now stop before uploading anything, name the .cloudflare/output directory they found, and tell you to run cf deploy instead. If that directory is just left over from an earlier build, deleting it restores the Wrangler workflow.

    Ordinary Wrangler projects are unaffected, and --dry-run still works on deploy and versions upload. This is a new guard for the experimental Build Output Specification rather than a fix, and it gives three stable commands a failure mode they did not have before, so it is a minor.

Patch Changes

  • #16161 fcf625d Thanks @​dario-piotrowicz! - Clarify the Worker not found error during CI deploy validation

    Wrangler now reports that the configured Worker could not be found in the account instead of incorrectly describing the failure as a name mismatch.

  • #16156 18f061c Thanks @​armancharan! - Ignore .wrangler writes in the dev assets watcher

    wrangler dev reloaded in a loop when assets.directory was the project root, because the assets watcher treated wrangler's own writes under .wrangler as asset changes and dropped in-flight requests. The watcher now ignores the project's .wrangler directory and dev.persist, except when that path is the assets directory.

  • #16025 61e07fd Thanks @​kohjunhao! - Fix optional Docker lookups printing Docker CLI errors during successful builds

    cf build looks for Container images left behind by earlier builds so it can remove them. This lookup is best effort, but when Docker could not be reached it still printed errors such as Cannot connect to the Docker daemon, even when the build succeeded and no image needed Docker. Docker commands whose output Wrangler reads no longer forward the Docker CLI's error output to the terminal. If one of these commands fails in a way that stops the command, the error message still includes the Docker CLI's output.

  • #16151 cafd3f9 Thanks @​DevVettel! - Time out the OAuth token request instead of waiting indefinitely

    The request that exchanges an authorization code or refresh token for an access token had no timeout, so a stalled connection (for example behind an HTTP proxy) could leave wrangler login hanging silently for many minutes after the browser step had succeeded. The request now gives up after 30 seconds and reports that the Cloudflare auth server could not be reached.

  • #15517 ea64ec4 Thanks @​xgame92! - Preserve binding options when provisioning resources through a redirected config

    Wrangler now writes provisioned resource identifiers to both the redirected and original config files without copying other binding options between them. This prevents generated relative paths such as D1 migrations_dir from replacing user-authored paths during Vite deployments.

  • #16219 d232454 Thanks @​petebacondarwin! - Honor X-Forwarded-Proto for incoming development requests behind TLS-terminating proxies

    Miniflare now uses the original client protocol when constructing URLs for network requests. This also prevents Wrangler from downgrading HTTPS URLs in response headers such as Location and WWW-Authenticate when a tunnel forwards requests over HTTP. Explicit programmatic request URLs and configured upstream origins remain authoritative.

  • Updated dependencies [5152bf8, 9f87de8, 9be5ec7, d232454]:

    • miniflare@5.20261006.2-beta

wrangler@4.149.0

Minor Changes

  • #16036 9a58244 Thanks @​edevil! - Support temporary event accounts in R2 and Containers commands

    wrangler r2 and wrangler containers commands now accept the hidden --temporary flag, so accounts created for an event can manage buckets, objects and containers directly. Every command that supports --temporary now also accepts a hidden --event-code flag, so the first command a participant runs can create the event account:

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.14
body:
### Added

- **rooms/keys/profile**: A room's own profile — name and description sealed inside the room, readable only by its members ([#807](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/807))

A member holding keys to many rooms saw a DID per room: nothing a member
  could read said what a room was, and the community's label for a room it
  owns reached only administrators and members it was offered to.

  - rooms/_shared/0.1: RoomProfile (name required ≤128, description ≤1000,
    tags ≤8, one emoji, ext) and RoomProfileStatement — the profile as a
    SealedRecordBody's new `roomProfile` member, signed by its author, with
    the author's authority chain and issuedAt. One record per epoch at
    profile_key(E) = HKDF(storage_key(E), "openvtc/room/profile/v1" ||
    roomId || u64be(E)) — 22 chars, indistinguishable from a random key, so
    the host cannot tell which record names the room; fixed key
    `room-profile` on open rooms. Readers accept only a chain conferring
    curate or admin, valid at issuedAt, issuedAt within the host's
    updatedAt window, not revoked at or before issuedAt; newest accepted
    epoch wins; a retraction (curate-gated at the host) clears it.
    Revocation is not retroactive.
  - rooms/keys/profile/read 0.1 (new): the member's key holder derives the
    location, walks epochs down, fetches as the member, verifies, and
    answers found/absent/cleared with stale, searched and rejected.
  - rooms/keys/profile/write 0.1 (new): the key holder signs as the member,
    embeds the chain, pads, seals under the current epoch and puts; clear
    retracts. Carries the rule that a key holder advancing an epoch
    re-writes the profile under the new one (fromJoin members can read it).
  - vtc/rooms/community/create 0.3, update 0.2: the community's VTA writes
    label/description (never tags) as the room's profile; the community's
    own authority confers admin, write and curate; response `roomProfile`.
  - Editorial pointers in rooms/owner/group/{add 0.2, remove 0.2, renew
    0.1}; vtc/_shared RoomLabel/RoomDescription say where they now go.
  - Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

- **rooms/keys/label**: A member's own private name, description, notes and tags for a room they hold ([#806](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/806))

A member holding several rooms could tell them apart only by names other
  parties gave them — the room's own profile, a community's offer label — or
  by their DIDs. Nothing let a member keep their own name for a room, and a
  person holding one room as two personas could not even tell the two
  rooms/keys/list entries apart (implementations carried the member in ext).

  - rooms/keys/label 0.1 (new): set, change or remove the member's personal
    label for one room — label (one line, 128), description (1000), notes
    (4000), tags (1–16 × 32) — kept by their key holder, keyed by room AND
    member, never sent to the room, its host, its owner or a community, never
    logged. Patch semantics (each detail given replaces, absent unchanged,
    removeX removes one), idempotent (changed: false on a repeat), no
    precondition. notHeld answers both "no group state" and "not a member you
    act as". Delegates refused. Kept and backed up with the group state for
    that room and member, discarded with it, and not on removal from the room.
  - rooms/keys/list 0.2: each entry names its `member` (one entry per room
    and member, for the members the caller may act as); `includePersonal`
    (off by default) returns each entry's `personal` label. A consumer sends
    a label nowhere but to the member; a wallet does not hand one to a
    website unless the member chose to.
  - rooms/_shared/0.1/personal-label (new): PersonalLabel and its details.

  Informative display precedence: personal label, then the room's own
  profile name, then the community's offer label, then the DID.

- **vtc/rooms/community**: Update — administrators name, describe and tag the rooms the community owns ([#805](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/805))

A community could name a room it owns only once, at create, with no
  description, and nothing could change it afterwards — so neither its
  administrators nor the members it offers a room to could tell what each
  room was for.

  - vtc/rooms/community/update 0.1 (new): change a community-owned room's
    label, description (or removeDescription) and tags. vtc.rooms.manage;
    proof and issuedAt REQUIRED; reason audited with each changed detail's
    previous and new value; same values answer changed: false and write
    nothing; notFound for a room the community only hosts. Designed for
    no operation-bound step-up: it reaches no key holder and confers
    nothing.
  - vtc/rooms/community/create 0.2: optional description and tags.
  - vtc/rooms/community/get 0.2, list 0.2: CommunityRoomV2 — description,
    tags, detailsUpdatedAt/detailsUpdatedBy; list filters by tag.
  - vtc/rooms/offers/list 0.2: OfferV2 carries the room's current
    description (never its tags).
  - vtc/_shared/0.1/community-room: additive $defs RoomDescription,
    RoomTag, RoomTags, CommunityRoomV2, OfferV2 (the RecordMetadataV2
    pattern), so every 0.1 task keeps its published shape.

  Details stay the community's owner-side record: never in the host
  record, the room, or anything sent on its host path.

- **rooms**: Revocation — a removal takes effect at the host at once ([#804](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/804))

A room can now withdraw credentials it issued before they expire, and a
  host refuses them from the moment it accepts the withdrawal.

  - rooms/_shared/0.1: RevocationList (room-signed, cumulative, sequenced,
    append-only), RevocationEntry (credential | subject | room, keyed on
    validFrom vs revokedAt so a party can be re-admitted), RevocationHead.
    AuthorityPresentation states that every credential's proof must be made
    by a key of its own issuer, and that a host holding a list refuses any
    chain containing a revoked link, under every task and version.
  - rooms/revocations/put 0.1 (new): an admin delivers the list; the host
    enforces it immediately on every path.
  - rooms/revocations/get 0.1 (new): an admin reads the held list, to
    confirm enforcement or recover a lost list.
  - rooms/owner/revoke 0.1 (new): the owner's key holder signs the next
    list as the room and pushes it to every host — outbound only.
  - rooms/owner/group/remove 0.2: withdraws the member first, then
    advances the group; refuses a private room.
  - vtc/rooms/community/members/remove 0.2: open and attributed rooms
    withdraw the member's credentials (and an open offer's) at the host.
  - Editorial pointers in group/remove 0.1, owner/claim 0.1 and
    vtc/rooms/community/members/remove 0.1.

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.31.13` → `0.31.14` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.31.13` → `0.31.14` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.31.13` → `0.31.14` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.31.13` → `0.31.14` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.31.13` → `0.31.14` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.31.13` → `0.31.14` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.31.13` → `0.31.14` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.31.13` → `0.31.14` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.14` → `0.26.15` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.15`) | `0.8.14` → `0.8.15` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.14` → `0.8.15` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.
