title: feat(witnessing)!: witness tasks 0.2, personhood assert 0.2, member link only on opt-in
body:
VTI #2147 (vta-service 0.62 / vta-sdk 0.70) serves the witness tasks only at **0.2**, and the VTC serves `vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.2` only. The old `ext["org.openvtc.witness"]` carriage is gone, so openvtc's 0.1 calls were answered `unsupportedVersion`, which broke witnessing and personhood. This PR moves openvtc to the 0.2 tasks.

## What changed

- **Witnessing → 0.2.** `vta/witness/{open,present,accept}/0.2`, `witness/session/0.2` and `witness/session/submit/0.2`, including their error codes and the dispatcher/inbound-gate reply types. Every `ext` carriage is removed.
- **Personhood assert → 0.2.** Outcome evidence is the payload's own `outcomeEvidence` member.
  - It is omitted when empty (`minItems: 1`) and refused locally above 16 (`maxItems`), never trimmed.
  - The payload is read against the generated `assert::v0_2::Payload` before it is sent.
  - The disclosure rule is unchanged: only the witness credentials the user selects are presented, and nothing by default.
- **The member link is opt-in, one witnessing at a time.**
  - Why: `witness/session/submit/0.2` (*The member presentation*) says a party **MUST** carry `memberPresentation` only when it intends the witness to learn the member DID, and **SHOULD** do so only for a witness whose policy asks for membership evidence. `vta/witness/open/0.2`'s `membership` field is that opt-in. VTA 0.62 dropped `member_link_witnesses`, so the client is now the only gate. It also follows the user's standing rule: present only what the user selects.
  - How: the witness prompt has *"Also present my community membership"*, toggled with **Tab**. It is off every time the prompt opens and is never remembered. When it is on, the prompt says plainly that the witness will learn which community member is behind this relationship. When it is off, no `membership` is sent, so there is no membership credential and no `memberPresentation`.
- **Rebuilding a lost witnessing record (`vta/witness/list/0.1`).**
  - At load, after the app-state sync, openvtc reads every page of the VTA's stored VWCs. It restarts once on `cursorInvalid` and stops after 100 pages.
  - It rebuilds any witnessing the VTA holds a VWC for that this device never kept (a crash between `accept` and the save), using the stored evidence exactly as listed.
  - Only relationships the account still holds are rebuilt, matched by `our_did` plus the session's `parties`. A removed relationship's witnessings stay forgotten.
  - Nothing is presented as a result. Rebuilt records only reappear as choices in the picker, which starts empty.
  - `SyncReport` gains `recovered_witnessings`.
- **Dependencies:** vta-sdk 0.70, trust-tasks-rs 0.31.12, did-git-sign 0.22, vgi-core 0.22, and dev-dependencies vta-service 0.62 and vti-vetting-pcs 0.3. The graph has one vta-sdk, one vti-common and one trust-tasks-rs.

**Breaking (openvtc-core API):** `assert_personhood` takes `outcome_evidence: Vec<Value>` instead of `ext`. `witness::personhood_ext` and `WITNESS_EXT` are replaced by `personhood_evidence`. `SyncReport` has a new field. `WitnessRequest.membership` is documented as the opt-in.

## Tests

- e2e against MockVta (`--include-ignored`):
  - the 0.2 round;
  - the witness refusal;
  - the member link with an explicit opt-in, carried in `memberPresentation` and never in `ext`;
  - **the default sends no membership and no member presentation**;
  - **list-based reconciliation**: the rebuilt record equals what `accept` returned, it is rebuilt only once, nothing is presented, and a removed relationship is not rebuilt;
  - **a relationship that uses the persona DID itself**, which was a known gap.
- Unit tests:
  - selected-only evidence;
  - the rebuild rules and matching by parties;
  - the assert payload shape and the 16-entry cap;
  - membership is off when the prompt opens and is never remembered;
  - `prepare` sends no membership unless it is chosen;
  - the prompt wording.
- Local: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `--no-default-features`, dev-overrides clippy and tests, and `cargo doc` are all green.

title: ci(release): pin release-plz to 0.3.171 in the Release PR job
body:
## Problem

Every push to `main` since #804 fails **Release PR** (`scripts/release-pr.sh` → `release-plz update`):

```
ERROR failed to determine next versions
  0: error while building changelog
  1: Template parse error:
 --> 1:1
  |
1 | # Changelog
  | ^---
  = stack limit reached
```

so no release can be cut (runs 38940602141, 38944076398, 38971273995, 38972100560).

## Root cause

Not the repo. `taiki-e/install-action` moved from release-plz **0.3.171** to **0.3.172** between the 15:32 run (0.3.171, built changelogs fine) and the 16:11 run on 2026-10-16. The 16:11 run was the #803 release merge: nothing to release, so it never rendered a changelog — it looked green only for that reason.

0.3.172 is the first release-plz on pest **2.9.3**, which added a native-stack guard (pest-parser/pest#1212): a parse fails with "stack limit reached" when `stacker::remaining_stack()` reports under 64 KiB. install-action installs the static **`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`** build, and on musl `stacker` measures the main thread's stack via `pthread_getattr_np`, which reports only the part mapped so far (~128 KiB), so the guard trips on the first byte of the Tera header template. This is rust-lang/stacker#155 (open).

Evidence (Docker, `rust:1.95`, on `main` 4e5d281):

| binary | result |
|---|---|
| 0.3.172 `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` | fails exactly as CI (also with `ulimit -s unlimited`, `RUST_MIN_STACK=64MiB`) |
| 0.3.172 `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` | ok — 0.31.14 bumps |
| 0.3.171 `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` | ok — 0.31.14 bumps, changelogs for #804–#807 |
| 0.3.172 on macOS | ok |

## Fix

Pin the Release PR job's install to `release-plz@0.3.171` (still installed and checksum-verified by install-action), with a comment saying why and when to unpin. The publish job is unaffected — `release-plz/action@v0.5.131` installs its own pinned 0.3.160.

## After merge

The merge itself is a push to `main`, so the Release PR job re-runs and should open the 0.31.14 Release PR.

title: fix(vtc-admin-ui): the rooms usage page asks from the community's oldest retained day
body:
The Usage tab (and a room's Activity and Members' usage cards) sent a fixed
30/90/365-day window ending today. `vtc/rooms/usage/0.1` item 2 requires the
community to refuse `invalidRange` for a range starting before its oldest
retained day, and that day is the first day any file activity was recorded
(`meta:first-day`, written by the first upload). So from a community's first
upload on, every window longer than its file history was refused, and the page
rendered the refusal as "Usage could not be read. This is a failure to ask,
not a community with none." Before the first upload there is no oldest day,
nothing was refused, and the page worked — which is why it broke as soon as
file uploads started working.

The server is conformant and is unchanged. `fetchUsage` now reads the
refusal's `details.earliest` and asks the same query once more from that day
when it lies inside the requested range; the report carries
`historyStartsAt`, and the page says "This community has kept usage since
<day>, so the report starts there." Any other refusal is passed on.

The usage reads' error branches now render the shared rooms `RefusalCard`
(message + code) instead of a fixed sentence, so the next failure explains
itself.

A new integration test sends the console's exact payloads — every grouping x
30/90/365 days x every sort, over open/attributed/private rooms, a
community-owned room and a room that has held nothing — on a history that
began today: each is refused `invalidRange` with `details.earliest` = today,
and each is answered when re-asked from that day.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3245 passed

title: fix(vtc-admin-ui): the rooms usage page asks from the community's oldest retained day (#2166)
body:
fix(vtc-admin-ui): the rooms usage page asks from the community's oldest retained day (#2166)

The Usage tab (and a room's Activity and Members' usage cards) sent a fixed
30/90/365-day window ending today. `vtc/rooms/usage/0.1` item 2 requires the
community to refuse `invalidRange` for a range starting before its oldest
retained day, and that day is the first day any file activity was recorded
(`meta:first-day`, written by the first upload). So from a community's first
upload on, every window longer than its file history was refused, and the page
rendered the refusal as "Usage could not be read. This is a failure to ask,
not a community with none." Before the first upload there is no oldest day,
nothing was refused, and the page worked — which is why it broke as soon as
file uploads started working.

The server is conformant and is unchanged. `fetchUsage` now reads the
refusal's `details.earliest` and asks the same query once more from that day
when it lies inside the requested range; the report carries
`historyStartsAt`, and the page says "This community has kept usage since
<day>, so the report starts there." Any other refusal is passed on.

The usage reads' error branches now render the shared rooms `RefusalCard`
(message + code) instead of a fixed sentence, so the next failure explains
itself.

A new integration test sends the console's exact payloads — every grouping x
30/90/365 days x every sort, over open/attributed/private rooms, a
community-owned room and a room that has held nothing — on a history that
began today: each is refused `invalidRange` with `details.earliest` = today,
and each is answered when re-asked from that day.

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): show a community's room offers in the member portal, accepted through the wallet
body:
Until now a member could take up a community's offer of one of its rooms only with `pnm rooms offers accept`. The member portal's Data rooms page now has an **Offers from this community** card. For each offer it shows the label, tier, actions, valid-until date and the identity the offer is addressed to ("as you" when that is the signed-in member).

- The card reads offers through the member's wallet (`window.vtaWallet.rooms.offers`). **Accept…** asks the wallet (`rooms.acceptOffer`), and the member decides in the wallet's own window.
- The wallet does the rest:
  - stores the offer's credentials in the member's VTA
  - has the VTA mint the KeyPackage
  - accepts as the member (`rooms/keys/act/0.3`)
  - joins from the Welcome
- None of it crosses to the page, and no `/v1/member/*` route carries any of it (data-rooms-files §8.5, which gains an *Offers* paragraph).
- After an accept, the card offers to share the room with this portal (`choose` with `suggest`).
- The card shows only with a wallet that has these methods, and only when an offer is waiting.
- If the member declines in the wallet, the card says "the offer stays open" rather than showing an error.
- If the wallet is not yet allowed to reach the community, the card says where to allow it.

Pairs with OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#335, which adds the wallet methods. The two can deploy in either order: without the wallet change the card simply does not appear.

## Checks run locally
- `npm run wire:check`, `npx tsc -b --noEmit`, `npx vitest run` (94 files, 1118 tests), `npm run build`, `npm run build:members`.
- No Rust was touched.

## Re-test
1. Install the wallet from vta-browser-plugin#335 and sign in to the portal.
2. Have the community offer a room to that identity.
3. Data rooms → *Offers from this community* → **Accept…** → confirm in the wallet window → *Joined …* → **Share it here…**.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). This PR adds no network calls; the page only talks to the wallet.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1). The page keeps no state beyond its query cache.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). Accept is never retried automatically.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). Not applicable: there are none.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). Not applicable.
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none. The page-facing types restate the wallet's views.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): with no wallet support the card does not appear.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered (R2.1)
- [x] No deviations from the guide

title: feat(rooms/keys/profile): a room's own profile — name and description sealed inside the room, readable only by its members
body:
## What

A room's own **profile** — name, optional description, tags and one emoji — that lives **inside the room**, sealed on `attributed`/`private` like every record, readable by every member (including later joiners and `fromJoin` rooms) and never by the host on a sealed tier.

| Spec | Version | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `rooms/_shared` | 0.1 (in place, draft, as #804) | `RoomProfile`, `RoomProfileStatement`; `SealedRecordBody.roomProfile` |
| `rooms/keys/profile/read` | **0.1 new** | key holder finds, fetches, verifies, returns newest accepted profile |
| `rooms/keys/profile/write` | **0.1 new** | key holder signs as member, seals, puts; clear = retract; epoch-advance re-write rule |
| `vtc/rooms/community/create` | **0.3** | VTA writes label/description as the profile; community authority = admin+write+curate; `roomProfile` in response |
| `vtc/rooms/community/update` | **0.2** | re-writes the profile when label/description change; `roomProfile` in response |
| `rooms/owner/group/{add 0.2, remove 0.2, renew 0.1}` | editorial | non-normative pointer to the re-write rule |
| `vtc/_shared` 0.1 | editorial | `RoomLabel`/`RoomDescription` say where they now go |

## Design, and the alternatives

**Location: a per-epoch derived key, not a well-known one.** `profile_key(E) = base64url(HKDF-SHA256(storage_key(E), info="openvtc/room/profile/v1"‖roomId‖u64be(E))[0..16])` — 22 characters, the shape of any random key, so the family's "sealed keys MUST be opaque" rule holds and the host cannot tell which record names the room. A new member finds it knowing only the room and the epoch. Open rooms (no storage key, nothing hidden) use the fixed key `room-profile`, with the signed body as `cleartext.body`.
- *Rejected — fixed key `profile` with existing `records/put` + `keys/read`:* tells the host which record is the room's name, when it changes, who changed it (attributed), its rough length, and makes withholding/rolling back the name a one-line policy. Violates the opaque-key MUST.
- *Rejected — random key, found by opening every record:* linear cost for every new member.
- *Rejected — in credentials, the host record, `rooms/owner/register`:* all host-visible; register explicitly forbids a name.
- *Rejected — signed by the room DID:* every change needs the room key, curators excluded, and on `attributed` the host records the presenting member as author, contradicting a room-signed body.

**Why two new tasks (`rooms/keys/profile/read|write`) rather than none.** On a sealed tier the location is derived from the storage key, which never leaves the key holder — so a client cannot even find the record without the key holder. And the profile's authorization is a chain check readers must do (below), which belongs with the keys, not in a wallet or portal page. One call each instead of a key-disclosure call + read + client-side chain verification.

**Who may write.** A host stores the record under `write` (it cannot tell the profile apart), so **readers** decide: the statement carries the author's authority chain, and readers MUST verify it (≤8 links, issuer-signed links, rooted in the room, no widening, leaf = `author`) confers **`curate` or `admin`**, valid at the signed `issuedAt`, with `issuedAt` within [updatedAt − 1h, updatedAt + 5m] of the host's record, plus the `SealedRecordBody` author-signature/location/attributed-author rules. A profile failing any check is ignored and reported (`rejected`), so a member with only `write` can overwrite the record but cannot rename the room.

**Which one is authoritative.** One record per key ⇒ one per epoch; the reader walks from its current epoch down and takes the **newest accepted**; a `retracted` record (curate-gated at the host) means deliberately cleared and stops the walk.

**Revocation (#804).** Not retroactive: a profile written while its author held the standing stays valid after removal/lapse/room reset. Backdating needs host collusion (the `updatedAt` window), a revoked party cannot write at all, and removal advances the epoch, after which the owner re-writes the profile anyway. A reader holding a `RevocationList` refuses a profile whose chain was revoked at or before `issuedAt`.

**Epochs / `fromJoin`.** A key holder that advances a sealed room's epoch (add/remove/renew, any version) SHOULD read the profile **before** the advance (a `fromJoin` holder can't open it after) and re-write it under the new epoch afterwards, as its principal; never failing or rolling back the advance; never retracting the earlier one (history; retracting would link the two for the host). Readers without one get `absent`/`stale` and fall back to the offer label.

**Community-owned rooms.** create 0.3 / update 0.2 relax item 8 exactly: label → `name`, description → `description` go to the community's own VTA in `rooms/keys/profile/write` and into the room sealed; still never the host record, credentials, register; **tags never** (admin filing). Profile-write failure doesn't fail the task (`roomProfile: pending`, retried). Rooms made with create ≤0.2 get their profile on the first update 0.2, after re-issuing the community authority with `write`+`curate`.

**Privacy.** Padding to 1 KiB multiples; emoji is text, never a fetched icon/URL (would be a tracking pixel per member). Residual leak: a host can *guess* the profile from pattern (owner writes one right after each advance) but cannot read it and can do nothing to it it couldn't do to any record. Readers render as plain text, never instructions.

## Implementation follow-ups (VTI)
- **VTA** (`vta-service`): serve `rooms/keys/profile/read` + `write` (HKDF location, chain embed + verify, padding, version-race retry → `contended`); the epoch-advance re-write in group/add, remove, renew; accept `roomProfile` in sealed bodies and hide profile records from `keys/read`/`browse` surfaces; classify both tasks in `vta_sdk::retry_safety`.
- **VTC** (`vtc-service`): create 0.3 / update 0.2 — community authority admin+write+curate, profile write via its VTA, `roomProfile` status, pending retry; first-update profile for older rooms.
- **vtc-client / pnm / cnm**: SDK methods for both tasks; `pnm rooms profile {show,set,clear}`; show room names in listings.
- **Browser plugin / portal**: show the profile in room lists via the wallet, render as text, surface `rejected` (somebody tried to rename the room) and `stale`.

## Checks run locally
`npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings` (all four languages agree), Rust conformance tests for the new/changed specs (87 passed), `go build`/`vet`, `tsc`, `dart analyze`, `cargo fmt --check`.

title: feat(rooms/keys/label): a member's own private name, description, notes and tags for a room they hold
body:
## Problem

A member holding several data rooms can tell them apart only by names other parties gave them: the room's own profile, which is drafted separately on `spec/room-profile` (a sealed in-room record that curators write and members read), or the label on a community's offer. Failing those, they have the DID. Those names belong to whoever wrote them. They may be missing or generic, or written for an audience the member is not part of. Nothing let a member keep **their own** name for a room.

A second problem sits next to it. `rooms/keys/list` 0.1 has no member field. A person who holds one room as two personas (their own place, and a seat they hold for an organisation) gets two entries with nothing to say whose each one is. VTI carries the member in `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].held` to cope (VTI #2161), and that PR noted a spec field as the follow-up.

## Change

- **`rooms/keys/label` 0.1 (new):** sets, changes or removes the member's **personal label** for one room they hold, with these fields:
  - `label`: one line, up to 128 characters
  - `description`: up to 1000 characters
  - `notes`: up to 4000 characters
  - `tags`: 1 to 16 tags, each up to 32 characters, in any script

  Rules:
  - The label is kept by the member's key holder and keyed by **room and member**, so each persona has its own.
  - It is plain text. Line breaks are allowed only in `description` and `notes`, and no other control characters are allowed anywhere.
  - Proof and `issuedAt` are REQUIRED. The task is `mutating`, ingests `personal` data, and is retained `durable`.
- **`rooms/keys/list` 0.2:**
  - Each entry names its `member` (REQUIRED), giving one entry per room and member.
  - Entries cover only the members the caller may act as, and this is now normative.
  - A new `includePersonal` flag, off by default, returns an optional `personal` object on each entry.
- **`rooms/_shared/0.1/personal-label` (new):** `PersonalLabel` and the types for each field.
- Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

The two specs stay distinct from the room profile. A **profile** is one room's name for itself: curators write it and every member reads it. A **personal label** is one member's name for one room: that member writes it and nobody else ever sees it.

## Design decisions and the alternatives

**Where the label lives: the member's key holder (VTA), next to the group state for (room, member).**
- *In the room*, as a profile field: shared with every member, which is the opposite of what is wanted. That is the other PR's job.
- *At the community*, as part of the offer label: it would tell the community what the member thinks of its room, and the community has no reason to know.
- *In the vault (`vault/upsert`)*: vault entries are context-scoped secrets with `targets`, not keyed by room and member. Their lifecycle would not follow the room's state, and storing a name as a secret would be misleading.
- *Client-local storage (wallet or extension)*: not shared across a member's devices and clients (pnm, wallet, mobile), and not backed up. The VTA already holds per-room, per-member state and is the member's custodian.

**How it is read: inside `rooms/keys/list` 0.2, not a separate get/list.** Every screen that shows rooms already calls `list`. Putting the label on the entry gives a client one round trip and no ID join, and rooms are bounded by how many a person is in, so the response stays small. A separate `label/get` plus `label/list` would add two tasks and a join for no extra capability. `includePersonal` is **off by default** so that a caller that does not need labels, or will pass the list on (a wallet answering a portal), never receives them. That matches the rule that absence means the most restrictive reading. Adding `member` to the entry is part of the same bump: a label keyed by (room, member) cannot be written back without it, and it standardises VTI's `ext` stop-gap.

**How it is written: one task, `rooms/keys/label`, with patch semantics.**
- Each field given replaces the stored value, an absent field is unchanged, and `removeLabel`, `removeDescription`, `removeNotes` and `removeTags` each remove one field. This follows the `const: true` pattern of `vtc/rooms/community/update` 0.1. A nullable field cannot distinguish "unchanged" from "remove" in libraries that map both to `None`. `dependentSchemas` forbids giving a field and removing it in the same request.
- Removing the last field removes the label. There is no empty label, so `PersonalLabel` has `minProperties: 2`.
- The slug is `rooms/keys/label` rather than `label/set`: one verb, and there is no `get` to sit beside it.
- *Rejected: full replacement plus a revision precondition.* A revision needs tombstones (the ABA problem after a remove), costs every client a read before every write, and guards against a race between a person and themselves. With patch semantics, renaming a room on a phone does not clobber notes written on a laptop. The spec says "No optimistic concurrency" explicitly.
- *Rejected: `anyOf` for "at least one change".* typify turns a top-level `anyOf` into an untagged enum with `deny_unknown_fields`. That cannot hold a label that has both `label` and `description`, which I checked in the generated Rust. `minProperties` is used instead (counting `roomId`/`member`, or `updatedAt` on the response), as #805 does, and the one gap it leaves (a request whose only extra member is `ext`) is a prose `malformedRequest` (Recipient item 3).

**`member` is REQUIRED on `label`.** It is never inferred. A label written under the wrong persona would be shown in the wrong context, and with list 0.2 the client always has the member at hand. So there is no ambiguity error.

**Authorization.**
- The caller must act as the member, which is the same act-scope question every `rooms/keys/*` task asks.
- Delegates holding a chain from `rooms/keys/present` get `permissionDenied` (mirroring `rooms/keys/act` item 3): a delegate is given narrow authority in one room and does not become the member.
- `notHeld` is one answer for both "no group state for this room as this member" and "not a member you act as". A client scoped to one context therefore cannot learn whether another persona holds the room.

**Privacy.**
- The key holder MUST NOT send a label to the room, host, owner or a community, or put it in anything it completes, signs or seals (`act`, `seal`, `present`). It MUST NOT log the text or write it to an audit record.
- A client that receives a label is bound by the same rule.
- A wallet SHOULD NOT hand a label to a website (for example a member portal) unless the member chose to show it to that site, and SHOULD call `list` without `includePersonal` when answering one.

**Retention.**
- The label is kept, protected and backed up with the group state for that room and member, and discarded when that state is discarded.
- It is **not** discarded when the member is removed from the room, when the room lapses, or when its host or owner changes. A room the member can still open but no longer write in is the one they most need to recognise.
- No history of earlier values is kept.

**Display precedence (informative):** personal label, then the room's profile name, then the community's offer label, then the DID. A surface should keep the room's own name reachable next to a personal one, so a member can see that the room was renamed after they labelled it, and should mark the personal label as "your name for it".

**Retry safety:** `label` is idempotent. A repeated request answers `changed: false`, so it can be retried as it is. `list` is a read.

## Versions touched

- `rooms/keys/label/0.1`: new
- `rooms/keys/list/0.2`: new version; 0.1 unchanged
- `rooms/_shared/0.1/personal-label.schema.json`: new shared file

## What implementers must do (follow-ups, no VTI code in this PR)

- **VTA:**
  - Store the label per (room, member) next to the group state, in a backed-up keyspace, and discard it with that state.
  - Serve `rooms/keys/label/0.1`: act-scope check, `notHeld` with no difference in answer between its two causes, delegate refusal, patch semantics, `changed`, no logging of the text.
  - Serve `rooms/keys/list/0.2` with `member` and `includePersonal`, still answering 0.1. `held[i].member` in `ext` can be retired once clients move to 0.2.
- **SDK (`vta-sdk`):**
  - Typed `rooms_keys_label` and `rooms_keys_list(include_personal)` built on the generated types.
  - Classify `rooms/keys/label` as idempotent in `vta_sdk::retry_safety`.
- **pnm:**
  - `pnm rooms keys label <room> --member <did> [--label …] [--description …] [--notes …] [--tag …] [--remove-…]`.
  - `pnm rooms keys list` shows the personal label, and the member, per entry.
- **Browser plugin (wallet):**
  - Show and edit personal labels in the rooms view, preferring them as described above.
  - Call `list` **without** `includePersonal` when a portal page asks for rooms.
  - Never pass a label to a page unless the member opted in for that site.

body:
A room's DID is all a member saw for a room in the portal's "Your rooms
here", the share prompt and the console. For a room the community owns,
the community knows a better answer: the label its administrators gave it,
which its offer to the member carries (vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1).

- @openvtc/pnm-core/rooms: communityRoomOffers reads a member's offers the
  way `pnm rooms offers list` does — the request built unsigned, completed
  by the member's VTA as the DID the offers are addressed to with
  rooms/keys/act/0.3 (roomsKeysAct gains a version parameter; 0.1 stays the
  default for host requests), and sent to the community unchanged.
  roomNamesFromOffers takes the labels out of an answer.
- RoomPageGates.roomNames is the one place a room's name is looked up. For
  `list` and `choose` it reads the offers to each member the shares (or the
  prompt) act as, only at the community whose portal the page is, at most
  once a minute per member. The community lists an accepted offer only for
  days (seven at the reference VTC), so names are remembered under
  room-names:<vtaDid>|<hostDid>; a fresh reading replaces a remembered one.

title: fix(rooms): let the offscreen document compile the room-file cipher (wasm-unsafe-eval)
body:
Encrypting or opening a room file failed in Chrome with 'WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(): ... neither wasm-eval nor unsafe-eval is an allowed source of script ... script-src self': the manifest declared no content_security_policy, and the MV3 default for extension pages does not allow compiling WebAssembly, which @openvtc/vti-rooms-wasm needs in the offscreen document.

extension_pages now allows 'wasm-unsafe-eval' beside 'self'. It permits compiling WebAssembly modules the extension itself ships; it does not allow eval() or new Function(), remote scripts or inline script. object-src stays 'self'.

title: fix(rooms): one row per (room, member), and every room request names its member
body:
## The problem (live test)

One VTA (`glenn-vta`) is also the community's VTA for a test VTC, so it holds **two members of one community-owned room**: the community's own place (owner, "whole history") and the administrator's own membership (persona = the VTA's own DID, "from joining"). The VTA lists the room once per member and **refuses to choose** between them (`rooms/keys/act` 0.3 recipient item 2; the custody tasks "act as the one the caller acts as, and refuse rather than choose"). The wallet keyed everything by room alone:

1. The console's Data rooms page listed the room twice with nothing saying whose each row was, and the duplicate React keys tangled the two rows' expanded panels (the duplicated host fields).
2. The portal's share prompt showed the room twice, both ticked, under "Share 1 room".
3. Sharing failed: `rooms/info` went through `rooms/keys/act` with no `issuer`, and the VTA refused it as `principalAmbiguous`.

## The fix

**Whose each listing entry is.** `rooms/keys/list`'s `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].held` (index for index with `rooms`; added by the VTI PR below) is read into `HeldRoom.member` / `context` / `actions`. `heldRoomKey` keys rows by (room, member).

**Every room request names its member** (`PersonaRoom.member`): `issuer` on `rooms/keys/act`, the sealed body's `author`, and `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].member` (`memberExt`) on `browse`, `read`, `open`, `file-key`, `backfill`, `chain`, `seal` 0.1. `roomsKeysAct` refuses an answer made as anyone but the member named.

**Console** (`manager/panes/rooms.tsx`): one row per (room, member), with an **As** column — a name the member's document claims, else a short DID, "(this agent's own DID)" where it is — its context, and its place (*administers the room* / *member*, from the grant's actions), plus "one of two places" where a room is held twice. Records, history and files from a row act as that row's member.

**Portal share prompt** (P7b):
- One row per (room, member), and **only as an identity the member uses at that community** — the principals of their `didSelfIssued` vault entries naming its DID (`membersAt`, the same listing the trigger-link sign-in uses) — **never as the community's own DID**. Rooms held only as other identities are counted, not offered.
- `choose({ hostDid, member })`: the portal says who is signed in; that only picks among the wallet's own candidates, never adds one.
- Two identities left: nothing pre-ticked unless the page's `member` names one; ticking a room as one identity unticks it as the other; an answer naming a room as both is refused. The button counts the ticks.
- The grant stores its member (`RoomGrant.member`); every page request (info, browse, read, putNote, file get/put) carries it. A grant without a member is not in force: the page asks again rather than the wallet guessing.

## Cut-over

Coordinated with the VTA (per CLAUDE.md, no compatibility fold): the VTA side is VTI PR **OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2161** (listing `held` ext + custody tasks' `member` ext + portal passing the signed-in member). Against a VTA without it, list entries carry no member, so the share prompt offers nothing and the console rows say "member not reported by this agent".

## Tests
- `room-page.test.mts`: two members of one room → offered only as the signed-in member, never the community, count/button "Share 1 room"; a share names its member and info/browse/read/putNote all carry it; two identities → member picks, page hint only chooses among them, both ticked refused; `membersAt` excludes the community; a pre-member grant asks again.
- `rooms-pane.render.test.mts`: two members of one room → two labelled rows.
- `core/tests/rooms.act.mjs`: act names the member and refuses an answer as someone else; listing maps `held`; every custody task carries `ext.member`.

Local: `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (all green), and the CI bundle guards.

title: fix(rooms)!: a member who leaves the community leaves its rooms, and a Welcome to an expired KeyPackage is refused
body:
Two gaps in community-owned data rooms (P13).

A departing member kept their community rooms. `vtc/rooms/community/members/add`
item 6 says the community SHOULD remove a member from every room it owns when
they leave; until now an administrator had to remove them room by room.

- A departure records a removal owed for each room the member holds an
  admission or an open offer in, durably, in the `community_rooms` keyspace
  (backed up), without asking the VTA anything: at the leave and admin-remove
  ceremony (`ceremony::execute::depart`, before the member row changes), an ACL
  revocation (`routes::acl::remove_entry`), a suspension
  (`admin_actions::save`), and `vtc acl remove` offline.
- `vtc_service::rooms::departures` is the one retry owner (R2.1). Its worker
  withdraws an open offer, records an open room's removal, and on a sealed
  room has the VTA remove the member from the group (`rooms/owner/group/remove`)
  before recording it — the removal and the dropped row one batch. A VTA that
  does not answer or refuses is retried with capped exponential backoff (30 s
  doubling to an hour); a retry after a lost answer is answered `notMember`,
  which counts as done. An administrator's own removal settles the row too.
  Each removal is audited (`memberRemoved` / `offerWithdrawn`, actor
  `vtc:member-departure`, reason naming the departure).
- A reconciler on the same worker finds what has no event — an ACL entry that
  expired — and any departure a crash cut off, from durable state only, after
  seeing it for a minute so a write in flight (a key rotation) is not read as
  one. Rejoining re-adds nothing.
- Owed removals are surfaced on `vtc/rooms/community/{get,list,members/list}`
  under `ext["org.openvtc"].departureRemovals` (cause, status
  pending/retrying, attempts, next attempt, last error), and on the console's
  room page.
- The administrator's `members/remove` now shares `remove_from_group` with the
  worker; its behaviour is unchanged.

`rooms/keys/welcome` joined from a pending KeyPackage without checking its
expiry, though `rooms/keys/act/0.3`'s `holds_key_package` already treats an
expired one as not held, and `rooms/keys/key-package/0.1` requires its private
half to be discarded at expiry. `room_groups::join` now refuses an expired
pending KeyPackage, deleting it, and the welcome handler answers the declared
`rooms/keys/welcome:welcomeInvalid`; the invitation is not spent.

## Breaking
`vta_service::operations::room_groups::JoinError` gains `KeyPackageExpired` and is now `#[non_exhaustive]`.

## Open questions for review
- **Suspension counts as a departure** (as asked). A cooling-off reduction that is later cancelled leaves the subject removed from community rooms, and not re-added. Easy to drop the `Suspended` cause if that is not wanted.
- A crash *inside* `acl/swap-key` (between moving the entry and the member row) could be read as `aclRemoved` by the reconciler; in normal operation the one-minute grace covers the in-flight window.

## Verified locally
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6156 passed
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3218 passed
- `cargo test --workspace --doc`: passed
- admin-ui: `npm run lint`, `vitest run` (1097 passed)

title: feat(vtc): a VTA permission refusal shows the pnm commands that fix it
body:
When the community's VTA refuses a community-room step for lack of permission, the console and `cnm rooms` now show the `pnm` commands that fix the VTC's entry at its VTA, filled in with this VTC's DID and contexts, each one copyable.

## The failure that prompted it

A console *New community room* got `vtc/rooms/community/create:keyHolderRefused` with the VTA's "`did:webvh:…:test-vtc` is not a persona you may act as, so it cannot be the owner's leaf in room …". The console's hint said to check key-mint/credential-write/vault-write "in the `[rooms.community]` context", which was misleading. The real cause: the VTC's entry was scoped to `vtc-test/rooms` (the rooms context), but its DID lives in `vtc-test`. Act scope covers a context's descendants, never its parent, so the VTA (`room_owner_group::founding_member` → `persona_signing_key`) refuses. The entry has to cover the context that holds the VTC's DID, and that also covers a rooms context beneath it.

## What changed

- **`vtc_service::rooms::vta_access`** (new) holds what the VTC knows: its DID, `vta_did`, the new `vta_context`, `[rooms.community] context`, and the contexts of `vta-account` storage. From these it builds four fixes (`noEntry`, `scope`, `capability`, and a catch-all `permission`). Each fix gives a summary, the filled-in commands, a note, the check command (`pnm acl list --context <ctx> --direction any`), and the refusals it answers (`when`: the refusal code plus phrases in the VTA's text, such as "DID not in ACL", "not a persona you may act as", "does not carry the … capability" or "no access to context").
- **Where the commands travel: the list read, not the refusal.** A `trust-task-error`'s `message` may not carry consumer-internal state (framework *What a `message` May Not Say*), and a VTA context is exactly that. `keyHolderRefused`'s `details` is `additionalProperties: false` with only `{code, message}`. So the fixes go in `vtc/rooms/community/list` → `ext["org.openvtc"].communityRooms.vtaAccess`, which is answered only to a holder of `vtc.rooms.manage`. That object also reports `roomsContextInside` and a `warning` when the rooms context is outside the context holding the VTC's DID, or when `vta_context` is unknown. Clients apply the `when` rules as data, so the classification lives in one place. The VTC also logs the chosen fix at `warn`, because the log is the right place for internal state. The refusals themselves are unchanged.
- **`vta_context`** is an optional top-level `config.toml` key: the VTA context holding the VTC's DID. `vtc setup` writes it from its `context`. When it is absent (any VTC set up before this change), the commands use a `<the context holding the VTC's DID>` placeholder and the list warns.
- **Console**: `RefusalCard` reads the cached list (same query key) for a `keyHolderRefused` or `noKeyHolder` refusal and renders the matching fix as command blocks with `CopyButton`s. The misleading `[rooms.community]`-context hint is replaced. The list page shows the configuration warning with the scope command. The "community rooms are off" card shows the create command.
- **`cnm rooms`**: on a `keyHolderRefused` or `noKeyHolder` refusal, it makes one signed list read and prints the matching fix. `cnm rooms list` prints the configuration warning.
- **Docs**: `community-rooms.md` now says the entry must cover both the context holding the VTC's DID and the rooms context, explains why, and adds a *Troubleshooting: permission errors* table. Quickstart §12 now passes `--contexts vtc` and adds the check. `non-interactive-setup.md` documents `vta_context`. Every command uses real `pnm` flags; I checked them against `pnm-cli/src/cli.rs`. `pnm acl update` does have `--capabilities`, and the existing docs' use of it was correct.

## What the user's case shows (rooms context `vtc-test/rooms`, DID in `vtc-test`)

```
pnm acl update did:webvh:…:test-vtc --contexts vtc-test
then check:
pnm acl list --context vtc-test --direction any
```

The note says to run these as someone with admin at the community's VTA, and that `--contexts` replaces the entry's list.

## Tests

- `vta_access` unit tests: each refusal shape renders the expected command with the real DID and contexts (the persona case, no entry, a missing capability, an unexplained refusal, `vta-account` contexts and capability, a placeholder when `vta_context` is unknown, a rooms context outside the DID's context, shell quoting).
- IT `vtc_rooms_community_listing_carries_the_commands_that_fix_a_vta_refusal`: the refusal names no context, and the list carries the fixes. A client's pick gives `permission` for the stand-in's refusal and `scope` for the persona refusal.
- Console: copyable command blocks render under the refusal, the old hint is gone, the list warning shows, and `vtaFixFor` matches the same way the Rust code does.
- `cnm rooms`: `pick_fix` and `render_fix`.

When the community's VTA refuses a community-room step for lack of
permission, the console and `cnm rooms` show the `pnm acl` commands that
fix the VTC's entry at its VTA, filled in with the VTC's DID and contexts.

The entry must cover the context holding the VTC's own DID, not only the

body:
### Added

- **witness**: Witness 0.2 — the member presentation and personhood outcome evidence as spec members, and vta/witness/list ([#1068](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1068)) ([#2147](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2147))

* feat(witness)!: witness 0.2 — the member presentation and personhood outcome evidence as spec members ([#1068](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1068))

- **rooms**: Rooms/keys/act 0.3 — a member takes up a community's offer as themself, with only a KeyPackage their VTA minted ([#2148](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2148))

Serve `rooms/keys/act/0.3` (trust-tasks-tf #797) beside 0.2 and 0.1.

  - The table gains `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1` and
    `vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1`, with no presentation inserted
    (`room_act::OFFER_TYPES`, apart from the 0.1/0.2 host-bound table;
    0.1 and 0.2 still refuse them by schema).
  - Recipient item 2b: for the offer types `issuer` is required
    (`principalAmbiguous` without it, never picked for the caller), and the
    VTA acts as it only where it holds a key that DID lists for
    `authentication` and the caller may act as it (`issuerNotPrincipal`).
    No room credential is asked for.
  - Recipient item 10 (security): an acceptance's `keyPackage` is completed
    only when this VTA minted it with `rooms/keys/key-package` for that room
    and member and still holds its unused, unexpired private half —
    compared by KeyPackageRef (`room_groups::holds_key_package`), never by
    the leaf credential — else `keyPackageNotHeld`. The existing per-member
    pending-KeyPackage row is the record: a Welcome consumes it (used), its
    `expiresAt` bounds it. Completing an acceptance does not consume it, so
    a retry after a lost answer is the identical acceptance and is answered
    with the same Welcome (rooms/owner/group/add 0.2 item 8).
  - Policy and audit subject is the member, as at 0.2.

- **rooms**: Rooms/owner/group/add 0.2 — a repeated admission is answered with its Welcome ([#2146](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2146))

* feat(rooms)!: rooms/owner/group/add 0.2 — a repeated admission is answered with its Welcome

  Serve `rooms/owner/group/add/0.2` (trust-tasks-tf #795) beside 0.1, and
  raise the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.31.11, which carries it.

  Under 0.1 a caller that lost an admission's answer and sent the identical
  request again was refused `alreadyMember`: the member had a leaf and no
  Welcome anyone could give them. 0.2 item 8:

  - The owner's VTA keeps the last admission it applied for a room —
    member, the KeyPackage's KeyPackageRef (RFC 9420 §5.2), epoch and
    Welcome — in `room_groups` (`room-admitted/<room>/<persona>`, beside the
    pending advance that already holds the same Welcome, under the same
    storage encryption and backup membership). It is discarded when the
    owner builds its next advance of the room, after 24 hours (checked on
    read, and swept by the storage thread), and with the member's group.
  - A request naming the same room, a string-equal member and a KeyPackage
    with the same KeyPackageRef is answered — after item 1 and the
    authorization checks — with that epoch and Welcome: the host is not
    contacted, the group not changed, no new Welcome built. Anything else
    for a member with a leaf stays `alreadyMember`.
  - Item 6 hands over to item 8: a pending admission settled by the
    identical request becomes the retained one and answers it.
  - 0.1 is unchanged.

- **rooms**: Rooms/keys file-key, open and act 0.2 — removed, beyondChain, and the member as act's subject ([#2145](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2145))

trust-tasks-rs 0.31.10 (trust-tasks-tf #786, #787, released in #788) publishes
  rooms/keys/file-key/0.2, rooms/keys/open/0.2 and rooms/keys/act/0.2. The
  workspace floor moves to 0.31.10.

  VTA (served beside 0.1, whose behaviour is unchanged):

  - file-key 0.2: a file sealed at or after the member's removal is
    `unknownEpoch` with `{reason: removed, removedAtEpoch}` (oracle item 4 —
    an oracle that knows of the removal MUST NOT answer `notDelivered`). 0.1's
    closed details schema has no `removed`, so 0.1 still answers
    `notDelivered` with the removal in its message.
  - open 0.2: `unknownEpoch` carries the declared closed details. An older
    epoch the retained chain does not reach is `{reason: beyondChain,
    earliestEpoch}`; 0.1 still answers it as a bare validation failure.
    `room_groups::OpenError` gains `BeyondChain` (the enum is
    `#[non_exhaustive]`).
  - act 0.2: `subjectPath` is `/document/issuer`. The policy gate evaluates
    act 0.2 against the member — `issuer`, or where it is absent the one member
    of the room the caller may act as (`room_act::act_subject`) — never against
    no subject. The 0.2 audit row names the member as its target, with the type
    and room in its detail; a 0.1 row still names the room. Recipient item 2a
    (a room-less type is completed only as its `issuer`; absent is
    `principalAmbiguous`, never a member picked here) was already this VTA's
    behaviour and is now tested at 0.2.
  - Dispatch, conformance witnesses, and `vta_sdk::retry_safety`
    (open/file-key ReadOnly, act RetrySafe) for the three new URIs.



### Fixed

- **rooms**: Say a removed member's file key is a removal, and keep NoMatchingProtocol typed ([#2135](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2135))

Three rough edges from the end-to-end data-rooms run.

  FileKeyError gains Removed and becomes #[non_exhaustive] (breaking for
  vta-service). file_key now reads the room-removed row exactly as
  open_record_detailed does, so a file sealed at or after the member's
  removal is Removed rather than NotDelivered. On the wire it stays
  rooms/keys/file-key:unknownEpoch with reason notDelivered: the spec's
  detailsSchema for that code is closed (reason in {notDelivered,
  beyondChain}, additionalProperties false), so there is no `removed` to
  send until the specification declares one. The message says it was a
  removal, and `pnm rooms file get` now prints the same remedies a record
  refusal prints (catch up / backfill / removed), sharing one hint function.

  AppError gains NoMatchingProtocol(Box<vti_common::error::NoMatchingProtocol>)
  (peer, ours, theirs, note; boxed for clippy::result_large_err), breaking
  for vti-common. Outbound::pick_transport returned AppError::Validation,
  which the Trust Task spine renders as malformedRequest: the producer was
  told its document was wrong and lost both transport sets. It is now
  taskFailed (SPEC 8.3 defines no transport code, and the peer is not
  unavailable), not retryable, with details.reason no_matching_protocol
  plus counterpartyDid/ours/theirs; REST renders 502 with the same members.
  The SDK maps both back to VtaError::NoMatchingProtocol and the CLI prints
  which side can add which service.

title: fix(rooms): say whose each rooms/keys/list entry is, and let a client name the member a custody task acts as
body:
## Problem (live test)

`glenn-vta` is also the test VTC's VTA, so it holds **two members of one community-owned room**: the community's own place (persona = the VTC's DID, context `vtc-test`) and the administrator's own membership (persona = glenn-vta's DID). Then:

- `rooms/keys/list` returned the room twice with nothing saying whose each entry is;
- every custody task (`browse`, `read`, `open`, `file-key`, …) refused as ambiguous ("act from the context of the one you mean"), which a wallet session that acts in both contexts cannot do;
- the portal's share (`rooms/info` through `rooms/keys/act` without `issuer`) refused as `principalAmbiguous` (correctly, per act 0.3 item 2b — the VTA never picks).

## Change

- **`rooms/keys/list`**: `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].held`, index for index with `rooms`: `{ member, context?, actions? }`. The spec's entry is `additionalProperties: false` and has no member field, so it rides in `ext`.
- **Naming the member on custody tasks**: `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].member` on `read`, `browse`, `backfill`, `open`, `seal` 0.1, `file-key`, `commit`, `chain` (`room_member::named_member` / `acting_as` / `require_acting_as`, `room_oracle::principal_named`, `presenting_member(.., named)`). It only narrows — a persona the caller may not act as is the same "no group state" as one nobody holds; not a DID → `malformedRequest`; absent → unchanged (still refuses for two). `rooms/keys/act` keeps using `issuer`.
- **`pnm rooms keys list`** prints `as <member> (context …)` per entry.
- **Member portal**: `Share rooms…` calls `wallet.choose({ hostDid, member: me.did })` (a hint the wallet only uses to pick among identities it already holds for this community); each shared room shows whom it is shared as; a refusal for a room held as two identities (from an older wallet) is explained with the fix.
- Docs: `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md`, `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md` §8.5.

Not a divergence from the spec: both members are `ext`, and the custody tasks' rule ("acts as the one its caller acts as, and refuses rather than choose") is kept — the ext is how the caller says which one. A `member` field in the specs themselves (trust-tasks-tf) would be the cleaner long-term home; noted as a follow-up.

Wallet side: OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#332 (cuts over together).

## Tests
- `two_members_of_one_room_are_listed_apart_and_named_to_act`: two personas in one room → two list entries with distinct `held[i].member` + context; a single-context caller sees only its own; `open` naming each persona opens; naming one the caller can't act as → no group state; a non-DID member → malformed.
- Portal (`Rooms.test.tsx`): choose carries the signed-in member and the row says "as you"; an ambiguity refusal shows the plain-words fix.

Local: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p vta-service -p vta-cli-common --all-targets -D warnings` (+ the `--no-default-features --features rest` variant), `cargo nextest run -p vta-service -p vta-cli-common`; admin-ui `wire:check`, `tsc`, `vitest` (1101 pass), `build`.

title: fix(rooms): say whose each rooms/keys/list entry is, and let a client name the member a custody task acts as (#2161)
body:
fix(rooms): say whose each rooms/keys/list entry is, and let a client name the member a custody task acts as (#2161)

One VTA can hold two members of one room: an administrator whose VTA is also
the community's holds the community's own place in a room the community owns
and their own membership in it. rooms/keys/list then returned the room twice
with nothing saying whose each entry was, and every custody task refused as
ambiguous ("act from the context of the one you mean") — which a client whose
session acts in both contexts cannot do. The wallet and the member portal hit
both in a live test: the room listed twice, and sharing it with the portal
refused as rooms/keys/act:principalAmbiguous.

- rooms/keys/list: one entry per (room, member) as before, and
  ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].held, index for index with rooms: the member
  (persona DID), the trust context its key lives in, and the actions the
  room's grant to it confers. The specification's entry has no member of its
  own and forbids extra members, so it rides in ext.
- read, browse, backfill, open, seal 0.1, file-key, commit and chain take
  ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].member, naming the persona to act as. It only
  narrows: a persona the caller may not act as answers as "no group state",
  the same as one nobody here holds. Naming none keeps the refusal for two
  (rooms/keys/read/0.1: "acts as the one its caller acts as, and refuses
  rather than choose"); rooms/keys/act keeps taking the member as issuer
  (act 0.3 recipient item 2).
- pnm rooms keys list prints the member of each entry.
- Member portal: Share rooms passes the signed-in member to the wallet
  (choose({ hostDid, member })), which only picks among the identities it
  holds for this community; each shared room says whom it is shared as; a
  wallet refusal for a room held as two identities is explained in plain words.

Docs: data-rooms.md (one VTA, several members of one room) and
data-rooms-files.md §8.5 (as whom a portal share acts).

### Added

- **rooms**: Rooms/owner/group/add 0.2 — a repeated admission is answered with its Welcome ([#2146](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2146))

* feat(rooms)!: rooms/owner/group/add 0.2 — a repeated admission is answered with its Welcome

  Serve `rooms/owner/group/add/0.2` (trust-tasks-tf #795) beside 0.1, and
  raise the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.31.11, which carries it.

  Under 0.1 a caller that lost an admission's answer and sent the identical
  request again was refused `alreadyMember`: the member had a leaf and no
  Welcome anyone could give them. 0.2 item 8:

  - The owner's VTA keeps the last admission it applied for a room —
    member, the KeyPackage's KeyPackageRef (RFC 9420 §5.2), epoch and
    Welcome — in `room_groups` (`room-admitted/<room>/<persona>`, beside the
    pending advance that already holds the same Welcome, under the same
    storage encryption and backup membership). It is discarded when the
    owner builds its next advance of the room, after 24 hours (checked on
    read, and swept by the storage thread), and with the member's group.
  - A request naming the same room, a string-equal member and a KeyPackage
    with the same KeyPackageRef is answered — after item 1 and the
    authorization checks — with that epoch and Welcome: the host is not
    contacted, the group not changed, no new Welcome built. Anything else
    for a member with a leaf stays `alreadyMember`.
  - Item 6 hands over to item 8: a pending admission settled by the
    identical request becomes the retained one and answers it.
  - 0.1 is unchanged.

- **vtc**: The `rooms` topic on the admin console's live channel (vtc/admin/events 0.2) ([#2136](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2136))

Serve `vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.2` beside 0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #767, in
  trust-tasks-rs 0.31.2+). The topic set is closed per version: 0.2 adds `rooms`
  and nothing else, a 0.1 subscribe that names it is refused by its schema, and
  every stream answers — its `#response` and every hint — at the version it was
  opened with, so 0.1 consoles and `cnm actions watch` are unchanged.

  `rooms` is effective for holders of `vtc.rooms.admin` (subscribe 0.2
  §Authorization; `admin_events::read_capability`), who are answered on
  `vtc/rooms/list`, `vtc/rooms/usage` and `vtc/storage/configs/list`. It is a
  countless hint, sent per event 0.2 producer rule 4 when a room is registered or
  removed, a room's lifecycle state changes, a room's usage or a storage config's
  held bytes crosses 80/95/100 % of its limit or capacity in either direction, or
  a storage config is created, changed or changes state. The stream fingerprints
  exactly those facts, read as the rooms reads report them, so holdings moving
  inside a band or a live room renewing send nothing. Lifecycle is computed from
  the clock and never written, so a stream holding `rooms` also wakes itself at
  the next transition (`vti_rooms::Room::next_lifecycle_change`).

title: vti-common-v0.46.0
body:
### Added

- **witness**: Witness 0.2 — the member presentation and personhood outcome evidence as spec members, and vta/witness/list ([#1068](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1068)) ([#2147](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2147))

* feat(witness)!: witness 0.2 — the member presentation and personhood outcome evidence as spec members ([#1068](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1068))

- **rooms**: Rooms/keys file-key, open and act 0.2 — removed, beyondChain, and the member as act's subject ([#2145](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2145))

trust-tasks-rs 0.31.10 (trust-tasks-tf #786, #787, released in #788) publishes
  rooms/keys/file-key/0.2, rooms/keys/open/0.2 and rooms/keys/act/0.2. The
  workspace floor moves to 0.31.10.

  VTA (served beside 0.1, whose behaviour is unchanged):

  - file-key 0.2: a file sealed at or after the member's removal is
    `unknownEpoch` with `{reason: removed, removedAtEpoch}` (oracle item 4 —
    an oracle that knows of the removal MUST NOT answer `notDelivered`). 0.1's
    closed details schema has no `removed`, so 0.1 still answers
    `notDelivered` with the removal in its message.
  - open 0.2: `unknownEpoch` carries the declared closed details. An older
    epoch the retained chain does not reach is `{reason: beyondChain,
    earliestEpoch}`; 0.1 still answers it as a bare validation failure.
    `room_groups::OpenError` gains `BeyondChain` (the enum is
    `#[non_exhaustive]`).
  - act 0.2: `subjectPath` is `/document/issuer`. The policy gate evaluates
    act 0.2 against the member — `issuer`, or where it is absent the one member
    of the room the caller may act as (`room_act::act_subject`) — never against
    no subject. The 0.2 audit row names the member as its target, with the type
    and room in its detail; a 0.1 row still names the room. Recipient item 2a
    (a room-less type is completed only as its `issuer`; absent is
    `principalAmbiguous`, never a member picked here) was already this VTA's
    behaviour and is now tested at 0.2.
  - Dispatch, conformance witnesses, and `vta_sdk::retry_safety`
    (open/file-key ReadOnly, act RetrySafe) for the three new URIs.

- **vtc**: Community-owned data rooms — the community's VTA as key holder (vtc/rooms/community/*, vtc/rooms/offers/*) ([#2141](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2141))

* feat(vtc): community-owned data rooms — vtc/rooms/community/* and vtc/rooms/offers/*, the community's VTA as key holder

  P13 of data-rooms-files.md §8.4 (trust-tasks-tf #768, trust-tasks-rs 0.31.2).
  The community owns and hosts the room; its own VTA mints the room's DID from
  the `room` template, founds the group, issues and vaults the community's own
  VMC + admin VAC, and issues members' VIC/VMC/VAC, over vta_link, signed as the
  VTC's DID (a persona the VTA holds in `[rooms.community] context`). The VTC
  holds no room key and never falls back to one (noKeyHolder).

  - vtc.rooms.manage capability (community-admin ceiling), distinct from
    vtc.rooms.admin.
  - Optional [rooms.community] (absent = off; the list answer says what to add).
  - community_rooms keyspace (backed up): the owner's record, never read on the
    host path (I5).
  - Remote first: create stores the room only after mint/group/credentials; an
    offer, an admission and a removal are recorded only after the VTA answered.
  - Creates, adds and removes take the requester's bound step-up and are
    audited (AuditEvent::CommunityRoomChanged); no Welcome, KeyPackage or
    credential is logged or audited.
  - Serverless room identities are served at /room-dids/<id>/did.jsonl.
  - rooms policy input gains room.communityOwned; the shipped default allows
    community-owned open/attributed rooms, and a VTC still on the earlier
    shipped default is upgraded at boot (an operator's own policy untouched).
  - Integration tests against a stand-in VTA signing real DTG credentials,
    including a record written and read on the host path with the offered
    credentials; every declared code witnessed in the error-code census.



### Fixed

- **vta-sdk**: A presign part carries uploadId only when one of its operations needs it ([#2134](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2134))

`external/credentials/issue/0.3` Conformance item 4 has a batch name
  `uploadId` exactly when an operation acts on an existing multipart upload
  (`upload-part`, `list-parts`, `complete-multipart`, `abort-multipart`).
  `VtaClient::external_credentials_issue_presign` split a batch refused
  `responseTooLarge` but copied the batch's `uploadId` onto every part, so
  splitting the checks-and-completion batch of consumer item 4 sent a lone
  `head` with `uploadId` and the VTA refused it `invalidBatch`
  (`vta_external::batch::check_batch`). Each part now keeps `uploadId` only
  when one of its operations needs it, as consumer item 5 says (clarified in
  dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#783).

  The VTC's rooms presigner (`vtc-service` `rooms::vta_storage`) builds each
  part itself and had the same flaw, also reachable through the 64-operation
  chunking in `vti_common::blob_store::presigned`; `batch_request` now names
  `uploadId` only when an operation needs it, via the new
  `StorageOp::needs_upload_id`.

- **rooms**: Say a removed member's file key is a removal, and keep NoMatchingProtocol typed ([#2135](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2135))

Three rough edges from the end-to-end data-rooms run.

  FileKeyError gains Removed and becomes #[non_exhaustive] (breaking for
  vta-service). file_key now reads the room-removed row exactly as
  open_record_detailed does, so a file sealed at or after the member's
  removal is Removed rather than NotDelivered. On the wire it stays
  rooms/keys/file-key:unknownEpoch with reason notDelivered: the spec's
  detailsSchema for that code is closed (reason in {notDelivered,
  beyondChain}, additionalProperties false), so there is no `removed` to
  send until the specification declares one. The message says it was a
  removal, and `pnm rooms file get` now prints the same remedies a record
  refusal prints (catch up / backfill / removed), sharing one hint function.

  AppError gains NoMatchingProtocol(Box<vti_common::error::NoMatchingProtocol>)
  (peer, ours, theirs, note; boxed for clippy::result_large_err), breaking
  for vti-common. Outbound::pick_transport returned AppError::Validation,
  which the Trust Task spine renders as malformedRequest: the producer was
  told its document was wrong and lost both transport sets. It is now
  taskFailed (SPEC 8.3 defines no transport code, and the peer is not
  unavailable), not retryable, with details.reason no_matching_protocol
  plus counterpartyDid/ours/theirs; REST renders 502 with the same members.
  The SDK maps both back to VtaError::NoMatchingProtocol and the CLI prints
  which side can add which service.

title: vta-sdk-v0.70.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Run membership-sync jobs waiting on a backoff now — sync-jobs/retry/0.2 ([#2154](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2154))

Adding a trust registry to a running community queues a publish job for
  every existing member, and the first failures put them on an exponential
  backoff that reaches an hour. retry/0.1 only requeues failed jobs, so an
  operator who had fixed the cause could only wait.

  The VTC serves vtc/registry/sync-jobs/retry/0.2 (trust-tasks-tf #802,
  trust-tasks-rs 0.31.13) beside 0.1: jobId accepts a pending job waiting out
  its backoff, and allWaiting brings every such job forward with a fresh
  attempt budget, each reported with from: failed | pending. An RTBF-batched
  job is held and never brought forward, whichever member names it — the
  batch window is what keeps a removal from being timed back to the request.
  An in-flight job is skipped as inFlight.

  The console moves to 0.2 and shows "Run waiting jobs now" under the queue
  tiles while any job is backing off; skip toasts name inFlight / held /
  notFound. Operator docs updated.

- **vtc-admin-ui**: Community rooms tab — create and run rooms the community owns ([#2152](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2152))

* feat(vtc-admin-ui): Community rooms tab — create and run rooms the community owns

  Data rooms gains a fourth tab, Community rooms (/rooms/community, one room at
  /rooms/community/<room DID>), shown to holders of vtc.rooms.manage — the
  owner's authority, distinct from hosting's vtc.rooms.admin. Everything goes
  through the signed Trust Task door as vtc/rooms/community/*/0.1; no REST route.

  - List: label, tier, lifecycle, admitted / offered counts, and when the
    community's own authority over each room lapses (flagged 30 days ahead).
    When [rooms.community] is absent, the tab shows the section to add from the
    list's ext["org.openvtc"].communityRooms.
  - New community room: label, tier (attributed by default; private shown but
    not offered), history, retention, storage location (for vtc.rooms.admin
    holders) and a reason.
  - A room's page: its facts and members, filtered by state. Add a member makes
    an offer (actions, days valid, reason); Remove / Withdraw says what removal
    does on the tier and the member's validUntil before anything is signed
    (members/remove producer item 1) and reports validUntil and epoch from the
    answer (item 2).

  create, members/add and members/remove use postSignedWithStepUp: the VTC's
  operation-bound step-up (passkey or step-up approver), then the identical
  document again. Refusals carry the fix (noKeyHolder, visibilityNotPermitted,
  notAMember, alreadyMember, keyHolderUnavailable with the minted DID, missing
  vtc.rooms.manage).

  The generated shapes reach the console through vta_sdk::openapi wrappers for
  the vtc/rooms/community payloads and responses, registered in the VTC's
  OpenAPI document (snapshot and wire.ts regenerated). The two listings are
  pinned in list-limits.json.

  The pages poll once a minute: the live channel's rooms topic hints on a
  create (a room registered) but carries no offer, admission or removal, and
  goes only to vtc.rooms.admin holders — a specification gap, recorded in
  community-rooms.md rather than hinted outside event 0.2 producer rule 4.

- **witness**: Witness 0.2 — the member presentation and personhood outcome evidence as spec members, and vta/witness/list ([#1068](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1068)) ([#2147](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2147))

* feat(witness)!: witness 0.2 — the member presentation and personhood outcome evidence as spec members ([#1068](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1068))

- **rooms**: Rooms/keys/act 0.3 — a member takes up a community's offer as themself, with only a KeyPackage their VTA minted ([#2148](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2148))

Serve `rooms/keys/act/0.3` (trust-tasks-tf #797) beside 0.2 and 0.1.

  - The table gains `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1` and
    `vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1`, with no presentation inserted
    (`room_act::OFFER_TYPES`, apart from the 0.1/0.2 host-bound table;
    0.1 and 0.2 still refuse them by schema).
  - Recipient item 2b: for the offer types `issuer` is required
    (`principalAmbiguous` without it, never picked for the caller), and the
    VTA acts as it only where it holds a key that DID lists for
    `authentication` and the caller may act as it (`issuerNotPrincipal`).
    No room credential is asked for.
  - Recipient item 10 (security): an acceptance's `keyPackage` is completed
    only when this VTA minted it with `rooms/keys/key-package` for that room
    and member and still holds its unused, unexpired private half —
    compared by KeyPackageRef (`room_groups::holds_key_package`), never by
    the leaf credential — else `keyPackageNotHeld`. The existing per-member
    pending-KeyPackage row is the record: a Welcome consumes it (used), its
    `expiresAt` bounds it. Completing an acceptance does not consume it, so
    a retry after a lost answer is the identical acceptance and is answered
    with the same Welcome (rooms/owner/group/add 0.2 item 8).
  - Policy and audit subject is the member, as at 0.2.

- **vta-mobile-core**: Connect a did:peer relationship DID to its mediator for witnessing ([#1068](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1068)) ([#2139](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2139))

A wallet carries every witness document from the relationship DID: the

An RTBF-batched job is held and never brought forward, whichever member names it — the batch window is what keeps a removal from being timed back to the request. A relationship DID is a did:peer:2 with an independent signing key V and key-agreement key E under their own #key-N ids. MediatorSession::connect and TspMediatorSession::connect derive both secrets from one did:key seed, so they could not open that session at all. - vta-sdk: TspSession::connect_with_secrets{,_on}, mirroring DIDCommSession's. connect / connect_on derive the did:key secrets and delegate. Additive. - vta-mobile-core: MediatorSession::connect_with_secrets(holder, secrets, peer, mediator) and TspMediatorSession::connect_with_secrets(holder, secrets, mediator), taking HolderSecret {key_id, private_key_multibase} records (the SecretEntry shape; Debug redacts the key). Before any socket opens, the holder's document is resolved and every secret must sit under the holder DID, name a published verification method and carry its public key, with an Ed25519 authentication key and an X25519 keyAgreement key present. A wrong key is refused by name instead of surfacing as a mediator authentication failure. - docs/02-vta/witness-party.md and the witness module doc name the new constructors for a did:peer relationship DID. ### Fixed - **vta-sdk**: A presign part carries uploadId only when one of its operations needs it ([#2134](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2134)) `external/credentials/issue/0.3` Conformance item 4 has a batch name `uploadId` exactly when an operation acts on an existing multipart upload (`upload-part`, `list-parts`, `complete-multipart`, `abort-multipart`). `VtaClient::external_credentials_issue_presign` split a batch refused `responseTooLarge` but copied the batch's `uploadId` onto every part, so splitting the checks-and-completion batch of consumer item 4 sent a lone `head` with `uploadId` and the VTA refused it `invalidBatch` (`vta_external::batch::check_batch`). Each part now keeps `uploadId` only when one of its operations needs it, as consumer item 5 says (clarified in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#783). The VTC's rooms presigner (`vtc-service` `rooms::vta_storage`) builds each part itself and had the same flaw, also reachable through the 64-operation chunking in `vti_common::blob_store::presigned`; `batch_request` now names `uploadId` only when an operation needs it, via the new `StorageOp::needs_upload_id`. - **rooms**: Say a removed member's file key is a removal, and keep NoMatchingProtocol typed ([#2135](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2135)) Three rough edges from the end-to-end data-rooms run. FileKeyError gains Removed and becomes #[non_exhaustive] (breaking for vta-service). file_key now reads the room-removed row exactly as open_record_detailed does, so a file sealed at or after the member's removal is Removed rather than NotDelivered. On the wire it stays rooms/keys/file-key:unknownEpoch with reason notDelivered: the spec's detailsSchema for that code is closed (reason in {notDelivered, beyondChain}, additionalProperties false), so there is no `removed` to send until the specification declares one. The message says it was a removal, and `pnm rooms file get` now prints the same remedies a record refusal prints (catch up / backfill / removed), sharing one hint function. AppError gains NoMatchingProtocol(Box) (peer, ours, theirs, note; boxed for clippy::result_large_err), breaking for vti-common. Outbound::pick_transport returned AppError::Validation, which the Trust Task spine renders as malformedRequest: the producer was told its document was wrong and lost both transport sets. It is now taskFailed (SPEC 8.3 defines no transport code, and the peer is not unavailable), not retryable, with details.reason no_matching_protocol plus counterpartyDid/ours/theirs; REST renders 502 with the same members. The SDK maps both back to VtaError::NoMatchingProtocol and the CLI prints which side can add which service.

title: security(rooms): a room credential must be signed by its issuer
body:
security(rooms): a room credential must be signed by its issuer

A room credential's proof was verified against whatever key its own
`verificationMethod` named, but that method's DID was never compared with
the credential's `issuer`. Everything downstream trusts `issuer` -- the
authority chain is rooted at it and the membership check compares it to the
room -- so a credential could claim an issuer whose key never signed it.
That is the issuer-not-bound-to-proof-key class: a valid signature by
somebody, read as the issuer's.

`vti_rooms_dtg::open_credential` now requires the proof's verification
method to be a DID URL under the credential's `issuer` (exact DID match,
non-empty fragment) before resolving any key, and refuses with the same
opaque "could not be verified" as every other proof failure, logging a
`security_alert`. Every room credential goes through it: the VMC, each VAC
in the chain (root and attenuations), and succession nominations, on both
the VTC host and `room-host`. The rule is the VTC's existing
`check_issuer_binding`, moved to `vti_common::auth` so the two share one
implementation (the VTC re-exports it unchanged).

Spec: framework SPEC 4.7; rooms `AuthorityPresentation.authority` ("the
last MUST be one issued by the room itself", rooms/_shared/0.1/
room.schema.json); `rooms/records/put` consumer item 1.

Also:

- The membership credential is held to its validity window
  (validFrom <= now <= validUntil, the same clock and no-skew rule
  `verify_chain` applies to every VAC). It was checked only for being
  well-formed.
- `room-host` now applies the spine checks the VTC applies to every
  inbound document: the VTI acceptance window with `issuedAt` required
  (SPEC 7.2 item 13), expiry and -- once the host has a DID -- the
  `recipient` binding (items 4-5), and issuer == proof signer (4.7). Every
  document id is recorded in the replay guard, reads included; a read's
  answer is not retained, so a replayed read gets 204 with no body.
  Replay records are kept to the end of the acceptance window.

Tests: forged issuer refused for a root VAC, an attenuated (and a
middle) link, a VMC, a nomination, and the full forged chain through
`authorize`; honest owner, agent and successor chains still verify; VMC
outside its window refused; room-host refuses stale, expired, no-issuedAt,
misaddressed and issuer != signer documents and a replayed read.
