title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): show a community room's name on the host pages
body:
A room the community owns showed only its DID on Data rooms → Rooms and on
the room's host page, so an administrator could not tell which room was
which. The community knows each such room's label (set at
vtc/rooms/community/create, returned by vtc/rooms/community/list/0.1).

For a viewer holding vtc.rooms.manage, the host pages now join the
community's list on room DID (`rooms/useRoomNames.tsx`, sharing the
Community rooms tab's query under ["rooms"], so the live `rooms` hint
re-reads it): the label is the page title, the list's primary text and
the breadcrumb, with a "Community room" badge linking to
/rooms/community/<DID>, and the DID kept as secondary text with its copy
button. A room missing from a complete list is a member's, and says
"Named by its owner; this community never sees room names" — no name is
ever fetched for it. A viewer with only vtc.rooms.admin, or a refused or
failed read, sees the DID as before, with no error.

The Rooms list also gains a search over name and DID, tier and lifecycle
filters, and sortable Room / Tier / Lifecycle / Created columns. A
community room's page always shows its created date and, for a holder of
vtc.audit.read, links to the Audit trail — unfiltered, since the trail
cannot filter to one room (a CommunityRoomChanged row names the room in
its event data, not its target). It leaves a marked place for renaming
and a description, which wait on a community-room update task.

Console-only: no spec change, no new route, no new Trust Task URI.

## Tests
vitest (Rooms.test.tsx): label/badge/DID on the list; search + tier/lifecycle filters; DID-only and no community read without `vtc.rooms.manage`; title + breadcrumb carry the label; member-owned note; failed community read leaves the host page intact; community room page's Audit link + created + counts. Locally: wire:check, tsc, vitest (1104 passed), build.

title: feat(vtc/rooms/community): update — administrators name, describe and tag the rooms the community owns
body:
## Why

The problem, from a community administrator: *"we don't change the room name or description anywhere — how does the community admin/owner know what room is what?"* Today `vtc/rooms/community/create/0.1` takes a `label` and nothing else, `get`/`list` return it, and no task changes it. A room's DID says nothing about it, so after a few rooms neither the administrators running them nor the members being offered them can tell them apart.

## What

| Spec | Version | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `vtc/rooms/community/update` | **0.1 (new)** | Change a community-owned room's `label`, `description` (or `removeDescription: true`) and `tags`. |
| `vtc/rooms/community/create` | **0.2** | Optional `description` and `tags`; response is `CommunityRoomV2`. |
| `vtc/rooms/community/get` | **0.2** | Response is `CommunityRoomV2`. |
| `vtc/rooms/community/list` | **0.2** | Items are `CommunityRoomV2`; optional `tag` filter. |
| `vtc/rooms/offers/list` | **0.2** | Items are `OfferV2`: the room's current `description` beside its label. |
| `vtc/_shared/0.1/community-room` | in place, additive | New `$defs` only: `RoomDescription`, `RoomTag`, `RoomTags`, `CommunityRoomV2`, `OfferV2`. |

### Versioning (SPEC §5.2, §6.6)

Every affected response schema is `additionalProperties: false`, so a new member is a wire change and gets a new MINOR directory; the 0.1s are untouched. The shared component gains **new `$defs` beside the old ones** rather than changing `CommunityRoom`/`Offer` — the `RecordMetadata` / `RecordMetadataV2` pattern from `rooms/_shared/0.1` (#804 also added `$defs` to a shared 0.1 in place). Adding an unreferenced `$def` changes no published spec's wire shape, so no `vtc/_shared/0.2` copy is needed. The `members/*` tasks don't use the changed shapes and stay at their current versions.

### What a room's record now carries (`CommunityRoomV2`)

- **`description`** (1–1000 chars, plain text): what the room is for. This is the core of the request.
- **`tags`** (≤ 8 lower-case identifiers, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`, a set) plus `list`'s `tag` filter. Kept because a community with a board, working groups and a library needs to *find* rooms, not only read them. Tags are for administrators only and never go into an offer: they are filing, not a description, and members don't need to see how administrators group rooms. An empty list means "none". That is safe here because a tag grants nothing, so "empty" has no more dangerous reading.
- **`detailsUpdatedAt` / `detailsUpdatedBy`**: when label/description/tags last changed, and which administrator changed them. These are kept separate from `room.updatedAt`, which belongs to the host record and moves with epoch/lifecycle, so it can't answer "who renamed this?".
- **Creation**: no new members. `room.createdAt` (host record) and `createdBy` (the creating administrator's DID) already exist in `CommunityRoom`. `createdBy` was already shown to `vtc.rooms.manage` holders, so `detailsUpdatedBy` follows the same privacy rule: an administrator's DID, shown to holders of the same capability in the same community.
- **Dropped: `purpose`.** It would just be a shorter `description`, and two free-text fields give two places to disagree.
- **Not on the wire: history.** Earlier values live in the audit trail (below), not in the response.

### `update/0.1`

- **Authority:** `vtc.rooms.manage`, the same as create/get/list/members.
- **Step-up class:** it is *designed for* no operation-bound step-up and no consent. Create and `members/add` are designed for a step-up because they make the community's VTA mint an identity, sign credentials and admit a party. An update reaches no key holder, confers nothing, changes nobody's access, and the same task undoes it. Policy can still ask for more (§7.3 item 13); the spec doesn't declare it either way.
- **Proof and `issuedAt`: REQUIRED.** The label and description are shown to offered members and attributed to an administrator. Members are replaced wholesale, so a replayed old update would silently revert a rename (the same rationale as `vtc/storage/configs/update`).
- **Semantics:** each member given replaces the stored one and absent members are unchanged. `tags: []` clears the tags. Removing a description uses `removeDescription: true`, not `description: null`: a nullable optional collapses "unchanged" and "remove" into one value in generated libraries. The two are mutually exclusive (`dependentSchemas`), and at least one detail is required (`minProperties: 3`, as `vtc/storage/configs/update` does). I chose these over a root `anyOf`/`not` because those turned the generated Rust `Payload` into a four-variant enum.
- **Idempotent:** if every given value already matches, the answer is `changed: false`, nothing is written, `detailsUpdated*` doesn't move, and no audit row is written. Tags compare as sets.
- **Errors:** `vtc/rooms/community/update:notFound` (including a room the community only hosts) and standard `permissionDenied`.
- **Lifecycle:** any state the community still owns the room in. A lapsed or dormant room is the one an administrator most needs to recognise.
- **No optimistic concurrency:** no `vtc/rooms/community/*` task uses a version precondition. A lost rename is visible and repairable, and both writes are in the audit trail with their reasons. That differs from room records (`rooms/records/put` `expectedVersion`), where a lost write loses content.
- **Audit:** one record per executed change, carrying the requester, the room, the previous and new value of each detail that changed, and `reason`.

### Where the details live, and who sees them

They are the community's **owner-side** record, kept beside the room. They are never put in its host record (`HostedRoom`), its records or credentials, or anything sent on its host path, including `rooms/owner/register` to the VTA. That host path already forbids a description for member-owned rooms, whose names the community as host never learns. This task answers only for rooms the community owns.

- **Label and description:** `vtc.rooms.manage` holders (community `get`/`list`), and each member a room is offered to (`offers/list` 0.2, which shows the room's details *as they stand when read*, so a rename reaches open offers).
- **Tags:** `vtc.rooms.manage` only.
- **`vtc.rooms.admin` alone:** sees none of them. The host view (`vtc/rooms/list`/`get`) looks the same for every stored room, whoever owns it.
- All three are administrator-written free text or identifiers. They must not carry personal data or credentials, and readers (including wallets and agents) must not treat them as instructions.

### Live events

The `rooms` topic of `vtc/admin/events/subscribe` 0.2 covers the **host** view for `vtc.rooms.admin`, which carries no room details, so an update produces no hint. That is consistent with the topic as specified. A hint for other administrators' consoles would need a topic for the owner's view in a later events version; this PR doesn't expand that spec.

### Known gap (not in this PR)

An **admitted** member sees the label/description only while their offer is still listed. No member-side read of "rooms of this community I'm in" exists yet, so a later rename doesn't reach admitted members. A future `vtc/rooms/memberships/list`-style task would close this.

## What VTI must implement

- `vtc/rooms/community/update/0.1`: store label/description/tags and `details_updated_{at,by}` on the owned-room record, not the host record. Gate on `vtc.rooms.manage` with no step-up. Write nothing on a no-op. Write an `AuditEvent::CommunityRoomChanged` with a new event `detailsUpdated` carrying before/after label, description and tags plus `reason` (`CommunityRoomChangedData` needs those fields). `notFound` for hosted-only rooms.
- Serve `create`/`get`/`list` 0.2 (description, tags, `detailsUpdated*`, `tag` filter) and `offers/list` 0.2 (current description, no tags) beside the 0.1s.
- `cnm` / admin console: show the description and tags, plus edit and filter controls.
- Classify the new task in `vta_sdk::retry_safety`. It is idempotent by value, but replay-sensitive, which is why `issuedAt` is required.

## Checks

`npm run validate`, `npm run build`, codegen + `cargo fmt`, TS/Go/Dart bindings regenerated, `npm run check-bindings` (all four agree), `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features vtc,validate --test conformance -- vtc::rooms` (67 pass).

title: feat(vtc): renew the community's own authority over the rooms it owns before it lapses
body:
P13: the VTC renews the community's own `admin` authority over each room it owns before it lapses. This implements `vtc/rooms/community/create` item 6's SHOULD ("renew it well before it lapses") using only tasks the community's VTA already serves. No spec change is needed.

## Design
- **Sweeper** (`vtc-service/src/rooms/community_renewal.rs`, new module; `rooms/community.rs` untouched): runs every 5 minutes. It picks each room whose `ownerAuthorityValidUntil` is within `[rooms.community] authority_renew_within_days`. That setting is new and optional, defaults to 30 and is capped at half of `authority_valid_days`. For each room the VTA issues a fresh **membership + `admin` authority** (`rooms/owner/issue-membership/0.1`, `rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.2`, same four actions). The membership is renewed with the authority because create gave both the same expiry.
- **Replacement in place**: each credential goes to `vault/credentials/receive` with the `id` of the one it renews. The VTA's room oracle refuses a persona holding two VACs from one room (`principals` → Conflict), so adding one alongside the old would break every admission and removal. Create now records the handles `receive` answered (`authority-renewal:<room>` in `community_rooms`). Rooms created earlier find theirs with `vault/credentials/query` (issuer + type) + `get` (subject = this community). That path needs **`vault-read`** on the VTC's entry at the VTA. The documented grant lacks it, so the docs and the failure message say how to add it.
- **Remote first (R2.1)**: the new `ownerAuthorityValidUntil` is the one local write, made after the VTA holds both credentials. If a pass is cut off, the next pass renews again under the same handles, and the VTA still ends with one of each.
- **One retry owner**: the sweeper retries; nothing inside an attempt does. Backoff runs 1 min doubling to 6 h, with jitter, persisted in the record. No lock is held across an await: the config read guard is dropped before any VTA call, and the owner's record is re-read before it is written.
- **Failures are visible**: every failure logs at `warn` (`error` once the authority has lapsed). Audit row `CommunityRoomChanged`: `authorityRenewalFailed` when a run of failures starts, `authorityRenewed` on success. `vtc/rooms/community/{get,list}` carry `ext["org.openvtc"].authorityRenewal` (`CommunityRoom` is closed, so nothing goes in the room object). The console shows a "renewal failing" chip with the reason and the next attempt. `put_room` hints the `rooms` topic (`vti_rooms::observe::changed` is crate-private; `admin_events::notify(Topic::Rooms)` is the VTC's equivalent).
- **Skipped**: community rooms off, no VTA link, no VTC DID; a room no longer hosted here, owned by someone else at its host, or `reclaimable`. A room whose authority has already lapsed **is** renewed: the VTA holds the room's key, so that is how such a room recovers.
- **No "renew now"**: no spec task defines one.

## Tests
`vtc-service/tests/it/community_authority_renewal.rs` uses a stand-in VTA with a real-shaped vault, where `receive` with an existing `id` replaces:
- renews inside the window; not outside it (default and configured window)
- VTA unreachable → recorded, audited, shown in get/list `ext`; no retry before the backoff, then renews
- cut off after the VTA stored the authority → the next pass (a fresh process's state) finishes, still one credential of each
- rooms that are not hosted, transferred or reclaimable are skipped
- a room from before this change is found in the VTA's vault, and another subject's credential from the same room is left alone
- a lapsed authority is renewed
- off or unlinked → no-op
- unit tests for backoff bounds, the window cap and the status shape; console vitest for the list chip and the detail text

## Pre-merge checklist (R-rules)
- R1.1: success is never read off a bare send; every step waits for the VTA's `#response`
- R1.2/R1.3: no new HTTP client; no lock across an await
- R2.1: remote first, idempotent on re-run
- R3.x: wire types are the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs` payloads/responses; nothing new on the wire
- R6.2: renewal status comes from the last attempt and goes back to `ok` on success

handle of the one it replaces: the VTA refuses to act for a persona holding
two authority credentials from one room, so a copy beside the old one would
stop every admission and removal. A create now records the handles the VTA
answered (`authority-renewal:<room>` in the community_rooms keyspace); for a

title: feat(rooms): revocation — a removal takes effect at the host at once
body:
## What this changes

Today a member removed from a data room keeps every credential the room gave them (VMC + VAC chain), and the host honours those until `validUntil`. On sealed rooms the MLS removal stops them opening *new* content, but they can still read everything the host serves, fetch blobs, the commit relay and the key chain, and write into the room. On `open` rooms removal withdraws nothing at all. This PR makes a removal take effect **at the host, immediately**: from the moment the host accepts the withdrawal it refuses the removed party's credentials — and anything delegated from them — on every task.

| Spec | Version | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json` | in place (additive defs + prose) | `RevocationList`, `RevocationEntry` (`credential` / `subject` / `room`), `RevocationHead`; two normative paragraphs on `AuthorityPresentation` |
| `rooms/revocations/put` | **0.1 (new)** | Admin → Host: deliver the room-signed list; host enforces it at once, on every task and version |
| `rooms/revocations/get` | **0.1 (new)** | Admin → Host: read the held list (confirm enforcement; recover a lost list) |
| `rooms/owner/revoke` | **0.1 (new)** | Owner → KeyHolder: sign the next list as the room, keep it, push it to every host |
| `rooms/owner/group/remove` | **0.2** | Withdraw first, then advance the group; `signingKeyId` REQUIRED; `mirrors`; refuses `private` |
| `vtc/rooms/community/members/remove` | **0.2** | `open`/`attributed`: the member's (and an open offer's) credentials withdrawn at the host; answer carries the list head |
| `group/remove 0.1`, `owner/claim 0.1`, `vtc/.../remove 0.1` | in place, editorial | Prose that said "nothing in this family is revoked" now points at the mechanism |

Registry + Rust/TS/Go/Dart bindings regenerated (the `AuthorityPresentation` description change reaches every rooms module's doc text).

## Design rationale

### Options considered

1. **W3C Bitstring Status List via `credentialStatus`.** Rejected. The host would have to *fetch* the list — the same reasons this family forbids dereferencing a chain's `parent` apply: verification depends on the list server's availability, every check signals credential use to it, and the location is chosen by the issuer/holder. A cached list is stale by its TTL, which is not "immediate". Its privacy comes from herd size, which a room's few dozen credentials do not have. And every existing credential would need re-issuing with a status entry.
2. **Host-held list fed only by a push (no room signature).** Rejected. It is the host's own state: unverifiable by the next host, lost on migration, and it makes the host part of the membership — what the family's invariants are built to avoid ("a host that consults state of its own has made the room unmovable").
3. **Room-signed, cumulative, sequenced list, pushed to each host — chosen.** The list is *room* state, not host state: signed with the room's key, carrying every live withdrawal, numbered. Pushed (outbound from the owner's key holder), so it needs **no inbound surface at the owner's VTA** and **no fetch at the host**. Any host it reaches makes the same decision, so it is portable; `rooms/revocations/get` makes it re-derivable from any host holding it. It is never published (privacy): it goes only to hosts serving the room.

### Keying: credential id, subject + time, or room + time

- `credential` — one credential by `id` (e.g. a leaked agent VAC). Permanent for that id.
- `subject` — every link whose subject **or issuer** is the party, with `validFrom < revokedAt`. Issuer-matching withdraws what they delegated, and no re-admission revives it. Keyed on time, so **re-admitting the same DID works**: fresh credentials have `validFrom` after the entry and verify; nothing has to be un-revoked (and nothing may be).
- `room` — every credential with `validFrom < revokedAt`: a reset after compromise, and the only kind permitted on a `private` room.

A chain containing any revoked link is refused whole; the membership credential is checked too. A credential with no `validFrom` is treated as issued before every entry (fail closed).

### Who may revoke

Only the **room** signs a list (the same entitlement as minting chain roots — `rooms/owner/issue-authority`): one signer, one sequence per room, which is what keeps rollback detection a comparison of two integers. Any **admin** may *deliver* a room-signed list (`rooms/revocations/put`), so hosts can be brought up to date without the key. Delegator-signed lists were considered and rejected: every delegator becomes a second signer each host must sequence and protect from rollback, and the host holds state for parties the room never named. A member withdraws an agent's credential by its short expiry, or by asking the room to revoke it by `credentialId`.

### Rollback, equivocation, migration

- A host accepts only a **higher sequence**, and only a list that keeps every live entry it holds (append-only; an entry may be dropped only after its `until`). Lower → `stale` (with `heldSequence`); same sequence, different list → `sequenceConflict` (evidence the room's key is signing in two places); dropped live entry → `notAppendOnly`. Nothing changes on refusal.
- The deliverer's `admin` presentation is checked against the **held** list, not the delivered one; the list's own authority is the room signature.
- The key holder keeps the list with the room key (backed up with it), signs serially, and **must deliver the list to a host it registers the room with before answering the registration** — so a room moving hosts arrives with its withdrawals. A key holder restored from an old backup recovers via `rooms/revocations/get`, taking the highest sequence among hosts.
- A 24h margin on dropping expired entries keeps clock skew from tripping the append-only check.

### Immediacy, on every path

From acceptance, with nothing cached: records, blobs (including storage-target issuance), epoch mint / commit relay / key chain, info, usage, succession, and the revocation tasks' own presentations — at every version the host serves, including pre-existing ones. Acceptance and authorization are serialized per room, so no mutation verified before acceptance commits after it; a multi-step upload is re-authorized at each step and its commit refused. **Residual window, stated honestly:** a presigned storage target already issued is a bearer URL at a store the host may not control and lives out its (minutes-long) lifetime; no new one is issued.

### Interplay with `group/remove` and the VTC

`group/remove 0.2` **withdraws first, then advances**: there is no instant where the member is outside the group but still credentialed (the reverse order lets a removed party write records labelled with the new epoch, which the host cannot tell from real ones). If the withdrawal lands and the advance fails, the member is refused at the host and holds keys only to the epoch the room was already at. At the host the two are independent requests, each effective on acceptance in whichever order they arrive — a host must not wait for one to apply the other (on `private` it could not tell which leaf left anyway). Pending-removal crash safety follows 0.1: everything (advance + signed list) retained durably before any send; settle on next request.

### `private` rooms

The host verifies membership in zero knowledge and does not know who the member is, so a `credential`/`subject` entry is both inapplicable and a disclosure of who was in the room — the host refuses such a list (`entryNotPermitted`). Only `room` resets apply, and a host must refuse any presentation for which it cannot establish no credential predates the latest reset. `group/remove 0.2` therefore refuses `private` (`privateRoom`) rather than silently resetting everyone; the owner chooses 0.1 (group only) and/or `rooms/owner/revoke` with a `room` entry. Per-member immediate revocation on `private` needs a ZK non-revocation proof, which waits on the private-room profile (itself unsettled).

### Errors

Revoked credentials are refused with the framework's standard **`permissionDenied`**, identical to any other failed presentation — no `credentialRevoked`. A distinct code would tell whoever holds a captured credential that its withdrawal was noticed and propagated, and tell a removed party which host has caught up; it matches the family's existing discipline of opaque chain refusals. The *administrator* delivering a list gets specific codes (`stale`, `sequenceConflict`, `notAppendOnly`, `listInvalid`, `entryNotPermitted`) — only after their `admin` presentation verified.

### Issuer ↔ proof-key binding

`AuthorityPresentation` now states plainly that every credential (membership and each authority link) must be verified with a key the credential's **own `issuer`** lists for `assertionMethod`, and a proof by any other key is refused however well it verifies; the same binding applies to the room-signed list. This is a clarification of what "verify every link" already means, made in place.

### Versioning (SPEC §5.2 / §6.6)

Least churn that is still normative: the cross-cutting rule lives in **`rooms/revocations/put` 0.1** (a host that *accepts* a list takes on enforcement for every task it serves for that room) and is mirrored in the shared `AuthorityPresentation` description. It is conditional on having accepted a list, which only the new task can produce, so no existing task's conformance changes for a host that does not implement it — hence **no MINOR bumps of records/*, blobs/*, epoch/***. Shared defs are additive (precedent: #739, #747). `group/remove` and `vtc/.../members/remove` change behaviour and response shape → new MINOR directories. Prose pointers in 0.1 specs are editorial → in place.

### Threat model (summary)

| Threat | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Removed member keeps acting until expiry | Room-signed list; host refuses from acceptance, every task/version |
| Agent delegated by removed member | `subject` matches issuer too; any revoked link refuses the chain |
| Forged withdrawal / reinstatement | Room signature with a room `assertionMethod` key; append-only; admin-only delivery |
| Rollback (host, relayer, old backup) | Monotonic sequence; `stale`; key holder keeps list, recovers highest sequence |
| Room key used in two places | Same-sequence different-list → `sequenceConflict`, held list kept, surfaced as a security signal |
| Host migration loses withdrawals | Key holder must deliver list on registration; `get` to re-derive |
| Revocation oracle | Opaque `permissionDenied` |
| Membership disclosure on `private` | Only `room` entries permitted there |
| Malicious host ignores the list | Not preventable (the host is the enforcement point); the signed `head` + `inForceAt` make its claim checkable |
| Presigned target already issued | Bounded by target lifetime (minutes); no new issuance |

## What VTI will need to implement

- **Host (`vti-rooms`, `vti-rooms-dtg`)**: store one `RevocationList` per room (durable, migrated with the room); `rooms/revocations/{put,get}` with the accept rules; check membership + every chain link against it in `ChainVerifier::verify` (credential id, subject/issuer + `validFrom`, room floor); serialize list acceptance against authorization per room; refuse with the same `Forbidden`. **Bind each credential's `verificationMethod` to its `issuer`'s DID** in `open_credential` (it currently checks only that the proof verifies under the named method).
- **VTA (key holder)**: per-room list storage (backed up, in `BACKED_UP` keyspaces), serialized signing as the room, `rooms/owner/revoke`, `rooms/owner/group/remove` 0.2 (withdraw → advance, pending-state settle), deliver the list on `rooms/owner/register`; recovery via `get`; classify the new Trust Tasks in `vta_sdk::retry_safety`.
- **VTC**: `vtc/rooms/community/members/remove` 0.2 (open → owner/revoke; attributed → group/remove 0.2; private → group/remove 0.1), withdraw an open offer's credentials too; update the remove notice in `community_room_tasks.rs` and `docs/03-vtc/data-rooms.md` §5/§10.
- Bump `trust-tasks-rs` to pick up the generated types.

Spec PR only — not for merge by me.

title: feat(vtc): run membership-sync jobs waiting on a backoff now — sync-jobs/retry/0.2
body:
## Problem

Adding a trust registry to a running VTC queues a publish job for every existing member. The first failures put those jobs on an exponential backoff that reaches an hour. `retry/0.1` only requeues **failed** jobs, so an operator who had fixed the cause could only wait. #2153 made the console say so ("4 retrying — next in 12m"). This PR lets the operator act on it.

## Change

- **Serves `vtc/registry/sync-jobs/retry/0.2`** (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#802, `trust-tasks-rs` 0.31.13) beside 0.1:
  - `jobId` also accepts a pending job waiting out its backoff.
  - `allWaiting: true` brings every such job forward.
  - Requeued jobs have their attempts reset and are due on the next tick, through the same `sync_jobs_cli::requeue` mutation as before.
  - Each requeued job is reported with `from: failed | pending`.
  - An **RTBF-batched job is held** and never brought forward, whichever member names it (`skipped: held`). The batch window is what keeps a removal from being timed back to the request that caused it.

- **Console** moves to 0.2:

- Workspace floor raised to `trust-tasks-rs` 0.31.13.

## Tests

- `tests/it/registry_admin.rs`:
  - `allWaiting` moves only backing-off jobs and resets their attempts.
  - A held job is never released, by `jobId` or by `allWaiting`.

title: security: a credential's proof must be made by a key of its issuer
body:
## Defect

`DTGCredential::verify_proof_with_public_key` verified the Data Integrity proof under the key the caller passed, but never checked that the proof's `verificationMethod` belongs to the credential's `issuer`. A caller that resolves the method the proof names and then trusts `issuer()` accepted a credential naming any issuer, signed by any key. `verify_grant_with_public_key` already made this check; the credential-level entry point did not.

## Fix

One private helper, `check_proof_from_issuer`, now runs after the signature in both public verification entry points:

| Entry point | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `DTGCredential::verify_proof_with_public_key` | no binding | binding |
| `verify_grant_with_public_key` | binding (inline) | same binding, shared helper |

`authority::verify_chain` and `delegation::verify_chain` check no signatures themselves (by design, documented); they rely on each link having gone through `verify_proof_with_public_key`, so they gain the binding through it. No other public function verifies a proof.

A method belongs to the issuer when:
- the DID before its `#` is exactly the issuer (`did:x:a#key-1`), or
- it is the issuer itself, with no fragment, or
- it is a bare `#fragment`, read against the issuer (previously refused by the grant path).

Comparison is verbatim (a DID URL with a query or path before the fragment is not the issuer); an empty issuer matches nothing. On the grant path the issuer may be a string or an object with an `id`.

## Compatibility

- **Not API-breaking.** `DTGCredentialError::ProofNotFromIssuer` already existed and the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`. No version bump here; CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]`.
- **Behaviour change:** a credential signed with a key whose id is not a method of the issuer no longer verifies. Two unit tests signed with randomly-named keys and were given issuer-bound key ids.

## Tests

`tests/issuer_binding.rs`, each case against both entry points: another DID refused; a DID that merely extends the issuer's refused; a DID URL with a query refused; a method of the issuer accepted; the issuer itself as the method accepted; a relative `#fragment` accepted; object-form issuer bound by its `id` (accept and refuse).

Locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-features`, `cargo test --no-default-features`, `cargo check` on 1.95.0, `cargo package`, and both examples run.

title: fix(vtc): the sync queue's Pending tile says when backing-off jobs retry
body:
## Problem

After a trust registry is added to a running VTC, the syncer walks the audit log from the start and queues a publish job for every existing member. Jobs that fail once wait out an exponential backoff (up to 1h). The console's Pending tile then read **"4 — nothing waiting"**: `oldestPendingAgeSeconds` counts only jobs *due now*, so a queue that is waiting looked idle.

## Change

- `vtc/registry/diagnostics/0.1` response gains `ext["org.openvtc"].backingOff`: `{ count, nextAttemptAt? }`, meaning pending jobs waiting on a retry backoff and the soonest next attempt. RTBF-held jobs are excluded (they have their own `rtbfBatchedCount`). It is under `ext`, so there is no spec change.
- The console's Pending foot: `oldest Xm` when a job is due, else `N retrying — next in Xm` / `next attempt due`, else `nothing waiting`.
- `openapi.json` + `wire.ts` regenerated.

## Follow-up

A "Run now" control for backing-off jobs needs `vtc/registry/sync-jobs/retry/0.2` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#802), since 0.1 only requeues failed jobs. It lands after that ships in `trust-tasks-rs`.

## Tests

- `tests/it/diagnostics.rs`: backing-off count + soonest retry, RTBF exclusion, empty queue.
- `admin-ui/src/plugins/recognition/pending.test.ts`.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: the full suite passed. The admin-UI-embedding tests were re-run with the UI built.
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings`, `npm run lint` (wire:check + tsc) and `vitest` (1077) all pass.

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): Community rooms tab — create and run rooms the community owns
body:
Adds the console pages for P13 (community-owned data rooms): a **Community rooms** tab on Data rooms, rather than a new menu entry.

## What the pages do

- **`/rooms/community`**, shown to holders of `vtc.rooms.manage` (a `vtc.rooms.admin`-only viewer keeps the host's three tabs; a manage-only viewer lands here from `/rooms`). Lists each room the community owns: label, tier, lifecycle, admitted / offered counts, and `ownerAuthorityValidUntil` (flagged 30 days ahead, "lapsed" after).
- **Off by default**: with no `[rooms.community]`, the tab shows the section to add, from the list's `ext["org.openvtc"].communityRooms`.
- **New community room** (header button, `?create=1`, and a ⌘K action): label, tier (`attributed` default, `open`; `private` shown disabled — not served for community rooms and refused by the shipped policy), history (`chained`/`fromJoin`), retention days, storage location (listed only to `vtc.rooms.admin` holders), reason.
- **`/rooms/community/<room DID>`**: the room's facts and its members, filtered All / Offered / Admitted / Removed. **Add a member** → an offer (DID, `read`/`write`/`curate`, days valid, reason). **Remove** / **Withdraw** shows what removal does on the tier and the member's `validUntil` *before* anything is signed (members/remove producer item 1), takes a reason, and reports `validUntil` and `epoch` from the answer (item 2).

## Step-up

`create`, `members/add` and `members/remove` go through `postSignedWithStepUp`, as the ACL and admission pages do: the VTC answers `permissionDenied` + `details.stepUpRequest` (`acl::bound_step_up`), the console's confirm dialog is the click the passkey (or the wallet plugin's step-up approver) runs in, and the identical signed document is sent again. Nothing is parked — the server never parks these.

## Refusals carry the fix

`noKeyHolder` (the server's message names the config, plus the `pnm acl create … --capabilities key-mint,credential-write,vault-write` the VTA needs), `visibilityNotPermitted` (the rooms policy, `room.communityOwned`), `unknownStorageConfig`, `keyHolderUnavailable` (and the DID it may have minted, from `details.roomId`; for a removal, "remove again"), `keyHolderRefused`, `notAMember`, `alreadyMember`, `notInRoom`, `notFound`, and `permissionDenied` without a step-up (missing `vtc.rooms.manage`).

## Wire types

`vta_sdk::openapi` gains transparent wrappers for the `vtc/rooms/community/*` payloads and responses (additive — new structs only), registered in the VTC's OpenAPI components; `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` regenerated, aliased in `wire-types.ts`. The two listings are pinned in `list-limits.json` (100, as the schemas say) with census entries.

## Live updates — a spec gap, not hand-rolled

`vtc/admin/events` 0.2's `rooms` topic already hints when a community room is **created** (room registration fires `vti_rooms::observe`), and these pages sit under the `["rooms"]` query key so they re-read on it. But producer rule 4 names only hosted rooms, lifecycle, usage bands and storage configs, and the topic goes to `vtc.rooms.admin` holders. An offer, an admission or a removal is in no topic, and a `vtc.rooms.manage`-only administrator gets no `rooms` stream. Hinting membership changes would go outside rule 4 (and the fingerprint would swallow them anyway), so the pages poll once a minute instead, and the gap is recorded in `community-rooms.md`. Closing it is a dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf change (a topic for the owner's record, read with `vtc.rooms.manage`).

## Docs

`community-rooms.md` (a console section; "What is not here yet" now lists portal offers and the live-topic gap), `data-rooms-quickstart.md` §12 (console path), `website-and-admin.md` (the `rooms` row and the Community rooms poll), `data-rooms-files.md` P13 row.

## Verified locally

- admin UI: `npm run wire:check`, `tsc -b --noEmit`, `vitest run` (93 files, 1088 tests), `npm run build`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `UPDATE_OPENAPI` snapshot regenerated and `openapi_snapshot` / `console_list_limits` green; `vta-sdk` openapi + generated-wire-types census green

title: spec(vtc/registry/sync-jobs/retry): 0.2 — bring a job waiting on its backoff forward
body:
## Why

`vtc/registry/sync-jobs/retry/0.1` requeues only jobs in the terminal `failed` state. A pending job waiting out its retry backoff is skipped as `notFailed`, and that backoff reaches an hour. An operator who has just fixed what the registry was refusing — or who added a registry to a community that had been running without one, which queues every existing member — has no way to stop members waiting.

## What 0.2 changes

- **Payload**: exactly one of `jobId`, `allFailed: true` or `allWaiting: true` (new).
  - `jobId` now accepts a `failed` job or a `pending` job that is waiting out a backoff.
  - `allWaiting` brings forward every pending job that is waiting out a backoff. It is separate from `allFailed` because repairing work the reconciler gave up on and hurrying work it hasn't are two different decisions.
- **Held jobs are never brought forward.** These are jobs delayed on purpose, for example a removal batched so it cannot be timed back to a right-to-be-forgotten request. They are skipped as `held`, and the spec forbids any member, extension or version that releases one.
- **Skip reasons**: `notFailed` is replaced by `inFlight` (being dispatched now) and `held`. `notFound` is unchanged.
- **Response**: `requeued[].from` (`failed` | `pending`), required.
- The attempt count is reset for both kinds of job.

0.1 is unchanged. All four libraries are regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart), `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --test conformance` pass.

## Consumer

openvtc VTC (`verifiable-trust-infrastructure`) — the admin console gets a "Run now" for the membership-sync queue once this ships in `trust-tasks-rs`.

title: feat(vtc): hidden-vetting publish and withdraw park for administrators' consent (VTI-APV-023)
body:
Follow-up to #2149. VTI-APV-023 (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#66, which now says this explicitly) treats publishing or withdrawing hidden vetting on a criterion as a change to the join criteria. #2149 left `vtc/vetting/hidden/{publish,withdraw}` ungated; this PR gates them.

## Behaviour

| Operation | Kind | Approvers |
|---|---|---|
| `vtc/vetting/hidden/publish` that changes the stored parameters (on, relabel, drip/tick, add/approve/remove an event) | `join.criteria.hiddenVetting` | other holders of `vtc.vetting.manage` |
| `vtc/vetting/hidden/withdraw` from a criterion that has hidden vetting | same | same |

- The gate runs last, after every refusal the tasks declare, and just before the criterion is written. The requester's gesture comes first, then the operation parks; the N-th approval re-runs the task (VTI-APV-017). The consent is pinned to the stored criterion.
- A publish of exactly what is stored, or a withdraw with nothing to withdraw, asks nothing.
- Single-administrator mode applies the change on the gesture, audited `Critical` with `VTI-APV-023`.
- An event approval stays in the requester's name: the second administrator consents to it and does not become its approver.

## Why a sibling act, not `ChangeJoinCriteria`

`Act::ChangeHiddenVetting` shares the pin and the requirement with `ChangeJoinCriteria`, but it is a separate act. These tasks are gated on `vtc.vetting.manage`, not `vtc.surface.admin`. With the same act, approvers would be surface admins, and a vetting-manage-only requester would fail the requester re-check at execution. Approvers and that re-check follow the capability that makes the change.

## Console

There are two new pinned templates (server and `action-summary.ts`, 40 → 42) with shared vectors. `publishHiddenVetting` / `withdrawHiddenVetting` go through `postSignedWithStepUp`. The hidden-vetting section shows a parked change as a success.

## Tests

- `hidden_vetting_tasks.rs` runs its harness in single-administrator mode and answers each step-up with the signer's passkey (a new `Gesturer::approval`), so every publish and withdraw goes through the gate.
- New two-administrator tests:
  - `vti_apv_023_publishing_hidden_vetting_parks_and_completes`
  - `vti_apv_023_withdrawing_hidden_vetting_parks_and_a_decline_keeps_it`
  - `vti_apv_022_a_sole_admin_publishes_hidden_vetting_on_the_gesture`
- The template URIs come from the generated `Payload::TYPE_URI`, not literals, so a default build's conformance census doesn't count tasks it can't serve as bound.
- Local runs, all green:
  - `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3206 tests
  - the same with `--features vtc-service/vetting-pcs`: 3252 tests
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, and clippy `-p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs`
  - doctests and `fmt --check`
  - admin-ui `vitest` (1077 tests) and `tsc -b`

feat(vtc): hidden-vetting publish and withdraw park for administrators' consent (VTI-APV-023) (#2151)

Hidden vetting is a way of meeting a join criterion: turning it on lets an
applicant prove vetting without naming the vetters, and turning it off takes
that route away. Under VTI-APV-023 (dtgwg-vti-spec#66, now explicit about
it) that is a change to the criteria, and #2149 left vtc/vetting/hidden/
{publish,withdraw} ungated.

- Both tasks now settle consent right before they write the criterion, after
  every refusal of their own: the requester's bound gesture, then parked as
  Act::ChangeHiddenVetting (kind join.criteria.hiddenVetting) for the other
  holders of vtc.vetting.manage; the N-th approval re-runs the task against
  the criterion as it is then (VTI-APV-017), pinned to the stored criterion.
- A sibling of Act::ChangeJoinCriteria rather than the same act: the tasks
  are vtc.vetting.manage's, not vtc.surface.admin's, so the approvers and the
  requester's re-check at execution follow the capability that makes the
  change. The pin and the requirement are shared.
- A publish that leaves the stored parameters exactly as they are, and a
  withdrawal from a criterion with nothing to withdraw, ask nothing. An event
  approval is still recorded in the requester's name; the second
  administrator consents to it.
- Single-administrator mode waives it on the bound gesture, audited Critical.
- Two pinned summary templates (server and console, shared vectors); the
  console's hidden-vetting section asks for the gesture and shows a parked
  change as sent for approval.

Tests: the hidden-vetting suite runs its community in single-administrator
mode and answers each gesture, so every publish and withdraw goes through the
gate; new vti_apv_023_* tests park, approve and decline with two
administrators.

Docs: join-criteria.md, vetting.md, admin-access.md, vtc-action-list.md,
CLAUDE.md.

title: feat(witness)!: witness 0.2 — the member presentation and personhood outcome evidence as spec members, and vta/witness/list (#1068)
body:
Spec first: trust-tasks-tf #799 (trust-tasks-rs 0.31.11) and #800 (0.31.12). Two commits.

### 1. Witness 0.2 — the `ext` stop-gaps become spec members
- **`witness/session/submit/0.2`** carries `memberPresentation`; **`vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.2`** carries `outcomeEvidence`. `witness/session/0.2` exists because the outcome-evidence declaration is per initiating version (SPEC §7.3 item 20), so the versions pair one to one.
- **Only 0.2 is served** (no compatibility shims). The `ext["org.openvtc.witness"]` carriage is retired: never read, never written.
- **vti-witness**: serves `witness/session{,/submit}/0.2` (0.1 → `unsupportedVersion`). `memberPresentation` is read as received, relied on — and verified whole — only where the identity asks for membership evidence; `communities = ["*"]` ignores it; it never counts for anything else. The member DID may not be either party or the witness. A submit on a session whose stored document is not 0.2 is `challengeMismatch`.
- **VTA**: `vta/witness/{open,present,accept}/0.2` (conventions `vta/_shared/0.6`). `memberLinkUnsupported` and `[witness] member_link_witnesses` are gone (an old config still loads, with the standard unknown-key warning). A session record not opened at 0.2 is `sessionUnknown`.
- **VTC**: `personhood/assert/0.2` only; `outcomeEvidence` read as received (1–16 whole documents). An entry's terminal type is the one its session document's own version declares (`submit/0.1` for a 0.1 session, `/0.2` for 0.2, never crossed).
- **Census**: main already took the generated join/consent codes (#790). The four supplement `challenge*` codes it had to baseline are now witnessed by a new test (`a_refused_supplement_challenge_says_which_way`), and `UNWITNESSED_CEILING` drops 13 → 9.

### 2. `vta/witness/list/0.1`
Reads back every VWC `accept` stored, each with its evidence **exactly as stored** (vault tags `witness:session` / `witness:outcome`), so a client that lost `accept`'s answer, or a second device, can rebuild its record. `witness-request` gate; only active entries in contexts the caller may act in; an unknown or unreachable DID filter is an empty page, never an error; oldest first, `pageSize` ≤ 100, opaque cursor, `cursorInvalid`. SDK `witness_list`, `retry_safety` ReadOnly, mobile `WitnessTask::List` (whose builder now checks the payload against the schema before signing).

### openvtc consequence
openvtc (vta-sdk 0.69) still calls `vta/witness/*/0.1` and puts outcome evidence in `ext` on `personhood/assert/0.1`. Against a VTA/VTC with this change those are `unsupportedVersion` — it fails closed, and openvtc must move to 0.2 with this release (follow-up PR there).

### Local
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, after rebasing on main: workspace nextest (6146; `audit_coverage` timed out under load and passes alone), `vtc-service`/`vtc-client` nextest (3199 passed), the hidden-vetting tests under `--features vetting-pcs`, doc tests.

Adds **VTI-APV-023** to the Approvals chapter: a change to configuration that decides who may become a member (join/admission criteria), what evidence counts (the trusted-witness list), or who is recognised as a person (personhood policy) SHOULD require consent from an administrator other than the requester — every add, replace or removal, not only a loosening. Tied to VTI-CMP-090 (configuration change is governance change) and VTI-VTC-022 (policy confers no authority); VTI-APV-022 (single-administrator mode) now lists it among the recommendations it governs.

Also registers the current community-node behaviour in Appendix F.5a (trusted-witness list already gated; join criteria and personhood policy are not yet).

title: feat(vtc): join criteria and personhood policy changes park for administrators' consent (VTI-APV-023)
body:
Implements **VTI-APV-023** (spec PR trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#66): changes to the configuration that decides who may become a member, what evidence counts, and who is recognised as a person take a second administrator's consent. The trusted-witness list already did (#2140); this adds the join criteria and the personhood policy.

## What parks

| Operation | Kind | Approvers |
|---|---|---|
| `vtc/schemas/accepts/register` (new criterion, or any changed requirement / admission / description) and `vtc/schemas/accepts/delete` | `join.criteria.change` | other holders of `vtc.surface.admin` |
| `policy/upsert`, `policy/activate` for purpose `personhood` | `policy.recognition.change` | other holders of `vtc.policy.admin @ policy:personhood` |

Same machinery as #2140: requester's operation-bound gesture, then parked (202 + `trust-task-next-step`), runs on the N-th approval with every check re-run (VTI-APV-017). The consent is pinned to the stored criterion or the active personhood revision. Single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022) waives it on the bound gesture, audited `Critical`. An unchanged re-save and a write the handler would refuse ask nothing. First-boot default seeding is ungated.

## The personhood / `decides_authority` choice

Personhood is **not** added to `PolicyPurpose::decides_authority`. That predicate also decides `Capability::is_authority_conferring` for `vtc.policy.admin @ policy:<purpose>`, so adding it would make granting or removing personhood-policy admin an APV-018/-019 act. Recognising a person confers no authority. What needs a second party is each change. Instead there is a new `decides_recognition()` and `requires_consent()` (= authority ∨ recognition), plus a separate `Act::ChangeRecognitionPolicy`, so approvers are told the policy decides recognition, not authority, and the requirement is VTI-APV-023 rather than VTI-VTC-022.

## Console

There are four new summary templates, pinned in the server and in `action-summary.ts` with shared vectors. `saveCriterion` / `deleteCriterion` now go through `postSignedWithStepUp`, and the editor and panel show a parked change as a success toast.

## Not covered

Hidden-vetting `publish` / `withdraw` write parameters onto a criterion through their own tasks and are not gated here. Whether VTI-APV-023 should reach them is a follow-up decision.

## Tests

- New: `vti_apv_023_*` in `unrestricted_admin_consent.rs` (add parks and completes, delete parks and a decline keeps it, unchanged/refused ask nothing, action voided when the criterion moves, personhood upsert + activate park, personhood capability stays non-conferring). Also `single_admin_mode.rs` (sole admin on gesture, audited with `VTI-APV-023`; refused without the mode).
- Suites that registered criteria only as setup now seed them through the store (`common::signed::seed_criterion`). The registration-path tests (`surface_verbs_spine` round trip, hidden-vetting "saving keeps hidden vetting") now go through the gate with a second approver.
- Local: `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` green after fixes, plus doctests, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `fmt --check`, admin-ui `vitest` (1073) and `tsc -b`.

body:
feat(vtc): join criteria and personhood policy changes park for administrators' consent (VTI-APV-023) (#2149)

Who may become a member, what evidence counts and who is recognised as a
person are the inputs every membership decision follows from. #2140 put the
trusted-witness list behind a second administrator; the join criteria and the
personhood policy it feeds were still one administrator's to change alone.
VTI-APV-023 (dtgwg-vti-spec#66) recommends second-party consent for all three.

- vtc/schemas/accepts/register and /delete park as Act::ChangeJoinCriteria
  (kind join.criteria.change) for the other holders of vtc.surface.admin, after
  the requester's operation-bound gesture. Every change parks: a new criterion,
  any changed requirement, admission mode or description, and a removal. A
  re-save of a criterion exactly as stored is no change, and a write the
  handler refuses (invalidQuery, notFound, ...) is refused before any gesture.
  The consent is pinned to the stored criterion, so another write to it voids
  the action; the N-th approval re-runs the handler (VTI-APV-017).
- policy/upsert and policy/activate for the personhood purpose park as
  Act::ChangeRecognitionPolicy (kind policy.recognition.change) for the other
  holders of vtc.policy.admin @ policy:personhood.
- Personhood is deliberately not added to PolicyPurpose::decides_authority:
  that predicate also makes vtc.policy.admin at the purpose
  authority-conferring (Capability::is_authority_conferring), which would turn
  granting or removing it into an APV-018/-019 act. Recognising a person
  confers no authority; what needs a second party is each change. A new
  decides_recognition predicate and requires_consent (= authority or
  recognition) drive the gate instead, and approvers are told the policy
  decides recognition, not authority.
- Single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022) waives both on the bound gesture,
  audited at Critical. Seeding default criteria at first boot is not gated.
- Four new summary templates, pinned in the build and in the console, with
  shared vectors. The console's criteria editor and removal ask for the
  gesture and show a parked change as sent for approval.

Hidden vetting's publish/withdraw, which write parameters onto a criterion
through their own tasks, are not gated here.

title: feat(rooms)!: rooms/keys/act 0.3 — a member takes up a community's offer as themself, with only a KeyPackage their VTA minted
body:
Builds on #2146 and targets `main` so CI runs (CI does not run on PRs into a feature branch); until #2146 merges, this PR also shows its three commits. Only the last commit, `rooms/keys/act 0.3`, is new here. Serves `rooms/keys/act/0.3` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#797) beside 0.2 and 0.1; the `trust-tasks-rs` 0.31.11 floor comes from #2146.

### VTA
- **Table:** `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1` and `vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1` are actable at 0.3 only (`room_act::OFFER_TYPES`, kept apart from the 0.1/0.2 host-bound `ACT_TABLE`). No presentation is inserted. At 0.1/0.2 the request is still checked against the 0.2 schema, which refuses these types.
- **Recipient item 2b:** for the offer types `issuer` is required (`principalAmbiguous` without it, and the VTA never picks one). The VTA acts as `issuer` only where it holds a key that DID lists for `authentication` and the caller may act as it (`issuerNotPrincipal` otherwise). No room credential is required.
- **Recipient item 10 (security):** an acceptance's `keyPackage` is completed only if this VTA minted it with `rooms/keys/key-package` for that room and that member, and still holds its unused, unexpired private half. The comparison is by `KeyPackageRef` (`room_groups::holds_key_package`), never by the leaf credential. Anything else is refused `keyPackageNotHeld` and nothing is signed. The record used is the existing per-member pending-KeyPackage row (`room-kp/<room>/<member>`):
  - **used** means a Welcome consumed it (`join` deletes the row);
  - **expired** is its `expiresAt`.
- **Policy/audit subject** is the member, as at 0.2. Registered in dispatch, the conformance census and `retry_safety` (`RetrySafe`).

**Deliberate deviation from the brief:** the brief asked to "mark used on accept". I did not. Act 0.3 is `retention: transient` / "stores nothing", and the spec's "not yet used" means the private half was consumed by a Welcome. Marking it used when act completes an acceptance would make the identical retry of a lost acceptance fail `keyPackageNotHeld`. That retry is exactly what add 0.2 item 8 exists to answer. A test pins that a held KeyPackage completes twice and stops completing once a Welcome consumes it.

### SDK
- `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_3`.
- `room_act` asks 0.3 → 0.2 → 0.1 for a room request. For an offer type it asks 0.3 only, and a VTA without 0.3 surfaces `UnsupportedTaskType`.
- `room_act` now takes and returns the 0.3 generated types (**breaking**).
- `unsigned_room_request` requires `issuer` for an offer type; new `is_offer_type`.

### CLI
`pnm rooms offers list|accept --vtc <url> --vtc-did <did> --member <persona>`:
- The VTA signs each document as the persona (act 0.3). The CLI sends it unchanged to the community over Trust Task HTTPS (`VtcClient::send_signed_room_document`).
- `accept`:
  - stores the offer's membership and authority credentials in the VTA vault;
  - on a sealed room, has the VTA mint the KeyPackage against the offer's invitation;
  - accepts, then joins from the Welcome (`rooms/keys/welcome`).
- `--key-package` retries a lost acceptance identically.

Docs: `docs/03-vtc/community-rooms.md` (the "no client signs these" gap is closed), `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md`, design-note version table.

### Tests
- Offer types complete as the named `issuer`, with no presentation, `proofPurpose: authentication`, and the payload unchanged.
- `principalAmbiguous` without `issuer`; `issuerNotPrincipal` for another context's persona and for a stranger.
- 0.1 and 0.2 refuse the offer types, and an admin `vtc/rooms/community/members/add` is not actable at 0.3.
- `keyPackageNotHeld` for: a foreign KeyPackage whose leaf names the member, a non-KeyPackage, one minted for another room, one minted for another member, an expired one, and a used one (consumed by a real Welcome).
- Success path, including an identical second completion.
- An open room's acceptance needs no KeyPackage; a room request at 0.3 works as at 0.2.
- SDK: 0.3 → 0.2 → 0.1 fallback; an offer type never falls back; `issuer` is required for offer types.

### Verified locally
- Clean: `cargo fmt --check`, workspace clippy `-D warnings`, workspace doctests, vtc doctests, vta-service feature combos.
- `nextest -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3197 passed.
- Workspace nextest: 6143 passed, 1 timed out. The timeout was `audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry`, which took over 300 s while a second full suite ran on the same machine. It passes alone in 34 s, and it already took over 180 s in PR1's loaded run.

title: feat(rooms)!: rooms/owner/group/add 0.2 — a repeated admission is answered with its Welcome
body:
Serves `rooms/owner/group/add/0.2` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#795) beside 0.1 and raises the `trust-tasks-rs` floor to **0.31.11** (release #794).

### VTA — item 8 (and item 6 → 8 handover)
- The owner's VTA keeps the **last admission it applied** per room — member, the KeyPackage's `KeyPackageRef` (RFC 9420 §5.2, new `vti_rooms::mls::key_package_ref`), epoch, Welcome — as `room-admitted/<room>/<persona>` in `room_groups`.
  - Storage decision: same keyspace as the pending advance it is promoted from, which already holds the same Welcome — same at-rest encryption (`apply_encryption`), same backup membership (backed up), cascades with the member's DID. No new keyspace, so the `vta-keyspaces` partition is unchanged (doc updated). A restored row is still bounded by its `appliedAt`.
  - Discarded when the owner builds its next advance (`retain`, add/remove/renew), after 24 h (lazy on read + storage-thread sweep `sweep_retained_admissions`), and on `forget`.
- A request with the same room, string-equal `member` and equal `KeyPackageRef` is answered — after item 1 and the authorization checks — with the kept epoch/Welcome: no host contact, no advance, no new Welcome. Anything else for a member with a leaf stays `alreadyMember`. 0.1 is unchanged.
- Item 6: a pending admission promoted (including the crash-recovery "already promoted" branch) becomes the retained one, so the identical retry after a lost host answer is settled and answered with the Welcome.
- `PendingAdvance` gains `key_package_ref` (breaking for a struct literal → `!`).

### SDK
- `TASK_ROOMS_OWNER_GROUP_ADD_0_2`, `Keyed` in `retry_safety`, budget list. `room_group_add` asks 0.2 then 0.1 on `unsupportedType`/`unsupportedVersion`, and returns the 0.2 type (breaking).

### VTC
- Offer acceptance asks its VTA at add 0.2, falling back to 0.1 (as the external-issue 0.3→0.2 fallback does). A member's retry after a **lost VTA answer** now gets the Welcome; `alreadyAccepted` remains for a Welcome no longer kept or a 0.1-only VTA (comment fixed).
- `REMOVAL_NOTICE` re-cited against `members/remove` item 4 as clarified in #796 (structured members say what removal did; the `ext` notice is a courtesy).

### Collateral from the floor raise (separate commit)
0.31.11 also declares codes this VTC already minted: `vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden` (#789) and the four `challenge*` codes on `join-requests/submit/0.3` and `supplement/0.1` (#790). Constants now come from the generated types; they leave `CONSUMER_MINTED`; consentGrantForbidden and the four **submit** codes are witnessed by existing tests. The four **supplement** codes share the same arm but no test drives a supplement to its challenge, so they are **baselined** (`UNWITNESSED_CEILING` 9 → 13) — a human decision worth reviewing.

### Tests
VTA: identical retry returns the stored Welcome without advancing (and still joins); 0.1 repeat still `alreadyMember`; different KeyPackage → `alreadyMember`; after next advance / after 24 h → `alreadyMember`; sweep; item 6 → item 8 handover. VTC (`tests/it/community_rooms.rs` stand-in now serves add 0.2 item 8): retry after a lost VTA answer gets the Welcome without a second advance; 0.1-only VTA fallback and its `alreadyAccepted`. SDK: 0.2 → 0.1 fallback.

### Verified locally
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `nextest --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` (6134 passed), workspace doctests, `nextest -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (3197 passed), vtc doctests, vta-service feature combos, vti-rooms `mls` clippy + wasm32 check, vtc-service `vetting-pcs` clippy.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.12
body:
### Added

- **vta/witness**: List — read back stored witness credentials with their outcome evidence ([#800](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/800))

vta/witness/accept stores a VWC with its outcome evidence (the
  witness/session document and the witness's submit #response), and its
  answer was the client's only copy of that evidence: vault/credentials/query
  returns body-free descriptors and vault/credentials/get the credential alone.
  A client that stopped between accept returning and recording the result, or
  another device of the same principal, could see the VWC and not present it,
  since a VWC without its evidence counts for nothing at a verifier.

  vta/witness/list/0.1 returns every stored VWC the caller may read, each as
  accept answered it (credentialId, witness, relationshipDid,
  vwcDigestMultibase) plus acceptedAt and the evidence byte for byte, the VWC
  travelling once inside evidence.outcome. Filters relationshipDid and witness
  (AND-combined); pageSize (<= 100) / cursor / truncated as vta/credentials/list.
  Only VWCs in contexts the caller may act in (witnessRequest, never sign alone),
  active vault entries only; an unreachable or unknown DID matches nothing,
  never an error. Lists VWCs accepted under 0.1 and 0.2 alike. A read:
  sideEffects none, discloses secret, so request and response proofs and
  issuedAt are REQUIRED; retention transient.

  accept/0.2's "Reading the evidence back later" and the 0.6 conventions now
  point at it. Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.13`) | `0.8.12` → `0.8.13` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.12` → `0.8.13` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: spec(appendix): register vtc.rooms.admin and vtc.rooms.manage
body:
Registers the two community capabilities the data-room Trust Task specifications presuppose. C.3 listed neither.

- **`vtc.rooms.admin`** — the community's authority as a room's **host**. The room-files specifications (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #739: `vtc/storage/*`, `vtc/rooms/storage/*`, `vtc/rooms/{get,limits/set,usage}`) let a community hand room hosting to someone who is not a full administrator. Not conferring; the storage changes it gates are parked for consent by their own task definitions.
- **`vtc.rooms.manage`** — the community's authority as a room's **owner**: creating the rooms it owns, offering admission, admitting and removing members (`vtc/rooms/community/*`, dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #768). Not conferring: it grants no community authority, and the room authority the community's agent issues on it never includes `admin` on the room. It confers nothing inside a room on its holder.

Kept apart because a community may let someone run its board room without letting them reassign every room's storage, and the reverse. `community-admin`'s ceiling ("every `vtc.*` capability") includes both without change, which is the default grant to community administrators.

Implemented in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure (`Capability::RoomsAdmin`, and `Capability::RoomsManage` in #2141).

title: Specify trigger links: the QR code or link that starts an exchange with a wallet (VTI-LNK-001 – 124)
body:
## Summary

Adds a chapter, **Trigger Links** (`spec/07a-links.md`, area `LNK`, profile `Links`), for the text an inviter shows as a QR code or a link so that whichever wallet a person uses can start an exchange with it. The chapter has two parts: **the trigger-link format**, which is protocol-neutral, and **VTI's use of trigger links**, which adopts the Trust Task first request (from #59). Two flows are registered: `sign-in`, a person signing in to a service's portal (a VTC, or another service such as DID hosting) by scanning or clicking the code it shows, and `vta-claim`, a wallet claiming a VTA from a VTA Farm.

```
https://link.trustoverip.org/t#_from=<VID>&_id=<handle>&_exp=<epoch>&_type=/vti/flow/sign-in/0.1
```

## What the chapter specifies

- **The link.** An `https` URL. Every field a reader uses is in the fragment, which no server receives. Readers ignore unknown names, so appended tracking parameters don't break a link. A repeated reserved name is refused.
- **Reading.** One reading order with named reasons, and five outcomes a person sees (`update`, `expired`, `unreachable`, `pass-on`, `invalid`). The reader never says which field failed.
- **Fields.**
  - `_from` is any VID.
  - `_id` is 16–32 random bytes as unpadded base64url, with one spelling per handle.
  - `_exp` is epoch seconds, with a 60 s clock allowance.
  - `_type` is a versioned flow URI. It may be written as a path that resolves against `https` and the link's lowercased host.
- **Flows.** A registry under `https://link.trustoverip.org/vti/flow/`, governed by this specification, with MAJOR/MINOR version rules.
- **After the link.**
  - Show the contact as unverified before any network activity. There's an exception for contacts already in the reader's records.
  - Verify the DID document, and take the transport only from it.
  - Each flow states its first request (VTI-LNK-057). VTI flows sign it with a fresh Ed25519 `did:key` and carry the handle as `parentThreadId` (VTI-LNK-054).
- **Security of the handle.** It confers nothing, no GET spends it, and readers never log it.
- **Producers.**
  - Emit ASCII only.
  - Keep the `https` form within 251 bytes at QR level M, or 177 at level Q (version 11).
  - Serve pages showing a link with `no-referrer` and `no-store`, with no third-party scripts.
  - Give redirects an explicit fragment.
  - Never put the link host on the page's own domain.
- **Link host.** Association files claim only the trigger path. A no-wallet page never reads the fragment.
- **`sign-in`.**
  - `_exp` is required, at most 300 s.
  - A reader acts only for a service already in its records. For one that isn't, it sends nothing until the person adds it, offering the relationship the verified document advertises (joining a community, or using a DID hosting service), then may continue with the same link (VTI-LNK-101).
  - The contact's document must list a `SignInPortal` service, or the reader stops with `no-portal-service` (VTI-LNK-102).
  - Before the first request the reader shows its own name for the service and the verified portal origin; a different name in a signed reply is flagged before anything else is approved (VTI-LNK-104).
  - The VTC uses a 16-byte handle.
  - Includes a size-budget note.
- **`vta-claim`** (VTI-LNK-110 – 117, added after review by the VTA Farm).
  - The contact is the Farm, not the VTA. `_exp` is required, at most 300 s.
  - The Farm is a first contact, so nothing is resolved before the person continues.
  - The fresh identifier that issues the first request becomes the VTA's administrator.
  - The Farm accepts one claim per handle.
  - A claim check (SHOULD) catches a bystander who scans first: the page and the wallet both show 6 characters derived from the claimed identifier, and the person confirms they match; if not, the Farm discards the identifier and returns the VTA to the pool (VTI-LNK-115).
  - A code that adds an administrator to a running VTA is shown only to the account that already controls it, after the claim check (VTI-LNK-117).
- **The contact rule** (VTI-LNK-118 – 124). A contact qualifies by what the reader can prove, not by naming DID methods, so future methods (`did:scid`, `did:webs`, ledger DIDs) need no spec change:
  - **Route A, host-named:** the DID names the host serving its document (`did:webvh`, `did:web`, `did:webs`).
  - **Route B, domain-linked:** any other method, if the portal's origin serves a DIF Well-Known DID Configuration with a valid Domain Linkage Credential from the DID (JWT EdDSA/ES256 or `eddsa-jcs-2022`), fetched only after the person continues, and served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Failure is `domain-not-linked`.
  - A reader with no resolver for a method answers `unsupported-vid` (update). `did:key` and `did:peer` are `from-not-allowed`: a peer DID is pairwise, not a service identity.
- **Clicking the code** (VTI-LNK-056, 086, 105): a page SHOULD make its QR code a link to the same text, so a wallet on the same device can be used without scanning. A reader that sees the click, such as a browser extension, records the page's origin. For `sign-in` that origin MUST match the portal origin in the verified document (`wrong-origin`), which stops a page relaying a genuine portal code. This replaces the browser plugin's SIOPv2 login.
- **Path DIDs** (VTI-LNK-050): before the person continues, the reader shows the path as well as the domain.
- **Early resolution** (VTI-LNK-051): after a click on a page, a reader may resolve and verify the contact before the person continues (never for camera scans, pastes or `vta-claim`), and sends nothing to its services.
- **Services with several surfaces** (VTI-LNK-105), such as an operator console, serve them all from the `SignInPortal` origin.

Wiring: `specs.json`, the intro's structure and reading tables, `STRUCTURE.md`, the conformance area, profile and target tables, references, and one glossary term (`trigger link`). `Links` is MAY for every target. VTI-LNK-001 binds any target that reads, produces or hosts trigger links.

## Not in this revision

- **Agent names** in `_from` are reserved (VTI-LNK-032). Readers refuse them with `update` until three things are settled with the agent-names authors: their canonical form, what a community name resolves to, and the redirect contract.
- **The sign-in exchange after the first request** is specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#738 (`auth/oob/*`). The chapter notes that the first claimer locks the request.

## Open dependencies outside this PR

- Trust Over IP hosting `link.trustoverip.org`.
- Device tests of fragment survival across camera, browser and OS hand-offs (Keyring). If a platform drops the fragment, the link form needs another answer there.
- ~~How the VTA signs the sign-in approval documents.~~ Settled: the VTA signs `auth/oob/grant` as an attestation (`assertionMethod`), and the service signs its replies for `assertionMethod`.

## Implementations

- Browser plugin (reader): OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin #303, #315 (join flow), #316 (parser aligned with this chapter), #317 (pluggable DID methods and route B).
- VTC (producer and service): OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure #1997, #1998, #2024.
- Website library (producer): OpenVTC/rp-sdk-js #7, #9 (contact rule).
- DID hosting (producer and service): affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#253.

## Origin

Agreed between Affinidi and the Keyring authors from [keyring-wallet PR #354](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/pull/354). That PR's spec and annex will refer to this chapter, and its trigger and transport-selection vectors will be updated to this wording as the conformance vectors. The informative examples at the end of the chapter cover the cases settled in that exchange.

Rendered locally with `npm run render`: no errors.
