title: Specify trigger links: the QR code or link that starts an exchange with a wallet (VTI-LNK-001 – 124) (#58)
body:
Specify trigger links: the QR code or link that starts an exchange with a wallet (VTI-LNK-001 – 124) (#58)

* Specify trigger links: the QR code or link that starts an exchange with a wallet (VTI-LNK-001 – 104)

A new chapter, Trigger Links (area LNK, profile Links), for the text an
inviter shows as a QR code or link so that whichever wallet a person uses
can start an exchange with it. The link is an https URL whose fragment
names the contact (_from, any VID), a handle (_id), an expiry (_exp) and a
flow (_type); the fragment never reaches a server, and a reader ignores
every parameter it does not know so that appended tracking parameters
cannot break a link.

The chapter fixes the reading order and the few outcomes a person sees;
the field grammars (_id is 16 to 32 bytes of unpadded base64url with one
spelling per handle; _type may be a path resolved against https and the
link's lowercased host); a flow registry under
https://link.trustoverip.org/vti/flow/ governed by this specification;
what a reader does after the link (show the contact unverified before any
network activity, verify the DID document, take the transport only from
it, sign the first request with a fresh identifier and carry the handle as
parentThreadId); host rules; producer limits sized to QR version 11 at
levels M and Q; requirements on the link host; and the first registered
flow, sign-in.

Agent names in _from are reserved, not yet admitted. The Trust Tasks of
the sign-in exchange after the first request are specified separately.

The text was agreed between Affinidi and the Keyring authors from
keyring-wallet PR #354, which will refer to this chapter.

The Links profile is MAY for every target; VTI-LNK-001 binds any target
that reads, produces or hosts trigger links.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* Register the vta-claim flow and show the path of a path DID (VTI-LNK-050, 110 – 116)

- vta-claim: the Farm is the contact, _exp required (<= 300 s), first
  contact (no VTI-LNK-051), claim service in the Farm's document, fresh
  identifier as first-request issuer, one claim per handle, and a claim
  check against a bystander scanning first.
- VTI-LNK-050: a reader shows the path of a path DID as well as its domain,
  as agreed with Keyring and lost from the first draft.
- References: FIPS 180-4 for SHA-256; RFC 4648 base32 for the claim check.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* Let a page's QR code be clicked, and check the page's origin for sign-in (VTI-LNK-056, 086, 105)

- VTI-LNK-086: a page SHOULD make its QR code a link to the same text, so a
  wallet on the same device (a browser extension, or an app via its
  association) can be used without scanning.
- VTI-LNK-056: a reader that sees the activation records the page's origin
  and ignores activations the person did not make.
- VTI-LNK-105: for sign-in, that origin MUST match the portal origin in the
  verified DID document (wrong-origin), which stops a page relaying a
  genuine portal code.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* Keep the trigger-link format protocol-neutral; make the Trust Task first request VTI's adoption (VTI-LNK-054, 055, 057) (#59)

- VTI-LNK-054: a flow states its first request. Every first request is sent
  only after the person approves (052), only over the transport chosen under
  053, and with the handle; one the reader signs uses a key made for this
  exchange, unless the flow defines a signature by an identifier the person
  chose when approving.
- VTI-LNK-057 (new): every flow in this specification's registry uses the
  Trust Task first request, with the text 054 carried before. VTI-LNK-113
  now points at 057.
- VTI-LNK-055: discovery when `_type` is absent goes through a protocol both
  sides implement; `trust-task-discovery` is the Trust Tasks case.
- Design principles, stated at the top of the chapter and grounded in the
  specification's own: the Abstract's "deliberately modular" DTG components,
  and Layering's rule that what an artefact is belongs to its component.
  Modular (any kind of first request), no central party (any host, any flow
  URI, the same shorthand for every host), and simple inside VTI. A note
  proposes moving the trigger-link format to its own component
  specification later, deferred until the format has settled.
- The chapter is split in two parts. "The trigger-link format" holds every
  protocol-neutral section, one heading level down. "VTI's use of trigger
  links" holds the first request for VTI flows (057), the flow registry
  (046, moved out of Flows), and the sign-in and vta-claim flows. Sections
  move; no requirement is renumbered.
- Flows: any party may define a flow under an https URI it controls without
  registering it here; the registry holds the flows this specification
  defines.
- The link-host note: a shared host is a convenience for camera scans, not a
  requirement; a link on any host meeting the host rules is equally valid.

No VTI flow, outcome or other requirement changes.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* spec(links): apply review feedback and align with the implementations

- VTI-LNK-054 is again the Trust Task first request (fresh Ed25519 did:key
  issuer, handle as parentThreadId, sent after approval over the 053
  transport), in the VTI part; VTI-LNK-057 is the format's general rule that a
  flow states its first request. Implementations cite 054 for the Trust Task
  request; 113 points at 054. The chosen-identifier exception now requires
  the flow to state why it needs one and the reader to tell the person which
  identifier the inviter will see; no registered flow uses it.
- VTI-LNK-115: discard, not revoke. New VTI-LNK-117: an add-device vta-claim
  code is shown only to the account that controls the VTA, and the claim check
  is required before the identifier is written. Note on adding a device
  replaced (geoffturk).
- sign-in generalised from community to service (101, 104, intro, table):
  a service not in the reader's records gets nothing until the person adds
  it; the reader may then continue with the same link.
- VTI-LNK-102: SignInPortal service required (no-portal-service); contact
  rule is a capability allow-list (method names its host, document lists
  services, document verified), in practice did:webvh and did:web. 112 uses
  the same rule.
- VTI-LNK-104: show the recorded name and the verified portal origin; flag a
  different name from a signed reply before further approval.
- VTI-LNK-051: early resolution after a person's page activation, never for a
  camera scan, a paste or vta-claim, and never contacting the services.
- VTI-LNK-105: several sign-in surfaces are served from the SignInPortal
  origin. VTI-LNK-055: `untyped`. VTI-LNK-084: registrable domain.
- Note on the exchange that follows: auth/oob/* (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#738),
  first claimer locks, later claims get alreadyClaimed.
- Precision (bmiller59): non-DID _from is unsupported-vid; /@ is tested
  before DID syntax; the absolute _type form gets the path form's constraints
  plus lowercase scheme and host, no userinfo or port; empty path segments are
  bad-type; wrong-host compares the path without its version; host rules apply
  to the host a DID endpoint names. New example rows for each.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(links): qualify contacts by what the reader can prove, not by DID method

Replace the method-capability contact rule of VTI-LNK-102 (and 112 by
reference) with two routes. Route A (host-named: did:webvh, did:web,
did:webs) needs no further check. Route B (domain-linked) admits any other
method once the portal's origin is linked to the DID by a DIF Well-Known DID
Configuration, fetched only after the person continues. A reader without a
resolver for a method stops with unsupported-vid; from-not-allowed is kept
for contacts no route can qualify. Adds VTI-LNK-118 to VTI-LNK-124 and the
domain-not-linked reason.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(links): refuse did:peer contacts; serve the DID configuration with open CORS

VTI-LNK-118 now refuses a did:peer contact by either route: a peer DID is
for one pairwise relationship, not a service's public identity, and cannot
be updated in public. VTI-LNK-124 requires the route B DID configuration to
be served with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and no credentials, so that
browser and extension readers can read it. The did:peer example row now
shows from-not-allowed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(links): allow showing the contact in the reader's own window; a portal host is not a different name

title: feat(vta/witness): list — read back stored witness credentials with their outcome evidence
body:
`vta/witness/accept` stores a Verifiable Witness Credential with its **outcome evidence** — the `witness/session` document and the witness's `witness/session/submit` `#response` — and its answer was the client's only copy of that evidence. `vault/credentials/query` returns body-free descriptors and `vault/credentials/get` the credential alone, so a client that stopped between `accept` returning and recording the result, or a second device of the same principal, could see the VWC and could not present it: a VWC without its evidence counts for nothing at a verifier (SPEC §4.9.4).

Found while syncing witnessing records in OpenVTC (OpenVTC/openvtc#495), which closes the gap except for that crash window. Implementation tracking: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1068.

### `vta/witness/list/0.1`

- **Request:** optional `relationshipDid` (the VWC's `credentialSubject.id`) and `witness` (its `issuer`), AND-combined; `pageSize` (≤ 100) and `cursor`, as `vta/credentials/list`.
- **Response:** `witnessings[]`, each `{credentialId, witness, relationshipDid, vwcDigestMultibase, acceptedAt, evidence}` — what `accept` answered plus the time it stored it — with `truncated` and `cursor`. `evidence` is the shared `witness/_shared/0.1` `OutcomeEvidence`, each document exactly as stored, never re-serialised. The VWC travels once, inside `evidence.outcome`, as in `accept`.
- **Rules:** only VWCs `accept` stored (0.1 or 0.2) in contexts the caller may act in, active vault entries only; capability `witnessRequest`, never `sign` alone; a filter naming an unknown or unreachable DID matches nothing, never an error; ordered by `acceptedAt`.
- **Front matter:** `sideEffects: none`, `exposure.discloses: secret` (credential material), so request and response proofs and `issuedAt` are REQUIRED (the build enforces a proven response for secret disclosure); `retention: transient`; one error code, `cursorInvalid`.

`accept/0.2`'s *Reading the evidence back later* and the `vta/_shared/0.6` conventions now point at it. Bindings regenerated for Rust, TS, Go and Dart.

Local: `npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `check-bindings` (all agree), conformance tests, `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, `go build`/`go vet`, `dart analyze`.

title: feat(rooms): a community's member portal uses shared rooms through window.vtaWallet.rooms
body:
P7b — the page-facing room channel. **Stacked on #330** (files act as the persona); retarget to `main` once that merges. Design: VTI `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md` §8.5 (VTI PR linked from there).

## What a page gets

`window.vtaWallet.rooms.{list, choose, forget, info, browse, read, putNote, getFile, putFile}`. Every call names `hostDid` — the community whose portal the page is.

`requestTask` / `signTrustTask` still refuse the whole `rooms/` family (`page-task-policy.ts`, wording updated to name this route). The methods fix the verb, run the flow in the extension, and return **views the wallet built** (`PageRoomView`, `PageRecordView`, …) — never a task reply, presentation, signed document or key.

## Gates (`room-page-background.ts`), in order, before the offscreen document does anything

1. **Well formed** (`roomsPageParamsRefusal` / `roomFilesPageOpenRefusal`).
2. **The community's own portal**: the page's browser-attested origin must equal the origin of `hostDid`'s first usable `SignInPortal`, resolved and verified as the trigger-link sign-in does (domain-linked contacts need their DID Configuration). Host requests go to the same document's `TrustTaskHTTPS`.
3. **Shared by the member**: a room's DID names no host and `rooms/keys/list` returns identifiers only, so the member ticks rooms in the wallet's own window (`confirm.html?kind=room`). Each ticked room is confirmed with the host as the member (`rooms/info`) before it is shared. Grants `(origin, hostDid, vtaDid, roomId)`, 30 days, revocable in the console (new *Rooms shared with portals* panel). **A private room is never shared with a portal** — its host is not to learn who reads, and the portal is the host's page.
4. **Every write confirmed** (note or file), naming room, signing persona, and what is written; no "remember".

Downloads: the background holds the offscreen document's provisional pieces and releases them only on `got` (whole file verified); dropped on failure.

## Also
- `consent-window.ts`: a decision can carry `selectedRooms`.
- CI: new guard — `provider.js`, `content.js`, `background.js` name no `rooms/*` task URI.
- CLAUDE.md: "A portal page uses rooms through the wallet's own methods (P7b)".

## Tests
`tests/room-page.test.mts` (16): origin/portal refusal, grant scoping and lapse, choose (host-confirmed, private refused, untick unshares), reads need a share and never prompt, write confirmation, download held until verified, failed download releases nothing, upload confirm → ready → bytes → record, declined upload opens no transfer, record bodies verified before a view is built. Full `npm test`, `npm run build`, and every CI bundle assertion green locally.

title: feat(rooms): files act as the member's persona, never the wallet
body:
First of two PRs for data-room P7b/P8 (VTI `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md` §8.5). The page channel follows, stacked on this.

## What changes

Every request the room's host receives is now **the member's**:

- built **unsigned** here and completed by the member's VTA **as the persona** (`rooms/keys/act/0.1`, new `@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms` `actAndSend` / `roomsKeysAct`), then sent unchanged (`RoomHostChannel.sendCompleted`);
- a record body is signed by the VTA as the persona and sealed in one call (`rooms/keys/seal/0.2`, `signAsPrincipal`; `writeSealedAsMember`);
- a proxied upload's chunks, commit and abort are signed by a `did:key` minted in the offscreen document for that one upload (`rooms/blobs/upload/*/0.2` `uploadKey`), then dropped.

The wallet's own DID is only the caller of the VTA tasks; no host sees it (the fake host in `rooms.file-engine.mjs` asserts that on every request).

`roomsKeysAct` checks the completed document before anything is sent: same id, type, recipient, payload (apart from the inserted presentation), issued and signed by the member named.

## Why

The engine (P7a, #327/#328) presented for the wallet's DID (`rooms/keys/present`) and signed record bodies with the wallet key, so an `attributed` room recorded the wallet's `did:key` as member and author — a DID the room never admitted. User decision: rooms act as the persona DID, never the client `did:key`. This is the CLI's flow (`pnm rooms file put/get`, VTI #2107 / #2110 / #2108) step for step, so a file either writes opens in the other.

## Proxied, for now

Browser transfers ask for proxied mode (begin omits `directParts`, get asks `direct: false`). A direct target is on the storage provider's origin, which the extension holds no permission for and cannot ask for outside a gesture on its own page. Recorded in §8.5 as a follow-up.

## Also

- `@openvtc/trust-tasks` floor `^0.26.9` (act, seal 0.2, blobs 0.2).
- `task-surface.json` resynced from vta-sdk 0.69.0; coverage 213 → 216 (act, plus `rooms/info` / `rooms/records/get`, which the SDK now names).
- CLAUDE.md: "The member is the persona, never the wallet".

## Tests

`npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (all workspaces) green locally; the CI bundle assertions (file-key confined to offscreen, etc.) run locally green.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.11
body:
### Added

- **vtc/members**: Registry-consent — a member grants or withdraws their own trust-registry consent ([#798](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/798))


### Specifications

- **witness**: Add 0.2 — a member presentation on submit, and outcome evidence on personhood/assert, replace the ext stop-gaps ([#799](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/799))

Two members implementations carried in a vendor extension,
  ext["org.openvtc.witness"], become specified members, so any witness and
  any community reads them.

  - witness/session/submit/0.2: optional memberPresentation — a VP by the
    member DID, for authentication, bound to the session's challenge and
    domain, carrying the eligibility credentials (a membership credential
    naming the member DID). Neither party nor the witness; a failure where
    relied on is presentationInvalid; a witness not using it MUST NOT treat it
    as satisfying anything. The member DID never appears in the VWC, and the
    witness keeps neither it nor the presentation. Privacy: links the pairwise
    relationship DID to the member DID at the witness; proves co-possession in
    one session, not one person; the alternatives are recorded.
  - witness/session/0.2: same payload; its outcomeEvidence names
    submit/0.2#response. The declaration belongs to the initiating document's
    specification (SPEC §7.3 item 20, §4.9.4 check 3), so a 0.1 session cannot
    close with a 0.2 submit. Versions pair one to one.
  - vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.2: optional outcomeEvidence (1–16
    entries, each {session, outcome} carried byte for byte). A VWC counts only
    from a trusted witness, paired by §4.9.4's four checks and the witnessing
    checks; unpaired entries are ignored. A member presents only the VWCs it
    selects.
  - witness/_shared/0.1/outcome-evidence: OutcomeEvidence, shared by
    personhood/assert/0.2 and vta/witness/accept/0.2.
  - vta/witness/{open,present,accept}/0.2 + vta/_shared/0.6 conventions:
    conduct 0.2 sessions; present puts the member presentation in
    memberPresentation; open drops memberLinkUnsupported; a 0.2 session is
    continued only by 0.2 tasks. The 0.1 tasks are unchanged.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

- **rooms/keys**: Act 0.3 — a member takes up a community's offer of a room as themself, with only a KeyPackage their key holder minted ([#797](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/797))

`vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1` and `vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1` must be signed
  as the DID the community addressed its offer to. That DID is the member as
  the community knows them — typically a persona their key holder holds — so
  no surface the member acts from can sign either, and `rooms/keys/act/0.2`
  could not complete them: its `type` pattern admits only `rooms/`, and its
  closed table lists neither. A member could be offered a room and never
  reach it.

  act 0.3:
  - The table gains `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1` and
    `vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1`, with no presentation inserted: the member
    holds no room authority yet, and the community checks the offer against
    the document's proof. The `type` pattern admits `vtc/rooms/offers/` beside
    `rooms/` and nothing else of the vtc family (new invalid example: an
    administrator's `vtc/rooms/community/members/add` is refused by schema).
  - Producer item 2: `issuer` REQUIRED for the offer types (the DID the offer
    is addressed to); `recipient` is the community.
  - Recipient item 2b (new): for the offer types, act as `issuer` iff the
    recipient holds a key `issuer`'s DID document lists for `authentication`
    and the caller may act as it; `issuerNotPrincipal` otherwise,
    `principalAmbiguous` when absent; never pick for the caller. No room
    credential is required.
  - Recipient item 10 / Producer item 5 (new): an acceptance's `keyPackage`
    is completed only when the recipient minted it with rooms/keys/key-package
    for that room and that member and still holds its private half (unused,
    unexpired), compared by KeyPackageRef, never by its leaf credential;
    otherwise the new code `keyPackageNotHeld`.
  - Security & Privacy: why item 10 is required — a KeyPackage the key holder
    did not mint becomes the member's leaf with keys someone else holds (the
    client), opening every later record and signing group messages as the
    member outside the key holder and beyond any withdrawal of the client's
    standing; the leaf credential is signed by the leaf key, not the member's
    DID, so the community cannot tell, and only the minting key holder can.
    And why the offer types belong in act rather than a task of their own:
    same entitlement, same delegate refusal (item 3), same closed table — one
    signing-as-the-member surface to audit, not two — and a key holder that
    accepted itself would call the community and route the answer, which item
    7 rules out.
  - Examples: an acceptance completed as the member; a `keyPackageNotHeld`
    refusal.

  vtc/rooms/offers/{list,accept}/0.1, in place: one paragraph each under
  Authorization pointing a surface without the member's keys at act 0.3.
  Prose only; their wire is unchanged (SPEC §5.2 editorial, as #783).

- **rooms/owner/group**: Add 0.2 — a repeated admission is answered with its Welcome, not alreadyMember ([#795](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/795))

`rooms/owner/group/add/0.1` item 6 settles a pending admission at the next
  request, which keeps the room and the owner's group in step across a lost
  host reply. But the next request is, in the case that matters, the same
  request again: the caller lost the answer and retries. 0.1 settled the
  pending admission, found `member` already in the group, and refused the
  retry `alreadyMember`. The Welcome — the only way the newcomer can join —
  was returned to nobody. The same happens when the recipient applied the
  admission and its own reply to its caller was lost. `vtc/rooms/offers/accept`
  already promises its callers that retrying is safe; under 0.1 it was not.

  add 0.2:
  - Item 8 (new): the recipient keeps, with the group state, the last
    admission it applied for the room — `member`, the KeyPackage's
    `KeyPackageRef` (RFC 9420 §5.2), epoch, Welcome and ratchet tree — until
    its next advance of the room or 24 hours, whichever comes first. A request
    naming the same room, the same `member` (string-equal) and a KeyPackage of
    the same `KeyPackageRef` is answered, once item 1 and the authorization
    checks pass, with that admission's epoch, Welcome and tree; the recipient
    does not advance the room, contact the host, change its group or build a
    fresh Welcome. Anything else for a member with a leaf is `alreadyMember`.
  - Item 6 hands over to item 8 when the pending admission it applies is the
    one the request repeats.
  - New section *Repeating an admission*: why re-serving is safe (the Welcome
    is HPKE-sealed to the KeyPackage's init key and addressed by its
    KeyPackageRef, RFC 9420 §12.4.3.1; the joiner discards the private half on
    use or expiry, so a late copy opens nothing), why the match is exact (equal
    KeyPackageRefs mean byte-identical KeyPackages, hence the same init key; a
    different KeyPackage for the same member would be a second leaf), and why
    retention is short.
  - `alreadyMember` and `hostUnreachable` meanings updated; retention and
    exposure rationales say what is kept. No code added; payload and response
    schemas unchanged.

  vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1, in place: "Repeating an accept" now points at
  group/add 0.2 items 6 and 8, says the community repeats its own request to
  its VTA unchanged, and that the community's VTA serves group/add at 0.2 or
  later. Prose only; its wire is unchanged, and it now describes what its own
  existing retry promise requires (SPEC §5.2 editorial, as #783).

- **vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root**: A member may recover a lost enrolment answer within the same label ([#791](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/791))

pcs-root/0.1 refused every second enrolment under a label as
  alreadyEnrolled. That is right for counting, but it made a lost answer
  unrecoverable for the rest of the label: if the community issued and the
  answer never reached the vetter in a form it could open (late arrival, a
  client restart losing the blinding state, a transport drop), the vetter
  held no credential and was locked out of hidden vetting until the next
  vetter/<YYYY-MM> label. This happened in a live run.

  vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root/0.1 (draft, in place per SPEC §5.2), new
  "Recovering a lost answer" section under Authorization:
  - A community MAY answer a second request under a label the member is
    enrolled in with a fresh issuance over the new blinded request, when its
    `id` is the one recorded for the member. Every first-enrolment check still
    applies (live grant, proof, issuedAt, wrongLabel, badRequest).
  - It MUST NOT re-issue unless its suite binds the blinded request to the
    secret `id` is derived from, so every credential under one `id` yields
    the same tags. That binding is what stops a re-issue counting as a second
    vetter; without it the community refuses with alreadyEnrolled.
  - A different `id` is still identifierRebound. No second enrolment is
    recorded. Re-issues SHOULD be bounded per member per label, refused beyond
    the bound with alreadyEnrolled, and audited.
  - What this gives up is "exactly one credential object per member per
    label", not "each member counted once". Distinctness is by tag.
  - Client note: re-run vta/pcs/root-request for the label (it replaces the
    blinding state and keeps the key, so the `id`), send, and pass the answer
    to vta/pcs/root-accept. alreadyEnrolled now means the community does not
    re-issue, or no longer will for this label.

  The alreadyEnrolled meaning, the proof rationale and the "record only after
  signing" note say the same. hidden/publish/0.1's pointer to pcs-root no
  longer says a second enrolment is impossible. Bindings regenerated.

  The issue's alternative, an administrator task to clear an enrolment, is
  not taken: re-issuance under the same `id` recovers without an operator
  and without a record of the member's enrolment being erased.

- **vtc/join-requests**: Submit and supplement say why a hidden-vetting challenge was refused ([#790](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/790))

A hidden-vetting proof is bound to a single-use challenge issued over
  vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge, and the community spends that challenge when it
  counts the proof. Neither vtc/join-requests/submit nor
  vtc/join-requests/supplement declared a code for a refused challenge, so
  implementations fell back to malformedRequest. An applicant could not tell
  an expired challenge from a spent one, or either from a client bug.

  submit/0.2, submit/0.3 and supplement/0.1 (draft, in place per SPEC §5.2)
  each declare four codes under the task's own name, none retryable:
  - challengeNotIssued: no challenge held for the applicant's DID;
  - challengeAlreadyUsed: spent by an earlier submission or supplement;
  - challengeExpired: past expiresAt, details MAY carry expiredAt (the
    details schema does not close the object, so an implementation's own
    markers still validate);
  - challengeMismatch: bound to a value other than the open challenge,
    which this attempt spends.

  A new "Hidden-vetting challenge" section in each says where the proof
  travels (extensions.hiddenVetting), that counting it spends the open
  challenge whether or not the applicant is then admitted, that the message
  never echoes the challenge value, that the value is discarded on use, and
  that a value-free spent marker MAY be kept until expiry so a repeat attempt
  is told challengeAlreadyUsed rather than challengeNotIssued. Recovery is a
  new challenge and a new proof. submit/0.3 adds that a producer SHOULD name
  its criterion on a hidden-vetting submission. supplement/0.1's
  `extensions` is no longer described as wholly uninterpreted, and
  pcs-challenge/0.1's Retention permits the spent marker and points at the
  codes.

  The issue's note about several hidden-vetting criteria spending one
  challenge is moot: vtc/vetting/hidden/publish refuses a second criterion
  (otherCriterion, #734). Bindings regenerated (Rust ERROR_CODES).

- **vtc/members/update**: PublishConsent may be withdrawn by an administrator, never granted — consentGrantForbidden ([#789](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/789))

A member's consent to trust-registry publication is the member's own
  privacy decision, given with `registryConsent` on vtc/join-requests/submit.
  update/0.1 listed `publishConsent` among the fields an administrator may
  change with no direction, so an administrator could raise it and publish
  someone who said no.

  vtc/members/update/0.1 (draft, in place per SPEC §5.2):
  - `publishConsent` MAY lower consent (true -> false, e.g. a takedown) and
    MAY restate the current value. It MUST NOT raise it: consent becomes true
    only through the member's own registryConsent on a join submit, including
    a rejoin, which writes a fresh member record.
  - New error vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden (not retryable),
    checked after notFound and adminRoleForbidden. A refused raise rejects the
    whole update; no other field in the request is applied.
  - A withdrawal: the community SHOULD remove the member's published registry
    record at its next sync, and MUST NOT publish the member again until the
    member consents anew.
  - Security & Privacy says why consent runs one way. Bindings regenerated.

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.31.10` → `0.31.11` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.31.10` → `0.31.11` | patch |

| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.31.10` → `0.31.11` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.31.10` → `0.31.11` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.31.10` → `0.31.11` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.31.10` → `0.31.11` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.31.10` → `0.31.11` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.11` → `0.26.12` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.12`) | `0.8.11` → `0.8.12` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.11` → `0.8.12` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(witnessing): sync witnessing records through the VTA's app state
body:
A witnessing was kept only in this installation's protected config, so a second device never listed it, and a crash between `vta/witness/accept` and the local save left the VWC in the VTA's vault with nothing pointing at it.

**What changes**
- New app-state record kind `v1/witnessing/<hash of the session id>` (`openvtc-core/src/vta_sync/records.rs`). The value is the local `WitnessRecord` whole, outcome evidence included — the same choice VRC records make for their credentials. It applies live. Removing a relationship's witnessings tombstones them at the VTA through the existing diff.
- **Remote-first** (R2.1): the witnessing job writes the record to the VTA create-only (`vta_sync::put_new`) as soon as `accept` returns, before the loop thread saves it locally. An installation that crashed in between pulls it at the next launch; one that did save pushes the same record create-only, loses the race and merges it as identical, with no conflict reported. A failed write is logged and loses nothing.
- `Witnessings::push` replaces a record of the same session: a running sync can pull the job's record before its outcome is applied.
- `docs/design/vta-authoritative-state.md` lists witnessings among the synced records.

**Why not reconcile from the vault.** The VTA keeps the evidence in the vault entry's reserved tags (`witness:session`, `witness:outcome`). `vault/credentials/query` returns body-free descriptors and `vault/credentials/get` only the credential, so no client task reads the evidence back, and a VWC without its evidence counts for nothing at a VTC. The remaining window — a crash between `accept` returning and the app-state write, one round trip — needs a spec change to close (a task, or a `get` member, returning a stored VWC's evidence), so it is not built here.

**Tests** (`openvtc-core/src/vta_sync/tests.rs`): a witnessing reaches another device whole; two devices' witnessings merge in time order; removal tombstones everywhere; the crash window (recorded before the save) survives and converges; a record pulled before its outcome is kept once; a record under another key is refused.

Local: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `clippy -p openvtc --features dev-overrides`, `cargo doc`, `cargo test --workspace`, `--no-default-features`, `-p openvtc --features dev-overrides` all pass.

title: feat(witnessing): sync witnessing records through the VTA's app state (#495)
body:
feat(witnessing): sync witnessing records through the VTA's app state (#495)

A witnessing was kept only in this installation's protected config, so a
second device never listed it, and a crash between vta/witness/accept and the
local save left the VWC in the VTA's vault with nothing pointing at it. The
outcome evidence a personhood assertion needs is kept by the VTA in the vault
entry's reserved tags, which no client task reads back, so the vault alone
cannot restore a witnessing either.

Witnessings are now an app-state record kind (v1/witnessing/<hash of the
session id>) carrying the local record whole, evidence included, as VRC
records carry their credentials. They apply live, and removing a
relationship's witnessings tombstones them at the VTA.

The witnessing job writes the record to the VTA create-only as soon as accept
returns, before the loop thread saves it locally (R2.1): the next launch of an
installation that crashed in between pulls it, and one that did save pushes
the same record create-only and merges it as identical. A failure to write it
there is logged and loses nothing, since the save and the next sync carry it.
Witnessings::push now replaces a record of the same session, because a sync
can pull the job's record before its outcome is applied.

What remains: a crash between accept returning and that write (one round
trip) still leaves an unlisted VWC. Closing it needs a way to read a stored
VWC's evidence back from the VTA, which is a spec change, not something to
build here.

title: feat(rooms)!: rooms/keys file-key, open and act 0.2 — removed, beyondChain, and the member as act's subject
body:
Adopts the three Trust Task versions released in `trust-tasks-rs` 0.31.10 (trust-tasks-tf #786, #787; release #788). The workspace floor moves to 0.31.10.

## VTA — served beside 0.1, which is unchanged

- **`rooms/keys/file-key/0.2`**: a file sealed at or after the member's removal is `unknownEpoch` `{reason: "removed", removedAtEpoch}` (oracle item 4: an oracle that knows of the removal MUST NOT answer `notDelivered`). 0.1's closed details schema has no `removed`, so 0.1 still says `notDelivered`, with the removal in its message.
- **`rooms/keys/open/0.2`**: `unknownEpoch` carries the declared closed details. An older epoch the retained chain does not reach is now `{reason: "beyondChain", earliestEpoch}`. Before, it was a bare validation failure, and 0.1 still answers it that way. `room_groups::OpenError` gains `BeyondChain` (the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`).
- **`rooms/keys/act/0.2`**: `subjectPath` is `/document/issuer`. The policy gate evaluates act 0.2 against the member: `issuer`, or, when it is absent, the one room member the caller may act as (`room_act::act_subject`). The 0.2 audit row names the member as its target, with type and room in the detail. Recipient item 2a (a room-less type is completed only as its `issuer`; absent → `principalAmbiguous`, never a guessed member) was already this VTA's behaviour and is now tested at 0.2.
- Dispatch table, conformance witnesses and `vta_sdk::retry_safety` entries cover the three new URIs. `vta-mcp`'s guard is slug-based and needs no change.

## Clients

- **vta-sdk (breaking, hence `!`)**: `room_act` takes and returns act 0.2's types, and `room_file_key` returns file-key 0.2's response. `unsigned_room_request` returns act 0.2's `UnsignedRoomRequest`, and it refuses a payload with neither `roomId` nor `issuer`: for chunk, commit and abort, the client must always send `issuer`. `room_open`, `room_file_key` and `room_act` ask at 0.2 and fall back to 0.1 on `unsupportedType` / `unsupportedVersion`, the same pattern as external/credentials/issue 0.3 → 0.2.
- **pnm**: the operator hears about a removed member's file from `reason: removed`, and is not sent to `keys commit`. A 0.1-only VTA's `notDelivered` that carries the removal message reads the same way.
- `vtc-client` doesn't call these tasks. `vti-rooms-wasm` only names file-key 0.1 in a doc comment, since the extension makes the call, so it is unchanged.

## Docs
`docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` (the three reasons, room-less act documents, the subject, task table), `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md`, and the quickstart: the "act sets no subjectPath" limitation is gone. Its other two bullets still hold.

## Tests
- file-key 0.2 `removed` against 0.1 `notDelivered`, and the reasons before the removal (details are checked against each version's declared schema)
- open 0.2 `beyondChain`, `notDelivered` and `removed`; 0.1 unchanged
- act 0.2: room-less types need a named issuer (`principalAmbiguous`, `issuerNotPrincipal`); audit target is the member for 0.2 and the room for 0.1; `act_subject` resolution; the policy gate decides on the member (a rego rule on `input.request.subject`)
- SDK: unsigned room-less requests need an `issuer`; file-key and act fall back to 0.1 against a wiremock VTA that serves only 0.1
- CLI hint tests updated

title: spec(witness): add 0.2 — a member presentation on submit, and outcome evidence on personhood/assert, replace the ext stop-gaps
body:
## Why

The Verifiable Trust Infrastructure carries two witnessing members in a vendor extension, `ext["org.openvtc.witness"]`, as stop-gaps (VTI #2114, #2123, #2128; tracking VTI #1068):

- **The member presentation** on `witness/session/submit`. A party submits from a pairwise relationship DID, but a community's membership credential names the member's own DID. A witness that witnesses only members of its communities cannot judge eligibility without a second presentation, by the member DID, bound to the same session.
- **Outcome evidence** on `vtc/members/personhood/assert`. A Verifiable Witness Credential counts only with the outcome evidence of the session it cites (SPEC §4.9.4), and 0.1 has no member to carry it.

Another implementation never reads a vendor extension. This PR makes both specified members.

## What changes

| Spec | Change |
|---|---|
| `witness/session/submit/0.2` | Optional `memberPresentation`: a VP held by the member DID, proven for `authentication`, bound to the session's `challenge`/`domain` like `vp`, carrying the eligibility credentials. The member DID is neither party and not the witness. A failure, where the witness relies on it, is `presentationInvalid`. A witness that doesn't use it MUST NOT treat it as satisfying anything. The member DID MUST NOT appear in the VWC, and the witness MUST NOT keep the presentation or record the member DID. Response unchanged. |
| `witness/session/0.2` | Payload unchanged. `outcomeEvidence.response` names `witness/session/submit/0.2#response`. |
| `vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.2` | Optional `outcomeEvidence`: 1 to 16 `{session, outcome}` entries, carried byte for byte. A VWC counts only if its witness is trusted, an entry pairs with it by §4.9.4's four checks, and the witnessing checks of submit pass. Entries that pair with no VWC are ignored. A member presents only the VWCs it selects. |
| `witness/_shared/0.1/outcome-evidence` | New shared `OutcomeEvidence`, used by personhood/assert/0.2 and vta/witness/accept/0.2. |
| `vta/witness/{open,present,accept}/0.2`, `vta/_shared/0.6` | The VTA party tasks conduct 0.2 sessions. `present` puts the member presentation in `memberPresentation` and never in `ext`. `open` drops `memberLinkUnsupported`, the carriage check. A 0.2 session is continued only by 0.2 tasks. |

The 0.1 versions are untouched.

### Why `witness/session` needs a 0.2 with no payload change

Under SPEC §7.3 item 20, the outcome-evidence declaration belongs to the specification of the **initiating** document. §4.9.4 check 3 takes the declared terminal type from that document's own `type`. A `witness/session/0.1` session closed with a `submit/0.2#response` would therefore carry evidence of the wrong type. The versions pair one to one:

| Session | Submit |
|---|---|
| 0.1 | 0.1 |
| 0.2 | 0.2 |

A submit in the other version is `challengeMismatch`.

## Privacy

- **The member presentation** links the pairwise relationship DID to the member DID at the witness: *which member*, not only which community. It proves co-possession of both keys in one session, not that they belong to one person; a member can lend its eligibility. It is optional and sent only to a witness whose policy asks for membership evidence. The witness keeps none of it, and the VWC never names the member DID. The alternatives that remove this correlator are recorded in submit/0.2 Correlation:
  - a membership credential naming the relationship DID;
  - a zero-knowledge membership proof;
  - a standing linkage credential;
  - recording eligibility in `witnessContext`;
  - a per-member link bound.
- **Outcome evidence** discloses both documents of each session whole (SPEC §13 item 6): both relationship DIDs, the threads and the witness. personhood/assert/0.2 requires that a member present only the VWCs it selects, and advises a community to keep neither the presentation nor the evidence after deciding.

## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate`
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`
- `npm run build-ts-bindings`, `build-go-bindings`, `build-dart-bindings`
- `npm run check-bindings`: all agree
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --test conformance -- witness personhood`: 47 pass
- `tsc --noEmit`
- `go build ./...` and `go vet` on the new packages
- `dart analyze` on the new libraries

title: spec(witness): add 0.2 — a member presentation on submit, and outcome evidence on personhood/assert, replace the ext stop-gaps (#799)
body:
spec(witness): add 0.2 — a member presentation on submit, and outcome evidence on personhood/assert, replace the ext stop-gaps (#799)

Two members implementations carried in a vendor extension,
ext["org.openvtc.witness"], become specified members, so any witness and
any community reads them.

- witness/session/submit/0.2: optional memberPresentation — a VP by the
  member DID, for authentication, bound to the session's challenge and
  domain, carrying the eligibility credentials (a membership credential
  naming the member DID). Neither party nor the witness; a failure where
  relied on is presentationInvalid; a witness not using it MUST NOT treat it
  as satisfying anything. The member DID never appears in the VWC, and the
  witness keeps neither it nor the presentation. Privacy: links the pairwise
  relationship DID to the member DID at the witness; proves co-possession in
  one session, not one person; the alternatives are recorded.
- witness/session/0.2: same payload; its outcomeEvidence names
  submit/0.2#response. The declaration belongs to the initiating document's
  specification (SPEC §7.3 item 20, §4.9.4 check 3), so a 0.1 session cannot
  close with a 0.2 submit. Versions pair one to one.
- vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.2: optional outcomeEvidence (1–16
  entries, each {session, outcome} carried byte for byte). A VWC counts only
  from a trusted witness, paired by §4.9.4's four checks and the witnessing
  checks; unpaired entries are ignored. A member presents only the VWCs it
  selects.
- witness/_shared/0.1/outcome-evidence: OutcomeEvidence, shared by
  personhood/assert/0.2 and vta/witness/accept/0.2.
- vta/witness/{open,present,accept}/0.2 + vta/_shared/0.6 conventions:
  conduct 0.2 sessions; present puts the member presentation in
  memberPresentation; open drops memberLinkUnsupported; a 0.2 session is
  continued only by 0.2 tasks. The 0.1 tasks are unchanged.

title: feat(vtc/members): registry-consent — a member grants or withdraws their own trust-registry consent
body:
After #789, registry consent is the member's own decision, and the only
place to give it was registryConsent on vtc/join-requests/submit. A member
admitted before consent existed, one who said no at join, or one admitted
by an administrator (admit, make-membership start without consent) could
become listed only by leaving and rejoining, losing credentials, role and
vetter grants. A member wanting to be unlisted had to ask an administrator.

vtc/members/registry-consent/0.1 (new, draft):
- Member-signed (issuer = the member, no target field), proof and issuedAt
  REQUIRED; the signed document is the evidence of consent.
- `publishConsent: true | false`. A restatement answers changed: false.
  A change is recorded with the document's id and issuedAt and audited;
  a grant queues publication, a withdrawal MUST queue removal and stop
  publication until the member consents anew.
- `superseded` refuses a document issued before the consent change already
  in force (the member's own, or an administrator's withdrawal), so
  out-of-order documents never undo a later decision. `notMember` for a
  signer with no live member record.
- Response: did, publishConsent, changed, registrySync
  (queued | notConfigured | unchanged), effectiveAt.

The issue's open questions:
- No registry configured: the consent is recorded anyway and governs any
  registry configured later (registrySync: notConfigured). Consent permits
  publication, it does not oblige it; a withdrawal always binds and may
  not carry a step a grant does not.
- Per-registry consent: not modelled. A community syncs to one trust
  registry and the member record holds one boolean; a per-registry model
  would be a later version.

vtc/members/update/0.1 (draft, in place): names this task as the second
way consent becomes true, and records a withdrawal's issuedAt so that an
earlier-issued member grant arriving later is refused as superseded. An
administrator who wants a member unlisted for the community's own reasons
uses publication policy, not the member's consent.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

Closes #793

title: vtc/members: a member-signed task to grant or withdraw their own registry consent
body:
## Problem
After #737 (PR #789), registry consent is the member's own decision, and it can be given in only one way: `registryConsent` on `vtc/join-requests/submit`. `vtc/members/update` can withdraw consent but never grant it.

That leaves no way back for a member who:
- was admitted before consent existed;
- answered "no" at join and has since changed their mind;
- was admitted by an administrator through `vtc/members/admit` or `vtc/members/make-membership`, whose member record starts without consent.

Today such a member can become listed only by leaving and rejoining. That costs them their credentials, their role and any vetter grants.

There is also the opposite gap: a member who wants to withdraw their own consent has to ask an administrator to do it.

## Proposal
A **member-signed** task, for example `vtc/members/registry-consent/0.1`. The member sets their own `publishConsent` to `true` or `false`.

- **Parties:** the member is the `issuer`, the community maintainer is the `recipient`. `proofRequirement` and `issuedAtRequirement` are both REQUIRED, because consent must be attributable to the member and ordered in time.
- **Authorization:** the `issuer` MUST be the member whose record changes, and no other party may use this task. The administrator path stays withdraw-only (`vtc/members/update`).
- **Effect:** `true` publishes the member at the community's next registry sync. `false` removes their published record at the next sync, as `vtc/members/update` now says for a withdrawal.
- **Response:** the resulting `publishConsent` value, and when it took effect.
- **Audit:** the consent change, attributed to the member's signed document. That document is the evidence that the member consented.
- **Consent/purpose:** scoped exactly as `registryConsent` on submit: trust-registry publication and nothing else.

## Open questions
- Should a grant be refused when the community runs no registry sync (no registry configured)? Or should it be recorded anyway, for when one is configured?
- Should the task carry the registry it consents to? Consent today is a single boolean, not per registry.

Follow-up to #737.
author: stormer78

title: spec(rooms/keys): act 0.3 — a member takes up a community's offer of a room as themself, with only a KeyPackage their key holder minted
body:
`vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1` and `vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1` must be signed
as the DID the community addressed its offer to. That DID is the member as
the community knows them — typically a persona their key holder holds — so
no surface the member acts from can sign either, and `rooms/keys/act/0.2`
could not complete them: its `type` pattern admits only `rooms/`, and its
closed table lists neither. A member could be offered a room and never
reach it.

act 0.3:
- The table gains `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.1` and
  `vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1`, with no presentation inserted: the member
  holds no room authority yet, and the community checks the offer against
  the document's proof. The `type` pattern admits `vtc/rooms/offers/` beside
  `rooms/` and nothing else of the vtc family (new invalid example: an
  administrator's `vtc/rooms/community/members/add` is refused by schema).
- Producer item 2: `issuer` REQUIRED for the offer types (the DID the offer
  is addressed to); `recipient` is the community.
- Recipient item 2b (new): for the offer types, act as `issuer` iff the
  recipient holds a key `issuer`'s DID document lists for `authentication`
  and the caller may act as it; `issuerNotPrincipal` otherwise,
  `principalAmbiguous` when absent; never pick for the caller. No room
  credential is required.
- Recipient item 10 / Producer item 5 (new): an acceptance's `keyPackage`
  is completed only when the recipient minted it with rooms/keys/key-package
  for that room and that member and still holds its private half (unused,
  unexpired), compared by KeyPackageRef, never by its leaf credential;
  otherwise the new code `keyPackageNotHeld`.
- Security & Privacy: why item 10 is required — a KeyPackage the key holder
  did not mint becomes the member's leaf with keys someone else holds (the
  client), opening every later record and signing group messages as the
  member outside the key holder and beyond any withdrawal of the client's
  standing; the leaf credential is signed by the leaf key, not the member's
  DID, so the community cannot tell, and only the minting key holder can.
  And why the offer types belong in act rather than a task of their own:
  same entitlement, same delegate refusal (item 3), same closed table — one
  signing-as-the-member surface to audit, not two — and a key holder that
  accepted itself would call the community and route the answer, which item
  7 rules out.
- Examples: an acceptance completed as the member; a `keyPackageNotHeld`
  refusal.

vtc/rooms/offers/{list,accept}/0.1, in place: one paragraph each under
Authorization pointing a surface without the member's keys at act 0.3.
Prose only; their wire is unchanged (SPEC §5.2 editorial, as #783).

Versioning: act is a new 0.3 directory, not an in-place edit to 0.2. The
table and the `type` pattern widen, a refusal is added and a code declared —
changes with wire effect, so per SPEC §5.2 a MINOR increment (#786/#787).

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart); additive modules only.

---
Found implementing community-owned data rooms in VTI (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2141): the VTC serves `vtc/rooms/offers/*` to the proven signer, but a member whose community DID is a persona their VTA holds has no client able to sign them.

Touches `specs/vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1/spec.md` in a different section from #795; both merge cleanly in either order (generated `schema_index.rs` / `index.ts` / `conformance/main.rs` may need a regenerate after the first lands).

Checked locally: `npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings`, and the generated Rust conformance tests for `rooms/keys/act` (`--features validate`).

title: spec(vtc/rooms/community/members/remove): the answer says what removal did in its structured members, not in a notice — clarified in place
body:
Item 4 required the community to "say in its record and its answer that
removal does not recall what was read", but the response schema has no
member to say it in (`additionalProperties: false`). An implementation
could comply only through `ext`, which a caller cannot depend on — so the
requirement promised callers something the wire never guaranteed.

Two ways out: add an optional `notice` member, or drop "and its answer".
This drops it, and puts the obligation where it does its work:

- Community item 4: MUST NOT represent a removal, in its record or answer,
  as recalling what was read, re-sealing what was written, or revoking the
  authority credential. The answer's structured members are what it says:
  `member.state` `removed`, `member.validUntil` (when a host stops honouring
  the authority credential), and `epoch` (sealed tier, admitted member: the
  first epoch sealed without them; absent means nothing was withdrawn
  cryptographically — an open room, or a withdrawn offer).
- Producer (new): the administrator's surface SHOULD show what removal does
  and does not do on the room's tier, and the member's `validUntil`, before
  the request is signed and before any step-up gesture bound to it; SHOULD
  report the answer from `validUntil`/`epoch`; MUST NOT report any removal
  as ending access to what was already read.
- New subsection *Why the answer carries no notice*.

Why not a field: the statement is identical for every removal on a tier, so
it carries nothing the caller cannot render from the specification, the
tier, `validUntil` and `epoch`; as a field it would be server-chosen,
unlocalised prose shown to an administrator as guidance; and it would
arrive after the decision. The moment it matters is before the requester
commits, when a bound step-up ties them to this one document — which is a
producer obligation, not a response member. An implementation MAY still
carry a statement under `ext`; a caller MUST NOT depend on one.

Versioning: an in-place edit to 0.1, not a new version. 0.1 is `draft`;
SPEC §5.2 requires an editorial change with no wire effect to be made in
place (precedent #783). Nothing on the wire moves — no schema, no code —
and every implementation conformant before stays conformant (one that
carried a notice under `ext` still may). Adding a `notice` member would have
been a MINOR version minted to carry a constant. Bindings regenerate
unchanged.

---
Found implementing community-owned data rooms in VTI (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2141), which currently satisfies item 4 with `ext["org.openvtc"].notice`.

Checked locally: `npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings`; all four bindings regenerate with no diff.

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): one Data rooms page — rooms, usage and storage as tabs
body:
Reduces the clutter in the console's Community group: **Data rooms**, **Storage** and **Room usage** become one **Data rooms** entry with tabs **Rooms · Usage · Storage**.

## Routes

| Route | What |
|---|---|
| `/rooms` | Rooms tab |
| `/rooms/usage` | Usage tab |
| `/rooms/storage` | Storage tab (`?create=1` opens New storage, as before) |
| `/rooms/storage/<configId>` | one storage location |
| `/rooms/r/<roomId>` | one room |

**Why `r/` for a room:** a room's identifier is whatever its owner minted. The `rooms/create/0.1` schema types `roomId` as a plain string, and neither `vti-rooms` (`authz::authorize_create` checks only non-empty) nor the VTC requires it to be a DID. So a bare `/rooms/<roomId>` could be `/rooms/usage`.

**Redirects:** `/rooms/<roomId>` → `/rooms/r/<roomId>`, built from the still-encoded path so a `did:web` port's `%3A` survives. The shell redirects `/storage`, `/storage/<id>` and `/room-usage` to their tabs (`lib/legacy-routes.ts`), unless a plugin registers the old path. In-app links now point at the new paths directly.

## Gating

Each tab names its own capabilities in `DATA_ROOMS_TABS` (all `vtc.rooms.admin` today) and is shown only to a viewer who holds one. A room's page and a storage location's page are gated the same way as their tab. The menu entry is registered on the **union** of the tabs' capabilities (`DATA_ROOMS_CAPABILITIES`). That means a later *Community rooms* tab on `vtc.rooms.manage` (#2141) needs one entry in that list plus a route. Holders of only `vtc.rooms.manage` would then get the menu entry and see only that tab.

## Other changes
- Command palette: Data rooms now matches "storage" and "usage". Two new actions open the Usage and Storage tabs directly.
- Live updates are unchanged. Query keys `["rooms"]`, `["room-usage"]` and `["storage"]` are kept, so the `rooms` topic still re-reads all three.
- Docs updated: `03-vtc/website-and-admin.md`, `03-vtc/data-rooms-quickstart.md`, `02-vta/data-rooms.md`, and an "as built" note in `05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md` §8.1.
- No Rust change. The admin UI is served with a history-mode fallback, so new paths need nothing from the server.

## Tests
New `plugins/DataRooms.test.tsx` covers:
- one registered entry
- the tab links and which tab is current
- the header action
- `/rooms/r/usage` reads a room called `usage`
- the legacy room redirect keeps the encoding
- a viewer without the capability gets no tab and no reads
- a room page is gated
- the `/storage*` and `/room-usage` redirects

New `lib/legacy-routes.test.ts` and palette tests were added. The existing Rooms and Storage tests now mount the combined page.

Locally (as in the "Test (VTC admin UI)" job): `npm run wire:check`, `tsc -b --noEmit`, `vitest run` (1066 passed), `npm run build`.

title: spec(rooms/owner/group): add 0.2 — a repeated admission is answered with its Welcome, not alreadyMember
body:
`rooms/owner/group/add/0.1` item 6 settles a pending admission at the next
request, which keeps the room and the owner's group in step across a lost
host reply. But the next request is, in the case that matters, the same
request again: the caller lost the answer and retries. 0.1 settled the
pending admission, found `member` already in the group, and refused the
retry `alreadyMember`. The Welcome — the only way the newcomer can join —
was returned to nobody. The same happens when the recipient applied the
admission and its own reply to its caller was lost. `vtc/rooms/offers/accept`
already promises its callers that retrying is safe; under 0.1 it was not.

add 0.2:
- Item 8 (new): the recipient keeps, with the group state, the last
  admission it applied for the room — `member`, the KeyPackage's
  `KeyPackageRef` (RFC 9420 §5.2), epoch, Welcome and ratchet tree — until
  its next advance of the room or 24 hours, whichever comes first. A request
  naming the same room, the same `member` (string-equal) and a KeyPackage of
  the same `KeyPackageRef` is answered, once item 1 and the authorization
  checks pass, with that admission's epoch, Welcome and tree; the recipient
  does not advance the room, contact the host, change its group or build a
  fresh Welcome. Anything else for a member with a leaf is `alreadyMember`.

  one the request repeats.
- New section *Repeating an admission*: why re-serving is safe (the Welcome
  is HPKE-sealed to the KeyPackage's init key and addressed by its
  KeyPackageRef, RFC 9420 §12.4.3.1; the joiner discards the private half on
  use or expiry, so a late copy opens nothing), why the match is exact (equal
  KeyPackageRefs mean byte-identical KeyPackages, hence the same init key; a
  different KeyPackage for the same member would be a second leaf), and why
  retention is short.
- `alreadyMember` and `hostUnreachable` meanings updated; retention and
  exposure rationales say what is kept. No code added; payload and response
  schemas unchanged.

vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1, in place: "Repeating an accept" now points at
group/add 0.2 items 6 and 8, says the community repeats its own request to
its VTA unchanged, and that the community's VTA serves group/add at 0.2 or
later. Prose only; its wire is unchanged, and it now describes what its own
existing retry promise requires (SPEC §5.2 editorial, as #783).

Versioning: group/add is a new 0.2 directory, not an in-place edit to 0.1.
A request 0.1 refused `alreadyMember` is answered here with a Welcome — a
change to what a conforming recipient returns, not an editorial one, so per
SPEC §5.2 a MINOR increment (#786/#787 precedent).

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart); additive modules only.

Found implementing community-owned data rooms in VTI (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2141): the community's `vtc/rooms/offers/accept` retry path, after a lost answer from its VTA, could only answer `alreadyAccepted` because `group/add` 0.1 refused the identical retry `alreadyMember`.

title: spec(vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root): a member may recover a lost enrolment answer within the same label
body:
pcs-root/0.1 refused every second enrolment under a label as
alreadyEnrolled. That is right for counting, but it made a lost answer
unrecoverable for the rest of the label: if the community issued and the
answer never reached the vetter in a form it could open (late arrival, a
client restart losing the blinding state, a transport drop), the vetter
held no credential and was locked out of hidden vetting until the next
vetter/<YYYY-MM> label. This happened in a live run.

vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root/0.1 (draft, in place per SPEC §5.2), new
"Recovering a lost answer" section under Authorization:
- A community MAY answer a second request under a label the member is
  enrolled in with a fresh issuance over the new blinded request, when its
  `id` is the one recorded for the member. Every first-enrolment check still
  applies (live grant, proof, issuedAt, wrongLabel, badRequest).
- It MUST NOT re-issue unless its suite binds the blinded request to the
  secret `id` is derived from, so every credential under one `id` yields
  the same tags. That binding is what stops a re-issue counting as a second
  vetter; without it the community refuses with alreadyEnrolled.
- A different `id` is still identifierRebound. No second enrolment is
  recorded. Re-issues SHOULD be bounded per member per label, refused beyond
  the bound with alreadyEnrolled, and audited.
- What this gives up is "exactly one credential object per member per
  label", not "each member counted once". Distinctness is by tag.
- Client note: re-run vta/pcs/root-request for the label (it replaces the
  blinding state and keeps the key, so the `id`), send, and pass the answer
  to vta/pcs/root-accept. alreadyEnrolled now means the community does not
  re-issue, or no longer will for this label.

The alreadyEnrolled meaning, the proof rationale and the "record only after
signing" note say the same. hidden/publish/0.1's pointer to pcs-root no
longer says a second enrolment is impossible. Bindings regenerated.

The issue's alternative, an administrator task to clear an enrolment, is
not taken: re-issuance under the same `id` recovers without an operator
and without a record of the member's enrolment being erased.

Closes #736

title: vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root/0.1: let a member recover a lost enrolment answer within the same label
body:
## Problem
`pcs-root/0.1` requires a community to refuse a second enrolment under a label it has already issued under (`vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-root:alreadyEnrolled`, plus the authorization check "this member has not already enrolled under this label"). That's right for counting: one credential per member per label is what makes distinct tags distinct people.

But it makes a **lost answer unrecoverable for the rest of the label**. If the community issues the root credential and the response never reaches the vetter in a form it can open, the vetter holds no credential and every retry is refused as `alreadyEnrolled`. They can't attest under hidden vetting until the next `vetter/<YYYY-MM>` label, which can be weeks away. Causes include:
- the answer arriving after the client stopped waiting,
- a client restart between request and answer, losing the blinding state,
- a transport drop, or a client defect.

This happened in a live run: the community enrolled the vetter, the client dropped the answer, and the vetter was locked out for the month. The client defect is fixed in OpenVTC/openvtc#456 and the error wording in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1961, but the protocol still has no way back. The only workaround is for the operator to republish the criterion with the next period live early, which changes the requirements digest for everyone.

## Proposal
Allow the community to **re-issue to the same bound identifier** within a label, as an idempotent recovery, instead of refusing:

- A second `pcs-root` request under a label the member is already enrolled in, **with the same `id`** (the PCS identifier recorded at first enrolment, which the spec already requires to be stable across labels), MAY be answered with a fresh issuance over the new blinded request, instead of `alreadyEnrolled`.
- Every check that applies today still applies: live vetter grant, signed request, `issuedAt` freshness.
- A request under an already-enrolled label with a **different** `id` is still refused (`alreadyEnrolled`, or the existing identifier-mismatch refusal).

**Why this looks safe for counting:**
- The member's `id` is unchanged, so any credential they end up holding derives the same per-label tags as the first.
- A member can't use two credentials to appear as two vetters: distinctness is by tag, and the tags are the same.
- What this gives up is the guarantee that the community issued exactly one credential object, not that it counts each member once.

Suite authors should confirm that re-issuing over a new blinded request with the same `id` produces identical tags and leaks nothing linkable. A rate limit per member per label (e.g. at most N re-issues) would bound abuse.

**Alternative**, if re-issuance is judged unsafe: define an administrator task to clear a member's enrolment for a label (audited), so an operator can unblock a vetter without republishing.

## Requested change
- Amend the "Two further checks" paragraph and the `alreadyEnrolled` entry in `errorCodes` to allow same-`id` re-issuance (or define the admin clear task).
- Add a short "Recovering a lost answer" note so client implementers know retrying with the same `id` is the recovery path.

title: spec(vtc/join-requests): submit and supplement say why a hidden-vetting challenge was refused
body:
A hidden-vetting proof is bound to a single-use challenge issued over
vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge, and the community spends that challenge when it
counts the proof. Neither vtc/join-requests/submit nor
vtc/join-requests/supplement declared a code for a refused challenge, so
implementations fell back to malformedRequest. An applicant could not tell
an expired challenge from a spent one, or either from a client bug.

submit/0.2, submit/0.3 and supplement/0.1 (draft, in place per SPEC §5.2)
each declare four codes under the task's own name, none retryable:
- challengeNotIssued: no challenge held for the applicant's DID;
- challengeAlreadyUsed: spent by an earlier submission or supplement;
- challengeExpired: past expiresAt, details MAY carry expiredAt (the
  details schema does not close the object, so an implementation's own
  markers still validate);
- challengeMismatch: bound to a value other than the open challenge,
  which this attempt spends.

A new "Hidden-vetting challenge" section in each says where the proof
travels (extensions.hiddenVetting), that counting it spends the open
challenge whether or not the applicant is then admitted, that the message
never echoes the challenge value, that the value is discarded on use, and
that a value-free spent marker MAY be kept until expiry so a repeat attempt
is told challengeAlreadyUsed rather than challengeNotIssued. Recovery is a
new challenge and a new proof. submit/0.3 adds that a producer SHOULD name
its criterion on a hidden-vetting submission. supplement/0.1's
`extensions` is no longer described as wholly uninterpreted, and
pcs-challenge/0.1's Retention permits the spent marker and points at the
codes.

The issue's note about several hidden-vetting criteria spending one
challenge is moot: vtc/vetting/hidden/publish refuses a second criterion
(otherCriterion, #734). Bindings regenerated (Rust ERROR_CODES).

Closes #731

title: vtc/join-requests submit & supplement: error codes for a refused PCS challenge
body:
## Summary
A hidden-vetting (PCS zero-knowledge) join submission carries a proof bound to a single-use challenge, which the community issues over `vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge/0.1`. Neither `vtc/join-requests/submit` (0.2, 0.3) nor `vtc/join-requests/supplement` defines an error code for the ways that challenge can be refused. Implementations therefore fall back to `malformedRequest` or a generic validation error. The applicant can't tell an expired challenge from an already-spent one, or either from a client bug.

This proposes four task-specific codes for each of the two tasks, under the task's own name as SPEC §8.5 permits.

## Proposed `errorCodes` additions
For `vtc/join-requests/submit` (0.3, and 0.2 if it is still maintained):

```yaml
  - code: vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeNotIssued
    meaning: The submission's hidden-vetting proof is bound to a challenge, but the community holds no challenge for the applicant's DID — none was requested, or it expired and has since been discarded. The applicant requests a new challenge over vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge, builds the proof over it, and resubmits.
    retryable: false
  - code: vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeAlreadyUsed
    meaning: The challenge the proof is bound to was spent by an earlier submission. Challenges are single-use. The applicant requests a new one, rebuilds the proof, and resubmits.
    retryable: false
  - code: vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeExpired
    meaning: The challenge the proof is bound to is past its validity window. The details MAY carry `expiredAt`. The applicant requests a new one, rebuilds the proof, and resubmits.
    retryable: false
  - code: vtc/join-requests/submit:challengeMismatch
    meaning: The proof is bound to a challenge other than the one the community issued to this applicant, typically one it replaced when the applicant asked again. The current challenge is spent by this attempt. The applicant requests a new one, rebuilds the proof, and resubmits.
    retryable: false
```

`vtc/join-requests/supplement` gets the same four codes, as `vtc/join-requests/supplement:challenge…`, for a supplement carrying the proof.

`retryable: false` is intended: retrying the *same* document can't succeed. Recovery is a new challenge and a new proof, which is a new submission.

## Why each one matters to an applicant
All four have the same remedy, but they say different things:
- **`challengeExpired` / `challengeNotIssued`:** usually time. The person was slow, or the client asked too early.
- **`challengeAlreadyUsed`:** a resubmit or a race.
- **`challengeMismatch`:** usually a client defect, such as reusing an old challenge after asking again. A client should report it as such, not as something the person did.

## Related notes for the spec text (non-normative suggestions)
- **"Discard on use":** an implementation may keep a value-free spent marker until the challenge's expiry, so a repeat attempt reports `challengeAlreadyUsed` rather than `challengeNotIssued`. The spec could say whether that's permitted. The challenge value itself must still be discarded.
- **Multiple hidden-vetting criteria:** when a community publishes more than one and the submission names none, the first criterion checked spends the challenge. Clients should name the criterion (`criterion`, 0.3) on hidden-vetting submissions.

## Reference implementation
OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1954 implements these codes in `vtc-service`. That includes the `details` shapes (`reason` marker, plus `expiredAt` for expiry) and an error-code census test that will fail once the spec defines the codes, prompting a switch to the generated constants.

title: spec(vtc/members/update): publishConsent may be withdrawn by an administrator, never granted — consentGrantForbidden
body:
A member's consent to trust-registry publication is the member's own
privacy decision, given with `registryConsent` on vtc/join-requests/submit.
update/0.1 listed `publishConsent` among the fields an administrator may
change with no direction, so an administrator could raise it and publish
someone who said no.

vtc/members/update/0.1 (draft, in place per SPEC §5.2):
- `publishConsent` MAY lower consent (true -> false, e.g. a takedown) and
  MAY restate the current value. It MUST NOT raise it: consent becomes true
  only through the member's own registryConsent on a join submit, including
  a rejoin, which writes a fresh member record.
- New error vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden (not retryable),
  checked after notFound and adminRoleForbidden. A refused raise rejects the
  whole update; no other field in the request is applied.
- A withdrawal: the community SHOULD remove the member's published registry
  record at its next sync, and MUST NOT publish the member again until the
  member consents anew.
- Security & Privacy says why consent runs one way. Bindings regenerated.

Closes #737

title: vtc/members/update/0.1: publishConsent may be withdrawn by an administrator, never granted — add consentGrantForbidden
body:
## Problem
A member's consent to be published in the community's trust registry is the member's own privacy decision. The member gives it with `registryConsent` on `vtc/join-requests/submit` (0.2, 0.3), and the community copies it onto the member record.

`vtc/members/update/0.1` lists `publishConsent` among the fields an administrator may change, with no direction. So an administrator can set it from `false` to `true`, which publishes someone who said no. Approving a join already doesn't consent on the applicant's behalf, and an update shouldn't either.

## Proposal
- **The direction rule:** `publishConsent` on `vtc/members/update` MAY lower consent (`true` → `false`, e.g. a takedown) and MAY restate the current value. It MUST NOT raise it (`false` → `true`).
- **Where consent comes from:** the only way consent becomes `true` is the member's own `registryConsent` on a join submit. That includes a rejoin, which writes a fresh member record.
- **A new error code** for the refused raise:

```yaml
  - code: vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden
    meaning: "The update would set `publishConsent` to true for a member who has not consented. Registry consent is the member's own decision, given on their join request; an update may withdraw it, never grant it. Nothing in the request was applied."
    retryable: false
```

- **A refused raise rejects the whole update.** No other field in the same request is applied, so a partial update can't be mistaken for a full one.
- **What a withdrawal does:** the community's registry sync should then remove the member's published record, and the spec text could say so.

## Related gap (not in this change)
A member admitted before consent existed, or who answered "no" at join, can only become listed by leaving and rejoining. That costs their credentials, role and vetter grants. A **member-signed** task for a member to grant or withdraw their own registry consent would close this. Is it worth tracking as a separate proposal?

## Reference implementation
OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1962 implements this in `vtc-service`:
- `vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden`, HTTP 400;
- withdraw and restate still work;
- an end-to-end test of publish → withdraw → sync → record removed;
- the code registered as service-defined (SPEC §8.5) in its error-code census, which will fail once the spec defines it, prompting a switch to the generated constant.

OpenVTC's join flow asks for consent explicitly and off by default (OpenVTC/openvtc#439).

title: spec(vtc/members/update): publishConsent may be withdrawn by an administrator, never granted — consentGrantForbidden (#789)
body:
spec(vtc/members/update): publishConsent may be withdrawn by an administrator, never granted — consentGrantForbidden (#789)

A member's consent to trust-registry publication is the member's own
privacy decision, given with `registryConsent` on vtc/join-requests/submit.
update/0.1 listed `publishConsent` among the fields an administrator may
change with no direction, so an administrator could raise it and publish
someone who said no.

vtc/members/update/0.1 (draft, in place per SPEC §5.2):
- `publishConsent` MAY lower consent (true -> false, e.g. a takedown) and
  MAY restate the current value. It MUST NOT raise it: consent becomes true
  only through the member's own registryConsent on a join submit, including
  a rejoin, which writes a fresh member record.
- New error vtc/members/update:consentGrantForbidden (not retryable),
  checked after notFound and adminRoleForbidden. A refused raise rejects the
  whole update; no other field in the request is applied.
- A withdrawal: the community SHOULD remove the member's published registry
  record at its next sync, and MUST NOT publish the member again until the
  member consents anew.
- Security & Privacy says why consent runs one way. Bindings regenerated.

Closes #737
