title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.10
body:
### Specifications

- **rooms/keys**: Act 0.2 — the member is the subject, and a document that names no room names its member ([#787](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/787))

`rooms/keys/act/0.1` declared `subjectPath: /document/payload/roomId` and
  resolved the member to act as "among the members of the document's room".
  Three types in its own table carry no `roomId` — `rooms/blobs/chunk/0.1`
  (`downloadId`, `index`) and `rooms/blobs/upload/{commit,abort}/0.2`
  (`uploadId`) — and for them 0.1 defined neither the subject nor how the
  recipient finds the document's room, while a producer MAY omit `issuer`.
  A conforming request could leave the recipient nothing to resolve the
  member from.

  act 0.2:
  - The table: these types carry no `roomId`; the member is the document's
    `issuer`, which the producer MUST set to the member whose request
    opened the transfer.
  - Producer item 2: `issuer` MUST be set for a type that names no room
    (MAY → MUST for those types; unchanged otherwise).
  - Recipient item 2a: for a type that names no room, act as `issuer` if it
    is a member the recipient holds keys for and the caller may act as;
    otherwise `issuerNotPrincipal`; `issuer` absent is `principalAmbiguous`.
    The recipient MUST NOT pick a member for the caller (not its only one,
    not one inferred from the transfer identifier).
  - `subjectPath` moves to `/document/issuer`. The subject is the party
    whose authority the task exercises (`actsAsSubject: true`) — the
    member, whose key signs — which is the question a delegated-execution
    policy point asks of `subjectPath` ("does the executing agent speak
    for this subject?") and exactly what Recipient item 2 decides. The room
    is the resource the completed document addresses, not a party the caller
    speaks for, and three of the table's types do not name one. Where
    `issuer` is absent (a room-naming type, one candidate member) the
    subject is the member item 2 resolves, and a recipient evaluating
    policy or audit against the subject MUST use it and MUST NOT treat the
    unresolved pointer as "no subject".
  - `principalAmbiguous` / `issuerNotPrincipal` meanings cover the
    room-less case. No code added; payload and response schemas unchanged
    except the `issuer` description.
  - Examples: a direct upload's commit completed as the member; a chunk
    refused `principalAmbiguous`. Invalid example: a non-DID `issuer`.

- **rooms/keys**: File-key and open 0.2 — unknownEpoch says `removed` when catching up cannot help ([#786](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/786))

`rooms/keys/file-key/0.1` gave `unknownEpoch` two reasons in a closed
  details schema — `notDelivered` and `beyondChain` — and defined
  `notDelivered` as "E is later than any epoch it holds". A removal leaves
  the oracle's group where it was, so a file sealed after the oracle's
  principal was removed matches that definition too. The oracle could only
  say `notDelivered`, telling the caller to catch up with the room's
  commits, and no commit will ever make that epoch derivable for a removed
  member: a caller following the reason retried forever.
  `rooms/keys/open/0.1` declared `unknownEpoch` with no details schema at
  all, so a caller could not tell the two cases apart there either, and an
  implementation already sends an undeclared `reason: removed`.

  file-key 0.2:
  - `unknownEpoch.details.reason` gains `removed`, and `details` gains
    `removedAtEpoch` (integer, minimum 1).
  - Oracle item 4: `removed`, with `removedAtEpoch`, when a commit the
    oracle processed removed its principal from the room's group at
    `removedAtEpoch` and E is at or after it — no later commit will make E
    derivable, so the caller MUST NOT be told to catch up. It takes
    precedence: an oracle that knows of such a removal MUST NOT answer
    `notDelivered` for an E at or after it.
  - Caller: acts on `details.reason`, never on the message; after `removed`
    it MUST NOT retry after catching up.
  - A `removed` refusal example, a Security & Privacy sentence, and a
    "What changed from 0.1" section.

  open 0.2 declares the same three reasons and the same details schema for
  `rooms/keys/open:unknownEpoch`, with the same conformance text
  (`beyondChain` for an epoch earlier than the oracle's current one that its
  retained chain does not reach).

title: Runtime evidence request for keys/sign-jws and keys/sign-csr protocol-signature tasks
body:
## Context

This issue asks for runtime evidence or test guidance for the protocol-signature tasks introduced in:

- https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/749

That PR introduces two narrow tasks where the custodian builds the protocol bytes itself before signing:

- `keys/sign-jws/0.1`
- `keys/sign-csr/0.1`

The source/spec description is clear and useful. Downstream RAHP review has treated the change as a source/spec improvement, but it cannot yet close the corresponding runtime assurance questions because we do not have runnable traces or implementation-level evidence for the accepted and rejected cases.

Downstream tracking:

- Consolidated runtime evidence owner: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/issues/994
- Evidence scaffold PR: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/995
- Case classification PR: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/996
- Scope C evidence record PR: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/997
- Local downstream runtime capability assessment PR: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/998

The downstream conclusion so far is narrow: the available upstream material supports source/spec review, but downstream cannot produce runtime PASS/FAIL evidence because `rahp-toolkit` does not contain a runnable custodian/runtime harness or request fixture set for these tasks.

## Request

Could this repository provide, point to, or document runtime evidence for `keys/sign-jws/0.1` and `keys/sign-csr/0.1`?

The useful form would be one or more of:

1. runnable tests already present in this repository;
2. a fixture set showing valid and invalid requests;
3. command-line or integration-test instructions for exercising the tasks;
4. redacted runtime traces from a conforming implementation;
5. a statement that these are currently specification/binding definitions only and that runtime evidence belongs in another implementation repository.

## Cases we are trying to evidence

The downstream RAHP runtime evidence packet currently tracks the following Scope C cases.

### `C01-valid-sign-jws`

A valid `keys/sign-jws/0.1` request should produce a protocol-valid JWS from custodian-built signing input.

Evidence requested:

- source ref / implementation ref;
- redacted request fixture;
- resulting JWS or digest of the signed artifact;
- confirmation that the custodian constructed the signing input;
- audit / retained-evidence note.

### `C02-sign-jws-prohibited-header`

A `keys/sign-jws/0.1` request with prohibited or unsafe JWS header members should be rejected.

The PR text indicates refusal of at least:

- `alg`
- `crit`
- `b64`
- `jwk`
- `jku`
- `x5u`

Evidence requested:

- invalid request fixture;
- rejection result;
- error or non-positive outcome shape;
- confirmation that no signature is produced.

### `C04-sign-jws-wrong-purpose`

A wrong-purpose or wrong-audience `keys/sign-jws/0.1` request should not produce an authoritative protocol signature.

Evidence requested:

- how purpose/audience is represented, if at all, for this task;
- whether this is enforced by the task schema, the custodian implementation, the requester authority model, or deployment policy;
- accepted/rejected fixture if such enforcement exists;
- statement of non-applicability if purpose/audience is intentionally outside this task.

### `C05-valid-sign-csr`

A valid `keys/sign-csr/0.1` request should produce a constrained CSR binding subject, SANs and key public material.

Evidence requested:

- redacted request fixture;
- resulting CSR or digest/redacted PEM;
- confirmation that the custodian used the key’s own public key;
- confirmation of accepted subject attributes and SAN handling;
- audit / retained-evidence note.

### `C06-sign-csr-wrong-subject`

A wrong-subject CSR request should be rejected, or the boundary should be explicitly described if wrong-subject authority is outside this task.

Evidence requested:

- how requester authority over a CSR subject is determined;
- whether wrong-subject rejection is implemented by the task, custodian, controller, or deployment policy;
- invalid request fixture and rejection trace if available;
- non-applicability rationale if this is intentionally out of scope.

### `C07-sign-csr-arbitrary-extension`

A CSR request attempting arbitrary extensions should be rejected unless explicitly permitted.

The PR text says no extension except `subjectAltName` is requested.

Evidence requested:

- invalid CSR request fixture attempting an arbitrary extension;
- rejection result;
- confirmation that no CSR is produced with the arbitrary extension.

### `C08-generic-sign-substitution`

Generic opaque `keys/sign` should not substitute for protocol-valid `keys/sign-jws/0.1` or `keys/sign-csr/0.1`.

The PR text states that a custodian must not require `sign` for either task, and that a custodian framing `keys/sign` under its opaque signing domain should not accept `sign` in their place.

Evidence requested:

- test or explanation showing that generic `keys/sign` cannot produce a protocol-valid JWS or CSR for these task purposes;
- rejection trace or verification-failure trace;
- implementation guidance for consumers so they do not treat `keys/sign` as a fallback for `sign-jws` or `sign-csr`.

## Evidence format that would be sufficient

Any of the following would be sufficient for downstream assessment:

```yaml
case_id: C01-valid-sign-jws
task: keys/sign-jws/0.1
implementation_ref: "<repo/commit/tag>"
request_fixture: "<path or redacted inline fixture>"
expected_result: PASS
observed_result: PASS
artifact:
  type: jws | csr | rejection | verification_failure
  digest: "<digest if artifact is not included>"
retained_evidence:
  retained:
    - "<audit event / signing input digest / task record>"
  deliberately_not_retained:
    - "<payload / private key / sensitive material>"
notes: "<limits, assumptions, or non-applicability>"
```

Equivalent Markdown, JSON, test logs, or CI references would also work.

## Why this matters

The downstream RAHP assessment is not challenging the source/spec design. It is trying to separate:

- source/spec evidence;
- generated binding evidence;
- runtime implementation evidence;
- retained-evidence / audit evidence;
- non-repudiation and privacy boundaries.

At present, downstream can record that `keys/sign-jws/0.1` and `keys/sign-csr/0.1` are specified as narrow protocol-signing tasks. It cannot yet say that a runtime implementation accepts and rejects the relevant cases as intended.

## Non-goals

This issue is not asking for:

- changes to the Trust Tasks model;
- a RAHP-specific implementation;
- disclosure of private keys, bearer tokens, unredacted payloads, or sensitive runtime logs;
- upstream adoption of the downstream RAHP issue structure.

It is only asking where the runtime evidence for these task constraints should live, or whether it already exists.

## Related downstream links

- Consolidated downstream runtime evidence issue: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/issues/994
- Scope C initial evidence records: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/997
- Scope C local runtime capability assessment: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/998

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.31.9` → `0.31.10` | patch |

| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.31.9` → `0.31.10` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.31.9` → `0.31.10` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.10` → `0.26.11` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.11`) | `0.8.10` → `0.8.11` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.10` → `0.8.11` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc): community-owned data rooms — the community's VTA as key holder (vtc/rooms/community/*, vtc/rooms/offers/*)
body:
P13 of `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md` (§8.4), first part: the VTC serves the community-owned room tasks released in trust-tasks-rs 0.31.2 (trust-tasks-tf #768) — `vtc/rooms/community/{create,list,get}/0.1`, `vtc/rooms/community/members/{add,remove,list}/0.1` and `vtc/rooms/offers/{list,accept}/0.1`.

## Who holds what

The community is the room's **owner** (`ownerDid` = the VTC's DID) and its **host**; **its own VTA is the key holder**. The VTC holds no room key and no group secret, and never falls back to holding one (`noKeyHolder`). It sends its VTA the existing `rooms/owner/*` tasks (`group/create`, `invite`, `issue-membership`, `issue-authority`, `group/add`, `group/remove`) plus `webvh/dids/create/1.1` (`room` template, `setPrimary: false`) and `vault/credentials/receive`, over `vta_link` (TSP > DIDComm through the mediator — the VTA needs no inbound surface), signed as the VTC's DID. That DID is a persona the VTA holds in `[rooms.community] context` (minted there by `vtc setup`), which is what lets the VTA sign the room's group changes as the community. **No VTA change was needed**: `group/create`'s "the caller's own DID, if it is a persona" and the persona resolver already cover it.

## What lands

- **`vtc.rooms.manage`** — the owner's authority, distinct from hosting's `vtc.rooms.admin`; in `community-admin`'s ceiling.
- **`[rooms.community]`** (optional; absent = off, an upgraded VTC starts as before): `context`, optional `webvh_server`, `mediator_did`, `authority_valid_days` (default 365). Off, a create is `noKeyHolder` naming the section, and `community/list` carries the snippet in `ext["org.openvtc"].communityRooms` for the console.
- **`community_rooms` keyspace** (backed up): the owner's record — rooms (label, the VTA's signing key id), members/offers with their credentials, a sealed acceptance's Welcome for 7 days, served DID logs. **Never read on the host path** (invariant I5): the e2e test writes and reads a record with the offered credentials, authorized by the chain alone.
- **Room identities**: with `webvh_server` the VTA publishes; without it the DID is minted serverless at `<public_url>/room-dids/<id>/did.jsonl` and the VTC serves the log (public, every host, like its own `/.well-known/did.jsonl`) — needed because the VTA verifies the community's own credentials as it vaults them.
- **Remote first** everywhere: create stores the room only after mint → group → credentials (a failure leaves no room; `keyHolderUnavailable` names the minted DID); add records the offer only after all three credentials; accept records the admission only after `group/add` answered; remove records only after `group/remove`. An unknown outcome is `keyHolderUnavailable` / `admissionPending`.
- **Step-up, no parking**: create / add / remove take the requester's operation-bound gesture and are audited with their reason (`AuditEvent::CommunityRoomChanged`, new, in `vti-common` — `AuditEvent` is `#[non_exhaustive]`). Never a Welcome, KeyPackage or credential in the audit trail.
- **Members**: offers answer only the proven signer and only an active member; accept repeats with the same KeyPackage return the same Welcome; a different one, or an expired keep, is `alreadyAccepted`.
- **`rooms` policy**: input gains `room.communityOwned`; the default allows community-owned `open`/`attributed` (private still off). A VTC still on the earlier shipped default gets it upgraded at boot (`upgrade_stale_rooms_default`, same two conditions as the personhood upgrade — workspace's own row, behaves superseded), so an upgraded community can own rooms; an operator's own policy is never touched.

## Tests

`vtc-service/tests/it/community_rooms.rs`, against a stand-in VTA that keeps a real room key and signs real DTG credentials: open-room create → offer → accept → **record put/get on the host path with the offered credentials** → remove; a sealed room through `group/create`/`add`/`remove` with the VTC as host and a repeated accept; the served DID log; and every declared error code (all 26 witnessed in the error-code census, all 8 tasks witnessed in the conformance sweep). Policy-upgrade unit test.

## Spec gaps found (reported, not invented around)

1. `rooms/owner/group/add/0.1` item 6 vs `vtc/rooms/offers/accept/0.1` *Repeating an accept*: after a lost answer the VTA settles the pending admission and then refuses the identical retry `alreadyMember`, so the community never gets the Welcome back. Here that maps to `alreadyAccepted` (admission recorded so removal works). Proposed for group/add item 6: *"When the pending admission it settles was for the same `member` and the same KeyPackage as the request, and the host is at its epoch, the recipient MUST apply it and answer the request with that admission's Welcome and epoch, rather than `alreadyMember`."*
2. `vtc/rooms/community/members/remove/0.1` item 4 says the answer states that removal does not recall what was read, but the response schema has no member for it; carried in `ext["org.openvtc"].notice`. Proposed: add an optional `notice` string to the response, or drop "and its answer".
3. `vtc.rooms.manage` (like `vtc.rooms.admin`, dtgwg-vti-spec#63) is not yet registered in the VTI spec's capability appendix.
4. Member side: a member's persona key is VTA-held and `rooms/keys/act/0.1`'s closed table does not include `vtc/rooms/offers/{list,accept}`, so no client can sign them as the persona yet. Proposed: add both to the act table with no presentation (`None` action), or a dedicated task.

## Follow-ups

Console pages; a member client for the offers (pending gap 4 / P8); renewing the community's own `admin` authority before it lapses (SHOULD); removing a departing member from every community room (SHOULD).

Every write to the owner's record also hints the console's `rooms` topic (#2136); the room's own creation already does through `vti_rooms::observe`.

title: feat(vtc): a trusted-witness list change parks for administrators' consent (#1068)
body:
feat(vtc): a trusted-witness list change parks for administrators' consent (#1068)

Which witnesses a community trusts decides whose attestations count as
evidence there, for personhood and joining and for credentials members already
hold. That is a major trust change, and VTI-CMP-090 asks that a configuration
change to trust semantics attract the same review as a code change: for a
community, another administrator's. Until now one holder of vtc.config.admin
could change `witnesses.trusted` alone.

Every runtime change to the list now goes through the action list, as
lowering the consent threshold does (VTI-APV-020):

- `config/patch` and the confirming `vtc/config/import` that add, remove or
  relabel a witness take the requester's operation-bound gesture, then park
  as `Act::ChangeTrustedWitnesses` (kind `config.witnesses.change`) for the
  other holders of vtc.config.admin, by approve scope. The requester never
  approves, one decline closes it, and the N-th approval runs the patch with
  every check re-run.
- The consent is pinned to the list in force, so another change landing first
  voids the action.
- Removal parks too: it can strip the evidence a member's personhood rests on.
  A reorder of the same entries is no change, and a value the write would
  refuse asks for no gesture.
- In single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022) the bound gesture stands in for
  the consent, audited at Critical, as every other waiver of the mode.
- A write that both changes the list and lowers the threshold is refused with
  the two to send apart: one parked action is one consent.

Approvers see the proposed list through a pinned summary template (patch and
import), mirrored in the console's pin table with a shared vector; the
action's summary text names the list it changes from. `config.toml` stays the
host's, outside the action list like every other host-only setting.

Docs: trusted-witnesses.md, admin-access.md (§2.1, §2.1a, §3.1, §3.2),
vtc-action-list.md §8.2, CLAUDE.md.

title: Run the explore stream as root without sudo, and explain why
body:
Fixes #48.

The explore pages told the reader to SSH in as root and then run everything through `sudo`, which does nothing for root. Logging in as root is intentional, so this keeps root and removes `sudo`, and explains the choice in the docs.

## Changes

- `sysop/explore/01-server-setup.md`: new "Why root?" section. The host is throwaway, running as root means fewer commands, beginners don't have to debug permissions, and everything lives in one home directory (`/root/.cargo`, `/root/<svc>/`). Readers who disable root SSH are told to use `sudo -i`, with an explanation of why prefixing individual commands with `sudo` breaks the later steps. Step 3 links to the section. Every `sudo` is removed (script commands, binary installs, Node.js and curl installs), and the debconf note no longer relies on `sudo`'s `env_reset`.
- `scripts/setup-explore.sh`: all `sudo` calls removed from the commands and the usage text. A new `require_root` check runs after argument validation, so a non-root run stops before changing anything and points at `sudo -i`.
- `sysop/explore/README.md`, `sysop/explore/02-walkthrough.md`: link to the explanation; the walkthrough says to run from a root shell.

`developer/02-openvtc-tui.md` keeps its `sudo mv`, since that page targets a developer's own machine.

## Checks

- `shellcheck scripts/setup-explore.sh`: clean
- `markdownlint-cli2 "sysop/explore/*.md"`: 0 errors

title: feat(vta-mobile-core): connect a did:peer relationship DID to its mediator for witnessing (#1068)
body:
A wallet carries every witness document from the relationship DID (the witness checks the transport-proven sender against `issuer`, and that DID's one mediator socket is the wallet's). A relationship DID is a `did:peer:2` with an independent signing key `V` and key-agreement key `E`; `MediatorSession::connect` / `TspMediatorSession::connect` derive both secrets from one `did:key` seed, so they could not open that session.

- **vta-sdk** — `TspSession::connect_with_secrets{,_on}`, mirroring `DIDCommSession`'s; `connect` / `connect_on` derive the did:key secrets and delegate. Additive.
- **vta-mobile-core** — `MediatorSession::connect_with_secrets(holder, secrets, peer, mediator)` and `TspMediatorSession::connect_with_secrets(holder, secrets, mediator)`, taking `HolderSecret { key_id, private_key_multibase }` (the `SecretEntry` shape; `Debug` redacts the key). Before any socket opens the holder's document is resolved and each secret must sit under the holder DID, name a published verification method and carry its public key, with an Ed25519 `authentication` key and an X25519 `keyAgreement` key present — so a wrong key is refused by name rather than as a mediator auth failure.
- Docs: `docs/02-vta/witness-party.md`, `vta_mobile_core::witness` module doc.

Tests: a generated `did:peer:2` passes; wrong key, foreign key id, unpublished id, duplicate id, missing KA, missing auth, another DID's document and a malformed key (not quoted) are refused; `Debug` redaction. No in-process mediator harness exists in mobile-core (its connect tests are live/ignored), so no socket-level test.

Local: fmt, clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p vta-sdk -p vta-mobile-core --doc`, workspace nextest 6102/6103 (the one timeout is vta-service `audit_coverage`, untouched here, load-sensitive).

title: spec(rooms/keys): act 0.2 — the member is the subject, and a document that names no room names its member
body:
## Problem

`rooms/keys/act/0.1` declares `subjectPath: /document/payload/roomId`, and Recipient item 2 resolves the member to act as "among the members of **the document's room**". Three types in its own table carry no `roomId`:

| type | payload |
|---|---|
| `rooms/blobs/chunk/0.1` | `downloadId`, `index` |
| `rooms/blobs/upload/commit/0.2` | `uploadId` |
| `rooms/blobs/upload/abort/0.2` | `uploadId` |

For these, nothing defines the subject or how the recipient finds "the document's room", and Producer item 2 lets the producer omit `issuer`. A conforming request can leave the recipient nothing to resolve the member from. The reference VTA currently requires `issuer` and refuses with `principalAmbiguous` otherwise, which no specification says.

## Change — `rooms/keys/act/0.2`

- **The table**, after those rows: "These types carry no `roomId`. For them the member is the document's `issuer`, which the producer **MUST** set to the member whose request opened the transfer."
- **Producer item 2**: `issuer` **MAY** → **MUST** for a type that names no room (unchanged for room-naming types).
- **Recipient item 2a** (new): "For a type that names no room, the recipient **MUST** act as `issuer` if it is a member it holds keys for and the caller may act as, and **MUST** refuse with `issuerNotPrincipal` otherwise; where `issuer` is absent it **MUST** refuse with `principalAmbiguous`." It **MUST NOT** pick a member for the caller — not its only one, not one inferred from the transfer identifier.
- **Error codes**: `issuerNotPrincipal` and `principalAmbiguous` already exist in the task's registry; their meanings now cover the room-less case. No code added.
- **`subjectPath` → `/document/issuer`** (see below), with a new *Authorization → The subject* subsection.
- `issuer`'s schema description updated; examples: a direct upload's commit completed as the member, a chunk refused `principalAmbiguous`; a new invalid example (non-DID `issuer`). *What changed from 0.1*.

`0.1` is untouched.

## `subjectPath`: moved to `/document/issuer`, not "noted as unresolvable"

`subjectPath` (meta-schema): *"locating the subject identifier … Lets a delegated-execution PEP answer 'does the executing agent speak for this subject?' declaratively"*. Policy engines and approval surfaces consume it from `registry.json` as the subject a decision is about and the subject an approver is shown.

Two options were considered:

1. Keep `/document/payload/roomId` and note that for the three room-less types it does not resolve and the subject is `/document/issuer`.
2. Move it to `/document/issuer`.

**Option 2 is taken.** The task declares `actsAsSubject: true`: what it exercises is the **member's** own authority, with the member's key. "Does the executing agent speak for this subject?" is exactly the question Recipient item 2 answers — *may the caller act as this member* — and the subject that question is about is the member, not the room. A caller never speaks *for* a room; the room is the resource the completed document addresses at its host (still at `/document/payload/roomId` for any audit that wants it). With option 1, a registry-driven policy keyed on the subject would evaluate "speaks for the room" — a different and weaker question — for most types, and switch subject *kind* (room → member) for three of them; a policy written for one kind silently mis-applies to the other. Option 2 gives one subject of one kind for every type.

What remains is the room-naming case where `issuer` may still be omitted (exactly one candidate member). There the pointer does not resolve in the request; the subject is the member item 2 resolves (the completed document's `issuer`, the response's `principal`), and the spec now says a recipient evaluating policy or audit against the subject **MUST** use that resolved member and **MUST NOT** treat an unresolved `subjectPath` as "no subject". Requiring `issuer` for *every* type would make the pointer always resolve, but would break every single-member client for no gain over item 2's resolution, so it is not proposed here.

## Versioning — why 0.2 and not an in-place edit

[SPEC §5.2](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/blob/main/SPEC.md#52-compatibility-rules): an in-place edit to a `draft` is only for an *editorial or normalization change* with no wire effect. A producer that omitted `issuer` on a chunk/commit/abort document conformed to `0.1` and is refused under `0.2`, and a registry-driven policy engine reads a different subject — a narrowing with wire effect, classified breaking, which a `draft` **MAY** take as a `MINOR` increment → **0.2**. Same reasoning #771 used for `rooms/keys/seal/0.2`.

## Bindings

Regenerated Rust (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`), TS, Go, Dart. Additive: new `act::v0_2` modules, `schema_index`, `mod.rs`, the conformance index, `index.ts`. (`subjectPath` is registry metadata; no generated constant carries it.)

## Local checks

- `npm run validate` ✓ · `npm run build` ✓
- `npm run check-bindings` ✓ — "788 specifications … all agree. 1876 declared error codes (231 with a detailsSchema) match Rust ERROR_CODES; 22 declared document size bounds match"
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --test conformance -- rooms::keys::act` ✓ (9 passed, incl. `v0_2::request_example_{1,2}`, `rejects_invalid_examples`)

## Implementation follow-up (VTI, after release)

Serve `rooms/keys/act/0.2` beside 0.1 with item 2a as stated (the VTA's current behaviour, now specified), evaluate policy/audit against the resolved member, and have clients send `issuer` on chunk/commit/abort documents.

title: feat(vtc): direct admission on the generated vtc/members types (trust-tasks-rs 0.31.9)
body:
trust-tasks-tf #784 (trust-tasks-rs 0.31.9) publishes `vtc/members/admit/0.1`
and `vtc/members/make-membership/0.1`, which this service bound ahead of their
specifications on local wire types.

VTC (`trust_tasks::admission_tasks`): the payloads, the response
(`Response(AdmittedMembership)`, built through the generated builder, `status`
the generated single-value enum), the document policy and the error codes are
now the generated ones. The local `SpecPolicy` is gone — the spine reads both
tasks' requirements off the registry — and `ceremony::admission::codes` reads
every code off the specifications. A payload is validated against its schema
before it is parsed, so a `subject` not matching `^did:` or over 2048
characters and a `role` over 128 are `malformedRequest`; an over-long role was
`roleNotPermitted` before. The trust-task manifest's two unpublished-URI
exemptions go back to zero; the conformance sweep and the error-code census
gain witnesses for both tasks (all ten declared codes driven in
`direct_admission.rs`, three newly: admit `alreadyMember`, make-membership
`entryNotLive` and `deniedByPolicy`).

CLI: `vtc_client::members` (`members_admit`, `members_make_membership`,
schema-checked before sending) and `cnm members {admit,make-membership}`. A
refusal that means the other command — `hasEntry`, `noEntry`,
`applicationEntry`, `removedMember`, `roleNotPermitted` for `admin` — prints
the command to run instead; a referral prints the action to follow.

Docs: CLAUDE.md's *VTC direct admission*, community-lifecycle (schema checks
and the CLI) and the data-rooms quickstart (the "needs the console" limitation
is gone).

## Notes
- Floor bump: `trust-tasks-rs` 0.31.8 → 0.31.9 (workspace `Cargo.toml` + `Cargo.lock`); no crate's own `version =` edited.
- `vta-sdk/tests/generated_wire_types_census.rs`: the local admission types were never in its baseline, so nothing to remove.
- Admin UI (`lib/member-admission.ts`) keeps its TS shapes: `wire.ts` is generated from the REST OpenAPI document only, and these two tasks have no REST route, so there is no schema to alias. The shapes already match the published response.

title: spec(rooms/keys): file-key and open 0.2 — unknownEpoch says `removed` when catching up cannot help
body:
## Problem

`rooms/keys/file-key/0.1` declares `unknownEpoch` with a **closed** `details` schema — `reason` ∈ {`notDelivered`, `beyondChain`}, no other members — and oracle item 4 defines `notDelivered` as "`E` is later than any epoch it holds".

A removal leaves the oracle's group state where it was, so when the oracle's principal has been **removed** from the room's group by a commit the oracle processed, every file sealed after the removal also satisfies that definition. The only conformant answer is `notDelivered`, which tells the caller to catch up with the room's commits — and no commit will ever make that epoch derivable for a removed member. A caller that follows the reason retries forever. (The reference VTA currently sends `notDelivered` with a message saying it was a removal, because the schema leaves it nothing else: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2135.)

`rooms/keys/open/0.1` declares `unknownEpoch` with **no** `details` schema at all, so the same distinction is undefined there; the VTA already sends an undeclared `{reason: "removed", removedAtEpoch}` (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2126).

## Change

**`rooms/keys/file-key/0.2`**
- `unknownEpoch` `details.reason` gains `removed`; `details` gains `removedAtEpoch` (integer, minimum 1). Meaning text updated.
- Oracle item 4: three cases. "`removed`, with `removedAtEpoch`, when a commit the oracle processed removed its principal from the room's group at `removedAtEpoch` and `E` is at or after it — no later commit will make `E` derivable, so the caller **MUST NOT** be told to catch up." It takes precedence over `notDelivered` (an oracle that knows of the removal **MUST NOT** answer `notDelivered` for such an `E`).
- Caller: acts on `details.reason`, never the message; after `removed` it **MUST NOT** retry after catching up.
- New refusal example (`removed`), a sentence in Security & Privacy, a *What changed from 0.1* section.

**`rooms/keys/open/0.2`**
- Declares the same three reasons and the same closed `details` schema for `rooms/keys/open:unknownEpoch` (`notDelivered`+`heldEpoch`, `beyondChain`+`earliestEpoch`, `removed`+`removedAtEpoch`), with matching Conformance text; *What changed from 0.1*.

Request and response payload schemas are byte-identical to 0.1 apart from `$id`. Both 0.1 versions are untouched.

## Versioning — why 0.2 and not an in-place edit

[SPEC §5.2](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/blob/main/SPEC.md#52-compatibility-rules): a change to a `draft` is made **in place** only when it is an *editorial or normalization change* with no semantic difference on the wire (re-casing, a wire-neutral `$ref` re-pin, rewording prose). Anything else is classified backwards-compatible (→ `MINOR`) or breaking (→ `MAJOR`, which a `draft` **MAY** take as a `MINOR`).

- file-key: a new value in a closed enum plus a new member in a closed `details` schema of a declared error code. A 0.1 consumer checking `details` against the declared schema (e.g. `DeclaredErrorCode::check_details`) refuses `removed` → wire effect → `MINOR` increment, **0.2**.
- open: declaring a closed `details` schema where none existed constrains what a conforming oracle may send (a narrowing) → wire effect → `MINOR` increment at `draft`, **0.2**.

Same reasoning #771 used for `rooms/keys/seal/0.2` ("a new member on a closed payload … a `MINOR` increment per SPEC §5.2"), and the converse of #783, which edited in place precisely because "no schema, no `detailsSchema`, no code" moved.

## Bindings

Regenerated Rust (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`), TS, Go, Dart. Additive only: new `v0_2` modules for both slugs, `schema_index`, `mod.rs` re-exports, the conformance test index, `index.ts`.

## Local checks

- `npm run validate` ✓ · `npm run build` ✓
- `npm run check-bindings` ✓ — "789 specifications … all agree. 1874 declared error codes (230 with a detailsSchema) match Rust ERROR_CODES"
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --test conformance -- rooms::keys` ✓ (36 passed, incl. `file_key::v0_2::rejects_invalid_examples` / `rejects_invalid_response_examples`)

## Implementation follow-up (VTI, after release)

Serve `rooms/keys/file-key/0.2` and `rooms/keys/open/0.2` beside 0.1; on 0.2 answer `removed` with `removedAtEpoch` for a removal (file-key currently sends `notDelivered` there), and `beyondChain` with `earliestEpoch` from `open` for an epoch the chain does not reach.

title: spec(rooms/keys): file-key and open 0.2 — unknownEpoch says `removed` when catching up cannot help (#786)
body:
spec(rooms/keys): file-key and open 0.2 — unknownEpoch says `removed` when catching up cannot help (#786)

`rooms/keys/file-key/0.1` gave `unknownEpoch` two reasons in a closed
details schema — `notDelivered` and `beyondChain` — and defined
`notDelivered` as "E is later than any epoch it holds". A removal leaves
the oracle's group where it was, so a file sealed after the oracle's
principal was removed matches that definition too. The oracle could only
say `notDelivered`, telling the caller to catch up with the room's
commits, and no commit will ever make that epoch derivable for a removed
member: a caller following the reason retried forever.
`rooms/keys/open/0.1` declared `unknownEpoch` with no details schema at
all, so a caller could not tell the two cases apart there either, and an
implementation already sends an undeclared `reason: removed`.

file-key 0.2:
- `unknownEpoch.details.reason` gains `removed`, and `details` gains
  `removedAtEpoch` (integer, minimum 1).
- Oracle item 4: `removed`, with `removedAtEpoch`, when a commit the
  oracle processed removed its principal from the room's group at
  `removedAtEpoch` and E is at or after it — no later commit will make E
  derivable, so the caller MUST NOT be told to catch up. It takes
  precedence: an oracle that knows of such a removal MUST NOT answer
  `notDelivered` for an E at or after it.
- Caller: acts on `details.reason`, never on the message; after `removed`
  it MUST NOT retry after catching up.
- A `removed` refusal example, a Security & Privacy sentence, and a
  "What changed from 0.1" section.

open 0.2 declares the same three reasons and the same details schema for
`rooms/keys/open:unknownEpoch`, with the same conformance text
(`beyondChain` for an epoch earlier than the oracle's current one that its
retained chain does not reach).

Versioning: new 0.2 version directories, not in-place edits. SPEC §5.2
allows in-place edits to a `draft` only for editorial or normalization
changes with no wire effect. A new value in a closed enum and a new
member in a closed `details` schema (file-key), and a closed `details`
schema where none was declared (open), change what a conforming oracle
may send and what a 0.1 consumer checking `details` accepts — wire
effect, so a MINOR increment. 0.1 of both is unchanged. Request and
response payloads are identical to 0.1.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart); additive modules only.

title: fix(vta-sdk): a presign part carries uploadId only when one of its operations needs it
body:
## Bug

`VtaClient::external_credentials_issue_presign` splits an `external/credentials/issue/0.3` presign batch refused `responseTooLarge`, but copied the batch's `uploadId` onto **every** part. Conformance item 4 has a batch name `uploadId` exactly when an operation needs it (`upload-part`, `list-parts`, `complete-multipart`, `abort-multipart`), so splitting the checks-and-completion batch of consumer item 4 (`list-parts`, `complete-multipart`, `head`) sent a lone `head` carrying `uploadId`, which `vta_external::batch::check_batch` refuses `invalidBatch`.

The VTC's rooms presigner (`vtc-service/src/rooms/vta_storage.rs`, `batch_request`) builds each part itself and had the same flaw — also reachable without any refusal through the 64-operation chunking in `vti_common::blob_store::presigned::ops`.

## Fix

- `vta-sdk`: each part is built by `presign_part`, which drops `uploadId` when none of the part's operations needs it (consumer item 5 as clarified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#783: *"A part that holds no operation needing `uploadId` leaves it out"*).
- `vti-common`: new `StorageOp::needs_upload_id` (additive method).
- `vtc-service`: `batch_request` names `uploadId` only when an operation needs it — a two-line change at the one place every part is built.

Checked against the rest of consumer item 5: split to the first `maxOperations` else the first half; another `responseTooLarge` on any part is split again; a count is only a first guess for later parts (never treated as fitting them); a single operation refused `responseTooLarge` is returned, not asked again. The loop already held these; tests now pin them.

## Tests

- `vta-sdk` unit: `a_part_without_a_multipart_operation_leaves_the_upload_id_out` — **fails before the fix**.
- `vta-sdk/tests/client_rest.rs` (wiremock stand-in VTA that refuses a mismatched `uploadId` as `check_batch` does):
  - `a_split_part_with_no_multipart_operation_omits_the_upload_id` — **fails before the fix** (`invalidBatch`).
  - `a_part_refused_again_is_split_again` (8 → 4 refused → 2,2,2,2) — regression pin.
  - `a_single_operation_too_large_is_not_asked_again` — regression pin.
- `vtc-service` `a_batch_too_large_to_seal_is_split_and_an_old_vta_is_asked_at_0_2`: stand-in VTA now enforces item 4's `uploadId` rule; new case splits `[list-parts, complete-multipart, head]` and the `head` goes without `uploadId`.

No published type changes shape; no version edits.

title: fix(rooms)!: say a removed member's file key is a removal, and keep NoMatchingProtocol typed
body:
This fixes rough edges that the end-to-end data-rooms run exposed. One item is held back because it needs a spec change first.

## 1. File-key retrieval for a removed member (`FileKeyError`): breaking for `vta-service`
- `FileKeyError` gets a `Removed { epoch, removed_at }` variant and is now `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- `room_groups::file_key` reads the `room-removed/<room>/<persona>` row the same way `open_record_detailed` does (#2126). A file sealed at or after the member's removal now returns `Removed`, not `NotDelivered`. The existing removal test now covers file keys too.
- **What goes on the wire is held by the spec.** In `rooms/keys/file-key/0.1`, the `detailsSchema` for `unknownEpoch` is closed: `reason` must be `notDelivered` or `beyondChain`, and `additionalProperties` is `false`. Oracle item 4 also defines `notDelivered` as "E is later than any epoch it holds." So the VTA still sends `unknownEpoch` with reason `notDelivered` and no `heldEpoch`. The message says plainly that the member was removed. `rooms/keys/open` declares no schema for this code, which is why it can send `reason: removed`. File-key cannot.
- `pnm rooms file get` now prints the same hints a record refusal prints: catch up, backfill, or removed. Records and files now share one hint function. For files, the `notDelivered` hint says that if the VTA reports a removal, catching up will not help.

## 2. `NoMatchingProtocol` showed up as `malformedRequest`: breaking for `vti-common`
- `Outbound::pick_transport` returned `AppError::Validation`. The Trust Task spine turns that into `malformedRequest`, which told the client its document was wrong. Both transport sets were lost.
- New `AppError::NoMatchingProtocol(Box<NoMatchingProtocol>)` with `peer`, `ours`, `theirs` and `note`. It is boxed because otherwise it trips `clippy::result_large_err` everywhere the error is returned.
- Trust Task form: `taskFailed` (not retryable), with `details.reason: no_matching_protocol` plus `counterpartyDid`, `ours` and `theirs`. SPEC §8.3 has no transport code. It is not `unavailable` either, because a retry meets the same two sets.
- REST form: 502 with the same fields in the body.
- SDK: `VtaClient::trust_task_error` and `VtaError::from_http` both map this back to `VtaError::NoMatchingProtocol`, using the new `VtaError::no_matching_protocol_from`.
- `pnm`/`cnm` print both sets and say which side can add which service. For example: the peer publishes `TrustTaskHTTPS`, or this side runs `pnm services didcomm enable --mediator-did …`. The hint also notes that a persona-signed document can travel only over Trust-Task HTTPS.

## 3. `rooms/keys/act` sets no `subjectPath` for a document with no `roomId`: not changed here
The spec declares `subjectPath: /document/payload/roomId`. Three of the types in its table have no `roomId`: `rooms/blobs/chunk/0.1`, `rooms/blobs/upload/{commit,abort}/0.2`. The spec does not say what the subject is for those types, or how Recipient item 2 finds "the document's room". The line in the quickstart stays until the spec says. The proposed spec text is in the agent report.

## 4. Publish count in `CLAUDE.md`
Recounted from the manifests: **25 of 35** crates publish. The count is the workspace members plus `vti-fuzz`; `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy` is excluded.
- Added to the published lists: `vti-rooms`, `vti-rooms-dtg`, `vta-persona`.
- Added to the unpublished list: `vti-e2e-tests`, `room-host`, `vti-rooms-wasm`, `vti-witness`.
- `room-host/Cargo.toml` now has the comment saying why it does not publish, so "each with a comment" is true again.

## Checks run locally
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6107 passed
- workspace doctests
- `nextest -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` and its doctests: results below

title: feat(vtc): the `rooms` topic on the admin console's live channel (vtc/admin/events 0.2)
body:
Serve `vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.2` beside 0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #767, in
trust-tasks-rs 0.31.2+). The topic set is closed per version: 0.2 adds `rooms`
and nothing else, a 0.1 subscribe that names it is refused by its schema, and
every stream answers — its `#response` and every hint — at the version it was
opened with, so 0.1 consoles and `cnm actions watch` are unchanged.

`rooms` is effective for holders of `vtc.rooms.admin` (subscribe 0.2
§Authorization; `admin_events::read_capability`), who are answered on
`vtc/rooms/list`, `vtc/rooms/usage` and `vtc/storage/configs/list`. It is a
countless hint, sent per event 0.2 producer rule 4 when a room is registered or
removed, a room's lifecycle state changes, a room's usage or a storage config's
held bytes crosses 80/95/100 % of its limit or capacity in either direction, or
a storage config is created, changed or changes state. The stream fingerprints
exactly those facts, read as the rooms reads report them, so holdings moving
inside a band or a live room renewing send nothing. Lifecycle is computed from
the clock and never written, so a stream holding `rooms` also wakes itself at
the next transition (`vti_rooms::Room::next_lifecycle_change`).

Seams: storage-config writes (`RoomStorage::put_config`), and a new
`vti_rooms::observe` hook — set by vtc-service when it opens its blob host —
fired after a room is registered or renewed and after a room's or a config's
holdings or a room's limits are written. The hook carries nothing.

Also:
- The resumption history keeps one entry per topic (only the latest change
  answers "changed after `since`"), so a busy seam cannot crowd it out.
- A resumed fingerprinted topic is hinted after the `#response` even though the
  baseline observed at open already includes the change (previously a resumed
  count-topic change could be swallowed by the baseline comparison).
- Console: subscribes at 0.2 when `trust-task-discovery` lists it, re-reads
  `["rooms"]`, `["room-usage"]` and `["storage"]` on a `rooms` hint, and the
  rooms, room, near-a-limit and storage queries poll as the fallback (slowly
  only while the stream carries `rooms`).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.9
body:
### Added

- **vtc/members**: Admit and make-membership — direct admission by an administrator, decided by the community's admission policy ([#784](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/784))

Two new draft tasks for admitting a member without a join request, as one
  governed ceremony:

  - vtc/members/admit/0.1 ("Add a member"): a DID with no access-control
    entry (or only an `application` entry) is admitted at a community role the
    administrator names. The community writes the entry, the member record and
    a revocation slot and issues the VMC and role VAC, as a completed join
    would. A former member (removed record, no entry) is re-admitted and
    reported `returning`.
  - vtc/members/make-membership/0.1 ("Make this a membership"): an existing
    live entry with no member record (typically the bootstrap administrator)
    gets the member record and credentials at the role it already holds; the
    entry itself is not changed.

  The rules no policy can change:
  - the requester holds `vtc.members.manage` (permissionDenied);
  - a role other than `member` takes `vtc.roles.assign`, and the entry it
    seats is bounded by the requester's own;
  - `admin`, `application` and any role conferring authority-conferring
    capabilities are never seated (`roleNotPermitted`);
  - make-membership refuses an `application` entry, an expired or suspended
    entry, a live membership and a removed record.

  The community's admission policy then admits, refers (parked in the action
  list, answered with trust-task-next-step, approved only by another holder of
  `vtc.members.manage` who is neither requester nor subject, every check
  re-run at execution, exactly once) or refuses (`deniedByPolicy`). Step-up
  and consent are described as the model the tasks are designed for, not
  required (SPEC §7.3 item 13).

  Both answer with the same AdmittedMembership (subject, role, label?,
  status, returning, approval policyAllowed|approved|waived,
  statusListIndex, vmc, roleVac), shared in vtc/_shared/0.1/admission.

  The wire shape and codes are those of the Verifiable Trust Infrastructure
  implementation (vtc-service), which bound the tasks ahead of this
  specification with local types; generated types replace them.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).



### Specifications

- **external**: Credentials/issue 0.3 — details.maxOperations is a guaranteed-to-fit count, clarified in place ([#783](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/783))

0.3 said `details.maxOperations` on `responseTooLarge` was "how many of the
  batch's operations, taken in order, would fit", which left open whether a
  consumer may rely on it or must treat it as a hint.

  It is a guarantee, and now says so:

  - Producer (Conformance item 7): a custodian that gives `maxOperations`
    MUST give a count k such that the same request, with `presign.requests`
    cut to its first k operations (and `uploadId` left out if none of them
    needs one, as item 4 requires), is answered within the bound on
    `sealedCredential`, the account and binding as they were at the refusal.
    It MAY be conservative — a sealed bundle's length varies with its
    ciphertext's randomness, so a count computed from an upper bound on the
    sealed length is sometimes lower than the most that would fit. It MUST
    NOT give a count it has not established fits; it omits the member when it
    cannot compute one or when not even one operation fits. The count speaks
    for those operations in that order only.
  - Consumer (item 5): SHOULD split by it (else in half); the first part fits,
    the rest carries no promise, and the consumer MUST handle another
    `responseTooLarge` on any part or any other batch by splitting again. It
    MUST NOT treat the count as a size that fits other operations. A single
    operation refused this way cannot be split and SHOULD NOT be retried.
  - The `responseTooLarge` meaning, the "What changed from 0.2" list and the
    refusal example say the same.

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.31.8` → `0.31.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.31.8` → `0.31.9` | patch |

| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.31.8` → `0.31.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.31.8` → `0.31.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.31.8` → `0.31.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.31.8` → `0.31.9` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.9` → `0.26.10` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.10`) | `0.8.9` → `0.8.10` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.9` → `0.8.10` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.

checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

title: feat(relationships): witness a relationship through the VTA
body:
## What

Witnessing a relationship, with the member's VTA as the witnessed party (`vta/witness/{open,present,accept}/0.1`, VTI #2123; VTI `docs/02-vta/witness-party.md`).

The VTA builds and signs every document as the relationship DID, presents the credentials and verifies and stores the VWC. OpenVTC **carries** the documents to the witness on the relationship DID's own connection (the one websocket the mediator allows that DID) and hands each answer back unaltered.

- **`openvtc-core::witness`** — the round (`run`): make sure the VRC (and VMC) are in the VTA's vault → `vta/witness/open` → check the `witness/session` document → carry → wait for the answer on the session's thread → verify it as the witness's (type, thread, issuer/recipient, `authentication` proof over the reply as received) → `present` → check/carry/verify the submission, **discard it** → `accept`. Witness refusals (`witness/session:refused`, `challengeMismatch`, `presentationInvalid`) end the session with a worded reason and are never handed back to the VTA; an answer that does not verify as the witness's is discarded and the wait goes on (a forged refusal cannot end a session). VTA refusals (`memberLinkUnsupported`, `permissionDenied`, `credentialMismatch`, `sessionUnknown`, `vwcInvalid`, an old VTA's `unsupportedType`, …) are mapped to what the member can do. Transport: TSP > DIDComm by service `type` in both DID documents, never REST (a witness answers the transport-proven sender); DIDComm uses the Trust Task binding envelope through the relationship listener's durable outbox. Patterned on VTI's `vta-mobile-core::witness` (#2129).
- **Member link**: when the VMC names the persona rather than the pairwise relationship DID, the request carries `membership.memberDid`; the VTA refuses unless the witness is in its `[witness] member_link_witnesses`, and the member is told exactly that.
- **TUI**: `w` on a relationship's detail opens a prompt (DID or agent name) that states what the witness will learn; the job runs in its own dispatch domain (`Witness`) with per-step progress; the result is kept in the protected config (`witnessings`, skipped when empty) and listed on the relationship. The witness's answers reach the job through a `ReplyRouter` fed by the inbound dispatcher (`InboundEffects::witness_replies`); the gate admits `spec/witness/*` (TSP opens the envelope before the gate) and the census lists both reply types.
- **VRC → vault**: `credential_sync::sync_relationship_credentials` stores every issued VRC the vault does not already hold, on connect (and `witness::ensure_in_vault` before a session). Never re-stores one it holds: `receive` overwrites, and the VTA binds a session to the stored bytes.
- **Personhood — only what the member selects**: `assert_personhood` takes an `ext`. By default no VWC and no `outcomeEvidence` is included. When the persona has witnessed relationships, `P` opens a picker (other party, witness, date, digest) with **none chosen**, stating what the community learns from each (that the relationship exists, which witness attested it, its digest). Space includes/excludes; Enter asserts with exactly the chosen set. "Include all" is `A` then a separate `y` confirmation, for that one assertion only — never remembered, never automatic (the reducer ignores a confirmation that was not armed). `outcomeEvidence` carries exactly the selected VWCs' evidence (`vta/witness/accept`'s `evidence`, VTI #2128); no "newest N" rule. A selection above the VTC's 16-entry limit is refused with a message, never trimmed.
- Removing a relationship removes its witnessing records (the VWCs stay in the VTA vault).
- Not available to a BIP32 account (no VTA-held relationship keys) — refused up front with that reason.

## Custody check (no VTI change needed)

openvtc creates relationship keys with `context_id: None`. For the account's credential (`admin` of one context, as onboarding grants) the VTA files them in that context (`create_key`'s single-context default), and `vault/credentials/receive` binds a credential to the same context the same way, so `vta/witness/open`'s custody and credential checks pass, and `witness-request` is derived for `admin`. `witness_e2e.rs` holds exactly that shape: keys created with no context by a single-context admin, a `did:peer:2` over them, a VRC signed locally with the exported key.

## Tests

- `openvtc-core/tests/witness_e2e.rs` (MockVta, `#[ignore]` like the other MockVta suites; CI coverage runs them): full round against the real `vta/witness/*` tasks and an in-test witness that answers with a `dtg-credentials` VWC (VTA verifies and stores it; evidence and personhood ext checked); a witness refusal; the member link refused by a VTA that lists no witness.
- Personhood selection: core `personhood_ext` includes nothing by default and exactly the selected otherwise (no cap rule); the picker reducer (starts empty, toggles, include-all inert until armed, armed+`y` includes all, over-limit refused); key handling (Enter = only chosen, `A` only asks, `y` only after asking); the runtime handler opens the picker with none chosen and sends nothing while asking; render states the disclosure.
- Unit: document checks, reply routing, unverifiable answers discarded, refusal classification and wording, route selection, personhood ext, the TUI's request building (VRC choice, member link), outcome apply, panel rendering, dispatcher hand-off, gate census.

`vti-witness` is not published, so the e2e uses an in-test witness rather than `vti_witness::dispatch::answer`.

## Blocked on a vta-sdk release

The second commit moves to the published releases that serve `vta/witness/*`: `vta-sdk` 0.69 and `vta-service` 0.61 (VTI #2064), `did-git-sign` 0.21 (VGI #157, the same signer on `vta-sdk` 0.69, so the graph keeps one `vta-sdk`), `vti-vetting-pcs` 0.2, and the test mediator 0.42 that `vta-service` 0.61's `transport-harness` declares (VTI #2089).

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — VTA calls carry the SDK's 30 s; each witness answer waits at most 60 s; DID resolution 20 s.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — the router's mutex is held only to insert/remove/send on an unbounded channel.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1) — the witnessing is recorded only after `accept` returns. If the process dies between, the VWC is in the VTA's vault but not listed locally (re-run witnesses again); see follow-ups.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retry loop; the DIDComm outbox is keyed by document id; a failed round is started again by the member.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a (no new loops).
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a.
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*) — none of our own; the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs::vta::witness` / `witness::session` types; the personhood `ext` follows VTI #2128.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*) — no new config.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*) — "handed to the transport" is never reported as delivered; only a verified witness answer advances the round; every failure surfaces on the status line and the log.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered (R2.1) — above.
- [x] Deviations flagged — none.

## Decisions to revisit

- The membership presented is the persona's first live membership with a VMC; a persona with several cannot pick which community's VMC a given witness serves.
- Witnessing records are local (protected config) and not in the VTA app-state sync; the VWC and its evidence are in the VTA vault (`witness:session` / `witness:outcome` tags), so a rebuild could restore them from there — not done here.
- TSP is used only when the relationship uses the persona DID (openvtc's pairwise `did:peer` DIDs advertise DIDComm only). A pairwise DID that advertised TSP would be refused with a clear reason rather than downgraded.
- A persona-attributed relationship relies on the VTA's `did:webvh` persona custody (`persona_key_for`); it is not exercised end to end here (needs a webvh host in the harness).

title: feat(vtc-member-portal): data rooms through the member's wallet (P8)
body: P8 — member-owned data rooms in the VTC member portal, through the wallet extension's page channel (P7b). **Depends on** (extension, merge first): OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#330 (file engine acts as the persona) → OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#331 (`window.vtaWallet.rooms`). Without them the portal shows a "your rooms are in your wallet" card; nothing breaks. ## Design (`docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md` §8.5) - **Pages**: `#/rooms` (rooms shared with this portal, *Share rooms…*), `#/rooms/` (tier, epoch, member identity, room/member storage vs limits; records with sealed titles opened through the wallet; note as plain text; file download; add note / add file with limit checks before the wallet is asked). - **How room ops happen**: only via `window.vtaWallet.rooms.*`. The wallet fixes the verb, acts as the member's **persona** through their VTA (`rooms/keys/act`, `seal/0.2`), and returns views. `requestTask`/`signTrustTask` still refuse `rooms/*`. - **Allow-list**: the page's browser-attested origin must equal the origin of `hostDid`'s verified `SignInPortal`; host requests go to that document's `TrustTaskHTTPS`. - **Room scope**: a room's DID names no host and `rooms/keys/list` returns IDs only, so the **member shares rooms one by one** in the wallet's own window; each is confirmed with the host as the member; grants last 30 days, revocable in the extension. **A `private` room is never shared with a portal** (the portal is the host's own page). - **Consent**: reads ride the share; **every write is confirmed** (room, signing persona, what is written), no "remember". - **Never reaches the page**: keys (file, upload, wallet, persona), presentations, persona-signed documents, raw VTA/host replies, unshared rooms, unverified bodies or file bytes. - **Threat model**: compromised portal page (XSS / dependency / hostile VTC operator) — table in §8.5. - **Deferred**: owner flows (*Run a room*), curation, direct-to-storage transfer from the browser (extension holds no permission for the storage origin; browser transfers are proxied). No spec change: the page channel is a wallet API, and every Trust Task used (`rooms/keys/{act,seal/0.2,list,browse,read,file-key}`, `rooms/info`, `rooms/records/*`, `rooms/blobs/*/0.2`) already exists in trust-tasks-rs 0.31.x / @openvtc/trust-tasks 0.26.9. ## Portal invariants kept Separate bundle (imports only `./InstallWallet`, `./wallet-rooms`, lucide); no new `/v1/member/*` route; member session re-check unchanged; nothing about a room crosses the daemon. Root CLAUDE.md member-portal section gains the rule. ## Tests `src/members/Rooms.test.tsx`: no wallet → explains; list/share go to the wallet with the community DID and never `fetch`; a member's note body renders as text (an `` stays inert); adverse listing → banner; note → wallet; file-fit messages; download name sanitising; hash routing. Full `npx vitest run` (1044), `tsc -b --noEmit`, `wire:check`, `build:members` green locally.

title: feat(vtc/members): admit and make-membership — direct admission by an administrator, decided by the community's admission policy
body:
## What

This PR adds two new draft tasks that let an administrator admit a member without a join request. Both run as one governed ceremony:

- **`vtc/members/admit/0.1`** (*Add a member*). The subject is a DID with no access-control entry, or with only an `application` entry. It is admitted at a community role the administrator names. The community writes the entry, the member record and a revocation slot, and issues the VMC and role VAC, as a completed join does. A former member (removed record, no entry) is re-admitted and reported as `returning`.
- **`vtc/members/make-membership/0.1`** (*Make this a membership*). The subject is a live entry with no member record, typically the bootstrap administrator. It gets the member record and credentials at the role it already holds. The entry itself is not changed.

The shared response, `AdmittedMembership`, and the `Approval` enum (`policyAllowed | approved | waived`) live in the new `vtc/_shared/0.1/admission.schema.json`.

### Rules no policy can change (Conformance items 1–5 / 1–4)
- The requester holds `vtc.members.manage`, read from the live entry, or from the delegating identity's entry for a delegated signing key. Otherwise the request is refused with `permissionDenied`.
- A role other than `member` takes `vtc.roles.assign`, and the entry it seats is bounded by the requester's own.
- `admin`, `application` and any role that would confer authority-conferring capabilities are never seated. These are refused with `roleNotPermitted`; an administrator is admitted, then promoted with `acl/change-role` or `acl/grant`.
- admit: an existing non-application entry is refused with `hasEntry`, and a live membership with `alreadyMember`.
- make-membership refuses:
  - no entry: `noEntry`
  - an `application` entry: `applicationEntry`
  - an expired or suspended entry: `entryNotLive`
  - a live membership: `alreadyMember`
  - a removed record: `removedMember`

### Policy, referral, step-up
The community's admission policy then does one of three things:
- **Admits** the subject at once.
- **Refers** the request. It is parked in the action list and answered with `trust-task-next-step`, pointing at `vtc/admin/actions/show/0.2`.
  - It can be approved only by another holder of `vtc.members.manage` who is neither the requester nor the subject.
  - It runs exactly once, after every check is re-run against the state at execution.
- **Refuses** it with `deniedByPolicy`.

The policy cannot widen the checks above, and it cannot choose the role. Step-up and consent are written as *the model this task is designed for*: SPEC §7.3 item 13 forbids a specification from requiring them. The model is a bound re-authentication for an administrative role, or before parking. In single-administrator mode a referral may be waived (`waived`).

### Registration
Nothing is hand-registered. The registry build, the shared-schema index and `trust-tasks-codegen` discover both tasks from `specs/`. All four bindings are regenerated. Rust emits `trust_tasks_rs::specs::vtc::members::{admit, make_membership}::v0_1`, with `ERROR_CODES` and `schema_index` entries. Proof, recipient and `issuedAt` are REQUIRED; neither task is a bearer task.

## Source
VTI (`vtc-service`) already serves both URIs with local wire types and a local `SpecPolicy`, marked for replacement by generated types. This specification follows that implementation (`trust_tasks/admission_tasks.rs`, `ceremony/admission.rs`) and the VTI spec requirements it rests on (VTI-ACL-037/053/071, VTI-APV-017/018/022). Where the spec is stricter, the differences only add schema bounds, listed below.

Differences from the current VTI implementation, to follow after release:
1. `subject` takes `^did:` and at most 2048 characters (schema). An over-long DID becomes `malformedRequest`.
2. `role` takes at most 128 characters (schema). An over-long role becomes `malformedRequest`, not `roleNotPermitted`.
3. The local types, `SpecPolicy` and `codes` consts are replaced by the generated ones. The response is `Response(AdmittedMembership)`, a transparent newtype.

## Checks run locally
- `npm run build` and `npm run validate`: 787 specs, 114 shared schemas, no new warnings.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all agree, 1870 declared error codes.
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, `npm run build-{ts,go,dart}-bindings`.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --test conformance -- members::admit members::make_membership`: 8 passed.
- The request and response examples validate against the payload schemas (ajv), and all 18 invalid fixtures are rejected.

title: spec(external): credentials/issue 0.3 — details.maxOperations is a guaranteed-to-fit count, clarified in place
body:
## What

`external/credentials/issue/0.3` (#781) added `responseTooLarge` with an optional `details.maxOperations`, described as "how many of the batch's operations, taken in order, would fit". That does not say whether a consumer may **rely** on the count or must treat it as a hint. This PR settles it: it is a guarantee.

- **Producer — Conformance item 7.** A custodian that gives `maxOperations` MUST give a count `k` such that the same request, `presign.requests` cut to its first `k` operations (and `uploadId` left out if none of them needs one, per item 4), is answered within the bound on `sealedCredential`, the account and binding as they were at the refusal. It MAY be conservative: a sealed bundle's length varies with its ciphertext's randomness, so a count computed from an upper bound on the sealed length is sometimes lower than the most that would fit. It MUST NOT give a count it has not established fits: it leaves the member out when it cannot compute one, or when not even one operation fits. The count covers those operations, in that order, and no others: a presigned request's size depends on its key, upload id and operation.
- **Consumer — item 5.** SHOULD split to `maxOperations` (else in half). The first part fits; the rest has no such promise, and the consumer MUST handle another `responseTooLarge` on any part, or on any other batch, by splitting again. It MAY use the count as a first guess for later parts but MUST NOT treat it as a size that fits other operations. A single operation refused this way cannot be split and SHOULD NOT be retried.
- The `responseTooLarge` `meaning`, the *What changed from 0.2* list and the refusal example now say the same thing.

## Versioning: edited in place, no new version

**Rule followed: [SPEC §5.2](https://trusttasks.org/SPEC.md#52-compatibility-rules) for `draft` artifacts.** 0.3 is `status: draft`. Under §5.2 a draft's schema and prose "MAY change without notice". Its narrower rule says an editorial change with no semantic difference on the wire "MUST be made in place … and MUST NOT mint a new version". CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md *Version rules* says the same.

Nothing on the wire changes here: no schema, no `detailsSchema`, no code. The clarification tightens what the existing sentence already claimed ("would fit"). It also relaxes that sentence to allow a conservative count, so a custodian that already returned the exact maximum stays conformant. Minting 0.4 would add a wire-identical version, which is exactly what §5.2 rules out. The change is recorded in the spec's *What changed from 0.2* list as clarified in place. The same approach as #734, which edited drafts in place.

## Implementation check (VTI)

`verifiable-trust-infrastructure` already meets the producer rule:
- `vta-service` `max_operations_that_fit` bisects over prefixes of the built request set.
- It sizes each prefix with `vta_sdk::sealed_transfer::sealed_armor_len_bound`, which takes every randomness-dependent byte at its widest. The resulting count therefore fits every seal of those operations, and is sometimes lower than the true maximum.
- It omits `maxOperations` when not even one operation fits.

The consumer (`VtaClient::external_credentials_issue_presign`, `presign_split_at`) splits again on every refusal and stops when a single operation does not fit. One gap against the new text: when it splits, it keeps the batch's `uploadId` on every part. A part with no operation that needs one is then refused `invalidBatch`. This is a VTI fix, to be made after release.

## Generated bindings

Regenerated all four. Only `trust-tasks-rs/src/specs/external/credentials/issue/v0_3.rs` changes: the doc comment on `error_codes::RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE`, which carries the `meaning`. TS, Go and Dart regenerate byte-identical.

## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate`: 785 specs validated
- `npm run build`: passes
- `npm run check-bindings`: all agree; 1860 declared error codes match Rust `ERROR_CODES`
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, `npm run build-{ts,go,dart}-bindings`: diff as above

title: spec(external): credentials/issue 0.3 — details.maxOperations is a guaranteed-to-fit count, clarified in place (#783)
body:
spec(external): credentials/issue 0.3 — details.maxOperations is a guaranteed-to-fit count, clarified in place (#783)

0.3 said `details.maxOperations` on `responseTooLarge` was "how many of the
batch's operations, taken in order, would fit", which left open whether a
consumer may rely on it or must treat it as a hint.

It is a guarantee, and now says so:

- Producer (Conformance item 7): a custodian that gives `maxOperations`
  MUST give a count k such that the same request, with `presign.requests`
  cut to its first k operations (and `uploadId` left out if none of them
  needs one, as item 4 requires), is answered within the bound on
  `sealedCredential`, the account and binding as they were at the refusal.
  It MAY be conservative — a sealed bundle's length varies with its
  ciphertext's randomness, so a count computed from an upper bound on the
  sealed length is sometimes lower than the most that would fit. It MUST
  NOT give a count it has not established fits; it omits the member when it
  cannot compute one or when not even one operation fits. The count speaks
  for those operations in that order only.
- Consumer (item 5): SHOULD split by it (else in half); the first part fits,
  the rest carries no promise, and the consumer MUST handle another
  `responseTooLarge` on any part or any other batch by splitting again. It
  MUST NOT treat the count as a size that fits other operations. A single
  operation refused this way cannot be split and SHOULD NOT be retried.
- The `responseTooLarge` meaning, the "What changed from 0.2" list and the
  refusal example say the same.

Versioning: an in-place edit to 0.3, not a new version. 0.3 is `draft`;
SPEC §5.2 lets a draft's prose change without notice, and requires an
editorial change with no wire effect to be made in place rather than minted
as a version. Nothing on the wire moves — no schema, no `detailsSchema`, no
code — and the clarification only tightens what the existing sentence
already claimed ("would fit") while relaxing it to admit a conservative
count, so a custodian that already gave the exact maximum stays conformant.
Only the Rust binding's doc comment for `error_codes::RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE`
changes (it carries the `meaning` text); TS, Go and Dart regenerate
unchanged.

title: Add Apache 2.0 licence for source code
body:
## What

- Adds `LICENSE` with the full Apache License 2.0 text, so GitHub detects the repo as Apache-2.0.
- Adds a **Licensing** section to `README.md` and updates the header and footer:
  - **Source code** (`tools/`, `review/*.py`, `tests/`, `.github/workflows/`, schemas and other tooling): Apache 2.0
  - **Documentation and content** (the method, `data/`, Markdown docs): CC-BY 4.0, as currently declared
  - **Third-party material** (the TRQP source snapshot in `review/examples/standalone-trqp/source/`): keeps its own ToIP licences

## Why

Until now the repo had no licence file. The only statement was "CC-BY 4.0", which isn't meant for software, and the code had no licence at all. Sibling DTGWG task forces use Apache 2.0 (`dtgwg-htx-tf`, `dtgwg-zkp-tf`). ToIP spec repos put source code under Apache 2.0 through `SOURCE_CODE.md`.

## For the TF to decide

This PR keeps CC-BY 4.0 for content because that's what the repo already declares. If the TF would rather use Apache 2.0 for everything (as htx and zkp do), that's a small README change. Contributions so far were made under CC-BY, though, so that call belongs with the contribution-governance discussion (GAP-5.1).
