title: vta-sdk-v0.69.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: External/credentials/issue 0.3 — responseTooLarge, sized before the rate, and the VTC splits ([#2127](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2127))

* build(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.31.8 — external/credentials/issue 0.3 (trust-tasks-tf #781)

- **vta**: Vta/witness/{open,present,accept} — the VTA is its principal's witnessed party, the client carries the documents ([#1068](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1068)) ([#2123](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2123))

The VTA side of witnessing (P3), per trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#779
  (rules in vta/_shared/0.5/CONVENTIONS.md). A witness checks that each
  document's transport-proven sender is its issuer and replies to that sender,
  and the relationship DID's one mediator socket belongs to the client holding
  the relationship, so the VTA builds, signs and verifies while the client
  carries every document. The VTA never contacts the witness and never signs as
  itself. vta/witness/request/0.1 is retired upstream and not implemented.

  - open: key custody for the relationship DID (and the member DID) in the
    caller's contexts, distinct DIDs, the VRC/VMC by vault handle, the
    member-link carriage and witness resolution, all checked before anything is
    disclosed. Returns the witness/session document signed as the relationship
    DID and opens a session record.
  - present: checks the handed-back session #response against the record (type,
    issuer = witness, recipient = relationship DID, thread, witness proof)
    through VerifiedWitnessAnswer, re-reads the bound credentials, and returns
    the signed witness/session/submit. Under the member link that carries a
    member presentation in ext["org.openvtc.witness"].memberPresentation.
  - accept: checks the submit #response the same way, then verifies the VWC as
    a VerifiedWitnessOutcome: witness issuer and assertionMethod proof,
    taskContext and task digest over the session document, subject and object
    digest, vwcDigestMultibase. Stores the VWC in the relationship key's context
    with both evidence documents (vault tags witness:session / witness:outcome).
    A repeated accept of the same outcome is answered again and stores nothing.

  The session record lives in a new keyspace, witness_sessions: encrypted,
  excluded from backup, cascades on DID delete, swept by the storage thread. It
  moves opened -> presented -> accepted with compare-and-set transitions.
  sessionUnknown is one answer for unknown, expired, out-of-scope and
  wrong-state sessions.

  Supporting changes:

  - Capability::WitnessRequest (witness-request) is derived by admin and
    initiator, never by application, and is not satisfied by sign.
  - persona_key_for gains a did:peer arm: the document is derived with no I/O,
    and its methods are matched against key records in the caller's contexts.
  - New [witness] config: session_ttl_secs and member_link_witnesses.
  - retry_safety: all three RetrySafe.
  - vta-mcp guard: open and present are Sensitive, accept is Mutating.
  - SDK: VtaClient::witness_{open,present,accept}.
  - trust-tasks-rs floor raised to 0.31.7.

- **rooms**: Direct uploads — rooms/blobs 0.2 straight to storage, presigned by the VTA (trust-tasks-tf #775) ([#2121](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2121))

* build(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.31.5 floor — external/credentials/issue 0.2 (trust-tasks-tf #775)

- **vta**: Rooms/owner/group/renew renews a sealed room; pnm rooms renew refuses a sealed room ([#2112](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2112))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#773.

  A sealed room's (`attributed` / `private`) epoch is its MLS group's epoch plus
  one, so a bare `rooms/epoch/mint` moves the host and no member: every write is
  then refused as sealed under a superseded epoch, and the owner's next
  group/{add,remove} fails epochConflict. Until now a sealed room with a stable
  membership had no correct way to renew, and one way to brick itself that
  looked like a renewal.

  The VTA now serves `rooms/owner/group/renew/0.1`, the third advance beside add
  and remove, on the same remote-first machinery:

  - Item 1: `noGroup` (an open room renews with rooms/epoch/mint), `noAuthority`
    before anything is settled or built.
  - Items 2, 3, 7: `vti_rooms::sealed::SealedRoom::renew` builds a self-update
    commit (no proposal adding or removing anyone) and the epoch link on a copy;
    `room_groups::prepare_renew` retains it durably as the room's one pending
    advance, of the new kind `AdvanceKind::Renewal`, before anything is sent.
  - Items 4, 5: `rooms/epoch/mint` (epoch, link, commit, the owner persona's
    `admin` presentation, reason), signed as the owner persona; applied on
    acceptance, discarded on refusal (`hostRefused`, or `epochConflict` with
    `details.hostEpoch` on `nonSequential`), kept on an unknown outcome
    (`hostUnreachable`).
  - Item 6: any pending advance — admission, removal or renewal — is settled
    through `rooms/info` before another is built.

- **rooms**: Act as the member's persona — rooms/keys/act, seal 0.2, and read/browse/backfill as the principal ([#2107](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2107))

Implements the member-acts-as-persona half of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#771
  (trust-tasks-rs 0.31.3, now the workspace floor).

- **witness**: Vti-witness host service skeleton and witness DID template (P1, #1068) ([#2105](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2105))

* feat(witness): vti-witness host service skeleton and witness DID template (P1, #1068)

  Phase P1 of docs/05-design-notes/witness-host-service.md: the witness as an
  independent host service (VTI-KEY-007), skeleton only.

  - vta-sdk: built-in `witness` DID template (did:webvh; Ed25519 auth +
    assertionMethod, X25519 keyAgreement, #tsp + #didcomm at MEDIATOR_DID, no
    VTARest; kind `witness`) and ProvisionAsk::witness.
  - vti-witness (publish = false): two-phase VTA-provisioned setup with no
    admin-DID hand-off, keys in the [secrets] store; config with at most 10
    identities (enabled defaults to false); one supervised mediator session per
    identity (TSP + DIDComm on one socket, self-resolution gate, jittered
    backoff, MIN_HEALTHY_SESSION, graceful_shutdown on every error path); a
    socket-free dispatcher applying the SPEC 7.2 pipeline that answers
    trust-task-discovery 0.3/0.1, signs every reply with the identity's own key,
    and refuses witness/session* as unsupportedType without listing them until
    P2 serves them; shared-mediator / shared-domain correlation warnings (3.6).
  - vta-cli-common: `witness` is now a canonical built-in name, no longer an
    init alias for did-host-didcomm.
  - Dockerfile.nitro copies the new member; docs/06-witness, did-templates.md,
    CLAUDE.md.

- **rooms**: Backfill from the CLI, and say plainly when a member was removed ([#2097](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2097))

Found in a live run of a two-VTA room on a VTC:

  - A member who had just joined could not read anything written before they
    joined from the CLI: the VTA's rooms/keys/backfill fetches the history from
    the host, but nothing called it. New `pnm rooms keys backfill --room
    --host-did` (VtaClient::room_backfill) walks the chain down until the whole
    retained history reads or the host has no more.
  - `pnm rooms get` told every member who could not open a record to ask for the
    latest commit, including one whose record was older than their group. It now
    names the remedy for each case: backfill for an older record, `keys commit
    --host` for a newer one.
  - A removed member applying their own removal got GroupStateError
    (UseAfterEviction) from the key export. vti-rooms now detects the eviction
    when the commit merges and returns RoomKeyError::Removed ("this commit
    removed this holder from the group…"), and the CLI says what it means.
  - Wording: "an authority credential"; group-create's next step no longer tells
    an owner to issue credentials they already issued.

- **pnm**: Rooms owner register/invite/issue-* and rooms keys verbs — a sealed room from the CLI end to end ([#2092](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2092))

The owner's credential tasks and the joiner's key-holder tasks had no `pnm`
  verb, so a sealed room could not be run on a VTC from the command line.

  Owner (`pnm rooms owner …`), each a call to the owner's own VTA:
  - `register` → rooms/owner/register/0.1 (the VTA signs rooms/create as the
    owner's persona DID)
  - `invite` → rooms/owner/invite/0.1, writes the VIC to --out
  - `issue-membership` → rooms/owner/issue-membership/0.1
  - `issue-authority` → rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.2 (expiry required)
    Both issue verbs write to --out and/or --store the credential in this VTA's
    vault.

  Key holder (`pnm rooms keys …`):
  - `key-package` → rooms/keys/key-package/0.1, writes the KeyPackage base64url
  - `welcome` → rooms/keys/welcome/0.1, from the file group-add wrote
  - `commit` → rooms/keys/commit/0.1, one commit from a file, or every missed
    commit fetched from the host's relay (rooms/epoch/commits) with --host
  - `list` → rooms/keys/list/0.1

  Every party these name — owner, subject, member — is a persona DID the VTA
  holds, never the CLI's session key, so none defaults to the session; that
  includes `owner group-create --member`, now required. `pnm rooms create` is
  marked as the client-key path for a standalone room-host or testing.

  The SDK gains typed `VtaClient::room_owner_*`, `room_key_package`,
  `room_welcome`, `room_commit` and `room_keys_list`, built through the
  generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs` payloads and read through the generated
  responses; vtc-client gains `epoch_commits`. The keys tasks speak MLS epochs
  per their specification; the CLI converts so every number it shows is a room
  epoch. docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md now uses the verbs.

- **sdk**: Keep a Trust Task rejection's code and details ([#1952](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1952)) ([#2093](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2093))

* feat(sdk)!: keep a Trust Task rejection's code and details ([#1952](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1952))

  A rejection no other variant covers now arrives as
  `VtaError::Rejected { code, message, details }` instead of
  `Protocol("trust task failed [code]: message")`. The code was only in a
  sentence and `details` was dropped, so callers string-matched codes and lost
  data the VTA sent: `persona/profile/delete:bound`'s `details.personaDids`,
  a `versionConflict`'s `details.currentVersion`.

  `Display` is unchanged, so logs, CLI output and anything reading the text
  see the same string. New helpers `rejection_code()` / `rejection_details()`.

- **vta**: Rooms/owner/group/remove — remove a member from a sealed room's group from the owner's agent ([#2090](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2090))

The VTA now serves `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1`, the mirror of
  `rooms/owner/group/add`, on the same remote-first machinery:

  - Item 1: `noGroup`, `notMember` and `ownLeaf` (the key holder's own leaf;
    an owner leaving hands the room on with rooms/owner/transfer). `ownLeaf`
    is answered before any host is contacted. No `admin` grant is
    `noAuthority`, before anything is built.
  - Items 2-3: the commit removing the leaf and the epoch link are built on a
    copy (`vti_rooms::sealed::SealedRoom::remove_member`, which already existed)
    and retained durably as the room's pending advance before anything is sent.
  - Items 4-5: `rooms/epoch/mint` (epoch, link, commit, the owner's `admin`
    presentation, reason) goes to the host; only an accepted advance replaces
    the live group. A refusal discards the pending removal (`hostRefused`, or
    `epochConflict` with `details.hostEpoch` on `nonSequential`); an unknown
    outcome keeps it (`hostUnreachable`).
  - Item 6: the next add or remove asks the host its epoch (`rooms/info`) and
    applies (host at the pending epoch), discards (host at the previous one) or
    discards and refuses `epochConflict` (anywhere else).

  One pending-advance slot per room (item 3). `room_groups::PendingAdd` becomes
  `PendingAdvance { kind: Admission | Removal, welcome: Option<_>, .. }`, stored
  at `room-advance:<room>` and claimed with an atomic insert-if-absent, so a
  second advance cannot be retained over a first. The admission-only row
  `room-add:<room>` is still read (its JSON deserialises with `kind`
  defaulting to `Admission`), settled like any other, and cleared with the
  slot; it is never written. `forget` clears the slot too. add and remove
  share `HostCall::{settle_pending, admin_presentation, advance}`, each with
  its own task's error codes, so a pending admission found at a removal is
  settled first and vice versa.

- **vta**: Rooms/owner/group/{create,add} — found a sealed room's group and admit members from the owner's agent ([#2088](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2088))

* feat(vta): rooms/owner/group/{create,add} — found a sealed room's group and admit members from the owner's agent

  A sealed room (`attributed`, `private`) cannot be written to until its MLS
  group exists, and the owner's half of a group — founding it, admitting a
  member — was library code only. The VTA now serves both owner tasks
  (trust-tasks-tf #763):

  - `rooms/owner/group/create/0.1` founds the group with the owner as its only
    leaf, at room epoch 1, the epoch a host records at registration. The gate
    is the one issuing the room's credentials uses — control of its signing
    key — checked by a new `keys::require_key_nameable` that applies
    `sign_payload`'s scope, status, context and caller-key-filter gates
    without signing anything. A room this VTA already holds a group for is
    refused `alreadyExists`, never replaced.
  - `rooms/owner/group/add/0.1` admits a member's KeyPackage, remote first:
    the add is built on a copy and kept as a pending admission
    (`room-add:<room>` in `room_groups`, the advanced group snapshot with its
    link, commit and Welcome) beside the untouched live group; the room is
    advanced at its host with `rooms/epoch/mint` (link, commit, the owner's
    `admin` presentation); only an accepted advance replaces the live group.
    A refusal (`hostRefused`, or `epochConflict` on `nonSequential`) discards
    it. An unknown outcome (`hostUnreachable`) KEEPS it, and the next admission
    asks the host its epoch (`rooms/info`) and applies or discards it first —
    a key holder cannot process its own commit from the wire, so the pending
    group is the only way to follow a host that did advance. The Welcome is
    returned for delivery to the newcomer's key holder, never sent to the host.
    The KeyPackage must identify `member` (`keyPackageInvalid` otherwise); a
    member already in the group is `alreadyMember`; no `admin` grant in the
    vault is `noAuthority`, before anything is built.

- **vtc**: Console Storage page, moving a room's storage, and the rooms' defaults ([#2081](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2081))

P9 part 3b (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §7, §8.1).

  - Storage (/storage, vtc.rooms.admin): every storage config with what it
    holds against its capacity, its credential state (never a credential) and
    its health; configs whose credential is `required` — as after a restore —
    are listed first. A config's own page probes it (optionally writing,
    reading back and deleting a canary) and shows each step, changes its
    label, capacity or default, and retires it. "New storage" creates a
    `local` config or an `s3` config through an external account at the
    community's VTA, named by its context and identifier: the form asks for
    nothing secret. Kinds and auth modes this build does not serve (ambient,
    sealed, gcs, walrus) are not offered.
  - A room's page gains "Send new uploads to other storage"
    (vtc/rooms/storage/assign/0.1). Its existing files stay where they are.
  - Create, update, retire and assign take the requester's operation-bound
    step-up and are parked for another holder of vtc.rooms.admin (§7.4); the
    screens say "Sent for approval" and link the action, never "Saved".
    Retiring the default or a config with rooms is not offered, as the VTC
    refuses both.
  - Data rooms gains a Defaults card (the design's Settings ▸ Rooms; the
    console has no Settings area): each room's and each member's limits, the
    host-wide largest file, capacity and how long a deleted file is kept,
    read-only, with the configuration sections that change them.

  To carry those defaults, vtc/rooms/list's ext["org.openvtc"].roomFiles now
  holds, when files are on, `defaults.{room,member}` (each byte measure capped
  at the host ceiling, as reported limits are), `maxFileBytes`,
  `orphanGraceHours` and `storageCapacityBytes` when set. Files off still
  answers `{ enabled: false }` and nothing else. vti-rooms gains a read-only
  BlobHost::host_limits() accessor.

  The storage response shapes are rendered from the specification
  (vta_sdk::openapi wrappers → admin-ui/openapi.json → wire.ts). Census
  updates: the list-limit census and its Rust counterpart gain
  vtc/storage/configs/list (100), the sidebar census gains Storage, and the
  console document-type manifest gains the seven storage tasks.

- **vtc**: Console room detail and Room usage pages — limits, per-member usage, activity and CSV ([#2079](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2079))

P9 part 3a (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §8.1): the admin
  console's view of what the community stores for its rooms, over the
  vtc/rooms/{get,usage,limits/set}/0.1 tasks #2077 serves.

  - Room detail (/rooms/<roomId>, linked from each row of Data rooms): the
    room's facts; its storage, files still on earlier configs and files
    awaiting deletion; its ten largest files by size only; its limits with
    where each came from (override, rooms policy, community default);
    per-member usage on rooms that are not private (members who added nothing
    are not listed — the host never saw them, so it is no roster); daily
    activity over 30, 90 or 365 days. From it an administrator overrides the
    room's limits, its members' default or one member's, clears an override,
    or pauses and resumes uploads (filesEnabled alone, leaving every limit as
    it is). Each change takes a reason, which the audit trail records.
  - Room usage (/room-usage): the figures grouped by room, member, storage
    config or day; rooms and configs past 80, 95 or 100 percent of a limit or
    of capacity, listed first; CSV export of what is shown, with cells a
    spreadsheet would run as a formula prefixed (OWASP CSV injection).
  - Both pages need vtc.rooms.admin, as the room list now does. Neither shows
    a record title, a file name or a file's contents: the host has none.

  The response shapes are rendered from the specification
  (vta_sdk::openapi wrappers → admin-ui/openapi.json → wire.ts), not written
  by hand. Charts are hand-drawn SVG; the console has no chart library.

  A size field is pre-filled in the largest unit that states it exactly
  ("1 GiB", "1536 KB"), so re-saving a form changes nothing it was not asked
  to. The room identifier is taken from the route as the router decoded it:
  decoding it again would turn a did:web port's %3A into ':' and ask for a
  different room.

  Census updates: the list-limit census and its Rust counterpart gain
  vtc/rooms/usage (100), the sidebar census gains Room usage, and the console
  document-type manifest gains the three tasks.

- **vtc**: DCQL trusted_authorities held at the response, not only published ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2067](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2067))

A criterion's credential query may carry `trusted_authorities` (OpenID4VP 1.0
  §6.1.1). The wallet uses it to choose a credential; the verifier still has to
  check it, and the DCQL matcher does not read it. Until now the VTC published it
  and ignored it.

  - `vta_sdk::x509_issuer::x5c_issuer` returns, beside the issuer key, the key
    identifiers of the authorities certifying it: each certificate's AKI, the SKI
    of every certificate above the leaf, and that of the anchor reached.
  - `aki` is held on both paths: a wallet response whose credential no named
    authority certifies is refused `issuerNotTrusted`, and the join criterion
    match rewrites a gated query to keys only such a credential offers. A DID
    issuer has no chain and meets no such query. The anchors still decide trust;
    `trusted_authorities` only narrows them.
  - Registration refuses what cannot be held: `etsi_tl`, `openid_federation`,
    `trusted_authorities` on a non-`dc+sd-jwt` query, an empty list, or an `aki`
    value that is not base64url.

- **vta**: Gate the TEE first-boot admin claim on a pre-registered c… ([#1987](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1987))

* feat(vta)!: gate the TEE first-boot admin claim on a pre-registered claim DID

  POST /bootstrap/request (Mode B) accepted an anonymous caller: whoever
  reached a fresh TEE VTA first claimed admin, gated only by the carve-out
  sentinel, which a hostile host can make vanish by forging its absence or
  dropping its write.

  - pnm: `bootstrap claim-did create|show|discard` mints an Ed25519 claim
    DID before the VTA exists; the private key lives only in the OS
    keyring (file store refused). `bootstrap connect --slug` signs the
    request with it and drops the key once attestation verifies.
  - vta-sdk: optional `claim_signature` on the sealed BootstrapRequest,
    over a domain tag || client pubkey || nonce.
  - vta-config: `tee.bootstrap_claim_did`, settable only via the tenant
    overlay (deny_unknown_fields kept; admin_did still forbidden),
    validated at boot and covered by the attested config digest.
  - vta-service: verify the signature, require client_did == the
    configured claim DID (403, nothing written), then the carve-out;
    burn the claim DID with the sentinel on success.



### Fixed

- **vta-external**: Probe honours VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS, lifecycle rule per bound prefix ([#2124](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2124))

* fix(vta-external): probe honours VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS; lifecycle rule per bound prefix

- **messaging**: Drop a `#response` no waiter took instead of answering it ([#1949](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1949)) ([#2095](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2095))

A reply that outlives its waiter (the messaging SDK fails pending requests
  when it reconnects at 80% of the token TTL, every 12 minutes for a 15-minute
  token) reached the VTC's DIDComm dispatcher as an ordinary request. The spine
  answered the `#response` with `unsupportedType`, the mediator refused to
  deliver that, and the pair repeated in the log every 12 minutes.

- **auth**: Logins complete behind a shared IP — per-step auth buckets, serialized challenge cap that evicts instead of refusing ([#2083](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2083))

* fix(auth)!: logins complete behind a shared IP — per-step auth buckets, serialized challenge cap that evicts instead of refusing

  Behind one address (a NAT gateway, an app host running many agents) logins
  could stop completing. A login is a challenge then an authenticate, both
  charged to one per-IP bucket: every token that refilled went to a new
  challenge, every authenticate was refused, and a client that started over
  added another pending challenge. At ten pending challenges the DID was
  refused until the cleanup sweep removed them, up to challenge_ttl plus
  session_cleanup_interval later, with a 400 a caller could not tell from a
  validation error.

  - vta-service: anonymous POST /trust-tasks is charged per step, chosen from
    the document's `type` (not the client-chosen header): auth/authenticate
    and auth/refresh each get their own per-IP bucket at the auth quota.
    `Limiter` gains `AuthAuthenticate` and `AuthRefresh` and becomes
    #[non_exhaustive] (breaking); 429s carry the new scopes
    `auth-authenticate` and `auth-refresh`.
  - vti-common: the per-DID cap counts only unexpired challenges
    (VTI-SES-003/005) and, at the cap, evicts the oldest outstanding challenge
    instead of refusing — the refusal only ever reached enrolled subjects, so
    it disclosed enrolment (VTI-SES-007). Listing, evicting and storing are
    serialized per DID. Pending challenges are indexed per DID instead of
    scanning every session. New `SessionStore::pending_challenges` (default
    `None`: a store that does not implement it keeps the count-and-refuse
    behaviour).
  - vta-sdk: auth_light retries a rate-limited authenticate with the challenge
    it already holds, until that challenge expires (at most 10 minutes), with
    jitter. Only the VTA's or VTC's own 429 is retried.

## `vta-sdk`

## [0.69.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.68.0...vta-sdk-v0.69.0) — 2026-10-15 ### Added - **vta**: External/credentials/issue 0.3 — responseTooLarge, sized before the rate, and the VTC splits ([#2127](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2127)) * build(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.31.8 — external/credentials/issue 0.3 (trust-tasks-tf #781) - **vta**: Vta/witness/{open,present,accept} — the VTA is its principal's witnessed party, the client carries the documents ([#1068](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1068)) ([#2123](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2123)) The VTA side of witnessing (P3), per trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#779 (rules in vta/_shared/0.5/CONVENTIONS.md). A witness checks that each document's transport-proven sender is its issuer and replies to that sender, and the relationship DID's one mediator socket belongs to the client holding the relationship, so the VTA builds, signs and verifies while the client carries every document. The VTA never contacts the witness and never signs as itself. vta/witness/request/0.1 is retired upstream and not implemented. - open: key custody for the relationship DID (and the member DID) in the caller's contexts, distinct DIDs, the VRC/VMC by vault handle, the member-link carriage and witness resolution, all checked before anything is disclosed. Returns the witness/session document signed as the relationship DID and opens a session record. - present: checks the handed-back session #response against the record (type, issuer = witness, recipient = relationship DID, thread, witness proof) through VerifiedWitnessAnswer, re-reads the bound credentials, and returns the signed witness/session/submit. Under the member link that carries a member presentation in ext["org.openvtc.witness"].memberPresentation. - accept: checks the submit #response the same way, then verifies the VWC as a VerifiedWitnessOutcome: witness issuer and assertionMethod proof, taskContext and task digest over the session document, subject and object digest, vwcDigestMultibase. Stores the VWC in the relationship key's context with both evidence documents (vault tags witness:session / witness:outcome). A repeated accept of the same outcome is answered again and stores nothing. The session record lives in a new keyspace, witness_sessions: encrypted, excluded from backup, cascades on DID delete, swept by the storage thread. It moves opened -> presented -> accepted with compare-and-set transitions. sessionUnknown is one answer for unknown, expired, out-of-scope and wrong-state sessions. Supporting changes: - Capability::WitnessRequest (witness-request) is derived by admin and initiator, never by application, and is not satisfied by sign. - persona_key_for gains a did:peer arm: the document is derived with no I/O, and its methods are matched against key records in the caller's contexts. - New [witness] config: session_ttl_secs and member_link_witnesses. - retry_safety: all three RetrySafe. - vta-mcp guard: open and present are Sensitive, accept is Mutating. - SDK: VtaClient::witness_{open,present,accept}. - trust-tasks-rs floor raised to 0.31.7. - **rooms**: Direct uploads — rooms/blobs 0.2 straight to storage, presigned by the VTA (trust-tasks-tf #775) ([#2121](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2121)) * build(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.31.5 floor — external/credentials/issue 0.2 (trust-tasks-tf #775) - **vta**: Rooms/owner/group/renew renews a sealed room; pnm rooms renew refuses a sealed room ([#2112](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2112)) Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#773. A sealed room's (`attributed` / `private`) epoch is its MLS group's epoch plus one, so a bare `rooms/epoch/mint` moves the host and no member: every write is then refused as sealed under a superseded epoch, and the owner's next group/{add,remove} fails epochConflict. Until now a sealed room with a stable membership had no correct way to renew, and one way to brick itself that looked like a renewal. The VTA now serves `rooms/owner/group/renew/0.1`, the third advance beside add and remove, on the same remote-first machinery: - Item 1: `noGroup` (an open room renews with rooms/epoch/mint), `noAuthority` before anything is settled or built. - Items 2, 3, 7: `vti_rooms::sealed::SealedRoom::renew` builds a self-update commit (no proposal adding or removing anyone) and the epoch link on a copy; `room_groups::prepare_renew` retains it durably as the room's one pending advance, of the new kind `AdvanceKind::Renewal`, before anything is sent. - Items 4, 5: `rooms/epoch/mint` (epoch, link, commit, the owner persona's `admin` presentation, reason), signed as the owner persona; applied on acceptance, discarded on refusal (`hostRefused`, or `epochConflict` with `details.hostEpoch` on `nonSequential`), kept on an unknown outcome (`hostUnreachable`). - Item 6: any pending advance — admission, removal or renewal — is settled through `rooms/info` before another is built. - **rooms**: Act as the member's persona — rooms/keys/act, seal 0.2, and read/browse/backfill as the principal ([#2107](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2107)) Implements the member-acts-as-persona half of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#771 (trust-tasks-rs 0.31.3, now the workspace floor). - **witness**: Vti-witness host service skeleton and witness DID template (P1, #1068) ([#2105](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2105)) * feat(witness): vti-witness host service skeleton and witness DID template (P1, #1068) Phase P1 of docs/05-design-notes/witness-host-service.md: the witness as an independent host service (VTI-KEY-007), skeleton only. - vta-sdk: built-in `witness` DID template (did:webvh; Ed25519 auth + assertionMethod, X25519 keyAgreement, #tsp + #didcomm at MEDIATOR_DID, no VTARest; kind `witness`) and ProvisionAsk::witness. - vti-witness (publish = false): two-phase VTA-provisioned setup with no admin-DID hand-off, keys in the [secrets] store; config with at most 10 identities (enabled defaults to false); one supervised mediator session per identity (TSP + DIDComm on one socket, self-resolution gate, jittered backoff, MIN_HEALTHY_SESSION, graceful_shutdown on every error path); a socket-free dispatcher applying the SPEC 7.2 pipeline that answers trust-task-discovery 0.3/0.1, signs every reply with the identity's own key, and refuses witness/session* as unsupportedType without listing them until P2 serves them; shared-mediator / shared-domain correlation warnings (3.6). - vta-cli-common: `witness` is now a canonical built-in name, no longer an init alias for did-host-didcomm. - Dockerfile.nitro copies the new member; docs/06-witness, did-templates.md, CLAUDE.md. - **rooms**: Backfill from the CLI, and say plainly when a member was removed ([#2097](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2097)) Found in a live run of a two-VTA room on a VTC: - A member who had just joined could not read anything written before they joined from the CLI: the VTA's rooms/keys/backfill fetches the history from the host, but nothing called it. New `pnm rooms keys backfill --room --host-did` (VtaClient::room_backfill) walks the chain down until the whole retained history reads or the host has no more. - `pnm rooms get` told every member who could not open a record to ask for the latest commit, including one whose record was older than their group. It now names the remedy for each case: backfill for an older record, `keys commit --host` for a newer one. - A removed member applying their own removal got GroupStateError (UseAfterEviction) from the key export. vti-rooms now detects the eviction when the commit merges and returns RoomKeyError::Removed ("this commit removed this holder from the group…"), and the CLI says what it means. - Wording: "an authority credential"; group-create's next step no longer tells an owner to issue credentials they already issued. - **pnm**: Rooms owner register/invite/issue-* and rooms keys verbs — a sealed room from the CLI end to end ([#2092](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2092)) The owner's credential tasks and the joiner's key-holder tasks had no `pnm` verb, so a sealed room could not be run on a VTC from the command line. Owner (`pnm rooms owner …`), each a call to the owner's own VTA: - `register` → rooms/owner/register/0.1 (the VTA signs rooms/create as the owner's persona DID) - `invite` → rooms/owner/invite/0.1, writes the VIC to --out - `issue-membership` → rooms/owner/issue-membership/0.1 - `issue-authority` → rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.2 (expiry required) Both issue verbs write to --out and/or --store the credential in this VTA's vault. ## [0.16.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-rooms-v0.15.0...vti-rooms-v0.16.0) — 2026-10-15 ### Added - **rooms**: Direct uploads — rooms/blobs 0.2 straight to storage, presigned by the VTA (trust-tasks-tf #775) ([#2121](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2121)) * build(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.31.5 floor — external/credentials/issue 0.2 (trust-tasks-tf #775) - **vta**: Rooms/owner/group/renew renews a sealed room; pnm rooms renew refuses a sealed room ([#2112](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2112)) Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#773. A sealed room's (`attributed` / `private`) epoch is its MLS group's epoch plus one, so a bare `rooms/epoch/mint` moves the host and no member: every write is then refused as sealed under a superseded epoch, and the owner's next group/{add,remove} fails epochConflict. Until now a sealed room with a stable membership had no correct way to renew, and one way to brick itself that looked like a renewal. The VTA now serves `rooms/owner/group/renew/0.1`, the third advance beside add and remove, on the same remote-first machinery: - Item 1: `noGroup` (an open room renews with rooms/epoch/mint), `noAuthority` before anything is settled or built. - Items 2, 3, 7: `vti_rooms::sealed::SealedRoom::renew` builds a self-update commit (no proposal adding or removing anyone) and the epoch link on a copy; `room_groups::prepare_renew` retains it durably as the room's one pending advance, of the new kind `AdvanceKind::Renewal`, before anything is sent. - Items 4, 5: `rooms/epoch/mint` (epoch, link, commit, the owner persona's `admin` presentation, reason), signed as the owner persona; applied on acceptance, discarded on refusal (`hostRefused`, or `epochConflict` with `details.hostEpoch` on `nonSequential`), kept on an unknown outcome (`hostUnreachable`). - Item 6: any pending advance — admission, removal or renewal — is settled through `rooms/info` before another is built. - **rooms**: Rooms/blobs 0.2 — the single-use upload key, and reads straight from storage (trust-tasks-tf #771) ([#2108](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2108)) * build(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.31.4 floor — rooms/blobs 0.2 and rooms/keys/act (trust-tasks-tf #771) - **rooms**: Backfill from the CLI, and say plainly when a member was removed ([#2097](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2097)) Found in a live run of a two-VTA room on a VTC: - A member who had just joined could not read anything written before they joined from the CLI: the VTA's rooms/keys/backfill fetches the history from the host, but nothing called it. New `pnm rooms keys backfill --room --host-did` (VtaClient::room_backfill) walks the chain down until the whole retained history reads or the host has no more. - `pnm rooms get` told every member who could not open a record to ask for the latest commit, including one whose record was older than their group. It now names the remedy for each case: backfill for an older record, `keys commit --host` for a newer one. - A removed member applying their own removal got GroupStateError (UseAfterEviction) from the key export. vti-rooms now detects the eviction when the commit merges and returns RoomKeyError::Removed ("this commit removed this holder from the group…"), and the CLI says what it means. - Wording: "an authority credential"; group-create's next step no longer tells an owner to issue credentials they already issued. - **vtc**: Console Storage page, moving a room's storage, and the rooms' defaults ([#2081](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2081)) P9 part 3b (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §7, §8.1). - Storage (/storage, vtc.rooms.admin): every storage config with what it holds against its capacity, its credential state (never a credential) and its health; configs whose credential is `required` — as after a restore — are listed first. A config's own page probes it (optionally writing, reading back and deleting a canary) and shows each step, changes its label, capacity or default, and retires it. "New storage" creates a `local` config or an `s3` config through an external account at the community's VTA, named by its context and identifier: the form asks for nothing secret. Kinds and auth modes this build does not serve (ambient, sealed, gcs, walrus) are not offered. - A room's page gains "Send new uploads to other storage" (vtc/rooms/storage/assign/0.1). Its existing files stay where they are. - Create, update, retire and assign take the requester's operation-bound step-up and are parked for another holder of vtc.rooms.admin (§7.4); the screens say "Sent for approval" and link the action, never "Saved". Retiring the default or a config with rooms is not offered, as the VTC refuses both. - Data rooms gains a Defaults card (the design's Settings ▸ Rooms; the console has no Settings area): each room's and each member's limits, the host-wide largest file, capacity and how long a deleted file is kept, read-only, with the configuration sections that change them. To carry those defaults, vtc/rooms/list's ext["org.openvtc"].roomFiles now holds, when files are on, `defaults.{room,member}` (each byte measure capped at the host ceiling, as reported limits are), `maxFileBytes`, `orphanGraceHours` and `storageCapacityBytes` when set. Files off still answers `{ enabled: false }` and nothing else. vti-rooms gains a read-only BlobHost::host_limits() accessor. The storage response shapes are rendered from the specification (vta_sdk::openapi wrappers → admin-ui/openapi.json → wire.ts). Census updates: the list-limit census and its Rust counterpart gain vtc/storage/configs/list (100), the sidebar census gains Storage, and the console document-type manifest gains the seven storage tasks. - **vtc**: Room usage, room detail and limit overrides — vtc/rooms/{get,usage,limits/set} and rooms/usage ([#2077](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2077)) P9 part 2 (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §6.2–6.3, §8.1): the host tasks the console's room detail and Usage pages read, over the history and overrides #2073 put in vti-rooms. vtc/rooms/get (vtc.rooms.admin): one room's host record, assigned config and every earlier config still holding its blobs, effective limits with each scope's source and the host ceiling, usage and orphans, the ten largest blobs by size only, and on rooms that are not private a count of members with files — never their DIDs (item 5). vtc/rooms/usage (vtc.rooms.admin): rows grouped by room, member, storage config or day, filtered by room, member, config and an inclusive date range (default the last 30 days; invalidRange past 400 days, inverted, or before the oldest kept day), sorted, and paged by a cursor bound to its query (invalidCursor otherwise). Member figures only on rooms that are not private (memberUsageUnavailable when one is named). Activity by config is attributed to each room's current assignment. vtc/rooms/limits/set (vtc.rooms.admin): an override for the room, its members by default, or one member; refuses aboveCeiling, memberLimitsUnavailable and invalidCombination as declared, answers the effective limits, the target scope's usage and overLimit, and is audited (new RoomLimitsChanged event: room, target, previous, current, reason). Not parked, as the specification says: an allowance is reversible and loses nothing. rooms/usage (the room owner's read, an admin chain) on both hosts, through vti_rooms::blob_tasks::usage: one entry per member holding storage or an override, paged; notAvailable on a private room. vtc/rooms/list moves to vtc.rooms.admin, as §6.2 says it should: a community can hand room hosting to someone who is not a full administrator. Both censuses carry the new tasks: conformance witnesses for the three, and error-code witnesses for every code they declare. - **rooms**: Daily usage history, member index and limit overrides for room files ([#2073](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2073)) The host-side data the console's room detail and Usage pages read (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §6.2–6.3, phase P9), in vti-rooms so a community and a standalone room host count the same way. ### Fixed - **pnm**: Rooms and setup messages say what happened and print the fix ([#2126](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2126)) Three operator-facing messages from a live run. A sealed-room write at a superseded epoch (after `pnm rooms owner group-renew`, before the member applied the commit) printed a raw HTTP 400 body. The VTC and room-host now refuse it with the declared `rooms/records/put:epochMismatch` (vti_rooms::blob_tasks::record_epoch_refused, checked before the store, which keeps its own check as the backstop), and pnm matches that code to say the room moved on and print `pnm rooms keys commit --room --host [--host-did ]` with the real values. A member removed from a sealed room was told "a commit has not been delivered" when reading a newer record. The VTA now records the removal (`room-removed//`) when it applies the commit that removed its member, clears it on a fresh join, and `rooms/keys/open` answers the declared `unknownEpoch` with `details.reason` `removed` or `notDelivered` (as `rooms/keys/file-key` already does). `pnm rooms get` tells a removed member so, without suggesting `keys commit`; a member who is only behind gets the catch-up command with the real values. `pnm setup continue` always ended with the `vta import-did` advice. It now authenticates as the phase-1 identity (which is also the cold start's rotation) and prints the advice only when the VTA refused it or could not be reached; on success it reports the rotated DID, which is also what the non-interactive JSON line now carries as `admin_did`. - **vtc**: Admit room traffic on what it proves, not the anonymous per-IP governor ([#2102](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2102)) Every `rooms/*` Trust Task reaches the VTC on the unauthenticated chain and was charged to the per-IP `unauth` governor: a burst of 10, then one request every 5 s, shared by everyone behind one address. Two members on one machine were refused within seconds, and `pnm rooms file get` of a 300 KB file 429'd every time. Upload chunks fared worse: above 64 KiB they also took the large-document budget, five a minute per address and sixty across the node. A `rooms/*` document (the closed set the rooms dispatcher serves) now leaves the anonymous governor and is charged, in `routing::trust_task_admission`: - before anything is verified, to its address's room ceiling (`room-address`, default burst 400 then one every 10 ms). A document that never verifies, or that its room never authorizes, costs that ceiling 25 more, so an unverifiable flood from one address is held to about four a second once its burst is spent; - once the room has authorized it and before the work, to the presenter's budget in that room (`room-presenter`, burst 120, one every 100 ms), or for an upload/download chunk, once the presenter is shown to hold the transfer (`BlobHost::transfer_room`), to the transfer budget (`room-transfer`, burst 200, one every 20 ms: a 100 MB file at 256 KiB chunks waits ~4 s past the burst). Keys are a hash of (room, presenter) under a per-process secret, and are charged only after the room's chain verifies, so two members behind one NAT have independent budgets and nobody drains a member's by naming them. An upload chunk charged to the room ceiling over HTTPS skips the large-document budget (`size::check_for_known_issuer_with`); over DIDComm/TSP it keeps it. Every refusal keeps the 429 contract (x-rate-limit-source: vtc, Retry-After, JSON body naming the limiter); the three limiter names join the table in `routing::rate_limit`. The budgets are an optional `[rooms.rate_limits]` section (address_*, presenter_*, transfer_* as `_burst` and `_interval_ms`); absent, the defaults above. Documented in docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md §8.2 and docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md. vtc-client's room calls now wait out a Retry-After of up to 30 s and retry (up to 5 attempts, re-signed each time) for reads only: records get/list, info, epoch chain/commits, blobs get and download chunks. Writes are never retried. vti-rooms gains `BlobHost::transfer_room` (additive).
## `vtc-client`
## [0.24.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vtc-client-v0.23.0...vtc-client-v0.24.0) — 2026-10-15 ### Added - **rooms**: Rooms/blobs 0.2 — the single-use upload key, and reads straight from storage (trust-tasks-tf #771) ([#2108](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2108)) * build(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.31.4 floor — rooms/blobs 0.2 and rooms/keys/act (trust-tasks-tf #771) - **rooms**: Act as the member's persona — rooms/keys/act, seal 0.2, and read/browse/backfill as the principal ([#2107](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2107)) Implements the member-acts-as-persona half of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#771 (trust-tasks-rs 0.31.3, now the workspace floor). - **pnm**: Rooms owner register/invite/issue-* and rooms keys verbs — a sealed room from the CLI end to end ([#2092](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2092)) The owner's credential tasks and the joiner's key-holder tasks had no `pnm` verb, so a sealed room could not be run on a VTC from the command line. Owner (`pnm rooms owner …`), each a call to the owner's own VTA: - `register` → rooms/owner/register/0.1 (the VTA signs rooms/create as the owner's persona DID) - `invite` → rooms/owner/invite/0.1, writes the VIC to --out - `issue-membership` → rooms/owner/issue-membership/0.1 - `issue-authority` → rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.2 (expiry required) Both issue verbs write to --out and/or --store the credential in this VTA's vault. Key holder (`pnm rooms keys …`): - `key-package` → rooms/keys/key-package/0.1, writes the KeyPackage base64url - `welcome` → rooms/keys/welcome/0.1, from the file group-add wrote - `commit` → rooms/keys/commit/0.1, one commit from a file, or every missed commit fetched from the host's relay (rooms/epoch/commits) with --host - `list` → rooms/keys/list/0.1 Every party these name — owner, subject, member — is a persona DID the VTA holds, never the CLI's session key, so none defaults to the session; that includes `owner group-create --member`, now required. `pnm rooms create` is marked as the client-key path for a standalone room-host or testing. The SDK gains typed `VtaClient::room_owner_*`, `room_key_package`, `room_welcome`, `room_commit` and `room_keys_list`, built through the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs` pay

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): wallet sign-in lets a known identity straight in
body:
After the wallet approved a sign-in, the portal and operator console always stopped at **"Continue as <identity>?"**, even for the same person on the same browser every time.

That question is the T4 defence (someone else signing this browser in as themselves), so it stays for any identity the browser doesn't know:

- **Continue** remembers the subject in `localStorage`, separately for the member portal and the operator console.
- A later redeem for **the same subject** goes straight to `onSignedIn`.
- A **different subject** is always asked, and **Not me** on it leaves the remembered identity alone.
- Cleared, blocked or private storage only means the question is asked again.

`docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md` updated to match.

Pairs with OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#329 (sign-in window closes itself once approved).

## Test
- New test: first sign-in asked and remembered → same identity not asked → different identity asked, Not me keeps the first.
- admin-ui `vitest run`: 1035 pass; `tsc -b` clean.

title: fix(mobile-core): sign the proof's created in the spelling the document carries
body:
## Root cause

Every signed mobile-core builder (auth, push, pcs, step-up, task consent) goes through `proof::attach_proof`. It put the caller's `issued_at` string into the proof configuration **verbatim** and signed that configuration. The document then leaves as a typed `TrustTask`, whose `trust_tasks_rs::Proof.created` is a `DateTime<Utc>`. So the wire carried chrono's rendering of the instant, not the string that was signed. The VTA verifies the JSON as received (`verify_trust_task_proof_value`, VTI-45), so any `issued_at` that chrono does not render byte for byte was refused as `proofInvalid`. That covers `Utc::now().to_rfc3339()` (nanoseconds, `+00:00`), JavaScript's `.000Z` and any offset, so it hit every signed task.

`issuedAt` was never affected. It is parsed into `DateTime<Utc>` before signing, so the signed document and the sent document both serialise it the same way. Only `created` crossed from a raw string to a typed value between signing and sending. This is the same class of bug the `verify_trust_task_proof_with` docs describe (a typed proof rewrites `created`), seen here from the producer side.

## Fix

`attach_proof` now parses `created` as RFC 3339 and renders it through the same type and serialiser that `Proof` uses (`serde_json` of a `DateTime<Utc>`). That makes the signed bytes the same as the sent bytes, and `created` matches `issuedAt`. An unparseable timestamp returns `InvalidInput`. The `attach_*_proof` signatures are unchanged, so the fix applies to every caller at once (including #2129's `witness.rs`) without a merge conflict.

## Test

`session::tests::authenticate_verifies_as_received_for_every_issued_at_shape` signs `auth/authenticate` with whole seconds `Z`, `.000Z`, millis, micros, nanos `+00:00`, `+00:00`, a `+05:30` offset and a lowercase `z`. It verifies each one as received with the VTA's verifier and asserts `issuedAt == proof.created`. Before the fix it fails on the first non-canonical shape (`.000Z`).

## Ran

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6090 passed
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`: passed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

title: ci: install libtss2-dev where semver-checks builds every feature, so the Release PR regenerates
body:
#2101 (#1820) added vti-secrets' optional `tpm` feature, whose
tss-esapi-sys links the system tss2 libraries. CI's all-features job
installs libtss2-dev; the jobs that run cargo-semver-checks do not, and
semver-checks builds rustdoc with the crate's features on. So the

command for tss-esapi-sys`) and the Release PR is left describing an
older main — #2064 has not regenerated since 2026-10-14.

Install libtss2-dev in the Release-plz PR job, the semver report, the
release bump guard and the release-branch preparation.

title: feat(vta-mobile-core): witnessing through the VTA — build/parse vta/witness/*, check and classify the carried documents (#1068)
body:
Client side of witnessing for wallets (issue #1068, P3 follow-up to #2123).

## API (`vta_mobile_core::witness`)
| Export | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `build_witness_task(env, WitnessTask::{Open,Present,Accept}, payload_json, signer)` | Holder-signed request to the VTA; payload checked against the generated type before signing (same shape as `pcs::build_pcs_task`). |
| `parse_witness_response(task, json)` | Schema-checked `#response` payload JSON; a VTA `trust-task-error` is `Decode`. |
| `check_witness_document(doc, WitnessDocument::{Session,Submit}, session_id, relationship_did, witness_did)` | Before carrying: expected type, bound to the session (`id` / `threadId`), signed, issued by the relationship DID, addressed to the witness (CONVENTIONS §6). |
| `classify_witness_reply(request, reply, witness_did)` (async) | Verifies the reply as the witness's, then `Answered{response_json}` or `Refused{refusal: SessionRefused\|ChallengeMismatch\|PresentationInvalid\|Other, code, message, retryable}` (codes from the generated `error_codes`). |
| `resolve_witness_route(relationship_did, witness_did)` (async) | TSP > DIDComm by service `type` in both DID documents; REST never. |

Carriage stays on the relationship DID's existing `TspMediatorSession` / `MediatorSession` (both already refuse a document not issued by their holder / not addressed to the peer).

## Tests
- Unit tests for each export.

  Answered (hand back unaltered) or Refused with SessionRefused /

  generated error_codes constants. A refusal is held to the same proof rule
  as a success.

  documents advertise by service type; never REST.

(TspMediatorSession / MediatorSession). tests/witness_e2e.rs drives the
whole round through this API against the real VTA tasks (MockVta over
HTTPS) and the real witness core (vti_witness::dispatch::answer).

title: feat(vtc): trusted witnesses — a VWC counts only from a listed witness, with its session's outcome evidence (#1068)
body:
The VTC's half of P3 of #1068 (`docs/05-design-notes/witness-host-service.md` §3.5).

## Why
Before this change, any `witnessed/1` statement whose digest bound to an edge the VTC held counted as personhood evidence, whoever had signed it. The personhood route does not verify the proofs of credentials embedded in a presentation, so anyone could mint a VWC that counted. VTI-CMP-030 says verifying a credential does not establish authority.

## What
- **`[witnesses] trusted`, runtime key `witnesses.trusted`**: a list of `{ did, label? }` entries.
  - Empty (the default) trusts no witness. A stored list that is corrupt or cannot be read also trusts none.
  - It is changed through `config/patch` and `vtc/config/import` under `vtc.config.admin`, and each change is audited as a `ConfigChanged` row carrying the old and new lists. The VTC reads the list live, so no reload is needed.
  - The list is refused if it holds a duplicate, a non-DID, a `#key` fragment, a bad label, or the community's own DID (VTI-KEY-007). At most 64 entries.
  - `ConfigKeyDef.trust_semantics` marks this key and the consent threshold, and every change to either is logged as a trust-semantics change (VTI-CMP-090, VTI-CMP-092).
- **One host verdict per VWC (`credentials::witness::assess`)**, checked in a fixed order:
  1. `untrustedWitness`
  2. `noOutcomeEvidence` / `outcomeInvalid` (VTI-CMP-022/023). The session document and the witness's `submit#response` are paired using the framework's four checks. On top of those, the VTC checks that the response's recipient is the VWC's issuer, that the session's opener and the response's addressee are the VWC's subject, that `vwcDigestMultibase` is the digest of the delivered VWC, and that the delivered VWC is the one presented.
  3. The existing digest states.

  Every later state implies the earlier checks passed, so a custom policy that accepts `unresolved` still gets only a trusted witness whose session completed (VTI-VTC-022).
- **Carriage**: `vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.1` payload `ext["org.openvtc.witness"].outcomeEvidence`. This is the `evidence` object that `vta/witness/accept` returns. The namespace is closed, and malformed carriage gets `malformedRequest`.
- **Join paths**: the ceremony facts and criteria matching use the same verdict. These paths carry no evidence yet, so a VWC there is `untrustedWitness` or `noOutcomeEvidence` and meets no criterion.

Why the list is community configuration and not a new Trust Task family (trust-tasks-tf #779): criteria and policy only read the list through the host's verdict, and remote management already exists through `config/*`. Why it is gated by `vtc.config.admin` and not the action list: a listed witness confers no authority. It only decides which evidence counts toward decisions that are themselves gated by `vtc.surface.admin` (join criteria) and `vtc.policy.admin` (personhood), and neither of those takes consent. A criterion with `credentialIssuers: any` already admits more than any witness list can.

## Tests
- Unit: the trusted-witness config. Listed, unlisted and empty-default witnesses. No evidence, or evidence for another session. Each pairing failure: tampered session, another thread, wrong type, forged signature, wrong `vwcDigestMultibase`, another VWC, unsigned response, session with another witness. The carriage parser. The criteria filter.
- Personhood end to end with the shipped default policy: trusted + evidence + bound is allowed. Default-empty, unlisted, no evidence, forged evidence, and the digest states are each refused.
- Integration (`admin_config`): shows the default; a patch is live and audited; a malformed list or the community's own DID is refused; a member gets `permissionDenied`.

Ran: `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (3160 passed), `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. No shared crate was touched.

## Follow-ups
- Standardise the outcome-evidence carriage upstream, and carry it on join submit and supplement.
- Clients (openvtc, vta-mobile-core) need to pass on `evidence` from `vta/witness/accept` when they assert personhood.
- Admin console / `cnm` surface for the list.

title: feat(vta): external/credentials/issue 0.3 — responseTooLarge, sized before the rate, and the VTC splits
body:
Moves VTI to `external/credentials/issue` **0.3** (trust-tasks-tf #781, released in trust-tasks-rs **0.31.8**; floor raised, lock diff is trust-tasks-rs only).

## What 0.3 asks, and what this does

| Spec | Here |
|---|---|
| batch `maxItems` 128 → 64 | spine schema refuses 65; the handler checks `MAX_OPERATIONS_0_3` too |
| item 7 `responseTooLarge`, after `noKeyAgreement`; presign + seal to learn the size; never truncate, never answer over 262144; discard the refused set unlogged | 0.3 batch path: key → presign → seal → size check → **then** rate. Refused set dropped (entries zeroize URLs), never returned or logged |
| `details.maxOperations` (1–63), "when it can compute it" | computed from new `vta_sdk::sealed_transfer::sealed_armor_len_bound` — the widest armor a payload can seal to — bisected over prefixes; so a part of that size *always* fits on the retry (a trial seal's length is random) |
| item 8: no refused request counts against the rate | rate taken only after the size check for 0.3 batches; tested across every refusal |
| consumer item 5: split to `maxOperations`, else halve | VTC `rooms::vta_storage` and SDK `external_credentials_issue_presign`, both via pure `client::presign_split_at` |

**0.2 is still served and unchanged** (rate first, oversized answer = `invalidBatch`): `responseTooLarge` is not a 0.2 code and no framework standard code fits. A VTC on an older build keeps getting what it got.

**Version fallback:** the VTC and SDK send 0.3 and drop to 0.2 on `unsupportedType` / `unsupportedVersion` — the pair the SDK (`VtaError::UnsupportedTaskType`) and the git bridge already treat as one signal. No caching; per call.

**Retry ownership:** the split is new, smaller requests, not the refused one re-sent; it ends when every op is answered or one op alone doesn't fit. `TASK_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIALS_ISSUE_0_3` is classified `RetrySafe` in `retry_safety` (census).

## Tests
- `issue_0_3_refuses_a_set_too_large_to_seal_and_counts_nothing` — 64 `upload-part` ops at a 1024-char `objectKey` and 1024-char `uploadId` → `responseTooLarge`, `maxOperations` = 10 (checked against the declared `detailsSchema`, deterministic across runs); splitting into parts of 10 issues all 64; binding rate set to exactly the number of parts → the next call is `rateLimited`, so the refusal counted nothing.
- `issue_0_3_refusals_spend_none_of_the_rate` — `requestShapeMismatch`, `invalidBatch`, `scopeOutsideCeiling`, `ttlTooLong`, `responseTooLarge` at rate 1, then a success, then `rateLimited`.
- `issue_0_3_refuses_a_65_operation_batch_by_schema` — spine `validate_payload` and the handler both refuse; 0.2 still accepts 65.
- `no_seal_is_longer_than_the_armor_bound` (vta-sdk) — bound ≥ actual over many random seals, within 10%.
- `a_batch_too_large_to_seal_is_split_and_an_old_vta_is_asked_at_0_2` (vtc-service) — named split `[64,10×6,4]`, halving `[64,32,16,16,16,16]`, one-op-too-large terminates, 0.2 fallback.
- `a_refused_batch_splits_to_max_operations_or_in_half` (vta-sdk).

Local, what CI runs: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, workspace nextest (excl. vtc), vtc-service + vtc-client nextest, both `--doc` runs — all green.

## Docs
`docs/02-vta/external-accounts.md`, `docs/03-vtc/data-rooms-quickstart.md` (the "Presign batches are 64" limitation bullet removed), `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md`, `docs/05-design-notes/vta-external-accounts.md`.

No published type changes non-additively (new const, fns, methods only) → `feat(vta)`, no `!`.

body:
feat(vta): external/credentials/issue 0.3 — responseTooLarge, sized before the rate, and the VTC splits (#2127)

* build(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.31.8 — external/credentials/issue 0.3 (trust-tasks-tf #781)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta): external/credentials/issue 0.3 — responseTooLarge, sized before the rate, and the VTC splits

trust-tasks-tf #781 (trust-tasks-rs 0.31.8) narrows a presign batch to 64
operations and adds `external/credentials/issue:responseTooLarge`: a custodian
whose sealed answer to a valid batch would exceed `sealedCredential`'s 256 KiB
refuses it rather than truncate or answer out of schema (item 7), and a request
refused at any check, that one included, counts nothing against the binding's
rate (item 8). The consumer splits — to `details.maxOperations`, else in half —
and asks again (consumer item 5).

VTA (`vta-service`): serves `issue/0.3` beside 0.1 and 0.2, sharing 0.2's
handler. For a 0.3 batch it resolves the key-agreement key (`noKeyAgreement`
first), presigns and seals — no provider contact — and refuses an oversized
set `responseTooLarge` before taking the rate; only a batch that fits counts.
The refused set is dropped unreturned and unlogged. `details.maxOperations` is
computed from a new `vta_sdk::sealed_transfer::sealed_armor_len_bound`, the
widest armor a payload can seal to (the sealed encoding carries ciphertext as
CBOR integer arrays, so a bundle's length varies with its random bytes; a count
read off one trial seal could be one too many on the retry). At the schema's
longest object key and upload id (1024 characters each) 10 of 64 upload-part
requests fit. A 65-operation 0.3 batch is refused by schema at the spine and by
the handler. 0.2 is unchanged: its rate is still counted first and an oversized
answer is still `invalidBatch` — `responseTooLarge` is not a 0.2 code and no
standard code says it.

VTC (`rooms::vta_storage`): direct-upload batches go to `issue/0.3`, split on
`responseTooLarge` (each part a new, smaller request; one operation that does
not fit ends it), and fall back to 0.2 on `unsupportedType` /
`unsupportedVersion`, as the SDK and the git bridge read those codes.

SDK/CLI: `TASK_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIALS_ISSUE_0_3` (retry class `RetrySafe`, as
0.1/0.2), `VtaClient::external_credentials_issue_v3`,
`VtaClient::external_credentials_issue_presign` (split + 0.2 fallback) and the
pure `client::presign_split_at`; `pnm external issue --presign` sends 0.3 and
prints an array of answers when it had to split.

Docs: external-accounts, the data-rooms quickstart (the "Presign batches are
64" limitation is gone), data-rooms-files and the external-accounts design note.

title: fix(pnm): rooms and setup messages say what happened and print the fix
body:
Three operator-facing messages from a live run.

A sealed-room write at a superseded epoch (after `pnm rooms owner
group-renew`, before the member applied the commit) printed a raw HTTP 400
body. The VTC and room-host now refuse it with the declared
`rooms/records/put:epochMismatch` (vti_rooms::blob_tasks::record_epoch_refused,
checked before the store, which keeps its own check as the backstop), and
pnm matches that code to say the room moved on and print
`pnm rooms keys commit --room <room> --host <url> [--host-did <did>]` with
the real values.

A member removed from a sealed room was told "a commit has not been
delivered" when reading a newer record. The VTA now records the removal
(`room-removed/<room>/<persona>`) when it applies the commit that removed
its member, clears it on a fresh join, and `rooms/keys/open` answers the
declared `unknownEpoch` with `details.reason` `removed` or `notDelivered`
(as `rooms/keys/file-key` already does). `pnm rooms get` tells a removed
member so, without suggesting `keys commit`; a member who is only behind
gets the catch-up command with the real values.

`pnm setup continue` always ended with the `vta import-did` advice. It now
authenticates as the phase-1 identity (which is also the cold start's
rotation) and prints the advice only when the VTA refused it or could not
be reached; on success it reports the rotated DID, which is also what the
non-interactive JSON line now carries as `admin_did`.

## Tests
- `room-host` / `vtc-service`: `a_record_sealed_under_a_superseded_epoch_is_epoch_mismatch` — put at a stale epoch answers `rooms/records/put:epochMismatch`.
- `vta-service`: `removal_tests::a_record_sealed_after_the_members_removal_says_removed` — NotDelivered before the removal commit is applied, Removed after, and pre-removal records still open.
- `vta-cli-common`: superseded-epoch put prints the catch-up command with real values; other refusals pass through; removed member is not told to `keys commit`; a member behind is.
- `pnm-cli`: `grant_report` prints `vta import-did` only for NotGranted / Unchecked; connect errors classified by `VtaError::is_auth`.

## Local run (what CI runs)
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6058 passed
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3141 passed
- doctests (both), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, narrowed vta-service clippy (`rest`; `setup,keyring,rest,tsp,cli-synthesis`), vtc-service `vetting-pcs` clippy, `cargo fmt --check`: clean

No version edits. Spec: the VTC now emits the code `rooms/records/put` declares (`epochMismatch`) instead of a generic validation error; no divergence introduced.

title: fix(vta-external): probe honours VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS, lifecycle rule per bound prefix
body:
Two bugs found by the data-rooms quickstart run (#2122).

## 1. The probe ignored `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS`

`vta_external::driver::probe_client()` always used `vta_sdk::http::foreign_fetch_client()`, whose resolver refuses every non-public answer. A store on LocalStack (`localhost.localstack.cloud` → 127.0.0.1) or a LAN MinIO could never complete a probe, so `providerSetupRequired` never cleared — whatever the operator set.

The opposite gap was there too: IP-literal hosts never reach a reqwest resolver, and neither `create` nor `probe` vetted the endpoint, so an account whose endpoint was `https://169.254.169.254` or `https://10.0.0.5` was dialled by the probe with no opt-in at all.

Fix: the same switch the rest of the VTA uses (`EndpointPolicy::process_default()`: `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS` / `set_allow_private_endpoints`, which already decides DID resolution through `webvh_host_policy`).

- `vta-sdk::http`: `foreign_fetch_client_for(policy)` — the same hardened client (no redirects, no proxy, same timeouts) whose resolver, under `private_allowed`, also admits private / CGNAT / loopback answers; `guard_foreign_url(url, policy)` — `guard_public_url` by default; under the opt-in also private/loopback literals, `localhost` and local names. Link-local, cloud metadata (addresses and names), other non-routable classes, IPv6-embedded IPv4, non-`https` and userinfo stay refused in both modes. A refusal the opt-in would lift names `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS`.
- `vta-external`: `probe_client()` follows the process policy (`probe_client_for(policy)` for explicit use). `s3-static-presign` checks the host it will dial (virtual-hosted included) at `create`/`update` (`validate_settings` → `invalidSettings`, member `endpoint`) and again before every probe signs or dials, since an account outlives the setting it was made under. HTTPS is still required (`ProviderHttpsUrl`).
- Public-only stays the default; nothing implicit was added.

## 2. The lifecycle rule covered only the first prefix

`setup` built `bucket-lifecycle.json` from `prefixes.first()`; with `rooms/` + `probe/` bound, sorted-first `probe/` was the only one covered, so abandoned room uploads were never reclaimed. Now one `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` rule per bound prefix (nested prefixes inside a shorter one are skipped, as S3 applies every matching rule), IDs `abort-incomplete-uploads-N`, unique. The permissions policy already listed every prefix; CORS names no prefix.

## Docs

- `docs/03-vtc/data-rooms-quickstart.md`: drops the two *What does not work yet* bullets and the §10.3 hand-written lifecycle workaround (`setup`'s file is used directly); §10.2 says the LocalStack probe needs the switch already set; with #2125 also merged, §10 needs no local fix to this workspace's binaries — stock builds plus `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1`.
- `docs/02-vta/external-accounts.md`: private / loopback stores and the switch.

## Tests

- `vta-sdk` (`--features client`): resolver vetting under both policies; a real request to a `localhost` listener fails through the default client and succeeds through the opt-in one; `guard_foreign_url` in both modes, including metadata and link-local refused even with the opt-in.
- `vta-external`: endpoint check in both modes (and the virtual-hosted host); a probe of a private endpoint stops at `sign` naming the switch without the opt-in, and gets past it to `put` with it; lifecycle covers `probe/` and `rooms/` with unique IDs, skips nested prefixes, defaults to `rooms/`.

## Local run

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6057 passed, 1 timeout — `vta-service trust_tasks::audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry` hit the 300 s cap under full-pool load on macOS; run alone it passes (154 s). vtc-service does not depend on vta-external; it sees only the internal `vta-sdk::http` resolver refactor.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`: clean

`vta-sdk` gains two public functions (additive, no `!`); `vta-external`'s `probe_client()` signature is unchanged and `probe_client_for` is added.

title: feat(vta)!: vta/witness/{open,present,accept} — the VTA is its principal's witnessed party, the client carries the documents (#1068)
body:
Implements the VTA side of witnessing (P3 of #1068): the VTA is the
participating party of a `witness/session` for its principal, and **the client
carries the documents** (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#779, which retires the
never-implemented `vta/witness/request/0.1`). Raises the `trust-tasks-rs` floor to
0.31.7, the release carrying #779.

A witness checks that each document's transport-proven sender is its `issuer`
and replies to that sender. The relationship DID's one mediator socket belongs to
the client that holds the relationship (openvtc registers a profile per R-DID),
so the VTA cannot send as it without a second socket for the same DID, and would
never see the replies. So the VTA builds, signs and verifies, and the client
sends and hands back.

## What the tasks do

- **`vta/witness/open/0.1`**: checks custody of the relationship DID's key and the
  member DID's key (if named) in the caller's contexts (`permissionDenied`). Checks
  distinct DIDs (`malformedRequest`) and the VRC/VMC by vault handle (`notFound`,
  `credentialMismatch`), the member-link carriage (`memberLinkUnsupported`) and
  that the witness resolves (`witnessUnresolvable`). Then it opens a session
  record and returns the `witness/session/0.1` document, signed as the
  relationship DID.
- **`vta/witness/present/0.1`**: checks the handed-back session `#response`
  against the record (type, issuer = witness, recipient = relationship DID,
  thread, witness proof → `responseInvalid`). It re-reads the bound credentials
  (`notFound` / `credentialMismatch` if they changed) and builds the relationship
  presentation. Under the member link it also builds the member presentation in
  `ext["org.openvtc.witness"].memberPresentation`. It returns the signed
  `witness/session/submit/0.1`.
- **`vta/witness/accept/0.1`**: checks the submit `#response` the same way, then
  verifies the VWC (`vwcInvalid`): issuer and `assertionMethod` proof are the
  witness's, `taskContext`/`taskDigestMultibase` point at the session document,
  the subject is the relationship DID, the object digest is the VRC's, and
  `vwcDigestMultibase` matches. It then stores the VWC in the relationship key's
  context with both evidence documents (reserved vault tags `witness:session` /
  `witness:outcome`) and answers. The same outcome handed back again gets the
  same answer and stores nothing new.

## Design points

- **Typestate**: `VerifiedWitnessAnswer` (only from `verify_answer`) is the only
  thing `present` reads a challenge from. `VerifiedWitnessOutcome` (only from
  `verify_outcome`) is the only thing `accept` stores.
- **Key custody**: `operations::persona::persona_key_for` gains a **`did:peer`
  arm** (its document is derived from the identifier with no I/O, and each method
  is matched against key records in the caller's contexts, as for `did:key`).
  Relationship DIDs are `did:peer:2`. Keys are then held to the oracle's gates by
  `keys::require_key_nameable`, and every signature is `ProtocolDefined` through
  `sign_payload`. This also lets the room tasks take a `did:peer` persona.
- **Capability `witness-request`** (`witnessRequest`): derived by `admin` and
  `initiator`, not by `application`, and not satisfied by `sign` (tested).
- **Session record**: new keyspace `witness_sessions`, encrypted at rest,
  **excluded from backup**, Cascade on DID delete, with a sweeper in the storage
  thread. States are `opened` → `presented` → `accepted`, with the accepted stub
  kept until expiry. Transitions are compare-and-set. A repeated `present` that
  loses the race to an identical transition is still a success. `sessionUnknown`
  is the same answer for unknown, expired, out-of-scope and wrong-state records.
- **Config**: new `[witness]` section with `session_ttl_secs` (default 600, range
  60–3600) and `member_link_witnesses`. The latter lists the DIDs of witnesses
  that read the OpenVTC carriage, or `["*"]`. The default is empty, which refuses
  the member link (spec: never build a presentation the witness would ignore).
- **`retry_safety`**: all three `RetrySafe` (conventions §5). The `vta-mcp` guard
  rates open/present `Sensitive` and accept `Mutating`.
- **Audit**: one row per step with the caller, context, session id and witness.
  It never records a presentation, a challenge or a member DID.
- **Approvals**: there is no default rule. The doc shows how to require consent
  on `present` with `pnm approvals require`.
- **SDK**: `VtaClient::witness_{open,present,accept}` over the generated types;
  declared refusals arrive as `VtaError::Rejected` with their code. **No `pnm`
  command**: pnm holds no relationship-DID socket, and nothing consumes a file
  carriage. The carrier is the wallet or agent that holds the relationship.

## Tests

`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/witness_tests.rs` drives the real
`vti_witness::dispatch::answer` as the witness, with the test as the carrier:

- the full member-link round (open → witness → present → witness → accept),
  including the repeated accept and present-after-accept;
- the round with a VMC naming the relationship DID;
- a repeated present, where only one submission is accepted and the other gets
  `challengeMismatch` from the witness;
- splices and forgeries: another session's answer, a tampered challenge,
  another witness's signature, and a refusal handed to accept are all
  `responseInvalid`; a genuinely signed answer carrying another session's VWC is
  `vwcInvalid` and stores nothing;
- uniform `sessionUnknown` (unknown, other context, wrong state);
- key custody: another context's relationship DID, an unheld relationship or
  member DID;
- `sign` without `witness-request` is refused;
- open's refusals (`notFound`, `credentialMismatch`, `malformedRequest`,
  `memberLinkUnsupported`) leave no session behind;
- a credential re-issued between open and present is `credentialMismatch`.

There are also conformance witnesses for the three URIs, a sweeper unit test,
VWC digest parity with `vti-witness`, and the capability test.

`specs/vta/witness/{open,present,accept}/0.1`).
