title: feat(vta)!: vta/witness/{open,present,accept} — the VTA is its principal's witnessed party, the client carries the documents (#1068) (#2123)
body:
feat(vta)!: vta/witness/{open,present,accept} — the VTA is its principal's witnessed party, the client carries the documents (#1068) (#2123)

The VTA side of witnessing (P3), per trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#779
(rules in vta/_shared/0.5/CONVENTIONS.md). A witness checks that each
document's transport-proven sender is its issuer and replies to that sender,
and the relationship DID's one mediator socket belongs to the client holding
the relationship, so the VTA builds, signs and verifies while the client
carries every document. The VTA never contacts the witness and never signs as
itself. vta/witness/request/0.1 is retired upstream and not implemented.

- open: key custody for the relationship DID (and the member DID) in the
  caller's contexts, distinct DIDs, the VRC/VMC by vault handle, the
  member-link carriage and witness resolution, all checked before anything is
  disclosed. Returns the witness/session document signed as the relationship
  DID and opens a session record.
- present: checks the handed-back session #response against the record (type,
  issuer = witness, recipient = relationship DID, thread, witness proof)
  through VerifiedWitnessAnswer, re-reads the bound credentials, and returns
  the signed witness/session/submit. Under the member link that carries a
  member presentation in ext["org.openvtc.witness"].memberPresentation.
- accept: checks the submit #response the same way, then verifies the VWC as
  a VerifiedWitnessOutcome: witness issuer and assertionMethod proof,
  taskContext and task digest over the session document, subject and object
  digest, vwcDigestMultibase. Stores the VWC in the relationship key's context
  with both evidence documents (vault tags witness:session / witness:outcome).
  A repeated accept of the same outcome is answered again and stores nothing.

The session record lives in a new keyspace, witness_sessions: encrypted,
excluded from backup, cascades on DID delete, swept by the storage thread. It
moves opened -> presented -> accepted with compare-and-set transitions.
sessionUnknown is one answer for unknown, expired, out-of-scope and
wrong-state sessions.

Supporting changes:

- Capability::WitnessRequest (witness-request) is derived by admin and
  initiator, never by application, and is not satisfied by sign.
- persona_key_for gains a did:peer arm: the document is derived with no I/O,
  and its methods are matched against key records in the caller's contexts.
- New [witness] config: session_ttl_secs and member_link_witnesses.
- retry_safety: all three RetrySafe.
- vta-mcp guard: open and present are Sensitive, accept is Mutating.
- SDK: VtaClient::witness_{open,present,accept}.
- trust-tasks-rs floor raised to 0.31.7.

Breaking: new pub fields on AppConfig (witness) and AppState
(witness_sessions_ks).

Tests drive the real vti_witness::dispatch::answer as the witness, end to end
with and without the member link. They also cover splice and forgery refusals,
vwcInvalid, a uniform sessionUnknown, key custody, sign-is-not-
witness-request, open's refusals, and a credential changed between open and
present.

title: fix(vta): send a persona-signed room request on the binding whose sender is its signer
body:
Two defects in `Outbound` transport selection (`vta-service/src/operations/outbound.rs`), found in a live data-rooms run against a VTC on a mediator.

## 1. DIDComm was selectable without a mediator session
`initiable_protocols` dropped TSP when it was not wired, but never DIDComm. A REST-only VTA (`[messaging] kind = "skip"`) picked DIDComm for a VTC advertising DIDComm and HTTPS, then failed with *"DIDComm messaging not initialized"*. That broke `pnm rooms owner register`, `group-add/remove/renew` and `keys backfill` whenever the VTC was on messaging.

**Fix:** DIDComm is in this VTA's set only while the bridge holds a live session, the same rule TSP already followed. The protocol chosen is the best one both sides can actually use. An empty intersection gets the existing refusal that names both sets.

## 2. Persona-signed documents went out authenticated as the VTA
Room requests are signed by the member's persona. They went over DIDComm or TSP authenticated as the VTA's own DID, and the VTC refused them with `identityMismatch`.

**That refusal is required by the spec, and it is unchanged:**
- Framework SPEC §4.8.1 and §7.2 item 6: when the in-band `issuer` is present, it is authoritative, and the transport-authenticated sender is a cross-check. A mismatch is a validation failure.
- `bindings/didcomm/0.2` §3: the transport-authenticated sender is the verified authcrypt `sender_kid`, and a mismatch with `issuer` is `identityMismatch`. `bindings/tsp/0.1` §3 says the same for `VID_sndr`.
- `bindings/https/0.3` §3: the transport-authenticated sender comes only from an `Authorization` bearer, and it is *absent* when there is none. `send_rest` never sends one, so the document's proof is the whole authentication. VTI-OPS-020/021 require that proof on every binding.

**Fix:** a messaging transport is in the set only when the DID it authenticates this VTA as **is** the document's `issuer` (or when the document has no in-band issuer). So a persona-signed document goes over the Trust-Task HTTPS binding. The VTA still needs no inbound surface: the reply comes back on the same connection. As a side effect, the VTA's DID no longer reaches the host, which the rooms tasks already intend (`presenting_member`).

I rejected the alternative of sending *as the persona* over DIDComm or TSP. Each persona would need a key-agreement key and its own mediator socket to receive replies, and that is new inbound surface per persona.

The rule lives in `Outbound`, so every caller of `Outbound::send` gets it: rooms owner/group/keys and the webvh host client. VTA-signed documents keep TSP and DIDComm exactly as before.

## Tests
- `outbound` unit tests on the pure gate `initiable_for` and on `pick_transport`:
  - a REST-only VTA can start REST alone;
  - REST-only against a DIDComm+HTTPS peer selects REST;
  - REST-only against a DIDComm-only peer gets the refusal naming both sets;
  - a persona-issued document rides REST only, while the VTA's own document still prefers DIDComm.
- `room_act` end-to-end against a loopback host advertising DIDComm and `TrustTaskHTTPS`:
  - `a_rest_only_vta_reaches_a_host_advertising_didcomm_over_https`;
  - `a_persona_signed_request_from_a_vta_on_a_mediator_goes_over_https`, where the bridge reports a live session as the VTA through a `cfg(test)` seam, `DIDCommBridge::pretend_live_as`.
- Both `room_act` tests fail with the old selection.
- Local runs:
  - `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6057 passed;
  - workspace doctests: green;
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`: clean;
  - the three reduced-feature `vta-service` clippy builds: clean;
  - `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

## Docs
`docs/03-vtc/data-rooms-quickstart.md` (from #2122):
- the "What does not work yet" bullet for this is removed;
- §1 now says members' VTAs reach the VTC over its `TrustTaskHTTPS` endpoint;
- §3 and §10 no longer point at this fix.

## Not in this PR
The empty-intersection refusal is still `AppError::Validation`, which goes out as `malformedRequest`. Carrying `NoMatchingProtocol` typed through to `pnm` would take a new variant on `vti-common`'s `AppError`, and that is a breaking change. It should be a separate PR.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.8
body:
### Specifications

- **external**: Credentials/issue 0.3 — at most 64 presigned requests per batch, responseTooLarge when the sealed answer would exceed its bound ([#781](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/781))

0.2 let a presign batch hold 128 operations and bounded the response's
  sealedCredential at 262144 characters, on the estimate that 128 presigned
  requests are about 128 KiB of cleartext and a third more once armored.
  That estimate does not hold: a sealed-transfer bundle's overhead depends
  on how its cleartext is encoded inside the seal and can be several times
  the cleartext, and objectKey and uploadId may each be 1024 characters, so
  a long key or upload id lengthens every URL in the set. A batch of 128
  could produce an answer the schema forbids, and 0.2 said nothing about
  what a custodian does then.

  external/credentials/issue 0.3 (draft; a narrowed constraint, so a new
  MINOR per SPEC §5.2):
  - PresignBatch.requests maxItems 128 -> 64; every prose 128 for this task
    updated (summary, Direct uploads, Definitions, examples, Security).
  - New error external/credentials/issue:responseTooLarge: a custodian whose
    sealed answer to a valid batch would exceed the sealedCredential bound
    refuses it — never truncates the set, never answers over the bound —
    with optional details.maxOperations; the caller SHOULD split and ask
    again. It is a new conformance item 7, after the batch, ceiling and TTL
    checks and before the rate check; a refused batch does not count
    against the binding's rate. The custodian learns the size by presigning
    and sealing (no provider contact), so noKeyAgreement precedes it, and a
    set built and refused is discarded unreturned and unlogged.
  - The maxDocumentBytes rationale is corrected; sealedCredential stays at
    262144 and maxDocumentBytes at 65536 / 294912, which still hold a bundle
    at its bound plus the echoed batch, envelope and proof.

  Why cap rather than raise the bound: presigned requests are bearer
  authority until they expire (five minutes at most for direct-upload
  targets), so presigning more than can be used before expiry only widens
  exposure; 64 parts of S3's 5 MiB minimum is 320 MiB per batch, and larger
  uploads use larger parts or ask again; a larger answer must cross
  mediators, DIDComm envelopes whose nesting multiplies base64 expansion,
  and memory-constrained custodians and hosts.

  Invalid examples: a 65-operation batch (request) and a response echoing
  65 operations. external/_shared/0.1 already names PresignedRequestSet for
  "0.2 and later" and keeps its own 128 bound for 0.2, so it is unchanged.
  rooms/blobs/upload/begin/0.2's 128 part targets per answer stays true: a
  host fills such an answer with two issuances. Bindings regenerated.

title: chore: release 11 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.31.7` → `0.31.8` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.31.7` → `0.31.8` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.31.7` → `0.31.8` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.31.7` → `0.31.8` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.31.7` → `0.31.8` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.31.7` → `0.31.8` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.31.7` → `0.31.8` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.31.7` → `0.31.8` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.8` → `0.26.9` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.9`) | `0.8.8` → `0.8.9` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.8` → `0.8.9` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

exposure; 64 parts of S3's 5 MiB minimum is 320 MiB per batch, and larger
uploads use larger parts or ask again; a larger answer must cross
mediators, DIDComm envelopes whose nesting multiplies base64 expansion,
and memory-constrained custodians and hosts.

Invalid examples: a 65-operation batch (request) and a response echoing
65 operations. external/_shared/0.1 already names PresignedRequestSet for
"0.2 and later" and keeps its own 128 bound for 0.2, so it is unchanged.
rooms/blobs/upload/begin/0.2's 128 part targets per answer stays true: a
host fills such an answer with two issuances. Bindings regenerated.

title: docs(vtc): data-rooms quickstart re-run end to end, with S3 direct transfer
body:
Re-ran `docs/03-vtc/data-rooms-quickstart.md` from zero against main at 7882a7f1 (#2121, #2112, #2110/#2107, #2102, #2097 in) and rewrote it from the actual output.

What changed in the guide:
- Topology: the VTC runs on its own community VTA (C). A member's VTA cannot yet reach a VTC that speaks DIDComm (below), so §1–§9 keep the VTC off messaging.
- Build split in two: `--features` on `pnm-cli` applies to every package in one `cargo build`.
- A headless alternative to the console for the first administrator (`vtc acl add`, offline) and for admitting a member (a signed `vtc/members/admit/0.1`).
- Bob's backfill and writes run from a scoped client: `application` role, context `bob` only.
- Group renewal moved into the main flow. `pnm rooms renew` refusing a sealed room is shown.
- What a removed member sees: the "removed this holder" message comes back as an error, and later records read as "a commit has not been delivered".
- New §10: S3 direct transfer against LocalStack. Covers the local mediator, bucket, account at the community VTA (bind/setup/secret/probe), lifecycle and CORS, the storage config and room assignment, a 3 KB single-PUT upload, a 40 MiB six-part multipart upload, download with digest checks, the bucket inspected, and what changes for real S3.
- New §11: room rate limits. Defaults never throttled the run; tightened values give a 429, and the client waits out `Retry-After` on reads.
- "What does not work yet" refreshed.

Two code blockers for §10 are listed in the guide and not fixed here; the reviewer decides on them:
1. `Outbound::initiable_protocols` (`vta-service/src/operations/outbound.rs:817`) drops TSP when it is not wired but keeps DIDComm. A VTA with `[messaging] kind = "skip"` therefore picks DIDComm for a VTC that advertises it and fails with "DIDComm messaging not initialized". A VTA that does have messaging sends a persona-signed room document authenticated as the VTA, and the VTC refuses it (`identityMismatch`, `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs:686`).
2. The external-account probe uses `foreign_fetch_client` (`vta-external/src/driver.rs:161`), which is public-only whatever `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS` says. An S3 store on a private address never completes a probe.

§10 was run with local patches for both. Docs only; no code in this PR.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.7
body:
### Added

- **vta/witness**: The client carries the witness messages — vta/witness/{open,present,accept} replace vta/witness/request ([#779](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/779))

vta/witness/request/0.1 ([#777](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/777)) had the VTA make both round trips to the
  witness itself, as the principal's relationship DID. It cannot: a witness
  checks that the transport-proven sender of each document is its issuer and
  replies to that sender, and the relationship DID's one mediator connection
  belongs to whoever holds the relationship, normally the client. So the
  client carries the messages and the VTA builds, signs and verifies, in
  three steps:

  - vta/witness/open/0.1: checks key custody, the credentials and the member
    link up front, opens a session record, and returns the witness/session
    document signed as relationshipDid for the client to send.
  - vta/witness/present/0.1: takes the witness's session #response verbatim,
    checks it is the witness's for this session, builds the relationship
    presentation (and the member presentation) bound to its challenge and
    domain, and returns the signed witness/session/submit document.
  - vta/witness/accept/0.1: takes the submit #response verbatim, verifies the
    VWC as #777 did, stores it with its evidence, and answers as #777 did.

  The record is keyed by the session id within the caller's contexts,
  expires, holds no presentation or challenge, and moves opened -> presented
  -> accepted. Every handed-back document is checked against it (type,
  issuer = the witness, recipient = relationshipDid, threadId, the witness's
  proof) before it is read, so nothing from another session can be spliced
  in. Each step is safe to repeat: open's duplicate is inert, present's
  duplicates are spent by the witness's single-use challenge, and accept
  answers the same outcome again without storing twice.

  Shared rules are in vta/_shared/0.5/CONVENTIONS.md and the shared shapes
  (SessionId, CarriedDocument) in witness-party.schema.json. The
  witnessRequest capability now covers the three tasks.

  vta/witness/request/0.1 is published (release #778), so it is not edited:
  it is retired in place, supersededBy vta/witness/open/0.1, with a status
  note naming its successors, why it cannot be implemented, and that no
  implementation shipped it.

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.8`) | `0.8.7` → `0.8.8` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.7` → `0.8.8` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: method(assurance): deliver a usable shared RAHP baseline through upstream convergence
body:
### Lifecycle stage

Not stage-specific

# RAHP upstream convergence: a functionally usable shared baseline

## Context and scope extension

The [maintainer proposal on #9](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/9#issuecomment-6035912760) called for bringing reusable assurance-testing foundations from the downstream toolkit into this repository.

This issue began as a bounded inventory and fit assessment. [Draft PR #18](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/18) supplies that assessment. The scope is now extended to track the sequenced convergence contributions below, informed by a local feasibility exercise. The original assessment remains supporting evidence; this extension does not imply task-force acceptance of every design choice or a wholesale toolkit import.

Use this issue as the parent delivery tracker. #9 remains the source of adoption requirements and feedback. Individual implementation issues/PRs should reference the relevant increment and its acceptance criteria.

## Objective

Deliver an upstream baseline that another working group can productively use to:

1. Select an immutable specification source and its own risk corpus.
2. Verify retained source identity.
3. Execute bounded evaluation checks.
4. Record findings, reasoning, supporting evidence and limitations.
5. Validate and reproduce the examination.
6. Reassess after material change while preserving earlier evidence.

Repository validation, examination results and assurance decisions remain distinct. Successful execution does not establish target assurance or risk acceptance.

## Basis and current evidence

- **#9:** adoption requirements, repository usability and maintainer direction.
- **Draft PR #18:** source-pinned inventory of eight candidate groups and 46 source assets, upstream mapping and proposed dispositions.
- **Local feasibility package:** isolated prototype, exact component/function manifest, proposed patch, 29 passing tests, seven reproduction checks, seven removal checks and TRQP replay compatibility evidence. Reproduction also passed after extracting the package.
- **Existing upstream foundations:** review schema/validator, explicit `--risks` selection, method/corpus structure, adoption documentation and worked examples.

The local exercise used upstream `ab191485b48bca805ea2cc962c2ea9476a65db66` and downstream `af58247e83d0aff4d47650d929bfc6280d9e41d3`. It retained zero corpus errors and 32 warnings with validation dependencies installed.

The feasibility package is a local artifact, not merged upstream evidence. It demonstrates a bounded TRQP examination, not VRC coverage, complete toolkit portability or unfamiliar-adopter success. The prototype's vocabulary parity check does not implement full consolidation, and its evidence sidecar is experimental. Refresh accepted source and pending PR state before implementation, including CI #14.

### Preparation status

- [x] Candidate inventory and upstream overlap assessment prepared in draft PR #18.
- [x] Local dependency trace and exact transfer manifest prepared.
- [x] Isolated bounded examination and negative tests executed.
- [x] Local TRQP replay compatibility and extracted-package reproduction checked.
- [ ] Increment 1 delivered upstream.
- [ ] Increment 2 delivered upstream.
- [ ] Increment 3 delivered upstream.
- [ ] Increment 4 delivered upstream.
- [ ] Increment 5 delivered upstream.
- [ ] Increment 6 aligned downstream with accepted upstream contracts.
- [ ] Increment 7 qualified and released.

Checked preparation items mean the stated work was performed; they do not mean upstream acceptance or completion of an implementation increment.

## Proposed architectural choices

| Topic | Proposed approach |
|---|---|
| First subject | TRQP first to establish the demonstrated foundations; VRC Spec 0.3 second to demonstrate reuse |
| Source acquisition | Explicitly supplied retained source initially; automated retrieval only when needed |
| Risk selection | Reuse upstream's existing `--risks` interface |
| Evaluation | Keep specification-specific checks alongside their examples |
| Assessment | Reuse the upstream review format, with explicit reasoning and limitations |
| Evidence representation | Start with a documented, structurally validated example-local sidecar; reconsider standardization after the second examination |
| Validation | Compose corpus and review checks through a supported entry point |
| Vocabulary | Maintain consistent definitions with tested schema synchronization |
| Transfer boundary | Move demonstrated foundations; retain controllers, portfolio routing, full engine contracts and bulk catalogue transfer downstream |

## Delivery sequence

### Increment 1 — Retained-source integrity and TRQP replay

**Purpose:** establish a reproducible source-to-observation path.

**Components**

- Extract and harden source-integrity verification from downstream `examples/standalone-trqp/replay.py::source_integrity` into a small helper, provisionally `review/source_integrity.py::verify_source`.
- Adapt `authorization_examples` and `replay` into an upstream real-source example without downstream orchestration dependencies.
- Retain the source manifest, source bytes, attribution, constructed fixtures and expected results.
- Add the example walkthrough and negative tests.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Target and method revisions are explicit.
- [ ] Altered, missing, unsafe or duplicate source entries are rejected.
- [ ] Positive and negative checks reproduce.
- [ ] Schema validity and semantic correctness remain distinguishable.
- [ ] Constructed fixtures and unassessed runtime behavior are identified.
- [ ] Execution requires no downstream checkout.

**Proposed commit:** `test(adoption): add retained-source specification replay`

### Increment 2 — Evidence-linked assessment

**Purpose:** connect observations to an inspectable RAHP assessment.

**Components**

- Reuse `review/spec-review.schema.json` and `review/validate_spec_review.py::validate_record`.
- Add the bounded examination adapter, provisionally `review/examine.py`.
- Define and validate the example-local evidence sidecar.
- Record justified risk references, inference, limitations and proposed treatment.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Review target matches the retained-source manifest.
- [ ] Evidence references resolve and cover every finding.
- [ ] Missing evidence and execution failures cannot become assurance success.
- [ ] Example-local hypotheses are distinguished from canonical corpus records.
- [ ] Existing review records remain valid.
- [ ] Missing authority, delegation and revocation evidence remains explicitly unassessed.

**Design question:** settle the sidecar's structure and relationship to the review record before treating it as a reusable contract. The current review schema disallows extra evidence/reasoning members; do not bypass that constraint with undocumented additions.

**Proposed commit:** `feat(review): bind examination evidence to review records`

### Increment 3 — Vocabulary and validation consolidation

**Purpose:** make the baseline consistent and convenient to operate.

**Components**

- Consolidate review vocabulary definitions.
- Implement schema synchronization or shared runtime checks.
- Compose corpus and explicitly selected review validation.
- Preserve existing commands and distinguish normal records from intentionally invalid fixtures.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Existing vocabulary meanings and valid records remain compatible.
- [ ] Vocabulary/schema drift is detected.
- [ ] Unknown risks, duplicate finding IDs, invalid values and missing resolution evidence are rejected.
- [ ] Invalid teaching fixtures are exercised through negative tests.
- [ ] Errors, warnings and exit behavior are documented.

**Proposed commit:** `feat(validation): compose review checks with shared vocabulary`

### Increment 4 — Validation hardening and CI evidence

**Purpose:** ensure successful checks mean the required validation actually occurred.

**Components**

- Reject missing schema-validation dependencies.
- Integrate with the CI contribution in #14 without duplicating its workflow.
- Preserve execution provenance, warnings, reports and generated-output evidence.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Missing dependencies cannot produce a misleading complete-validation result.
- [ ] Failed, skipped and incomplete checks remain distinguishable.
- [ ] Relevant checks run against the proposed changes.
- [ ] CI output distinguishes repository integrity from target assurance.
- [ ] Reproduction commands and retained evidence are documented.

**Proposed commit:** `fix(validation): reject missing schema-validation dependencies`

### Increment 5 — VRC examination and bounded reassessment

**Purpose:** demonstrate reuse beyond the initial TRQP example.

**Components**

- Recover the exact VRC Spec 0.3 source and relevant historical assessment materials associated with #6.
- Establish source-derived propositions and justified risk mappings.
- Apply the accepted ingestion, evaluation and assessment foundations.
- Demonstrate reassessment at another immutable revision when available.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] VRC source identity, scope and attribution are established.
- [ ] Checks and findings derive from actual source.
- [ ] Earlier records and evidence remain preserved.
- [ ] Changed source cannot silently inherit the previous assessment.
- [ ] Constructed reassessment examples are labeled when real revised-source evidence is unavailable.
- [ ] Findings identify their evidence, reasoning and remaining limitations.

**Dependency:** immutable VRC source reconstruction. The historical #6 description alone does not establish the specification revision to examine.

**Proposed commit:** `test(adoption): add source-pinned VRC examination`

### Increment 6 — Downstream compatibility alignment

**Purpose:** make convergence durable after upstream acceptance.

**Components**

- Consume or reference accepted upstream contracts and shared fixtures.
- Test common positive and negative behavior.
- Identify downstream extensions and version dependencies.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Shared behavior produces compatible results.
- [ ] Upstream versions and source provenance are recorded.
- [ ] Canonical definitions are not maintained in conflicting copies.
- [ ] Downstream extensions remain explicit.
- [ ] Neither repository silently depends on unpublished changes elsewhere.

**Proposed downstream commit:** `test(convergence): verify accepted upstream compatibility`

### Increment 7 — Adoption qualification and release

**Purpose:** establish a baseline another working group can use without contributor assistance.

**Components**

- Conduct an unfamiliar-adopter trial using a different target or instance.
- Resolve observed setup and interpretation gaps.
- Complete supported-workflow documentation and release evidence.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Installation, examination, validation and reassessment instructions are actionable.
- [ ] Trial results and unresolved limitations are retained.
- [ ] Supported and experimental capabilities are clearly distinguished.
- [ ] Documentation links and generated outputs are checked.
- [ ] Release notes identify capabilities, compatibility and reproduction instructions.

**Proposed commit:** `docs(adoption): qualify the shared RAHP baseline`

## Integration queue and maintainer merge order (2026-10-12)

The three implementation PRs are **stacked**, not independent main-branch changes. Review and merge only after the relevant acceptance criteria, CI and contribution checks pass:

1. **[#19 — Increment 1](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/19)**: target `main`; independent review and maintainer acceptance first. Verify tests, source provenance and current-head DCO.
2. **[#20 — Increment 2](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/20)**: currently targets `convergence/issue-17-increment-1`; after #19 merges, **retarget #20 to the then-current `main`**, remove any already-accepted duplicated commits/diff, rerun all regression and examination checks, verify DCO and seek independent review. Merge only the Increment 2 delta.
3. **[#21 — Increment 3](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/21)**: draft, currently targets `convergence/issue-17-increment-2`; after #20 merges, retarget to accepted `main`, reconcile the commit stack without duplicating #19/#20, rerun the corpus/review examples and negative regression tests, verify author-matching DCO on every contribution commit, and seek maintainer review. Do **not** mark ready or merge until these checks are evidenced.

**Related but not on the hard dependency chain:**

- [#14 — CI validation](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/14) targets `main` independently. It may be reviewed/merged before or alongside the above sequence. Before declaring Increment 4 complete, reconcile its workflow with the accepted combined validator; do not install competing workflows or silently assume unmerged CI is active.
- [#18 — baseline assessment](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/18) remains draft supporting inventory/feasibility evidence, not a prerequisite to #19–#21. Maintainers may request its completion/merge separately.

**Evidence and acceptance boundaries:** PRs #19 and #20 contain reported implementation test evidence and passing current-head DCO assertions, but independent review remains pending. PR #21 contains implementation, tests and documentation. On 2026-10-12, its three commits were reconstructed with author-matching DCO sign-off trailers (head `a3919f221ddcfb934bbbb05aad0db97a65c9506a`), with their exact file trees retained. GitHub EasyCLA is green; automated DCO and test workflows were not returned for that head. Complete-checkout test execution and maintainer review remain pending. GitHub EasyCLA success is **not** DCO proof. Never treat absence of a CI run as PASS or a draft's reported mergeability as substantive review. Any accepted predecessor change can require retargeting and renewed verification. Existing unchecked increment delivery criteria remain unchecked until accepted upstream.

**After #21:** draft PR #22 proposes Increment 4's fail-closed dependency fix; #14 supplies CI evidence after upstream acceptance. Increment 5 exercises source-pinned VRC and reassessment; Increment 6 aligns downstream; Increment 7 qualifies adoption and release. Keep #17 open through those gates.

### Increment 4 implementation and CI qualification status (2026-10-12)

- [Draft PR #22](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/22) is stacked on #21 and addresses a concrete **fail-open dependency** in `tools/validate.py`: missing `jsonschema` previously produced a warning and a successful schema check; the proposed change now fails nonzero and includes a negative regression test and documentation.
- Integration becomes **#19 → #20 → #21 → #22**. After each predecessor merges, retarget the next PR to `main`, reconcile inherited commits, run tests and reverify DCO.
- [PR #14](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/14) already contains the intended canonical CI validation workflow and retained provenance/results. Its workflow includes a test-discovery step, so the new regression test will be discovered after both changes land. PR #22 intentionally does not duplicate the workflow. Once #14 and the relevant increments are accepted, require execution evidence from that CI.
- **Qualification gaps:** no GitHub Actions workflow runs were returned for PR #21's current head, and complete local checkout access was unavailable. The test commands have been specified, but there is no defensible full-suite PASS report. PRs #21 and #22 must remain draft pending execution results and maintainer review.
- **DCO:** the three #21 commits have matching trailers; #22's three new file commits include matching trailers. Automated DCO checks were not established from available status results.
- **Scope:** PR #22 covers missing schema dependency only; other CI outcome classification and retained reporting remain dependent on #14 and independent verification. This is not closure of Increment 4.

## Non-goals

- Porting the full downstream toolkit or assurance controller.
- Integrating DPIP or Interop Lab orchestration.
- Introducing automatic terminal assurance decisions, specialist routing or continuous reassessment.
- Bulk replacement of the canonical upstream corpus.
- Treating repository CI as assurance of a specification or deployment.
- Pursuing downstream feature parity as the definition of convergence.

## Completion boundary

This convergence tranche is complete when another working group can perform and reproduce the defined examination and reassessment, supply explicit instance inputs, and understand the results and limitations.

Additional catalogue, freshness, lineage or controller capabilities should follow demonstrated adopter needs. Keep this tracker open until the implementation and adoption criteria are satisfied; local preparation alone does not close it.

## Tracking approach

| Location | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **#17** | Convergence plan, design questions, increment status and completion evidence |
| **#9** | Adoption requirements and feedback |
| **PR #18** | Supporting inventory and fit assessment |
| **Implementation issues and PRs** | Exact changes, tests and acceptance criteria for each increment |

**Next integration action:** obtain review/acceptance of PR #19; reconcile #20 and #21 in sequence. Continue bounded preparation without implying merged acceptance. No new umbrella issue is needed.

## References

- [Issue #9 and maintainer proposal](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/9#issuecomment-6035912760)
- [Assessment progress summary](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/17#issuecomment-6052250024)

title: docs(assurance): explain incremental RAHP assurance model
body:
## Purpose

Adds an explanatory design note for #17 describing how RAHP builds assurance incrementally across source preparation, evidence generation, RAHP assessment and assurance interpretation.

This is intended to help reviewers interpret the current convergence sequence before further increments build on #19, #20 and #21.

## What this note clarifies

- Why Increment 1 is part of RAHP even though it only establishes reproducible source preparation and replay.
- How observations, such as the TRQP time mismatch, should be treated before they become specification findings.
- Why validation and replay evidence do not by themselves establish assurance success.
- Why review vocabulary and reviewer accountability are method concerns, not merely implementation details.
- How example-local hypotheses should remain distinct from canonical corpus risks.
- What future convergence PRs should explain up front.

## Scope boundary

This PR is documentation-only. It does not change schemas, validators, corpus records, review records, examples, CI, or the accepted #17 delivery sequence. It also does not resolve the method questions raised on #20 or #21; it frames them so the task force can decide them more cleanly.

## Provenance

Prepared with AI assistance following review discussion on #19, #20 and #21 and the #17 convergence plan.

body:
#777 specified `vta/witness/request/0.1`, in which the VTA makes both round trips to the witness itself as the principal's relationship DID. Implementing it showed that the VTA cannot do this. The witness checks that the transport-proven sender of each document is its `issuer`, and it replies to that sender. The relationship DID's one mediator connection belongs to whoever holds the relationship, which is normally the client: in OpenVTC it is a `did:peer` whose websocket the wallet holds. The VTA could only send as that DID by taking the connection over.

So **the client carries the messages and the VTA builds, signs and verifies**. This is the same split as `rooms/keys/act`, and the step shape follows `vta/pcs/tokens/{request,accept}`.

## The tasks

| Step | URI | Request | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vta/witness/open/0.1` | `witness`, `relationshipDid`, `counterpartyDid`, `relationshipThreadId`, `relationshipCredentialId`, `membership?: { credentialId, memberDid? }`, `storeAs?` | `{ sessionId, document, expiresAt }`. `document` is the `witness/session/0.1` document, signed as `relationshipDid`, for the client to send |
| 2 | `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vta/witness/present/0.1` | `{ sessionId, response }`. `response` is the witness's session `#response`, verbatim | `{ sessionId, document }`. `document` is the signed `witness/session/submit/0.1` carrying the relationship presentation (and the member presentation) |
| 3 | `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vta/witness/accept/0.1` | `{ sessionId, response }`. `response` is the witness's submit `#response`, verbatim | `{ sessionId, credentialId, witness, vwcDigestMultibase, evidence: { session, outcome } }`, as in #777 |

The family's shared rules are in `vta/_shared/0.5/CONVENTIONS.md`: custody, the session record, authorization, retries, what the client sees, and the shared error vocabulary. The shared shapes (`SessionId`, `CarriedDocument`) are in `witness-party.schema.json` beside it. This is the layout #756 used for `vta/pcs/*`.

**Errors**
- `open`: `notFound`, `credentialMismatch`, `memberLinkUnsupported`, and `witnessUnresolvable` (retryable).
- `present`: `sessionUnknown`, `responseInvalid`, `notFound`, `credentialMismatch`.
- `accept`: `sessionUnknown`, `responseInvalid`, `vwcInvalid`.
- Standing and custody failures use the standard `permissionDenied`.
- #777's `witnessRefused`, `challengeMismatch`, `presentationInvalid`, `witnessUnreachable` and `noMatchingProtocol` are gone. The client receives the witness's refusals directly, and transport is now the client's concern.

## Binding the steps: the session record

- **Created at open.** It is keyed by the session id (the `witness/session` document's `id`, which is also the VWC's `taskContext`) and lives in the context of `relationshipDid`'s key.
- **Holds:** the witness, both relationship DIDs, the relationship thread, the session document exactly as signed, the credential handles and their digests at open, the member DID, `storeAs`, its state and its expiry.
- **Does not hold:** any presentation or the challenge.
- **States:** `opened` → `presented` → `accepted`. It expires after a VTA-set bound, which should be minutes, close to the witness's own session lifetime.
- **Found only within the caller's contexts.** An unknown, expired, out-of-scope or wrong-state record all get the same `sessionUnknown`, so the answer reveals nothing about sessions the caller cannot see.
- **No splicing.** Every handed-back document is checked against the record before anything is read from it: `type`, `issuer` = the record's witness, `recipient` = `relationshipDid`, `threadId` = the session id, and the witness's proof. So nothing from another session, witness or party can be spliced in.
- **Credentials are bound at open.** `present` takes only the witness's answer, so no later step can change what is shown. `present` re-reads the credentials and refuses ones that changed since open (by digest).

## Retry classification, per step

All three tasks are safe to retry without an idempotency key. In VTI `retry_safety` terms they are all `RetrySafe`:

- **open:** a duplicate is an unsent session document plus a record that expires. It is inert.
- **present:** it can be repeated while the record is `opened` or `presented`, and each call builds a fresh submit document. The witness spends its challenge on the first submission it accepts and refuses the rest as `challengeMismatch`, so at most one VWC results.
- **accept:** handing back the same outcome again (matched by VWC digest) is answered again from a stub kept until expiry, and nothing is stored twice. A different outcome for an accepted session is `sessionUnknown`.

## Decisions worth a second look

1. **The VTA builds and signs the session document**, rather than the client building it itself. The VTA custodies the relationship keys, since it mints them. It also has to hold the exact session document as signed, both to check `taskDigestMultibase` at accept and to store it as evidence. And it is the place to check custody, the credentials and the member link before the witness learns anything. A client that holds the relationship key could build the document itself, but would then have to hand it back verbatim, which buys nothing.
2. **Retired, not edited.** `vta/witness/request/0.1` was published by release #778, so editing it in place is not an option. Following the repository's retirement rule and the `confirm/response/0.1` precedent, it is now `status: retired` with `supersededBy: vta/witness/open/0.1`. Its schema is unchanged, and its Status section now names the three successors, explains why it cannot be implemented, and says that no implementation shipped it. Its generated module stays in the libraries.
3. **Names.** `open` / `present` / `accept`. `accept` follows `vta/pcs/tokens/accept` ("takes the community's answer … into the wallet"). `present` names what the VTA does at that step. I avoided `submit` because `vta/witness/submit` would read as the witness's own task.
4. **No `abandon` task.** A refused session ends at the client and the record expires on its own. `vta/pcs/tokens/abandon` exists because an unreturned PCS draw holds a token; nothing here is held that matters.
5. **`present` may be repeated rather than being single-use.** Single use is enforced where it counts: by the witness's challenge and by `accept` consuming the record. Making `present` single-use would have meant either keeping the presentation-bearing submit document to replay it, or stranding a client whose reply was lost.
6. **The member-link check moved to `open`** (`memberLinkUnsupported`), so it fails before anything is sent. The carriage is still the witness's to define. The OpenVTC `ext["org.openvtc.witness"].memberPresentation` is cited non-normatively, and a `memberPresentation` member on `witness/session/submit` is still the right long-term fix.
7. **Capability.** `witnessRequest` is kept and now covers all three tasks. I considered a split (for example, presenting separately from storing) and decided against it: none of the steps is useful alone, and a grant of one without the others would only strand sessions.
8. **Classification.**
   - open: `mutating`, discloses and ingests `metadata`, actsAsSubject, retention `exchange`.
   - present: `mutating`, discloses `metadata`, actsAsSubject, retention `transient`.
   - accept: `mutating`, ingests `personal` (the VWC), retention `durable`, not actsAsSubject.
   - All three: proof REQUIRED on the request and RECOMMENDED on the response, and issuedAt REQUIRED.

9. **`CarriedDocument` is an open object.** Its schema lists no members, so the generated types are open maps, and every member of a carried document survives a round trip, `proof` included. I tried requiring `id`/`type`/`payload` first, and the codegen produced a struct that silently dropped `issuer`, `proof` and the rest. That defeats the purpose of carrying documents verbatim, and the conformance round-trip tests caught it. The VTA checks the envelope against the session record (conventions §3), not against the schema.

## Privacy

- **The client now sees the presentation it carries.** The spec states that this is the principal's own material, carried by the principal's own delegate, and bound under its holder's proof to one session's challenge and domain, which the witness spends on first acceptance. The client SHOULD discard the submit document once it has been answered.
- **What the witness sees is unchanged:** the presented credentials in full, and, under the member link, the member DID beside the pairwise relationship DID.

## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate` / `npm run build`: 784 specs, no new warnings
- `npm run check-bindings`: Rust, TS, Go and Dart all agree; 1846 declared error codes match
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate`
- `tsc --noEmit` (trust-tasks-ts), `go build ./... && go vet` (trust-tasks-go), `dart analyze` (trust-tasks-dart)

title: feat(vta/witness): the client carries the witness messages — vta/witness/{open,present,accept} replace vta/witness/request (#779)
body:
feat(vta/witness): the client carries the witness messages — vta/witness/{open,present,accept} replace vta/witness/request (#779)

vta/witness/request/0.1 (#777) had the VTA make both round trips to the
witness itself, as the principal's relationship DID. It cannot: a witness
checks that the transport-proven sender of each document is its issuer and
replies to that sender, and the relationship DID's one mediator connection
belongs to whoever holds the relationship, normally the client. So the
client carries the messages and the VTA builds, signs and verifies, in
three steps:

- vta/witness/open/0.1: checks key custody, the credentials and the member
  link up front, opens a session record, and returns the witness/session
  document signed as relationshipDid for the client to send.
- vta/witness/present/0.1: takes the witness's session #response verbatim,
  checks it is the witness's for this session, builds the relationship
  presentation (and the member presentation) bound to its challenge and
  domain, and returns the signed witness/session/submit document.
- vta/witness/accept/0.1: takes the submit #response verbatim, verifies the
  VWC as #777 did, stores it with its evidence, and answers as #777 did.

The record is keyed by the session id within the caller's contexts,
expires, holds no presentation or challenge, and moves opened -> presented
-> accepted. Every handed-back document is checked against it (type,
issuer = the witness, recipient = relationshipDid, threadId, the witness's
proof) before it is read, so nothing from another session can be spliced
in. Each step is safe to repeat: open's duplicate is inert, present's
duplicates are spent by the witness's single-use challenge, and accept
answers the same outcome again without storing twice.

Shared rules are in vta/_shared/0.5/CONVENTIONS.md and the shared shapes
(SessionId, CarriedDocument) in witness-party.schema.json. The
witnessRequest capability now covers the three tasks.

vta/witness/request/0.1 is published (release #778), so it is not edited:
it is retired in place, supersededBy vta/witness/open/0.1, with a status
note naming its successors, why it cannot be implemented, and that no
implementation shipped it.

title: feat(rooms)!: direct uploads — rooms/blobs 0.2 straight to storage, presigned by the VTA (trust-tasks-tf #775)
body:
This PR does direct-to-storage uploads for room files, the part #2108 stopped on. It uses `external/credentials/issue/0.2` (trust-tasks-tf #775) and raises the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.31.5.

## VTA
- **`external/credentials/issue/0.2`** is served beside 0.1. It accepts `presign` batches for `s3-static-presign` accounts.
  - The checks run in the specification's order: binding, capability, account, shape and batch rules, ceiling (each operation needs its ceiling action), TTL, and finally the rate, which a batch spends once.
  - Every operation is signed exactly as the specification's table says and nothing else is signed. Unit tests recompute the SigV4 signature from the URL and the headers, and show that each signed header, the signed query and the method are covered by it.
  - The response is sealed as a `PresignedRequestSet`. It is a new variant of the sealed-transfer credential payload, which is `#[non_exhaustive]`.
  - The audit row names the object, the upload id and the operations, never a URL.
- **One deviation from the spec's expectations: about 90 presigned requests fit in a response, not 128.**
  - Sealed transfer encodes byte fields as CBOR arrays, so one presigned request is about 2.9 KiB once sealed and armored.
  - The response's `sealedCredential` is capped at 256 KiB, so 128 requests do not fit.
  - The VTA refuses a batch whose sealed answer would not fit, with `invalidBatch`, rather than answer outside the schema. The VTC asks in batches of 64.
  - The real fix is either a byte-string encoding in sealed transfer (a format change, which CLAUDE.md forbids doing here) or a spec note bounding the count. Maintainer call.
- **`pnm external issue --presign <json|@file>`** sends a batch from the CLI.
- **Setup artifacts** for the bucket now include:
  - the multipart permissions (ListMultipartUploadParts, AbortMultipartUpload);
  - PUT in the CORS rule;
  - an `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` lifecycle rule.

## VTC and hosts: direct mode
- **begin** (items 16–17):
  - The host chooses the object, unique to the upload, never the uploader.
  - It starts the multipart upload and reserves space.
  - It answers with up to 64 part targets, each bound to the part's length and checksum.
  - A repeat begin answers fresh targets for the parts storage does not hold yet.
  - The `direct_transfer` policy is unchanged (`not_private` by default).
- **commit** (item 3, signed by the owner): before recording anything, the host checks at storage:
  - every part's length and checksum, from storage's part listing;
  - a completion bound to the total size;
  - the object's length and composite checksum.
  - Any difference deletes what storage holds and answers `digestMismatch`.
- **abort and the sweep** abort the multipart upload and delete the object.
- **Usage** is reserved at begin and recorded at the verified commit. Admission is as in #2102: begin, commit and abort are charged as presenter operations.

## CLI
`pnm rooms file put/get` now use blobs 0.2 through `rooms/keys/act`:
- The persona signs the begin, the record, the read and the direct commit.
- A proxied upload is signed by a single-use upload key.
- Direct mode is used when the host offers it.

No file document carries the client's key any more. The test `a_file_moved_by_the_members_own_client_is_the_personas` runs this end to end through a real room-host and a mock S3.

## Not changed
The VTC's own proxied-commit PUT still uses issue 0.1: that path has no part checksum to bind.

## Tests
- `vti_common::blob_store::mock_s3` is an S3-shaped store. In enforcing mode it refuses bytes that don't match the signed checksum; in lax mode it accepts them but reports the true checksums.
- It covers: begin → PUT parts → verified commit → record; a tampered part ending in `digestMismatch` and deletion; abort; the sweep; single-part plans; plans storage can't take.
- VTA tests cover batch issuance order and the rate. vta-external has the SigV4 tests and the batch-rule tests.

## Checks run locally
All green: fmt, workspace clippy `-D warnings`, the three reduced-feature vta-service clippy runs, vti-rooms `mls` clippy, nextest for vtc-service and vtc-client (3125), the workspace nextest (6014), both doctest runs, and `cargo deny`.

  `partNumber` / `max-parts` / `part-number-marker` in the signed query,
  `x-amz-checksum-algorithm`, `x-amz-mp-object-size`, `x-amz-checksum-mode`)
  and nothing else; the set is sealed as a `PresignedRequestSet`
  (`ExternalCredentialPayload::PresignedRequests`, additive), audited by
  object, upload id and operations, never by URL.
- A batch whose sealed answer exceeds the response's 256 KiB is refused
  `invalidBatch`: sealed transfer carries byte fields as CBOR arrays, so a
  presigned request is ~2.9 KiB sealed, and 128 do not fit. Consumers ask in
  batches of 64.

  ListMultipartUploadParts / AbortMultipartUpload, PUT CORS and an
  AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle rule.

VTC / hosts — `rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,commit,abort}/0.2` direct mode
(begin items 16–17, commit item 3, abort item 2):
- begin chooses the object (`BlobKey::for_upload`, unique per upload),
  creates the multipart upload, reserves, and answers ≤ 64 bound part
  targets; a re-begin answers fresh targets for parts storage does not hold.
  Plans storage cannot take (parts < 5 MiB) fall back to proxied or
  `noTransferMode` naming both modes. `[rooms.files] direct_transfer` still
  governs (`not_private` default).
- commit (owner-signed) verifies at storage before recording: every part's
  length and checksum from list-parts, completion bound to the total size,
  head length + composite checksum; any difference deletes what storage holds,
  releases the reservation and answers `digestMismatch`.
- abort and the sweep abort the multipart upload and delete the object.
- `BlobStore::direct_*` and `Presigner::presign_ops` (vti-common), the
  vta-account presigner over issue 0.2, and `blob_store::mock_s3` — an
  S3-shaped test store enforcing (or, lax, ignoring) the signed checksums.

begin, record, read and the direct commit are the persona's; a proxied
upload's chunks and commit are signed by a single-use upload key; direct

title: fix(vtc): a vetter resend re-signs a grant that names a retired status list URL
body:
## Problem

`vtc/vetting/vetters/resend` delivered the stored grant credential byte for byte. A grant issued before `public_url` changed still names the old status-list URL after the list itself was re-pointed (#2087). No holder can establish that credential's status, so openvtc refuses it as `StatusUnknown` and every resend repeats the refusal. Asking again could never help.

Seen on `test-vtc`: a grant minted 2026-10-14 names `https://test-vtc.storm.ws/v1/status-lists/revocation`, which no longer resolves. Membership renewal recovered, because it mints new credentials. The vetter resend replayed the dead link, and openvtc dropped it without telling the user (fixed separately in OpenVTC/openvtc).

## Fix

- `resend` compares the credential's `credentialStatus.statusListCredential` with the URL the revocation list is served at. When they differ, it re-signs the credential before delivering it (`reissue_if_stale`).
- The re-issue keeps the credential `id`, the revocation slot and the exact validity window (new `credentials::dtg::issue_role_action_in`). Only the list URL and the proof change.
- The row is written with `endorsements::replace_if_unchanged`, a conditional `Batch` that requires the row's stored bytes to be unchanged, so a revocation landing meanwhile is never overwritten. On a race the resend re-reads: it delivers the grant if it is still live and answers `notGranted` if it is gone. After two races it answers `unavailable`.
- The re-issue is audited as `VecIssued` under the same credential id.

## Tests

- New: `vetting_journey::a_resend_reissues_a_grant_that_names_a_retired_status_list_url`. It grants under an old URL, re-points the list, and checks that the resend carries the new URL with the same id, slot, `validFrom`, `validUntil` and subject but a new proof. A second resend delivers the re-issued credential unchanged.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -E 'test(/vett|endorse|status_list/)'`: 170 tests passed, 1 reported as leaky.
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The full vtc-service suite was not run locally.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): none added
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): no lock taken; the write is a conditional batch
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the re-signed row is stored before delivery; a crash in between leaves a valid credential that the next resend delivers
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): at most two attempts, each re-reading the row
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none; the resend response is unchanged
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): an unprovisioned status list is an error, never a skip
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): the log says "re-signed", and delivery is still "handed to the transport"
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): see above
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.6
body:
### Added

- **vta/witness**: Vta/witness/request — the VTA runs a witnessed session for its principal's relationship ([#777](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/777))

A Verifiable Witness Credential is issued to the participating party of a
  witness/session, who presents its relationship credential bound to the
  session's challenge. A principal whose keys and credentials live in a VTA
  cannot do that from a client that holds neither. This adds
  vta/witness/request/0.1: the client names a witness, the relationship
  (relationshipDid, counterpartyDid, the enclosing thread) and credentials by
  vault handle; the VTA opens the session as the relationship DID, builds and
  signs the presentation itself, submits, verifies the VWC as a verifier of
  the evidence would (issuer = session recipient = response signer,
  taskContext/taskDigest over the session document as sent, subject and
  object digest, vwcDigestMultibase), and stores it in the credential vault
  with its evidence — the session document as sent and the submit #response
  as received. It answers with the vault handle, the digest and the two
  evidence documents (which carry the VWC); never a key, a presentation or
  the challenge.

  Membership evidence is optional. A VMC naming the relationship DID rides
  in the relationship presentation; one naming a member DID needs an
  explicit memberDid, and the VTA builds a second presentation by that DID
  bound to the same session. witness/session/submit/0.1 has no member for
  it, so its carriage is the witness's own (SPEC 4.5.1 leaves an ext
  namespace's semantics to its controller); the OpenVTC carriage is cited
  non-normatively.

  Authorization is standing over every context the task touches, expressed
  as the new witnessRequest capability (witness-request in device/_shared
  0.1), which is not sign and is not satisfied by sign. Errors: notFound,
  credentialMismatch, noMatchingProtocol, witnessUnreachable (retryable),
  witnessRefused, challengeMismatch, presentationInvalid (the witness's own
  code and message in details), vwcInvalid.

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in

checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

title: fix(vetting)!: say when a vetter credential is refused, not only in the debug log
body:
## Problem

When a delivered vetter grant failed its check, openvtc dropped it with a `warn!`. The failure could be an unreachable status list, a bad proof, a credential naming the wrong subject, no membership, or a delivery not signed by the community. That warning only reaches a file when `OPENVTC_DEBUG_LOG` is set. After "… is sending your vetter credential again" nothing followed, so a resend that arrived and was refused looked exactly like one that never came.

Seen in practice: the community's grant named a status-list URL that no longer resolves, every resend was refused, and nothing appeared anywhere. The VTC side is fixed in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure (resend re-signs a grant that names a retired URL).

## Fix

- New `Notice::GrantRefused { community, reason }`, raised from every refusal path in `vetting::inbound::{statement, vetter_grant}`. The activity log shows "Refused the vetter credential from <community>: <reason>. You are not a vetter there until one is accepted." The reason is the `IssuedCredentialError` text, which names what failed and never the credential.
- Only a community the receiving persona is a member of can raise it. A stranger's delivery is still only logged at `warn!`, so nobody else can write to the activity feed this way.
- **Breaking:** `openvtc_core::vetting::inbound::Notice` gains a variant.

## Tests

- Updated three tests that expected a refusal to be silent: `a_tampered_vetter_grant_is_not_kept`, `a_grant_whose_status_cannot_be_read_is_not_kept` (which now asserts that the reason names the revocation status) and `a_vetter_grant_is_kept_only_from_its_community`. The relayed-by-a-stranger test still expects no notice.
- `cargo nextest run -p openvtc-core`: 1104 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p openvtc`: 970 passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): none added
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1): nothing new is stored, only an activity-log line
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): this PR is that fix
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): n/a
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: Memory audit: item-level reads and tamper-evident chaining
body:
## Problem
Memory audit rows (`memory.put/list/delete`) record the actor DID and context, but:
- `list` logs that the context was read, not *which items* the caller then used. For agent memory, "which agent saw what" is the question a user will ask.
- Rows are best-effort and not tamper-evident. Hash-chaining is designed (`docs/05-design-notes/vta-audit-chaining.md`) but has no code.

## Proposal
- Log item-level reads: once the `query`/`get` path exists (see the versioned-memory issue), log the keys returned per call. For whole-context `list`, log the count and a digest of the key set.
- Implement `vta-audit-chaining.md` for the memory and rooms audit streams first: each row commits to the previous row's hash, with periodic checkpoints.
- Expose a user-facing "who read or changed my memory" query, filterable by agent DID and time, through pnm and vta-mcp.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Audit rows for memory reads identify the items returned.
- [ ] The chain verifies end-to-end, and a deleted or altered row is detected.
- [ ] `pnm audit memory --actor <did>` (or equivalent) works.
author: stormer78

title: vti-rooms: add basis / confidence / evidence to the signed record body
body:
## Problem
Sealed room records are signed by their writer (`SealedRecordBody`), so a reader can prove *who* wrote a record and whether it was a member or that member's agent under an attenuated VAC (`data-rooms.md` §6.1). They cannot say *what kind of claim* the record is. In a room used as shared memory or an evidence locker, an agent's inference ("customer is price-sensitive") looks the same as an observed fact or a credential-backed statement.

## Proposal
Extend the signed body schema (`rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json`) with optional:
- `basis`: `declared | observed | verified | inferred` (aligned with the vta-agent-memory provenance issue)
- `confidence` (0–1)
- `evidence`: references to other record keys or credential ids
- `validFor`: an optional statement of permitted use (e.g. "instructional personalisation only")

All of these sit inside the signature. Agent writers should default to `inferred`. Clients show the basis, and agent recall weights by it.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Schema bump with the new fields inside the signed body; old records still verify.
- [ ] `pnm rooms get/list` display the basis.
- [ ] Tests show a basis changed after signing fails verification.

title: Unified recall across personal memory and Data Rooms with per-result provenance
body:
## Problem
An agent's knowledge is split between personal memory (`vta/memory/*`) and the Data Rooms it belongs to (`rooms/*`). Recall only searches personal memory. `data-rooms.md` §12–13 plans "recall union across personal memory and rooms, provenance on each result (room, author, human/agent)", but nothing implements it.

## Proposal
- `memory_recall` gains an optional `sources` filter (personal, rooms the agent's credentials admit, or both).
- Each result carries its source (personal or room DID), author DID, human-or-agent authorship (from the in-body signature), status, and basis (see the provenance issue).
- Room records are fenced in the same way as personal memory (see `src/fence.rs`). Deprecated room records are demoted.
- Writing to a room stays an explicit user act. Recall never saves to a room implicitly.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Recall across one personal context plus at least one room, with per-result provenance.
- [ ] A room record whose signature fails verification is excluded, with a test.
author: stormer78

title: Memory lifecycle: status, expiry, supersede and dispute instead of overwrite
body:
## Problem
Memory has no lifecycle beyond overwrite and hard delete:
- `memory_save` upserts, so the previous content is lost and concurrent writers race (last write wins).
- There is no expiry. A preference from last year has the same standing as one from today.
- `memory_forget` is permanent. There is no way to retract or dispute a memory while keeping a record that it existed.

Data Rooms already have the pieces: `status` `active|deprecated|retracted`, `expectedVersion` preconditions where the conflict returns the winner, and tombstones (`data-rooms.md` §6).

## Proposal
- `status`: `active | deprecated | retracted | disputed`. Recall excludes retracted, demotes deprecated and disputed, and shows the status.
- `validUntil` (optional) and `reviewAfter` (optional). Expired memories drop out of recall, and stale ones are flagged for confirmation.
- `supersedes`: a save that replaces a memory links to the previous version rather than erasing it.
- Optimistic concurrency via `expectedVersion` (depends on the server-side issue in verifiable-trust-infrastructure).
- New tools or commands: `memory_retract`, `memory_dispute` (with a reason), and a `/memories --stale` review.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Status, validUntil and supersedes round-trip and are honoured by recall.
- [ ] A conflicting concurrent save is rejected, with the winning version returned.
- [ ] Retract keeps a tombstone; forget remains the hard-delete path.
author: stormer78

title: Add epistemic provenance to memories: declared / observed / verified / inferred + confidence
body:
## Problem
Memory types (`user|feedback|project|reference`) say what a memory is *about*, not *what kind of claim* it is. The store can't tell something the user stated, something an agent observed, something backed by a credential, and something a model inferred. A transient behaviour inferred once ("prefers short answers") then becomes indistinguishable from a durable, user-stated preference, and it is reused across every session and agent with the same weight.

## Proposal
Add an epistemic provenance block to the record (signed with it; see the signed-records issue):
- `basis`: `declared` (user said it) | `observed` (agent saw it happen) | `verified` (backed by a VC — carry the credential id/issuer) | `inferred` (model conclusion)
- `confidence`: optional 0–1 for `inferred`/`observed`
- `source`: optional reference (session, room record, credential)

Recall ranking and the skill's guidance should down-weight `inferred`. The `memory_save` tool should require `basis` and default agent saves to `inferred` unless the user stated the fact. Reuse the persona provenance vocabulary (`selfAsserted` / `credentialBacked`) where it maps, so memory and persona don't diverge.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `basis` is required on new saves, and the MCP tool schema and skill are updated.
- [ ] Recall summaries display `basis` and confidence.
- [ ] Ranking applies a basis weight, with a test.

title: Purpose binding on room VACs and memory grants
body:
## Problem
Grants for memory and rooms say *who* may do *what* until *when*: VAC verbs, audience and `validUntil`, plus memory context ACLs with `--expires`. They don't say *what for*. An agent granted `read` on a room or a memory context can use the content for any purpose, and nothing records the intended use for a later audit.

## Proposal
- Add an optional `purpose` claim to VACs and to memory ACL grants, drawn from a small registered vocabulary (e.g. `personalisation`, `task-execution`, `analytics`, `training` — the last denied by default). Free text is allowed as a qualifier.
- Presentations must carry the purpose, and it is written to the audit row with every read.
- vta-mcp and the agent memory plugin pass the purpose through from configuration.
- Governance (`rooms.rego`, VTC policy) can restrict which purposes may be granted.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The purpose claim is specified (DTG VAC extension and memory ACL field).
- [ ] Audit rows include the purpose.
- [ ] A policy test denies a disallowed purpose.
author: stormer78

title: vti-rooms: per-record validUntil, retentionPolicy + prune verb, crypto-deletion verb
body:
## Problem
Room lifecycle is room-level (Live → Lapsed → Dormant → Reclaimable, `retentionDays`). Records don't expire individually. The room `retentionPolicy` and a prune verb are still pending, and cryptographic deletion (`prune_epoch_links_before`) is "primitive only, no verb reaches it" (`docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md`).

Shared agent memory needs per-item expiry: a meeting note may be useful for 30 days, a decision for years.

## Proposal
- Optional signed `validUntil` per record. Expired records are excluded from default `list`/recall, and the host may reclaim their blobs after a grace period.
- Specify and implement the room `retentionPolicy` plus a `rooms/records/prune` verb (curate/admin).
- Wire `prune_epoch_links_before` to an admin verb once its spec lands, so "delete everything before X" is real on encrypted tiers.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Records with a past `validUntil` are hidden by default and visible with `--include-expired`.
- [ ] The prune verb is specified and implemented, with audit rows.
- [ ] The crypto-deletion verb is tracked or implemented.
author: stormer78

title: vta/memory: versioned writes, tombstones and a vta/memory/query task
body:
## Problem
`vta-service/src/operations/memory.rs` implements `vta/memory/{put,list,delete}/0.1` as an upsert KV store:
- `put` overwrites unconditionally, with no version and no precondition, so multi-writer contexts race.
- `delete` is a hard delete with no tombstone, so other devices' caches can't converge.
- `list` returns the whole context in key order, with no prefix, cursor or search (see vta-agent-memory README: "no prefix, no cursor, no search").

The app-state and rooms stores already follow a better pattern: `expectedVersion` preconditions where the conflict carries the winner, `expectedVersion: 0` for create-only, `sinceVersion` watermarks, cursor pagination (`vti_common::pagination`), and tombstones.

## Proposal
- Version the memory keyspace per context. `put` accepts `expectedVersion` (create-only with 0), and a conflict returns the current record.
- Delete writes a tombstone. `list` supports `sinceVersion` for sync.
- Add `vta/memory/query/0.1` with prefix and cursor pagination. This starts with a spec PR in `trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf`.
- Keep `0.1` behaviour for existing clients and gate the new semantics on `0.2`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A concurrent put with a stale `expectedVersion` returns a conflict carrying the winner.
- [ ] `list --since` returns changes and tombstones.
- [ ] `query` with prefix and cursor is implemented, with conformance tests.
