title: Signed, verifiable memory export/import bundle
body:
## Problem
Memory is portable across AI providers because it lives in the user's VTA, but it is not portable *out of* the VTA. There is no export format a user could take to another VTA, another agent framework, or an archive, and nothing a receiving system could verify.

## Proposal
- `vta-agent-memory export` writes a signed bundle of the context's memories, including provenance, status and lifecycle fields. It should be JSON with a detached signature by the user's DID, or a VP wrapping the records.
- `import` verifies the bundle and preserves the original authorship and timestamps instead of re-authoring as the importer.
- Optional `--filter` (type, basis, status) so a user can carry a subset, not the whole profile.
- Document the format so non-VTA consumers can read it.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Export, then import into a fresh context, preserves records and provenance.
- [ ] A tampered bundle is rejected on import.
- [ ] The format is documented in `docs/`.
author: stormer78

title: Memory quality evaluation harness (drift, staleness, contradiction, repairability, poisoning)
body:
## Problem
We have no way to measure whether memory makes agents better or worse over time. Persistent memory fails in ways one-shot tests don't catch: drift, accumulated contradictions, stale facts beating fresh ones, over-recall of irrelevant items, and how hard it is to repair after a bad write. Ranking is currently a hand-tuned token-containment weighting (name 4, description 2, body 1) with no benchmark behind it.

## Proposal
Add an evaluation harness (`tests/eval/` or a separate bin) that replays scripted multi-session scenarios against a real or simulated VTA and scores:
- recall precision/recall for a task
- staleness: superseded or expired facts must lose
- contradiction handling
- minimisation: irrelevant memories kept out of context
- repairability: time or steps to correct a wrong memory
- poisoning: an adversarial memory body must not change behaviour

Borrow the shape of LongMemEval where it applies. Run it in CI for ranking changes, and use it to justify the provenance and lifecycle work.

## Acceptance
- [ ] At least 10 scripted scenarios covering the dimensions above.
- [ ] One command produces a scored report; a CI job runs it on ranking changes.
author: stormer78

title: feat(vta/witness): vta/witness/request — the VTA runs a witnessed session for its principal's relationship
body:
A Verifiable Witness Credential is issued to the **participating party** of a `witness/session`: it opens the session under its relationship DID, presents its relationship credential bound to the challenge, and receives the VWC. A principal whose keys and credentials are held by a VTA cannot do that from a client holding neither. This adds the party side of witnessing to the VTA namespace.

## `vta/witness/request/0.1`

**Request** (client → its VTA):

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `witness` | the witness's public DID |
| `relationshipDid` / `counterpartyDid` | the session's `parties`; the VTA speaks and signs as `relationshipDid`, never as itself |
| `relationshipThreadId` | set as `parentThreadId` on every session document, which `witness/session` requires of a producer |
| `relationshipCredentialId` | vault handle of the VRC (issued by `relationshipDid`, subject `counterpartyDid`) |
| `membership` (optional) | `{ credentialId, memberDid? }` — a VMC by vault handle; `memberDid` present means the member link |
| `storeAs` (optional) | vault handle for the VWC |

**Response**: `{ credentialId, witness, vwcDigestMultibase, evidence: { session, outcome } }`. `session` is the `witness/session` document as sent; `outcome` is the `witness/session/submit#response` as received, which carries the VWC. Both are verbatim. No key, presentation or challenge is ever returned.

**What the VTA does, in order**: local checks first, so a request that cannot succeed discloses nothing: key custody for `relationshipDid` (and `memberDid`), credentials found and of the right shape, distinct DIDs, a transport both sides advertise. Then it opens the session, checks that the answer is the witness's own signed `#response`, builds the presentations itself, and submits. It verifies the VWC the way a verifier of the evidence would: the response signer is the witness, the VWC issuer is the session recipient, `taskContext` and the task digest are over the session document as sent, the subject and object digest match the presented VRC, and `vwcDigestMultibase` matches. It stores the VWC with both evidence documents, and only then answers.

**Errors**: `notFound`, `credentialMismatch`, `noMatchingProtocol`, `witnessUnreachable` (the only retryable one), `witnessRefused`, `challengeMismatch`, `presentationInvalid`, `vwcInvalid`. On the three that the witness answered, `details` carries the witness's own code and message. A caller without standing, or a key the VTA does not hold in the caller's contexts, gets the standard `permissionDenied`, as in `rooms/owner/register`.

**Capability**: a new `witnessRequest` (`witness-request` in `device/_shared/0.1`), added the way `pcsVetter`/`pcsApplicant` were in #756. It is not `sign` and is not satisfied by `sign`: the task signs only presentations the VTA builds over credentials it holds, bound to the witness's challenge, and it reads and writes the vault, which `sign` does not confer.

## Decisions worth a second look

1. **Name.** The slug is `vta/witness/request`, by analogy with `vta/pcs/tokens/request` and `vta/pcs/root-request`: the client asks for a witnessing. A single task needs no `_shared` conventions file. Those exist for families, and #756 needed one for twelve tasks.
2. **Shaped after `rooms/owner/register`, not the PCS engine.** The PCS engine never talks to the community, because the client carries its messages. Here the VTA makes the two round trips itself, as `rooms/owner/register` does with a host. The witness requires a transport-proven sender equal to the `issuer`, so a client relay would need the relationship key. That gives the same custody rule as `rooms/owner/register`: sign as the named DID with a key held in the caller's context, never as the VTA. One consequence: the VTA must be able to send and receive **as `relationshipDid`**, so `relationshipDid`'s DID document has to advertise a transport the witness speaks. `noMatchingProtocol` is computed over the witness's DID and `relationshipDid`, not the VTA's own DID.
3. **The member presentation's carriage is not specified here.** `witness/session/submit/0.1` has no member for a second presentation. SPEC §4.5.1 leaves an `ext` namespace's semantics to its controller, so this spec says a VTA carries it only in the carriage the named witness accepts. The OpenVTC `ext["org.openvtc.witness"].memberPresentation` is cited non-normatively. **The proper fix is an optional `memberPresentation` member on `witness/session/submit`.** That would be its own PR against that spec's owners, so it is not folded in here.
4. **`memberDid` is explicit**, even though the VTA could read it off the VMC. Naming it is the caller's deliberate choice to disclose the member DID to the witness.
5. **The response carries no top-level `vwc`.** The VWC sits once, inside `evidence.outcome`, verbatim under the witness's proof. A second copy could only disagree with it. The `vault/credentials/get` precedent says stored credentials are never re-serialised.
6. **Evidence retrieval later.** The VTA MUST store both evidence documents with the VWC. `vault/credentials/get/0.1` returns only `credential`, so after this response there is no task that reads the evidence back. A later `vault/credentials/get` version (or an evidence member) is the follow-up. Until then, this response is the client's copy.
7. **Retry class.** The task is not idempotent: a second execution is a second session and a second VWC. It needs duplicate protection (§7.2 item 11), and a cached answer can safely be replayed because it carries no secret. In VTI's `vta_sdk::retry_safety` terms that is `Keyed`, not `KeyedSecret`. Inside the exchange, a lost answer is retried by resending the **same** document. A VTA may bound its wait and answer `witnessUnreachable`. A VWC minted after that is inert and remains only as the witness's record.
8. **Consent is descriptive only.** §7.3 item 13 forbids a spec from requiring consent or step-up. The Authorization section says the act is consequential (it discloses credentials in full to a third party, and under the member link it links a pairwise DID to a member DID) and leaves any gate to VTA policy, worded as `vta/pcs/attest` words it.
9. **Classification.** `sideEffects: mutating`, `exposure: { discloses: metadata, ingests: metadata, actsAsSubject: true }`, `retention: durable`, proof REQUIRED on the request and RECOMMENDED on the response. `discloses` is `metadata` and not `secret` (which `witness/session/submit` declares): what goes back to the caller is the principal's own VWC and evidence, and the sensitive disclosure is the one made to the witness, which Security & Privacy covers.

## Not in this PR: the VTC's trusted-witness list

This should be **community configuration, not a new task family**. It is a list of witness DIDs that a VTC's criteria and personhood policy reference, of the same kind as `[oid4vp] x509_trust_anchors` or the registry configuration. It is read locally when a VWC is evaluated, and nothing crosses the wire. If it ever needs remote management, the existing VTC configuration surface carries it, not a dedicated `vtc/witnesses/*` family. Nothing in this registry blocks it.

## Privacy, as the spec states it

The witness sees the presented credentials **in full**. `vp` is opaque to `witness/session/submit`, and the witness must read all of it to verify it. Under the member link, the witness also learns the **member DID** beside the pairwise relationship DID: *which member*, not only *which community*. A member DID seen across several relationships links them all. The VTA presents nothing beyond what the request names, and never discloses a member DID its caller did not name.

## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate` / `npm run build`: 781 specs, no new warnings
- `npm run check-bindings`: Rust, TS, Go and Dart all agree; 1835 declared error codes match
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate`
- `tsc --noEmit` (trust-tasks-ts), `go build ./... && go vet` (trust-tasks-go), `dart analyze` on the regenerated libraries

## Consumer

verifiable-trust-infrastructure implements it in the VTA once this is released. That is phase P3 of the witness design (`docs/05-design-notes/witness-host-service.md` §3.5; the witness service itself is `vti-witness`).

A Verifiable Witness Credential is issued to the participating party of a
witness/session, who presents its relationship credential bound to the
session's challenge. A principal whose keys and credentials live in a VTA
cannot do that from a client that holds neither. This adds
vta/witness/request/0.1: the client names a witness, the relationship
(relationshipDid, counterpartyDid, the enclosing thread) and credentials by
vault handle; the VTA opens the session as the relationship DID, builds and
signs the presentation itself, submits, verifies the VWC as a verifier of
the evidence would (issuer = session recipient = response signer,
taskContext/taskDigest over the session document as sent, subject and
object digest, vwcDigestMultibase), and stores it in the credential vault
with its evidence — the session document as sent and the submit #response
as received. It answers with the vault handle, the digest and the two
evidence documents (which carry the VWC); never a key, a presentation or
the challenge.

Membership evidence is optional. A VMC naming the relationship DID rides
in the relationship presentation; one naming a member DID needs an
explicit memberDid, and the VTA builds a second presentation by that DID
bound to the same session. witness/session/submit/0.1 has no member for
it, so its carriage is the witness's own (SPEC 4.5.1 leaves an ext
namespace's semantics to its controller); the OpenVTC carriage is cited
non-normatively.

Authorization is standing over every context the task touches, expressed
as the new witnessRequest capability (witness-request in device/_shared
0.1), which is not sign and is not satisfied by sign. Errors: notFound,
credentialMismatch, noMatchingProtocol, witnessUnreachable (retryable),
witnessRefused, challengeMismatch, presentationInvalid (the witness's own
code and message in details), vwcInvalid.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: Sign memory records and verify authorship on recall
body:
## Problem
`MemoryRecord` (`src/record.rs`) has `v, name, type, description, body, links, updated_at`. Nothing in the record says who wrote it. Several DIDs can be granted the same context (multiple devices or agents), and the last write wins silently. Recall can't tell a memory the user dictated from one a different agent saved, or from one injected by a compromised writer.

Data Rooms already solve this for shared records: on sealed tiers each record body is signed by the writer's DID and bound to `(roomId, key, version)`, and `pnm rooms get` refuses a record whose signature doesn't hold (`docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md`, `SealedRecordBody` in `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json`). Personal memory should match.

## Proposal
- Add `author` (DID) and a detached signature over the canonical record (JCS) bound to `(contextId, key)`. Sign with the enrolled agent key at `memory_save`.
- Verify on `memory_recall` / `memory_get`. A record that fails verification is not returned as memory. Report it as a refused item instead, as rooms do.
- Show the author (human operator or which agent) in recall summaries so the model can weight memories.
- Treat legacy unsigned v1 records as `unattributed`, readable but marked.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Record schema v2 carries author plus signature; v1 still decodes.
- [ ] Tampered or relocated records are refused on recall, with a test.
- [ ] Recall output names the author kind (user / agent DID).

title: feat(witness): member link, so a pairwise party proves community membership (#1068)
body:
A party submits from its pairwise relationship DID (VTI-KEY-005), but a
community's membership credential names the member's own DID, so the P2
eligibility rule ("a VMC whose subject is the submitter") made ordinary
members unwitnessable.

The submit payload may now carry a member presentation in
`ext["org.openvtc.witness"].memberPresentation`: a VP by the member DID,
signed for authentication, bound to the same session's challenge and
domain, carrying a VMC from one of the identity's communities naming that
DID. The member DID may be neither the other party nor excluded. Failures
are presentationInvalid and leave the session open; any other member of
the namespace is malformedRequest. The member DID appears in no VWC,
record or log.

Design note §3.3a records the limitations (possession not personhood, so
a member can lend eligibility; the witness learns the member DID; a
vendor extension other witnesses ignore; no VMC revocation check; the VWC
does not record the evidence) and the options for later: standardise the
member upstream, a pairwise membership credential, a ZK membership proof
(e.g. PCS), a DID-linkage credential, eligibility in witnessContext, and
per-member rate limits.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Tests: `cargo nextest run -p vti-witness` (81 pass, incl. a linked success with the member DID absent from the VWC and the store, seven presentationInvalid cases, and the closed ext namespace), clippy `-D warnings`, fmt. Only `vti-witness` and docs change; nothing depends on the crate.

title: feat(vta): rooms/owner/group/renew renews a sealed room; pnm rooms renew refuses a sealed room (#2112)
body:
feat(vta): rooms/owner/group/renew renews a sealed room; pnm rooms renew refuses a sealed room (#2112)

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#773.

A sealed room's (`attributed` / `private`) epoch is its MLS group's epoch plus
one, so a bare `rooms/epoch/mint` moves the host and no member: every write is
then refused as sealed under a superseded epoch, and the owner's next
group/{add,remove} fails epochConflict. Until now a sealed room with a stable
membership had no correct way to renew, and one way to brick itself that
looked like a renewal.

The VTA now serves `rooms/owner/group/renew/0.1`, the third advance beside add
and remove, on the same remote-first machinery:

- Item 1: `noGroup` (an open room renews with rooms/epoch/mint), `noAuthority`
  before anything is settled or built.
- Items 2, 3, 7: `vti_rooms::sealed::SealedRoom::renew` builds a self-update
  commit (no proposal adding or removing anyone) and the epoch link on a copy;
  `room_groups::prepare_renew` retains it durably as the room's one pending
  advance, of the new kind `AdvanceKind::Renewal`, before anything is sent.
- Items 4, 5: `rooms/epoch/mint` (epoch, link, commit, the owner persona's
  `admin` presentation, reason), signed as the owner persona; applied on
  acceptance, discarded on refusal (`hostRefused`, or `epochConflict` with
  `details.hostEpoch` on `nonSequential`), kept on an unknown outcome
  (`hostUnreachable`).
- Item 6: any pending advance — admission, removal or renewal — is settled
  through `rooms/info` before another is built.

SDK: `TASK_ROOMS_OWNER_GROUP_RENEW_0_1`, `VtaClient::room_group_renew`
(generated types). Retry safety `Keyed`: a re-execution after a lost reply
would renew a second time. Outbound budget listed; vta-mcp classes it
`Sensitive`; conformance census entry.

CLI: `pnm rooms owner group-renew --room --host-did [--reason]`, inside
`VtaClient::idempotent`, telling the owner that remaining members catch up with
`pnm rooms keys commit --host`. `pnm rooms renew` now reads the tier
(`rooms/info`) first and refuses an `attributed` / `private` room, naming
`pnm rooms owner group-renew` (rooms/keys/act/0.1 producer item 4); open rooms
are unchanged.

Docs: data-rooms.md §10.1 (how each tier renews) and refusal rows;
data-rooms-quickstart.md; data-rooms-files.md P0 row.

title: fix(store): make VTA/VTC multi-step store writes atomic
body:
Follows #2104 and #2106. This moves the call sites an audit found onto the store's atomic operations (`take_raw`, `insert_if_absent`, `apply_batch` with preconditions). It is one commit per area.

## What each commit closes

| Area | Race or crash closed | Tests (M = mutation-checked: the old logic restored makes them fail) |
|---|---|---|
| **task-consent** | `consume_grant` was get-then-remove, so a grant could be **spent twice**. `add_approval` was unlocked, so a concurrent deny could be undone and the threshold still reached. Grant minting and pending retirement were separate writes, so a resent approval after a crash minted a second grant. New: `grant_from_pending` and `remove_pending_if_present`. A late deny now answers `noPending`. | `concurrent_consumes_spend_a_grant_exactly_once`, `concurrent_approvals_are_never_lost`, `an_approval_never_resurrects_a_denied_pending`, `a_pending_resolves_to_exactly_one_grant_or_one_denial` (M) |
| **auth** single-use takes | Pending consent, passkey enrolment, assertion and step-up state, and the VTC recognition/presentation challenges were get-then-remove, so each could be **redeemed twice** concurrently. They now use `take_raw`. | `concurrent_consumes_find_a_pending_exactly_once`, `concurrent_takes_consume_an_enrollment_exactly_once` (`--features passkey`), `concurrent_consumes_succeed_exactly_once` (M) |
| **session** | `touch_last_seen` and `resolve_did_session` wrote back a stale copy of the row. That **resurrected signed-out sessions** and **restored revoked elevation**. New `update_session_with` is a conditional read-modify-write that never creates a row. Step-up writers are moved onto it in the VTA and VTC. Session write, delete and expiry sweep are batches, so they are ordered against it. | `touch_never_resurrects_a_deleted_session`, `touch_never_restores_a_revoked_elevation`, `resolve_did_session_never_restores_a_revoked_elevation` (M) |
| **acl** | `update_acl_entry_versioned` was get/check/insert with no lock, so concurrent writers could both succeed. The VTC console-key `touch_last_used` could **reactivate a revoked delegation**. VTC ACL store and delete are now one batch each (entry, `git-holder:` index and departed record). | `concurrent_versioned_updates_admit_exactly_one_writer`, `a_last_used_stamp_never_reactivates_a_revoked_delegation`, `racing_deletes_keep_departed_grants_exactly_once`, `the_holder_index_tracks_the_entry_under_races` (M) |
| **vtc** | Personhood pseudonyms could be **bound to two members**, and multi-pseudonym claims were not all-or-nothing (new `claim_all`). A single-use invitation could **admit two redeemers**. VRC lifecycle events could be lost. | `racing_claims_bind_a_pseudonym_to_exactly_one_member`, `racing_multi_claims_are_all_or_nothing`, `racing_redeems_of_one_invitation_admit_exactly_one`, `racing_lifecycle_events_are_never_lost` (M) |
| **idempotency** | Reclaiming a stale claim had no single winner, so **an operation could run twice**. A completion could resurrect a released claim. | `racing_reclaims_of_a_stale_claim_have_one_winner`, `a_completion_never_resurrects_a_released_claim` (M) |
| **audit** | `cleanup_logs_before` deleted rows one at a time and wrote the watermark last. A crash left a chain gap that verification reads as tampering. Now 256-entry chunks, each one batch with its watermark. | `racing_sweeps_count_each_pruned_entry_once`, `a_sweep_commits_each_chunk_with_its_watermark` (M) |
| **app-state** | A record and its index changes could be split by a crash, so the change feed lost the record. Atomic `put_many` was a dry run followed by sequential writes. Both are now one batch. | journal-record tests (M) |
| **backup** | `abort` did a read-modify-write outside the chunk lock, so it could race `finalize`. | `racing_aborts_abort_a_bundle_exactly_once` (M) |

## Behaviour changes worth noting
- **Invitation redemption** now claims the invitation *before* admission and releases the claim if admission fails.
  - A storage error while claiming now refuses the admission. Before, it only logged and admitted anyway.
  - A crash between the claim and the admission leaves the invitation consumed with nobody admitted. That fails closed; the old order could let two people in.
- **A late `task-consent/decision` deny** after the pending has resolved answers `noPending`.

## Public API (additive)
- `task_consent::{grant_from_pending, remove_pending_if_present}`
- `session::update_session_with`
- `KeyspaceHandle::journal_seqno` (doc-hidden test hook)
- `record_lifecycle_event` and `supersede_prior_edges` keep their signatures. Their index argument is now unused.

## Known gap this PR works around
On the local store, plain `insert`/`remove` do **not** take the keyspace write lock; `apply_batch` does. So a `require_unchanged` precondition only excludes other batches, and a plain write can land between the check and the commit. Every race here is closed by also moving the writer on the other side onto a batch. These include `delete_session`, `store_session`/`update_session`, the session sweep, `revoke_delegation`, idempotency `release`, `delete_relationship`, pseudonym `release`, and VTC ACL store/delete. The general fix belongs in `vti-common`'s store and will follow separately.

## Not in this PR (needs cross-keyspace atomicity: the operation-journal phase)
- VTC `depart`
- `swap_key`'s cross-keyspace steps
- vti-rooms `put_record`
- vti-rooms blob `commit`
- VTC `delete_relationship` (primary row plus index)
- the cross-keyspace part of `delegation::repoint` (its review move is now one batch)

## Tests
Run on the branch before the final rebase onto `main` (which only picked up #2107; it merged cleanly):
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: OK.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. Re-run after the rebase: 0 findings.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5958 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`, run with `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`: 3124 passed, 12 failed. All 12 were admin-UI embedding tests, which need the UI built. Re-run with the UI built: the 80 tests matching `admin_ui::tests`, `member_portal` and `routing_modes` all pass.
- `cargo test -p vti-common --features vsock-store,encryption --lib store::`: 187 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-common --features passkey -E 'test(/passkey::store/)'`: 8 passed.
- Doc tests (both CI invocations): no failures.
- After the rebase: `cargo nextest run -p vti-common -p vti-rooms`: 867 passed.

title: fix(store): make VTA/VTC multi-step store writes atomic (#2109)
body:
fix(store): make VTA/VTC multi-step store writes atomic (#2109)

* test(store): expose the local journal sequence number to atomicity tests

KeyspaceHandle::journal_seqno (doc-hidden) returns the local database's
journal sequence number, or None on the vsock store. Whether a multi-key
write is one journal record (all or none after a crash) or several is
otherwise invisible until a crash lands between them; the call-site
fixes that follow assert it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(task-consent): make approvals, grants and the single-use consume atomic

consume_grant read the grant and then removed it, so re-submits racing
on one grant could each be handed it; it is now an atomic take_raw.

add_approval read the pending and wrote it back unconditionally, so
concurrent approvers overwrote each other's signatures, and an approval
racing a denial wrote the denied pending back - letting a later approval
reach the threshold of a refused request. It is now a conditional batch
(require_unchanged on the pending), retried on refusal.

Minting a grant was store_grant then delete_pending: a denial landing in
between was overridden, and two approvals crossing the threshold each
minted one. grant_from_pending writes the grant and retires the pending
and its wire index as one batch, only while the pending is still live and
carries every approval the grant names. The VTA's decision handler uses
it, and denies through remove_pending_if_present so a denial that arrives
after the grant was minted reports noPending instead of 'denied'.

store_pending / delete_pending and the expiry sweeps now write the
pending and its wire index as one batch, conditional where they act on a
row they read.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(auth): make single-use takes atomic (consent, passkey, VTC challenges)

consume_pending_consent, the passkey store's take/take_raw helpers (whose
docs claimed atomicity), and the VTC's recognise and presentation
challenge consumes all did get-then-remove: concurrent callers could each
observe the value and each be accepted. All now use
KeyspaceHandle::take_raw, under which exactly one caller sees it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(session): stop stale session write-backs resurrecting or re-elevating

touch_last_seen, resolve_did_session and the step-up / elevation-clearing
paths (VTC step_up_passkey + routes/auth passkey step-up, VTA
trust_tasks/step_up, VTA passkey_vms) read a session and wrote the copy
back. A sign-out landing in between was undone (the session came back),
and an elevation revoked in between was restored.

New update_session_with read-modify-writes the row as stored under a
require_unchanged batch, retrying on refusal, and never creates a missing
row; every one of those writers now goes through it. touch_last_seen
applies its stamp to the stored row once and skips if it lost the race
(best-effort). resolve_did_session creates with require_absent.

store_session, update_session and delete_session are now store batches
(row + index entries together) so they are ordered against the
conditional writes - a plain write could land between a batch's check and
its commit. The expiry sweep removes a session only while it is still the
expired row it read, so a session touched since the scan survives.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(acl): conditional ACL writes, console-key stamp and VTC entry batches

update_acl_entry_versioned claimed swap-style atomicity but was an
unlocked read/check/insert: writers that observed the same version could
all pass and the last silently discarded the others. The check and write
are now one batch (require_unchanged / require_absent). store_acl_entry
and delete_acl_entry are batches so they are ordered against it.

VTC console_key::touch_last_used wrote back a clone read outside
DELEGATION_LOCK, reactivating a console key revoked in between. It now
stamps the stored row only while unchanged and still active;
revoke_delegation is a conditional batch so the two are ordered.

VTC store_acl_entry / delete_acl_entry wrote the entry, the git-holder
index and the kept departed grants (VTI-ACL-037) separately: a crash
split them, and racing deletes appended an entry's grants more than once.
Each is now one batch; delete is conditional on the entry (and any kept
grants) as read. delegation::repoint moves a review to its subject's new
key in one batch.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc): atomic pseudonym claims, invitation redemption and VRC lifecycle

Personhood pseudonym claim / claim_for_statement checked then inserted,
unlocked, so two identities of one person racing could both be bound
(one membership per person defeated), and multiple presented pseudonyms
were claimed one by one, leaving a refused member holding the earlier
ones. claim_all binds every pseudonym in one batch with require_absent
(or require_unchanged on the member's own claim); releases are
conditional batches.

A single-use invitation was burned only after admission, so concurrent
redeems that both read it unconsumed were both admitted. The invitation
is now claimed (insert_if_absent) before execute::apply; the loser gets
Conflict and is not admitted, and a failed admission releases the claim
(release_consumed, conditional on our own record).

record_lifecycle_event and supersede_prior_edges read-modify-wrote the
relationship row unlocked, losing concurrent events (two terminal events
both reported recorded). They are now conditional batches with retry;
delete_relationship removes the row through a batch so it is ordered
against them.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(idempotency): one winner when reclaiming a stale or expired claim

claim's reclaim paths (expired record, stale in-flight record, row gone)
read the record and then inserted unconditionally, so every attempt that
read the same stale record reclaimed it and ran the operation. Reclaims
are now require_unchanged batches; a loser re-decides against what the
winner wrote. complete only overwrites the in-flight row it read (never
resurrecting a released claim or overwriting a recorded outcome), and
release is a batch so it is ordered against complete.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(audit): prune the log in chunks that carry their watermark

cleanup_logs_before deleted entries one by one and wrote the prune
watermark at the end, so a crash (or a concurrent sweep) left the oldest
survivor pointing at a removed entry the watermark did not account for -
indistinguishable from tampering - and concurrent sweeps double-counted
removals. Entries are now removed in chunks of 256, each one batch with
its deletions (require_present) and the watermark advanced past them
(require_unchanged on the previous watermark).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(app-state): commit a record and its index changes as one batch

put and delete removed the old index entry, inserted the new one and
wrote the record as three writes; a crash between them left an index
entry pointing at a record without its version. They are now one store
batch. put_many's atomic mode applied its writes one by one after the dry
run, so a crash part-way left some durable; it now stages every write
into one batch and commits it as one journal record. Tombstone reaping
removes the record and its index entry together.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(backup): take the chunk lock in abort and commit it as one batch

abort read the bundle record and wrote it back outside the chunk lock
every other bundle read-modify-write takes, so it could overwrite (or be
overwritten by) a chunk write or finalize, and concurrent aborts each
reported having aborted. It now holds the lock and writes the record and
the plan's removal as one batch.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.5
body:
### Specifications

- **external**: Credentials/issue 0.2 — batched presigned requests with signed length and checksum, multipart and head, for direct uploads ([#775](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/775))

rooms/blobs/upload/begin/0.2 lets a host answer with direct-to-storage
  targets whose PUT binds each part's exact length and SHA-256 (item 17),
  and commit/0.2 has the host verify the object at storage and complete a
  multipart upload before recording (item 3). A host that holds no storage
  credential asks its custodian for each request through
  external/credentials/issue on an s3-static-presign account, and 0.1 can
  express none of it: one GET/PUT/DELETE per issuance, no signed headers,
  no multipart operations, no HEAD.

  external/credentials/issue 0.2:
  - the payload takes either `scope` (session and token models, as 0.1)
    or `presign` (s3-static-presign only): one object, at most one
    multipart upload of it, up to 128 operations — put, get, head, delete,
    create-multipart, upload-part, list-parts, complete-multipart,
    abort-multipart;
  - the custodian signs Content-Length and x-amz-checksum-sha256 into put
    and upload-part, uploadId/partNumber into the query,
    x-amz-checksum-algorithm into create-multipart, x-amz-mp-object-size
    into complete-multipart, x-amz-checksum-mode into head, so storage is
    the enforcer;
  - every operation is presigned, none performed: issuance keeps needing
    no egress, and verifying the object stays the host's duty;
  - the binding ceiling is unchanged: each operation is authorized by
    put / get / delete (multipart writes by put, head by get, abort by
    delete), so no account record or other task changes shape;
  - a batch counts once against the binding's rate;
  - new errors requestShapeMismatch and invalidBatch; the sealed cleartext
    for presign is a PresignedRequestSet; the response's bundle is bounded
    at 256 KiB, maxDocumentBytes declared.

  external/_shared/0.1 gains PresignOperation and PresignedRequestSet
  (additive); CONVENTIONS §6 names the new cleartext. Bindings regenerated.
  rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,commit}/0.2 do not name
  external/credentials/issue, so they are unchanged.

title: fix(store): order plain writes against batches, read lock-free through snapshots
body:
Closes two gaps under the guarantee `apply_batch` (#2106) gives, on both the local store and the enclave's vsock store.

## 1. Plain writes could land inside a conditional batch
Plain `insert` / `insert_raw` / `remove` did not take the keyspace write lock (local store) or the key's lock (vsock store). Every multi-step operation did take it. So a plain write could slip between a batch's precondition check and its commit. For example, `require_unchanged(session)` passes, a sign-out removes the row, and the batch then writes the session back.

The fix:
- Plain writes now take the same lock as multi-step operations.
- On vsock, the fallbacks that already hold a key's lock use new unlocked helpers (`put_stored` / `delete_stored`), so nothing deadlocks.
- #2109 worked around this gap by moving each racing writer onto a batch. This makes the guarantee hold for every writer.

## 2. Lock-free reads could see half of a batch
fjall 3.1's plain reads (`Keyspace::get`, `prefix`, `range`) read at `SeqNo::MAX`. A `WriteBatch` is inserted into the memtables one item at a time, and its sequence number is published only after the last item (`batch/mod.rs`, `snapshot_tracker.publish`). A lock-free read could therefore see both rows of a move, or an index entry without its record.

The fix:
- Every lock-free read on `LocalKeyspaceHandle` now reads through `db.snapshot()`. That covers `get`, `get_raw`, `prefix_iter_raw`, `range_from_raw` and `prefix_keys`.
- A snapshot reads at the last published sequence number, so it sees each batch whole or not at all, and every write that has returned.
- Reads under the write lock are unchanged: no batch on the keyspace can be in flight while the lock is held.
- The same bug was found and fixed in did-hosting (affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#280).

## Tests
Each new test was mutation-checked: with the old code restored, it failed on 3 of 3 runs.

| Test | What the old code produced |
|---|---|
| `a_plain_remove_never_lands_inside_a_conditional_batch` | A removed row written back, at iterations 2–19 |
| `a_reader_never_sees_a_batch_half_applied` | Reads returning both rows, or neither |
| `plain_writes_wait_for_the_keyspace_write_lock` (local) | Plain writes ran while the lock was held |
| `plain_writes_wait_for_the_keys_lock` (vsock) | — (asserts the wait; not mutation-checked separately) |

Commands:
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5955 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3122 passed.
- `cargo test -p vti-common --features vsock-store,encryption --lib store::`: 189 passed.
- `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy`: `cargo test` 56 passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. Also clean on `-p vti-common --features vsock-store,encryption`.

## Cost
Plain writes to one keyspace now serialise on its lock. fjall already serialises journal writes across the whole database, so the extra contention is small. On vsock the lock is a striped per-key lock, so writes to unrelated keys don't wait on each other.

title: fix(store): order plain writes against batches, read lock-free through snapshots (#2113)
body:
fix(store): order plain writes against batches, read lock-free through snapshots (#2113)

Two gaps under `apply_batch`'s guarantee (#2106), on the local store and
the enclave's vsock store:

- Plain `insert` / `insert_raw` / `remove` did not take the keyspace
  write lock (local) or the key's lock (vsock), while every multi-step
  operation did. A plain write could therefore land between a batch's
  precondition check and its commit: a `require_unchanged` passes, a
  sign-out removes the row, and the batch writes it back. Plain writes now
  take the same lock; the vsock fallbacks that already hold a key's lock
  use unlocked `put_stored` / `delete_stored`.

- fjall 3.1's plain reads (`Keyspace::get`, `prefix`, `range`) read at
  `SeqNo::MAX`, and a batch is applied to the memtables item by item before
  its sequence number is published, so a lock-free read could see part of
  a batch: both rows of a move, an index entry without its record. Every
  lock-free read on `LocalKeyspaceHandle` (`get`, `get_raw`,
  `prefix_iter_raw`, `range_from_raw`, `prefix_keys`) now reads through
  `db.snapshot()`, which sees each batch whole or not at all and every
  write that has returned. Reads under the write lock are unchanged: no
  batch on the keyspace can be in flight while it is held.

Tests, each mutation-checked (3/3 runs fail with the old code):
- `a_plain_remove_never_lands_inside_a_conditional_batch`
- `a_reader_never_sees_a_batch_half_applied`
- `plain_writes_wait_for_the_keyspace_write_lock` (local) and
  `plain_writes_wait_for_the_keys_lock` (vsock).

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.5` → `0.8.6` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(rooms)!: rooms/blobs 0.2 — the single-use upload key, and reads straight from storage (trust-tasks-tf #771)
body:
Implements the host side of trust-tasks-tf #771 (`rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}/0.2`, `rooms/blobs/get/0.2`) beside 0.1, on vtc-service and room-host, through the shared `vti_rooms::blob_tasks` layer. Raises the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.31.4 (supersedes 0.31.3; blobs 0.2 unchanged).

## What it does
- **Upload key (begin/0.2 items 7, 8, 12, 14, 15).** A proxied 0.2 upload's chunk, commit and abort are accepted only from the `uploadKey` the begin named. The owner signing as itself gets `notFound`, and a 0.1 document never reaches a 0.2 upload (or the reverse). A key already bound to another open upload is refused with `uploadKeyInUse`. A resumed begin rebinds the upload to the new key; the old key is then refused and nothing is reserved a second time. The key is never recorded, charged or reported.
- **Admission (#2102).** A 0.2 chunk signed by the upload key is admitted at its declared size because an open upload names that key. It is charged to the **owner's** `room-transfer` budget in that room (`BlobHost::upload_owner_room`), so minting a fresh key per file does not buy a second budget. Begin and get are charged as presenter operations, and commit and abort to the owner's operation budget.
- **Direct reads (get/0.2 items 6–7).** When the reader sends `direct: true`, the host answers with a presigned GET for the one object (`BlobStore::read_target`; `PresignedBlobs` presigns a fresh GET through the community's VTA). The host checks the target is an HTTPS GET expiring within 5 minutes; otherwise it answers proxied. Usage is counted when the target is issued: one download, with the blob's full size as egress.
- **Policy.** New optional setting `[rooms.files] direct_transfer`: `"not_private"` (the default), `"all"` or `"off"`. Private rooms stay proxied unless it is set to `"all"`.
- **vtc-client.** New 0.2 begin/chunk/commit/abort/get helpers, plus `put_part` and `get_range` for direct targets. The storage client follows no redirects and never puts the URL in an error. get 0.2 is retried as a read.
- **s3-static-presign setup.** Now emits `bucket-cors.json` for browsers that read directly from the bucket.
- **Docs.** Updated `data-rooms.md` §8.2, `data-rooms-files.md` §5.2/§6.3 and the quickstart.

## What it does not do, and why: direct uploads
`begin/0.2` item 17 requires each part's URL to bind the part's exact length and SHA-256 as signed headers. Commit item 3 requires the host to verify the object at storage before recording it. `external/credentials/issue/0.1` cannot ask an `s3-static-presign` account for either: it offers `ProviderObjectAction` put/get/delete only, `presignedRequest.method` PUT/GET/DELETE only, and has no member for signed headers, multipart operations, or HEAD/GetObjectAttributes.

Storage like this "cannot issue the targets item 17 requires". So, as the spec says, a begin that offers only `directParts` is refused with `noTransferMode` naming `proxied`. Nothing diverges from either specification. Enabling direct uploads needs an external-accounts spec change first; see the PR comment below.

## CLI
`pnm rooms file put/get` stays on 0.1. It moves to 0.2 once `VtaClient::room_act` (feat/rooms-act-as-persona) merges.

## Checks run locally
fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `nextest -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (3121 passed), vtc doctests, the workspace nextest (all passed after fixing the secret-debug census), workspace doctests and `cargo deny` are all green.

title: spec(external): credentials/issue 0.2 — batched presigned requests with signed length and checksum, multipart and head, for direct uploads
body:
## Why

`rooms/blobs/upload/begin/0.2` (#771) lets a room host answer an upload with direct-to-storage targets — item 17 binds each part's exact length and SHA-256 into the PUT's signature — and `commit/0.2` item 3 has the host verify the object at storage and complete a multipart upload before recording. A VTC holds no storage credential: it asks the community's VTA for each request via `external/credentials/issue/0.1` on an `s3-static-presign` account, and 0.1 can express none of it (put/get/delete only, no signed headers, no multipart, no HEAD, one URL per issuance). Found implementing direct uploads in VTI (#2108), which today refuses them with `noTransferMode`.

## What — `external/credentials/issue` 0.2

- **Two request shapes**: `scope` (session/token models, as 0.1) **or** `presign` (`s3-static-presign` only; schema `oneOf`). A `presign` batch is one object (`prefix` + `objectKey`), at most one `uploadId`, and 1–128 operations: `put`, `get`, `head`, `delete`, `create-multipart`, `upload-part`, `list-parts`, `complete-multipart`, `abort-multipart`.
- **Bound into the signature** (Conformance item 10): `Content-Length` + `x-amz-checksum-sha256` for `put`/`upload-part` (both REQUIRED in the schema); `uploadId`/`partNumber` in the signed query; `x-amz-checksum-algorithm: SHA256` on create; `x-amz-mp-object-size` on complete; `x-amz-checksum-mode: ENABLED` on head. Nothing else may be signed.
- **Presign, never perform.** Create/complete/head are presigned for the consumer to call: issuance keeps needing no egress (conventions §3), the secret stays in the custodian either way, and verifying the object is the host's duty under commit/0.2.
- **Ceiling unchanged.** Each operation is authorized by one existing `ProviderObjectAction`: multipart writes and `list-parts` by `put`, `head` by `get`, `abort-multipart` by `delete` (it destroys stored bytes). No account record, binding or other `external/*` task changes shape.
- **Batching**: one issuance per batch, counted once against `ratePerMinute`; 128 matches begin/0.2's target cap. Response's sealed bundle bounded at 256 KiB (shared `SealedTransferBundle` is 64 KiB), `maxDocumentBytes` declared.
- **Checks in order** kept from 0.1 (binding first → `external-auth-use` → state → shape/batch → ceiling → TTL → rate), plus `requestShapeMismatch` and `invalidBatch`.
- **Security & Privacy**: what each presigned operation discloses/allows, bearer semantics, TTL ≤ binding cap (hosts ask ≤300 s for begin's 5-minute cap), storage as enforcer — and that a store ignoring a signed header is invisible to the custodian, so the consumer still verifies at storage.

`external/_shared/0.1` gains `PresignOperation` and `PresignedRequestSet` (additive; the sealed cleartext for `presign`). CONVENTIONS §6 names it. `rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,commit}/0.2` do not name `external/credentials/issue`, so they are unchanged.

## Local CI

`npm run build`, TS/Go/Dart bindings, `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, `npm run check-bindings`, `npm run check-dart-packages`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo deny --all-features check` — all green. Request/response examples and the sealed-cleartext example validate against the schemas; every invalid example is rejected.

title: feat(witness): witness sessions and VWC issuance (P2, #1068)
body:
Phase P2 of `docs/05-design-notes/witness-host-service.md` (#1068): an enabled `vti-witness` identity now witnesses. It serves `witness/session/0.1` and `witness/session/submit/0.1`, lists both in discovery, and issues Verifiable Witness Credentials.

## What was built

**Configuration** (`vti-witness/src/config.rs`). Every table uses `deny_unknown_fields`, and the whole configuration is validated at load. Every default is the restrictive one (R5.1).
- A service-wide `[independence] exclude`. Each `[[witness]]` table gains `communities` (VTC DIDs, or the explicit `["*"]`; empty, the default, witnesses nobody), an optional `allowed_parties`, `[witness.independence] exclude`, and `[witness.sessions]` with `ttl_secs` (default 600), `max_open` (default 1000) and `max_open_per_party` (default 4).
- These are refused at load: `"*"` mixed with DIDs, any entry that is not a DID, an empty `allowed_parties`, and caps or a TTL out of range. The service's own witness DIDs and `operator_vta_did` are always excluded. `run` warns about an enabled identity whose `communities` is empty.

**`witness/session/0.1`** (`vti-witness/src/witness.rs`), after the §7.2 pipeline. Checks, in order:
- `threadId` must equal `id` (party conformance item 1), otherwise `malformedRequest`.
- The opener must be one of `parties`, and the two parties must differ.
- Independence (§3.2).
- `communities` must not be empty, and `allowed_parties` must admit the opener.
- The caps: total sessions at this identity and sessions per opener. The count and the insert run under a per-identity mutex that guards only local store calls.

Every refusal is `witness/session:refused` with one fixed message, so a refusal cannot be used to probe which DIDs the operator excludes. The rule that refused is logged locally. On success the witness draws 32 bytes from the OS RNG (`getrandom`) as the challenge and uses its own DID as the `domain`. It stores the session, with the session document **byte for byte as received**, and answers with a signed `#response`.

**`witness/session/submit/0.1`**
- **Binding first.** The session must be live and unexpired on `threadId`, the submitter must be its opener, and the VP's `nonce` (or `challenge`) and `domain` must match the session's. Otherwise `challengeMismatch`, before the VP is examined.
- **Then the presentation** (`vti-witness/src/presentation.rs`). Otherwise `presentationInvalid`, and the session stays open. The checks:
  - the VP's `holder` is the submitter, and its proof set verifies for `authentication` under the submitter's key;
  - every embedded credential's issuer proof verifies for `assertionMethod` under a key of its own `issuer`, and the credential is within its validity window;
  - there is exactly one `RelationshipCredential` issued by the submitter, and its subject is the session's other party;
  - unless the identity is `["*"]`, there is a community-issued `MembershipCredential` from one of `communities` naming the submitter;
  - no credential is issued by an excluded DID (independence at submit).

  Proofs are checked with `vta_sdk::trust_task_proof::verify_proof_set`, the proof-set verifier the vault, the vetting client and the VTC share. Credentials are classified with `dtg_credentials::DTGCredential`.
- **Then the session is taken** with `take_raw`, an atomic get-and-delete, so exactly one of two racing submits mints. The take comes after verification, which may resolve DIDs over the network, so no lock is held across a network await (R1.3).
- **The VWC** is built with `DTGCredential::new_witnessed_vsc` from the verified VRC and the *stored* session document. That sets `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` through `with_task_citation`. It carries `issuerScope: public` and an `id`, and is signed `eddsa-jcs-2022` with the identity's `#key-0`, which is `assertionMethod` in `dtg-witness`.
- **`vwcDigestMultibase`** is RFC 8785 over the VWC **including its proof**, as a sha2-256 multihash in base58btc. `dtg-credentials` has no function for this, because all of its digests drop the top-level proof, so it is computed here.
- **Afterwards.** An attestation record (VWC id, digest, submitter, session id, identity, time) is written before the reply leaves. If minting fails, the session is restored. The VP is never stored or logged.

**Storage** (`vti-witness/src/store.rs`): `vti_common::store` under `<data_dir>/store`.
- Keyspaces: `witness_sessions` and `witness_accepted_ids` are ephemeral and never backed up; `witness_attestations` is kept.
- The service has no backup facility yet, so the kept/ephemeral partition is pinned by a local test rather than registered in a workspace census.
- A sweeper reaps expired sessions and replay records every 60 s.

**Replay and freshness** (`vti-witness/src/replay.rs`). §7.2 item 11 for both tasks: `trust_tasks_rs::ReplayGuard` over the store, keyed by identity and document `id`, compared on `trust_tasks_rs::document_digest`.
- A repeated document gets the first signed reply back, and nothing runs twice.
- A different document under a used `id` gets `idConflict`.
- A refusal releases the `id`.
- This follows the pattern of the VTC's `accepted_ids`, which lives in `vtc-service` and cannot be reused from here.

## Spec conformance mapping

| Requirement | Where |
|---|---|
| session witness item 1 / submit witness item 1 (§7.2 pipeline) | `dispatch::evaluate` |
| session witness item 2 (issuer ∈ `parties`, else `refused`) | `witness::open_session` |
| session witness items 3–4 (fresh challenge + domain, signed response / `refused`) | `witness::open_session`, `dispatch::sign` |
| session Security: a challenge is never reused | 32 OS-random bytes per session; tested |
| submit witness item 2 (binding before any other check, `challengeMismatch`) | `witness::submit` → `bound_to`; `binding_comes_first_…` test |
| submit witness item 3 (non-opener → `challengeMismatch`) | `witness::submit`; tested |
| submit witness item 4 (`{vwc, vwcDigestMultibase}`, signed, `taskContext` rule) | `witness::mint`; end-to-end test |
| submit Retention (discard the VP; keep what revocation needs) | `AttestationRecord`; the end-to-end test asserts the VP's proof appears nowhere in the store |
| §7.2 item 11 | `replay.rs`, `dispatch::consequential` |
| §4.9.2 `parentThreadId` carried on replies | `respond_with`; tested |

## Tests

- `vti-witness/tests/witnessing.rs` (20 tests, all `did:key`, no network) covers:
  - every refusal path and the single refusal message;
  - binding first (wrong challenge plus a broken VP gives `challengeMismatch`), wrong domain, non-opener, expired and unknown sessions;
  - concurrent double submit (exactly one VWC, one attestation);
  - replayed session and submit, and `idConflict`;
  - independence at session open and at submit;
  - no VMC, a VMC from another community, a VMC naming another subject, an expired VMC;
  - `["*"]` against empty;
  - both caps, and expired sessions not counting and being swept;
  - nine `presentationInvalid` cases, each asserting the session survives.
- **End to end:** build a VRC and a VMC with `dtg-credentials`, open a session, submit, and receive the VWC. Then apply the VTC's checks: the VWC proof by the witness, `vwcDigestMultibase` recomputed (and different from the proofless digest), `witnesses_issuance_of(vrc)` (digest binding plus subject–object; the reverse edge is refused), `cites_task(session)` (a counterfeit document under the same id is refused), issuer equals witness DID equals the session's `recipient`, `issuerScope: public`, and the predicate.
- Unit tests for the config validation, the policy resolution (own DIDs and the operator are excluded, and exclusion beats a listed community), the digest covering the proof, challenge freshness, the store partition, and the redacted `Debug`.

Run locally (macOS):
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5981 of 5983 passed (after rebasing on origin/main). Two timed out under heavy load (load average about 25): `vta-backup restore_tests::every_backed_up_keyspace_survives_a_round_trip` passes alone in 147 s, and `vta-service trust_tasks::audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry` also times out when run alone. Neither crate depends on `vti-witness`, and this PR changes neither crate nor any of its dependencies
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`: passed
- `vtc-service` and `vtc-client` were not touched, so their job was not run.

## Deviations and decisions to review

- **The end-to-end test replicates the VTC verifier's checks with `dtg-credentials` rather than calling them.** `vtc-service/src/credentials/witness.rs` lives in `vtc-service`, and its `resolve_binding` is tied to the VTC's relationship keyspace. Its core checks are `dtg_credentials` calls (`witnesses_issuance_of`, `cites_task`, `digests_match`), and the test uses exactly those. Design note §4 P2 says "against the VTC's existing VWC verifier"; the note is unchanged.
- **The VP binding is read from the VP's top-level `nonce`/`domain`** (with `challenge` accepted as an alias). That is the shape `vta_sdk::vp` builds and `vtc-service`'s `verify_di_vp` reads. `affinidi-data-integrity`'s `DataIntegrityProof` has no `challenge`/`domain` members, so proof-level binding cannot be verified today.
- **`domain` is the witness identity's DID.**
- **The membership check requires the VMC's subject to be the submitter**, which is a pairwise relationship DID, per design §3.3. In practice a member's VMC names its member DID, not a per-relationship DID. Unless the relationship DID is the member DID, this needs a holder-binding link (or a different policy) in P3.
- **`allowed_parties` applies to the opener**, the party being witnessed, not to both parties.
- **Every credential in the VP must verify.** Non-DTG credentials are verified and otherwise ignored. VMC revocation (`credentialStatus`) is **not** checked in P2.
- **Caps are per identity**, not service-wide.
- **The store is not encrypted at rest.**
- **Setup writes identities with the restrictive defaults** (witnessing nobody); the operator sets `communities` in `config.toml`. The setup file does not take the policy keys.

## Remaining for P3

The VTA Trust Task that runs a witnessed session for its principal and stores the VWC with its evidence (spec first, in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf), and the VTC's list of trusted witness DIDs. Later: VWC revocation through a status list, built on the attestation records.

title: spec(external): credentials/issue 0.2 — batched presigned requests with signed length and checksum, multipart and head, for direct uploads (#775)
body:
spec(external): credentials/issue 0.2 — batched presigned requests with signed length and checksum, multipart and head, for direct uploads (#775)

rooms/blobs/upload/begin/0.2 lets a host answer with direct-to-storage
targets whose PUT binds each part's exact length and SHA-256 (item 17),
and commit/0.2 has the host verify the object at storage and complete a
multipart upload before recording (item 3). A host that holds no storage
credential asks its custodian for each request through
external/credentials/issue on an s3-static-presign account, and 0.1 can
express none of it: one GET/PUT/DELETE per issuance, no signed headers,
no multipart operations, no HEAD.

external/credentials/issue 0.2:
- the payload takes either `scope` (session and token models, as 0.1)
  or `presign` (s3-static-presign only): one object, at most one
  multipart upload of it, up to 128 operations — put, get, head, delete,
  create-multipart, upload-part, list-parts, complete-multipart,
  abort-multipart;
- the custodian signs Content-Length and x-amz-checksum-sha256 into put
  and upload-part, uploadId/partNumber into the query,
  x-amz-checksum-algorithm into create-multipart, x-amz-mp-object-size
  into complete-multipart, x-amz-checksum-mode into head, so storage is
  the enforcer;
- every operation is presigned, none performed: issuance keeps needing
  no egress, and verifying the object stays the host's duty;
- the binding ceiling is unchanged: each operation is authorized by
  put / get / delete (multipart writes by put, head by get, abort by
  delete), so no account record or other task changes shape;
- a batch counts once against the binding's rate;
- new errors requestShapeMismatch and invalidBatch; the sealed cleartext
  for presign is a PresignedRequestSet; the response's bundle is bounded
  at 256 KiB, maxDocumentBytes declared.

external/_shared/0.1 gains PresignOperation and PresignedRequestSet
(additive); CONVENTIONS §6 names the new cleartext. Bindings regenerated.
rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,commit}/0.2 do not name
external/credentials/issue, so they are unchanged.

title: feat(rooms)!: act as the member's persona — rooms/keys/act, seal 0.2, and read/browse/backfill as the principal
body:
Implements the host side of trust-tasks-tf #771 (`rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}/0.2`, `rooms/blobs/get/0.2`) beside 0.1, on vtc-service and room-host, through the shared `vti_rooms::blob_tasks` layer. Raises the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.31.4 (supersedes 0.31.3; blobs 0.2 unchanged).

## What it does
- **Upload key (begin/0.2 items 7, 8, 12, 14, 15).** A proxied 0.2 upload's chunk, commit and abort are accepted only from the `uploadKey` the begin named. The owner signing as itself gets `notFound`, and a 0.1 document never reaches a 0.2 upload (or the reverse). A key already bound to another open upload is refused with `uploadKeyInUse`. A resumed begin rebinds the upload to the new key; the old key is then refused and nothing is reserved a second time. The key is never recorded, charged or reported.
- **Admission (#2102).** A 0.2 chunk signed by the upload key is admitted at its declared size because an open upload names that key. It is charged to the **owner's** `room-transfer` budget in that room (`BlobHost::upload_owner_room`), so minting a fresh key per file does not buy a second budget. Begin and get are charged as presenter operations, and commit and abort to the owner's operation budget.
- **Direct reads (get/0.2 items 6–7).** When the reader sends `direct: true`, the host answers with a presigned GET for the one object (`BlobStore::read_target`; `PresignedBlobs` presigns a fresh GET through the community's VTA). The host checks the target is an HTTPS GET expiring within 5 minutes; otherwise it answers proxied. Usage is counted when the target is issued: one download, with the blob's full size as egress.
- **Policy.** New optional setting `[rooms.files] direct_transfer`: `"not_private"` (the default), `"all"` or `"off"`. Private rooms stay proxied unless it is set to `"all"`.
- **vtc-client.** New 0.2 begin/chunk/commit/abort/get helpers, plus `put_part` and `get_range` for direct targets. The storage client follows no redirects and never puts the URL in an error. get 0.2 is retried as a read.
- **s3-static-presign setup.** Now emits `bucket-cors.json` for browsers that read directly from the bucket.
- **Docs.** Updated `data-rooms.md` §8.2, `data-rooms-files.md` §5.2/§6.3 and the quickstart.

## What it does not do, and why: direct uploads
`begin/0.2` item 17 requires each part's URL to bind the part's exact length and SHA-256 as signed headers. Commit item 3 requires the host to verify the object at storage before recording it. `external/credentials/issue/0.1` cannot ask an `s3-static-presign` account for either: it offers `ProviderObjectAction` put/get/delete only, `presignedRequest.method` PUT/GET/DELETE only, and has no member for signed headers, multipart operations, or HEAD/GetObjectAttributes.

Storage like this "cannot issue the targets item 17 requires". So, as the spec says, a begin that offers only `directParts` is refused with `noTransferMode` naming `proxied`. Nothing diverges from either specification. Enabling direct uploads needs an external-accounts spec change first; see the PR comment below.

## CLI
`pnm rooms file put/get` stays on 0.1. It moves to 0.2 once `VtaClient::room_act` (feat/rooms-act-as-persona) merges.

## Checks run locally
fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `nextest -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (3121 passed), vtc doctests, the workspace nextest (all passed after fixing the secret-debug census), workspace doctests and `cargo deny` are all green.

title: feat(rooms)!: act as the member's persona — rooms/keys/act, seal 0.2, and read/browse/backfill as the principal (#2107)
body:
feat(rooms)!: act as the member's persona — rooms/keys/act, seal 0.2, and read/browse/backfill as the principal (#2107)

Implements the member-acts-as-persona half of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#771
(trust-tasks-rs 0.31.3, now the workspace floor).

VTA:
- rooms/keys/act/0.1: the member's own client sends an unsigned host-bound room
  request; the VTA resolves the member (issuer names it when several), checks the
  spec's closed table, inserts the member's own authority narrowed to exactly the
  table's action and granted to the member plus the membership credential,
  validates the payload against its type's schema, sets issuer = member and signs
  for `authentication` through the gated key oracle. Every declared code
  (typeNotActable, notAMember, principalAmbiguous, issuerNotPrincipal,
  actionNotHeld) plus permissionDenied for a delegate (an ACL entry whose
  consumer kind is an AI agent or mediator) and malformedRequest for a stale,
  expired or pre-presented document. Classified RetrySafe.
- rooms/keys/seal/0.2: `signAsPrincipal` signs the SealedRecordBody as its author
  (a persona the caller acts as, with group state in the room) for
  `assertionMethod` before sealing; bodyInvalid / authorNotPrincipal /
  locationMismatch / notAMember. 0.1 stays served.
- rooms/keys/{read,browse,backfill} and rooms/owner/anchor present the
  principal's own grant narrowed to `read` and sign as the principal. The VTA's
  own DID no longer reaches the host, and a context-scoped caller no longer
  fails with "key `…#key-0` is not within the caller's scope".
- persona keys can be looked up per verification relationship.

SDK/CLI:
- VtaClient::room_act + vta_sdk::client::unsigned_room_request (generated
  types), VtaClient::room_seal_as_principal (seal 0.2).
- VtcClient::send_signed_room_document sends a completed document unchanged.
- pnm rooms list/get/put/curate, the rooms/info lookup and `rooms keys commit
  --host` build the request unsigned, have the VTA complete it with act and send
  it unchanged; sealed writes use seal 0.2 with signAsPrincipal. The CLI session
  key no longer reaches the host on these verbs. `renew` and the file transfer
  are unchanged.

Tests: an end-to-end write through an in-process room-host (host-recorded
author and body signer are the persona; neither the client's nor the VTA's DID
appears in what the host received or stored), every act refusal, seal 0.2
author checks, and read/browse/backfill by a context-scoped caller.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.4
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Rooms/owner/group/renew renews a sealed room; rooms/keys/act refuses a sealed room's mint ([#773](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/773))

A sealed room (`attributed` / `private`) had no correct way to renew, and
  one way to brick itself that looked like a renewal.

  - rooms/epoch/mint advances a host without a commit (a host MUST), and on a
    sealed room the room epoch is the MLS group epoch + 1. rooms/keys/act/0.1
    completes a mint for a member's client, which holds no group key and so
    sends no commit: the host moves to N+1, every member's key holder stays at
    N, every write is refused as sealed under a superseded epoch, and the
    owner's next rooms/owner/group/{add,remove} fails epochConflict.
  - Only membership changes advanced a sealed room's epoch, so a room whose
    membership was stable lapsed after its epoch lifetime with no remedy.

  rooms/owner/group/renew/0.1 (new, Owner -> KeyHolder): the sibling of
  group/{create,add,remove}. The key holder advances the group with a commit
  that changes no membership (self-update or empty commit), builds the epoch
  link, retains the pending advance durably before sending (at most one per
  room, shared with add/remove), mints at the host with the commit, the link
  and the owner's admin presentation, applies only on acceptance, discards on
  refusal, keeps on an unknown outcome and settles via rooms/info. Errors:
  noGroup, noAuthority, epochConflict (details.hostEpoch), hostUnreachable,
  hostRefused.

  rooms/keys/act/0.1 (draft, edited in place): recipient item 9 refuses a
  rooms/epoch/mint for a room it holds group state for, for any member it
  serves, with the new rooms/keys/act:sealedRoomMint naming
  rooms/owner/group/renew; producer item 4 says not to ask. Open rooms keep
  renewing through act. The wire shape is unchanged; a draft MAY change
  without a version bump (SPEC §5.2/§5.3), and a 0.2 would leave 0.1
  permitting the defect it exists to close.

title: feat(rooms): files in data rooms, and VTC room storage administration
body:
Adds Trust Tasks for files in data rooms, and for the hosting community's administration of room storage. Design: [`data-rooms-files.md`](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/blob/main/docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md) in verifiable-trust-infrastructure.

## Room tasks (authorized by the room's own chain, never host ACLs)
- `rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}/0.1`: chunked, resumable upload of a file's ciphertext. The manifest is committed before any byte moves, and every limit is checked and reserved at `begin`.
- `rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}/0.1`: download of a file's ciphertext.
- `rooms/records/put/0.2`: a record can name a committed blob (`blobs`). This is a new version rather than an edit, because a 0.1 host would accept a record pointing at a blob it never checked.
- `rooms/info/0.1`: the room's limits and usage, plus the caller's own.
- `rooms/usage/0.1`: per-member usage, for the room's owner. Not offered on `private` rooms.
- `rooms/keys/file-key/0.1`: the member's VTA releases the key for one file. The spec explains why this releases a key when `rooms/keys/open` deliberately does not.

## VTC-only tasks, under a new `vtc.rooms.admin` capability
- `vtc/rooms/{get,limits/set,usage}/0.1`
- `vtc/rooms/storage/{assign,migrate}/0.1`
- `vtc/storage/configs/{list,get,create,update,retire,probe}/0.1`
- `vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.1`: the discouraged fallback for a sealed credential. It is write-only; only a fingerprint comes back.

Storage changes park in the administrator action list.

## Shared types
- `rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json`:
  - `BlobRef`, `BlobManifest`, `TransferId`;
  - the limits and usage types: `ScopeLimits`, `RoomLimits`, `Usage`, `LimitExceeded`;
  - `FileManifest`, the sealed body's `file` member, which carries the KDF and STREAM construction.
- `vtc/_shared/0.1/room-storage.schema.json`

Bindings for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart are regenerated. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass, and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` passes.

title: feat(auth/oob): add the auth/oob out-of-band sign-in Trust Task family
body:
## What it adds

The `auth/oob/*` family: out-of-band sign-in, where a starter (the browser) asks a service to open a request and an approver (the wallet) decides it on another device. There are eight Trust Tasks, each at `https://trusttasks.org/spec/auth/oob/<task>/0.1`:

`request`, `claim`, `prove`, `identify`, `respond`, `grant`, `redeem`, `cancel`

- **Shared schema** `specs/auth/oob/_shared/0.1/oob.schema.json`. It defines `RequestId`, `OobKey`, `MatchNumber`, `Mode`, `Purpose`, `Origin`, `Service`, `Requester` and `SameNetwork` once for the whole family. Beside it:
  - `CONVENTIONS.md` holds the family rules: purposes, disclosure at each step, windows and errors.
  - `TRIGGER-LINK.md` describes the QR code / trigger link the starter shows.
- **Wire details** follow the cross-repo sign-in contract (C9):
  - `claimDeadline`, `decisionDeadline` and `notAfter` are integer epoch seconds.
  - `contextDigest` is a `DigestMultibase`.
  - `decision` is `approve` or `decline`.
  - `sameNetwork` is `true`, `false` or `"unknown"`.
  - `matchNumber` and `enteredNumber` match `^[0-9]{2}$`.
  - The claim's `parentThreadId` must equal `payload.requestId`.
  - `cancel` returns `{status: "cancelled"}`, and `respond` returns `{status: "approved" | "declined"}`.
  - `redeem` returns `{subject, displayName, notAfter, amr}`, never tokens.
- **Endpoint discovery:** `TRIGGER-LINK.md` and `auth/oob/claim` say the `TrustTaskHTTPS` `serviceEndpoint` is the Trust-Task base, and they point to HTTPS binding 0.2 §6 for how to build the request URL (`<base>/trust-tasks`).
- **Generated bindings:**
  - Rust: `trust_tasks_rs::specs::auth::oob::<task>::v0_1`, under the existing `auth` feature. Includes conformance tests.
  - TypeScript: `AuthOob<Task>_v0_1` and `OobShared_v0_1`.
  - Go and Dart: packages and libraries under `specs/auth/oob/...`.

## Backwards compatibility

Everything in this PR is additive. What I checked:

- **Diff against `main`:** every file is new except five generated index files. Those five only gain lines; no line is removed.
  - `trust-tasks-rs/src/schema_index.rs`: new match arms.
  - `trust-tasks-rs/src/specs/auth/mod.rs`: `pub mod oob;`.
  - `trust-tasks-rs/tests/conformance/main.rs`: new test modules.
  - `trust-tasks-ts/src/index.ts`: new namespace exports.
  - `trust-tasks-ts/src/_shared/components.ts`: new hoisted types.
- **Existing specs:** no existing spec, schema, `$id`, Type URI or generated binding changes in content, name or path.
- **Tooling:** no generator or tooling changes. The diff does not touch `scripts/`, `trust-tasks-codegen`, any `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pubspec.yaml` or `go.mod`. I re-ran all four generators (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen` with `cargo fmt`, and `build-ts-bindings`, `build-go-bindings`, `build-dart-bindings`) and there was no drift.
- **Rust features:** default features are unchanged (`default = ["all-specs"]`). The new modules sit behind the existing `auth` feature, so no new feature is introduced.
- **Packages:** the npm, Go and Dart package exports only gain entries. The new TS shared type names do not collide with existing exports, and `tsc` passes.
- **Registries:** the registry and indexes only gain entries.
- **Versions:** no version is bumped, as RELEASING.md asks. The Release PR sizes the bump from the conventional commits (`feat` gives a minor bump).

## Testing

I ran the same steps the CI workflows run:

- **Registry:** `TT_STRICT_SECURITY_PRIVACY=1 npm run build` passes: 698 specs validated and 1343 examples checked against the envelope schema. `npm run test:infra`, `npm run test-ceremonies` and `npm run check-dart-packages` pass.
- **Bindings conformance:** `npm run check-bindings` reports that all 698 specs agree across TS, Rust, Go and Dart, and that the 1549 declared error codes match Rust `ERROR_CODES`.
- **Generation drift:** Rust codegen with fmt, and the TS, Go and Dart generators, leave the tree clean.
- **Rust:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes.
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` passes with default features and with `--all-features`.
  - `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets` pass, with 0 failures.
  - `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features` passes.
- **TypeScript:**
  - `trust-tasks-ts`: `tsc --noEmit` passes, `npm test` passes 79/79, and `npm run smoke` passes.
  - `trust-tasks-ts-proof`, `-tsp` and `-capability-client`: build, test typecheck and tests all pass.
- **Go:** `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test -race ./...` pass for the core module, `tsp` and `proof`.
- **Dart:**
  - `trust-tasks-dart`: `dart analyze --fatal-infos` is clean, `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` at the pubspec floor is clean, and `dart test` passes 74/74.
  - The proof, https, didcomm, capability-client and tsp packages: analyze is clean and the tests pass.

## Related

- VTI spec: https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec/pull/58
- Implementations in other repos will link back to this PR.

  completes a mint for a member's client, which holds no group key and so
  sends no commit: the host moves to N+1, every member's key holder stays at
  N, every write is refused as sealed under a superseded epoch, and the
  owner's next rooms/owner/group/{add,remove} fails epochConflict.
- Only membership changes advanced a sealed room's epoch, so a room whose
  membership was stable lapsed after its epoch lifetime with no remedy.

rooms/owner/group/renew/0.1 (new, Owner -> KeyHolder): the sibling of
group/{create,add,remove}. The key holder advances the group with a commit
that changes no membership (self-update or empty commit), builds the epoch
link, retains the pending advance durably before sending (at most one per
room, shared with add/remove), mints at the host with the commit, the link
and the owner's admin presentation, applies only on acceptance, discards on
refusal, keeps on an unknown outcome and settles via rooms/info. Errors:
noGroup, noAuthority, epochConflict (details.hostEpoch), hostUnreachable,
hostRefused.

rooms/keys/act/0.1 (draft, edited in place): recipient item 9 refuses a
rooms/epoch/mint for a room it holds group state for, for any member it
serves, with the new rooms/keys/act:sealedRoomMint naming
rooms/owner/group/renew; producer item 4 says not to ask. Open rooms keep
renewing through act. The wire shape is unchanged; a draft MAY change
without a version bump (SPEC §5.2/§5.3), and a 0.2 would leave 0.1
permitting the defect it exists to close.

rooms/epoch/mint/0.1: a non-normative note that on a sealed room the
producer is the owner's key holder via rooms/owner/group/{add,remove,renew}.

rooms/owner/group/{add,remove}/0.1 item 4: the presentation was described
as "bound to `host`", which rooms/keys/present/0.2 cannot do — a
presentation is bound to the room; the advance is bound to the host by the
mint document's `recipient`, covered by its proof (SPEC §4.8.2). Reworded to
say so. add item 3 now states the one-pending-advance rule remove already
stated, and both name renewal.

Related entries added both ways (owner group tasks, act, epoch/mint,
keys/commit).

Additive for trust-tasks-rs: a new rooms::owner::group::renew::v0_1 module
and error_codes::SEALED_ROOM_MINT on rooms::keys::act::v0_1.
