title: spec(vtc)!: a vta-account storage config names the account's context as well as its identifier
body:
`StorageAuth`'s `vta-account` variant named only `account`, but a VTA names an
external account by the context that owns it and its identifier there: the
`external/credentials/issue` task the community sends requires both. A
community could only fill the gap from something outside the config, which
makes a config mean something only on the host that stored it, confines every
account a community uses to one context, and leaves each implementation to
fill the gap its own way.

`vta-account` now requires `context` (`ExternalAccountContextId`, the issue
task's `AccountContextId` form), and `CredentialState` carries it beside
`account`. Naming a context grants nothing: the VTA issues only to a consumer
bound to the account and holding `external-auth-use` in that context.
`vtc/storage/configs/create` item 5 addresses the account by that pair and
never by an identifier resolved against a context of the community's own
choosing; `unknownAccount` on create and update says so. A new invalid
example covers a missing context.

Breaking for the generated types: a new required member. No community could
create a `vta-account` config before this (the one implementation refused
every kind but `local`), so no stored config lacks it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Checked locally: `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings` (Rust, TS, Go and Dart regenerated and in agreement), and the `vtc::storage` conformance tests, including the new invalid example.

title: spec(rooms)!: rooms/info and rooms/usage require a proof, like every other rooms/* task
body:
`rooms/info/0.1` and `rooms/usage/0.1` declared `proofRequirement: RECOMMENDED`. Every other `rooms/*` task declares REQUIRED.

**Why RECOMMENDED doesn't work.** Both rationales say the room-issued chain is "bound to whoever the host authenticated". A room operation deliberately carries no session or token: authority is the room's credentials, never the host's. So the only party a host can authenticate is the request proof's signer, and the chain's leaf must be that party. Without a proof there is nobody to bind the chain to, and the presentation is a bearer token for anyone who sees it. A host that implements the chain rule refuses an unsigned `info`/`usage` anyway.

Found implementing `rooms/info` on the VTC (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure): its spine-proof census asks every served `rooms/*` task's spec to agree with the arm, which refuses unsigned requests.

**Change:** both now say REQUIRED, with a rationale matching the family's. This is breaking for a producer that sent them unsigned; both specs are drafts. Regenerated the bindings, which carry the spec policy. `npm run validate`, `check-bindings` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` (2035 tests) pass.

title: spec(rooms): define the sealed record body, signed by its author and bound to its location
body:
`rooms/records/put` 0.2 relies on "the sealed body the author signed" to detect a substituted blob, and `blobs.schema.json` defines the body's `file` member (`FileManifest`), but the body itself was never defined. So two clients couldn't read each other's records, and no reader could check the signature. I hit this implementing `pnm rooms file put/get` in VTI: the CLI would have had to invent a format the portal and extension then copy.

### What this adds
`SealedRecordBody` in `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json`, the JSON inside `SealedRecord.ciphertext` on `attributed` and `private` rooms:

| member | |
|---|---|
| `roomId`, `key`, `version` | required: the record's location, signed |
| `author` | required: the writing member or agent |
| `title`, `description`, `body`, `tags` | same constraints as the open tier's `cleartext` |
| `file` | `FileManifest`, when the record carries a file |
| `proof` | required: Data Integrity proof by `author`, `assertionMethod`; writers MUST support `eddsa-jcs-2022`, MAY use `ecdsa-jcs-2019` |

**Readers MUST**, before showing anything or trusting `file`:
1. refuse unknown members;
2. verify the proof against `author`;
3. check the signed location matches where the record was read;
4. on `attributed`, check `author` equals the host-recorded author.

A failing record is refused, not shown with a warning.

### Why the location is signed as well as sealed
The AEAD binds `roomId`/`key`/`version`/epoch against the **host**. But every member can open and re-seal a record. Without the location under the author's signature, a member could copy another member's signed body to a new key or a later version. On a `private` room, where the host records no author, readers would attribute it to the original author.

### Also
- `records/put` 0.2 producer rules 3 and 6 point at the definition.
- `keys/seal` 0.1: the plaintext is a signed `SealedRecordBody`. A key holder seals what it's given and never signs for the writer.

No payload or response schema changes, so no version moves. The definition isn't referenced by any task schema, so codegen output is unchanged (as with `FileManifest`, clients implement it). `npm run validate` passes.

title: feat(rs): declared error codes carry their detailsSchema, and a titled variant no longer generates doctests
body:
This PR fixes two `trust-tasks-codegen` defects that turned up while implementing `rooms/keys/file-key` (#739) and `external/*` (#740) in verifiable-trust-infrastructure.

### 1. Declared error codes carry their `detailsSchema`
- **New field:** `DeclaredErrorCode` gains `details_schema: Option<&'static str>`, the JSON Schema a spec declares for an error's `details` (SPEC §7.3 item 9).
- **Self-contained:** a `$ref` into a shared schema file is resolved and carried inline, by the same resolver `PAYLOAD_SCHEMA` uses. The 7 schemas written as refs include the `vault/*` step-up challenge.
- **New method:** with the `validate` feature, `DeclaredErrorCode::check_details(&Value)` checks a `details` value against the declared schema.
- **Why:** an implementation previously had to hand-copy the schema to test what it emits, and the copy drifts silently when the spec changes.
- **Not breaking:** the struct is already `#[non_exhaustive]`, and its doc had reserved the member for this.
- **`check-bindings` now checks each code's `details_schema`:**
  - it must match the front matter, with shared-file refs inlined as the registry publishes them;
  - it must be `Some` exactly when a schema is declared;
  - it must compile with ajv.
- **Result:** all 195 declared `detailsSchema`s agree. A deliberately altered constant is reported as `details_schema differs from the detailsSchema the front matter declares`.

### 2. A titled inline variant no longer generates doctests
**Cause:**
- typify documents an enum variant as `"{title}\n\n{description}"`.
- prettyplease prints that as `/**…*/`, with the first line flush against the opener.
- rustdoc therefore reads the second paragraph as an indented code block and compiles it.
- Titling the `AccountSettings` branches of `external/_shared` broke 77 doctests.

**Fix:**
- The old description-only pre-pass could not see text that typify assembles itself.
- It is replaced by a `syn::visit_mut` pass over every `#[doc]` attribute in the generated module, which starts any multi-paragraph doc on its own line.

**Verified:** with those branches titled, the old generator fails 77 doctests and the new one generates none.

The regenerated tree differs only in:
- the new `details_schema` members;
- doc-embedded schemas, which no longer carry the stray leading `\n` the old pass wrote into `description`.

### Checks
- **`npm run validate`:** 739 specs, no errors.
- **`npm run check-bindings`:** all four languages agree; 1683 error codes, 195 with a `detailsSchema`.
- **`cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features`:** passes, doctests included.
- **`cargo test -p trust-tasks-codegen`:** passes.
- **Clippy (`-D warnings`) and fmt:** clean.

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.5`) | `0.8.4` → `0.8.5` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.4` → `0.8.5` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(store): conditional atomic batches across local and vsock backends
body:
Follows #2104 (merged).

## What

`KeyspaceHandle::apply_batch(Batch) -> BatchOutcome` applies several writes to one keyspace, guarded by preconditions on keys (`require_absent`, `require_present`, `require_unchanged`). All the writes apply or none do, and only if every precondition holds. A refused batch reports the first precondition that failed and writes nothing.

| Backend | How |
|---|---|
| Local (fjall) | Checks and commit run under the keyspace write lock. The writes are one `WriteBatch`, so one journal record. |
| Vsock (enclave) | New `OP_APPLY_BATCH` (0x0C, capability bit `1 << 4`), served by the enclave proxy as one write batch under its keyspace lock. `require_unchanged` is compared in plaintext inside the enclave; the parent only compares ciphertext. |
| Vsock against an older proxy | Falls back to single operations under the enclave's key locks. This is exclusive but not crash-atomic, the same as every other atomic op's fallback. |

**Rollout:** either side can be upgraded first. Enclaves get the crash-atomic path once the parent proxy is redeployed.

## Callers moved onto it

- **`vta-vault` credential `put`/`delete`:** the record and its index rows change in one batch, and only if the record is still what was read. Before this, two concurrent puts could leave an index row naming a value the credential no longer holds. `concurrent_puts_leave_exactly_the_final_records_index` fails 3 out of 3 runs without the precondition.
- **`store_refresh_index`:** the current-token record and the reverse index are one batch.

## Tests

- **Local store:** an applied batch is one journal record (sequence number +1); a refusal writes nothing; the first failing precondition is the one reported; a key written twice in one batch is refused; exactly one of concurrent claims wins; plaintext comparison works on an encrypted keyspace.
- **Vsock, both proxy modes:** every outcome is reported correctly; exactly one of concurrent claims wins; the batch is one request on an atomic proxy; the parent never sees plaintext.
- **Proxy:** an applied batch is one write batch commit, a refusal commits nothing; exactly one of concurrent claims wins; malformed batches are rejected before any write.
- **`vti-common/tests/crash_recovery.rs`:** SIGKILLs a real writer 8 times and checks that no move is torn and that every acknowledged write survives replay. I did not mutation-check it, because a crash between two separate writes is too narrow a window to hit reliably. The journal-record tests cover that deterministically.

Commands run:
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-common -p vta-vault`: 860 passed
- `cargo test -p vti-common --features vsock-store,encryption --lib store::`: 185 passed
- `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy`: `cargo test` 56 passed
- `cargo nextest run -p vta-service -E 'test(/refresh|auth|vault|cred/)'`: 314 passed (nextest marked 1 as leaky; not investigated)
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -E 'test(/refresh|auth|session/)'`: 259 passed
- fmt and clippy `-D warnings` are clean on every touched crate, including `--features vsock-store,encryption` and the proxy.

I have not run the full workspace suite locally.

title: feat(store): conditional atomic batches across local and vsock backends (#2106)
body:
feat(store): conditional atomic batches across local and vsock backends (#2106)

`KeyspaceHandle::apply_batch` applies several writes to one keyspace,
with preconditions on keys (absent, present, or unchanged plaintext),
as one operation: every write or none, and only if every precondition
holds. A refused batch reports the first precondition that failed and
writes nothing.

- Local store: the checks and the commit run under the keyspace write
  lock, and the writes are one fjall `WriteBatch` — one journal record,
  so crash recovery replays all of them or none.
- Vsock store: a new opcode, OP_APPLY_BATCH (0x0C, capability bit
  1 << 4), served by the enclave proxy under its keyspace lock as one
  write batch. `require_unchanged` is compared in plaintext in the
  enclave; the parent only compares the ciphertext the enclave just
  read. A proxy without the opcode gets the batch as single operations
  under the enclave's key locks — still exclusive, not crash-atomic, as
  with every other atomic op's fallback. Either side may be upgraded
  first.

Callers moved onto it:
- `vta-vault` credential `put` / `delete`: the record and its index
  rows change together, and only over the record that was read, so a
  concurrent writer or a crash can no longer leave an index row naming
  a value the credential no longer holds.
- `store_refresh_index`: the current-token record and the reverse index
  are one batch.

A kill-9 test (`vti-common/tests/crash_recovery.rs`) re-runs its own
binary as a writer, SIGKILLs it mid-stream and checks every batch is
whole and every acknowledged write survives replay.

title: feat(witness): vti-witness host service skeleton and witness DID template (P1, #1068)
body:
Implements **phase P1** of the accepted design note [`docs/05-design-notes/witness-host-service.md`](docs/05-design-notes/witness-host-service.md) (#1068): the witness as an independent host service, the service skeleton only. The witnessing protocol itself (§3.2–§3.4) is P2.

## What was built

### The `dtg-witness` built-in DID template (§3.1, §3.5)
- `vta-sdk/templates/dtg-witness.json`, registered in `BUILTIN_NAMES` / `load_embedded`. `did:webvh`; Ed25519 `#key-0` under both `authentication` and `assertionMethod`; X25519 `#key-1` under `keyAgreement`; `#tsp` (`TSPTransport`) then `#didcomm` (`DIDCommMessaging`), both naming `MEDIATOR_DID` (required); **no `VTARest`** or any HTTP endpoint. Integration kind `dtg-witness`. Named `dtg-witness`, not `witness`: `pnm did-templates init witness` is an existing alias, used by operators, for the did:webvh log witness's shape (`did-host-didcomm`), and it still resolves exactly as on `main`. `URL` / `WEBVH_SERVER` only tell the VTA where to publish the log, as for `did-host-didcomm`.
- `ProvisionAsk::dtg_witness(context, mediator_did)` + `BUILTIN_DTG_WITNESS_TEMPLATE` (additive; the builtin-constant drift test now covers the TSP and witness constants too).
- Every census over the built-ins picks it up (`every_builtin_document_lists_an_assertion_method_key`, the historical-key-pair census, the sign-in-portal census, vta-service's `every_builtin_webvh_integration_template_has_the_bundle_shape`). New rendered-shape fixture `vta-sdk/tests/fixtures/dtg-witness.rendered.json`.

### The `vti-witness` crate and binary (§3.1)
`publish = false` (comment says why), workspace member (not a default member, like `room-host`), depends only on `vti-common` (`tsp`), `vti-secrets`, `vta-sdk` plus existing workspace dependencies.

- **`setup`** — the VTC's two-phase, VTA-provisioned flow, reusing the SDK pieces rather than reimplementing them:
  - `vti-witness setup --setup-key-out <path> [--context witness]` → `vta_sdk::provision_client::driver::run_phase1_init` with a `WitnessMessages` `OperatorMessages` impl.
  - `vti-witness setup --from <toml>` → one `provision-integration` per `[[witness]]` with the `dtg-witness` template, driven by `run_connection_test` / `run_provision_flight` exactly as `vtc setup` drives them (explicit webvh choice passes through). The sealed bundle's key material becomes a `DidSecretsBundle` per identity, kept in the `[secrets]` store via `vti_secrets::create_seed_store` — never in `config.toml` (`config_seed` is refused). Refuses to overwrite an existing `config.toml` or a store already holding witness keys; on a part-way failure it names the identities already minted at the VTA.
  - **No admin-DID hand-off**: a witness administers nothing at its VTA (§3.5: the VTA is a custodian, not a party), so each ask sets no admin template — no long-term VTA admin is minted and no VTA credential reaches the witness host. One setup key provisions every identity; its grant runs out at `--admin-expires` (the summary prints `pnm acl delete` to end it sooner).
- **Config** (`config.toml`, snake_case like the VTC's): `data_dir`, `operator_vta_did`, optional `resolver_url`, `[secrets]`, and `[[witness]]` tables `{name, did, mediator_did, enabled = false}`. **At most 10** — an 11th is a load error. `deny_unknown_fields` on every table this crate defines, plus a `serde_ignored` pass so an unknown key inside `[secrets]` (whose type accepts unknowns) is refused too. Unique names/DIDs; an identity may not be the operator VTA's own DID (VTI-KEY-007).
- **Runtime** (`vti-witness run`): one ATM, one registered profile and one `DidCommTransport` per enabled identity — one websocket per DID carrying DIDComm and TSP. A per-identity supervisor follows CLAUDE.md *Mediator connection*: self-resolution gate (throwaway resolver, `did:key` not gated, 300 s positive window), capped exponential backoff with full jitter (2 s → 60 s), `MIN_HEALTHY_SESSION` = 60 s before the backoff resets, `ATM::graceful_shutdown` on every error path after the ATM exists and at every session end, shutdown checked at every await (gate, connect, sleep, serve), and the startup path reaches its SIGINT/SIGTERM wait at once (even the correlation check is spawned). `vti_common::inbox::run_inbox_watch` (`Escalation::EndSession`) collects what live delivery missed and ends a non-delivering session for the supervisor to rebuild. TSP replies go through `vti_common::tsp_route::send_reply` (cross-mediator routing); TSP relationship invites are accepted; per-sender ordering via `vti_common::sender_order`.
- **Dispatch** (`dispatch.rs`, socket-free): classify with `vta_sdk::inbound::{classify, names_a_reply}` (an error or unclaimed `#response` is dropped, never answered) → parse → freshness (`VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW`, `issuedAt` required) → expiry + `recipient` = this identity (`validate_basic`) → in-band issuer vs transport-proven sender (`TransportHandler::resolve_parties` → `identityMismatch`) → routing (before any verification work) → the task spec's own policy (`schema_index::spec_policy_for`) → proof verified over the document as received, signer = `issuer`. Discovery answered with `vti_common::trust_task::discovery::respond_v0_3` / `respond_v0_1` from the identity's own `SERVED` table. Every reply's `issuer` is set to that identity (never copied from the request — the framework builder would copy a misaddressed request's `recipient`), its `recipient` is the proven sender, and it is signed with that identity's own key via `vta_sdk::trust_task_sign::sign_in_place_with`; a reply that cannot be signed is not sent.
- **Correlation warnings (§3.6)**: at setup and at every start, a **warning** (never a refusal) when an identity shares a mediator with the operator VTA (read from its resolved DID document) or its DID-log host shares a domain with the VTA's, each saying it is a possible correlation source the operator may accept.

## The P1 choice for the unserved witness tasks
`witness/session/0.1` and `witness/session/submit/0.1` are answered `unsupportedType`, with a message saying witnessing is not enabled in this release — and **discovery does not list them**. Discovery answers "which tasks does this agent serve"; listing a type that is always refused would tell a client to send what can never be answered, and only with them unlisted is `unsupportedType` honest. `witness/session:refused` was rejected because it means the witness weighed and *declined* the request (and `submit` declares no such code); `unavailable` promises a retry will work, which in P1 it never will. `dispatch::SERVED` is the one table routing and discovery both read; P2 adds the witness types to it.

## Also changed
- `Dockerfile.nitro`: `COPY vti-witness/ vti-witness/` (the enclave image copies every workspace member).

## Docs
- New `docs/06-witness/README.md` (Part VI in `docs/README.md`): what the service is, setup, config, runtime, what it serves, the correlators, and the v1 no-ZKP statement from §6.
- `docs/02-vta/did-templates.md`: the `dtg-witness` built-in.
- The design note names the template `dtg-witness` and says why.
- Root `CLAUDE.md`: layout block, crate-map row, the built-ins list, and a *Witness host service* integration-flow entry.

## Tests
- `vta-sdk` `did_templates`: loads/validates, exact rendered shape, services by `type` (TSP then DIDComm at the mediator; no `VTARest`, `VTCRest`, `TrustTaskHTTPS`, `WebVHHosting`, `SignInPortal`), keys in the right relationships + key slots, missing `MEDIATOR_DID` refused; `ProvisionAsk::dtg_witness` ≡ `for_template`.

title: feat(rooms): rooms/owner/group/renew renews a sealed room; rooms/keys/act refuses a sealed room's mint (#773)
body:
feat(rooms): rooms/owner/group/renew renews a sealed room; rooms/keys/act refuses a sealed room's mint (#773)

A sealed room (`attributed` / `private`) had no correct way to renew, and
one way to brick itself that looked like a renewal.

- rooms/epoch/mint advances a host without a commit (a host MUST), and on a
  sealed room the room epoch is the MLS group epoch + 1. rooms/keys/act/0.1
  completes a mint for a member's client, which holds no group key and so
  sends no commit: the host moves to N+1, every member's key holder stays at
  N, every write is refused as sealed under a superseded epoch, and the
  owner's next rooms/owner/group/{add,remove} fails epochConflict.
- Only membership changes advanced a sealed room's epoch, so a room whose
  membership was stable lapsed after its epoch lifetime with no remedy.

rooms/owner/group/renew/0.1 (new, Owner -> KeyHolder): the sibling of
group/{create,add,remove}. The key holder advances the group with a commit
that changes no membership (self-update or empty commit), builds the epoch
link, retains the pending advance durably before sending (at most one per
room, shared with add/remove), mints at the host with the commit, the link
and the owner's admin presentation, applies only on acceptance, discards on
refusal, keeps on an unknown outcome and settles via rooms/info. Errors:
noGroup, noAuthority, epochConflict (details.hostEpoch), hostUnreachable,
hostRefused.

rooms/keys/act/0.1 (draft, edited in place): recipient item 9 refuses a
rooms/epoch/mint for a room it holds group state for, for any member it
serves, with the new rooms/keys/act:sealedRoomMint naming
rooms/owner/group/renew; producer item 4 says not to ask. Open rooms keep
renewing through act. The wire shape is unchanged; a draft MAY change
without a version bump (SPEC §5.2/§5.3), and a 0.2 would leave 0.1
permitting the defect it exists to close.

rooms/epoch/mint/0.1: a non-normative note that on a sealed room the
producer is the owner's key holder via rooms/owner/group/{add,remove,renew}.

rooms/owner/group/{add,remove}/0.1 item 4: the presentation was described
as "bound to `host`", which rooms/keys/present/0.2 cannot do — a
presentation is bound to the room; the advance is bound to the host by the
mint document's `recipient`, covered by its proof (SPEC §4.8.2). Reworded to
say so. add item 3 now states the one-pending-advance rule remove already
stated, and both name renewal.

Related entries added both ways (owner group tasks, act, epoch/mint,
keys/commit).

Additive for trust-tasks-rs: a new rooms::owner::group::renew::v0_1 module
and error_codes::SEALED_ROOM_MINT on rooms::keys::act::v0_1.

title: fix(store): commit swap and move_if_unchanged as one journal record
body:
## Problem

`LocalKeyspaceHandle::swap` and `move_if_unchanged` wrote the new row and removed the old one as two separate fjall writes, so two journal records. If the process crashed between them, recovery left both rows live. For a member key rotation, that means the old DID keeps its authority beside the new one. This is the residual gap the comment in `vtc-service/src/routes/members/rotate.rs` described.

The per-keyspace write lock already protected these operations against concurrent callers. It could not protect them against a crash.

## Fix

Both operations now commit through `commit_move`, a single fjall `WriteBatch`. That is one journal record under one sequence number, so crash recovery replays both writes or neither. The enclave proxy's `move_locked` (`deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy/src/storage.rs`) already commits the same way, so the local and vsock backends now make the same crash guarantee.

The stale "tracked as a follow-up" comment in `rotate.rs` is removed.

## Test

`moves_commit_as_one_journal_record` checks that each `swap` and `move_if_unchanged` advances the journal sequence number by exactly one, and that a refused move writes nothing. I mutation-checked it: with the old two-write code restored, it fails with `swap is one record: left 2, right 1`.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p vti-common -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-common`: 721 passed
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -E 'test(/rotat|swap|acl/)'`: 239 passed

I have not run the full workspace suite locally.

## Context

This is the first of a series hardening store durability and recovery on fjall's journal:
1. (this PR) Multi-row moves are one journal record.
2. A conditional atomic batch (writes plus preconditions as one record, locally and over vsock), adopted by vault `put` and `store_refresh_index`, with a kill-9 crash test.
3. Group commit for durable writes.
4. An operation journal with a boot-time reconciler for multi-step and remote operations.

title: feat(secrets)!: encrypted-at-rest file backend (#1820)
body:
Closes #1820.

## What

A new `vti-secrets` backend, `encrypted_file`: the secret is kept in one file under AES-256-GCM, keyed from a key-encryption key (KEK) source the operator names explicitly. A headless host with no OS keychain now has a secure local option instead of `plaintext`. Every consumer of `vti-secrets` gets it: the VTA (`backend = "encrypted_file"`), the VTC (`backend = "encrypted-file"`, its kebab-case vocabulary), and external integrations through `create_seed_store`.

KEK sources (all three from the issue; cloud-KMS envelope is out of scope):

| `kek.source` | file key | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `passphrase` | Argon2id(passphrase, salt), m = 64 MiB, t = 3, p = 4 | passphrase from `file = <path>` or `credential = <systemd credential name>`; **never** from the config or an env var (there is no field for it) |
| `systemd_creds` | HKDF-SHA256(KEK, salt) | 32-byte KEK from `$CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY/<credential>` (32 raw bytes or 64 hex chars); systemd does the TPM / host-key sealing |
| `tpm` | HKDF-SHA256(KEK, salt) | random KEK sealed by the TPM 2.0 under the owner-hierarchy SRK, optionally bound to SHA-256 PCRs; the sealed object is stored in the file header. Feature `tpm` (off by default), Linux only, via `tss-esapi` 7.7 |

## Config

```toml
[secrets]
backend = "encrypted_file"            # VTC: "encrypted-file"

[secrets.encrypted_file]
path = "/var/lib/vta/seed.enc"        # optional; default <data_dir>/seed.enc (VTC: secret.enc)
kek = { source = "passphrase", file = "/etc/vta/seed-passphrase" }
# kek = { source = "passphrase", credential = "vta-seed-passphrase" }
# kek = { source = "systemd_creds", credential = "vta-seed-kek" }
# kek = { source = "tpm", pcrs = [7], tcti = "device:/dev/tpmrm0" }
```

`EncryptedFileConfig` / `KekSource` live in `vti-secrets` (`deny_unknown_fields`, `#[non_exhaustive]`) and are shared by the VTA's and the VTC's `SecretsConfig`. `SecretsConfig` stays `#[non_exhaustive]`.

**Selection.** Explicit only. Implicit resolution never picks it, and a `[secrets.encrypted_file]` table *without* `backend = "encrypted_file"` is a `Config` error rather than being silently ignored (otherwise an operator who meant to encrypt at rest would quietly land on the keyring). Both factories (`vti_secrets::create_seed_store`, `vtc_service::keys::seed_store::create_secret_store`) do this. The VTA setup TOML (`SecretsBackendInput::EncryptedFile`) and the VTA interactive wizard offer it; a TPM source is a config error on a build without `tpm`, or on a non-Linux target.

## Envelope (format v1)

```
magic "VTISECF\0" | version 1 | AEAD 1 (AES-256-GCM) | KEK source (1 passphrase, 2 systemd-creds, 3 tpm) | reserved 0
salt[32] | nonce[12] | descriptor_len u16 BE | descriptor | ciphertext+tag
```

The whole header is the AEAD's associated data. Descriptors: Argon2id m/t/p (12 bytes); empty for systemd-creds; for TPM, PCR bank + PCR list + the TPM-marshalled sealed public part + the TPM2B_PRIVATE. Salt and nonce are fresh on every write, so each write has its own file key; the TPM source also seals a fresh KEK per write. Argon2 parameters below the floors (m < 64 MiB, t < 3) or above the ceilings (2 GiB, t 64, p 16) are refused on read. HKDF `info` includes the source id, so one KEK used under two sources yields unrelated file keys.

**Writes**: `vti_common::secure_file::write_secret_file` to a temp file beside the target (0600 from creation, `create_new`, fsynced), `rename` over the target, fsync the directory. A missing parent directory is created at 0700.

**Fail closed**: a missing file is `Ok(None)` ("no secret yet", as for every backend). Anything else is an error: wrong passphrase / KEK, any tampered byte (header included), unknown version, unknown AEAD / source id, non-zero reserved byte, truncated file, a header from a different KEK source than configured, a missing credential or `$CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY`, an empty passphrase.

**Memory**: the KEK, file key and passphrase are `Zeroizing`; passphrase/credential reads are pre-sized so a reallocation leaves no copy. No derived `Debug` holds a secret (the store's `Debug` prints the path and the source name only). Argon2id and TPM calls run on `spawn_blocking`.

## Threat model (documented in `docs/02-vta/secret-backends.md`)

Protects the secret in a copy of the file taken away from the running host (stolen disk or image, backup, snapshot), provided the KEK does not travel with it (a TPM-sealed KEK or a TPM-sealed systemd credential stays behind; a passphrase file on the same disk does not). Does **not** protect against root or the service user on the running host: whoever can read the passphrase / credential, use the TPM as this host, or read process memory can decrypt it.

## Tests

- `vti-secrets` (24 new): round trip for passphrase-from-file, passphrase-from-credential, systemd-creds (raw and hex KEK), each with the credentials directory passed in explicitly (`with_credentials_directory`, so no test mutates the process env); wrong passphrase; wrong KEK; malformed KEK credential; missing credential; empty passphrase; tamper detection (ciphertext byte, tag byte, salt byte, nonce byte, Argon2 `t_cost` within range); KDF parameters below the floor; unknown version; magic / AEAD / reserved bytes; truncated and empty files; source mismatch; mode 0600 on create and on overwrite of a 0644 file; no temp file left behind; parent dir created 0700; delete; config validation; TOML parsing incl. `deny_unknown_fields` and no inline passphrase; factory: explicit selection needs the table, the table alone is refused, a factory-built store round-trips. Envelope unit tests: header round trip, every malformed-header path, Argon2 floors/ceilings, HKDF source separation, TPM descriptor encode/decode and its rejections.
- `vtc-service`: explicit `encrypted-file` without a table, table without the selector, round trip under `secret.enc`; `encrypted-file` in the selector-spelling test.
- `vta-service`: setup-TOML `encrypted_file` parses, lands in `[secrets.encrypted_file]`, round-trips, refuses an inline passphrase; added to the every-choice-states-its-selector test.
- TPM (`tpm` feature): three tests that run only when `VTI_SECRETS_TEST_TCTI` names a TPM: round trip without PCRs; PCR-16-bound round trip, unseal failure after extending PCR 16, re-seal on the next write; tampered sealed blob fails. These passed against `swtpm` (Debian bookworm, `libtss2-dev`, aarch64 Linux container), including the PCR-policy refusal (`TPM_RC_POLICY_FAIL`, 0x99d) after extending PCR 16. See Limitations for how they were run.

CI-equivalent runs: on macOS, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5862 passed, 23 skipped; workspace doctests pass; `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -E 'test(seed_store) | test(secret)'`: 48 passed; `cargo deny check` ok.

## Limitations

- **The TPM path is not exercised by CI** (no TPM, and the default build does not compile the `tpm` feature). I verified it in a Linux container against `swtpm`: `tpm.rs` and `envelope.rs` compiled and clippy-clean (`-D warnings`) with `--features tpm`, and the three TPM tests passed. That build used a standalone copy of the module with a stub `vti-common`, because building the full workspace graph in the container was OOM-killed compiling `trust-tasks-rs`; the module code is byte-identical. Nothing ran against a hardware TPM.
- `tss-esapi` 7.7 adds lockfile entries even with the feature off (optional deps are always resolved), and its build dependency `target-lexicon` is `Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception`, now allowed in `deny.toml`.
- The TPM SRK is the transient owner-hierarchy primary re-derived on each use (ECC P-256, AES-128-CFB storage template); it assumes an empty owner-hierarchy auth. `tpm2_clear` or moving the disk makes the file unreadable (by design); with PCRs, a firmware/bootloader update that changes them locks the file until they are restored.
- The VTC's interactive `vtc setup` wizard does not offer `encrypted-file`: its backend menu is `vti_common::setup::secrets_prompt`, and adding a choice there is a breaking change to `vti-common` (non-`#[non_exhaustive]` `SecretsBackendChoice`, all-pub `AvailableBackends`). VTC operators select it with `vtc setup --from <toml>` or in `config.toml`. The VTA's interactive wizard does offer it.
- No offline "decrypt to stdout" tool, so migrating *away* from this backend is by restoring the mnemonic into the new backend.

## Breaking

`SecretBackend` (vti-secrets, re-exported by vta-config) is not `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new `EncryptedFile` variant is breaking; so is the new `SecretsBackendInput::EncryptedFile` variant in `vta-service`. Hence the `!`.

title: vti-secrets: encrypted-at-rest file backend for hosts without an OS keychain
body:
## Problem

`vti-secrets` has no secure local option for a host without an OS credential store. On a headless Linux server with no Secret Service (no gnome-keyring, KWallet or KeePassXC, and no D-Bus session), the only local backend is `plaintext`, which keeps the secret in clear text. `vta-sdk::secure_store`'s `file` store is also plaintext at 0600.

Such a host must use a remote backend (Vault, Kubernetes, AWS, GCP or Azure) or a TEE. That is right for production, but a small single-host deployment has no secure option at all.

affinidi-webvh-service now takes every backend from `vti-secrets`, and refuses at setup on such a host with the list of secure backends. It does not implement its own crypto. This issue asks for the missing backend in `vti-secrets`, so every consumer (VTA, VTC, webvh, vti-message-bridge) gets it at once.

## Proposal: an encrypted-at-rest file backend (`encrypted_file`)

- The file holds an AEAD envelope: a versioned header, a KDF or sealing descriptor, a nonce, and ciphertext. Use XChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-256-GCM, with the header as associated data. Write it at 0600 via `vti_common::secure_file`, and write it atomically.
- The key-encryption key comes from one of these, chosen explicitly:
  1. **TPM 2.0 sealed** (Linux, `tss-esapi`): a KEK sealed to the TPM, optionally bound to PCRs. This gives an unattended boot without a passphrase.
  2. **systemd-creds** / `CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY`: the host encrypts the credential (TPM or host key), and the service reads the KEK from its credential directory. This is thin, and it is how systemd is meant to be used.
  3. **Passphrase via Argon2id**: store the salt and parameters in the header (m ≥ 64 MiB, t ≥ 3). The passphrase comes from a file or a systemd credential, never from an environment variable or the config.
  4. **Cloud KMS envelope** (optional): a data key wrapped by AWS, GCP or Azure KMS, for hosts that have KMS but not Secrets Manager.
- It fails closed: a wrong key, a bad tag or an unknown version is an error, never "no secret".
- `SecretBackend::EncryptedFile` is added to `SecretsConfig`, with the new fields documented. Implicit resolution never picks it. It is always explicit.
- Tests cover a round trip per KEK source that CI can run (passphrase, systemd-creds with a test key), tamper detection, and a wrong passphrase.

## Consumers

When it ships, webvh would make it the recommended backend for a headless host with no keychain, with the operator's explicit selection.

* feat(secrets)!: encrypted-at-rest file backend (#1820)

Add `encrypted_file` to vti-secrets: the secret is kept in one file under
AES-256-GCM, keyed from an explicitly configured key-encryption key, so a
headless host with no OS keychain has a secure local option instead of
`plaintext`.

KEK sources (`[secrets.encrypted_file] kek = { source = ... }`):
- `passphrase`: Argon2id (m = 64 MiB, t = 3, p = 4; salt and parameters in
  the header, floors enforced on read), passphrase from a file or a systemd
  credential, never from the config or an environment variable;
- `systemd_creds`: a 32-byte KEK from $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY, HKDF-SHA256;
- `tpm` (feature `tpm`, Linux, tss-esapi 7.7): a random KEK sealed under the
  owner-hierarchy SRK, optionally bound to SHA-256 PCRs, stored sealed in the
  header, HKDF-SHA256.

Envelope v1: magic, version, AEAD id, KEK source id, salt, nonce and a
length-prefixed descriptor, all of it the AEAD's associated data. Fresh salt
and nonce per write. Writes are atomic (0600 temp file via
`secure_file::write_secret_file`, fsync, rename, directory fsync). Fails
closed: only a missing file is "no secret"; a wrong key, any modified byte,
an unknown version, a malformed header or a header from another KEK source
is an error. Key material and passphrases are zeroized; no derived Debug
holds a secret.

Selection is explicit only, in both the VTA factory and the VTC's
`create_secret_store` (`encrypted-file`): implicit resolution never picks it,
and a `[secrets.encrypted_file]` table without the selector is a config
error. The VTA setup TOML and interactive wizard offer it; vta-keys

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.3
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Act as the member's persona — rooms/keys/act, seal 0.2, direct-to-storage blob transfer ([#771](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/771))

A member of a data room is the DID the room admitted — usually a persona
  their key holder (VTA) holds for them — but the member's own client (CLI,
  extension, phone) holds none of that DID's keys. Until now it could reach a
  host only through rooms/keys/present, which grants the leaf to the caller,
  and then signed with its own key: the host recorded the client's did:key as
  the actor and, on an attributed room, as the author of every record.

  - rooms/keys/act/0.1 (new): the client builds a host-bound room request
    without presentation or proof; the key holder completes it as the member
    (the member's own authority narrowed to the one action a closed table
    fixes per type, granted to the member; issuer = member; the member's
    authentication proof) and returns it for the client to send. Refused to
    delegates, which keep using rooms/keys/present.
  - rooms/keys/seal/0.2: optional signAsPrincipal — the key holder signs the
    SealedRecordBody as its author (a member the caller acts as) before
    sealing, so the record is attributed to the member.
  - rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}/0.2 and rooms/blobs/get/0.2:
    two transfer modes. Direct: the host authorizes and reserves as before,
    then issues per-part presigned PUTs (one object, one method, exact length
    and SHA-256 as signed headers, <= 5 min), verifies the object at storage
    before commit records it, and serves reads with a presigned GET. Proxied:
    bytes through the host as chunk documents signed by a single-use upload
    key the begin names, so file bytes never pass through the key holder.
    A host SHOULD NOT offer direct transfer on a private room unless its
    policy allows; the response always names the mode.
  - In place (drafts, wire unchanged): rooms/keys/{read,browse,backfill}
    present as the principal and never let the key holder's own identifier
    reach the host; rooms/keys/welcome and rooms/keys/open keep one group
    state per member per room.
  - rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs: TransferMode, PartPlan, TransferTarget (additive).

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags

- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*

- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(rooms): rooms/keys/act, seal 0.2 and direct-to-storage blobs — act as the member's persona
body:
## Why

A member of a data room is the DID the room admitted — usually a persona their key holder (VTA) holds — yet the member's own client holds none of that DID's keys. Through `rooms/keys/present` (leaf granted to the caller) and its own signature, the client became the host's recorded actor and, on `attributed` rooms, the author of every record (observed live: `"author": "did:key:z6Mk…"` of a CLI session key). This lets the client act **as the persona** with no key leaving the key holder, and lets file bytes go straight to storage.

## What

| Spec | Version | How |
|---|---|---|
| `rooms/keys/act` | **0.1 (new)** | Key holder completes a host-bound room request as the member: own VAC narrowed to the one action a closed table fixes per type, granted to the member; `issuer` = member; member's `authentication` proof. Returned, not sent. Refused to delegates (they keep `present`). |
| `rooms/keys/seal` | **0.2 (new version)** | Optional `signAsPrincipal`: sign the `SealedRecordBody` as its `author` (a member the caller acts as) before sealing. |
| `rooms/blobs/upload/begin` | **0.2** | Two modes. Producer offers `directParts` (part plan, sha2-256) and/or `uploadKey` (single-use `did:key`); response `mode`, `targets`. Direct: per-part presigned PUT — one object, one method, exact length + SHA-256 as signed headers, ≤ 5 min, never logged. Proxied: chunks signed by the upload key. Host SHOULD NOT choose direct for `private` rooms unless policy allows. |
| `rooms/blobs/upload/chunk` | **0.2** | Proxied only; authenticated by the upload key. |
| `rooms/blobs/upload/commit` | **0.2** | Upload key (proxied) or owner (direct, via `act`). Direct: verify the object at storage (part lengths/checksums, size, storage checksum) before recording anything. |
| `rooms/blobs/upload/abort` | **0.2** | Upload key (proxied) or owner (direct); direct deletes parts at storage. |
| `rooms/blobs/get` | **0.2** | Optional `direct`; response `mode`, `target` (presigned GET, Range allowed, ≤ 5 min) or `downloadId`. Removal does not recall an issued URL before its TTL (stated). |
| `rooms/keys/read`, `browse`, `backfill` | 0.1, **in place** | Present as the principal, document issued/signed by the principal; the key holder's own identifier MUST NOT reach the host. |
| `rooms/keys/welcome`, `rooms/keys/open` | 0.1, **in place** | One group state per member per room; another member's state is not `alreadyJoined` and is never used to open. |
| `rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs` | additive | `TransferMode`, `PartPlan`, `TransferTarget`. |

**New version vs in place.** New versions where the wire shape changes (seal gains a member; begin/get gain request and response members, `mode` REQUIRED) or where who may send a document changes (chunk/commit/abort: payload unchanged but authenticated by a different party, which is a behavioural break for consumers). In-place where the spec is a draft and the wire is unchanged (read/browse/backfill presenter wording; welcome/open per-member clarification; additive shared defs).

**Other decisions.** The `act` table excludes `rooms/epoch/prune`, `owner/transfer`, `owner/claim`, `create` (destructive or ownership-changing); includes `usage` and `epoch/mint` (`admin`), and `blobs/upload/{commit,abort}/0.2` without a presentation (direct mode only). The error code `unsupportedType` would shadow the §8.3 standard code, so it is `typeNotActable`. The direct-mode part plan is separate from the 256 KiB chunk manifest because S3-class multipart needs ≥ 5 MiB parts; readers still check the chunk manifest. A nested `not` on `act`'s inner payload broke typify, so "no presentation in the payload" is a conformance rule (`malformedRequest`) rather than schema.

Consumer: verifiable-trust-infrastructure (VTA `rooms/keys/act` + seal 0.2, `pnm rooms put/get/list/curate` as the persona; VTC host direct mode via vta-account `s3-static-presign`).

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart). Local: `npm run build`, `check-bindings`, `check-dart-packages`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo deny` — all green.

title: fix(vtc): admit room traffic on what it proves, not the anonymous per-IP governor
body:
Every `rooms/*` Trust Task reaches the VTC on the unauthenticated chain and
was charged to the per-IP `unauth` governor: a burst of 10, then one request
every 5 s, shared by everyone behind one address. Two members on one machine
were refused within seconds, and `pnm rooms file get` of a 300 KB file 429'd
every time. Upload chunks fared worse: above 64 KiB they also took the
large-document budget, five a minute per address and sixty across the node.

A `rooms/*` document (the closed set the rooms dispatcher serves) now leaves
the anonymous governor and is charged, in `routing::trust_task_admission`:

- before anything is verified, to its address's room ceiling
  (`room-address`, default burst 400 then one every 10 ms). A document that
  never verifies, or that its room never authorizes, costs that ceiling 25
  more, so an unverifiable flood from one address is held to about four a
  second once its burst is spent;
- once the room has authorized it and before the work, to the presenter's
  budget in that room (`room-presenter`, burst 120, one every 100 ms), or for
  an upload/download chunk, once the presenter is shown to hold the transfer
  (`BlobHost::transfer_room`), to the transfer budget (`room-transfer`, burst
  200, one every 20 ms: a 100 MB file at 256 KiB chunks waits ~4 s past the
  burst). Keys are a hash of (room, presenter) under a per-process secret, and
  are charged only after the room's chain verifies, so two members behind one
  NAT have independent budgets and nobody drains a member's by naming them.

An upload chunk charged to the room ceiling over HTTPS skips the
large-document budget (`size::check_for_known_issuer_with`); over DIDComm/TSP
it keeps it. Every refusal keeps the 429 contract (x-rate-limit-source: vtc,
Retry-After, JSON body naming the limiter); the three limiter names join the
table in `routing::rate_limit`.

The budgets are an optional `[rooms.rate_limits]` section (address_*,
presenter_*, transfer_* as `_burst` and `_interval_ms`); absent, the defaults
above. Documented in docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md §8.2 and
docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md.

vtc-client's room calls now wait out a Retry-After of up to 30 s and retry
(up to 5 attempts, re-signed each time) for reads only: records get/list,
info, epoch chain/commits, blobs get and download chunks. Writes are never
retried.

vti-rooms gains `BlobHost::transfer_room` (additive).

## Tests
- `tests/it/room_rate_limits.rs` (through the real router, one address): 40 room reads from one member; a 24-chunk file downloads with no 429, interleaved with other reads; an 8-chunk upload of >64 KiB documents lands (was capped at 5/min); two presenters behind one address get independent budgets; an unauthorized-document flood is refused by `room-address` within a handful while a member elsewhere is unaffected.
- Unit: room/presenter/transfer keys charged apart, failure penalty, keyed hash, no-op off the HTTPS door; config defaults when `[rooms.rate_limits]` is absent, partial section, zero clamps, unknown keys refused; vtc-client retries only reads and only short `Retry-After`s.

## Verified locally
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (3119 passed), doc tests
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` (5845 passed), doc tests
- `cargo deny --all-features check`

Note: with presigned S3 transfers in progress in the spec, S3-config files will move few documents through the VTC; the transfer budget stays for `local` configs' proxied chunks.

title: feat(rooms)!: backfill from the CLI, and say plainly when a member was removed
body:
Found in a live run of a two-VTA room on a VTC:

- A member who had just joined could not read anything written before they
  joined from the CLI: the VTA's rooms/keys/backfill fetches the history from
  the host, but nothing called it. New `pnm rooms keys backfill --room
  --host-did` (VtaClient::room_backfill) walks the chain down until the whole
  retained history reads or the host has no more.
- `pnm rooms get` told every member who could not open a record to ask for the
  latest commit, including one whose record was older than their group. It now
  names the remedy for each case: backfill for an older record, `keys commit
  --host` for a newer one.
- A removed member applying their own removal got GroupStateError
  (UseAfterEviction) from the key export. vti-rooms now detects the eviction
  when the commit merges and returns RoomKeyError::Removed ("this commit
  removed this holder from the group…"), and the CLI says what it means.
- Wording: "an authority credential"; group-create's next step no longer tells
  an owner to issue credentials they already issued.

BREAKING: vti-rooms RoomKeyError gains a Removed variant and is now
#[non_exhaustive], so later variants are not breaking.

## Verified live
Run against two VTAs and a VTC on localhost (the end-to-end run that found these):
- `pnm rooms keys backfill`: a member who joined at epoch 3 fetched 4 links, reads back to epoch 1, and opened the epoch-1 record it could not open before.
- A removed member applying their removal now gets *this commit removed this holder from the group* instead of `GroupStateError(UseAfterEviction)`.

## Checks
fmt; clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, vti-rooms `mls`-only, vta-service `rest`-only; workspace nextest and doctests; vtc-service/vtc-client nextest; cargo-deny. One workspace test (`audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry`) hit the 300 s timeout under load and passes alone in 34 s. Rebased on #2096 and re-checked (clippy + 236 room/persona tests).

title: feat(vault): present P-256-bound SD-JWT-VCs with an ES256 kb-jwt (#1988)
body:
Part of #1988: the "ES256 key-binding JWT when presenting from a VTA vault" item.

## What

- **`vta-service` `holder_keys::resolve_holder_keys`** accepts a derived **P-256** holder key as well as Ed25519. For P-256, `HolderSdJwtSigner` signs the `kb-jwt` with **ES256** (fixed-width `r||s`, RFC 7518 §3.4), and the consent secret is P-256. The algorithm comes from the key; the caller never chooses it. The ACL and key-custody gates are unchanged.
- **`vta_vault::consent::holder_suite`** sets the Data Integrity suite from the holder key: `eddsa-jcs-2022` for Ed25519, `ecdsa-jcs-2019` for P-256. Consent receipts and DI presentations (`present_di_vc`) sign under it.
- **`ConsentRecord::verify_proof`** decodes the subject `did:key` (Ed25519 or P-256, through `vta_sdk::jws::JwsKey`) and requires the suite that key type takes, so a proof can't pick its own verification. secp256k1 has no DI suite and is refused.
- **CLAUDE.md**: the key policy now lists the holder-key exception next to the foreign-protocol identity one. The user approved this widening for #1988.

## Bug fixed along the way

mdoc presentation signs its consent receipt with the P-256 **device key**, but `consent::create` always asked for `eddsa-jcs-2022`, and `affinidi-data-integrity` refuses that suite for a P-256 key. So no mdoc could be presented: `present_query` failed at consent creation. The existing mdoc tests cover matching only, which is why nothing caught it. The suite now follows the key, which fixes this.

## Tests

- `vta-vault`: `a_p256_holder_signs_and_verifies_under_ecdsa_jcs_2019` (the mdoc and P-256 holder consent path) and `a_proof_in_the_wrong_suite_for_the_holder_is_refused`.
- `vta-service`: `a_p256_holder_signs_its_kb_jwt_es256`. A derived P-256 holder resolves through the real ACL and custody gates, and its ES256 `kb-jwt` verifies under the holder's own `did:key` via `vta_sdk::jws`.
- 382 vault, holder, credential, consent, mdoc and present tests pass. Workspace clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` and fmt are clean.

## Not here

An end-to-end mdoc or P-256 SD-JWT presentation through `present_query` with a real verifier. The pieces are each covered, but no test drives the whole OID4VP response. The other #1988 item, the swiyu/EUDI sandbox, needs operator accounts.

title: fix(vta)!: room group state is per member (room, persona), so two personas on one VTA can share a room
body:
## The defect (observed live)

One VTA held persona Alice (context alice) and persona Bob (context bob). Alice owned room R and founded its group; Bob was invited, his KeyPackage minted, Alice's `group/add` admitted him — and `rooms/keys/welcome` for Bob failed: *"this VTA already holds group state for room R"*. Group state was keyed by room alone, so a VTA could hold one member's group per room.

## The fix

Everything kept per room in `room_groups` is keyed per **member** — `room-group/<roomId>/<persona>`, `room-kp/…`, `room-advance/…`, `room-roots/…`. Which member a task acts as is decided in the new `operations::room_member`:

| task | member |
|---|---|
| `key-package`, `welcome` | the invitation's subject |
| `read`, `browse`, `backfill`, `owner/anchor` | the persona whose credentials are presented (`room_oracle::principal`), one resolution for both |
| `owner/group/{create,add,remove}` | the owner persona |
| `open`, `seal`, `file-key`, `commit`, `chain` | exactly one persona the caller may act as holding the room; else Conflict "act from the context of the one you mean"; never the client DID |
| `list` | every room held by a persona the caller may act as |

Context isolation: a persona in a context the caller cannot act in is invisible — its group answers like a room nobody holds. Root memory is per member for the same reason. `welcome` now answers the declared `rooms/keys/welcome:alreadyJoined` for the *same* persona.

## Migration

Rows from the per-room build (`room-group:<roomId>`, `room-kp:`, `room-advance:`, `room-add:`, `room-roots:`) move under their member on first touch — atomic `move_if_unchanged` per row, group last, never over a member's own row. The member is the persona the group's own leaf identifies (when the caller may act as it); a group joined before personas (leaf = client DID) is attributed to the persona its room credentials name, only when the caller *is* that client. Nobody else moves it.

`room_groups` stays in `BACKED_UP`; the keyspace partition is unchanged.

## Spec note (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf, not edited here)

`rooms/keys/welcome/0.1` §"Joining twice is refused, not merged": *"A recipient already holding group state for `roomId` MUST answer `alreadyJoined`."* — read per member. Proposed clarification in the PR report.

## Breaking

`vta-service` public API: `room_groups` fns take `&Member`; `JoinError`; `list_rooms` → `held_members`/`holders`/`held_room`; `send_room_task{,_typed}` / `refuse_if_caught` take `&Member`; `is_own_leaf` removed.

## Verified locally

fmt, workspace clippy `-D warnings`, `vta-service --no-default-features --features rest` clippy, `rest,didcomm` check, workspace nextest (5845 passed), doc tests, `cargo deny`.

title: fix(vta)!: room group state is per member (room, persona), so two personas on one VTA can share a room (#2096)
body:
fix(vta)!: room group state is per member (room, persona), so two personas on one VTA can share a room (#2096)

One VTA serves several principals, and a person may hold several personas.
Group state was keyed by room alone, so a VTA could hold only one member's
group per room: with Alice (context alice) owning room R and Bob (context bob)
admitted, Bob's rooms/keys/welcome failed with "this VTA already holds group
state for room R". A family on one VTA, or a team on a company VTA, could not
be in the same room.

Everything the VTA keeps per room in `room_groups` is now keyed per member:
`room-group/<roomId>/<persona>`, `room-kp/…`, `room-advance/…` and
`room-roots/…` (DIDs carry no `/`, so the key is unambiguous; `Member::new`
refuses anything that does). Consumed invitations stay keyed by credential id,
which already names one subject.

Which member a task acts as (`operations::room_member`):
- key-package / welcome: the invitation's subject;
- read / browse / backfill / owner anchor: the persona whose credentials are
  presented (`room_oracle::principal`), one resolution for both;
- rooms/owner/group/*: the owner persona (`HostCall`), with noGroup / ownLeaf
  answered against the persona the caller holds the group as;
- open / seal / file-key / commit / chain: exactly one persona the caller may
  act as holding the room, else Conflict "act from the context of the one you
  mean"; never the client DID;
- list: every room held by a persona the caller may act as.
A persona in a context the caller cannot act in is invisible: its group answers
like a room nobody holds, and nothing of it is read, advanced or listed. Root
memory is per member for the same reason. rooms/keys/commit now resolves its
group this way (before, any authenticated caller reached the one group).

rooms/keys/welcome answers the declared `rooms/keys/welcome:alreadyJoined` when
the invitation's persona already holds the room's group; another persona on
the VTA is no obstacle.

Migration: rows the per-room build wrote (`room-group:<roomId>`, `room-kp:`,
`room-advance:`, `room-add:`, `room-roots:`) move under their member on first
touch, each with one atomic `move_if_unchanged`, group last, never over a
member's own row. The member is the persona the group's own leaf identifies,
when the caller may act as it; a group joined before personas (leaf = client
DID) is attributed to the persona its room credentials name, and only when the
caller is that client. Anyone else leaves the row untouched. A pre-upgrade
KeyPackage moves when the Welcome for its leaf's persona arrives; pre-upgrade
root memory is read as a fallback until the member writes its own.

Breaking (vta-service public API): `room_groups` functions take `&Member`
instead of a room id; `JoinError`; `list_rooms` replaced by `held_members` /
`holders` / `held_room`; `room_host::send_room_task{,_typed}` and
`refuse_if_caught` take `&Member`; `is_own_leaf` removed.

Tests: two personas in two contexts on one VTA both join one room and each
reads and writes; a caller in context A cannot open, seal, commit or list B's
group; a migrated single-key row still opens (and B's caller neither opens nor
moves it); one persona holding state resolves for a caller acting as both, two
ask the caller to choose; storage-level migration, per-member root memory and
an upgraded owner store with a legacy pending admission.

title: feat(review): bind examination evidence to review records (Increment 2)
body:
## What changed

Implements Increment 2 of #17 on top of #19. Adds `review/examine.py`, which reruns the installed bounded TRQP evaluator and validates source identity, the existing review contract, selected risk references, exact review/corpus digests and example-local evidence bindings. Missing, incomplete, stale or contradictory evidence cannot emit a successful validation report. Successful validation still reports `overall_assurance: review-required`.

The strict existing review schema stays unchanged. An experimental sidecar carries observations, inference, limitations, proposed treatment and per-risk mapping rationale. Two example-local hypotheses are explicitly selected through the existing `--risks` interface; the canonical DTG corpus is unchanged. Authority, delegation, revocation and runtime authorization remain unassessed. Both findings remain open.

## Dependency and design choice

Stacked on #19 so the diff contains only Increment 2. Merge/reconcile Increment 1 first, then retarget this PR to accepted main without duplicating its changes. Pending CI #14 is not imported or duplicated. Keep #17 open.

A sidecar preserves compatibility and exposes evidence without undocumented review members or a wholesale downstream pressure-test import. It remains example-local until a second subject tests reuse. The adapter checks structural coverage, reference identity and reproducibility; independent reviewers still need to assess whether the evidence supports the inference. Digest consistency is not publisher authentication. User-supplied bundle code is never executed.

## Artefact IDs affected

Example-local SR-001, F-001/F-002, E-001–E-009 and RK-AU01/RK-TM01. No canonical risk IDs or scores changed.

## Provenance — what triggered this change?

#17 Increment 2 and the existing upstream review schema/validator at `ab191485b48bca805ea2cc962c2ea9476a65db66`. TRQP source remains pinned by #19. Risk hypothesis provenance and evidence reasoning are retained in the example. Prepared with AI assistance; proposed treatment is not task-force acceptance, risk scoring, governance approval or independent review.

## Validation output

```text
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 41 tests passed (12 existing + 10 Increment 1 + 19 Increment 2).
TRQP replay --check: retained observations reproduce.
review/examine.py: validation complete; overall assurance review-required; four runtime evidence areas not-assessed.
Existing review validator with explicit example --risks: PASS.
Corpus validator: 0 errors / 32 retained warnings.
Temporary build: 6 site pages and 12 JSON-LD files, exit 0.
```

Negative tests cover omitted finding evidence, unresolved references/files, failed/incomplete execution, stale observations, target/method/assessment mismatch, bound-byte changes, unknown risks, missing risk reasoning, duplicate evidence/findings, contradictory results, unsafe source paths, unretained sources, invalid line anchors, malformed sidecars and unauthorized success labels. CLI failure returns nonzero with no success report. Existing review regressions remain valid.

## Acceptance evidence

- [x] Review target agrees with retained manifest.
- [x] Evidence references resolve and structurally cover each finding.
- [x] Missing evidence and execution failure cannot become assurance success.
- [x] Local hypotheses distinguished from canonical corpus records.
- [x] Existing review records and tests remain compatible.
- [x] Authority, delegation and revocation remain explicitly unassessed.
- [x] Walkthrough, sidecar relationship, limitations and design choice documented.
- [x] Contributor DCO certification and passing current-head DCO check for every commit.
- [ ] Independent review and maintainer acceptance.

The contributor explicitly authorized matching DCO sign-offs on both increment commits. Current head `06208687de30f742d6a3c3b6a3f8536176e5d16c` passes GitHub DCO; its parent is the certified Increment 1 commit `ea150587f431fb320ca2412601af9f8bf96d6b47`. Both file trees and author identities are unchanged, so prior execution evidence remains applicable. No automatic merge enabled; no release proposed.

title: feat(pnm): rooms owner register/invite/issue-* and rooms keys verbs — a sealed room from the CLI end to end
body:
`docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` said "no `pnm` verb reaches these yet" for the owner's credential tasks, and the joiner's key-holder tasks had no verbs either, so a sealed room could not be run on a VTC from the CLI. This adds them, following #2088.

**Merge order:** this is meant to merge together with, or after, the persona-identity change (`feat/rooms-persona-identity`). Under that change, every room party is a **persona DID**: a DID the member's VTA holds for them, never the CLI session's `did:key`. The help text, the error hints and the docs here are written for that model. No verb here defaults a party to the session DID. This branch is rebased onto #2090 (`owner group-remove`), and that verb's `--member` help now calls it a persona DID too.

### Verbs → tasks

| Verb | Task |
|---|---|
| `pnm rooms owner register --room --host-did --owner --visibility [--retention-days] [--retention-policy]` | `rooms/owner/register/0.1` (the VTA signs `rooms/create` as `--owner`) |
| `pnm rooms owner invite --room --signing-key --subject [--valid-until\|--valid-for] --out` | `rooms/owner/invite/0.1` |
| `pnm rooms owner issue-membership --room --signing-key --subject [--valid-until\|--valid-for] [--out] [--store]` | `rooms/owner/issue-membership/0.1` |
| `pnm rooms owner issue-authority --room --signing-key --subject --action … (--valid-until\|--valid-for) [--out] [--store]` | `rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.2` |
| `pnm rooms keys key-package --room --invitation --out` | `rooms/keys/key-package/0.1` |
| `pnm rooms keys welcome --room --invitation --welcome` | `rooms/keys/welcome/0.1` |
| `pnm rooms keys commit --room (--commit <file> --epoch <n> \| --host <url> [--host-did])` | `rooms/keys/commit/0.1` (+ host `rooms/epoch/commits` with `--host`) |
| `pnm rooms keys list` | `rooms/keys/list/0.1` |

- **Typed SDK helpers** on `VtaClient`: `room_owner_register`, `room_owner_invite`, `room_owner_issue_membership`, `room_owner_issue_authority`, `room_key_package`, `room_welcome`, `room_commit` and `room_keys_list`. Each builds its payload through the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs` builder and reads the reply through the generated `Response`. There are no hand-written payload structs.
- **Retry safety:** every task was already classified in `vta_sdk::retry_safety`. The `Keyed` ones (invite, the two issue tasks, key-package, welcome) run inside `VtaClient::idempotent`.
- **`vtc-client`:** gains `epoch_commits` (`rooms/epoch/commits`). `pnm rooms keys commit --host` uses it to fetch every commit this VTA lacks and apply them in order.
- **Epoch numbering:** `rooms/keys/{welcome,commit}` speak MLS epochs, as their specification says. The owner tasks, `keys/list` and the host speak room epochs, which are one higher. The CLI converts, so every number it prints or takes is a room epoch.
- **`owner group-create --member` is now required.** Before, it defaulted to the session DID.
- **`pnm rooms create`** is marked as the client-key path, for a standalone `room-host` or for testing. Its help points VTC users at `owner register`, and it notes that a VTC needs the `/v1` mount and `--host-did`.
- **Fixed a stale `pnm rooms put` doc comment.** It said "open rooms only", but `put` seals on `attributed`/`private`.
- **Updated `data-rooms.md`:** §2, §5.2, §5.3, §5.4, §6, the commits section, §9 and the reference table now use the verbs. `issue-authority` is listed as 0.2.

### Checks run locally (after the rebase onto #2090)
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` ✅
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --no-default-features --features rest --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` ✅ 5783 passed
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc` ✅
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` ✅ 3105 passed
- `cargo deny --all-features check` ✅

`Cargo.lock` is unchanged.

title: fix(messaging): drop a #response no waiter took instead of answering it (#1949)
body:
Fixes the VTC half of #1949.

## What

A Trust Task reply that no waiter takes is now dropped instead of being dispatched as a request:

- `vta_sdk::inbound::names_a_reply(&Value)`: a document is a reply by its **type**, either `…#response` or a trust-task error. Threading alone isn't enough, because `approve-response` and `task-consent/decision` thread but are requests (`Inbound::Response` stays a shape, not a verdict).
- **VTC, DIDComm** (`messaging::dispatch`): after the waiter check fails, an enveloped reply is logged at `debug` and dropped. The TSP path already did this (`tsp_reply_document`).
- **VTA** (`accept_from_proven_sender`, both transports): the same rule. It had the same gap: a `#response` with no waiter fell through to dispatch and got an error back.

## Why

Per the issue's diagnosis, affinidi-messaging-sdk reconnects the websocket at 80% of the token TTL and fails pending requests. The mediator's `message/status` reply then has no waiter. The VTC routed it as a request, answered `422 unsupportedType`, and the mediator refused to deliver that (`e.p.delivery.refused`). The result was a warning pair every 12 minutes.

## Not here

The lost waiter itself (`fail_pending_requests()` on reconnect) is in affinidi-messaging-sdk and needs fixing there. This change stops the VTI side from turning a late reply into an error exchange. Deliveries were never lost, as the issue notes.

## Tests

- `vta-sdk`: `a_reply_is_named_by_its_type_not_its_threading`
- `vtc-service`: `an_enveloped_reply_with_no_waiter_is_dropped_not_answered` (through `dispatch`)
- `vta-service`: `a_response_with_no_waiter_is_dropped_not_answered` (through `accept_from_proven_sender`)
- Workspace clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` and fmt are clean.

fix(messaging): drop a `#response` no waiter took instead of answering it (#1949) (#2095)

A reply that outlives its waiter (the messaging SDK fails pending requests
when it reconnects at 80% of the token TTL, every 12 minutes for a 15-minute
token) reached the VTC's DIDComm dispatcher as an ordinary request. The spine
answered the `#response` with `unsupportedType`, the mediator refused to
deliver that, and the pair repeated in the log every 12 minutes.

`vta_sdk::inbound::names_a_reply` names a reply by its type (`…#response` or
a trust-task error), unlike threading, which an `approve-response` request
also has. The VTC's DIDComm path and the VTA's proven-sender path now drop
such a document when no waiter takes it; the VTC's TSP path already did. The
lost waiter itself is the messaging SDK's and is unchanged here.

title: feat(vta)!: data rooms act as the member's persona DID, never the client's
body:
In a data room a member is one DID: the invitation's subject, the identity on
their MLS leaf, the subject of their VMC/VAC, the owner a host records, and the
signer of every leaf their VTA narrows. That DID is now always a **persona** —
a DID this VTA holds for the person in one of their trust contexts — and never
the did:key of the interface client (pnm session, wallet extension, agent)
that happens to be calling.

One resolver, `operations::persona::persona_signing_key`, generalised from
`room_host::owner_signing_key`, decides "a persona the caller may act as, and
the key it signs with":

- a did:webvh this VTA minted (webvh builds only): the caller acts in the
  DID's context (`has_context_access`, act_scope-based); the key is the first
  `assertionMethod` entry under the DID in its own published log whose public
  key is an active Ed25519 record of that same context;
- a did:key: an active Ed25519 record with that key, in a context the caller
  acts in (super-admin for a context-less record).

Anything else is `None`, indistinguishably for unknown DIDs and DIDs held in
another context, so no refusal says whose personas live here. The VTA's own
DID is not a persona (it is shared by every principal and would link their
rooms); `rooms/owner/register` keeps accepting it as `ownerDid`, there only.

Changes:

- rooms/keys/{key-package,welcome}: the invitation's subject must be a persona
  the caller may act as, replacing subject == caller DID. The KeyPackage's leaf
  identifies that persona (it carried the caller's DID). Room issuer, proof,
  window and single use are unchanged; consumption stays keyed on the
  invitation id.
- rooms/keys/present (room_oracle): credentials are selected by issuer ==
  roomId **and** subject == a persona the caller may act as — a context-less
  vault row naming another context's persona is no longer presentable. One
  persona or a Conflict; the VMC must name the same persona. The leaf is signed
  as the persona through the gated oracle (`keys::sign_payload`,
  ProtocolDefined) instead of `holder_keys::resolve_holder_keys`, so did:webvh
  personas work and no key is derived outside key custody.
  `resolve_holder_keys` is unchanged for its credential-exchange callers. The
  leaf is still granted to the caller, as the spec's Presenter binding requires.
- rooms/owner/group/create: `member` must be a persona the caller may act as;
  absent, it is the persona the room's credentials name, else the caller only
  if it is itself a held persona, else a refusal asking for `member` — never
  the client DID.
- rooms/owner/group/{add,remove}: rooms/epoch/mint and rooms/info are signed
  as the owner persona, presenting an `admin` leaf the persona narrowed to
  itself, instead of as the VTA's own DID ("speaks to the host as its
  principal"). The owner persona is resolved before anything is settled or
  built; without one the answer is `noAuthority`. `member` is the joiner's /
  departing member's persona.

Breaking: `room_invitation::verify` takes a subject predicate instead of an
expected subject; `room_host::{OwnerKey, OwnerKeyStores}` are aliases of
`persona::{PersonaKey, PersonaStores}`. An invitation naming a client did:key,
or presentation credentials naming a DID the VTA holds no key for, are now
refused.

Docs: docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md states the identity model (§5) and updates
§5.2–§7, §10.3, §11 and the reference tables.



## Spec check

title: feat(vta)!: data rooms act as the member's persona DID, never the client's (#2094)
body:
feat(vta)!: data rooms act as the member's persona DID, never the client's (#2094)

In a data room a member is one DID: the invitation's subject, the identity on
their MLS leaf, the subject of their VMC/VAC, the owner a host records, and the
signer of every leaf their VTA narrows. That DID is now always a **persona** —
a DID this VTA holds for the person in one of their trust contexts — and never
the did:key of the interface client (pnm session, wallet extension, agent)
that happens to be calling.

One resolver, `operations::persona::persona_signing_key`, generalised from
`room_host::owner_signing_key`, decides "a persona the caller may act as, and
the key it signs with":

- a did:webvh this VTA minted (webvh builds only): the caller acts in the
  DID's context (`has_context_access`, act_scope-based); the key is the first
  `assertionMethod` entry under the DID in its own published log whose public
  key is an active Ed25519 record of that same context;
- a did:key: an active Ed25519 record with that key, in a context the caller
  acts in (super-admin for a context-less record).

Anything else is `None`, indistinguishably for unknown DIDs and DIDs held in
another context, so no refusal says whose personas live here. The VTA's own
DID is not a persona (it is shared by every principal and would link their
rooms); `rooms/owner/register` keeps accepting it as `ownerDid`, there only.

Changes:

- rooms/keys/{key-package,welcome}: the invitation's subject must be a persona
  the caller may act as, replacing subject == caller DID. The KeyPackage's leaf
  identifies that persona (it carried the caller's DID). Room issuer, proof,
  window and single use are unchanged; consumption stays keyed on the
  invitation id.
- rooms/keys/present (room_oracle): credentials are selected by issuer ==
  roomId **and** subject == a persona the caller may act as — a context-less
  vault row naming another context's persona is no longer presentable. One
  persona or a Conflict; the VMC must name the same persona. The leaf is signed
  as the persona through the gated oracle (`keys::sign_payload`,
  ProtocolDefined) instead of `holder_keys::resolve_holder_keys`, so did:webvh
  personas work and no key is derived outside key custody.
  `resolve_holder_keys` is unchanged for its credential-exchange callers. The
  leaf is still granted to the caller, as the spec's Presenter binding requires.
- rooms/owner/group/create: `member` must be a persona the caller may act as;
  absent, it is the persona the room's credentials name, else the caller only
  if it is itself a held persona, else a refusal asking for `member` — never
  the client DID.
- rooms/owner/group/{add,remove}: rooms/epoch/mint and rooms/info are signed
  as the owner persona, presenting an `admin` leaf the persona narrowed to
  itself, instead of as the VTA's own DID ("speaks to the host as its
  principal"). The owner persona is resolved before anything is settled or
  built; without one the answer is `noAuthority`. `member` is the joiner's /
  departing member's persona.

Breaking: `room_invitation::verify` takes a subject predicate instead of an
expected subject; `room_host::{OwnerKey, OwnerKeyStores}` are aliases of
`persona::{PersonaKey, PersonaStores}`. An invitation naming a client did:key,
or presentation credentials naming a DID the VTA holds no key for, are now
refused.

Docs: docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md states the identity model (§5) and updates
§5.2–§7, §10.3, §11 and the reference tables.
