title: feat(vtc): room usage, room detail and limit overrides — vtc/rooms/{get,usage,limits/set} and rooms/usage (#2077)
body:
feat(vtc): room usage, room detail and limit overrides — vtc/rooms/{get,usage,limits/set} and rooms/usage (#2077)

P9 part 2 (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §6.2–6.3, §8.1): the host
tasks the console's room detail and Usage pages read, over the history and
overrides #2073 put in vti-rooms.

vtc/rooms/get (vtc.rooms.admin): one room's host record, assigned config and
every earlier config still holding its blobs, effective limits with each scope's
source and the host ceiling, usage and orphans, the ten largest blobs by size
only, and on rooms that are not private a count of members with files — never
their DIDs (item 5).

vtc/rooms/usage (vtc.rooms.admin): rows grouped by room, member, storage config
or day, filtered by room, member, config and an inclusive date range (default
the last 30 days; invalidRange past 400 days, inverted, or before the oldest
kept day), sorted, and paged by a cursor bound to its query (invalidCursor
otherwise). Member figures only on rooms that are not private
(memberUsageUnavailable when one is named). Activity by config is attributed to
each room's current assignment.

vtc/rooms/limits/set (vtc.rooms.admin): an override for the room, its members by
default, or one member; refuses aboveCeiling, memberLimitsUnavailable and
invalidCombination as declared, answers the effective limits, the target scope's
usage and overLimit, and is audited (new RoomLimitsChanged event: room, target,
previous, current, reason). Not parked, as the specification says: an allowance
is reversible and loses nothing.

rooms/usage (the room owner's read, an admin chain) on both hosts, through
vti_rooms::blob_tasks::usage: one entry per member holding storage or an
override, paged; notAvailable on a private room.

vtc/rooms/list moves to vtc.rooms.admin, as §6.2 says it should: a community can
hand room hosting to someone who is not a full administrator.

Both censuses carry the new tasks: conformance witnesses for the three, and
error-code witnesses for every code they declare.

title: fix(vtc): a relative data_dir no longer stops the VTC at first start
body:
## Symptom
Starting a fresh VTC whose `[store] data_dir` is relative fails:
```
ERROR vtc: server error: internal error: storage config does not conform: data did not match any variant of untagged enum StorageSettings
```

## Cause
On first start, `open_room_storage` seeds a `local` storage config with `root = [rooms.files] blob_dir`, which defaults to `<data_dir>/room-blobs`. With a relative `data_dir`, that root is relative. The spec's `LocalSettings.root` is `pattern: "^/"`, so the seed's own `checked()` conformance check refuses it and startup stops.

Explicit `local_storage_bases` were already required to be absolute, so they passed. The default bases (`<data_dir>/room-storage`) would have been refused too, with a clearer config error.

## Fix
`absolute_dir` handles the paths the VTC derives, or that are given relative: `blob_dir` and the default bases. It creates each beneath the working directory the store is opened from, and canonicalises it, so no `.` or `..` remains.

Absolute paths are unchanged, so a stored `local` root still compares equal. Explicit bases keep their absolute-only rule.

## Tests
- `storage_opens_over_a_relative_data_dir` is end to end. It reproduces the reported error with the fix stubbed out, and passes with it.
- Unit tests check that a relative path is resolved and normalised, and an absolute one kept.
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

On first start the VTC seeds a `local` storage config whose root is
`[rooms.files] blob_dir`, defaulting to `<data_dir>/room-blobs`. With a relative
`[store] data_dir` that root was relative, the spec's StorageConfig requires an
absolute one (`root` pattern `^/`), and the seed's own conformance check refused
it:

  server error: internal error: storage config does not conform: data did not
  match any variant of untagged enum StorageSettings

A relative blob_dir, or a root or default local_storage_bases derived from a
relative data_dir, is now created beneath the working directory the store is
opened from and resolved to an absolute path. Absolute paths are unchanged, and
explicit local_storage_bases must still be absolute, as documented.

title: feat(join)!: present a credential from a swiyu or EUDI wallet while joining
body:
A community whose join criterion asks for an SD-JWT VC (`dc+sd-jwt`) can be
answered by a digital-identity wallet over OpenID4VP, through the VTC's
`vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/{start,status}/0.1` (VTI #1988). Nothing in
the client opened such a session, so the VTC's verifier had no way in.

The join now offers it, after the trust-registry question and before the
request goes out:

- **Offer.** When the manifest has a criterion a wallet can answer, the join
  presents an existing persona, and that persona has no vetting application,
  the wallet page says what the community asks for. Enter opens a session;
  `s` goes on without it.
- **Session.** The persona signs `start`. The page shows the `walletUri` as a
  QR code and as a link, and says when the wallet has fetched the request. The
  runtime loop polls `status` on its sweep tick and owns the wait, as it does
  for a hidden-vetting challenge.
- **Submit.** On `presented`, the launch resumes and the submit names that
  criterion, under which the community counts the evidence it holds. A
  refused, expired or unanswered session returns to the offer with the reason;
  Esc stops waiting.

The wallet answers the community directly; nothing it presents passes through
this client.

Breaking for openvtc-core:
- `CommunityCriterion` gains `wallet`, `wallet_types` and `description`
  (`vetting::book::wallet_query` reads them from the criterion's DCQL).
- `QueryKind` gains `WalletSessionStart` and `WalletSessionStatus`.
- `CommunityAnswer` gains `WalletSessionStarted` and `WalletSessionStatus`.
- `vetting::wire` gains the two request builders, and `vetting::queries`
  re-exports the generated `wallet_session` types.

A new persona cannot open a session: it does not exist until the request goes
out, and the evidence is bound to the applicant who opened the session.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: feat(rooms)!: daily usage history, member index and limit overrides for room files
body:
This is P9, part 1 of 3: the host-side data behind the admin console's room detail and Usage pages (`docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md` §6.2–6.3). It lives in `vti-rooms`, so the VTC and the standalone `room-host` count usage the same way.

The specs (`vtc/rooms/get`, `vtc/rooms/usage`, `vtc/rooms/limits/set`, `rooms/usage`) are already in `trust-tasks-rs` 0.31, so no spec change is needed. The handlers come in part 2.

## What this adds
- **Daily history** (`daily:` / `mdaily:` rows in `room_blobs`):
  - One row per room per UTC day. Rooms that are not `private` also get one row per member per room per day.
  - Each row holds the day's closing files and bytes, plus uploads, downloads and egress bytes for that day.
  - Activity is counted under its own lock, so serving a chunk never waits behind a commit.
  - The cleanup pass (`sweep`) writes a row for quiet days, prunes rows older than 400 days, and on its first run indexes files stored before this change.
- **Limit overrides**:
  - An override can target the room, its members by default, or one named member, and it replaces that scope's limits whole.
  - Both upload checks enforce it.
  - An override above the host's file-size ceiling is refused, never clamped. Member scopes on a `private` room are refused.
  - Clearing a room's limits keeps a "files off" override in place.
- **Reads**:
  - `effective_limits`, which now also says where each scope's limits came from.
  - `member_limits` and `members_with_usage`.
  - `room_days` and `member_days`; a quiet day carries the previous day's totals.
  - `room_activity` and `member_activity`.
  - `oldest_retained_day` and `rooms_with_files`.
  - `room_blobs_summary`: holdings per storage config, orphans, and largest blobs by size only.
- **Design note §6.3** is updated to the layout as built.

## Breaking change

title: feat(rooms)!: daily usage history, member index and limit overrides for room files (#2073)
body:
feat(rooms)!: daily usage history, member index and limit overrides for room files (#2073)

The host-side data the console's room detail and Usage pages read
(docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §6.2–6.3, phase P9), in vti-rooms so
a community and a standalone room host count the same way.

History: one row per room per UTC day, and one per member per room per day on
rooms that are not private, holding the day's closing files and bytes and its
uploads committed, downloads begun and chunk bytes served (egress, which is
what a cloud bills). Activity is counted as it happens under its own lock, so a
chunk served never waits behind a commit writing to a store. The collection
pass writes today's row for every room and member that has one, drops rows
older than 400 days (vtc/rooms/usage item 7), and on first run indexes the
rooms and members a host charged before the index existed — the usage counters
key members only by hash.

Overrides (vtc/rooms/limits/set): the room, its per-member default, or one
named member, each replacing its scope wholesale. Both upload checks enforce
them: begin, under the upload lock, so an override applies to the next begin
after it and reserved uploads complete under their old limits (item 5), and
re-referencing an orphaned blob. A maxFileBytes above the host ceiling is
refused, never clamped (item 4); member scopes on a private room are refused
(item 3). Clearing a room's limits leaves a filesEnabled override in place:
turning files back on is its own decision.

Reads: effective_limits (now async, with each scope's source and the host
ceiling), member_limits, members_with_usage (rooms/usage item 3: holders and
overridden members only, never a roster), room_days / member_days with quiet
days carried, room_activity, oldest_retained_day, rooms_with_files and
room_blobs_summary (holdings per config, orphans, largest blobs by size only).

BREAKING CHANGE: BlobHost::effective_limits is async and EffectiveLimits gains
room_source, member_source and host_ceiling_bytes (now #[non_exhaustive]).
BlobHost::open_download takes the room and the reader's member, and
blob_tasks::get takes the AuthorizedAction, so a download counts under the
member it is charged to. Both hosts are updated.

title: fix: a seated vetter can hand out tickets before its membership credential lands
body:
## Problem

On openvtc main (9e274b1) with one mediator, after a vetter is seated ("You vet for … until …"), pressing `t` still answers "You can hand out tickets once a community you belong to has named you a vetter". The same flow worked with 9b493e2 + vta-sdk 0.61.

## What the code shows

`git diff 9b493e2..9e274b1` doesn't change the check. The ticket form's list is built in `sync()` (`vetting_actions.rs:148`), which keeps a membership only if it is **Active** and has a live vetter grant. The "You vet for" row looks only at the stored grant, and `inbound::vetter_grant` stores a grant for a membership of any status. So both messages appear together exactly when the membership exists, is not Active, and has a live grant: in practice, an approved join whose membership credential hasn't arrived (`approved_awaiting_credential`, added in #406/#411).

## Why draft

- **The cause is inferred, not confirmed.** To check it, look at the vetter's row in the Communities panel. "✓ approved — membership credential not received yet" or Pending would confirm it; Active would rule it out.
- **This may be a symptom of VTI-61 (#415).** If the vetter's membership credential is lost on the way in over TSP (#413 moved member traffic to TSP after a TSP join), the membership stays Pending. #415 would then remove the cause, and this PR becomes a stricter-vs-looser UX choice rather than a bug fix. Worth retesting the `t` flow on #415 first.

## Change

The `sync()` filter becomes `m.status.is_active() || m.approved_awaiting_credential()`. The live-grant requirement stays. The community decides who can vet, and it has already approved and seated this persona.

## Tests

- New test `a_seated_vetter_can_hand_out_tickets` covers four cases: Active with a grant (listed); approved and awaiting the credential, with a grant (listed, and fails before the fix); Pending and never approved, with a grant (not listed); Active with no grant (not listed).
- `cargo test -p openvtc --bin openvtc`: 784 passed. `cargo fmt --check` is clean. The `openvtc-core` and end-to-end tests have not been run.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] R1.2 / R1.3 / R1.4 / R1.5 / R1.6: n/a, local UI gate only
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1): n/a
- [x] Wire types (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): still requires a live grant from the community
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] Deviations: none

title: feat(vetting)!: hidden vetting runs on the VTA — no PCS key on the device
body:
Hidden vetting now runs on the person's VTA (`vta/pcs/*`, vta-service 0.60 / vta-sdk 0.68, VTI #2056). The device no longer holds a PCS key: the VTA holds every applicant and vetter key and builds every enrolment request, token draw, attestation and proof. OpenVTC carries what the VTA builds to the community and the other member.

Two commits:
1. `chore(deps)!` moves to vta-sdk 0.68, trust-tasks 0.31, affinidi-tdk 0.26, messaging-sdk 0.36, did-git-sign / vgi-core 0.20, test-mediator 0.22, and the vta-service 0.60 dev-dep.
2. `feat(vetting)!` makes the switch.

### What changed
- **Adapter:** `openvtc_core::vetting::pcs_vta` builds requests through the generated `vta/pcs` types. It reads each reply document, so a refusal arrives as its declared code.
- **Off the UI loop:** VTA calls run in their own dispatch domain (`HiddenVetting`). Each outcome returns to the loop, which records it and sends the community whatever the VTA built.
- **Survives restarts:** inbound answers wait in a persisted queue (`pcs_inbox`) until the VTA has taken them in.
- **Restart races handled:**
  - A stale draw the VTA still holds is dropped before its tick is asked for again.
  - An enrolment the VTA holds is waited on for up to an hour, not replaced. Replacing it would leave the community's answer unopenable.
- **Spec fix:** the vetter's attestation now has the `vetting/attestation/0.1` shape the spec states.
- **Removed:** the `openvtc-vetting-pcs` crate (now VTI's `vti-vetting-pcs`) and the `zkp_reference_flow` example.

### Upgrade: hard cut-over
- Locally held PCS state (an application's `hidden_state`, a vetter's snapshot and enrolment blinding) is read and then dropped on load.
- Vetters re-enrol under a key the VTA holds. A community that still knows the old key refuses with `identifierRebound`, so its admins must let the vetter re-enrol.
- In-progress applications restart their hidden vetting.
- Each case gets one notice on the Vetting page.

### Tests
- New end-to-end test `openvtc-core/tests/hidden_vetting_onboarding.rs` runs the whole flow through OpenVTC's own VTA calls, against an in-process VTA and VTI's community verifier: two vetters enrol and draw tokens, both attest, the applicant proves, and the community admits.
- Local results: fmt and clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored` green.

### Dependencies
did-git-sign / vgi-core 0.20.0 (OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#156) and trql-client 0.25.0 (affinidi-trust-registry-rs#152) are published, and `Cargo.lock` is locked to them. `cargo tree -d` shows one vta-sdk, trust-tasks-rs, affinidi-tdk and messaging-sdk.

Two commits plus the lockfile commit.

body:
Bumps the npm-production group with 1 update: [spec-up-t](https://github.com/trustoverip/spec-up-t). Updates `spec-up-t` from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0
Release notes

Sourced from spec-up-t's releases.

v2.4.0

Workflow files

custom-update no longer overwrites .github/workflows/menu.yml, render-and-deploy.yml, or zenodo-update.yml when they differ from the boilerplate. The plan lists those files as keep.

Missing known workflows are still added. Extra workflows stay. Stale files such as set-gh-pages.yml are still removed.

To replace the known workflows with the current boilerplate, run this locally and commit:

npx spec-up-t@latest custom-update --force-workflows

The GitHubUi Custom Update button does not pass --force-workflows. GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push changes under .github/workflows/.

Plan colors

On a terminal, the custom-update plan is colorized (add green, remove red, keep magenta, and so on). CI and piped logs stay plain.

v2.3.1

Fixes

custom-update no longer adds a bare .env* gitignore rule. That pattern also matches .env.example, and git keeps the last matching rule, so it could ignore the template Spec-Up-T ships.

Boilerplate and custom-update now use:

.env .env.* !.env.example

On custom-update, an existing .env* line is removed. If !.env.example sits above a later .env.*, it is moved below it.

Install is unchanged.

title: npm(deps): bump spec-up-t from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0 in the npm-production group
body:
Bumps the npm-production group with 1 update: [spec-up-t](https://github.com/trustoverip/spec-up-t). Updates `spec-up-t` from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0
Release notes

Sourced from spec-up-t's releases.

v2.4.0

Workflow files

custom-update no longer overwrites .github/workflows/menu.yml, render-and-deploy.yml, or zenodo-update.yml when they differ from the boilerplate. The plan lists those files as keep.

Missing known workflows are still added. Extra workflows stay. Stale files such as set-gh-pages.yml are still removed.

To replace the known workflows with the current boilerplate, run this locally and commit:

npx spec-up-t@latest custom-update --force-workflows

The GitHubUi Custom Update button does not pass --force-workflows. GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push changes under .github/workflows/.

Plan colors

On a terminal, the custom-update plan is colorized (add green, remove red, keep magenta, and so on). CI and piped logs stay plain.

v2.3.1

Fixes

custom-update no longer adds a bare .env* gitignore rule. That pattern also matches .env.example, and git keeps the last matching rule, so it could ignore the template Spec-Up-T ships.

Boilerplate and custom-update now use:

.env .env.* !.env.example

On custom-update, an existing .env* line is removed. If !.env.example sits above a later .env.*, it is moved below it.

Install is unchanged.

title: Sync tooling with toip-template: spec-up-t 2.4.0 and katex override
body:
Copies `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and the two shared workflows from trustoverip/toip-template at #22 so this repo's tooling files are byte-identical to the template again. This lands in one commit what Dependabot has open here as two PRs (spec-up-t 2.3.0 to 2.4.0 and actions/setup-node 7.0.0 to 7.1.0), plus the override changes from the template. Those Dependabot PRs can be closed once this merges.

Dependabot's security job fails on the template because katex is stuck at 0.16.47. GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 (prototype pollution, low severity) is fixed in 0.18.2, but spec-up-t 2.4.0 pins `katex@^0.16.47` and its `@traptitech/markdown-it-katex@3.6.0` pins `^0.16.0`, so Dependabot has no update path. The npm override to `^0.18.2` forces the patched line until spec-up-t moves its own pin.

The `puppeteer: ^25.9.0` override was added while this repo was on spec-up-t 1.9.0, which declared puppeteer `^23`. Every spec-up-t release from 2.0.0 declares `^25.9.0` itself, so the override no longer changes resolution and is removed. The lockfile resolves puppeteer 25.10.0 either way.

**Changes**

| Package or action | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| spec-up-t | 2.3.0 | 2.4.0 |
| katex | 0.16.47 | 0.18.10 |
| commander (katex's CLI dependency) | 8.3.0 | 15.0.0 |
| brace-expansion | 5.0.9 | 5.0.12 |
| actions/setup-node | 7.0.0 | 7.1.0 |

**Verification, in a `node:20-bookworm` container against this repo's spec content**

- `npm ci` from the new lockfile succeeds.
- `npm run render` writes `docs/index.html` without errors.
- commander 15 declares Node >= 22.12, but it is only required by katex's `cli.js`, which spec-up-t never calls. spec-up-t 2.4.0 and puppeteer already print the same engine warning on Node 20, so nothing new.

**Not addressed**

The braces alert (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) has no patched release. The Dependabot security job will keep failing on it wherever it is open until it is dismissed or a fix ships.

Sync tooling with toip-template: spec-up-t 2.4.0 and katex override (#65)

Copy package.json, package-lock.json, and the two shared workflows from
trustoverip/toip-template at #22 so this repo's tooling files are
byte-identical to the template again. This lands in one commit what
Dependabot has open as two PRs here (spec-up-t 2.3.0 -> 2.4.0 and
actions/setup-node 7.0.0 -> 7.1.0), plus the override changes from the
template.

Dependabot's security job fails on the template because katex is stuck
at 0.16.47: GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 (prototype pollution, low) is fixed in
0.18.2, but spec-up-t 2.4.0 pins katex ^0.16.47 and its
@traptitech/markdown-it-katex 3.6.0 pins ^0.16.0, so there is no update
path Dependabot can take. An npm override forces the patched line until
spec-up-t moves its own pin.

The puppeteer ^25.9.0 override was added while this repo was on
spec-up-t 1.9.0, which declared puppeteer ^23. Every spec-up-t release
from 2.0.0 declares ^25.9.0 itself, so the override no longer changes
resolution and is removed.

- package.json: spec-up-t ^2.3.0 -> ^2.4.0; replace the puppeteer
  override with katex ^0.18.2.
- package-lock.json: spec-up-t 2.3.0 -> 2.4.0, katex 0.16.47 -> 0.18.10
  with its CLI dependency commander 8.3.0 -> 15.0.0, brace-expansion
  -> 5.0.12. puppeteer stays at 25.10.0 without the override.
- .github/workflows: actions/setup-node 7.0.0 -> 7.1.0.

Three transitive packages were resolved fresher here than in the
template and move back to the template's pins to keep the lockfile
byte-identical: @types/node 26.6.3 -> 25.9.8 and undici-types 8.9.0 ->
7.24.6 are type definitions with no runtime effect, and docx 9.8.0 ->
9.7.2 is one patch step inside spec-up-t's declared range. Dependabot
lifts them again on its next production bump.

Verified in a node:20-bookworm container against this repo's spec
content: npm ci from the new lockfile succeeds and npm run render
writes docs/index.html without errors.

The braces alert (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) has no patched release and is not
addressed here.

Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk <geoff@ic3.dev>

body:
Copies `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and the two shared workflows from trustoverip/toip-template at #22 so this repo's tooling files are byte-identical to the template again. This lands in one commit what Dependabot has open here as two PRs (spec-up-t 2.3.0 to 2.4.0 and actions/setup-node 7.0.0 to 7.1.0), plus the override changes from the template. Those Dependabot PRs can be closed once this merges.

Dependabot's security job fails on the template because katex is stuck at 0.16.47. GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 (prototype pollution, low severity) is fixed in 0.18.2, but spec-up-t 2.4.0 pins `katex@^0.16.47` and its `@traptitech/markdown-it-katex@3.6.0` pins `^0.16.0`, so Dependabot has no update path. The npm override to `^0.18.2` forces the patched line until spec-up-t moves its own pin.

The `puppeteer: ^25.9.0` override was added while this repo was on spec-up-t 1.9.0, which declared puppeteer `^23`. Every spec-up-t release from 2.0.0 declares `^25.9.0` itself, so the override no longer changes resolution and is removed. The lockfile resolves puppeteer 25.10.0 either way.

**Changes**

| Package or action | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| spec-up-t | 2.3.0 | 2.4.0 |
| katex | 0.16.47 | 0.18.10 |
| commander (katex's CLI dependency) | 8.3.0 | 15.0.0 |
| brace-expansion | 5.0.9 | 5.0.12 |
| actions/setup-node | 7.0.0 | 7.1.0 |

**Verification, in a `node:20-bookworm` container against this repo's spec content**

- `npm ci` from the new lockfile succeeds.
- `npm run render` writes `docs/index.html` without errors.
- commander 15 declares Node >= 22.12, but it is only required by katex's `cli.js`, which spec-up-t never calls. spec-up-t 2.4.0 and puppeteer already print the same engine warning on Node 20, so nothing new.

**Not addressed**

The braces alert (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) has no patched release. The Dependabot security job will keep failing on it wherever it is open until it is dismissed or a fix ships.

title: feat(vtc): swiyu trust statements in verifier_info — vtc oid4vp trust-statement (#1988)
body:
Under swiyu Trust Protocol 2.0 a verifier tells the wallet who it is by
carrying the statements the trust registry issued about it in every request
object's `verifier_info`, each `{"format": "jwt", "data": <JWS>}`, the
Identity Trust Statement first (the generic test wallet reads it by position).

- `vtc oid4vp trust-statement --identity <id> --file <jwt>…` installs them on a
  swiyu identity. Each is checked first: a swiyu `typ`, `sub` equal to the
  identity's DID, not expired; one bad file installs none. A newer identity
  statement replaces the held one; protected-verification statements are told
  apart by `jti`. The wallet verifies the signature against the registry.
- A session's request object leaves out a statement that has expired, with a
  warning naming the command, rather than sending one every wallet refuses.
- `vtc oid4vp list` shows each statement's expiry, and says when a swiyu
  identity has no current identity statement.
- A Verification Query Public Statement is refused for now: it describes one
  query and pairs with `scope`, where the VTC sends each criterion's DCQL.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78
significance_reasons: Interoperability, canonicalisation, conformance, or protocol behaviour

title: npm(deps): bump spec-up-t from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0 in the npm-production group
body:
Bumps the npm-production group with 1 update: [spec-up-t](https://github.com/trustoverip/spec-up-t). Updates `spec-up-t` from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0
Release notes

Sourced from spec-up-t's releases.

v2.4.0

Workflow files

custom-update no longer overwrites .github/workflows/menu.yml, render-and-deploy.yml, or zenodo-update.yml when they differ from the boilerplate. The plan lists those files as keep.

Missing known workflows are still added. Extra workflows stay. Stale files such as set-gh-pages.yml are still removed.

To replace the known workflows with the current boilerplate, run this locally and commit:

npx spec-up-t@latest custom-update --force-workflows

The GitHubUi Custom Update button does not pass --force-workflows. GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push changes under .github/workflows/.

Plan colors

On a terminal, the custom-update plan is colorized (add green, remove red, keep magenta, and so on). CI and piped logs stay plain.

v2.3.1

Fixes

custom-update no longer adds a bare .env* gitignore rule. That pattern also matches .env.example, and git keeps the last matching rule, so it could ignore the template Spec-Up-T ships.

Boilerplate and custom-update now use:

.env .env.* !.env.example

On custom-update, an existing .env* line is removed. If !.env.example sits above a later .env.*, it is moved below it.

Install is unchanged.

title: feat(rooms): put and get room files from the console
body:
The console pane for room files, on top of #327's offscreen engine.

**What changes**
- `manager/panes/rooms-files.tsx` (new): `PutRoomFile`, `GetRoomFile`, `RoomFilesUnavailable`.
- `rooms-records.tsx`:
  - Listing a room's records also calls `prepareRoomFiles(host)`.
  - A put section sits under the listing.
  - An opened record that carries a file shows a download, with the raw record folded beneath it.
- `manager/room-files.ts`: pure helpers `roomFileClaimOf`, `describeProgress` and `formatBytes`, with tests.

**Rules this keeps**
- **Gesture first.** Each click handler's first statement is `askForHost(prepared)`, which calls `requestOriginPermission(endpoint)` when the host is not yet granted. The endpoint is resolved at listing time, so nothing is awaited before that call.
- **A claim is not a verified file.**
  - The name and size shown before a download come from a body the console cannot verify, and they are labelled as the record's own account.
  - After a download, the pane shows what the offscreen document verified, including the signing author.
  - The saved file is named by `safeFileName` and typed `application/octet-stream`.
- **The key stays offscreen.**
  - The pane imports only `manager/room-files.ts`, never `@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms/files`.
  - The CI guard passes on this build.
- **Size limit.** Files over 64 MiB are refused before anything is sent, with a pointer to `pnm rooms file put`.

**Verified locally**
- `npm run lint` passes.
- Extension tests: 1,081 pass (3 new).
- `npm run build` and `scripts/package.mjs` succeed.
- All 12 CI `Assert …` guards pass against the build.

**Not yet exercised against a live community.** The first real transfer is what will check these:
- the VTC accepting a room request signed by the wallet's `did:peer`;
- the host's CORS under the just-in-time permission;
- wasm under the extension's CSP.

The records view of a room now moves files. Listing a room's records also
learns the host's endpoint (`prepareRoomFiles`), so that a click on "Put the
file" or "Download the file" can ask for the host's origin as its first act,
before anything is awaited and the gesture spent.

An opened record whose body carries a file manifest is offered as a file. Its
name, size and type are shown as the record's own account: the console cannot

is saved only after the offscreen document reports that every byte matched the
digest its author signed, under a name `safeFileName` has made safe, as
`application/octet-stream` whatever type the author claimed.

title: feat(rooms): room files in the offscreen document — the file key never leaves it
body:
P7a, step 2 of 3: the engine and the bridge for data-room files. The console pane that uses them comes next.

## What lands

**Core (`@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms/files`)**
- `putRoomFile` / `getRoomFile` follow the same steps as `pnm rooms file put` / `get` (`vta-cli-common::commands::rooms`), so a file written by either one opens in the other.
- The wasm cipher (`@openvtc/vti-rooms-wasm` 0.1.0) is passed in, so core carries no wasm.
- `RoomHostChannel`: HTTPS to the host's `TrustTaskHTTPS` endpoint, signed by the caller, with no bearer token. It accepts only `https:` and public addresses, refuses redirects, and accepts a reply only if the host signed it and it is threaded to the request.
- Files are capped at 64 MiB, because the whole file is sealed before the first chunk is uploaded. `pnm rooms file put` handles larger files.

**Extension**
- `room-files-offscreen.ts` serves `ROOM_FILES_PORT`. The wasm loads on the first transfer, as its own chunk.
- `manager/room-files.ts` is the console's end. A download's pieces become a `Blob` only after the file is verified; otherwise they are dropped.
- `RUNTIME_ROOM_FILES_PREPARE` resolves the host's endpoint and checks whether the wallet has a host permission for it. The pane requests the permission in the click.
- The service worker drops its end of each transfer port immediately, so the console sees when the offscreen document goes away.

**CI guard and CLAUDE.md**
- `rooms/keys/file-key/0.1` may appear only in the offscreen entry chunk. It is banned from `manager.js` too, and the guard also checks that it is still present in the offscreen chunk.
- CLAUDE.md's "Key material never reaches a browser" section now covers this one exception. The rooms section explains why files go to the host directly and records do not.

## Verified locally
- `npm run lint` and `npm test` across all workspaces pass: core 981 tests (2 skipped), extension 1,078, plus the other packages.
- 18 new engine tests run against the real published wasm with an in-memory VTA and host:
  - a round trip across three chunks
  - a write that loses the version race and is re-sealed
  - a host that commits the wrong blob, alters a chunk, or serves another file's blob
  - a body signed by someone other than the recorded author
  - an aborted upload releasing what `begin` reserved
  - refusals that happen before any file key is requested
- 13 tests cover the port boundary.
- Every CI `Assert` step was run against a local build and passed. The new guard was also checked negatively: planting the URI in `manager.js` trips it.

## Still needs a live check (not covered locally)
- A VTC accepting a room request signed by the wallet's `did:peer` holder.
- The host origin's CORS under a just-in-time permission. The extension now ships wasm; MV3's default CSP should allow `wasm-unsafe-eval`, but the first live transfer will confirm it.

title: feat(rooms): room files in the offscreen document — the file key never leaves it (#327)
body:
feat(rooms): room files in the offscreen document — the file key never leaves it (#327)

The wallet can now put a file in a data room and get one out, end to end, with
the same steps as `pnm rooms file put` / `get`, so a file either writes opens in
the other. The console pane that drives it is the next change; this one is the
engine, the bridge, and the rule that keeps a file's key in one place.

Core (`@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms/files`):
- `putRoomFile` / `getRoomFile`: presentations and the file key from the
  member's VTA; sealing and opening with `@openvtc/vti-rooms-wasm` (passed in,
  so core carries no wasm); upload begin / chunks / commit, aborting what
  `begin` reserved on failure; the signed record body sealed through the VTA and
  re-sealed for the version the host actually assigned (four attempts, as the
  CLI); on the way back, the body verified, the record checked to still name the
  blob, every chunk checked against the manifest, and the plaintext released
  only once it hashes to the author's digest.
- `RoomHostChannel`: HTTPS to the host's `TrustTaskHTTPS` endpoint, signed by
  the caller, no bearer, `https:` and public addresses only, and the reply
  believed only once signed by the host and threaded to the request.
- `roomsHeadVersion`, and a 64 MiB in-memory ceiling (`ROOM_FILE_MAX_BYTES`):
  the blob manifest must exist before an upload begins, so a file is sealed
  whole before its first chunk moves.

Extension:
- `room-files-offscreen.ts` runs a transfer over `ROOM_FILES_PORT`; the cipher
  is loaded on the first transfer, as its own chunk. The console sends intents
  and bytes and gets progress and plaintext — never a key, a presentation or a
  host reply. `manager/room-files.ts` holds a download's pieces out of a pane's
  reach and makes them a Blob only once the file is verified, typed
  octet-stream whatever its author claimed; `safeFileName` is the CLI's
  `local_name`.
- `RUNTIME_ROOM_FILES_PREPARE` resolves the host's endpoint and reports whether
  the wallet holds a host permission for it, so a pane's click can request one
  first. The worker lets go of each transfer port at once, so the console hears
  the offscreen document going away instead of waiting on the worker's end.
- CI: `rooms/keys/file-key/0.1` is banned from every bundle but the offscreen
  entry chunk — `manager.js` included — and asserted present there.
- CLAUDE.md: "Key material never reaches a browser" records the one piece of
  material that does, and where; the rooms section records why files, unlike
  records, go to the host directly.

Tests: the whole flow against the real published wasm and in-memory VTA and
host — a round trip across three chunks, a lost version race, a tampered chunk,
another file's blob served under this record, a misattributed body, refusals
before a file key is asked for — plus the host channel's reply checks and the
port's boundary (no release before verification, declared sizes held).

Needs live verification against a VTC: the host resolving the wallet's
did:peer signer, and the host origin's CORS under a just-in-time permission.

title: feat(vtc): DCQL trusted_authorities held at the response, not only published (#1988)
body:
A criterion's credential query may carry `trusted_authorities` (OpenID4VP 1.0
§6.1.1). The wallet uses it to choose a credential; the verifier still has to
check it, and the DCQL matcher does not read it. Until now the VTC published it
and ignored it.

- `vta_sdk::x509_issuer::x5c_issuer` returns, beside the issuer key, the key
  identifiers of the authorities certifying it: each certificate's AKI, the SKI
  of every certificate above the leaf, and that of the anchor reached.
- `aki` is held on both paths: a wallet response whose credential no named
  authority certifies is refused `issuerNotTrusted`, and the join criterion
  match rewrites a gated query to keys only such a credential offers. A DID
  issuer has no chain and meets no such query. The anchors still decide trust;
  `trusted_authorities` only narrows them.
- Registration refuses what cannot be held: `etsi_tl`, `openid_federation`,
  `trusted_authorities` on a non-`dc+sd-jwt` query, an empty list, or an `aki`
  value that is not base64url.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: chore(core): task surface synced to vta-sdk 0.68 — and what twelve releases of drift hid
body:
**Two commits, meant to land with Rebase and merge** so each keeps its own message:

1. `chore(core): task surface synced to vta-sdk 0.68 — and what twelve releases of drift hid`
2. `feat(core): room files — the host's blob tasks, one file's key, and the signed record body (#326)` — #326 was stacked on this branch and merged into it

Rebased onto main after #324 merged; build, lint and every test pass (core 963 / 2 skipped, extension 1065, 124, 6, 9).

---

Stacked on #324 (trust-tasks 0.26).

`task-surface.json` was last synced at vta-sdk 0.56.1, so the census in
`tests/task-surface.mjs` has been checking this library against a surface
twelve releases old. Room files need `rooms/keys/file-key`, which is newer
than that, so the sync could not wait — and it could not run: vta-sdk now
names three tasks (`keys/sign-sshsig`, `keys/sign-jws`, `keys/sign-csr`) by a
generated type it re-exports under its own name from another module,
`<crate::protocols::key_management::sign_jws::SignJwsPayload as …>::TYPE_URI`,
and the script stopped on the unrecognised form, as it is meant to.

- `scripts/sync-task-surface.mjs` learns that form: it indexes every
  `pub use trust_tasks_rs::specs::…::vN_M::{Payload as Name, …}` in the crate
  first, and resolves `crate::module::Name` against it. An alias it cannot
  find still stops the sync.
- `task-surface.json` regenerated at vta-sdk 0.68.0 (331 tasks).

The synced census then named four URIs this library sends that the SDK no
longer exports. Each was looked at against what the services serve:

- `auth/refresh/0.1` from `refreshAuthSession` (vta/auth-tasks.ts) is sent to
  the VTA, which serves only `auth/refresh/0.2` on `/trust-tasks`. 0.2 changes
  no payload member, so the function moves to 0.2.
- `auth/refresh/0.1` from the did-hosting step-up (rp-login/step-up.ts) and
  `auth/authenticate/0.1` from the deprecated bare DIDComm login
  (rp-login/didcomm.ts) go to a relying party, not the VTA. Listed in
  NOT_IN_SDK with that reason.
- `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.1` and `submit/0.2` came from `joinManifest`
  and `submitJoinRequest` in vtc/membership.ts — a second implementation of
  applying, which only a test called. The extension applies through
  vtc/join.ts at manifest 0.3 and submit 0.3, the versions the VTC serves, so
  the duplicate is removed rather than migrated. The property its test held
  (an explicit `registryConsent: false` is sent) is `buildJoinSubmit`'s, and
  tests/vtc.join.mjs holds it there.

Checked locally: `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` — every workspace green (core 948 passed / 2 skipped, extension 1065, 124, 6, 9).

* feat(core): room files — the host's blob tasks, one file's key, and the signed record body (#326)

The library half of files in data rooms (verifiable-trust-infrastructure
`data-rooms-files.md` P7), in a new subpath, `@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms/files`.
Nothing calls it yet; the offscreen document's file engine and the console's
pane follow.

- The host: `rooms/info`, `rooms/records/{get,put}/0.2` (a record naming its
  blob), `rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}` and
  `rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}`. Chunks cross as base64url and come back as bytes;
  a chunk answered for another index is refused.
- The member's own VTA: `rooms/keys/file-key/0.1`. The key is checked to be 32
  bytes, and a key released for another epoch than the one asked to open is
  refused, so a wrong answer is named as the VTA's rather than surfacing as a
  corrupt file.
- The sealed record body, ported rule for rule from
  `vtc-client::rooms::body`: `signRecordBody` refuses a key that is not the
  author's; `verifyRecordBody` is the only way to a `VerifiedRecordBody`, and
  refuses an unknown member, a proof that does not verify for the author under
  assertionMethod, a body signed for another location, and a signer other than
  the author an attributed room's host recorded. A file's manifest is believed
  only through it.
- `sameDigest` compares DigestMultibase values as bytes, so a host answering
  in the base64url spelling of a base58btc digest is not refused.

Why a subpath of its own: `rooms/keys/file-key` returns key material that
never expires. Only the offscreen document will import this, and the PR that
adds that engine also adds the CI guard banning the URI from every other
bundle. The console keeps importing `@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms`, which does not
contain it.

Interop with the Rust clients, both ways: a body signed by
`SealedRecordBody::sign` verifies here (pinned as a fixture in
tests/rooms.files.mjs), and a body signed here verified under
`verify_record_body` when the fixture was made.

The census: `rooms/keys/file-key` takes the implemented count 212 → 213, and
`rooms/blobs/*` and `rooms/info` join the host-served entries in NOT_IN_SDK.

title: feat(core): room files — the host's blob tasks, one file's key, and the signed record body
body:
Stacked on #325 (task surface sync), which is stacked on #324.

The library half of files in data rooms (verifiable-trust-infrastructure
`data-rooms-files.md` P7), in a new subpath, `@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms/files`.
Nothing calls it yet; the offscreen document's file engine and the console's
pane follow.

- The host: `rooms/info`, `rooms/records/{get,put}/0.2` (a record naming its
  blob), `rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}` and
  `rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}`. Chunks cross as base64url and come back as bytes;
  a chunk answered for another index is refused.
- The member's own VTA: `rooms/keys/file-key/0.1`. The key is checked to be 32
  bytes, and a key released for another epoch than the one asked to open is
  refused, so a wrong answer is named as the VTA's rather than surfacing as a
  corrupt file.
- The sealed record body, ported rule for rule from
  `vtc-client::rooms::body`: `signRecordBody` refuses a key that is not the
  author's; `verifyRecordBody` is the only way to a `VerifiedRecordBody`, and
  refuses an unknown member, a proof that does not verify for the author under
  assertionMethod, a body signed for another location, and a signer other than
  the author an attributed room's host recorded. A file's manifest is believed
  only through it.
- `sameDigest` compares DigestMultibase values as bytes, so a host answering
  in the base64url spelling of a base58btc digest is not refused.

Why a subpath of its own: `rooms/keys/file-key` returns key material that
never expires. Only the offscreen document will import this, and the PR that
adds that engine also adds the CI guard banning the URI from every other
bundle. The console keeps importing `@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms`, which does not
contain it.

Interop with the Rust clients, both ways: a body signed by
`SealedRecordBody::sign` verifies here (pinned as a fixture in
tests/rooms.files.mjs), and a body signed here verified under
`verify_record_body` when the fixture was made.

The census: `rooms/keys/file-key` takes the implemented count 212 → 213, and
`rooms/blobs/*` and `rooms/info` join the host-served entries in NOT_IN_SDK.

Checked locally: `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` — every workspace green (core 963 passed / 2 skipped incl. 14 new in tests/rooms.files.mjs; extension 1065; 124, 6, 9). The Rust-side check of a JS-signed body was run against `vtc-client` at VTI main 49d8fe3d.

title: feat(vta)!: gate the TEE first-boot admin claim on a pre-registered c…
body:
## Why

`POST /bootstrap/request` (Mode B) accepted an anonymous caller. Whoever reached a fresh TEE VTA first claimed super-admin, gated only by the carve-out sentinel. That sentinel lives in host-controlled storage: a hostile host can forge its absence or drop its write, and a crash, snapshot restore or lost volume write can produce the same state innocently. Any remote caller could then walk through the reopened window.

This PR removes the remote claimant: only the holder of a claim DID registered **before** the VTA exists can claim admin.

## How it works

1. **Before the VTA exists**, the operator runs `pnm bootstrap claim-did create --slug <slug>`. PNM mints an Ed25519 `did:key`, keeps the private key in the OS keyring only, and prints the public DID.
2. The provisioning stack delivers that public DID to the enclave in the tenant overlay as `bootstrap_claim_did`.
3. `pnm bootstrap connect --slug <slug>` sends that DID as `client_did`, signed with its key.
4. The enclave verifies the signature, requires `client_did` to equal the configured claim DID, then checks the carve-out. On success it mints the admin as before and burns the claim DID alongside the sentinel.

## Changes

- **vta-sdk:** optional `claim_signature` on the sealed `BootstrapRequest` (Ed25519 over `domain tag ‖ client pubkey ‖ nonce`), with `new_signed_claim()` / `verify_claim_signature()`.
- **vta-config:** `tee.bootstrap_claim_did`, settable only through the tenant overlay. `deny_unknown_fields` and the explicit assignment in `apply_tenant_overlay` are kept, and `admin_did` stays forbidden. It is validated as an Ed25519 `did:key` at boot, so a bad value fails at startup rather than at the one-shot claim, and it is covered by the attested effective-config digest (`skip_serializing_if` keeps existing VTAs' digests unchanged).
- **vta-service** (`routes/bootstrap.rs`), in this order:
  1. verify the signature (403, before the lock);
  2. under `MODE_B_LOCK`, require the configured claim DID (403; unset admits nobody);
  3. sentinel **or** burn record present → 410;
  4. on success, write the burn record (`tee:bootstrap-claim-did-burned`) in the same persist as the sentinel.

  A refused claim writes nothing. Checking the claimant before the carve-out means a stranger cannot learn whether the VTA was claimed.
- **pnm-cli:** new `bootstrap claim-did create|show|discard`.
  - The key is stored under `bootstrap-claim:<slug>`, separate from `vta:<slug>` so `pnm setup` can't overwrite or rotate it.
  - It fails closed without the `keyring` feature or with `VTI_SECURE_STORE=file`, and is read back after save.
  - `connect` loads the key before any network I/O and drops it only after attestation verifies, never on an unauthenticated 410.
- **deploy / docs:** `render-tenant-overlay.sh --bootstrap-claim-did`, plus the allowlist table and the PNM README.

## Breaking changes

- A TEE VTA without `bootstrap_claim_did` accepts no Mode-B claim.
- `pnm bootstrap connect` requires a claim DID from `claim-did create`, and `--slug` is required with `--vta-url`.
- Old and new versions don't interoperate in either direction: an old VTA rejects the unknown `claim_signature` field, and a new VTA refuses an unsigned claim. Upgrade PNM and the VTA together.

* feat(vta)!: gate the TEE first-boot admin claim on a pre-registered claim DID

POST /bootstrap/request (Mode B) accepted an anonymous caller: whoever
reached a fresh TEE VTA first claimed admin, gated only by the carve-out
sentinel, which a hostile host can make vanish by forging its absence or
dropping its write.

- pnm: `bootstrap claim-did create|show|discard` mints an Ed25519 claim
  DID before the VTA exists; the private key lives only in the OS
  keyring (file store refused). `bootstrap connect --slug` signs the
  request with it and drops the key once attestation verifies.
- vta-sdk: optional `claim_signature` on the sealed BootstrapRequest,
  over a domain tag || client pubkey || nonce.
- vta-config: `tee.bootstrap_claim_did`, settable only via the tenant
  overlay (deny_unknown_fields kept; admin_did still forbidden),
  validated at boot and covered by the attested config digest.
- vta-service: verify the signature, require client_did == the
  configured claim DID (403, nothing written), then the carve-out;
  burn the claim DID with the sentinel on success.

and pnm `bootstrap connect` needs a claim DID from `claim-did create`.
The hostile-host substitution vector stays open: the overlay is not
integrity-protected (follow-up: anchor the claim DID out of host reach).

Signed-off-by: Abdul Qadeer <abdul.q@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta): review follow-ups for the TEE bootstrap claim DID (#1987)

- Drop the `tee:bootstrap-claim-did-burned` record. The carve-out sentinel
  is already covered by the TEE integrity manifest (P0.2a) and the anchor
  (P0.2b); the burn record was not, and was written in the same persist,
  so it added no protection.
- Validate `tee.bootstrap_claim_did` in `AppConfig::validate`, so a baked
  (self-host, PCR0-committed) value fails at boot like an overlay one.
  `affinidi-crypto` becomes an optional dependency behind `tee`.
- `pnm bootstrap connect`: on 403, tell the operator the VTA is not
  configured with their claim DID and should not be trusted (VTI-CLT-016).
- Docs and deploy tooling: tee-architecture, sealed-bootstrap, CLAUDE.md,
  the nitro configs, README and build-vta.sh overlay template now carry the
  claim DID; the parent-delivered caveat is stated, not overclaimed.

body:
### Added

- **keys**: Serve keys/sign-jws and keys/sign-csr — a verifier key that never leaves the VTA ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2057](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2057))

Custody B for the OpenID4VP verifier, VTA side. A VTC signing request objects
  with a VTA-held key, or obtaining an EUDI access certificate for one, needs the
  VTA to produce a JWS or a PKCS#10 request; keys/sign cannot, since it frames
  caller bytes under the opaque signing domain.

  keys/sign-jws/0.1 (tt-tf #749): the VTA sets alg from the key (ES256 for P-256,
  EdDSA for Ed25519), refuses alg/crit/b64/jwk/jku/x5u, checks the registered
  header members' types and that an x5c's first certificate carries the named
  key, and builds the signing input itself (RFC 8785 header and payload;
  payloadBase64Url checked canonical; integers beyond 2^53 refused). The
  specification's example signing input and its digest are reproduced in a test.

- **vta**: The VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS ([#2056](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2056))

* feat(vta)!: the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS

  A community that runs hidden vetting admits an applicant on a zero-knowledge
  proof that distinct eligible vetters vetted them. Every vetter and applicant
  holds a PCS secret key, and until now the member side ran only in a client
  linking the PCS library, so a mobile wallet (Keyring) could not take part.

  The VTA now holds those keys and runs every member-side operation (design
  vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md §13 C7); the client carries messages and never
  holds a key. Twelve Trust Tasks (trust-tasks-tf #756):

  - applicant: applications/{create,show,delete}, verify-attestation, prove
  - vetter: root-request, root-accept, tokens/{request,accept,abandon}, attest,
    vetter/show

title: feat(vtc): room files in S3 through the community's VTA — one presigned request per object, no storage credential held
body:
A storage config of kind `s3` with `auth: {mode: vta-account, context,
account}` (vtc/_shared/0.1 room-storage, dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#758) keeps
room files in a bucket whose credential only the community's VTA holds.
For each object operation the VTC asks its VTA for one presigned request
(`external/credentials/issue/0.1` against an `s3-static-presign` account):
one action on one object, prefix `<config prefix>rooms/<hash>/`, for 300
seconds. The VTA checks the binding, `external-auth-use`, the account's
state, the scope against its ceiling, the TTL and the rate, audits the
issuance, and seals the request to this community's X25519 key inside a
`#response` whose proof is verified as the VTA's before it is read.

The VTA is reached over the VTC's existing messaging socket (TSP >
DIDComm, by the VTA's advertised services), so the VTA needs no inbound
address for this, and the community holds no storage secret at rest.

- vti-common: `blob_store::presigned` (feature `blob-presigned`) — a
  `BlobStore` over a `Presigner`. Each request is checked before use
  (https, the asked method, a path ending in the object's key); no
  redirects; GETs are reused until shortly before they expire; a put
  streams with Content-Length; a ranged get checks the length returned.
- vtc-service: one link to the VTA. `vta_link::VtaLink` (#2060's
  `keys/sign-jws` link) now runs on `outbound::PeerTasks`, the
  sign/send/await-verified-reply exchange the git bridge also uses, and
  `rooms::vta_storage::VtaStorage` issues storage credentials over it.
- storage configs: create/update ask the VTA about the account (a canary
  read under `<prefix>probe/`) and refuse `unknownAccount`, or name the
  member at fault for a scope or TTL the binding cannot cover; the probe
  authenticates through the store's own health check; `credentialState`
  carries the context.
- Docs: `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` setup at the VTA;
  `data-rooms-files.md` P4b.

## Checked locally
- fmt, clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`
- nextest workspace (excl. vtc): 5714 passed; vtc-service + vtc-client: 3067 passed; both doc-test runs
- `cargo check --workspace --locked` on 1.95.0; Cargo.lock unchanged

Not breaking: `vti-common` gains a feature-gated module; `vtc-service` is unpublished.

title: fix(vta): provision-integration refuses a template no bundle can carry, before minting (#1988)
body:
swiyu-verifier keeps its did:webvh update key out of the document and has no key agreement (the Swiss Profile Anchor forbids both), but an integration's sealed bundle carries its signing and key-agreement keys under the verificationMethod ids the published document gives them. provision-integration minted and stored the DID first and only then failed, as an internalError naming a template binding, leaving the DID behind.

A webvh template whose signing slot is publish: false, or that has no ka slot, is now refused as a validation error before the mint, naming the commands that do work: pnm did-mgmt dids create --template <name>, then pnm keys bundle (and, for an oid4vp-verifier, vtc oid4vp install or attach). did:key and did:peer templates mint their own pair and are unaffected; every other built-in passes, which a test pins. Documented as precondition 4 in provision-integration.md.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: vti-common-v0.44.0
body:
### Added

- **keys**: Serve keys/sign-jws and keys/sign-csr — a verifier key that never leaves the VTA ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2057](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2057))

Custody B for the OpenID4VP verifier, VTA side. A VTC signing request objects
  with a VTA-held key, or obtaining an EUDI access certificate for one, needs the
  VTA to produce a JWS or a PKCS#10 request; keys/sign cannot, since it frames
  caller bytes under the opaque signing domain.

  keys/sign-jws/0.1 (tt-tf #749): the VTA sets alg from the key (ES256 for P-256,
  EdDSA for Ed25519), refuses alg/crit/b64/jwk/jku/x5u, checks the registered
  header members' types and that an x5c's first certificate carries the named
  key, and builds the signing input itself (RFC 8785 header and payload;
  payloadBase64Url checked canonical; integers beyond 2^53 refused). The
  specification's example signing input and its digest are reproduced in a test.

- **vta**: The VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS ([#2056](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2056))

* feat(vta)!: the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS

  A community that runs hidden vetting admits an applicant on a zero-knowledge
  proof that distinct eligible vetters vetted them. Every vetter and applicant
  holds a PCS secret key, and until now the member side ran only in a client
  linking the PCS library, so a mobile wallet (Keyring) could not take part.

  The VTA now holds those keys and runs every member-side operation (design
  vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md §13 C7); the client carries messages and never
  holds a key. Twelve Trust Tasks (trust-tasks-tf #756):

  - applicant: applications/{create,show,delete}, verify-attestation, prove
  - vetter: root-request, root-accept, tokens/{request,accept,abandon}, attest,
    vetter/show

- **vtc**: Storage configs — where a community keeps its rooms' files, changed only with consent ([#2052](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2052))

Phase P4 (first part) of docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §7.

### Added

- **keys**: Serve keys/sign-jws and keys/sign-csr — a verifier key that never leaves the VTA ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2057](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2057))

Custody B for the OpenID4VP verifier, VTA side. A VTC signing request objects
  with a VTA-held key, or obtaining an EUDI access certificate for one, needs the
  VTA to produce a JWS or a PKCS#10 request; keys/sign cannot, since it frames
  caller bytes under the opaque signing domain.

  keys/sign-jws/0.1 (tt-tf #749): the VTA sets alg from the key (ES256 for P-256,
  EdDSA for Ed25519), refuses alg/crit/b64/jwk/jku/x5u, checks the registered
  header members' types and that an x5c's first certificate carries the named
  key, and builds the signing input itself (RFC 8785 header and payload;
  payloadBase64Url checked canonical; integers beyond 2^53 refused). The
  specification's example signing input and its digest are reproduced in a test.

- **vta**: The VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS ([#2056](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2056))

* feat(vta)!: the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS

  A community that runs hidden vetting admits an applicant on a zero-knowledge
  proof that distinct eligible vetters vetted them. Every vetter and applicant
  holds a PCS secret key, and until now the member side ran only in a client
  linking the PCS library, so a mobile wallet (Keyring) could not take part.

  The VTA now holds those keys and runs every member-side operation (design
  vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md §13 C7); the client carries messages and never
  holds a key. Twelve Trust Tasks (trust-tasks-tf #756):

  - applicant: applications/{create,show,delete}, verify-attestation, prove
  - vetter: root-request, root-accept, tokens/{request,accept,abandon}, attest,
    vetter/show

- **vtc**: Credential issuers known by an X.509 chain — x5c trust anchors for EUDI PID and Rulebook credentials ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2053](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2053))

An EUDI credential (the PID, or one a Rulebook governs) is issued by an https
  URL whose JWS names its key by an x5c chain, not by a DID. The VTC now trusts
  such an issuer only through operator-configured anchors, never by the chain
  alone.

  vta-sdk (feature `x509-issuers`): `x509_issuer` — `X509TrustAnchors`,
  `x5c_issuer_key` (validity, CA flags, chain signatures, ends at an anchor or a
  certificate an anchor signed, leaf key usage, leaf SAN URI = iss or dNSName =
  its host; P-256, secp256k1, Ed25519) and `issuer_jws_key`. Token Status Lists
  signed the same way verify through
  `verify_status_list_token_with_anchors` / `resolve_token_status_with_anchors`.

## [0.0.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/releases/tag/vti-vetting-pcs-v0.0.0) — 2026-10-13 ### Added - **vta**: The VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS ([#2056](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2056)) * feat(vta)!: the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS A community that runs hidden vetting admits an applicant on a zero-knowledge proof that distinct eligible vetters vetted them. Every vetter and applicant holds a PCS secret key, and until now the member side ran only in a client linking the PCS library, so a mobile wallet (Keyring) could not take part. The VTA now holds those keys and runs every member-side operation (design vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md §13 C7); the client carries messages and never holds a key. Twelve Trust Tasks (trust-tasks-tf #756): - applicant: applications/{create,show,delete}, verify-attestation, prove - vetter: root-request, root-accept, tokens/{request,accept,abandon}, attest, vetter/show - **vtc**: Join criteria state their own admission (Keyring VTI-13) ([#1907](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1907)) A community's join criteria are its join rules, and the VTC now decides a submission by them as vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3 specifies (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#710, trust-tasks-rs 0.26.1). Nothing in the service assumes a criterion: open admission, review only, invitation only and any combination are all criteria an administrator registers. - Criteria (vtc/schemas/accepts/{register,list,show}/0.2) carry `admission` (automatic | review), an optional DCQL query with `credentialIssuers` (community | recognised | any), `invitationRequired` and `vetting`. `recognised` without a trust registry is `unsupportedRequirement`. - The manifest (vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3) publishes them in the order the community decides by — registration order, kept on replacement. - A submission is decided under the criterion it names by digest, else the first it meets, else the first published. No criteria → `notAccepting`; an unpublished digest → `criterionUnknown`. Superseded versions are kept and govern while their `requirementsGrace` lasts. - The host verifies the presentation's embedded credentials (proof set, validity window, revocation, subject = applicant) and matches the query, applying DCQL `type_values`, which the matcher alone ignores. - The host holds the policy to the criterion: unmet → never admitted or referred (requestMore naming what is missing); met review → refer; met automatic → the policy's verdict. Policy may tighten, never loosen. The default join.rego follows the criterion. - A new community is seeded once with `invited` (automatic) → `member-credential` (automatic) → `review`. - The criterion and version that governed are recorded beside the request; a supplement re-decides under it. - DTG Credentials v1 — role VACs, vetted/1 and witnessed/1 statements, IDVCs, issuerScope ([#1859](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1859)) * feat(vta-sdk)!: vetting statements are vetted/1 VSCs; role credentials are VACs Conform the SDK's vetting artifacts to the DTG Credentials Core Specification (v1 context, `issuerScope`) and the DTG VSC predicate registry, following the regenerated vetting specifications (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/dtg-vsc-conformance). Vetting Statement (vetting/session/0.1): no longer an EndorsementCredential. `sign_statement` builds a StatementCredential with `new_vetted_vsc` under `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`; the body is `credentialSubject.object.value`, with no `type` member. `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` are both read from the `vetting/session` document, which `StatementDraft::session` now carries in place of `task_context`, and `StatementDraft::issuer_scope` is `directed` or `public` (pairwise is refused by the profile). `verify_statement` parses through `dtg-credentials`, so the v1 context, the one-subtype rule and the profile are checked by the code that issues them; `VerifiedVettingStatement::check_against_session` binds a statement to the session document by id and task digest. - `IdentityVettingEndorsement` -> `VettedObjectValue` (no `type`; digests and commitment must be base58btc, as the registry schema requires). - `IDENTITY_VETTING_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE` -> `VETTED_PREDICATE`. - `VerifiedVettingStatement::endorsement()` -> `value()`; new `issuer_scope()`, `task_digest_multibase()`. Vetter role credential (vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1, vetting/request/0.1): a community-issued VAC, `issuerScope` public, `authority` { scope: , actions: ["role:vetter"], maxAttenuation: 0 }. `eligibility::community_role` -> `community_roles`, returning every `role:` of a VAC the community issued in its own scope with no parent; `verify_eligibility_vp` parses the VAC strictly and refuses a non-public scope or an attenuation. - `COMMUNITY_ROLE_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE` removed; new `ROLE_ACTION_PREFIX`, `VETTER_ROLE_ACTION`, `role_action`, `role_of_action`. - `protocols::members::ENDORSEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` removed; new `AUTHORITY_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` and `STATEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE`. - `VerdictWith::role_vec` -> `role_vac` (wire `roleVac`).

Nothing in the service assumes a criterion: open admission, review only, invitation only and any combination are all criteria an administrator registers. - Criteria (vtc/schemas/accepts/{register,list,show}/0.2) carry `admission` (automatic | review), an optional DCQL query with `credentialIssuers` (community | recognised | any), `invitationRequired` and `vetting`. `recognised` without a trust registry is `unsupportedRequirement`. - The manifest (vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3) publishes them in the order the community decides by — registration order, kept on replacement. - A submission is decided under the criterion it names by digest, else the first it meets, else the first published. title: feat(vtc): verifier identities whose key the VTA keeps — request objects signed through keys/sign-jws (#1988)
body:
feat(vtc): verifier identities whose key the VTA keeps — request objects signed through keys/sign-jws (#1988)

Custody B, VTC side. A verifier identity can now name a key the VTA keeps
instead of caching it: every OpenID4VP request object is signed by the VTA
through keys/sign-jws (#2057), and the VTC holds no private key.

- VerifierSigner signs a whole JWS (header members + claims) rather than a
  signing input, since keys/sign-jws builds the input at the VTA. The signer
  sets alg; a caller's alg is refused. LocalP256Signer is unchanged in effect.
- VtaHeldSigner sends keys/sign-jws over a late-bound link and verifies each
  returned JWS under the identity's recorded public key before a wallet sees
  it (the spec's producer SHOULD).
- vta_link::VtaLink: the VTC's runtime link to its VTA (vta_did), TSP >
  DIDComm by the VTA's advertised service types on the existing mediator
  socket, documents signed with the operational key, replies accepted only
  when their proof verifies as the VTA (PendingReplies). No REST arm. One
  attempt per call; the session start owns the retry.
- VerifierIdentityRecord: privateKeyMultibase is optional and vtaKeyId new;
  exactly one must be present (KeyCustody). Records written before still read.
- vtc oid4vp attach records a VTA-held identity (swiyu with --did/--kid, EUDI
  without) from the VTA key id and its P-256 public key, and prints the
  pnm acl grant (sign-jws) and, for EUDI, the pnm keys sign-csr step;
  vtc oid4vp csr points a VTA-held identity there; list shows where each key
  is held.
- Boot refuses a VTA-held identity without vta_did, vtc_did, the signing key
  or a resolver, naming the identities.

Docs: oid4vp-verifier.md "Keeping the key in the VTA"; CLAUDE.md signing
oracle line. Tests: custody parsing, signer checks (wrong key, no link, caller

title: feat(vtc): verifier identities whose key the VTA keeps — request objects signed through keys/sign-jws (#1988) (#2060)
body:
feat(vtc): verifier identities whose key the VTA keeps — request objects signed through keys/sign-jws (#1988) (#2060)

Custody B, VTC side. A verifier identity can now name a key the VTA keeps
instead of caching it: every OpenID4VP request object is signed by the VTA
through keys/sign-jws (#2057), and the VTC holds no private key.

- VerifierSigner signs a whole JWS (header members + claims) rather than a
  signing input, since keys/sign-jws builds the input at the VTA. The signer
  sets alg; a caller's alg is refused. LocalP256Signer is unchanged in effect.
- VtaHeldSigner sends keys/sign-jws over a late-bound link and verifies each
  returned JWS under the identity's recorded public key before a wallet sees
  it (the spec's producer SHOULD).
- vta_link::VtaLink: the VTC's runtime link to its VTA (vta_did), TSP >
  DIDComm by the VTA's advertised service types on the existing mediator
  socket, documents signed with the operational key, replies accepted only
  when their proof verifies as the VTA (PendingReplies). No REST arm. One
  attempt per call; the session start owns the retry.
- VerifierIdentityRecord: privateKeyMultibase is optional and vtaKeyId new;
  exactly one must be present (KeyCustody). Records written before still read.
- vtc oid4vp attach records a VTA-held identity (swiyu with --did/--kid, EUDI
  without) from the VTA key id and its P-256 public key, and prints the
  pnm acl grant (sign-jws) and, for EUDI, the pnm keys sign-csr step;
  vtc oid4vp csr points a VTA-held identity there; list shows where each key
  is held.
- Boot refuses a VTA-held identity without vta_did, vtc_did, the signing key
  or a resolver, naming the identities.

Docs: oid4vp-verifier.md "Keeping the key in the VTA"; CLAUDE.md signing
oracle line. Tests: custody parsing, signer checks (wrong key, no link, caller
alg), the link's reply handling, attach records, and an end-to-end wallet

title: feat(keys): serve keys/sign-jws and keys/sign-csr — a verifier key that never leaves the VTA (#1988)
body:
feat(keys): serve keys/sign-jws and keys/sign-csr — a verifier key that never leaves the VTA (#1988)

Custody B for the OpenID4VP verifier, VTA side. A VTC signing request objects
with a VTA-held key, or obtaining an EUDI access certificate for one, needs the
VTA to produce a JWS or a PKCS#10 request; keys/sign cannot, since it frames
caller bytes under the opaque signing domain.

keys/sign-jws/0.1 (tt-tf #749): the VTA sets alg from the key (ES256 for P-256,
EdDSA for Ed25519), refuses alg/crit/b64/jwk/jku/x5u, checks the registered
header members' types and that an x5c's first certificate carries the named
key, and builds the signing input itself (RFC 8785 header and payload;
payloadBase64Url checked canonical; integers beyond 2^53 refused). The
specification's example signing input and its digest are reproduced in a test.

keys/sign-csr/0.1: the VTA checks the subject against the specification's
attribute table without repairing it, and builds the CertificationRequestInfo
from it, the optional subjectAltName and the key's own public key (P-256 or
Ed25519); the request's signature verifies under x509-parser.

Both sign their bytes as ProtocolDefined through the keys/sign chokepoint
(scope, context signing policy, daily quota) and audit once as keys.sign-jws
(alg, typ, SHA-256 of the signing input; never the payload) or keys.sign-csr
(subject, alternative names, SHA-256 of the signed DER). They are gated on new
capabilities, sign-jws and sign-csr, derived wherever sign is. Unlike
sign-sshsig, sign is not accepted in their place: this VTA frames keys/sign
payloads, and both specifications say such a custodian SHOULD NOT widen sign
into a JWS or a certificate request. Declared codes are rendered, including
keys:notFound (to a super-admin only; anyone else gets the scope refusal).

vta-sdk: TASK_KEYS_SIGN_JWS_0_1 / TASK_KEYS_SIGN_CSR_0_1 (ReadOnly),
VtaClient::sign_jws / sign_csr, protocols::key_management::{sign_jws,sign_csr}
re-exporting the generated types, x509_issuer::certificate_key. MCP guard
classifies both Sensitive; conformance witnesses from the specification's
examples.

Not done: binding a key to one protocol (the specifications' SHOULD) and
restricting a key to its provisioned typ values (MAY).

title: feat(vta)!: the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS
body:
The VTA becomes its principal's hidden-vetting (PCS) engine, so a client with no PCS implementation — the Keyring mobile wallet — can apply under, and vet for, a community whose criterion uses hidden vetting. Design §13 C7, both sides: applicant and vetter.

The client carries messages between the community and the other party; the VTA never talks to the community itself.

## Wire

The twelve `vta/pcs/*` Trust Tasks from trust-tasks-tf #756, released in `trust-tasks-rs` 0.30.2 (the floor is raised here):

- applicant: `applications/{create,show,delete}`, `verify-attestation`, `prove`
- vetter: `root-request`, `root-accept`, `tokens/{request,accept,abandon}`, `attest`, `vetter/show`

New capabilities `pcs-vetter` / `pcs-applicant`, derived by Admin and Initiator only — never `sign`, and `application` derives neither.

## Custody

- **No `usk` is stored or returned.** Each member key is re-derived on every use from a path allocated under its context's base (VTI-KEY-030), through `key_custody::derive_pcs_member_seed` → `vta_keys::custody::authorize_pcs_derivation` (custody rules 3 and 6), domain-separated from the Ed25519 node at the same path (`PCS_MEMBER_KEY_DOMAIN`).
- One vetter key per (context, community) for life; a second member DID is `memberMismatch`.
- No task returns a key, a class credential, an unspent token or blinding state. Engine state is wrapped under the seed-derived KEK in the new `pcs_engine` keyspace (backed up; cascades on DID delete).
- Audit never pairs a vetter with an applicant identifier, tag or statement metadata.

## Crates

- **`vti-vetting-pcs`** — now published (0.1.0, `vta-external` precedent) and an unconditional `vta-service` dependency. Ports `applicant`, `vetter`, `snapshot`, `community`, `token` from openvtc, plus seeded enrolment (`VetterEngine::enrol_from_seed`, `ApplicantEngine::from_seed`). Feature `harness` keeps the in-process community (`vtc::Vtc`) for tests.
- **`vta-service`** — `operations/pcs.rs`, `trust_tasks/pcs.rs` + `pcs_tests.rs` (an end-to-end admit: two vetters, an applicant and an in-process community, all through the VTA's handlers), dispatch, conformance witnesses, custody census.
- **`vta-sdk`** — `TASK_VTA_PCS_*`, `retry_safety` classes, `VtaClient::pcs_*`.
- **`vta-mobile-core`** — `PcsTask`, `build_pcs_task`, `parse_pcs_response` for Keyring.
- **`vta-mcp`** — `attest` / `abandon` destructive, the rest mutating.
- **`vtc-service`** — call sites for the new `TokenWallet::receive` signature.

Breaking (`!`): new `Capability` variants in `vti-common`.

## Not in this PR

- `vta/pcs/withdraw` — no VTC-side task accepts a withdrawal yet; that needs a spec first.
- A VTA-driven token drip (the client carries each tick today).
- Moving openvtc from its local engine to this one. Related: openvtc #486 stops openvtc syncing applicants' hidden-vetting keys to the VTA.

## Tested

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5689 tests; two timed out under machine load (`every_backed_up_keyspace_survives_a_round_trip`, `every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry`) and pass alone in 55 s / 66 s.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3023 passed. With `--features vetting-pcs`, only the admin-UI tests fail under `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD`; they pass with the UI built.
- Doctests, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (also vtc `--features vetting-pcs`, after rebasing on current main), `cargo fmt --check`.

Docs: `docs/02-vta/pcs-engine.md`; CLAUDE.md gains the layer-map entry, crate row, integration-flow section and published-closure update.

body:
feat(vta)!: the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS (#2056)

* feat(vta)!: the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS

A community that runs hidden vetting admits an applicant on a zero-knowledge
proof that distinct eligible vetters vetted them. Every vetter and applicant
holds a PCS secret key, and until now the member side ran only in a client
linking the PCS library, so a mobile wallet (Keyring) could not take part.

The VTA now holds those keys and runs every member-side operation (design
vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md §13 C7); the client carries messages and never
holds a key. Twelve Trust Tasks (trust-tasks-tf #756):

- applicant: applications/{create,show,delete}, verify-attestation, prove
- vetter: root-request, root-accept, tokens/{request,accept,abandon}, attest,
  vetter/show

Custody: no usk is stored or returned. Each member key is re-derived on every
use from a path allocated under its context's base (VTI-KEY-030), through a
new custody door (vta_keys::custody::authorize_pcs_derivation, wrapped by
key_custody::derive_pcs_member_seed) that holds the path to the context and
domain-separates the seed from the Ed25519 node there. One vetter key per
(context, community) for life. Credentials, tokens, blinding state and held
attestations are wrapped under the seed-derived KEK in the new, backed-up
pcs_engine keyspace.

Authorization: new capabilities pcs-vetter / pcs-applicant (published as
pcsVetter / pcsApplicant), derived by admin and initiator, never by
application, and never implied by sign (VTI-VTA-007). Audit never pairs a
vetter with an applicant identifier, tag or statement metadata.

vti-vetting-pcs gains the member-side engines (ported from openvtc, with
seed-derived key pairs and an in-process community behind feature `harness`)
and becomes publishable. Clients: VtaClient::pcs_* and
vta_mobile_core::pcs::{build_pcs_task, parse_pcs_response}.

Breaking: new variants on vti_common::acl::Capability are additive
(non_exhaustive) but AppState gains a field; vti-vetting-pcs's
CommunityParams::published and TokenWallet::receive take the drip rate and
the draw's (label, tick).

Deferred: attestation withdrawal (no community-side task accepts one yet) and a
VTA-driven token drip.
