## 🤖 New release * `vta-sdk`: 0.65.1 -> 0.66.0 (⚠ API breaking changes) * `vti-common`: 0.41.1 -> 0.41.2 (✓ API compatible changes) * `vti-rooms`: 0.12.0 -> 0.12.1 (✓ API compatible changes) * `vtc-client`: 0.20.0 -> 0.20.1 (✓ API compatible changes) * `vta-cli-common`: 0.38.0 -> 0.38.1 (✓ API compatible changes) * `cnm-cli`: 0.31.1 -> 0.31.2 * `pnm-cli`: 0.37.1 -> 0.37.2 * `vta-keys`: 0.18.0 -> 0.19.0 * `vta-vault`: 0.16.0 -> 0.16.1 * `vta-service`: 0.57.0 -> 0.58.0 (✓ API compatible changes) * `vti-rooms-dtg`: 0.14.0 -> 0.14.1 * `vti-secrets`: 0.14.0 -> 0.14.1 * `vta-audit`: 0.13.0 -> 0.13.1 * `vta-config`: 0.18.0 -> 0.18.1 * `vta-support`: 0.15.0 -> 0.15.1 * `vta-backup`: 0.17.0 -> 0.17.1 * `vta-external`: 0.1.0 -> 0.1.1 * `vta-policy`: 0.13.0 -> 0.13.1 * `vta-tee`: 0.17.0 -> 0.17.1 * `vta-webvh`: 0.14.0 -> 0.14.1 ### ⚠ `vta-sdk` breaking changes ```text --- failure constructible_struct_adds_field: struct exhaustively constructible through public API adds field --- Description: A pub struct that could be exhaustively constructed with a literal using only public API has a new pub field, breaking existing exhaustive literals. ref: https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/expressions/struct-expr.html impl: https://github.com/obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks/tree/v0.50.0/src/lints/constructible_struct_adds_field.ron Failed in: field KeySlot.publish in /tmp/.tmpbKvTZl/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/vta-sdk/src/did_templates/mod.rs:149 ```
Changelog

## `vta-sdk`

## [0.66.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.65.1...vta-sdk-v0.66.0) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **vtc**: OpenID4VP wallet sessions — swiyu wallets present evidence for a join ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2044](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2044)) A swiyu wallet speaks OpenID4VP 1.0 over HTTPS and signs no Trust Task, so the applicant's own agent opens the exchange for it. The VTC now serves the whole round trip against an installed verifier identity ([#2039](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2039)). - `vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/start/0.1`: the proof signer opens a session for a criterion named by its `requirementsDigest` (and optionally their own join request). The VTC signs an ES256 request object as a JAR in swiyu's profile (`profile_version`, `aud` https://self-issued.me/v2, `client_id` `decentralized_identifier:`), asking for the criterion's published DCQL query unchanged, with a fresh nonce, `state` and P-256 response key, and returns the `swiyu-verify://` wallet URI. Every declared code is served: criterionNotFound, noWalletPresentation, verifierNotConfigured, requestNotFound (unknown and somebody else's alike), requestClosed, tooManySessions. - `GET /v1/oid4vp/request/{session}` answers the request object once; `POST /v1/oid4vp/response/{session}` accepts one `direct_post.jwt` answer. It is checked in order: decrypts (A256GCM) under the session key and echoes `state`; each presentation's issuer signature, validity and KB-JWT over the session nonce with the prefixed `client_id` as audience (VTI-CRD-020…022), one holder; status valid, never assumed (VTI-CRD-014); every issuer admitted by the criterion's `credentialIssuers`; the query satisfied (`DcqlQuery::evaluate_presentation`). Both are a declared foreign-protocol exception (VTI-OPS-095): REST_EXCEPTIONS and GOVERNED_UNAUTH rows, behind the unauthenticated governor; the response reads its body against `[oid4vp] max_response_bytes`. - `vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/status/0.1`: only the signer who opened a session reads it; the evidence names the wallet's holder key beside the applicant and each credential's query id, format, issuer and vct, never a claim value; a refusal names its reason. - New keyspace `oid4vp_sessions`, encrypted at rest, excluded from backup. A minute sweeper closes unanswered sessions at `expiresAt` (dropping the response key) and drops records an hour after closing, or when held evidence lapses. State changes run under one lock, so one response wins. - `[oid4vp]` config: session TTL, open sessions per applicant, evidence hold, response cap, default identity, wallet URI scheme. - Workspace floors: affinidi-openid4vp 0.1.4 (`direct-post-jwt`), affinidi-oid4vc-core 0.1.10 (`jwe`), affinidi-sd-jwt 0.1.7; trust-tasks-rs 0.28.1 for the wallet-session specs. Evidence is recorded on the session. Deciding a join on it — on the named request, or on the applicant's next submission — follows. P3 of docs/05-design-notes/oid4vp-wallet-verifier.md; docs/03-vtc/oid4vp-verifier.md covers operating it. - SignInPortal in did-host-http* templates and a VTC DID self-check for wallet sign-in ([#2042](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2042)) * feat(vta-sdk): advertise SignInPortal from the did-host-http* templates Wallet sign-in with a trigger link (auth/oob, contract C4/C9) needs the service's DID document to list SignInPortal on the origin of its login page. DID hosting publishes /login for itself, but a node minted from a did-host-http* template lacked the entry, so wallets refused its sign-in links with "This code can't be used" (webvh.storm.ws). did-host-http, did-host-http-tsp and did-host-http-didcomm now declare SERVICE_SIGN_IN_PORTAL (null default, bare service member). When a template declares it and the caller does not supply it, the renderer derives { id: #sign-in-portal, type: SignInPortal, serviceEndpoint: /login } from URL, https only. A caller may supply its own entry or null to omit it. Templates for nodes with no login page (did-host-didcomm, did-host-tsp, didcomm-mediator) are unchanged. Existing DIDs are untouched; the doc explains adding the entry with pnm did-mgmt dids edit. New public helpers: sign_in_portal_endpoint, sign_in_portal_service, SIGN_IN_PORTAL_SERVICE_TYPE, SIGN_IN_PORTAL_SERVICE_VAR. - **rooms**: Pnm rooms file put/get, and signed sealed bodies for rooms put/get ([#2037](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2037)) A member can now put a file in a sealed room and fetch it from the CLI, end to end (data-rooms-files.md P6), and `pnm rooms put`/`get` work on sealed rooms. Sealed record body (vtc_client::rooms::body). This implements `SealedRecordBody` (rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json, trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#747): the JSON inside a sealed record. It is signed by its author with a Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022, or ecdsa-jcs-2019 for P-256) and names the room, key and version it was written for. `verify_record_body` is the only way to a `VerifiedRecordBody`. It refuses, rather than warns about, a body that: - names an unknown member or breaks a bound; - carries a proof that does not verify for `author` for assertionMethod, or uses another suite; - was signed for another location; - on attributed, was signed by someone other than the author the host recorded. There is no generated type for the body, because no host task carries it (the same as FileManifest). pnm rooms put on a sealed room: - reads the tier from `rooms/info`, signs the body as the operator, and seals it through the VTA's `rooms/keys/seal`, which seals what it is given and signs nothing; - predicts the version from the room head. The host assigns versions from a room-wide counter, so a write that lands at another version is re-sealed at the next one and rewritten over exactly what landed, up to 4 times, then named with the --expected-version to retry with. Without a file, `put` and `get` stay on records 0.1, which the VTC host serves. pnm rooms get: - verifies the sealed body before showing it; - reads `sealed` as the object the host returns. It had read it as a bare string, so it could open no sealed record. pnm rooms file put/get. A file is sealed and opened locally with one file's key from the VTA. `put` seals the file, uploads its ciphertext (begin, the missing chunks, commit; abort on failure), checks the committed blobRef, then writes a create-only record (records/put 0.2) whose signed body carries the FileManifest. `get` writes nothing unless every check holds: - the body is verified; - the blob is named on the record and is the one the author named; - each chunk matches the manifest; - the plaintext matches the author's digest. Another member's text has control characters stripped, and a file name keeps only its last path component, never written over an existing file. Files need records/put 0.2, which room-host serves and the VTC does not yet. Client calls: - vtc-client: begin/upload/commit/abort, get_blob/download_chunk, room_info, get_record_v2 and put_sealed_record_with_blobs, on the generated trust_tasks_rs types; - vta-sdk: VtaClient::room_seal, and trust_task_sign::sign_object_for_assertion for signing an object that is not a Trust Task. - **vta-sdk**: Foreign-protocol DID identities — JWK key slots, an unpublished update key, P-256 slots, and a swiyu-verifier template ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2036](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2036)) A VTC that verifies swiyu wallet presentations (OpenID4VP) needs an identity of its own, shaped by the Swiss Profile Anchor: a did:webvh with one P-256 key published as a publicKeyJwk (publicKeyMultibase is forbidden), no keyAgreement, service or @context, the Ed25519 update key kept to the log's updateKeys, and portable=false. DID templates could express none of that. This adds what they were missing, and the template. - `{SLOT}_KEY_JWK`: every key slot now also renders as a JWK object (kty, crv, x, y, alg), beside `{SLOT}_KEY_MB`. Either publishes the slot; a JWK placeholder for an undeclared slot, or declared as a variable, is refused like its multibase twin. - `KeySlot::publish` (default true; **breaking** — a new public field). Only the `signing` slot, the did:webvh update key, may be `publish: false`, and then the document must not use it. Its key record is named by its did:key, as the log names it, instead of a guessed `#key-0`. - Templates that declare slots but no `ka` slot get no key-agreement key published or recorded. - Additional signing slots may be P-256 (`derive_p256`'s domain-separated derivation). - `defaults.portable: false` is binding: the VTA mints the DID non-portable whatever the caller asked (pnm defaults to true). Only that direction. - Minted key records are matched to the document by publicKeyJwk as well as publicKeyMultibase. - Built-in `swiyu-verifier` template. Mint it serverless at the swiyu identifier-registry slot URL, then upload the log to that slot.
## `vti-common`
## [0.41.2](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-common-v0.41.1...vti-common-v0.41.2) — 2026-10-11 ### Fixed - **tsp**: A relationship accept beaten by a concurrent one was answered, not lost ([#2041](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2041)) Two invites from one peer that arrive together are both recorded first, each leaving the pair InviteReceived. The first accept moves it to Bidirectional and the second is refused (invalid transition: SendAccept in state Bidirectional), which both the VTA and the VTC logged as "could not send a TSP relationship accept ... the peer sees no answer". The peer did get an answer: an accept for the same pair went out a moment earlier, and receiving any accept completes its side. Seen at gt-vta on 2026-10-11 against the browser wallet, whose mediator socket was being replaced in a loop (fixed in vta-browser-plugin #319), so its invites arrived in pairs. accept_refusal_is_benign (vti_common::relationship_store) decides it the way the SDK's invite_refusal_is_benign does: re-read the relationship state after the refusal rather than match the error text (R3.7). Bidirectional means the invite was answered and is logged at debug; anything else is a real failure and keeps the warning. Both services use the one helper.
## `vti-rooms`
## [0.12.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-rooms-v0.12.0...vti-rooms-v0.12.1) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **vtc**: Serve room files — blobs, records 0.2 and rooms/info, off until enabled ([#2040](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2040)) A community VTC now hosts room files the way room-host does (data-rooms-files.md P5), so `pnm rooms file put/get` works against a VTC. One implementation for both hosts: vti_rooms::blob_tasks. room-host's file handlers mapped each task onto BlobHost, with the spec's declared codes and generated response types. That mapping moves into vti-rooms. Each function takes the room, the authenticated presenter and the chain's authorization, and returns a body checked against the generated response type, or a Refusal the host renders. room-host keeps only its transport, parsing and chain verification, and its 47 tests pass unchanged. The VTC renders the same results through its own reply helpers, so the two hosts cannot answer one task two ways. The VTC: - registers, by generated payload type: rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk, commit,abort}, rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}, rooms/info and rooms/records/{put,get,list} 0.2, and adds them to the shared ROOMS_DISPATCHED_URIS, pinned against the registry; - uses the same record path as room-host. put (0.1 too, since a rewrite that names no blobs releases them) holds prepare_record across the write and applies it after. A curate that retracts releases the record's blobs. get/list 0.2 read under a snapshot; - holds a BlobHost in AppState and runs a GC sweeper; - adds the keyspaces room_blobs (backed up: the index and usage) and room_blob_transfers (excluded: transfers in flight); - has a new `[rooms.files]` section mirroring room-host's flags. **Uploads are off by default** on a VTC (`enabled = false`). Until storage configs exist, a file goes to a local directory under limits that apply to every room alike, and an operator should choose that. When off, `begin` answers filesDisabled, while stored files and records without files are still served. room-host, a standalone host, keeps its default. Size gate. Upload chunks (360 KiB) and begin (320 KiB) declare sizes above the 64 KiB default, which the VTC granted only to issuers with an ACL entry, and room members hold none. Room tasks now count as served for sizes. A large upload/chunk is admitted only from a claimed issuer holding an open, unexpired upload here (BlobHost::holds_open_upload). A large begin is admitted only when uploads are on and its payload names a room hosted here. Both are charged to the same per-address LargeDocumentBudget, and a claim that fails verification doubles the address's cost, like any other. rooms/info's specification said RECOMMENDED for its proof, though the chain must bind to the signer. trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#750 makes it REQUIRED. Until that reaches trust-tasks-rs, an interim DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF entry records why the rooms arm refuses an unsigned caller anyway. The census fails once the specification agrees, which forces the entry out with that bump.

Its key record is named by its did:key, as the log names it, instead of a guessed `#key-0`. - Templates that declare slots but no `ka` slot get no key-agreement key published or recorded. - Additional signing slots may be P-256 (`derive_p256`'s domain-separated derivation). - `defaults.portable: false` is binding: the VTA mints the DID non-portable whatever the caller asked (pnm defaults to true). Only that direction. - Minted key records are matched to the document by publicKeyJwk as well as publicKeyMultibase. - Built-in `swiyu-verifier` template. Mint it serverless at the swiyu identifier-registry slot URL, then upload the log to that slot. ### Fixed - **tsp**: A relationship accept beaten by a concurrent one was answered, not lost ([#2041](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2041)) Two invites from one peer that arrive together are both recorded first, each leaving the pair InviteReceived. The first accept moves it to Bidirectional and the second is refused (invalid transition: SendAccept in state Bidirectional), which both the VTA and the VTC logged as "could not send a TSP relationship accept ... the peer sees no answer". The peer did get an answer: an accept for the same pair went out a moment earlier, and receiving any accept completes its side. Seen at gt-vta on 2026-10-11 against the browser wallet, whose mediator socket was being replaced in a loop (fixed in vta-browser-plugin #319), so its invites arrived in pairs. accept_refusal_is_benign (vti_common::relationship_store) decides it the way the SDK's invite_refusal_is_benign does: re-read the relationship state after the refusal rather than match the error text (R3.7). Bidirectional means the invite was answered and is logged at debug; anything else is a real failure and keeps the warning. Both services use the one helper.

title: Worker: pass a 304 from the asset store through instead of reporting it as a redirect
body:
## Problem

Refreshing any registry page in a browser rendered it unstyled; a second refresh brought the stylesheet back.

A refresh revalidates the cached stylesheet with `If-None-Match`. The worker forwards that header to the Pages asset store, which answers `304 Not Modified`. The redirect guard in `site/_worker.js` treated every 3xx as an asset-layout redirect and turned the 304 into a 500, so the page rendered with no stylesheet. The browser then dropped its cache entry, and the next refresh fetched the stylesheet unconditionally and got a 200, which is why the second refresh looked fine.

Reproducible against production today:

```
$ curl -sS -D - -H 'If-None-Match: "6580ca74306ee78ec5b17d29ab887a35"' https://registry.trustoverip.org/assets/site.css
HTTP/2 500
Asset layout error: /assets/site.css redirected (304). The build must emit <path>.html, not <path>/index.html.
```

The HTML pages would hit the same path if the edge sent an ETag for them; today it does not, so only the stylesheet was affected.

## Change

- A 304 from the asset store is no longer treated as a redirect. It passes through with the same headers a 200 carries (media type, Vary, CORS, Cache-Control, Link) and no body, so the cache entry it refreshes stays consistent.
- The asset-store stub in `site/_worker.test.mjs` now emits an ETag per asset and answers a matching `If-None-Match` with a 304. A new test covers the stylesheet, a negotiated JSON-LD path, and a stale validator still getting the full 200.

## Verification

- `docker compose run --rm test`: 26 pass. The new test fails with `actual: 500, expected: 304` on the old worker.
- Against `wrangler pages dev` in the container, a conditional request for `/assets/site.css` and for `/dtg` now returns 304 with the worker's headers.

title: feat(vtc): OpenID4VP wallet sessions — swiyu wallets present evidence for a join (#1988)
body:
A swiyu wallet speaks OpenID4VP 1.0 over HTTPS and signs no Trust Task, so the
applicant's own agent opens the exchange for it. The VTC now serves the whole
round trip against an installed verifier identity (#2039).

- `vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/start/0.1`: the proof signer opens a
  session for a criterion named by its `requirementsDigest` (and optionally
  their own join request). The VTC signs an ES256 request object as a JAR in
  swiyu's profile (`profile_version`, `aud` https://self-issued.me/v2,
  `client_id` `decentralized_identifier:<did>`), asking for the criterion's
  published DCQL query unchanged, with a fresh nonce, `state` and P-256
  response key, and returns the `swiyu-verify://` wallet URI. Every declared
  code is served: criterionNotFound, noWalletPresentation,
  verifierNotConfigured, requestNotFound (unknown and somebody else's alike),
  requestClosed, tooManySessions.
- `GET /v1/oid4vp/request/{session}` answers the request object once;
  `POST /v1/oid4vp/response/{session}` accepts one `direct_post.jwt` answer.
  It is checked in order: decrypts (A256GCM) under the session key and echoes
  `state`; each presentation's issuer signature, validity and KB-JWT over the
  session nonce with the prefixed `client_id` as audience (VTI-CRD-020…022),
  one holder; status valid, never assumed (VTI-CRD-014); every issuer admitted
  by the criterion's `credentialIssuers`; the query satisfied
  (`DcqlQuery::evaluate_presentation`). Both are a declared foreign-protocol
  exception (VTI-OPS-095): REST_EXCEPTIONS and GOVERNED_UNAUTH rows, behind the
  unauthenticated governor; the response reads its body against
  `[oid4vp] max_response_bytes`.
- `vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/status/0.1`: only the signer who opened a
  session reads it; the evidence names the wallet's holder key beside the
  applicant and each credential's query id, format, issuer and vct, never a
  claim value; a refusal names its reason.
- New keyspace `oid4vp_sessions`, encrypted at rest, excluded from backup. A
  minute sweeper closes unanswered sessions at `expiresAt` (dropping the
  response key) and drops records an hour after closing, or when held evidence
  lapses. State changes run under one lock, so one response wins.
- `[oid4vp]` config: session TTL, open sessions per applicant, evidence hold,
  response cap, default identity, wallet URI scheme.
- Workspace floors: affinidi-openid4vp 0.1.4 (`direct-post-jwt`),
  affinidi-oid4vc-core 0.1.10 (`jwe`), affinidi-sd-jwt 0.1.7;
  trust-tasks-rs 0.28.1 for the wallet-session specs.

Evidence is recorded on the session. Deciding a join on it — on the named
request, or on the applicant's next submission — follows. P3 of
docs/05-design-notes/oid4vp-wallet-verifier.md; docs/03-vtc/oid4vp-verifier.md
covers operating it.

This release bumps the workspace from 0.5.0, which is already on crates.io, to 0.6.0, and folds `[Unreleased]` into a dated `[0.6.0]` section.

**What's in 0.6.0**

title: feat: SignInPortal in did-host-http* templates and a VTC DID self-check for wallet sign-in
body:
Wallet sign-in with a trigger link (`auth/oob`, sign-in trigger-link contract C4 and C9) needs the service's DID document to list `TrustTaskHTTPS` (a base; clients POST `<base>/trust-tasks`) and `SignInPortal` (whose origin is the sign-in page's). On **webvh.storm.ws**, a DID hosting server minted from the `did-host-http` template, there was no `SignInPortal`, so wallets refused its codes with "This code can't be used" and nothing server-side noticed.

## A. vta-sdk: `SignInPortal` in the `did-host-http*` templates

- `did-host-http`, `did-host-http-tsp` and `did-host-http-didcomm` now publish exactly what DID hosting publishes for itself: `{ "id": "<did>#sign-in-portal", "type": "SignInPortal", "serviceEndpoint": "<origin of URL>/login" }`, placed after `TrustTaskHTTPS` (`{URL}/api`).
- The template format can't compute an origin. So the templates declare `SERVICE_SIGN_IN_PORTAL` (a null default, as a bare service member), and the renderer derives it from `URL`, the same way it derives `WS_URL`. It does this only for `https`. A plain-http dev URL gets no entry. A caller can supply its own entry, or `null` to omit it.
- Nodes that serve no `/login` page keep their templates unchanged: `did-host-didcomm`, `did-host-tsp` (witness/watcher) and `didcomm-mediator`. `vtc-host` already publishes its own `SignInPortal` (`/members/`).
- New additive public items: `sign_in_portal_endpoint`, `sign_in_portal_service`, `SIGN_IN_PORTAL_SERVICE_TYPE`, `SIGN_IN_PORTAL_SERVICE_VAR`. There are no breaking changes.
- Backwards compatible: existing DIDs are untouched, and only new mints get the entry. `docs/02-vta/did-templates.md` explains how to add it to an existing DID with `pnm did-mgmt dids edit --did <did>`.

## B. vtc-service: DID self-check for wallet sign-in

- `vtc-service/src/did_self_check.rs` resolves the VTC's own DID about 5 s after boot (spawned in `server::run`, off the startup path). After that it re-checks lazily, caching a result for 5 minutes, or 30 s if the result was unknown. It checks the **published** document using the portal's own checks (`member_portal::oob::check_trust_task_https` / `check_sign_in_portal`), so it can't disagree with the flow. `VTCRest` is not checked, because neither the portal nor the wallet flow reads it.
- When something is missing, it logs one warning. The warning names what is missing, gives the exact JSON entries, and gives the fix: `pnm did-mgmt dids edit --did <vtc-did>`, then `cnm did-log install` for a VTC serving its own log. It logs again only when the result changes.
- It never blocks startup. If resolution fails, the result is `unknown`, not `missing`.
- `GET /v1/member/sign-in/config` gains `didDocument`: `{"status":"ok"}`, `{"status":"unknown"}` or `{"status":"missing","missing":["SignInPortal"]}`. It carries only facts from the public document.
- The shared `WalletSignIn` component (member portal and console login) now fetches that config when it mounts. When the status is `missing`, it replaces "Show sign-in code" with a short note naming the missing services, and the other sign-in options stay as they are.

## Tests

- vta-sdk: `cargo nextest run -p vta-sdk -p vta-cli-common`, 1147 passed. New template tests cover: every `did-host-http*` template gets the exact entry; the origin is used, not the path; the `{DID}` sentinel is kept; plain http gets no entry; a caller can override or omit it; templates without a login page don't declare it.
- vta-service template, did_webvh and provision tests: 310 passed.
- vtc-service: full nextest run. The only failures were the 10 admin-UI-embedding tests, run with `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`; they pass with the UI built. New tests: `did_self_check` unit tests, plus the sign-in config route returning `didDocument: {status: unknown}` with no resolver.
- admin-ui: `npm test` (85 files, 988 tests) and `npm run lint` pass. New tests cover: the note names the missing services; there is no code button when services are missing; the code is still offered when the status is unknown, ok or absent.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.

title: fix(tsp): a relationship accept beaten by a concurrent one was answered, not lost
body:
When two TSP relationship invites from the same peer arrive at once, the VTA and the VTC both warned that "the peer sees no answer". The peer had in fact been answered.

## What happens

1. Both invites are recorded first, and each leaves the pair `InviteReceived`.
2. The first `accept_relationship` moves the pair to `Bidirectional` and sends the accept.
3. The second is refused by the state machine: `invalid transition: SendAccept in state Bidirectional`.
4. That refusal was logged as `could not send a TSP relationship accept; … the peer sees no answer`.

An accept for the same pair went to the same peer a moment earlier, and receiving any accept completes its side. So the invite was answered, and the warning said the opposite.

Seen at gt-vta on 2026-10-11 15:49:44 UTC, against the browser wallet. The wallet's mediator socket was being replaced in a loop (fixed in OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#319), so its invites arrived in pairs. A client retrying, or two sessions of one client re-forming the same relationship, can produce the same pair.

## Fix

`accept_refusal_is_benign` (`vti_common::relationship_store`) decides it the same way the SDK's `invite_refusal_is_benign` does: it re-reads the relationship state after the refusal rather than matching the error text (R3.7).

- **`Bidirectional`:** the invite was answered. Logged at debug.
- **Anything else:** the accept failed for its own reasons (no route, no key, the mediator refused it). The existing warning and the not-collecting accounting are unchanged.

The VTA (`messaging/service.rs`) and the VTC (`messaging.rs`) carried the same handler and now share the one helper.

## Tests

- 3 unit tests pin the decision: `Bidirectional` is benign; `InviteReceived`, `None` and `Pending` are not. The race itself sits between two awaits and cannot be staged, which is how the SDK pins its counterpart too.
- `cargo clippy -p vti-common -p vta-service -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `tsp` is on by default in both services, so this compiled the new code.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib messaging`: 129 passed. `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib messaging`: 41 passed.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): read-only re-read of the store.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): the listener is untouched; a failed re-read falls through to the existing warning.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): the point of the change; a real accept failure still warns.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutation added.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: feat(vtc): serve room files — blobs, records 0.2 and rooms/info, off until enabled
body:
A community VTC now hosts room files the way `room-host` does (`data-rooms-files.md` P5), so `pnm rooms file put/get` (#2037) works against a VTC.

### One implementation for both hosts
`vti_rooms::blob_tasks` (new) maps each file task onto `BlobHost`, with the spec's declared codes and generated response types. It takes `(room, presenter, authorization)` and returns a checked response body or a `Refusal`. Each host keeps only its transport, parsing, chain verification and reply rendering.
- `room-host`'s handlers become thin wrappers; all 47 of its tests pass unchanged.
- The VTC renders the same results through its own helpers, so the two can't answer one task two ways.

### The VTC
- **Tasks**, registered by generated payload type: `rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}`, `rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}`, `rooms/info` and `rooms/records/{put,get,list}` 0.2. All are added to the shared `ROOMS_DISPATCHED_URIS` and pinned against the registry.
- **Record path, as room-host's:**
  - put (0.1 too, since a rewrite naming no blobs releases them) holds `prepare_record` across the write and then `apply`s it;
  - retract releases the record's blobs;
  - get/list 0.2 read under a snapshot.
- **State:** `AppState::room_files: Arc<BlobHost>` plus a GC sweeper.
- **Keyspaces:** `room_blobs` is **backed up** (the index and usage); `room_blob_transfers` is **excluded** (transfers in flight).
- **`[rooms.files]`**: mirrors room-host's flags. **Uploads are off by default.** Until storage configs exist, files go to a local directory under limits that apply to every room alike, and an operator should choose that. When off, `begin` answers `filesDisabled`; stored files and records without files are still served.

### Size gate
Upload chunks (360 KiB) and `begin` (320 KiB) declare sizes above the 64 KiB default. The VTC only granted that to issuers with an ACL entry, and room members have none.
- A large `upload/chunk` is admitted only from a claimed issuer that **holds an open, unexpired upload** here.
- A large `begin` is admitted only when **uploads are on and it names a room hosted here**.
- Both are charged to the same per-address `LargeDocumentBudget`, and a claim that fails verification doubles that address's next cost, like any other.

### `rooms/info` proof
Its spec said RECOMMENDED though the chain must bind to the signer. trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#750 (merged) makes it REQUIRED. Until that reaches `trust-tasks-rs`, an interim `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF` entry records why the rooms arm refuses an unsigned caller anyway. The census fails once the spec agrees, forcing the entry out with that bump.

### Tests
- VTC, through the dispatcher with signed documents:
  - a file uploaded, named by put 0.2, read back by get/list 0.2, downloaded and counted;
  - `blobNotFound` for an uncommitted blob;
  - retraction and a 0.1 rewrite each releasing the file;
  - another party's chunks to someone's upload answered `notFound`.
- The size gate's room standing.
- `[rooms.files]`: off by default, a misspelt key refused.
- Census and backup tests updated.
- Full CI-equivalent run: fmt and clippy clean, 5,629/5,629 workspace tests, 2,979/2,979 vtc tests, doctests.

### Next
Storage configs, with credentials from the community VTA's external accounts (P4/P4b, `vtc/storage/*`), replace the single local directory.

title: fix(tsp): apply unclaimed relationship control frames instead of refusing them forever
body:
TSP relationship control messages (invite, accept, cancel) that no request is waiting for were refused and never acknowledged, so the mediator redelivered them on every reconnect, forever.

## What was happening

`ensureRelationship` claims the accept it is waiting for. Every other control frame reaches the inbox:
- an accept that arrives after the 5 s handshake stopped waiting
- a cancellation
- the VTA's own invite

The inbox read every TSP frame as a Trust-Task document. A control frame has an empty body, so `openTspEnvelope` threw `payload is not JSON: Unexpected end of JSON input`. The throw went back to the transport, so no ack was sent, and the mediator kept the frame.

Seen against glenn-vta on 2026-10-11: the offscreen console showed the same four 580-byte frames (`-EB4YTSP-AAC…`) refused after every reconnect.

## Fix

- **`unpackInboundTsp`** returns the verified control message (`InboundTspControl`, discriminated by `isInboundTspControl`) instead of parsing it as a document. Its sender is proven by the same `unpack` as a document's.
- **`applyInboundControl`** (`vta/tsp-relationship.ts`) applies it using the specification's own rules from `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js`:
  - **accept:** `resolveAccept` adopts only an accept that answers our outstanding invite, which moves the relationship to `bidirectional`. Anything else is ignored.
  - **cancel:** `resolveCancel` removes a relationship we hold. A cancellation naming one we do not hold is ignored rather than answered, so nobody can probe which relationships we hold.
  - **invite:** ignored. The wallet initiates its relationships, and a Rev 3 peer may send application messages over an invite it is still waiting on (§3.6).
- **The offscreen inbox** applies the message to the shared `tspRelationships` store and returns, so the frame is acknowledged. A control frame carries no consent request, so there is nothing for persist-before-ack to hold (R1.6).

## Not done

§7.3's answering cancellation when both halves were held. It is logged as owed, not sent: the peer has already forgotten the relationship, and the next request re-invites. Sending it needs a routed TSP send from the inbox path, which is more than this change should take on.

## Tests

- **`core/tests/tsp.inbound.mjs`:**
  - an accept and a cancel come back as control, from the proven sender
  - a control frame from a sender that cannot be verified is still refused (`e.p.msg.unauthorized`)
  - a document still comes back as a document
- **`core/tests/tsp.inbound-control.mjs` (new):**
  - a late accept completes the relationship
  - an accept to an invite we did not send, or with nothing outstanding, changes nothing
  - a cancellation of a bidirectional relationship removes it and reports the answer owed
  - a cancellation naming an unknown relationship is ignored
  - an invite is ignored

`npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the relationship store is in-memory and only reflects what the peer sent.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): removes an unbounded redelivery.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): a control frame is acked after it is applied, and carries no consent request to persist. Document frames are unchanged.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none on the wire. `unpackInboundTsp`'s return type widened; its one caller is updated.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): an unverifiable control frame is still refused.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): each outcome is logged, including the owed answer.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): an in-memory record lost to a teardown means the next request re-invites.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: feat(sign-in): explain document-level refusals in the window's Details
body:
## Problem

When a service's DID document had no `SignInPortal` service, the sign-in window said only "Code not accepted / This code can't be used." The operator testing it had no way to find out why.

## Change

The headline and message for every refusal stay as they were. Reasons that come from parsing the link (bad-from, bad-type, bad-id and so on) also stay vague, as VTI-LNK-021 requires: a reader never says which link field failed.

Refusals caused by the **contact's DID document or the page** are not link fields. These now carry a `detail` (`SignInRefusalDetail` in `bridge-protocol.ts`) from the flow to the window. The window shows it in a collapsed **Details** block with a Code row, a Meaning row and a DID row. The DID uses the existing `CopyableDid` pattern (selectable text plus a Copy button).

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `no-portal-service` | This service's DID document doesn't list a sign-in portal (a SignInPortal service). Ask its operator to add one. |
| `no-portal-service` (listed, unusable) | …lists a sign-in portal (a SignInPortal service), but its endpoint isn't usable: it must be an https URL on a public host name, with no port or credentials. Ask its operator to fix it. |
| `no-common-transport` (no `TrustTaskHTTPS`) | …doesn't list a Trust-Task endpoint (a TrustTaskHTTPS service), so the wallet has nowhere to send the sign-in. Ask its operator to add one. (There is also a listed-but-unusable variant.) |
| `wrong-origin` | This page (https://a) isn't the service's sign-in page (https://b). Start sign-in from https://b, or ask the operator to point the SignInPortal service at this page. |
| `did-document-unverified` | The wallet couldn't fetch or verify this service's DID document. Check that the DID below is published and its log verifies, and that its host is a public name on the default https port. (Shows the DID.) |
| `from-not-allowed` | Sign-in doesn't accept a did:key DID as the service's identifier. The service needs a DID that can list a sign-in portal, such as did:webvh. |
| `unsupported-vid` (resolver missing) | This wallet can't resolve did:x DIDs yet, so it can't check this service. An update may add it. |
| `domain-not-linked` | The website (https://portal) doesn't publish a DID Configuration that links it to the community's DID, so nothing was sent to it. Its operator needs to serve /.well-known/did-configuration.json with a Domain Linkage credential for the DID below. |

What changed in each layer:

- **Core:** `selectSignInServices` now says which service type is missing (`SignInPortal` or `TrustTaskHTTPS`) and whether one was listed but has an unusable endpoint. A missing `TrustTaskHTTPS` already had its own reason (`no-common-transport`, outcome `unreachable`), so it did not need to be split from `no-portal-service`. `parseTriggerLink`'s `from-not-allowed` now carries the contact's DID method.
- **Plumbing:** the offscreen and background layers already pass `SignInStepResult` through unchanged. The background console line still uses `failureLogFields`, so no DID or origin is ever logged (VTI-LNK-073). A test checks this.
- **README:** a new "When a sign-in code isn't accepted" section under the sign-in section. It lists what each Details line means, how an operator fixes it, the three services a DID hosting service needs, and `pnm did-mgmt dids edit --did <did>`.

This also closes the backlog item to make the wrong-origin error name both origins.

## Tests

- Core: `selectSignInServices` reports missing and unusable for both service types. `from-not-allowed` names the method and nothing else of the contact.
- Flows: each document-level refusal produces its detail and leaves the message unchanged. A bad link field (`bad-id`) carries no detail. `domain-not-linked` includes the DID and the origin.
- Render: one test per Details text, plus a test that a link-field refusal shows no Details.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` all pass.

No manifest, permission or dependency changes.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no network code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1) — n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase; all consumers updated (R3.*) — internal runtime message only (optional `detail`)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*) — n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*) — the console line is unchanged
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered (R2.1) — no mutations
- [x] Deviations flagged: the Details show the contact DID on screen. VTI-LNK-073 forbids putting the contact in an error; it is shown only in the person's own window (as VTI-LNK-050 already does) and is never logged.
```

title: perf(tsp): unpack each inbound frame once, however many requests are waiting
body:
Each inbound TSP frame is now unpacked once and the result shared by every request waiting on the socket. Previously each waiting request unpacked the frame itself.

## Why

Every inbound frame on a mediator socket is offered to each outstanding TSP request in turn (`onTspFrame` in `didcomm/index.ts`). Each request's `claims` did a full `unpack` (HPKE decrypt and signature verify) before it could read the thread id and decline. With N requests waiting, a burst of N replies cost about N²/2 unpacks, serially, on the offscreen thread that also sends.

A console switched between agents a few times a second leaves six requests waiting per page load for up to 30 s. Nothing cancels them when the page goes away.

Against gt-vta on 2026-10-11:
- The VTA log shows the same six-request bundle about 14 times in six seconds, so ~80 requests were outstanding at once.
- One unpack takes about 1.4 ms in Node, and longer in a browser. That's seconds of blocked thread per burst.
- The wallet's own sends came out bunched behind that work: four page loads reached the agent within 15 ms.

## Change

- **`openReplyOnce`** (`vta/tsp-channel.ts`) caches the opened reply, either `{ sender, doc }` or a decline reason.
  - It is keyed on the frame object, in a `WeakMap`, so the entry goes away with the frame. The transport hands every waiter the same `bytes` object.
  - It is also keyed on the public halves of the keys involved, so a waiter holding different keys never reads another's result.
- **`TspChannel.send`'s `claims`** uses it, then does only the sender and thread-id checks.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged, including the decline reasons reported on a timeout (`lastDecline`, `framesSeen`).

## Not claimed

This does not explain the six replies in the same incident that reached the wallet more than 30 s late. A backlog of a few seconds would have delayed most replies, not exactly six. That is still open, pending the `fpdev-mediator` log for the window.

## Tests

`core/tests/tsp.unpack-once.mjs` (new):
- 50 waiters offered one frame share one unpack
- a waiter with different keys gets its own result, and a decline
- a different frame object is unpacked afresh even with identical bytes

The existing `tsp.channel`, `tsp.relationship` and `tsp.timeout-diagnosis` tests pass unchanged. `npm run lint` and `npm test` pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): an in-memory cache keyed on the frame object.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): the frame dispatch and ack order are unchanged.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): a frame that does not verify under a waiter's keys is still declined for that waiter.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): nothing persisted.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: perf(tsp): unpack each inbound frame once, however many requests are waiting (#322)
body:
perf(tsp): unpack each inbound frame once, however many requests are waiting (#322)

Every inbound frame on a mediator socket is offered to each outstanding TSP
request in turn, and each request unpacked it itself (HPKE decrypt +
signature verify) before it could read the thread id and decline. With N
requests waiting, a burst of N replies cost about N^2/2 unpacks, serially, on
the offscreen thread that also sends.

A console switched between agents a few times a second leaves six requests
waiting per load for up to 30 s. Against gt-vta on 2026-10-11 that reached
~80 outstanding; at ~1.4 ms an unpack (measured in Node, slower in a
browser) that is seconds of blocked thread per burst, and the wallet's own
sends came out bunched behind it - four page loads reaching the agent within
15 ms.

openReplyOnce caches the opened reply per frame object (WeakMap, so it goes
with the frame) and per set of public keys, so a waiter holding different
keys never reads another's result. Each waiter then does only the sender and
thread-id checks. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged, including the decline
reasons reported on a timeout.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.30.0
body:
### Specifications

- **rooms**: Rooms/info and rooms/usage require a proof, like every other rooms/* task ([#750](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/750))

Both said a proof was RECOMMENDED, on the reasoning that the room-issued chain
  is "bound to whoever the host authenticated". A room operation carries no
  session, so the only party a host can authenticate is the proof's signer. The
  chain's leaf must be that party. Without a proof there is nobody to bind it
  to, and the presentation becomes a bearer token. Every other rooms/* task
  already requires a proof for this reason. A host implementing the chain rule
  refuses an unsigned info or usage request anyway, so the RECOMMENDED was
  already unworkable.

  Breaking for a producer that sent these unsigned. Both specs are drafts.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.6.2` → `0.7.0` | breaking |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc): OpenID4VP verifier identities — a sealed key hand-off and a separate ES256 signer (#1988)
body:
A swiyu wallet presents only to a verifier whose request object is signed by a
P-256 key of a DID in the swiyu Base Registry. That identity is not the
community's DID, and its key must not join the credential signer — every key
there puts a proof on every credential the community issues. The VTC keeps no
VTA credential after setup, so the key reaches it by a hand-off the operator
relays, the way other secrets move between these tools.

- `vtc oid4vp request --identity <id>` (offline) writes a sealed-transfer
  request and keeps its private half, with the nonce the bundle must carry,
  in the data directory (0600).
- On the admin workstation: `pnm did-mgmt dids create --template
  swiyu-verifier --did-url <swiyu slot URL> --context <ctx>`, upload the
  printed log to the slot, then `pnm keys bundle <ctx> --recipient
  request.json`.
- `vtc oid4vp install --identity <id> --bundle <file> --digest <hex>`
  (offline) opens the bundle — the request's key, the out-of-band digest, the
  request's nonce — takes the DID's P-256 key (`--kid` when there is more than
  one), checks it is a verification method of the bundle's DID and that its
  private half is the published key, and stores it.
- New keyspace `oid4vp_keys`, encrypted under the storage key like `install`
  and `passkey`, and backed up (a restore of the same key bundle reproduces
  the key that decrypts it). `server::offline_storage_key` derives that key
  for offline writers exactly as the daemon does.
- `crate::oid4vp::VerifierSigner`: the signer request objects will be signed
  with — `LocalP256Signer` (ES256, r||s) now, a VTA-held key through
  `keys/sign-jws` later. Loaded at boot into `AppState::oid4vp_signers`; a
  record that does not load fails the boot.
- `vtc oid4vp list` / `remove`.

docs/03-vtc/oid4vp-verifier.md walks the steps. P2 of
docs/05-design-notes/oid4vp-wallet-verifier.md; the wallet-facing endpoints
(P3) and EUDI's X.509 identity follow.

title: fix(transport): stop the warm pool duelling itself; one REST sign-in at a time; say who sent a 429
body:
A tester flipping the console between two agents saw `tsp: timed out awaiting reply frame` on every pane, then the REST-fallback warning, then `failed: 429`. The VTA and mediator logs from that session (gt-vta / ic3-mediator, 2026-10-11 15:37–15:51 UTC) trace it to three wallet defects, plus a fourth in how the console's warning expires.

## 1. The warm pool duelled itself (the TSP timeouts)

Mediator log for the holder `did:key:z6MkwWeu9…`: an authentication every ~2.4 s from 15:39:28 to 15:40:26, restarting at 15:49:43, with

> Sustained duplicate-WebSocket duel for this DID … Something is running more than one live session for this DID.

The duel started when the socket reached its token-expiry margin (`since_last_ms=872182`: the 15-minute token minus our 30 s margin).

1. `getWarmSession` retires the socket and opens a replacement.
2. The mediator keeps one socket per DID, so it closes the old one.
3. The old socket's `onClose` fires as an unexpected drop. The pool is keyed on the (relay, agent) pair, not the connection, so it deleted the **replacement's** entry and scheduled a reconnect.
4. The reconnect found the pool empty and opened a third socket. The mediator closed the second, whose `onClose` did the same, and so on.

Replies go to whichever socket is newest, so the request waiting on another one timed out. At 15:49:44 only `whoami` reached the VTA over TSP; `contexts/list` and `dids/list` never arrived.

**Fix:** `onClose` does nothing when the pool already holds a different connection (`isSuperseded`, `warm-session-health.ts`). The approver pool had the same unconditional delete and gets the same guard.

## 2. Concurrent REST sign-ins superseded each other (the 429s)

VTA log at 15:41:48:
- 6 `auth/challenge`s and 4 `auth/authenticate`s for the same holder within 2 ms.
- 401 `token superseded (jti mismatch)`: the VTA keeps one live token per DID.
- Then 429 from its own per-IP `auth` limiter (burst 10, one per 5 s).

**Fix:**
- `getVtaBearer` shares the sign-in already in flight for a (baseUrl, holder).
- `makeReauth` drops only the token that was refused, so the second of several refused requests reuses the replacement the first one minted instead of superseding it.

## 3. A 429 did not say who sent it

The agent's REST endpoint is behind Cloudflare, and the wallet rendered the VTA's 429 and a CDN's identically as `429`. A 429 is now read against the VTA's contract:
- `x-rate-limit-source` and `retry-after`;
- or, when CORS hides those headers, the VTA's `{"error":"rate_limited","limiter":…}` body.

It is reported as `rate limited by the agent's \`auth\` limiter — retry after 3 s`, or as something in front of the agent, with `details.rateLimit = { source, limiter?, retryAfterSecs? }`. The code stays `e.p.msg.rate_limited`.

## 4. The fallback warning outlived its cooldown

The warning was already per agent: it is recorded by `(vtaDid, mediatorDid)` and read from `byVta[activeAgent]`. But the no-reply record was only replaced by a session build after the cooldown, so switching back to an agent showed a fallback that had already ended until that agent's next request. The health snapshot now drops it once `isAnySittingOut` says the cooldown is over.

## Not addressed

- **Keeping a replaced socket open (`retireConnection`) buys nothing against this mediator.** It closes the old socket the moment the replacement connects, so requests still on it lose their replies whatever the wallet does. The duel is gone; that loss is not.
- **A VTA-side warning.** At 15:49:44 the VTA accepted a fresh TSP relationship invite from the wallet and then could not send the accept (`SendAccept in state Bidirectional`). Its log says traffic still flows. This belongs in a VTA issue, not here.

## Tests

- `core/tests/vta.rate-limit.mjs` (new):
  - three simultaneous sign-ins make 2 requests
  - a refused sign-in is shared with the callers already waiting, then retried fresh by the next caller
  - a stale 401 does not discard a fresh token
  - 429 attribution with and without readable headers, a CDN's HTML 429, the one-way POST path, `retry-after` parsing
- `extension/tests/warm-session-health.test.mts`: the `isSuperseded` cases.
- `extension/tests/mediator-fallback.test.mts`: per-agent isolation, including an agent DID that prefixes another; the cooldown ending; a status read not consuming the cooldown; other down reasons left alone.

`npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no new retries; the existing single 401 retry now discards less.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): a genuine drop still re-arms with backoff; only a superseded close is ignored, and its replacement carries the inbox.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound path untouched.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none. The 429 reading follows the existing VTA contract (`vta_sdk::rate_limit`) and matches on machine-readable fields, never message text (R3.7).
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): an unattributed 429 is reported as not the agent's own limiter rather than guessed; an expired fallback is no longer claimed.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): pool and bearer state are in memory and rebuilt on demand.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: spec(rooms)!: rooms/info and rooms/usage require a proof, like every other rooms/* task (#750)
body:
spec(rooms)!: rooms/info and rooms/usage require a proof, like every other rooms/* task (#750)

Both said a proof was RECOMMENDED, on the reasoning that the room-issued chain
is "bound to whoever the host authenticated". A room operation carries no
session, so the only party a host can authenticate is the proof's signer. The
chain's leaf must be that party. Without a proof there is nobody to bind it
to, and the presentation becomes a bearer token. Every other rooms/* task
already requires a proof for this reason. A host implementing the chain rule
refuses an unsigned info or usage request anyway, so the RECOMMENDED was
already unworkable.

Breaking for a producer that sent these unsigned. Both specs are drafts.

title: feat(sign-in): offer to join an unknown community (VTC) from a sign-in code (#318)
body:
feat(sign-in): offer to join an unknown community (VTC) from a sign-in code (#318)

A sign-in code from a community the wallet did not know dead-ended on "Not
one of your communities". A verified document that publishes `VTCRest` is now
offered to join, after the same checks as before (DID document resolved and
verified, the code clicked on its own portal), and nothing goes to it until
the person continues.

- "Join <host>?" sends nothing. "See what it asks" fetches
  `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3` as a throwaway did:key, so the community
  learns nothing about who is asking; the reply must be signed by the VTC for
  `authentication` with a key its verified document lists there.
- The wallet applies only under a criterion that asks for no credential, no
  invitation and no vetting (automatic first, else review). Otherwise it says
  what the community asks for and ends, with nothing about the person sent.
- "Ask to join <host>" shows the admission mode, the requested attributes as
  text fields (required ones enforced), an explicit registry-consent box
  (default no), and the agent's DIDs marked with any site they already sign
  in to.
- "Send request" records the same didSelfIssued vault entry a member's
  sign-in uses (`bindProfile`: portal origin + VTC DID), because the VTA signs
  only as an entry's principal and the VTC takes the applicant from that
  signature; then `vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3`, signed by the VTA.
  - allow: straight on to "Sign in to <host>?" for the same code.
  - refer / requestMore / requestAlreadyOpen: "Request sent - you can sign in
    once <host> approves it"; the entry stays, the flow ends, no sign-in
    document is sent.
  - deny, a refusal, an unreachable VTC or a VTA refusal to sign: the reason
    plainly, and the entry is deleted again.
- core: `vtc/join.ts` (planJoin, manifest/submit 0.3 builders, verdict
  reader); `postCommunityTask` shares sendOob's post-and-verify with a reply
  purpose.

No new permissions, host matches or dependencies.

Refs trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#58 (VTI-LNK-101), OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#315
